text:
Scope of Hacks on U.S. Water Supply Widens as Evidence Points to Iran. Michigan and Minnesota are among at least seven states coping with cyberattacks aimed at disrupting water systems nationwide.
The scope of cyberattacks on U.S. water systems has grown to include at least seven states and may be far wider,  officials and experts warned, as the authorities raced to safeguard the  nation’s water supply against an assault that increasingly appeared to  be the work of Iran.

While  there were no indications that any water supply had been altered or  made unsafe to drink, state and local officials throughout the country  were on high alert for potential problems in vulnerable computers that  are commonly used to monitor and adjust water quality, including  chemical-treatment levels and water pressure. Minnesota first publicly  reported the attacks, and now Michigan says its systems have also been  targeted.

The  attack has little precedent, experts said, but has long been the stuff  of nightmares and sensationalized Hollywood thrillers: an apparent  cyberattack by a foreign power during a time of war that could, at least  in theory, jeopardize the health and safety of Americans.

Officials  cautioned that they had not definitively determined that Iran was  responsible for the attack and that the investigation was still  preliminary. But they said Iran had stepped up cyberattacks since the  U.S. and Israel launched a war against the country five months ago, and  had previously targeted similar water systems and other critical  infrastructure in the U.S. There seemed no financial motive, making a  criminal attack less likely.

https://t.co/WOFKFyKjjN
#US #Iran #Cyberattack

Despite  growing concerns, President Trump sought to downplay the matter on  Friday by blaming Minnesota — which was early to spot and report the  recent surge in malicious hacking activity, helping to prompt other  states to probe their own water systems — for suffering intrusions his  own intelligence agencies believe were highly likely carried out by  Iran, officials familiar with the assessment said.

“I think Minnesota is behind it,” Mr. Trump said on Friday in response to a reporter’s question about Iran’s possible  involvement, which The New York Times earlier reported. “I don’t think  there was an Iranian cyberattack.”

The  state’s Democratic governor, Tim Walz, dismissed the accusation,  warning in a social media post that this “is what modern warfare looks  like.”

After  Mr. Trump’s remarks, federal officials privately said Iran remains the  top suspect but that the assessment remained preliminary and had not yet  established definitive forensic proof. That is not unusual in complex  cyber-investigations, which can often take months to reach authoritative  conclusions, if at all.

Nate  George, the mayor of Braham, a small city north of Minneapolis that was  among those affected by the cyberattack, said federal and local  officials had little doubt about the likely culprit.

“We’re  getting bits and pieces of information from the state of Minnesota and  the F.B.I.,” he said in an interview on Friday afternoon. “They are  pretty sure it’s Iranian actors” but are reluctant to say so publicly,  he added. A memo sent by an industry group that shares cyberthreat  information among water utilities that was obtained by Wired magazine said the attacks aligned with hacking activity being conducted by Iran-affiliated actors.

Mr.  George, a Republican who is running for state auditor, said he had  heard the president’s remarks casting doubt on Iranian culpability. He  said that the president was “entitled to his opinion,” but that it is  incumbent on state officials to help cities harden their defenses  against cyberattacks.

Minnesota was not the only state to suffer intrusions. In a public advisory published late Thursday, after the Times report, the F.B.I. and the  Environmental Protection Agency said that since Monday “at least seven  states have reported incidents to the F.B.I., and some of that activity  degraded water operations.”

Officials  have declined to say which states have been affected, but a spokesman  for the Michigan state government confirmed that his state’s system was  attacked.

“We  received a small number of reports from Michigan communities indicating  activity consistent with what federal agencies described,” Dale George,  the spokesman, said in an email. He added that all systems affected  continued to operate safely, and that there were “no known impacts that  posed a public health concern.”

Mr.  George later said that nine municipal water systems in Michigan had  reported issues. Earlier in the week, Minnesota reported hackers were  spotted targeting roughly three dozen municipalities.

Alex  Orleans, a former U.S. government cybersecurity contractor who  specializes in tracking Iranian hacking groups, said Tehran had been  engaging in a wide variety of hacking operations against U.S., Israeli  and Middle Eastern targets since the start of the war in February. But  the intrusions into the U.S. water systems appeared to be a significant  escalation.

“What’s  unprecedented here is that we’re seeing direct, tangible effects to  live industrial control systems inside U.S. critical infrastructure,”  said Mr. Orleans, who is now the chief of threat intelligence at Sublime  Security, an email protection company.

The  U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an advisory  issued Thursday, said the hackers were “targeting water entities of all  sizes” and recommended facilities unplug vulnerable controllers from the  internet. The hacking activity, it added, had “resulted in boil water  notices and sustained manual operations.”

The agency has for months been warning the public that Iran may seek to compromise water utilities and other critical infrastructure.

Former  intelligence officials and cybersecurity experts said the hackers were  likely engaging in opportunistic behavior rather than selecting specific  cities and towns to infiltrate. That means that potentially any  facility using the vulnerable internet-connected operational systems was  at risk.

Iran,  Mr. Orleans said, was likely looking to infiltrate as many victims  networks as possible throughout the states before they can protect  against “the opportunistic tradecraft that the U.S. government has  offered multiple, explicit warnings about.”

Mr.  George, the mayor in Minnesota, said city officials had received  guidance on how to patch water systems that had been affected and how to  bolster defenses against attacks Iranian hackers are capable of  carrying out.

While  manual workarounds are keeping water flowing for now, he said the  attack highlighted the rudimentary nature of critical infrastructure in  many small cities.

“I think the troubling thing on the horizon is how do we move forward to a more secure system,” Mr. George said.

“IT infrastructure upgrades are very costly and we are a very small municipality.”

text:
A STORMY SATURDAY IS IN STORE ⛈️
In the latest update from the Storm Prediction Center, most of Southern Middle Tennessee has been upgraded to a SLIGHT Risk (Level 2 of 5) for severe thunderstorms on Saturday. The primary threats will be damaging wind gusts over 60 MPH and isolated flash flooding. While the tornado risk remains very low, we’ll have a little more spin in the atmosphere than usual, so it’s something we’ll be watching closely. Rainfall totals between a quarter inch and one inch will be likely. Some localized totals upwards of 2-3 inches will be possible.

I’m expecting TWO ROUNDS of storms tomorrow…
🌅 ROUND ONE: EARLY MORNING (4 AM – 10 AM)
The first round will move through during the early morning hours, generally between 4 AM and 10 AM. That doesn’t mean it will rain the entire six hours at your location, but that’s the overall window for the area. Severe weather isn’t expected with this first round, but locally heavy rainfall and frequent lightning will be possible.

After that, we should catch a break in the weather during midday. Some locations may even see a few peeks of sunshine before the second round develops.

🌩️ ROUND TWO: AFTERNOON & EVENING (3 PM – 10 PM)
The second round is the one we’ll be watching most closely. Between 3 PM and 10 PM, scattered showers and thunderstorms are expected to develop along an approaching cold front before moving east across the area.

Unlike the morning activity, not everyone will see rain during this second round. Storms will be much more scattered, but any storm that develops could become strong, with damaging wind gusts being the main concern. This is also when the severe weather threat will be at its highest since storms will be developing during the warmest part of the day.

One of the biggest forecast questions is exactly where storms will first develop along the cold front. Right now, most guidance suggests storms will initiate across our central counties, generally along the US 231 corridor, before pushing east. If that happens, some of our far western communities may miss out on the afternoon storms altogether.

Of course, there’s still some uncertainty with exactly where those storms will form, so we’ll be watching trends closely tomorrow. For now, I’d say everyone has a chance of seeing storms, but the highest afternoon storm chances appear to be along and east of US 231.

Stay tuned for updates throughout the day tomorrow, and if you haven’t already, be sure to download the Southern Tennessee Weather app for the latest forecasts, live radar, and weather alerts. It’s 100% FREE!

I’m going to let you in on a little secret.

Campaigning is hard work. It’s time-consuming. It’s expensive.

I’m guessing you know all that — but here’s something that might surprise you:

It’s FUN.

I get to spend all my time meeting new people and convincing them to believe in themselves, each other and a better world.

I get to attend fairs and march in parades, shake hands, hand out freeze pops, candy and dog treats — and yes, sometimes dance.

I get to think about the issues facing us today, not just in the abstract, but with a sense of agency: “what would I do?”

I get to have conversations (both one-on-one and at our regular town halls) with people about the things that excite them, anger them, scare them … and provide an ear even when I can’t offer an immediate solution.

Heck, I get to drive an ambulance with my name on it. That’s incredibly cool.

Don’t get me wrong: our campaign is deadly serious, with the goal of electing new leadership and choosing a different way forward for Minnesota and the nation. We’re working hard to make that happen. But doing so is a gift, not a grind.

Bottom line: I’m not doing this for fun, but I’m having fun doing it.

I’d love to have you join us.

Here you go. Over the last few days, a few friends have been in touch and asked about what I think about Dr. Phil. 

Dr. Phil and Big D Disclosure:

I can't take the man seriously. The last show I happened to watch before I tuned him out forever was the segment where women came on the show to be evaluated for breast enhancement. I don't listen to or watch that kind of television. And in my defense, I was at someone else's house when I saw it.

Recently, in a high level group, one of the leaders of disclosure offered this on Dr. Phil's having seen the UFO/PURSUE files early before the public. He said, "the messenger becomes the medium." Since this came from someone I highly regard, that's all I needed to hear to step away from this roll out.

Here are some first quotes I saw on the issue from Dr. Phil: 

"What made the press was always some guy that was too drunk to fish. He was out there kind of stumbling around, said he was abducted and anally probed and then let go." --Dr. Phil on News Nation with Ross Coulthart

"You've been shown the drunks who 'got abducted' You were never shown the others. Military pilots. Navy pilots. Research scientists. There's a reason for that." --X Post 

I get his backward-land approach of casually citing the absurd to refer the general public to the serious cases (in his opinion) now being released by PURSUE and to give more credibility to military witnesses.

So here's my opinion from a UFO researcher and someone who helps experiencers one-on-one and in groups. 

Find a better way to make your point Dr. Phil. Where you aren't sketching caricatures of UFO victims. Learn victimology from a criminal justice perspective before you stigmafy a whole section of the population and globe.

And for god sake, don't make yourself a poor man's Nicholas Sparks whose formulaic 'man saves damaged woman' becomes your stock in trade....except yours is highly regarded professional or more specifically 'doctor saves ufo disclosure from itself.'

We don't need your kind of saving. We're doing fine on our own. And if your brand of crisis is wrapped up in the type of television your credibility is built on I'd rather say "no thanks" to disclosure and keep on keeping on.

For all of you following, I've been sharing a little bit of the toxicity I've found in the ufo sphere over my 11 years on this subject. I know it seems very Jerry Springer like, but please know it has only been for people to see how some of us have really been treated in this field (from people who have security clearances). Dr. Phil just appears to be a more polished nuanced version of the same. Are we so desperate for credibility in this field that we're willing to accept any form of acknowledgement from these types of shock and awe personalities? I would argue their influence will ultimately hurt us, not help us.

When you've been navigating the waters of ufo's, healing, meaning making, and transformation for so long and you have seen it first hand (and you have to see it to believe it) you can share the wisdom helping others navigate their own process safely and to WARN others what to look for. 

I'll post my thoughts on the new paper: A National Preparedness Framework for the Human Consequences of Disclosure

Which is what you all were also asking about anyway. Had to get the Dr. Phil bit out of the way first.

text:
A $150,000 bounty was placed on his head because he personally sank enemy boats: the story of the intelligence operative who became the target of the entire Russian special forces.

His name was Oleksandr Kusharev, callsign "Zelenyi" ("Green"). To the Russians, he was a constant thorn in their side—so dangerous that they launched a full-scale manhunt for him.

To his brothers-in-arms, however, he was a legend, the kind of commander who brought his men home with little or no casualties.

Before the war, Kusharev served as a corrections officer. He later fought in the Anti-Terrorist Operation with Ukraine's 79th Air Assault Brigade and completed 13 parachute jumps. He dedicated one of those jumps to his son, Ruslan.

His wife, Sofiia, is a Crimean Tatar. Her parents disapproved of their relationship, but, as she puts it, Oleksandr "basically kidnapped her." They dreamed of building a home together and raising their son—until the war changed everything.

On April 28, 2024, Zelenyi's unit liberated Nestryha Island. Armed with a heavy-caliber Browning machine gun, he personally sank enemy boats and cut down Russian landing forces. The Russians launched an assault with up to two companies of troops, but his unit destroyed one boat after another.

Eventually, they ran out of ammunition and were forced to withdraw. A 152-mm artillery shell exploded nearby, and shrapnel severely wounded Zelenyi's legs. It was his first serious injury.

His comrades say that thanks to his meticulous planning, many missions ended without a single casualty—not even a wounded soldier. He always knew how to lift morale when everyone else was losing hope.

"Guys, don't give a damn about the Russians! We'll break through anything. We are Ukraine!" he used to say.

In the Kherson region, Kusharev's team eliminated a Russian Navy intelligence colonel. After that operation, a $150,000 bounty was offered for Kusharev, while $100,000 was offered for each of the other members of his team.

At the end of September 2024, he was wounded again. Once more, his legs were torn by shrapnel. And once again, he returned to the front.

On April 27, 2025, he recorded what would become a prophetic message:

"When I die, no one will write that an entire era has come to an end."

On June 9, 2025, Oleksandr Kusharev was killed while carrying out a combat mission. He was 36 years old.

On February 24, 2026, he was posthumously awarded the "Mercy and Justice" distinction. His wife, Sofiia, and their 12-year-old son, Ruslan, accepted the award on his behalf.

He didn't have an era.

He was simply a soldier who did his job better than anyone else.

And that is precisely what made him irreplaceable.

Teresa gasped. “The sheer audacity!”

“Rule number two,” I cut her off effortlessly. “Sanitation. Look at this floor. It’s repulsive. You will clean up your own debris. Furthermore, my master bedroom is a restricted zone. Neither of you will cross that threshold without explicit permission.”

“And finally,” I leaned against the marble counter, locking eyes with my father-in-law. “Rule number three: Decibel control. When I return home, I require peace. The television volume drops by fifty percent, and after 10:00 PM, this apartment will be silent.”

Teresa’s face mottled with purple rage. She turned to Richard, her voice escalating into a shrill, piercing crescendo. “Richard! Do you hear this venom? David hasn’t been gone twenty-four hours, and she is treating us like stray dogs! Why is the Lord punishing me?”

Richard hoisted himself off the sofa, pointing a trembling, accusatory finger at my face. “You lack shame, Eleanor. We are your elders. You owe us reverence. This condo belongs to my son, and we will operate within it however we damn well please!”

A bitter, humorless laugh escaped my lips. “The deed is joint, Richard. But ninety percent of the initial down payment was wired from my parents’ estate. David merely contributes to a fraction of the mortgage—a mortgage I am currently servicing. So no, you will not do as you please.”

“Liar!” Richard roared. “My son is a titan! He’s in Japan building an empire for us! I’m calling him right now. He will put you in your miserable place!”

I crossed my arms, feeling a dark satisfaction bloom in my chest. “By all means, dial his number. Though I highly doubt he’ll answer. I’ve already triggered a freeze on all his financial assets. I’m giving you both a grace period of three days to adjust to these rules. If you cannot, I will have building security escort you to the sidewalk.”

With that, I turned on my heel, walked into my master suite, and engaged the heavy deadbolt.

Through the thick drywall, I could hear the symphony of their panic. The crashing of a remote control. Teresa’s hysterical sobbing as she dialed David’s number over and over.

“David, pick up! Your lunatic wife is terrorizing us!” she wailed into the voicemail void.

But the line remained dead. David was far too occupied with his new diamond-draped reality to care about the mess he left behind. Lying in the dark, I felt no guilt. Kindness offered to parasites is merely self-sabotage. It was time to sterilize my life.

The SAVE Act isn't just voter suppression. It's a transfer of billions of dollars from taxpayers and citizens to a handful of private companies. Here's where the money goes.
THE IMPLEMENTATION COSTS (Who Pays):
Washington State alone estimates $35.7–$39.3 million to implement the SAVE Act—$26.2M for one-time setup, $9.5M + annually. In a presidential year, ongoing costs jump to $12.25–$14.65 million for that single state.​​
The National Association of Counties says implementation costs exceed current federal HAVA funding by 11.3 times—roughly $510 million per election cycle nationwide. And the Senate version of the SAVE Act offers zero federal dollars to help states pay for it. Counties run 100,000+ polling places with 770,000 poll workers. They'd foot the bill alone.​​
THE VENDORS (Who Gets Paid):
Election Systems & Software (ES&S): The largest voting machine and election technology vendor in the U.S., controlling roughly 50% of the market. ES&S spent $250,000 on federal lobbying in 2024 and has a documented history of taking election officials on junkets to Las Vegas and New York while pitching multi-million dollar contracts.​​​​ Their machines and poll books are already deployed nationwide; the SAVE Act's new verification mandates would force states to buy upgrades.
KnowInk: Electronic poll book vendor whose "Poll Pad" is used across the country. Their units cost roughly $1,760 each plus $150 annual software fees per device. A single large county might need hundreds. The SAVE Act's in-person verification requirements would drive demand for their check-in systems.​​
ID. me: Identity verification contractor with tens of millions of dollars in federal contracts. The House Oversight Committee launched a probe into ID. me's government contracts, questioning their facial recognition technology and data handling. The SAVE Act's "documentary proof" mandate would expand the market for exactly this type of vendor.​​
Civix: Won a $10.6 million contract in Pennsylvania to upgrade the state's voter registration system. States nationwide would need similar overhauls to comply with SAVE Act citizenship verification requirements.​​
Votec: Voter registration software vendor serving Texas and Nevada counties. When states are forced to rebuild their registration systems, existing vendors get the first call.​​
THE LOBBYING ARMY (Who Opens the Door):
ES&S hired Peck Madigan Jones ($80,000 in one quarter) and Vectre Corp. Dominion Voting Systems hired Brownstein Farber Hyatt & Schreck, putting Nancy Pelosi's former chief of staff on their account.​​ These companies don't just sell machines—they buy access.
THE DARK MONEY PIPELINE (Who Funds the Push):
The Koch network is the financial backbone. In the 2024 cycle, their political operation raised $578 million and spent $548 million.​​ That money flows to:
• The Heritage Foundation (bill architect)
• Americans for Prosperity (grassroots pressure)
• Texas Public Policy Foundation (legal framework)
• Mercatus Center (academic cover)
The Kochs don't own stock in these vendors directly. They own the policy infrastructure that creates the demand. When Heritage writes the bill and AFP pressures legislators, the vendors get the contracts. The Kochs get the policy outcomes. Everyone in the chain gets paid except the voter.

THE MATH:
• ~100 cases of non-citizen voting in 40+ years (Heritage's own database)
• $510 million+ in new implementation costs per cycle (NACo estimate)
• 21 million eligible citizens at risk of disenfranchisement
• 5 years in prison for election workers who make paperwork errors
The SAVE Act creates a $500 million+ market to solve a 100-case problem. That's not election integrity. That's a business model.
Follow the money.

text:
🚨BREAKING NEWS (https://t.co/7eIjDNSucC): AARO Is Sole-Sourcing a UFO Data Subscription from National UFO Historical Records Center - One That Their Own Website Says Does Not Exist Yet

Washington Headquarters Services intends to award a five-year contract for digital access to a private archive whose materials are not digitized. 

On 31 July the Washington Headquarters Services posted a notice of intent to award a sole-source, firm-fixed-price contract to the National UFO Historical Records Center of Rio Rancho, New Mexico, for a multi-year subscription giving the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office digital access to the archive's pre-1990 case data, metadata and analytical products. The structure is one base year plus four one-year options. No dollar value is published. 

The notice, solicitation number NUFOHRC_20260731, cites 10 U.S.C. 3204(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302-1, "only one responsible source." It states that the vendor holds records that "exist exclusively within its archives and are not available in any other public or private repository," and that market research identified no other organisation able to meet the government's minimum needs. It specifies that the acquisition "is not for professional labor or advisory services," and describes the object of purchase as "a pre-existing, proprietary commercial data subscription."

That last phrase is the problem. The vendor's public materials do not describe a data subscription. They describe a building.

Access is another matter. The organisation's website offers two routes in: a general-interest open house on the last Saturday of each month between noon and 4pm, and an appointment scheduler for researchers, scientists and academics. 

There is no database, no login, no catalogue, no application programming interface and no published finding aid. The site's own statement of its access plan reads: "Efforts are underway to secure much-needed funding for this effort whereby materials can be accessed via cloud-based options."  That is written in the present tense, as an objective being fundraised for. The first item on the organisation's donation page is "Digitization of Material." In a June 2024 interview Marler described digitisation as an ambition: "we want to get actively involved in digitizing the material to make it available to researchers worldwide."

A volunteer-scale nonprofit operating out of school portables, still raising money to digitise its collection, is therefore being sole-sourced to supply the Pentagon with a pre-existing commercial digital subscription?

Why the wording matters

The commercial-item framing is not decoration. Calling the requirement a data subscription rather than a service keeps it clear of FAR Part 37 advisory and assistance review, avoids personal-services and organisational-conflict analysis, and supports the finding that competition is unavailable. Calling it "pre-existing" is what makes it a purchase rather than development. Remove that word and the government is paying a nonprofit to build a capability it does not yet have - which is the shape of a grant, and grants are competed through announcements that take months rather than an afternoon.

The context the AARO does not mention

AARO published Volume I of its congressionally mandated Historical Record Report in March 2024, concluding that it had found no evidence of extraterrestrial technology and no verifiable programme concealment. Volume II, required by Section 6802 of the FY23 National Defense Authorization Act, has not appeared. The office is now committing to five years of access to a body of pre-1990 material it did not previously hold, while its own records-release channel produces nothing: no fifth PURSUE tranche in 22 days, no instrument behind the NDA waiver on day 11.

Both positions can be held honestly. An office can conclude the record shows nothing and still want to read the rest of it. What sits less comfortably is the option structure. Documents are bought once. Four option years running to FY2031 imply a recurring relationship with an outside archive across two more administrations, which is a resourcing decision rather than a research one.

BLACKGROVE ASSESSMENT

We assess this is a grant structured as a purchase, and that the irregularity is more likely bureaucratic than concealing.

The ordinary explanation is available and has not been displaced. A program office wants the NICAP, APRO and CUFOS files, discovers the only route runs through one nonprofit in New Mexico, and a contracting officer reaches for the fastest instrument on the shelf. Federal agencies buy commercial data subscriptions constantly, and one base year plus four options is the boilerplate for one. On that reading the defects in the justification are the residue of speed, not of intent.

What the ordinary explanation does not cover is the term. If the requirement is a fixed corpus of pre-1990 documents, it is satisfied by a single delivery. The option years indicate that someone expects the archive to keep producing through the end of the decade, which means either continuing digitization funded by the government, or continuing analysis and the notice explicitly disclaims buying analysis.

The award value resolves this and nothing else will. Below roughly $50,000 the action is a records-access convenience buy and the paperwork irregularity is the whole story. At six figures a year into an organisation whose gross receipts sit under the Form 990 filing threshold, the government is standing up a capability quietly, off any visible programme line, in leased school portables. Those are different events with the same solicitation number.

This is an assessment of a contracting action. Readers inclined to treat the purchase as evidence that AARO expects to find something should note that the government has given no indication of the material's content, and that the vendor's collection has been openly available to any researcher willing to drive to Rio Rancho on the last Saturday of the month.

The staircase was built sometime between roughly 1877 and 1881. The wood has been identified as a type of spruce not native to New Mexico. The stairs rise approximately 20 feet (about 6.1 meters) to the choir loft, completing two full 360-degree turns. It was constructed without nails, metal fasteners, or glue; the pieces are joined with wooden pegs. There is no central newel post or pole for support in the classic sense.

According to the account long associated with the Sisters of Loretto (who commissioned the Gothic Revival chapel in the 1870s for their girls’ academy), the original architect died before a practical means of access to the choir loft could be provided.

After consulting builders who could not offer a satisfactory solution, the sisters undertook a nine-day novena to St. Joseph, the patron saint of carpenters. On the final day a mysterious stranger appeared (sometimes described as arriving with a donkey and a few simple tools), offered to build the staircase, worked alone (accounts vary on the duration, from weeks to several months), completed the work, and then disappeared without giving his name or accepting payment. The sisters came to regard the builder as St. Joseph himself and the staircase as miraculous.

Amateur historian Mary Jean Cook has argued that the likely builder was François-Jean (“Frank” or “Frenchy”) Rochas (c. 1843–1894), a French immigrant carpenter and rancher who lived in the region. Supporting points include an 1895 Santa Fe New Mexican notice of his death that credited him with building the Loretto Chapel staircase (and another staircase at St. Vincent Sanitarium), along with a logbook entry recording a payment to him for wood in 1881. The identification remains debated.

text:
This may be one of the more promising and interesting paths toward collective bargaining in college sports—not because Oregon State’s women’s basketball players are certain to win, but because they have chosen a forum that could produce a durable legal ruling (and quickly). 

Most athlete-organizing efforts have relied on federal labor law. That presents two problems: public universities generally fall outside the NLRA, and organizing at private universities depends on an NLRB whose doctrine can change with presidential administrations. Northwestern received a favorable regional ruling, only for the Board to decline jurisdiction. Dartmouth’s players won an election, but the effort ended before producing a contract.

Oregon State offers a different route. Because it is a public university, the players are proceeding under Oregon’s public-sector collective-bargaining law. The immediate question is whether they qualify as university employees under state law. That is uncertain, but it creates a potentially replicable strategy: organize athletes at public universities in states with favorable labor laws, one institution at a time.

That is exponentially more realistic than trying to create a single national bargaining unit from the outset. The path could therefore be incremental. One team establishes employee status and negotiates a contract. Other teams use that decision and agreement as a roadmap. Campus units then affiliate through a national organization, coordinate bargaining priorities, and eventually pursue broader conference-level arrangements. Tons of roadblocks for sure, but that has legs. 

The first contract could matter almost as much as the first ruling. It could address compensation, medical care, injury protections, scholarship security, practice and travel demands, grievance procedures, roster decisions, and academic conflicts. Future athletes would then be organizing around an actual agreement rather than an abstract promise.

There are serious obstacles. A team union cannot necessarily compel a conference to bargain unless the conference is also an employer. Different state laws may produce different rights, and some athletes may have no viable organizing route. A national system may ultimately require legislation or voluntary conference recognition.

But labor structures do not have to emerge fully formed. They can be built from legally recognized local units.

That is why this petition matters. A victory would not unionize college sports. It would establish one workable route: Oregon State, then other public universities in receptive states, then coordinated campus unions, and eventually broader bargaining.

Here’s a roundup of major Canadian news as of Friday, July 31, 2026.

Economy

Statistics Canada reported the economy grew 0.3% in May, exceeding expectations. This marks a second straight month of growth and puts Canada on track for its strongest quarterly performance in more than three years.

WestJet Labour Dispute

WestJet flight attendants (represented by CUPE, about 4,400 workers) issued a 72-hour strike notice. The airline responded with a lockout notice. A work stoppage could begin as early as Sunday, August 2, at 12:01 a.m. Mountain Time if no deal is reached. 

Talks continue on key issues, including pay for ground time (boarding, etc.). WestJet has offered flexible free changes/cancellations for travel between July 30 and August 4. No major cancellations were reported yet as of late Thursday/early Friday, but travellers should monitor closely.

Federal Politics & National Issues

RCMP future: Canada’s premiers are urging Ottawa to begin negotiations “urgently” on the future of the RCMP and clarify plans for provinces that want to keep the force as their primary policing service.

Canada-U.S. trade tensions: Ongoing tariff threats from the U.S. (including recent signals of higher duties). Prime Minister Mark Carney has said he does not see value in using Canadian energy as leverage, preferring other approaches. Ontario’s representative in Washington noted that Canadian retaliation appears to be registering with the U.S. administration. Some premiers have pushed for stronger countermeasures.

Public alerts: After the death of 11-year-old autistic boy Parker in Calgary, Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre and others are calling for reforms to the national emergency alert system so it better covers missing vulnerable children.

Other political notes include discussions on high-speed rail, rolling back certain Canadian content (Cancon) requirements for affordability reasons, and infrastructure/housing funding announcements.

Regional & Other Notable Stories

Alberta (Calgary): Community memorials and vigils continue for Parker after the near two-week search ended with his body found in a stormwater system.

Ontario: First Nations chiefs are calling for a public inquiry into the province’s wildfire response. Traffic issues persist near the Ambassador Bridge despite the new Gordie Howe International Bridge. A man linked to a Toronto police corruption probe has alleged global drug-trafficking ties.

British Columbia: Ongoing wildfire concerns (evacuation orders, some residents defying them, increased risks from weather). A B.C. court ruled that “blanket” forced treatment of involuntary psychiatric patients is unconstitutional. Other stories include lacrosse team eligibility disputes and art donation controversies.

Quebec: A man charged in connection with his son’s death was shot during arrest; the police watchdog is investigating. A bus crash near Gaspé sent 23 people to hospital (no serious injuries reported). A court blocked unauthorized peptide sales.

Nova Scotia / Atlantic: A man shot at a Halifax park criticized earlier cuts to security in the area, highlighting risks for unhoused people.

Manitoba & elsewhere: Storms caused power outages and damage in southern Manitoba. Wildfire updates continue in northwestern Ontario.

Additional Notes

Sports: Commonwealth Games ongoing; Canadian athletes (including boxers and others) are competing for medals.

Espionage case: A Canadian woman who worked as a NATO intern has been identified in connection with a Belgian investigation into alleged spying (reports link it to China-related suspicions).

Wildfires remain active in parts of the country, with varying levels of evacuations and response efforts.

News moves quickly—check CBC, CTV, Global News, The Globe and Mail, or The Canadian Press for the latest developments, especially on the WestJet situation and weather/wildfire updates.

I am overjoyed. I received this text message  from a woman who I meant two years ago in Chicago. Her name is Ebony. She attended a presentation I gave at Northwestern Hospital. She came up to me afterwards and told me that she experienced a freeing  relief when I was doing my portion of the presentation regarding caretakers. This portion is also in my first book and I have received probably more feedback on that particular chapter than any other. Ebony remembered my birthday. Although a few days late lol. I remember her speaking with me afterwards. She was emotional and grateful and was so pleased she made the decision to attend my lecture. If this is your first time reading  part of what I say regarding caretaking, I want you to know that a tendency which becomes a given reality for many who experience the death of a loved one will afterwards ask themselves what they could have done differently and or better? I call this The Caretakers Lament.  Let's go ahead and answer the question, what you could have done differently and the answer is nothing. And you were not and are  not supposed to. You have one thing to do. Do not make the mistake subconsciously to believe that you are a heal- taker. You are a caretaker. You cannot administer chemotherapy. You cannot provide  radiation nor can you perform  surgery. You did not create the cancer and you're not going to heal the cancer… remember you're not supposed to. Are you supposed to be present 24/7? No. Are you supposed to guarantee yourself that you will be there at the moment of death? That is not even realistic in terms of a guarantee. Are you supposed to stay by their side constantly and then be overwhelmed with guilt because you believe you should have been there more? You are human. You have one thing to do. And that is to love. Not to  be present 24/7. Not  to heal. Not take away the pain.  Instead through care.  Perhaps you are to hold a hand. Wipe a brow. Maybe prepare meals. Change linens. Rub their shoulders.  Listen. Cry. Perhaps play their favorite music when they can't reach the dial. Take messages. Give updates. Pray. Pray with them. Care taking is simply to love. Were you supposed to do more? If I were to say yes then I would have to make that a qualified statement which is not possible . We cannot turn back time. I would be  concerned if somebody intentionally deliberately willfully neglected someone when a  loved one who  sought your love. And that would be something to work through by engaging in therapy. 
So care for others. But don't heal them. Because if I find out you have the capacity to heal somebody from cancer and you're not healing me I will find your ass. 😂 
Care? Yes.
Heal? No. 
Love? Yes. 
Save? No. 
Empathize? Yes. 
Cure? No. 
Offer yourself? Yes. 
Neglect yourself? No. 
Carry guilt? No. 
Carry lovely memories? Yes.

text:
The Ottoman government accepted the Circassians as Muslim refugees and created institutions to organize their settlement. Officials offered some families land, grain, tools and temporary tax exemptions, but the empire lacked the resources to manage the crisis effectively.

Circassians were resettled across Anatolia, the southern shores of the Sea of Marmara, the Balkans, Thessaly, Syria and other Ottoman provinces. Many refugees died during their first years from disease, hunger and unfamiliar climates. Communities accustomed to mountain environments were sometimes placed in swamps, plains or regions already suffering from land shortages.

The settlement process also affected people already living in these areas. Ottoman authorities sometimes placed Circassian families on disputed lands or along politically sensitive frontiers. This created tension with local Arab, Turkish, Kurdish, Armenian, Bulgarian and other communities.

The Circassians were victims of imperial expulsion, but some later became participants in Ottoman military and settlement policies that harmed other populations. Their history in exile contains both suffering and complex relationships with the peoples among whom they were settled.

Large Circassian populations eventually developed in modern Turkey, Jordan, Syria and smaller communities elsewhere.

In Jordan, Circassian refugees helped rebuild and expand Amman during the late nineteenth century. They established farms, neighborhoods and local institutions before the city became the capital of modern Jordan.

Circassians in Syria created communities around the Golan Heights, Damascus and other regions. In Turkey, villages were established across central and northwestern Anatolia and near the Black Sea.

Many Circassians entered Ottoman military service, administration and politics. Their reputation as experienced cavalrymen and soldiers gave them opportunities within the imperial system, although most refugees remained farmers and villagers.

Over generations, tribal identities sometimes weakened as exiles developed a broader Circassian identity. Diaspora organizations later opened schools, published newspapers and attempted to preserve the Adyghe language and cultural memory. 

Circassian communities preserved their identity through family traditions, oral history, music, dance and a social code often called Adyghe Khabze. This cultural system emphasized hospitality, courage, dignity, respect for elders, proper conduct and responsibility toward guests and the community.

Traditional dances expressed courtship, honor and social discipline. Music preserved memories of heroes, battles, exile and lost villages.

Language survival proved more difficult. Circassian languages belong to the Northwest Caucasian family and contain complex sound systems. In many diaspora communities, Turkish, Arabic and other majority languages gradually replaced Adyghe in daily life.

Some families preserved Circassian identity even after losing language. Cultural organizations now teach Adyghe, organize dance groups and maintain connections between diaspora communities and Caucasus.

The description of events as Circassian genocide has become central to modern Circassian identity. Supporters of this term point to deliberate destruction of villages, mass killing, forced removal of the population and colonization of Circassian territory.

Some scholars prefer the term ethnic cleansing, while others describe expulsion as a genocidal process. Debate is influenced by differences in legal definitions, historical interpretation and contemporary politics.

The essential historical reality is less uncertain. Russian conquest removed most Circassians from their homeland and transformed them from a people living primarily in Caucasus into a people whose majority lived abroad.

The Circassian exile was not simply the movement of refugees after a lost war. It was the destruction of an Indigenous society across much of its historic territory.

text:
Sánchez

Dear President Costa,
Dear President von der Leyen,
Dear Taoiseach,

I am writing to express my serious concern regarding the recent reaction that some European governments have shown following the incident that took place at the external border of the European Union in Ceuta.

As you know, around 50,000 migrants entered this Spanish territory irregularly and unexpectedly earlier this week. In less than 48 hours, my Government has succeeded in fully restoring control over the border, in providing extensive humanitarian assistance, in returning virtually all of the migrants who crossed irregularly, and in preventing any unauthorized onward movement towards continental Europe.

This has been achieved in close coordination with the Moroccan authorities and with very little support from other European states, while pursuing the effective and solidarity-based migration policy that Spain has consistently implemented over recent years. A policy that has enabled us to reduce irregular arrivals through our territory dramatically, making Spain the second most secure external border in the EU, despite being the only Member State with a land border with Africa. This successful policy has also allowed us to assist other Member States when they faced similar crises, like when we hosted several of the migrants that arrived to Eastern Europe through Belarus in 2021 and to Lampedusa in 2023.

Despite these indisputable facts, the reaction of European governments over the past few hours has been rather asymmetric. Most have showed us their support and solidarity, and have offered their assistance. Others, however, have chosen to attack Spain and to call for its temporary exclusion from the Schengen Area.

Such an attitude –driven by prejudice, fake news, ignorance, or political interest– is not only contrary to European law, humanitarian law, and the principles of solidarity that bind us together. It is also contrary to Europe’s long-term interests and to the most basic common sense, because Ceuta is not part of the Schengen Area, because there are almost no irregular migrants left unreturned, and because Spain is, according to Frontex, one of the least porous external borders of the European Union, with a number of irregular entries that is half that recorded, for example, in Italy in recent years (2021–2026).

In the current international context, the European Union cannot afford this kind of selfish, polarising and unlawful reaction.

For this reason, in light of the seriousness of the situation, we would ask the Irish Presidency of the Council of the European Union to convene, as a matter of urgency, an extraordinary videoconference of the Ministers of the Interior. This meeting should enable us to establish a common response to situations of this kind and reaffirm that the security of our external borders is a shared responsibility of all Member States, and not only of those on the Union’s front line.

We count on your leadership to ensure that the European Union responds swiftly, effectively and in a coordinated manner.

Yours sincerely,

Pedro Sánchez

text:
A multi-year study from the Nasdaq Entrepreneurial Center, supported by JPMorganChase, set out to answer a question every founder eventually faces: what city should I start my company in?

The top five metro areas for entrepreneurship: Albany-Schenectady-Troy NY, Austin-Round Rock TX, San Diego-Carlsbad CA, San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward CA and Pittsburgh PA.

Shaolee Sen, who runs small-business philanthropy at JPMorganChase and grew up watching her mother build a small business in New York City, helped shape the research. Her breakdown of what actually separates the top markets is worth paying attention to.

The best cities make it easy to access real estate, talent, capital and customers — and they do it through strong public-private partnerships rather than fragmented, redundant programming. Columbus stands out in the report specifically because Ohio State's research ecosystem, a diversified industry base and capital partners who specialize in "hot handoffs" all point in the same direction at once.

A few of her most actionable insights for founders regardless of location:

Get feedback early and build relationships before you need them. Reach out to local networks, find a mentor and connect with potential customers and capital providers now. The founders who build those relationships in advance move faster when they need to.

Expand your definition of funding. Capital isn't just new dollars. Technical assistance, shared back-office services and advice on capital structure all strengthen a balance sheet. The best ecosystems offer a holistic approach, not just a check.

Build talent pipelines through local institutions. Research universities, community colleges and workforce development programs are underused recruiting channels. The regions pulling ahead invest in both traditional and nontraditional pathways — apprenticeships included.

And her personal focus practice: a card someone gave her years ago that read "Do What Matters Most." She repeats it several times a day when the volume of competing demands gets loud. Any repeatable phrase or ritual that restores focus is worth finding.

The city matters. So does what you do once you're in it.

Read more: https://t.co/8QAUGPZZsc

text:
He was 6 foot 6 with a silk touch. Won a bizarre set of trophies across club and country. Underwent heart surgery at the peak of his career. And scored a Premier League hat-trick in fifteen minutes off the bench.

Happy 50th birthday, Nwankwo Kanu.

He grew up in Owerri, Nigeria, his name meaning "child born on Nkwo market day" in Igbo tradition. He broke through domestically with Iwuanyanwu Nationale and moved to Ajax in 1993 as a teenager.

He won three successive Eredivisie titles there and in 1995 he lifted every club trophy in the world, the Champions League, the UEFA Super Cup and the Intercontinental Cup in Tokyo. An unpredictable and intelligent player, known for using feints, scoop finishes, backheels and the outside of his boot.

In the summer of 1996 Kanu captained Nigeria's Olympic squad in Atlanta. In the semi-final against Brazil, with Nigeria down 2-3, he scored twice late to make it 4-3 and send Nigeria to the final. They won the final 3-2 against Argentina and took Olympic gold.

Weeks later, Inter Milan's medical staff, examining him ahead of a $4.7 million transfer from Ajax, discovered a serious defect in his aortic valve. Doctors believed his career was over. He had open heart surgery at the Cleveland Clinic in Ohio that November and missed most of the following season. He returned to professional football in 1997, won the UEFA Cup, and went on to play another fifteen seasons.

Arsenal signed him in February 1999, and his debut in the FA Cup lasted just ten minutes before he became the centre of controversy. A a 1-1 score, a Sheffield United player had gone down injured, the ball was kicked out so he could get treatment, and when play resumed with a throw-in meant to go straight back to the opposition goalkeeper. Kanu, new to the country and unaware of the unwritten convention, intercepted it and set up the winning goal.

Sheffield United were furious. Arsène Wenger offered to replay the match. Arsenal won the replay too, 2-1 again, and the original result was wiped from the books.

His career quickly revived at Arsenal and later that year Kanu went on to score one of the most famous hat-tricks in Premier League history, coming off the bench against Chelsea and scoring three goals in fifteen minutes.

He won two Premier League titles at Arsenal, including the unbeaten Invincibles season in 2004, and two FA Cups. He moved to West Brom, then Portsmouth, where in 2008 he scored the only goal in the FA Cup final against Cardiff City, a third FA Cup winner's medal.

He retired in 2012. Between club and country, he ended up with a bizarre set of honours: a Champions League, a UEFA Cup, two Premier League titles, three FA Cups, an AFCON win, an Olympic gold medal, and two African Footballer of the Year awards.

In 2000, he founded the Kanu Heart Foundation, funding paediatric heart surgery for children across Africa who would never have had access to the kind of care that had saved his career.

He also went on to found his own club in Nigeria, Papilo FC, aimed at giving young Nigerian players a structured pathway into the game.

The streets remember Nwankwo Kanu.  🇳🇬

text:
Happy birthday to former Jenks, University of Oklahoma and NFL linebacker Rocky Calmus, born on this day in 1979 in Tulsa.

Calmus was a two-time state champion during his time at Jenks, including as a senior when he was a consensus All-State selection  after making 128 total tackles, 15 for losses, five sacks, forcing two fumbles, recovering two fumbles and breaking up three passes.

He also played running back on offense, rushing for 1,268 yards and 24 touchdowns and catching three passes for 74 yards and a touchdown as a senior while playing in only eight games.

He chose OU over several other Division I offers and earned Second-Team All-Big 12 as a sophomore. He was then the Big 12 Defensive Player of the Year in 2000 as the Sooners won the national championship.

He was a two-time First-Team All-Big 12 selection and two-time consensus All-American while also winning the Jack Lambert and Butkus awards as a senior in 2001.

The Tennessee Titans selected Calmus in the 2002 NFL Draft and he played for the Titans for three seasons, starting 12 games. His best season came in 2003, when he made 47 tackles, five for losses, one sack, and intercepted two passes.

He appeared in 27 NFL games, but injuries plagued his professional career and he retired following the 2005 season.

In 2026, Calmus was named one of the members of the first Hall of Fame class at Jenks Public Schools, which will be inducted during halftime of the Trojans' October 15th game against Edmond Santa Fe.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Thursday, July 31, 1975, Braniff International moved its Hostess College from 2801 Wycliff Avenue, in the Oaklawn Neighborhood of Dallas, Texas, to the Royal Coach Inn located at 3800 Northwest Highway at Lemmon Avenue, north of Love Field. Braniff had occupied the Wycliff location since January 5, 1968, when the unique facility was dedicated and opened for Hostess training.

For the past seven years, Hostesses from the domestic and Latin America Division were trained at the Wycliff facility and beginning in 1973, male Hosts were introduced and their training was conducted at the facility officially making it a coed training center. Between 1968 and 1975, Braniff had grown considerably and nearly doubled its size with revenues increasing from $301 million USD to an impressive near 100-percent increase to $598.8 million USD.

When it opened, the Wycliff College was touted as a facility that would take Braniff into the future, but with such precipitous growth during the time it was occupied, the demand for flight attendants became far greater than the small college could possibly handle. The decision was made to move the college to the massive Royal Coach Inn, which featured an abundance of rooms that were converted to dorms along with dining and office space that could accommodate the school for many years.

Braniff introduced its first Hostesses in 1937, when it purchased 14-passenger Douglas DC-2 twin-engine aircraft from Trans World Airlines. These new cabin-class airliners required a Hostess for each flight to ensure passenger safety and comfort.

Braniff opened its first Hostess College in Oklahoma City during that year at the company's 324 North Robinson Avenue Headquarters Building. Known as Braniff Tower, the facility opened in 1923, to house cofounder Thomas Elmer Braniff's burgeoning insurance company. The multi-story building boasted that it was the first skyscraper in Oklahoma City and today it has been fully restored and became the first Braniff structure to be listed in the National Register of Historic Places. In April 2017, a Braniff Trail Historical Plaque was placed and dedicated to mark the significance this historic building to Braniff's history.

The Hostess College remained in this building until the company's administration was moved to Dallas Love Field beginning in November 1941. The Hostess College was then housed at the 3309 Roanoke Drive Base, which was located where the current Love Field terminal building is today. Beginning in 1953, hostess training was also conducted at the historic Melrose Hotel, in the Oaklawn neighborhood of Dallas, Texas, not far from where the 1968 Hostess College was built. The college remained at the Melrose and Roanoke Headquarters until February 1958, when the plush new Braniff Tower Headquarters was opened at 6303 Forest Park Drive at Exchange Park in Dallas, located to the southeast of Love Field. However, some training continued to occur at the Melrose, which was also where the group hostess class photos were taken.

The college remained at the Melrose location until 1962 when all training was transferred to the Exchange Park location. Training was also conducted the Braniff Operations and Maintenance Base located at 7701 Lemmon Avenue and the adjacent Braniff International Airline Career Academy at 8001 Lemmon Avenue. Prior to the opening of the Airline Career Academy on June 15, 1971, in-water training was conducted in the swimming pool at the Holiday Inn directly across from the Operations and Maintenance Base at 7808 Lemmon Avenue in Dallas.

Training remained at the various locations until the new Blanton Tower was constructed to the east of the Cedar Springs entrance to Love Field on May 3, 1965. However, the Hostess Dormitory was moved earlier from Braniff Tower to Blanton Tower in July 1964. The impressive modern multi-story tower featured luxury amenities on the sixth floor for hostess training and was conveniently located within minutes of the Love Field terminal. The school remained at this location until the Wycliff Hostess College opened in January 1968.

Between 1968 and 1975, Braniff trained 2,336 hopeful Flight Attendant trainees at the facility that was owned by Wycliff Associates, Inc., and leased to Braniff for 20 years. However, Dresser Industries, purchased the five-story ultra-modern facility, decorated with Alexander Girard fabrics and artifacts, for use as a training facility. Local Dallas architects Pierce, Lacey and Associates designed the small footprint college while the interior was decorated by noted Florida, interior designer Chuck Ax. John Allen Pierce, lead architect, and Mr. Ax joined together again a couple of years later to design the Braniff Jetrail Carpark System Terminal Lounge and Outer Terminal buildings. Mr. Ax chose the bright colors for the unique monorail Air Coaches and their track and stanchions while Mr. Pierce designed the Jetrail terminal structures.

Braniff Vice President of Administrative Services Horace Bolding and Dresser Industries Senior Vice President Duane D. Rost jointly announced the agreement of sale of the 63,000-square foot building at the corner of Wycliff Avenue and the Dallas North Tollway. Dresser Industries was a leading supplier of high-technology products, service, and expertise to the natural resources industry. Mr. Bolding noted that a spectacular new Flight Attendant Training Academy was in the planning stages and would be announced soon. He further stated that training is, "A continuing process with initial, transitional, and recurrent training in many categories including flight and cabin crews, maintenance, operations, and management.

Bolding noted that Braniff's growth had also caused training to spread out over several facilities in the Dallas area and that in the interim Flight Attendant training would be conducted at the Royal Coach Inn until the new facility was completed. The current Hostess College Director Bill Smith noted that, "This building (Wycliff) is a great, unique facility, but it's to small for all of the outside training we do. The Royal Coach will give us space for more people and the new facility being planned shows even more progress.”

Dresser Industries occupied the Wycliff College until 1998, when it was purchased by a private individual who reopened it as a luxury retirement complex. The Park Gates Retirement Center left the college as it was during the time that Dresser owned the building. Dresser had removed the cabin mock-up and classrooms from the second floor and installed large executive apartments and on the dormitory floors, 3, 4, and 5, the rooms were enlarged to either one or two bedroom units. However, the basic layout of the dormitory rooms were retained including the unique locking wood closet drawers.

On June 1, 2014, Park Gates sold the college to Greenway Investment Group of Dallas, which planned to tear the building down. However, after considerable complaint from Preservation Dallas and Braniff Airways Foundation, the decision was made to offer the building for lease. As of July 2017, floors 3, 4 and 5 have been gutted and the building was still available for leasing. The remarkable lobby and Dream Parlor have been retained as they were when Braniff occupied the building.
However, in December 2019, the Wycliff building was sold to a local Dallas developer. The building has been saved and will undergo Dallas Landmark process, which will protect the building infinitely. Plans for the building will be revealed by Braniff Airways, Incorporated during 2020.

Braniff's cabin crew training remained at Royal Coach Inn until December 1, 1978, when it was moved to the spectacular new Braniff Place World Headquarters located on the West Side of Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional. All training, including pilot training, was housed at the new 445,000-square foot modern Mediterranean Villa-style compound, which featured a full gamut of recreational facilities including Olympic size swimming pool, tennis courts, football field, 9-hole professional golf course and a large lake. For the first time in its history, Braniff had combined all of its major functions under one roof, which saved the company considerably in facilities costs.

Photo: In July 1965, Braniff International moved its Hostess College to the massive Royal Coach Inn located on the south side of Northwest Highway at Lemmon Avenue/Marsh Avenue (the street changes from Lemmon to Marsh on the overpass over NW Hwy) at the north corner of Dallas Love Field. This luxurious hall leads to the training classrooms and dorm rooms that students enjoyed while learning to Fly Braniff Style. Two unique Retablos or dioramas are placed in the hall that is lined with Panamanian Molas and other South American artifacts. The Hostess College remained at this location until December 1978, when it was moved to the spectacular new Braniff Place World Headquarters Complex on the west side of Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional Airport.

text:
People know Robert E. Lee as the Confederate general. Almost nobody knows the 30 years that came before, and it's a wild resume.

He shows up at West Point in 1825 and graduates 2nd in his class of 46 with zero demerits in four years. Not one. That basically never happens.

Then the Army makes him an engineer. In the late 1830s the Mississippi River was shifting course and threatening to strand the St. Louis harbor on dry land. They send a young Lee. He builds a system of dikes to force the river to scour its own channel, and he saves the port. The city that would later sit in a war he fought against owed its harbor to him.

The Mexican War is where he becomes a legend. He isn't leading charges, he's the guy crawling on his stomach through lava fields and enemy lines to find the paths nobody else can find. At Cerro Gordo he scouts a route around the Mexican flank that wins the battle. Winfield Scott, the top general in the country, flat out called him "the very best soldier I ever saw in the field."

He runs West Point as superintendent. He chases Comanches in Texas with the cavalry. And in 1859 when John Brown seizes the arsenal at Harpers Ferry, the officer the government sends to end it is Lee. He takes it back in under three minutes.

Then in 1861 Lincoln's people offer him command of the entire Union army. He turns it down and goes home to Virginia. History remembers the choice. It forgets the man they were fighting so hard to keep.

text:
9,094 stores at the peak. Bankrupt 6 years later.

David Cook opened the first Blockbuster in Dallas in 1985.

Most video stores at the time carried a few hundred titles in a dim room.

He stocked 8,000 tapes, lit the place properly, and ran computerized inventory.

Wayne Huizenga took over in 1987 with 19 locations and turned expansion into a machine.

400 stores by the end of 1988.

By 1990 a new Blockbuster was opening every 24 hours.

Viacom bought the company for $8.4 billion in 1994.

2004 was the top. 9,094 stores, 84,300 employees, roughly $6 billion in revenue.

Late fees alone brought in about $800 million a year.

Here is the crack.

In 2000 Reed Hastings and Marc Randolph offered to sell Netflix to Blockbuster for $50 million.

Netflix had around 300,000 subscribers and was losing money.

CEO John Antioco passed. By Netflix's account he was trying not to laugh.

Blockbuster launched its own online service in 2004, 6 years behind.

It killed late fees in 2005, removing $800 million in revenue with nothing built to replace it.

Antioco fought the board over strategy and left in 2007. His successor pushed back toward stores.

Then the 2008 credit markets closed.

Blockbuster filed for bankruptcy in 2010 and the last company-owned stores closed in 2014.

One franchise survives in Bend, Oregon as a tourist stop.

The $50 million decision gets all the attention.

The debt gets almost none. Viacom spun the company off in 2004 and loaded it with roughly $1 billion to fund a special dividend on the way out.

Blockbuster spent its final years fighting Netflix with a balance sheet built for a monopoly.

Harvesting Grace, A Forty-Day Devotional by C.S. McDonald is a warm, reflective Christian devotional that invites readers to slow down and reconnect with God’s grace, especially during the beauty of autumn.

Inspired by the author’s love of the fall season—with its vibrant colors, crisp air, and sense of harvest and gratitude—the book offers forty days of gentle spiritual nourishment. Each entry includes a daily Bible verse, a peaceful and thought-provoking observation, and soft reflections designed to refresh faith and cultivate joy. McDonald encourages readers to pause amid life’s busyness, sit quietly or take a walk, and intentionally harvest God’s steadfast love and boundless grace. It serves as a humble, encouraging guide that can be used in autumn or anytime throughout the year. Readers looking for a calming, faith-centered companion will find it uplifting and accessible.

text:
Thinking about trekking but wondering if you're ready? Chiang Mai is one of the best places to begin, with scenic trails that range from easy boardwalks to gentle hikes that offer just a little more of a challenge.

🌿 Ang Ka Nature Trail
✨ Highlight: Cloud forest and high-altitude ecosystem
🥾 Approx. 320 meters | ⏳ Around 30 minutes
Take an easy boardwalk through the cloud forest of Doi Inthanon, where moss-covered trees, lush ferns, and cool mountain air create one of Thailand's richest high-altitude ecosystems. Open year-round and suitable for all experience levels.

🌿 Wat Pha Lat Nature Trail (Monk's Trail)
✨ Highlight: Forest hike, historic temple, and beautiful architecture in one trip
🥾 Approx. 2 km | ⏳ Around 2 hours
Walk beneath a leafy canopy alongside a gentle stream before reaching Wat Pha Lat, a temple with more than 650 years of history. Visit during the rainy season to see the famous Green Chedi, one of Chiang Mai's Unseen highlights, where the ancient stupa is blanketed in vibrant moss and ferns.

🌿 Doi Pui Summit Nature Trail
✨ Highlight: Hike to the highest peak in Doi Suthep–Pui National Park
🥾 Approx. 2.3 km | ⏳ Around 2 hours
A rewarding route for beginners, leading through lush montane forest to the highest point in Doi Suthep–Pui National Park. The cool mountain air and scenic views make every step worthwhile.

🌿 Pha Dok Siew Nature Trail (Rak Jung Waterfall)
✨ Highlight: Waterfalls, streams, and terraced rice fields—all on one trail
🥾 Approx. 2.6 km | ⏳ Around 2–3 hours
One of Chiang Mai's best-loved trails, with changing scenery from start to finish. Wander through the forest, cross streams, pass cascading waterfalls, and end among beautiful terraced rice fields. A great next step if you're ready to go beyond shorter walking trails.

Lace up your hiking shoes, take it at your own pace, and discover a greener side of Chiang Mai—or simply fall in love with it all over again. Save this post for your next outdoor adventure. 💚

text:
Not just the names.
They copied entire tales from Vedic era and embellished them.

I had previously posted only part of the section regarding Vaka Dālbhi from the Kāṭhaka-Saṃhitā for the sake of brevity.

Here is the complete narrative concerning Vaka Dālbhi in KS 10.6:

Naimiṣyā vai sattram āsata
ta utthāya saptaviṃśatiṃ Kuru-Pañcāleṣu vatsatarān avanvata
tān Vako Dālbhir abravīt:
"yūyam evaitān vibhajadhvam
imam ahaṃ Dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ Vaicitravīryaṃ gamiṣyāmi
sa mahyaṃ gṛhān kariṣyatīti."
tam āgacchat tan nāsūrkṣat
taṃ prākālayataitā gāḥ
"brahmabandha" ity abravīt
"Paśupatir gā hanti, tāḥ paraḥ pacamānaś care"ti
"tāsāṃ devasūr me rājānnaṃ prāsuṣod" iti
sakthāny utkartam apacat
tasmin pacamāne vyadasyat
so 'gnaye Rudravate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapat kṛṣṇānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ
tasya yatkiñca Dhṛtarāṣṭrasyāsīt tat sarvam avakarṇaṃ (= avakīrṇaṃ) vidrāṇaṃ abhivyaucchat
tā vipraśnikā avindan:
"brāhmaṇo vai tvāyam abhicarati tasmin nāthasve"ti
tam upāśikṣat, tasmai bahv adadāt
so 'gnaye Surabhimate 'ṣṭākapālaṃ niravapac chuklānāṃ vrīhīṇāṃ
tato vai tad vyadasyat

The Naimiṣyas were seated at the sacrifice.
Upon rising, they attained twenty-seven bullocks (as dakṣiṇā) from among the Kuru-Pañcālas.
Vaka Dālbhi said to them:
"You divide these amongst yourselves. I shall go to this Dhṛtarāṣṭra, son of Vicitravīrya. He will make a house for me."
He went to him, [yet] the king did not show pay him any heed.
He made Baka drive the cows forth, and said:
"O Brahmabandhu (i.e. Brāhmaṇa merely by birth)! Paśupati kills cows; go away and cook with them.
Their divine impeller (viz. Rudra) has delivered them up to me as royal food."
After cutting [the meat], Vaka cooked the thighs.
While it was cooking, it disappeared.
Vaka then offered a sacrificial cake (puroḍāśa) made out of black rice disributed in eight cups as an oblation to Agni Rudravat.
It then dawned on them (i.e. the people in the kingdom) that whatever wealth belonged to that [king] Dhṛtarāṣṭra had been scattered and dispersed.
The female fortune-tellers discovered [the cause]:
"This brahmin [i.e. Vaka] is performing abhicāra (black magic) against you; seek assistance from him."
He (Dhṛtarāṣṭra) then entered into Vaka's service and gave much to him.
He (Vaka Dālbhi) then offered an oblation of eight potsherds of white rice to Agni Surabhimat.
Then, that [abhicāra] disappered.

text:
THE PRICE OF TOMORROW

Chapter 1: A Promise in the Dark

The village was quiet before sunrise, but Adam was already awake.

Every morning began the same way. He fetched water from the stream, gathered firewood, and hurried to the local market to earn a few coins before school. At just seventeen years old, life had already taught him lessons that many adults never understood.

His father had passed away years earlier, leaving Adam and his widowed mother to struggle alone. Their small mud house barely protected them from the rain, and some nights they went to bed hungry.

Yet, his mother never allowed hardship to steal her faith.

"Allah never abandons those who refuse to give up," she would often remind him.

Adam believed her, but believing became harder each day.

At school, poverty followed him like a shadow.

His uniform was faded.

His shoes were worn out.

Some classmates ignored him, while others openly laughed.

One afternoon, as the students walked out of class, a wealthy boy pointed at Adam's torn shoes.

"Look at him," he laughed. "He dreams of success, yet he can't even afford a new pair of shoes."

The laughter echoed through the schoolyard.

Adam forced a smile and kept walking, but inside, every word felt like a stone placed upon his heart.

That evening, he returned home unusually quiet.

His mother noticed immediately.

"What happened today?" she asked gently.

Adam hesitated before answering.

"Do you think poor people are born to remain poor?"

His mother looked at him for a moment before taking his hands.

"My son," she said softly, "poverty is a condition, not a destiny. Never allow today's struggle to decide tomorrow's story."

Those words stayed with Adam long after she fell asleep.

Unable to rest, he stepped outside and sat beneath the old tree beside their house. The sky was filled with stars.

For the first time in months, he allowed himself to dream.

He imagined a future where his mother no longer worried about food.

A future where children would admire his story instead of mocking his appearance.

A future built not by luck, but by determination.

The next morning, while helping an elderly trader unload bags of rice at the market, Adam accidentally dropped one of the sacks.

The trader became angry.

"You careless boy!" he shouted.

Adam immediately apologized and offered to work the entire day without payment.

The old man stared at him in silence.

Most young people would have argued or walked away.

But Adam accepted responsibility.

Watching from a nearby shop was an elderly man named Mr. Ibrahim.

He had been observing Adam for weeks.

As the market became quiet later that afternoon, he called Adam over.

"My son," he said, "I have seen many young men with strength, but very few with character."

Adam lowered his head respectfully.

Mr. Ibrahim reached into his bag and handed him a small notebook.

"This is not a gift," he said with a smile. "It is an investment. Write one lesson every day. A person who learns daily is already richer than someone who only counts money."

That night, Adam opened the notebook.

On the first page, he wrote:

"People may laugh at where I am today, but they will never decide where I will be tomorrow."

He closed the notebook and smiled.

It was the first genuine smile he had worn in a long time.

He did not know how his life would change.

He did not know how many challenges still lay ahead.

But one thing had changed forever.

For the first time, Adam stopped seeing himself as a victim of poverty.

He started seeing himself as the author of his own future.

To be continued...

..spirit cannot be defeated.

Unfortunately, I also see enormous talent trapped by poor leadership.

I see graduates searching endlessly for jobs that do not exist.

I see entrepreneurs spending more money on diesel than on expanding their businesses.

I see brilliant young people leaving Nigeria, not because they have stopped loving their country, but because they no longer believe their country loves them back.

That must change.

And it is precisely why this election is about much more than politics.

It is about whether your generation will finally inherit a country that rewards merit instead of connections, innovation instead of patronage, productivity instead of propaganda, and competence instead of mediocrity.

My challenge to you today is simple:

What good is the strength of a giant if the giant refuses to rise?

Young Nigerians constitute the largest voting population in our country.

Yet, too often, you have allowed yourselves to be divided by tribe, religion and political manipulation while a much smaller political class decides your future.

That must end.

Your vote is far more valuable than any amount of money a politician can offer.

Do not exchange four years of your future for one afternoon of inducement.

A bag of rice will disappear.

A few thousand naira will be spent.

A campaign T-shirt will eventually fade.

But the consequences of electing incompetent leadership will remain with you long after the campaign has ended.

When you sell your vote, you are not merely exchanging a ballot paper.

You are surrendering opportunities that belong to your generation.

You are surrendering better schools.

Better hospitals.

Safer communities.

Reliable electricity.

More jobs.

A stronger economy.

And a government that truly works for everyone.

Never underestimate the value of your vote.

It remains the most powerful instrument any citizen possesses in a democracy.

My dear young Nigerians,

Please do not allow yourselves to become instruments of political violence.

Every election season, some politicians suddenly discover that you are "leaders."

They give you caps.

They give you T-shirts.

They give you a little money.

They ask you to insult opponents, disrupt campaigns or intimidate voters.

But immediately after the election, they disappear.

Your phone stops ringing.

The promises vanish.

And you are left exactly where they found you.

Do not mortgage your future to people who remember your name only during campaigns.

The greatest service you can render any politician is not fighting for him.

It is insisting that he earns your vote through ideas, character, competence and integrity.

That is the foundation of every successful democracy.

And that is the kind of political culture we must build together.

So, the question before us is simple:

How do we convert frustration into national renewal?

How do we transform the largest youth population in Africa into the greatest democratic movement our continent has ever witnessed?

I propose three strategic mandates.

 Mandate Number One: Move From Social Media Outrage to Democratic Participation. 

Young Nigerians have demonstrated extraordinary creativity in the digital space.

You influence conversations.

You shape opinions.

You hold governments accountable.

You have shown the world that Nigerian youths can organise, innovate and inspire.

But while social media can awaken a nation, it cannot by itself elect a government.

Hashtags do not count votes.

Livestreams do not secure polling units.

Tweets do not defend democracy.

Only citizens do.

Our challenge in 2027 is therefore clear.

We must transform online influence into offline participation.

Register to vote.

Verify your registration.

Understand the Electoral Act.

Volunteer.

Serve as polling agents.

Observe the process.

Protect the people's mandate peacefully and lawfully.

Remember this:

The old political establishment may have enormous financial resources, but you possess something far..
