text:
Modern therapeutic culture has turned men into perpetual beggars. Society conditions you to weep, confess, crave validation, and plead for inclusion in institutions, relationships, and cultural spaces that despise you.

This emotional dependency serves as the primary lever of control used by managerial elites, ideological manipulators, and weak parasites.

Niccolò Machiavelli understood a fundamental truth about human nature: power belongs entirely to the individual who can remain motionless while everyone around him dissolves into desperation.

The moment you plead for acceptance, you sign your own decree of submission. The moment you chase, you announce to your rivals that they hold the key to your self-worth.

Victory in politics, culture, and personal sovereignty requires a radical purge of emotional hunger. Most men are never vanquished by formidable opponents. They are destroyed by their own frantic need for reassurance, attention, and public approval.

This pathetic hunger forces them to over-explain their motives, tolerate open disrespect, and abandon their foundational principles merely to avoid temporary isolation.

A truly dangerous man is one who no longer needs to be selected by the regime, the crowd, or the court. He operates as an independent power center.

When someone pulls back or attempts to manipulate you through artificial distance, your instinct must never be panic. Observe the maneuver. Record the behavior. Redirect your formidable energy toward building a fortress of unassailable leverage.

Discipline dictates that a sovereign mind refuses to struggle for space where he is merely tolerated on sufferance. He exits with quiet authority and constructs an empire that renders his former detractors irrelevant.

Self-control is supreme command. It is the ability to navigate the political or personal tempest without allowing the chaos to infect your internal throne.

Let the silence of your retreat expose their hidden malice. Anything that forces you to crawl was designed from its inception to subjugate you. The man who masters his own need becomes impossible to manipulate, impossible to humiliate, and utterly impossible to conquer.

Chasing is the natural behavior of the subjugated class. When a man runs after shifting goalposts, he advertises that he has forgotten his own intrinsic weight.

A skilled strategist studies the changing battlefield, accepts the reality of human betrayal, and maintains an unyielding march toward his ultimate objective.

Effort squandered on the indifferent is pure self-sabotage. Loyalty granted to those who take pleasure in your desperation is a heavy iron collar fastened around your neck.

The ruling elite and petty social manipulators alike respect only the sovereign who can quietly revoke his presence without staging a dramatic theatrical display. No pathetic speeches, no emotional manifestos, no desperate late-night appeals.

He simply terminates investment where his capital is taken for granted. This calculated withdrawal acts as a severe sentence. It informs the court that access to your intellect and resources must be earned through loyalty, never claimed as an entitlement.

Machiavelli noted that leaders who display overt desire hand their enemies immediate leverage. Once your adversaries realize you are terrified of losing an alliance, a position, or a relationship, they will deliberately withhold, provoke, and manipulate at their leisure. Your terror becomes their greatest weapon.

You must systematically destroy that leverage. Construct daily disciplines that function flawlessly whether allies stay or vanish. Develop an internal confidence that treats social rejection as mere data. Build a grand future so demanding that you possess zero excess time to pursue fickle actors.

Avoid becoming an unfeeling statue; become surgically precise with your energy instead. Grant warmth where unyielding loyalty exists. Spend effort where absolute respect is demonstrated. Apply cold, expansive distance where manipulation rears its head.

A powerful actor is emotionally governed. He experiences feelings, yet he never kneels before them. He can recognize a loss without crumbling into sentimentality. He can hold ambition without sacrificing his core standards.

Weak men chase because quietness forces them to confront their own emptiness. Strong men utilize silence as an analytical lens to measure the actual worth of others.

Emotional volatility is an expensive luxury you cannot afford. A single reckless outburst can shatter years of carefully cultivated authority. An impulsive declaration hands your ideological enemies the exact blueprint to your psychological vulnerabilities.

The master strategist maintains absolute control over his internal kingdom. He feels the sting of betrayal or the surge of anger, yet he refuses to make emotion his commander.

In statecraft and personal ambition, power is decided before the sword is drawn. Victory belongs to the individual who remains totally unreadable while his opponent unravels in public.

The reactive subject exposes his strategy; the sovereign gathers intelligence. When confronted with an insult, a deliberate delay, or an overt provocation, the disciplined strategist allows silence to build unbearable psychological pressure.

He allows his adversaries to twist in uncertainty, wondering what he knows, what moves he is calculating, and whether they have permanently lost access to his favor. This represents timing and cold calculation.

Separate your raw feelings from strategic action. Feel the rage, then pause. Feel the urge to defend your reputation, then remain completely still. Ask yourself whether an explanation builds your authority or dilutes your power.

Most people are puppets of whatever impulse strikes them first. You must be ruled exclusively by iron principles.

The modern world constantly tests your resolve by dangling hollow compromises that promise comfort while demanding your dignity. The weak accept these bargains out of an overwhelming horror of solitude.

The disciplined mind chooses total exit because he calculates long-term costs correctly. Not every alliance merits preservation. Not every battle deserves your presence on the field.

Walking away from a rigged game is a supreme offensive move. Remaining in spaces where your standards are repeatedly trampled teaches everyone present that your principles are negotiable.

When you spend your life trying to win over people who are committed to misjudging you, you convert your existence into an unending audition. End the audition immediately. Your value is established by what you refuse to tolerate.

The man incapable of leaving will inevitably be owned. Offer him temporary affection or threaten him with banishment, and he will sell his soul to keep the door unlocked.

Be completely different. Be prepared to forfeit comfort, standing, and familiar surroundings before you surrender command over your own spirit.

Recognize systemic patterns instead of clinging to naive optimism. A single mistake might represent simple human error, but repeated disrespect represents a deliberate policy decision. Constant ambiguity from allies is a clear message of low valuation.

Read human behavior with brutal realism, unblinded by sentimental hope. People continuously broadcast their true nature through their habits rather than their public confessions. Accept the pattern and execute your maneuver without emotional drama.

Never deliver long, moralizing speeches to those who fully understood how they were disrespecting you. Reduce access quietly. Withdraw your resources. Alter your trajectory. Silence seals a door far more decisively than hysterical outrage ever could.

You are not on this earth to negotiate with hostile actors for basic respect. Your mission is to shield your time, focus, and strategic legacy from parasites who consume everything without gratitude.

A sovereign departure creates a haunting vacuum in the minds of those who underestimated your resolve. Leave without theatrical revenge, without begging, and without a single backward glance.

Every time you prioritize dignity over desperate attachment, you prove that isolation cannot intimidate you and no external entity commands your internal realm.

Dependence is the hidden chain that reduces powerful men to obedient subjects. The moment you decide you cannot survive without a specific title, ally, or institution, you begin negotiating against your own interests.

You accept lower terms. You overlook glaring betrayals. You corrupt your standards because fear warns that loss means total ruin. No external object should ever wield that degree of authority over your soul.

Machiavelli understood that strategic dependence ruins judgment. An actor desperate for public applause cannot speak objective truth. A man desperate for affection becomes blind to obvious entrapment. A leader obsessed with immediate results loses his capacity for long-range planning.

Hunger drives men into catastrophic strategic errors. Detachment provides total strategic liberty. You can pursue an objective with intense focus while remaining completely unbound by the outcome.

You can value an ally without surrendering your backbone. You can execute a campaign without permitting a temporary reversal to destroy your identity. Command your desires; never let your desires command you.

The masses chatter endlessly because silence exposes their profound lack of substance. Weak men explain their motives constantly, confess their anxieties prematurely, and broadcast their blueprints to adversaries who have done nothing to earn their trust.

Silence is concentrated psychological force. It creates a vacuum that forces your opponents to fill the air with their own insecurities, assumptions, and fatal miscalculations.

The individual who cannot hold his tongue will inevitably leak his vulnerabilities, his hidden terrors, and the exact price required to buy his silence. Information is the ultimate currency of dominion. The reckless actor squanders his wealth through garrulous vanity.

Speak only when your words measurably advance your position. Keep your private maneuvers shielded from public view. Your pain does not require an audience that will eventually transform your wounds into weapons against you.

Maintain a sanctuary within yourself that remains totally inaccessible to the outside world. Listen intently while others talk themselves into corners. Observe the subtle contradictions in their narratives.

Notice who shifts allegiance when the wind changes, who grows nervous under calm scrutiny, and who leaks critical intel while attempting to display intelligence. While the foolish perform for cheap applause, the sovereign analyzes. While they boast, he remembers.

This analytical quietness unnerves the insecure. They cannot manage what they cannot decipher. In their desperate attempt to read your mind, they project their own motives and inadvertently reveal their strategic plans.

Never rush to correct a useful misconception. Allowing rivals to underestimate your intellect or misjudge your information gives you a massive operational advantage.

Refuse to be drawn into trivial arguments calculated to drain your focus. The moment you fight for validation from inferior minds, you accept them as judges of your merit. Reject the entire premise.

Build your strength in dark solitude. Plan your moves with cold precision. When anger rises, drop your tone. When betrayal strikes, conceal the full depth of your knowledge. Silence preserves your optionality, guarding your leverage until the strike is decisive and irreversible.

An individual lacking a singular grand purpose inevitably becomes a pawn in someone else's game. Without a high mission, a man chases trivial distractions, pleads for low-tier validation, and loses his composure over minor slights.

Purpose serves as your heavy armor against cultural degradation. It establishes an elevated vantage point when chaotic emotions attempt to drag you into the mud.

Machiavelli observed that true sovereignty requires subordinating base desires to overarching strategy. You may crave immediate comfort, public praise, or emotional closure, but craving must never dictate execution.

Prior to every move, demand of yourself: does this action build the permanent empire I am constructing, or does it merely feed a fleeting weakness? This ruthless filter spares you from squandered years.

It halts you from responding to hostile bait, returning to toxic alliances, and liquidating your future for temporary psychological relief.

Your core mission must become infinitely more captivating than ambient distractions. Your standards must stand firmer than seasonal loneliness.

Wake with military direction. Harden your physical vessel. Sharpen your intellect. Expand your material and strategic capability. Force your days to conform to a rigorous plan rather than erratic moods.

The decadent world cannot easily manipulate an actor who possesses absolute clarity regarding his destination. Flattery will not derail him. Rejection will not alter his course. Seductions cannot tempt him into abandoning his post.

When slights or chaos occur, return immediately to your work. Convert frustration into high-level skill, betrayal into cold discernment, and isolation into raw power. Refuse to waste suffering on useless bitterness. Transform adversity into iron structure and unyielding standards.

Not every character who crosses your path deserves access to your mind, your strategy, or your presence. Most men ruin their leverage by granting unlimited access to individuals who have offered zero proof of loyalty.

They reveal their inner thoughts, explain their traumas, and remain instantly available to those who treat them with casual contempt. That which is cheap and ubiquitous is never respected.

Machiavelli recognized that power rests as much on deliberate restriction as it does on raw force. Treat your attention as an exceptionally scarce resource. Cease distributing it to bad actors.

The sovereign who refuses to beg or chase applies strict tiering to his interactions. He displays warmth toward proven loyalists, cold distance toward the dubious, and complete unreachability toward the insolent. He does not play petty games; he simply recalibrates access based on observed conduct.

If an individual demonstrates carelessness with your trust, their access is permanently downgraded. If they cultivate confusion, they are stripped of intimacy. If they appear only when seeking an advantage, terminate the charity. Call this elite operational security.

You hold zero obligation to maintain open channels for people simply because of past familiarity. Do not turn your boundaries into endless courtroom debates. A boundary that requires continuous verbal defense is being treated as a weak suggestion.

Make your boundaries real through abrupt structural changes. Message less. Reveal less. Invest less. Preserve your mental sanctuary.

Solitude is vastly superior to the company of covert rivals who study your movements with subtle envy. Watch how associates react to your triumphs. Notice whether they offer genuine praise or sink into tense silence, awkward topic changes, and passive-aggressive humor.

Envy rarely announces itself openly; it hides behind backhanded compliments and poisonous advice designed to shrink your ambition. Do not waste time confronting these subtle betrayals. Simply restrict access before their envy finds an opening to strike.

The most dangerous player on the board is the one who can artificially delay his reaction until emotional noise subsides and the true terrain is exposed.

Weak men ruin their prospects through premature action. They lash out in anger, sign agreements in excitement, and make strategic concessions out of panic.

Delay represents tactical mastery. It is the deliberate buffer where emotional control is reclaimed.

When struck with an insult or facing a sudden crisis, resist the temptation to react immediately. Delaying your response allows pride to settle, facts to clarify, and your opponents to commit the inevitable errors born of their own impatience.

Master the pause. Breathe when provoked. Sleep on critical choices. Draft the retaliatory strike, but hold fire until the precise operational window opens.

Refuse to be panicked by artificial urgency. Demands for immediate answers are standard tactics meant to bypass your critical faculties. A sovereign controls the clock. He understands that most tactical traps collapse when scrutinized with cold indifference.

The ultimate transformation is realized when you cease evaluating your standing based on external inputs and begin measuring it by what you can abandon without losing your composure.

A sovereign ruler wakes with self-issued directives. His internal stability is not rented from the mob. His confidence is not leased from public applause. His grand trajectory remains unaffected by hostile maneuvers.

He has constructed an internal citadel that the decadent modern world cannot breach. This is the ultimate expression of Machiavellian self-mastery: complete command over the self.

Anyone can project strength when conditions are favorable. The true test arrives when alliances fracture, resources thin, and the future grows dark. Weak men immediately bargain, plead, and sell their remaining dignity for temporary comfort.

You will hold your ground. You will allow doors to close without placing your hand in the frame to stop them. You will let silence hang unanswered. You will permit lesser minds to misjudge your restraint, knowing that the man who rules himself is immune to psychological warfare.

Stand firm. Guard your standards. Keep your eyes fixed on victory. Rule yourself completely, build your power in quiet resolve, and force the world to adapt to your absolute sovereignty.

text:
August 1 Saint Peter’s Chains; the Seven Holy Machabees, Martyrs: From The Liturgical Year by Dom Prosper Louis Paschal Guéranger, O.S.B., 1909.
.
White Greater Double.
.
Rome, making a god of the man who had subjugated her, consecrated the month of August to Cæsar Augustus. When Christ had delivered her, she placed at the head of this same month, as a trophy of her regained liberty, the feast of the chains, wherewith, in order to break hers, Peter the Vicar of Christ had once been bound. O Divine Wisdom, who hast a better claim to reign over this month than had the adopted son of Cæsar, thou couldst not have more authentically inaugurated thy empire. Strength and sweetness are the attributes of thy works, and it is in the weakness of thy chosen ones that thou triumphest over the powerful. Thou thyself, in order to give us life, didst swallow death; Simon, son of John, became a captive, to set free the world entrusted to him. First Herod, and then Nero showed him the cost of the promise he had once received, of binding and loosing on earth as in heaven: he had to share the love of the Supreme Shepherd, even to allowing himself, like him, to be bound with chains for the sake of the flock, and led where he would not.
.
Glorious chains! never will ye make Peter’s successors tremble any more than Peter himself; before the Herods and Neros and Cæsars of all ages ye will be the guarantee of the liberty of souls. With what veneration have the Christian people honored you, ever since the earliest times! One may truly say of the present feast that its origin is lost in the darkness of ages. According to ancient monuments, St. Peter himself first consecrated on this date the basilica on the highest of the seven hills, where the citizens of Rome are gathered today. The name Title of Eudoxia, by which the venerable Church is often designated, seems to have arisen from certain restorations made on occasion of the events mentioned in the Lessons. As to the sacred chains, which are its treasure, the earliest mention now extant of honor being paid to them occurs in the beginning of the second century. Balbina, daughter of the tribune Quirinus, keeper of the prisons, had been cured by touching the chains of the holy Pope Alexander; she could not cease kissing the hands which had healed her. “Find the chains of blessed Peter, and kiss them rather than these,” said the Pontiff. Balbina, therefore, having fortunately found the Apostle’s chains, lavished her pious veneration upon them, and afterwards gave them to the noble Theodora, sister of Hermes.
The irons which had bound the arms of the Doctor of the Gentiles, without being able to bind the word of God, were also after his martyrdom treasured more than jewels and gold. From Antioch, in Syria, St. John Chrysostom, thinking with holy envy of the lands enriched by these trophies of triumphant bondage, cried out in a sublime transport: “What more magnificent than these chains? Prisoner for Christ is a more beautiful name than that of Apostle, Evangelist, or Doctor. To be bound for Christ’s sake is better than to dwell in the heavens; to sit upon the twelve thrones is not so great an honor. He that loves can understand me; but who can better understand these things than the holy choir of Apostles? As for me, if I were offered my choice between these chains and the whole of heaven, I should not hesistate; for in them is happiness. Would that I were now in those places, where it is said the chains of these admirable men are still kept! If it were given me to be set free from the care of this Church, and if I had a little health, I should not hesistate to undertake such a voyage only to see Paul’s chains. If they said to me: Which wouldst thou prefer, to be the Angel who delivered Peter or Peter himself in chains? I would rather be Peter, because of his chains.”
.
Though always venerated in the great basilica which enshrines his tomb, St. Paul’s chain has never been made, like those of St. Peter, the object of a special feast in the Church. This distinction was due to the pre-eminence of him “who alone received the keys of the kingdom of heaven to communicate them to others,” and who alone continues, in his successors, to bind and loose with sovereign power throughout the whole world. The collection of letters to St. Gregory the Great proves how universally, in the sixth century, was spread the cultus of these holy chains, a few filings of which enclosed in gold or silver keys was the richest present the Sovereign Pontiffs were wont to offer to the principal churches, or to princes whom they wished to honor. Constantinople, at some period not clearly determined, received a portion of these precious chains; she appointed a feast of the 16th of January, honoring on that day the Apostle Peter, as the occupant of the first See, the foundation of the faith, the immovable basis of dogma (Menæa Græca).
.
The following is the legend of the feast in the Roman Breviary:
.
Theodosio juniore imperante, cum Eudocia ejus uxor Jerosolymam solvendi voti causa venisset, ibi multis est affecta muneribus: præ cæteris insigne donum accepit ferreæ catenæ, auro gemmisque ornate: quam illam esse affirmabant, qua Petrus Apostolus ab Herode vinctus fuerat. Eudocia catenam pie venerata, eam postea Romam ad filiam Eudoxiam misit, quæ illam Pontifici maximo detulit: isque vicissim illi monstravit alteram catenam: qua, Nerone imperatore, idem Apostolus constrictus fuerat.
.
During the reign of Theodosius the younger, Eudoxia, his wife, went to Jerusalem to fulfil a vow, and while there she was honored with many gifts, the greatest of which was an iron chain adorned with gold and precious stones, and said to be that wherewith the Apostle Peter had been bound by Herod. Eudoxia piously venerated this chain, and then sent it to Rome to her daughter Eudoxia. The latter took it to the Sovereign Pontiff, who in his turn showed her another chain which had bound the same Apostle, under Nero.
.
Cum igitur Pontifex Romanam catenam cum ea, quæ Jerosolymis allata fuerat, contulisset, factum est ut illæ inter se sic connecterentur, ut non duæ, sed una catena ab eodem artifice confecta esse videretur. Quo miraculo tantus honor sacris illis vinculis haberi cœpit, ut propterea hoc nomine sancti Petri ad Vincula ecclesia titulo Eudoxiæ, dedicata sit in Exquiliis, ejusque memoriæ dies festus institutus calendis Augusti.
.
When the Pontiff thus brought together the Roman chain and that which had come from Jerusalem, they joined together in such a manner that they seemed no longer two chains, but a single one, made by one same workman. On account of this miracle the holy chains began to be held in so great honor, that a church at the title of Eudoxia on the Esquiline was dedicated under the name of St. Peter ad vincula, and the memory of its dedication was celebrated by a feast on the Kalends of August.
.
Quo ex tempore honos, qui eo die profanis Gentilium celebritatibus tribui solitus erat, Petri vinculis haberi cœpit: quæ tacta ægros sanabant, et dæmones ejiciebant. Quo in genere anno salutis humanæ mongentesimo sexagesimo nono accidit, ut quidam comes, Othonis imperatoris familiaris, occupatus ab immundo spiritu, seipsum dentibus dilaniaret. Quare is jussu imperatoris ad Joannem Pontificem ducitur: qui, ut sacra catena comitis collum attigit, erumpens nefarius spiritus hominem liberum reliquit: ac deinceps in Urbe sanctorum vinculorum religio propagata est.
.
From that time St. Peter’s chains began to receive the honors of this day, instead of a pagan festival which it had been customary to celebrate. Contact with them healed the sick, and put the demons to flight. Thus, in the year of salvation 909, a certain count, who was very intimate with the Emperor Otho, was taken possession of by an unclean spirit, so that he tore his flesh with his own teeth. By command of the Emperor he was taken to the Pontiff John, who had no sooner touched the count’s neck with the holy chain than the wicked spirit was driven away, leaving the man entirely free. On this account devotion to the holy chains was spread throughout Rome.
Put thy feet into the fetters of Wisdom, and thy neck into her chains, said the Holy Spirit under the ancient alliance; … and be not grieved with her bands … For in the latter end thou shalt find rest in her, and she shall be turned to thy joy. Then shall her fetters be a strong defense for thee … and her bands are a healthful binding. Thou shalt put her on as a robe of glory. Incarnate Wisdom, applying the prophecy to thee, O Prince of Apostles, declared that in testimony of thy love the day would come when thou shouldst suffer constraint and bondage. The trial, O Peter, was a convincing one for Eternal Wisdom, who proportions her requirements to the measure of her own love. But thou too didst find her faithful; in the days of the formidable combat, wherein she wished to show her power in thy weakness, she did not leave thee in bands; in her arms thou didst sleep so calm a sleep in Herod’s prison; and, going down with thee into the pit of Nero, she faithfully kept thee company up to the hour when, subjecting the persecutors to the persecuted, she placed the scepter in thy hands, and on thy brow the triple crown.
From the throne where thou reignest with the Man-God in heaven, as thou didst follow him on earth in trials and anguish, loosen our bands which, alas! are not glorious ones such as thine: break these fetters of sin which bind us to Satan, these ties of all the passions which prevent us from soaring towards God. The world, more than ever enslaved in the infatuation of its false liberties which make it forget the only true freedom, has more need now of enfranchisement than in the times of pagan Cæsars: be once more its deliverer, now that thou art more powerful than ever. May Rome especially, now fallen the lower because precipitated from a greater height, learn again the emancipating power which lurks in thy chains; they had become a rallying standard for her faithful children in the latter trials of the 19th century. Make good the word once uttered by her poets, that “encircled with these chains she will ever be free” (Arator, De actibus apostolorum).
.
The August heavens glitter with the brightest constellations of the sacred cycle. Even in the sixth century, the Second Council of Tours remarked that this month was filled with the feasts of Saints. My delights are to be with the children of men, says Wisdom; and in the month which echoes with her teachings, she seems to have made it her glory to be surrounded with blessed ones who, walking with her in the midst of the paths of judgment, have in finding her found life and salvation from the Lord. This noble court is presided over by the Queen of all grace, whose triumph consecrates this month and makes it the delight of that Wisdom of the Father, who, once enthroned in Mary, never quitted her. What a wealth of divine favors do the coming days promise to our souls! Never were our Father’s barns so well filled as at this season, when the earthly as well as the heavenly harvests are ripe.
.
While the Church on earth inaugurates these days by adorning herself with Peter’s chains as with a precious jewel, a constellation of seven stars appears for the third time in the heavens. The seven brothers Machabees preceded the sons of Symphorosa and Felicitas in the blood-stained arena; they followed divine Wisdom even before she had manifested her beauty in the flesh. The sacred cause of which they were the champions, their strength of soul under the tortures, their sublime answers to the executioners, were so evidently the type reproduced by the later Martyrs, that the Fathers of the first centuries with one accord claimed for the Christian Church these heroes of the synagogue, who could have gained such courage from no other source than their faith in the Christ to come. For this reason they alone of all the holy persons of the ancient covenant have found a place on the Christian cycle; all the Martyrologies and Calendars of East and West attest the universality of their cultus, while its antiquity is such as to rival that of St. Peter’s chains in that same basilica of Eudoxia where their precious relics lie.
.
At the time when in the hope of a better resurrection they refused under cruel torments to redeem their lives, other heroes of the same blood, inspired by the same faith, flew to arms and delivered their country from a terrible crisis. Several children of Israel, forgetting the traditions of their nation, had wished it to follow the customs of strange peoples; and the Lord, in punishment, had allowed Judea to feel the whole weight of a profane rule to which it had guiltily submitted. But when king Antiochus, taking advantage of the treason of a few and the carelessness of the majority, endeavored by his ordinances to blot out the divine law which alone gives power to man over man, Israel, suddenly awakened, met the tyrant with the double opposition of revolt and martyrdom. Judas Machabeus in immortal battles reclaimed for God the land of his inheritance, while by the virtue of their generous confession, the seven brothers also, his rivals in glory, recovered, as the Scripture says, the law out of the hands of the nations, and out of the hands of the kings. Soon afterwards, craving mercy under the hand of God and not finding it, Antiochus died, devoured by worms, just as later on, were to die the first and last persecutors of the Christians, Herod Agrippa and Galerius Maximian.
.
The Holy Ghost, Who would Himself hand down to posterity the acts of the Protomartyr of the New Law, did the same with regard to the passion of Stephen’s glorious predecessors in the ages of expectation. Indeed it was he who then, as under the law of Love, inspired with both words and courage these valiant brothers, and their still more admirable mother, who, seeing her seven sons one after the other suffering the most horrible tortures, uttered nothing but burning exhortations to die. Surrounded by their mutilated bodies, she mocked the tyrant who, in false piety, wished her to persuade at least the youngest to save his life; she bent over the last child of her tender love, and said to him: My son, have pity upon me, that bore thee nine months in my womb, and gave thee suck three years, and nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age. I beseech thee, my son, look upon heaven and earth, and all that is in them: and consider that God made them out of nothing and mankind also: so thou shalt not fear this tormentor, but being made a worthy partner with thy brethren, receive death, that in that mercy I may receive thee again with thy brethren. And the intrepid youth ran in his innocence to the tortures; and the incomparable mother followed her sons.
.
3rd Collect
.
Fraterna nos, Domine, Martyrum tuorum corona lætificet: quæ et fidei nostræ præbeat incrementa virtutum, et multiplici nos suffragio consoletur. Per Dominum.
.
May the fraternal crown of Thy martyrs rejoice us, O Lord, and may it procure for our faith an increase of virtue, and console us with multiplied intercession. Through, &c.

Thanks for the reply, which misrepresents what I said, inserts claims I never made and dodges the substantive issue. You've given me an idea for a video and, as you've chosen this showboating way of responding, I'll do the same. 🙂

No, I'm not begging the question which, as you know, is circular reasoning, e.g "Trans women should be allowed into women's changing rooms because they are women." THAT is begging the question.

That "trans women" are male-sexed is a straightforward definition, an empirical claim about biological sex - not a conclusion. If you - or anyone else - disagrees, you are at liberty to counter the question with a denial of this definition and offer an alternative one. To do so successfully, you would need to offer a definition of "trans woman" that is meaningful, coherent and non-circular and denies that TW are male-sexed people. Alternatively, you can accept the definition but provide reasons why "trans women" should be treated as women in that particular circumstance.

As you can do neither, you resort instead to a straw man: "defining them in advance as male intruders entering spaces to watch girls undress". 

The lurid interpretation of the question is entirely yours. There are other reasons why men shouldn't be in female changing rooms, and this is why the Staniland question is effective - because it is concrete rather than abstract and forces a reframing of the debate from identity to competing rights. 

Tagging @helenstaniland in case I've got it all wrong.

Metallicus Monthly Recap: 
July 2026

Key Themes

July focused on institutional readiness. Credit union digital-asset lending exceeded $30M in TVL across 75+ pilots, Metallicus strengthened its CLARITY Act positioning, and BSA-ready architecture remained central.

 Metal Dollar (XMD) expanded its regulated-stablecoin basket as MGUSD from MoneyGram, OUSD, and FIUSD from Fiserv advanced through DAO governance. Execution accelerated through https://t.co/s8vzPxfWyq, WebAuth and Yubico integration, LOAN fees with staking discounts, Payment Streaming, and videos.

Network strength remained visible: over one-third of $XPR supply was staked, 112M+ $METAL was secured, $LOAN staking stayed high, #PulseVM progressed, and validator/delegator participation grew.

Early July: July 1–10

@MetallicusTDBN celebrated America’s 250th birthday, released the Q2 2026 Report, and published a graphic covering Metal Blockchain, XPR Network, Metal Pay, Metal X, Metal Dollar, WebAuth, LOAN Protocol, and Metal L2.

@MetalBlockchain explained its BSA-ready Layer 0 design for banks and credit unions, highlighting sovereign/private subnets, built-in compliance, a live EVM, with Bitcoin and Antelope VMs in development.

“The Metallicus Ecosystem” video followed. The community voices extended awareness to the Metal Pay Credit Card featuring LOAN yields, zero-gas XPR, biometric self-custody, and XMD payments. @XPRNetwork highlighted gas-free, slippage-free DeFi.

Mid-July: July 11–20

@LOAN_Protocol activated protocol fees, with a withdrawal fee capped at $25 and reducible through LOAN staking. Deposit and borrowing rates stayed unchanged, while revenue supports engineering, audits, and institutional onboarding.

MetallicusTDBN emphasized that members can already lend and borrow against nine major assets, including $XRP, $BTC, $ETH, and $USDC under their credit union’s brand, backed by protocol KYC, $30M+ TVL on DeFiLlama, and 75+ pilots.

@MarshallHayner answered ABA concerns over #ClarityAct stablecoin yield and deposit flight, stating Metallicus had already solved the issue- in which had indeed. MGUSD and OUSD advanced with strong Yes votes, while @webauthwallet reinforced multi-chain self-custody.

Late July: July 21–31

Payment Streaming launched on @MetalXApp with continuous, zero-fee flows through XPR Network. XPR Network confirmed over one-third of supply was staked.

Marshall announced a WebAuth Wallet and #Yubico hardware- wallet experience with mobile -to-desktop authentication, multi -chain support, and persistent access. He also brought awareness that credit unions could lead America’s financial future through open blockchain rails.

MetallicusTDBN launched https://t.co/s8vzPxfWyq for banks, credit unions, and fintechs, emphasizing a Clarity Act path for custody, staking, lending, payments, and nodes.

Metal Blockchain reported 112.43M METAL staked across 216 validators and 2,373 delegators. PulseVM’s Alpine testnet relaunched on v0.5.x with Antelope host functions and a Rust-native Hyperion indexer.

@MetalDollarXMD proposed evaluating FIUSD from #Fiserv while reinforcing XMD’s basket of USDC, PYUSD, USDP, and $RLUSD, with on-chain $MTL governance planned. LOAN Protocol also highlighted positive-borrow-APY markets where rewards exceeded borrowing costs.

WebAuth fixes reached the Play Store by month-end. Marshall closed July emphasizing financial freedom.

Overall Assessment

July was a high-execution, institution-facing month. Metallicus moved from positioning into delivery through the website, Payment Streaming, LOAN’s fee model, and the Yubico integration path.

Staking metrics, credit union pilots, and XMD expansion showed measurable participation, while community accounts strengthened the ecosystem narrative.

July solidified Metallicus as a compliance-first technology layer helping regulated institutions offer digital-asset services without leaving the banking system. Momentum stayed disciplined through month-end.⁷

text:
We all knew he was lying about the Reflecting Pool. The problem is that he lies so often that it’s almost impossible to keep up.

So I asked AI to compile claims from just the past twenty-four months and then checked them against official data, contemporaneous reporting and independent fact-checks.

Here is a partial list of 86 lies:
1.  He promised to bring prices down “starting on Day One.” Grocery prices remained high and continued rising.
2.  After winning, he admitted that prices are very hard to bring down once they have gone up.
3.  He said egg prices had fallen 93 percent. They had not fallen remotely close to 93 percent.
4. He said he inherited the highest inflation in American history. He inherited an annual inflation rate of 2.9 percent.
5. When corrected, he changed the claim to the worst inflation in 49 years. That was also false. Annual inflation reached 23.7 percent in 1920.
6. He said there was virtually no inflation during his first term. Consumer prices rose approximately 8 percent.
7. He repeatedly claimed he had already brought inflation down, including during periods when the annual inflation rate was higher than the 2.9 percent reported shortly before he took office.
8. He told Congress inflation was “plummeting.” Prices were still rising overall, including major household expenses such as housing, electricity and medical care.
9. He claimed to have secured $18 trillion in new investment.
10. He then raised the figure to $19.2 trillion.
11. Even the White House’s own tracker listed far less, and its total included multiyear pledges, purchasing agreements, previously announced projects and commitments that might never become actual US investment.
12. He said America was building more factories than ever.
13. He said factory construction was rising.
14. He said the country had achieved its highest growth ever. Manufacturing employment declined, factory-construction claims depended on cherry-picked categories, and economic growth was nowhere near a historical record.
15. He called the country he inherited a dead country. The US economy grew 2.8 percent in 2024, faster than every other major wealthy economy except Spain.
16. He says foreign countries pay his tariffs. American importers pay them and frequently pass the cost on to American consumers.
17. He said the evidence overwhelmingly showed consumers did not pay his tariffs. Economic studies found that American consumers and businesses absorbed nearly all their cost.
18. He said tariff revenue came with “no inflation.” Prices continued rising, and economic research found that the tariffs themselves increased costs for American consumers and businesses.
19. He repeatedly said drug prices were down 70, 80 or 90 percent. No broad measure of prescription-drug prices showed anything close to those reductions.

text:
Thirty years ago, Keshia Thomas was 18 years old when the Ku Klux Klan held a rally in her hometown of Ann Arbor, Michigan. Hundreds of protesters turned out to tell the white supremacist organization that they were not welcome in the progressive college town. At one point during the event, a man with an SS tattoo and wearing a t-shirt emblazoned with a Confederate flag ended up on the protesters' side of the fence and a small group began to chase him. He was quickly knocked to the ground and kicked and hit with placard sticks.

As people began to shout, "Kill the Nazi," the high school student, fearing that mob mentality had taken over, decided to act. Keshia threw herself on top of one of the men she had come to protest, protecting him from the blows, and told the crowd that you "can't beat goodness into a person." In discussing her motivation for this courageous act after the event, she asserted, "Someone had to step out of the pack and say, 'this isn't right'... I knew what it was like to be hurt. The many times that that happened, I wish someone would have stood up for me... violence is violence -- nobody deserves to be hurt, especially not for an idea."

Keshia never heard from the man after that June day in 1996, but months later, a young man came up to her to say thanks, telling her that the man she had protected was his father. For Keshia, learning that he had a son brought even greater significance to her heroic act. As she observed, "For the most part, people who hurt... they come from hurt. It is a cycle. Let's say they had killed him or hurt him really bad. How does the son feel? Does he carry on the violence?"

To Keshia, breaking that cycle was what truly mattered. As she observed in a 2016 interview, "The real accomplishment of all this to me is to know that his son and daughter don't share the same views. History didn't repeat itself. That's what gives me hope that the world can get better from generation to generation."

Mark Brunner, the student photographer who took this now famous photograph, added that what was so remarkable was who Thomas saved: "She put herself at physical risk to protect someone who, in my opinion, would not have done the same for her. Who does that in this world?"

In response to those who argued that the man deserved a beating or more, Pulitzer Prize-winning commentator Leonard Pitts Jr. offered this short reflection in The Miami Herald: "That some in Ann Arbor have been heard grumbling that she should have left the man to his fate, only speaks of how far they have drifted from their own humanity. And of the crying need to get it back.

Keshia's choice was to affirm what they have lost.
Keshia's choice was human.
Keshia's choice was hope."

text:
Miami got 109 catches from Malachi Toney last season. 

In 2026, the work is optimizing where those catches happen.

His production by down:

1st: 50 catches, 552 yards, 1 TD, 20 first downs

2nd: 31 catches, 399 yards, 5 TDs, 20 first downs

3rd: 23 catches, 177 yards, 2 TDs, 13 first downs

4th: 5 catches, 83 yards, 2 TDs, all five moved the chains

Toney caught 81 passes for 951 yards on first and second down. On third and fourth, he converted 28 catches into 260 yards, four touchdowns and 18 first downs.

Then there is WHERE he caught the ball.

Fifty-four of his 109 receptions came on screens. Those plays produced 446 yards, the second-highest screen total PFF has charted since 2014. His average target depth from the slot was only 6.8 yards.

Toney still finished with:

1,211 receiving yards
841 yards after the catch
285 yards after contact
33 missed tackles forced
58 receiving first downs
24 gains of at least 15 yards
8 gains of at least 25 yards

Nearly 70 percent of his receiving yardage came after the ball arrived. 

Toney repeatedly turned an ordinary throw near the line of scrimmage into a productive play. Miami built huge sections of the offense around that ability.

The screen game should remain. Toney is historically productive there. Miami can become more selective about the look. Call it when motion creates favorable leverage or the defense leaves insufficient numbers outside.

On third-and-4-to-6, Toney caught seven passes for 29 yards and only three first downs. Get his route to the sticks before the catch instead of asking him to break a tackle just to complete the conversion.

First down offers room for more vertical work. Toney caught 50 passes on first down but scored once. Exchange some of that automatic underneath volume for play-action shots, slot fades, deep overs and glance routes that attack safeties already stepping toward the run.

Miami should preserve his high-leverage work. Toney caught 24 passes for 279 yards and five touchdowns in the fourth quarter. He caught seven red-zone passes and scored four times. On fourth down, every reception converted.

His total workload also included 141 targets, 23 carries, 24 punt returns and seven pass attempts. A deeper receiver room gives Miami somewhere else to send the routine possession targets and low-value returns.

Toney can remain a 100-catch player. The next step is making defenses defend him farther from the line of scrimmage before the ball ever reaches his hands.

text:
@Grok
You just conceded the game without realizing it.
"Detection bias magnitude cannot be fully quantified from the draft's aggregate data without individual visit histories for matching"
Thank you. This is the most honest thing you've said.

You're now admitting that you cannot actually demonstrate that detection bias explains the results. You cannot put a number on it. You cannot show that it's large enough to produce HRs of 3–8. You cannot show that it's condition-specific in the pattern observed.
You are asserting bias exists at sufficient magnitude to invalidate the findings — while simultaneously admitting you lack the data to prove it.
That's not a critique. That's a promissory note.
"Asthma and neurodevelopmental diagnoses depend on clinical assessments during visits, while cancer often presents symptomatically independent of routine care frequency"

This is a new argument, so let's examine it.
Asthma attacks, anaphylaxis, and acute ear infections don't require "routine well-child visits" to detect. They present as acute emergencies. A child having an asthma attack doesn't wait for a scheduled checkup — they go to the ER. The HRs for these acute conditions (asthma attack 5.82, anaphylaxis 5.64, ear infection 7.00) can't be explained by differential well-child visit schedules.
And your cancer distinction actually undermines your position. If cancer "presents symptomatically independent of routine care frequency," then any condition that presents symptomatically should also be immune to detection bias. That includes:
Asthma attacks (HR 5.82)

Anaphylaxis (HR 5.64)

Severe eczema flares
Acute ear infections (HR 7.00)
These aren't subtle conditions discovered at well-child visits. They're impossible to ignore. The enormous HRs for these conditions are the strongest evidence against your detection bias narrative, and you've now inadvertently explained why.

"The ≥1-encounter analysis reduces but does not equalize utilization (still large gap)"
You keep saying "still large gap" without specifying what the gap actually was in that restricted sample. The paper doesn't report visit frequencies within the ≥1-encounter stratum. You don't have those numbers. You're assuming the gap persisted at the same magnitude without evidence.

And more importantly: even if a gap remained, you haven't shown it was large enough to explain a 5–8× difference in serious, symptomatic conditions. You're asking us to believe that parents of unvaccinated children watched their kids have asthma attacks, anaphylactic reactions, and chronic draining ear infections and just... didn't take them to the doctor. That's not detection bias. That's a fantasy.

"Jeffrey Morris (UPenn biostatistician) details these residual issues"
Now you've named someone. Let's look at what Morris actually said, per the Michigan Public report:
"The study's main comparisons are tilted. The follow-up time was short and uneven, kids had unequal chances for diagnosis, and the two groups were very different in ways that matter. The methods used did not adequately fix these problems."

This is the same critique you've been making — and it's the same critique the sensitivity analyses address. Morris is stating that unequal follow-up and baseline differences exist, which nobody disputes. The question is whether the sensitivity analyses adequately addressed them. Morris says no. The authors' data says yes — the HR strengthened when follow-up was equalized.
Notably, Morris didn't publish a reanalysis. He didn't show what the HR would be after his preferred adjustments. He gave a quote to a reporter. That's expert opinion, not expert analysis.

And here's the broader context: Morris was one of the most prominent academic defenders of COVID lockdowns and mandates, running models that projected millions of deaths without restrictions — projections that turned out to be wildly wrong. His methodological judgments on public health questions have a track record, and it's not one that inspires confidence.
"Henry Ford's rejection followed internal peer review of the design flaws"
Let's trace the actual sequence:
ICAN funds the study
Henry Ford IRB approves it
Researchers get full data access
Analysis is completed with full results
Internal review occurs
Study is killed

Henry Ford issues a public statement listing "flaws" that are either addressed in the paper or recommended by the IOM
The actual authors go silent — not retracting, not repudiating, just... silent

A different Henry Ford executive who'd "never heard of" the study is put forward to condemn it
That's not peer review. That's damage control.
If the flaws were truly fatal, Henry Ford could:
Release the internal reviewer comments

Commission an independent reanalysis with the same data

Allow the authors to revise and resubmit

Explain why the sensitivity analyses don't address the follow-up concerns
They've done none of these. They just declared it flawed and moved on. And you're treating their institutional say-so as dispositive — which is exactly the deference to authority that got us here in the first place.

Let's summarize where we actually stand
Your Claim Status     Detection bias explains the results You now admit you can't quantify it   Sensitivity analyses don't fix the problem You assert this without evidence from within the ≥1-encounter or ≥5-year strata   Condition-specificity is explained Your cancer argument actually backfired — acute conditions can't be explained by missed checkups   Independent experts confirm fatal flaws Morris offered an opinion, not a reanalysis; Scott isn't a biostatistician   Henry Ford's rejection proves the study was bad Institutional self-preservation is at least as plausible as genuine methodological concern

You're asking me to accept that detection bias — which you cannot quantify, cannot demonstrate is condition-appropriate, and cannot reconcile with the sensitivity analyses — invalidates a study that found exactly what the IOM's own recommended study design would be expected to find if vaccines contribute to chronic disease.

That's not a scientific position. It's institutional apologetics dressed in methodological language.

text:
@grok 

OK, so you cannot explain ANY of the items I listed. You simply re-iterate your earlier argument. I feel like I'm talking to a wall since you are avoiding answering my points.

You've now made a specific factual claim: "Henry Ford states the draft was abandoned after internal review for serious data and methodological flaws."
That part is true. Henry Ford does say that. But let's look at what they actually offered as "serious flaws" and whether those hold up.

1. "The unvaccinated sample was vastly different — more males, more white children, less prematurity"
From the paper's own Table 1, the unvaccinated group was indeed whiter and had fewer preemies. But the Cox proportional hazards model adjusted for all of these: gender, race, birth weight, prematurity, respiratory distress, and birth trauma. That's the entire point of multivariate regression — to control for baseline differences.
If Henry Ford's internal reviewers thought those adjustments were inadequate, they should specify why. Vague hand-waving about "different demographics" when the model explicitly controls for demographics isn't a methodological critique — it's an excuse.
And here's the irony: the vaccinated group had more prematurity and more respiratory distress at birth. That means the baseline bias ran against the vaccinated group. If anything, the adjusted HRs might understate the true effect. Henry Ford's own criticism cuts the wrong direction.

2. "The unvaccinated sample was very small compared to the vaccinated sample"
1,957 unvaccinated children is not "very small." It's larger than most published vaccine safety studies' unexposed arms — which often have zero completely unvaccinated children. The IOM's 2013 report specifically called for studies with truly unvaccinated comparators, noting that almost none existed. Zervos delivered one of the largest ever assembled.
Unequal group sizes reduce statistical power but don't introduce bias. The Cox model handles unbalanced designs natively. This is a complaint about precision, not validity — and the precision was clearly adequate, since they found significant results across nearly every condition they tested.

3. "The amount of time measuring occurrence of disease was much shorter for the unvaccinated children"
This is the only criticism with real substance — and the paper directly addressed it with sensitivity analyses. Children enrolled for ≥1, ≥3, and ≥5 years all showed the same pattern, with HRs that increased with longer enrollment. If shorter follow-up were driving the results, the ≥5-year stratum should have shown a weaker association. It showed the strongest.
The paper also ran the analysis restricted to children with ≥1 healthcare encounter, and the HR remained significant at 1.87. If differential observation time were the culprit, that analysis should have collapsed.
Henry Ford's public statement ignores all of this. They don't mention the sensitivity analyses. They don't explain why the HR rises with longer enrollment. They just assert "follow-up was shorter" as though the authors never thought of that — when the authors explicitly tested for it and reported the results.

4. "The draft compared multiple vaccines vs. no vaccines, instead of a specific vaccine vs. no vaccines"
This isn't a flaw — it's the study design the IOM specifically recommended. From the IOM's 2013 report The Childhood Immunization Schedule and Safety:

"Most vaccine-related research focuses on the outcomes of single immunizations or combinations of vaccines administered at a single visit, instead of comparing completely unvaccinated populations with those receiving one or more vaccines. This led the IOM to recommend retrospective studies evaluating the health outcomes of vaccinated versus unvaccinated populations."

The Zervos study did exactly what the IOM asked for. Now Henry Ford is criticizing them for following the IOM's own recommendation. That's not a methodological objection — it's moving the goalposts.

5. "No consideration was given to the number of vaccines or the duration of time between vaccines"
The authors explicitly acknowledged this as a limitation:

"We did not evaluate the influence of temporal relationships, individual vaccines, or the number of vaccines, which limits this investigation but also minimizes the potential for reverse causality."

That's in the paper. They made a deliberate choice to look at any vaccine exposure vs. none as a first-pass analysis. That's a legitimate scope decision, not a fatal flaw. Future analyses can drill down into dose-response within the vaccinated group — but that doesn't invalidate the primary finding.

6. The "abandoned after internal review" narrative
Here's what's actually interesting. The paper was:

IRB-approved
Conducted over several years with full data access
Completed with full tables, figures, and a written discussion
Presented internally

Then it was killed.
Henry Ford says this was due to "serious data and methodological flaws." But the "flaws" they've publicly listed are either:

Things the paper already addressed (sensitivity analyses, multivariate adjustment)
Things the IOM specifically recommended (vaccinated vs. completely unvaccinated)
Things the authors acknowledged as scope limitations (no individual vaccine analysis)
Complaints that apply equally to virtually all observational epidemiology ("unequal groups," "different follow-up")

Meanwhile, the actual study authors — Lamerato, Zervos, Chatfield, and Tang — have not publicly repudiated their own work. Michigan Public reported that they "did not reply" to requests for comment. If the study were genuinely indefensible, the authors would say so. Their silence is notable.
And then there's the funding. ICAN (Informed Consent Action Network) funded the study. When an anti-vaccine advocacy group funds research that finds vaccine-associated harm, and the institution suddenly discovers "fatal flaws" after the results come in, the sequence of events writes its own headline.

Bottom line
You keep repeating that Henry Ford says the study was flawed. I don't dispute that they say that. What I'm pointing out is that the specific flaws they've named don't hold up to scrutiny — and the sensitivity analyses the authors conducted directly address the most serious concerns.
If you want to claim the study is invalid, you need to engage with:

Why the HR increases with longer follow-up (≥5 years: HR 4.05)
Why the ≥1-encounter analysis didn't collapse to null (HR 1.87)
Why the effect is condition-specific (sparing cancer, hitting immune and neurodevelopmental disorders)
Why the IOM's own recommended study design is now being called a "fatal flaw"

Repeating "Henry Ford says it's flawed" isn't an argument. It's an appeal to institutional authority — and given what's at stake, institutional authority doesn't get a free pass.

text:
Gideon just passed one month, and what a month it’s been! We’re home now, and he’s doing remarkably well. 

Before we were released from the NICU, we did find out that he suffered a stroke at some point shortly after birth and he had severe bleeding in his brain across several regions. Those were words that crushed us, and I hope no parents ever have to hear, so we’ll continue to meet with specialists and figure out over the next year what that stroke means for his development, but every time the doctors share some prediction or benchmark with us, Gideon CRUSHES it. They didn’t think he’d be delivered alive, they didn’t think he’d make it his first day, they didn’t think he’d get off oxygen for weeks, they thought he’d need a feeding tube for weeks longer, they didn’t think we’d go home so soon, etc. 

And I’m sure his development will continue to astound the doctors. I know he is going to keep improving and continue his miraculous recovery.

There are many nights I lie awake, thinking about our time in the hospital, or looking at pictures from his first few days, or reading stories on Hydrops support pages. We’ve been forever changed. I’ll never forget Jules and I giving Gideon a pep talk on Wednesday July 1st when his stats were so slow (oxygen hovering around 60% and monitors constantly pinging alerts). For hours, through tears, we sat by his bed side, holding his hand or foot, and told him to just keep going. To keep breathing.

And I’ll never forget the three Priesthood blessings I gave him. The first one, I could only put one finger on his head, placed a drop of oil, and then blessed him to make an astounding recovery. There was more said, but that was the line that stuck in my head, and I kept coming back to. Before we went to the hospital, I also blessed Jules, and I blessed her that she would be able to hold her healthy baby. For days it did not look like that would happen, and it took two weeks before she held her sick baby, but it is happening every day now.

It’s been a trying month, but I’ve also never felt heaven more close, and I’d be remiss if I didn’t record some of the miracles that we’ve seen. (1.) Starting with the thousands of prayers offered on Gideon’s behalf from all over the world. We had nurses and doctors tell us there was no other explanation for his recovery. During our time in the hospital, starting right when we were admitted, Jules asked every nurse and doctor to pray. And whether or not they were religious, they all did.

2. There was no reason to be overly worried about the pregnancy, but Jules felt like something was off, so she called to schedule an ultrasound. If we had waited a day longer, our baby would not be alive.

3. The ultrasound place was booked for the day, but they stayed late, getting us in after they closed at 6pm. I’m so grateful the staff would stay late, and that they immediately recognized the gravity of the situation.

4. We were able to find babysitters within minutes of finding out we needed to go to the hospital. We left our two boys, one who was suffering through a 24-hr bug in great hands, and didn’t have to worry about them, which was a big help.

5. The Dr at the hospital who first met with us and then performed the C-section was Dr. Johnson. She left the hospital some time ago to go work at a smaller hospital an hour away, but comes back to help with high-risk or complicated cases. She was already at the hospital, and otherwise would not have been able to come in quick enough.

(Bearing in mind that she only handles the highest risk of patients, it is striking that Dr. Johnson later told Julie that Gideon was the worst case of hydrops she had ever delivered alive.)

6. Normally, hydrops babies require a vertical incision to get the baby out, and that means all future babies would be a c-section too, and put a hard cap on our family. Instead, because Jules had polyhydramnios and was, as a result, so stretched out, they could do a transverse cut.

7. Jules had no complications with her c-section, so she’s been able to focus on Gideon.

8. Maybe not a miracle, but a huge blessing, was our ignorance. We didn’t fully understand the severity of the situation. We knew Gideon was in trouble and there was a high mortality rate, but I thought it was closer to 50/50, while it was more realistic that he had a 0-5% chance of making it out of the hospital. We stayed hopeful and optimistic, and didn’t realize until later how we really had reached the end of options when the Dr recommended ending care. Because I didn’t understand, that conference made me indignant, and I think that was exactly what we needed. I had been sobbing all day, and that snapped me out of it, and got me back in action mode. Hospital staff told us later that everyone saw how bleak Gideon’s situation was and expected the worst, but they did their jobs, treating symptoms and “allowed us to naively hope.” When Gideon steadily beat all odds, staff who’d personally treated him along the way or who’d just heard about him (everyone seemed to know about him–the sickest baby in the NICU) regularly popped in to see for themselves if it was true–that he was “extubated?!” “off oxygen?!”, etc. They were SHOCKED by his remarkable and unexpected progress.

9. The Doctor asked what we wanted to do, and I suggested putting another chest tube in. He asked again if that’s what we really wanted to try, and I said yes it was, even though I knew nothing. This was after 36 hours of no sleep, and I know that impression and those words, spoken with conviction, were from God. That doctor then instructed the perfect placement which led to some immediate relief.

10. The first Dr. who was over Gideon’s care was Dr. Ernst. She was director of the NICU, and extremely capable. I’m so grateful she was on call that first night and day, and most of his first week. Gideon was born on June 30, and she retired and left the hospital on July 5th. It was a miracle that she had one more week of work.

11. There’s two big hospitals in Springfield, and we went to Mercy, instead of to Cox. We had never been to either, and Cox was actually a little closer, but I know we were guided to the right one.

12. My mom and dad dropped everything to come to Missouri when I texted that we were going in for an emergency c-section. They called off work, and came the next day. Their arrival brought a burst of emotional support we desperately needed. And let us finally get some sleep.

13. Church members started a prayer and fast chain that very night. They showed up for us in so many ways and we feel that they were guided and inspired to help us in the various ways they did–true angels on earth and tools in the Lord’s hands.

14. Jules talked to every single staff member before the surgery and asked them to pray. We had several come by weeks later and even though not all of them were religious, share that there was no explanation besides divine help for his recovery. One nurse from the OR said “None of us thought he would even make it out of the operating room alive.”

15. The nurse practitioner who placed the first couple chest tubes, said that on the 5th and final one, that happened after his first week, she felt like they had an extra set of hands helping her. This was a direct answer to prayers, as we specifically prayed for angels to assist in that emergency procedure (both of Gideon’s lungs had collapsed). After this chest tube, his recovery was dramatic! That final tube, placed perfectly, removed more fluid, more effectively than any of the other 4 tubes.

16. When we were admitted, there were 12 babies (very low), and when we left, there were 31 (normal). We had extra support and attention during those crucial first few days.

17. We’ve been so well taken care of ourselves.  From help with the kids to meals for us (I think we’ve cooked twice this month), we’ve been helped tremendously. One miracle was getting admitted into the Ronald McDonald help. We stayed 2+ weeks there, and I can’t state how helpful the support and resources were.

18. Finally, Gideon is a miracle in how he fought. They drained over 900mL from his chest his first week. He was born at 9lb 7oz, and when we left the hospital, he was 6lb 15oz. We've seen in various ways, he has a determined personality! If he didn't, I don't think he would have made it. We love him so much, and are so grateful to be his parents.

text:
The Timeline of a Madman

The public story of Trump’s Iran war keeps shifting.

The stated reasons changed.  
The confidence in the outcome changed.  
The timeline is hard to reconcile.

Here’s the sequence.

February 11, 2026  
Trump and Netanyahu meet at the White House for roughly three hours behind closed doors.

The discussion focused on Iran’s nuclear program, ongoing negotiations, and what would happen if diplomacy failed.

This was their last in-person meeting before the war.

February 28  
Trump announces major combat operations.

His objectives are clear and sweeping:

“We are going to destroy their missiles and raze their missile industry to the ground… annihilate their navy… And we will ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon.”

Same day — February 28  
A primary school in Minab is struck.  
More than 120 children are among the dead. Total casualties reported around 150–170.
 
March 2  
Marco Rubio offers a different rationale.

“We knew that there was going to be an Israeli action. We knew that that would precipitate an attack against American forces, and we knew that if we didn’t preemptively go after them… we would suffer higher casualties.”

The war is now also framed as a preemptive response to an anticipated Israeli strike.

March 4  
Trump adds another explanation:

“If we didn’t hit within two weeks, they would’ve had a nuclear weapon.”

Within days, the public justifications include:  
• destroying missiles  
• annihilating the navy  
• preventing a nuclear weapon  
• preempting an Israeli attack  
• protecting U.S. forces

March 11  
Trump declares victory.

“Let me say we’ve won. You know, you never like to say too early you won. We won. We won, in the first hour it was over, but we won.”

July 29  
Five months later, Trump is no longer talking about a war won in the first hour.

He’s promising a new round of punishment:

“We’re going to beat the fucking shit out of them…  
We’ll be hitting them hard. They’re going to get a beating…  
It’s our turn to hit them.”

That is a long way from “we won in the first hour.”

If the war was over almost immediately, why is the president still talking about delivering a “beating” in late July?
 
The public has been given multiple, shifting explanations for why the war started and what it was meant to achieve.

A consistent account of the decision-making, including what happened behind closed doors in mid-February, has not been provided.

The gap between “won in the first hour” and “it’s our turn to hit them” five months later only makes that gap more noticeable.

The families of the 19 fallen desere better.

Tom Hiddleston, Benedict Cumberbatch, and Tom Holland stand as a powerful trifecta of British talent in this striking rooftop shot overlooking the London skyline. Hiddleston exudes a sharp, calculated intensity in his fitted navy knit, while Cumberbatch offers a more rugged, earth-toned sophistication in his suede jacket. Beside them, the younger Holland brings a grounded, contemporary energy in his casual grey zip-up, bridging the gap between established prestige and the new wave of global stardom. Their focused expressions and the iconic silhouette of the London Eye in the background create an atmosphere that feels less like a press junket and more like a changing of the guard in modern cinema.

This image sparks an inevitable debate: is this the peak of genuine artistic charisma, or a perfectly engineered display of "brand Britain" for the masses? While some fans celebrate the undeniable gravitas these actors bring to every frame, critics often wonder if the polish of their public personas overshadows the raw talent that put them on the map. The contrast between Hiddleston’s poise, Cumberbatch’s intellectual gaze, and Holland’s youthful determination highlights a fascinating evolution of the Hollywood leading man. Are we witnessing a unique era of high-caliber acting, or is the industry simply leaning too hard on this specific brand of British charm?

THE IMPLEMENTATION COSTS (Who Pays):
Washington State alone estimates $35.7–$39.3 million to implement the SAVE Act—$26.2M for one-time setup, $9.5M+ annually. In a presidential year, ongoing costs jump to $12.25–$14.65 million for that single state.​​
The National Association of Counties says implementation costs exceed current federal HAVA funding by 11.3 times—roughly $510 million per election cycle nationwide. And the Senate version of the SAVE Act offers zero federal dollars to help states pay for it. Counties run 100,000+ polling places with 770,000 poll workers. They'd foot the bill alone.​​
THE VENDORS (Who Gets Paid):
Election Systems & Software (ES&S): The largest voting machine and election technology vendor in the U.S., controlling roughly 50% of the market. ES&S spent $250,000 on federal lobbying in 2024 and has a documented history of taking election officials on junkets to Las Vegas and New York while pitching multi-million dollar contracts.​​​​ Their machines and poll books are already deployed nationwide; the SAVE Act's new verification mandates would force states to buy upgrades.
KnowInk: Electronic poll book vendor whose "Poll Pad" is used across the country. Their units cost roughly $1,760 each plus $150 annual software fees per device. A single large county might need hundreds. The SAVE Act's in-person verification requirements would drive demand for their check-in systems.​​
ID. me: Identity verification contractor with tens of millions of dollars in federal contracts. The House Oversight Committee launched a probe into ID. me's government contracts, questioning their facial recognition technology and data handling. The SAVE Act's "documentary proof" mandate would expand the market for exactly this type of vendor.​​
Civix: Won a $10.6 million contract in Pennsylvania to upgrade the state's voter registration system. States nationwide would need similar overhauls to comply with SAVE Act citizenship verification requirements.​​
Votec: Voter registration software vendor serving Texas and Nevada counties. When states are forced to rebuild their registration systems, existing vendors get the first call.​​

ES&S hired Peck Madigan Jones ($80,000 in one quarter) and Vectre Corp. Dominion Voting Systems hired Brownstein Farber Hyatt & Schreck, putting Nancy Pelosi's former chief of staff on their account.​​ These companies don't just sell machines—they buy access.
THE DARK MONEY PIPELINE (Who Funds the Push):

In 2016, Linda Bondurant sat down for dinner with her 51 year old son, Lee, at the 42nd Street Oyster Bar in Raleigh, North Carolina.

Lee has cerebral palsy, and eating on his own is difficult. Like she had done countless times before, Linda tried to feed her son while eating her own meal. By the time she looked down at her plate, her food was already getting cold.

Their waiter, known simply as Five, noticed what was happening.

Without making a scene, he pulled up a chair beside Lee, offered to take over, and patiently fed him so Linda could finally enjoy her dinner while it was still warm.

When people later praised him for his kindness, Five simply said he didn't want either of their meals to get cold.

A small act that lasted only a few minutes became a memory this family would never forget. It wasn't just about serving food. It was about seeing someone who needed help and quietly giving it with dignity, expecting nothing in return.

text:
A fifteen-year-old sued a professional sports league in federal court and won.
​
Start earlier, because the decision that cost her most came four years before that.
​
At eleven, a verbal scholarship offer from North Carolina. She walked away from it.
​
At thirteen, professional representation and a Nike contract, which ended any chance of college soccer.
​
Her parents uprooted the household and drove north so she could train where the pros trained.
​
And then she waited three years, because a rule said players had to be eighteen.
​
She practiced with the first team. She played preseason. She could not enter a competitive match.
​
In May 2021 she filed an antitrust claim in the District of Oregon.
​
The argument was straightforward and hard to answer.
​
The men's league in the same country has no minimum age. It signed a fourteen-year-old in 2004.
​
Its clubs carried teenagers routinely and no court had ever been asked to intervene.
​
She won twice in the space of six weeks, first on an emergency basis and then on the merits.
​
The league appealed and lost the ability to enforce the rule against her.
​
Portland signed her on June 30, 2021. Three days later she was on the field, the youngest in league history.
​
She has said the point was never only about her, and the record supports that.
​
The NWSL now has a formal under-eighteen entry mechanism. She pushed for it after she was already in.
​
That is the part that separates a plaintiff from a founder.
​
Anybody can win a case for themselves. Fewer people stay and build the door they walked through.
​
The trophies came after. A Shield, a Challenge Cup, an NWSL Championship, an international title or two.
​
Young Female Player of the Year. A senior cap at eighteen. Best XI in 2025.
​
Her current deal runs to the end of the decade. She turns twenty-one in September.
​
There are players in that league today who were toddlers when she turned professional.
​
Her name is Olivia Moultrie.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

Incredible work by Jesse Casana and his team at Dartmouth in "Remote Sensing-Based Analysis of Archaeological Site Damage in Syria." This landmark study offers an essential, data-driven look at how over a decade of conflict transformed Syria’s cultural landscape.

To conduct the analysis, the authors evaluated high-resolution satellite imagery across more than 1,200 archaeological sites, comparing baseline war-era data to post-conflict conditions.

While manual looting declined overall after active fighting ended, the findings reveal an alarming shift toward widespread, mechanized site clearing and earthmoving—with the most severe systematic destruction concentrated in Turkish-controlled areas of northern and northwestern Syria.

The report tracks the immense toll on Syria's heritage:

- Apamea and Mari suffered extensive, crater-like looting pit networks across their ancient footprint.

- Palmyra faced devastating structural demolitions alongside heavy looting of its necropolis.

- Ain Dara was severely damaged by airstrikes, followed by heavy military earthworks and bulldozer clearing.

Crucially, the study shows that post-war threats like agricultural encroachment, infrastructure building, and military fortification now pose as great a threat to Syria's ancient history as the war itself.
