text:
“Confidence in who we are gives us the freedom to celebrate the richness of others. Culture need not divide us; at its best, it invites us to listen, to learn, and to discover.

This island has given the world extraordinary voices. The wit of Oscar Wilde, the poetry of W.B. Yeats, the beautiful depth of C S Lewis, the dark curiosity of a pint of the dark stuff, the quiet genius of Seamus Heaney - but also the music of countless traditional musicians, marching bands and musical talent that has travelled far beyond our shores. Irish, Anglo Irish, Ulster Scots - our history and heritage, our cultural legacy so deeply intertwined but also each so worthy. And now, new voices, new traditions. Every evolving. Ever changing. A cultural heritage that belongs to no single tradition. A cultural future that certainly does not. 

They remind us that, perhaps, the greatest art often grows, and flows, from places of complexity, of trauma and also too, shared humanity.

May every tune played here carry a little of the warmth that John Hewitt wrote of, a little of the grace that C.S. Lewis imagined, and a little of the hope that music has always offered to every community on this island.

May every visitor leave with a wee bit of Belfast in their heart. May the music and memory linger long after the performances end. And may we always have the confidence to celebrate every tradition that enriches our shared home, knowing that respecting another’s culture never diminishes our own—it strengthens the place we all call home.”

Thank you all for the warm welcome as I spoke at and visited so many different places throughout the day.

text:
Through Jesus' sacrifice, we are no longer condemned but offered new life, freedom, and eternal hope.

On the cross, He took upon Himself the weight of our sin, the punishment that we deserved, so that we could stand before God not in guilt, but in grace. In Him, the chains of our past are broken, and the judgment that once separated us from God has been completely removed. What we receive in return is not just survival, but new life, a life renewed, restored, and made whole in His presence.

His blood has the power to cleanse every sin, no matter how deep or how dark, for those who place their faith in Him. There is no stain too great that His mercy cannot wash away, no heart too broken that His love cannot heal. When we come to Him with sincere repentance and trust, we are forgiven fully and forever, not by our own works, but by His perfect sacrifice.

Every time we remember the cross, we are reminded of God's incredible love, mercy, and grace, a love that pursued us when we were lost, a mercy that withheld the wrath we deserved, and a grace that gives us what we could never earn. The cross is not just a symbol of suffering, but the greatest demonstration that we are cherished beyond measure.

So let us live each day with grateful hearts, not out of duty, but out of deep love for the One who loved us first. Let us honor the Lamb who gave everything, who laid down His life willingly so that we might receive forgiveness, salvation, and everlasting life. May our words, our actions, and our worship reflect the hope we now carry, that because He lives, we too shall live, now and for eternity in His presence.

#JesusChrist #AmazingGrace

text:
21 years ago, I arrived in the UK as a young international medical graduate with a dream.
Today, I celebrate 10 years as a Consultant Spinal Surgeon 🎉🥳

Exactly 10 years ago, I started my consultant journey at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust  Liverpool, and The Robert Jones and Agnes Hunt Orthopaedic Hospital NHS Foundation Trust Oswestry.

The journey was far from straightforward ! 

I failed PLAB 2 on my first attempt, struggled to secure my first NHS job and, when I almost lost hope, moved to Ireland in 2005. Ten years of hard work, perseverance and training eventually brought me to Alder Hey and RJAH for a combined Paediatric and Adult Spinal Fellowship.

I still remember taking the ferry across the Irish Sea, leaving behind Ireland and people who had become so dear to me, and once again starting from scratch.

That decision changed my life ! 

At the end of my fellowship, I was fortunate to be offered Consultant positions at both institutions.The last decade has been about much more than surgery.

I became a father to my twin girls, supported my wife through her training as she became an NHS Consultant, and experienced the profound loss of my father to cancer.

Professionally, I have learned from my patients, families, colleagues, mentors and multidisciplinary teams from successes, challenges and even complaints. International conferences and visiting great spinal centres around the world have continually broadened my perspective.

10 years as a Consultant is a milestone, but not the destination.

I remain grateful to everyone who has been part of this journey and especially to Alder Hey and RJAH for giving me the privilege of doing what I love.

21 years since arriving in the UK.
10 years as a Consultant.
A journey I could never have imagined.
And hopefully, only the beginning. 🙏

text:
Did you ever wonder what our prehistoric Irish ancestors really ate? The oldest confirmed meal on the island is reindeer venison, gnawed in Castlepook Cave in Cork around 33,000 BCE. Our ancestors also had a bit of Brown bear at Alice and Gwendoline Cave in Clare around 10,500 BCE. Though them lads mightve been Ice Age visitors passing through rather than settled inhabitants. 

The real story starts with the Mesolithic, roughly 8,000 to 4,000 BCE, when the first permanent colonists arrived by boat across the newly formed Irish Sea. What Ireland offered them was wild boar, and the suspicion among archaeologists is that even the boar may have been imported deliberately. 

The earliest evidence is piglet trotters from Mount Sandel in Derry. Fish filled the protein gap thats always been in Ireland. Seaonally salmon, trout and eel were caught using spears and fish-weirs, some of which have been found in Dublin. Coastal communities added cod, whiting and wrasse. And they gathered shellfish too. 

A lot of birds we'd not consider eating were hunted aswell, the likes of wood pigeon and the tastier capercaillie. Oh and a lot of hazel nuts were stored in pits for the winter months. The arrival of agriculure with farming communities around 4,000 BCE changed everything of course. 

Cattle, sheep, domestic pigs and possibly goat were introduced. And in a development that still puzzles archaeologists, fish largely just disappeared from the diet. Not gradually, abruptly. A people living on an island rich in rivers and coastline apparently stopped eating fish once they could eat beef instead. (In an unrelated incident when the DTM was experienced an asymmetric tachyon spurt over Brú na Bóinne in the Late Neolithic and me monthly Spice Bag ration was ejected from a porthole. But I digress.)

Dairy appeared alongside meat, with fatty residues found on Neolithic pots. Genetic analysis shows that Neolithic Irish people lacked lactase persistence, meaning raw milk would have made them sick. The likely solution was cheese, which reduces the problematic elements considerably. Wheat and barley started getting grown and eaten, though whether as gruel or bread we arent sure.

By the Bronze Age, fulachtaí fia, them burnt mound cooking sites found across Ireland in their hundreds, show a bigger session than just family meals. The amount of burnt stone, the scale of the troughs and the concentration of cattle bones suggest communal cooking, basically feasting. 

Bronze cauldrons began to appear then too, though a lot of these might also have doubled for religious ceremonies. The rotary stone quern arrived, making grain milling faster and more efficient. This also wrecked peoples teeth because of the tiny grains of rock which inevitably ended up in the dinner. 

And ceramic pottery vanished from these sites almost entirely, replaced by wooden and metal vessels, for reasons nobody has fully explained. The Iron Age royal sites at Tara, Emain Macha and Dún Ailinne show beef and pork dominating high-status tables. And we`ll visit them all in the DTM at some stage for a session.

text:
Irish EU Presidency Mobilises for Ceuta Crisis Amid Italy’s Schengen Suspension Against Spain

Irish Taoiseach Micheál Martin and Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan have been pulled into a major EU migration emergency after roughly 60,000 people crossed from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta within a single 24-hour period spanning Thursday and Friday.

The sudden influx, equivalent to about 70% of Ceuta’s population, prompted emergency coordination under Ireland’s current presidency of the EU Council. 

O’Callaghan has called an urgent meeting of EU ambassadors for Monday and activated the bloc’s Integrated Political Crisis Response mechanism, with senior officials already meeting on Saturday.

At least 67 people died during the crossing, either by drowning or being crushed while trying to scale a breakwater. By 6pm Friday more than 48,000 of those who entered had returned voluntarily to Morocco. The episode nevertheless triggered a political crisis for the Spanish government and led some other EU states to demand that Spain be suspended from the Schengen free-movement area.

Italy went further, announcing a one-month suspension of its Schengen arrangements with Spain. Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani attributed the surge to Spain’s recent programme that regularised more than a million undocumented migrants and asylum seekers, arguing it had incentivised trafficking networks.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez acknowledged that most EU partners had offered solidarity, but criticised those who attacked his government, calling their stance “contrary to European law, humanitarian law and the principles of solidarity.” He requested an urgent video conference of interior ministers.

O’Callaghan said he had spoken directly with Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska to express Ireland’s support and would stay in close contact with Spain, other member states and EU institutions as the situation develops.

@SecKennedy @DonaldTrump @DonaldJTrumpJr @FDA/ @HHSGov @GovStitt @SenatorLankford HHS Officials and Members of Congress,

My name is April. I am a wife, mother of three, and small business owner from Oklahoma. I am writing to share my personal experience with kratom and its alkaloids in hopes that my story will be considered before any further restrictions or bans are enacted.

Since the age of 15, I have struggled with social anxiety, depression, ADHD, substance abuse, and opioid dependence. Over the years, I was prescribed antidepressants and other medications in an attempt to manage these conditions, but none of them ever helped me feel like myself. Instead, I spent years searching for something that could quiet the constant feeling that something was wrong.

After becoming dependent on methadone for nearly ten years, my quality of life steadily declined. I was overweight, exhausted, falling asleep throughout the day, and emotionally disconnected. Worst of all, I felt like I was letting my children down. They were the ones who lost the most while I struggled just to get through each day.

Three years ago, I discovered kratom. It became the foundation of a wellness journey that allowed me to move away from pharmaceuticals and reclaim my life. Because of kratom, I was able to successfully stop taking methadone after ten years of dependence. Within the past year, I also discontinued Paxil and later Wellbutrin, which had begun causing significant irritability and anger.

As part of that journey, I have used small doses of kratom alkaloids, including 7-OH & MGM-15. I approach these products cautiously because I am a mother of 3, My goal has never been intoxication—it has always been health, stability, and being present for my family for many years to come.

Today, I no longer struggle with the anxiety &depression that once controlled my life. I no longer drink alcohol or misuse drugs. I am clear-headed, and genuinely joyful. I have been able to build and operate a successful business, & most importantly, I am present for my children.

I understand that kratom and 7-oh have controversial reputation. Like any substance, they can be misused. However, the actions of some should not determine access for everyone. We do not ban alcohol because some abuse it, drive intoxicated, & destroy lives. Instead, we regulate it while allowing responsible adults make their own choices.

It is true that stopping kratom abruptly may produce withdrawal symptoms. However, physical dependence is not unique to kratom. Many legally prescribed meds-including opioids, SSRIs & SNRIs, and other psychiatric medications—can also cause dependence & withdrawal. In my own case, severe Paxil withdrawal contributed to a suicide attempt in 2001. Every medication carries risks, yet we continue researching them, improving them, and making informed decisions rather than banning them outright.

Rather than prohibiting kratom and its alkaloids, I believe more research should be allowed. These compounds may offer safer alternatives for people living with chronic pain, PTSD, OCD, opioid dependence, and other difficult conditions. Many Americans are actively seeking options beyond traditional pharmaceuticals.

I respectfully ask that you consider the experiences of responsible consumers like me before supporting legislation that would remove access to something that has genuinely transformed my life. Policies should be guided by evidence, research, and balanced regulation—not solely by misuse or stigma.

If the goal is to protect public health, I respectfully ask that you consider whether prohibition will truly accomplish that, or whether research, thoughtful regulation, and responsible access would better serve the Americans whose lives have been improved by these products.

Thank you for your time, your consideration, and your commitment to protecting public health while listening to the voices of those whose lives have been positively impacted.

Sincerely,

April R.

text:
Estrogen is the key factor in trauma-related memory disorders.

New research just revealed how it works.

While long associated with memory and female reproductive health, estrogen produced locally within the brain plays a surprisingly pivotal role in how both sexes process trauma. A recent study demonstrates that levels of this hormone in the hippocampus—the brain's primary memory center—can determine the severity of post-traumatic stress responses. Researchers found that while estrogen usually aids brain flexibility, subjects with higher levels of the hormone in the brain experienced significant, long-lasting memory disruptions following intense stress. Conversely, those with lower hippocampal estrogen levels appeared largely protected from these long-term psychological impairments, showing little to no lasting disruption.

The mechanism behind this vulnerability lies in how estrogen interacts with the genome. By "opening up" specific parts of the DNA, the hormone increases the brain's sensitivity, which usually helps form new memories quickly. However, under extreme stress, this same biological process may inadvertently lock in harmful memories more permanently, making the brain more susceptible to the long-term effects of trauma. This discovery offers a critical biological lens through which to view conditions like Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD), potentially explaining why certain individuals are more vulnerable to the condition and paving the way for future treatments that could prevent traumatic events from becoming lifelong disorders.

source: Pennsylvania State University. How estrogen in the brain impacts stress and trauma response. Penn State News.

Top Quantum Computing Stocks a Leading Wall Street Analyst Says Could Soar

Benchmark analyst Gary Mobley, ranked among the top 4% of Wall Street analysts, remains bullish on quantum computing and believes investors should take a portfolio approach, as multiple technologies and architectures are likely to succeed rather than a single winner dominating the industry. He notes that advances toward fault tolerance and Quantum Advantage are accelerating commercial adoption. According to Grand View Research, the quantum computing market is expected to grow from $1.9 billion in 2026 to more than $8 billion by 2033.

$IONQ – IonQ

Benchmark: Buy | Price Target: $60 (~65% upside) | Wall Street Consensus: Strong Buy (7 Buys, 2 Holds) | Average Price Target: $69.31 (~90% upside)

Mobley believes IonQ has transformed from a quantum hardware company into a fully integrated quantum platform spanning quantum computing, networking, sensing, and cybersecurity. He sees this as a major competitive advantage that could allow IonQ to become a foundational company across the quantum ecosystem.

IonQ uses trapped-ion technology, widely considered one of the highest-fidelity quantum architectures. Its commercial systems include Aria (25 qubits), Forte (36 qubits), Forte Enterprise (data-center optimized), and Tempo (100 qubits). The company’s systems are available through AWS and Microsoft Azure.

A major catalyst is the completed $1.8 billion acquisition of SkyWater Technology, making IonQ the only quantum hardware company with a Pentagon-accredited, fully U.S.-based semiconductor foundry. The acquisition also expands its position as a supplier of foundry services, atomic clocks, and quantum networking equipment, strengthening its role across the industry’s supply chain.

Q1 2026: Revenue $64.7M (+700% YoY), beating estimates by nearly $15M, with EPS of ($0.34).

$RGTI – Rigetti Computing

Benchmark: Buy | Price Target: $25 (~67% upside) | Wall Street Consensus: Moderate Buy (6 Buys, 3 Holds) | Average Price Target: $30.71 (~105% upside)

Mobley views Rigetti as one of the strongest pure-play quantum computing companies, focusing on superconducting quantum chips while partnering with leading companies for cloud infrastructure and software. This capital-efficient strategy allows Rigetti to concentrate on advancing its quantum processors.

Its flagship Cepheus-1-108Q uses a modular architecture built from 12 interconnected 9-qubit chiplets, tripling the qubit count of previous systems. Rigetti also offers Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) and recently expanded collaborations with HPE, the Pittsburgh Supercomputing Center, AWS, Microsoft Azure, NVIDIA CUDA Quantum, Riverlane, and Quanta Computer.

Q1 2026: Revenue $4.4M (+199% YoY), beating estimates, with EPS of ($0.04).

$QBTS – D-Wave Quantum

Benchmark: Buy | Price Target: $30 (~66% upside) | Wall Street Consensus: Strong Buy (13 Buys, 1 Hold) | Average Price Target: $37.58 (~108% upside)

Mobley believes D-Wave is unique because it develops both quantum annealing and gate-model quantum computers, allowing it to target a much broader range of commercial applications. Annealing systems excel at optimization, logistics, manufacturing, and AI, while gate-model systems focus on chemistry, drug discovery, molecular simulation, and materials science.

Key catalysts include the $550 million acquisition of Quantum Circuits Inc., a $1.5 million NSF grant for fault-tolerant quantum research, a Nasdaq listing, and an expanded partnership with AT&T. Its Leap cloud platform gives businesses real-time access to quantum computing through the cloud.

text:
CRE Debt Restructuring, like Bankruptcy? Nope.

People assume restructuring in real estate works the way it does in corporate bankruptcy. It doesn’t. Bankruptcy reconfigures the capital stack. Valuation and the business plan sit behind that work as inputs. 

Firms that excel at bankruptcy usually lack the tools for a real estate restructuring where valuation and business plan are front and center. 

In single-asset real estate there are no competing creditor classes to trade against, just the borrower and the mortgage, maybe a mezzanine loan. Bankruptcy costs time and money, and the debtor seldom keeps the asset.

Some advisors still sell bankruptcy as a restructuring option. It isn’t. It is the last tool after everything else has failed, and the borrower carries the damage to its lending reputation for years.

In a workout your leverage is proving you are the best counterparty with the best plan and the best offer. Filing puts you in the bad-borrower camp and the rest stops mattering. Expect opposing counsel to just say no.

On a non-recourse loan you can trigger recourse and pay every cost of the case, yours and the lender’s. If an advisor promises a settlement built on bankruptcy leverage, ask whether he has read Harrington v. Purdue Pharma. In 2024 the Supreme Court held that a Chapter 11 plan cannot release claims against a non-debtor without that creditor’s consent. The borrower entity files. The guaranty belongs to the guarantor, who did not.

So a sponsor trying to keep an asset without paying full debt, triggers personal recourse on the whole loan plus the costs of a proceeding designed to take his asset from him and transfer it to his creditors. 

Outside narrow cases, it is illogical because the law is on the side of paying back one’s debts and courts enforce the law, so the venue carries more risk with little return. 

The best time to negotiate is early, not after the decision makers have set their approach. A plan is only as good as the person executing it and then new capital and operating capability.

Much of our early work is telling a sponsor what he does not want to hear before the lender says it for us. We then build around the objections we expect. The adage, “make the first offer objectionable” fails when your counterparty’s posture is enforcement. This is not willing buyer, willing seller.

The property is the collateral. The business plan is what makes it worth re-lending against. We build that argument from the rent roll, tenant-by-tenant risk, capital needs, and market velocity, and the output is cash flow after real carrying costs. Skip that work and the restructure is a shot in the dark.

The plan will not feel like a win to the borrower, and it will not feel like one to the lender. It only has to beat foreclosure, receivership, and an REO carry.

Workouts start from weakness because the lender holds the option to enforce. Stay rational, act early, and you will almost always get a rational negotiation in return.

text:
Shravan Somvar :

Shravan is a very holy month dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is named after the *Shravan Nakshatra*, which appears on the full moon day. Devotees believe that worshipping Shiva in this month brings special blessings.

According to the *Padma Purana*, visiting all 12 Jyotirlingas fulfills one’s wishes and leads to heaven and liberation. Kashi is also considered very sacred because it is believed to rest on the tip of Shiva’s trident and remain untouched even during cosmic destruction.

Shravan includes many sacred observances, such as four Mondays, one Pradosh, and one Shivratri. Each Monday, devotees offer different items:

- 1st Monday: Raw rice  
- 2nd Monday: White sesame seeds  
- 3rd Monday: Whole green moong beans  
- 4th Monday: Barley grains  
- 5th Monday, if there is one: Sattu  

Many women keep fasts during Shravan for the long life of their husbands. The *Solah Somvar Vrat* is also considered very sacred. It means fasting for 16 Mondays in a row and can be started in Vaishakh, Shravan, Kartik, or Magh. 
On the 17th Monday, food and gifts are offered to 16 married couples.

*Bilva leaves* are very important in Shiva worship. Devotees also pour water on the Shiva Linga as a form of *Jalabhishek*. This is linked to Lord Shiva’s act of consuming poison and the sacred flow of the Ganga from his hair.

For those who are unable to perform daily worship throughout Shravan, observing a fast and offering prayers on Mondays, the day most beloved to Lord Shiva, is considered highly auspicious and spiritually rewarding.

text:
#ATIKU2027: BREAKING!!! President Bola Tinubu, Nyesom Wike, INEC Chairman, Put On Red Alert; As Atiku Abubakar Announces That Nigerian Youths Will Decide The Next President Of Nigeria In The 2027 Presidential Election; Declares That The Time Has Finally Come...

The 2027 Presidential Candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s recent message to Nigerian youths, over the weekend, strikes at the heart of a recurring national dilemma: The paradox of a demographic giant that refuses to flex its political muscle.

“What good is the strength of a giant, if the giant refuses to rise?” Atiku asked the youths, framing his appeal around the urgent need for young Nigerians to overcome division, reject inducement and seize agency over their collective future.

The ADC Presidential Candidate delivered this charge during the RiseUpNaija Movement Leadership Retreat, in Abuja, addressing hundreds of young Political Activists and Leaders, ahead of the 2027 general elections. His statement underscores three interlocking themes: 

1. Demographic power: Young Nigerians constitute the largest voting bloc in the country, yet remain politically fragmented.
2. Division by design: Tribal, religious and partisan manipulation by a smaller political class, has repeatedly diluted youth influence. 
3. The economics of inducement: Short-term gratification cash, gifts or promises, must not be traded for four years of governance shaped by others. 

Atiku's rhetorical question is both a challenge and a lament: Nigeria’s youth hold numerical dominance, but that strength is nullified by apathy, disunity or transactional voting. 

This is not however, his first public plea to Nigerian youths. In recent months, Atiku has consistently warned against voter apathy, citing turnout rates of just 25–30% in past elections as deeply discouraging. He has urged young people to become “authors, dreamers, doers and builders” of a new Nigeria; and to reject despair, even when elections are marred by manipulation. 

His latest message to the youths sharpens this appeal with a direct economic analogy: No amount of money offered by Politicians can outweigh the long-term value of a single vote cast responsibly.

Furthermore, several factors make Atiku’s intervention particularly timely:

2027 electoral stakes: With the Presidential election on the horizon, youth mobilisation could decisively alter outcomes.

- Rising hardship and disillusionment: Many young Nigerians express frustration over unemployment, insecurity and perceived electoral fraud conditions, that fuel apathy or protest. 

- Strategic voting blocs: Political parties are increasingly targeting youth demographics with inducements, knowing that small incentives can swing large constituencies. 

Atiku’s counsel is clear: Competence, character and ideas; not bags of rice or cash. We must guide our voting decisions. 

For Political Communicators, Journalists and Campaigners, Atiku’s statement offers a ready-made narrative frame:

- Mobilisation messaging: Emphasise youth agency and the high cost of inducement.
- Unity appeals: Counter tribal and religious division with cross-cutting youth identity.
- Accountability focus: Shift discourse from personality to performance and policy.

His language, especially the “giant” metaphor, lends itself to visual storytelling, infographics and social media campaigns, that can amplify the call to action.

Atiku’s message is both a mirror and a mandate. It reflects the frustrating reality of a youth population that remains politically underutilised, and it mandates a collective shift towards disciplined, informed and unified participation. Whether this appeal translates into higher turnout and more issue-based voting in 2027, will depend on how effectively Youth Leaders, Civil Society and the Media, amplify and operationalise his very important call. 

In the end, the question remains: Will Nigeria’s giant finally rise?

To help you maximize the return on this massive investment, we have a humble suggestion: Please, start eating the billboards.

Why Billboards Make the Perfect Meal
•High in Fiber: Vinyl and wood planks offer excellent structural roughage, which is exactly what our national economy needs right now.
•Rich in Promises: Each poster is thoroughly coated in hundreds of thousands of unfulfilled promises, ensuring a very heavy, filling meal.
•100% Tax-Paid: Since these towering structures were funded by public revenue or inflated fees, they are technically a self-sustaining food source for your administrations.
•Immunity to Inflation: While the price of beans, rice, and bread multiplies daily, your giant faces on the highway remain entirely free for you to consume.

Our Recommended Recipe
1The Infrastructure Stew: Tear down one giant billboard celebrating "100 Days of Paving 2 Kilometres of Road."
2The Revenue Garnish: Chop up the heavy fee receipts that you charged opposition parties to add a bit of spicy crunch.
3The Photo-Op Simmer: Slow-cook the entire mixture under the hot sun until the ink runs, then serve it at your next executive council meeting.
Your Excellencies, please do not let these expensive structures go to waste. If the citizens cannot afford to eat because of the harsh economy, the least you can do is lead by example and feast on your own grand achievements.
Bon Appétit!
Yours faithfully,
The Association of Hungry Spectators

text:
Do not exchange 4 years of your future for inducements. A bag of rice will disappear — Atiku warns against vote buying

Former Vice President and 2027 ADC presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, has urged Nigerian youths to reject vote-buying and all forms of political inducement ahead of the next general election.

Speaking on Saturday during the inauguration of state coordinators for the RiseUpNaija (RUN) movement in Abuja, Atiku said his presidential ambition was driven by a desire to build a nation with accountable leadership, strong institutions and equal opportunities.

“I stand before you today not merely as a former vice president or an elder statesman, but as a lifelong democrat who has never stopped believing that Nigeria can become the great nation its people deserve,” he said.

Lamenting the growing exodus of young Nigerians, Atiku added, “I see brilliant young people leaving Nigeria, not because they have stopped loving their country, but because they no longer believe their country loves them back.”

He urged youths to use their numerical strength to shape the country’s future instead of allowing themselves to be divided.
“Young Nigerians constitute the largest voting population in our country. Yet, too often, you have allowed yourselves to be divided by tribe, religion and political manipulation while a much smaller political class decides your future. That must end.”

Warning against selling votes, he said, “Your vote is far more valuable than any amount of money a politician can offer. Do not exchange four years of your future for one afternoon of inducement. A bag of rice will disappear.”

Atiku also called on young Nigerians to move beyond social media activism.
“Hashtags do not count votes. Livestreams do not secure polling units. Tweets do not defend democracy. Only citizens do,” he said.

He urged them to register to vote, verify their registration, volunteer, serve as polling agents and peacefully protect the people’s mandate.

He further appealed for issue-based politics, saying, “In 2027, let us vote for competence. Let us vote for character, ideas and for the future.”

Ansem's fund transfer to cold storage

What happened: he announced it in advance, "moving funds to cold storage today, so dont be alarmed when you see the withdrawal later im not hacked lol," thanked @BitGo for the setup, calling it "one of the most trusted custodians with all the necessary banking infrastructure & insured licensing," then confirmed with "ok funds moved," "treasury multisig," and "keep the $ANSEM treasury safe lads."

The IRL art bounty

The big NFT events from late July

Two community games have also launched, Bullbump for combat and Land Race for territory, plus grants supporting artists, editors, designers, and builders in the community. On the King Bulls front, the Gold King, the last in the series, is currently up for raffle. Previous ones sold for 275 SOL, 295 SOL, and raffles brought in 452 and 505 SOL, all of it recycled into $ANSEM buybacks.

A Bulltoshi donation wallet opened on July 31, address FLToZoqnBTTnthDbYKaXP5VwyvCakFzgPAi7stCftj3L, with a goal of 1,000 Bulltoshi for a mass airdrop to $ANSEM holders. Everything that comes in goes back out entirely, nothing stays locked up, and the community keeps contributing to it regularly.

Slogan: "We all win together." The raffle stays active and strongly pushes the synergy between the two collections.

Market Bubble released episode 13 in late July, centered on "trading as creator business," social trading, and content as a growth engine, with Ansem's clear message: hold $ANSEM, watch Market Bubble, trade on Bullpen.

Community vibe and flywheel

Strong "Charge forward" energy. Two NFT collections running in a loop, feeding $ANSEM, royalties into LP and buybacks, then into airdrops. Smart money has started accumulating again. Liquidity is improving thanks to the NFTs and creator fees. Ansem stays fully aligned, still holding around 58% of supply and hasn't sold, and just professionalized custody of that treasury via BitGo cold storage.

What's next

The Bulltoshi epoch on August 13 with its airdrops, more King Bulls auctions including the Gold King, new product updates on Bullpen, the 1M holder target, and the continuation of the NFT flywheel and stimmy drops.

The ecosystem has gone from a simple meme to a real machine: token, trading terminal, two NFT collections, Discord, content, and recurring airdrops, now backed by institutional-grade treasury security.

4 years of folders on my machine. Not one connection between them.

He never revises. He just zooms out.

text:
A 13-year-old eighth-grade student in Tennessee was arrested, strip-searched, and forced to spend the night in a juvenile detention cell after making an inside joke during an online chat with classmates. 

This incident highlights the serious legal and social consequences that can arise from online communication. 

It serves as an important lesson for young people about the power and impact of their digital words. 

The situation unfolded when the student shared a private joke within an online group chat. 

Classmates who did not understand the context reported the message to school authorities out of caution. 

School officials felt the message could be interpreted as a potential threat. 

They quickly notified law enforcement, leading to the student's immediate arrest. 

At the police station, the teenager went through standard jail procedures, including a full strip-search. 

The student then spent an entire night in a juvenile detention facility away from family. 

This event offers critical lessons for students navigating the digital world. 

First, it shows that private online spaces are never truly private. 

Messages can easily be shared, misinterpreted, or reported by others. 

Second, schools and police take any perceived threat extremely seriously, regardless of whether it was meant as a joke. 

Finally, this case demonstrates how a single misunderstood text can lead to permanent legal consequences. 

Understanding these risks helps young people make safer, more thoughtful choices online.

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, Monday, August 2, 1971, Braniff's parent company, Dallas-based Ling-Temco-Vought, Inc., sold Braniff International, its airline subsidiary, as part of a settlement with the Department of Justice regarding an anti-trust suit over LTV's takeover of Jones & Laughlin Steel Co.

Braniff International's parent company LTV began selling its controlling interest in the airline on Monday, June 1, 1970. Former Braniff Chairman of the Board Troy Victor Post, who was succeeded as Chairman by Braniff President Harding L. Lawrence, was also reelected to Braniff's Board of Directors on the same day.

A decision was made by Braniff's parent company, Greatamerica Corporation, to sell all of its assets to Ling-Temco-Vought, Inc., in 1967. On November 17, 1967, the Civil Aeronautics Board approved the acquisition of Braniff Airways, Incorporated, d/b/a Braniff International by Dallas, Texas, based conglomerate Ling Temco Vought. LTV would purchase Braniff's parent company, Greatamerica Corporation, which had owned controlling interest in Braniff since 1964. Along with the purchase of Braniff would come the carrier's sister company, National Car Rental.

The original LTV purchase plan was announced a few months earlier on August 4, 1967. LTV would make an offer to purchase all of the shares of Greatamerica Corporation, which received unanimous approval from the Board's of both companies. The offer was submitted to the Civil Aeronautics Board shortly thereafter, because the purchase would involve controlling interest in Braniff Airways, Incorporated. Any purchase of an air carrier required a hearing by the Civil Aeronautics Board and then an ensuing approval before a purchase could occur.

The CAB rendered its decision on October 20, 1967, which mandated certain stipulations mainly designed to prevent LTV from using Braniff as a vehicle to promulgate its aerospace business. LTV could not transact more than $100,000 USD in air travel business with Braniff unless specifically approved by the CAB prior to the transaction. LTV could not market a new aircraft, if it were to build or sell one, to Braniff, again without prior CAB approval. And finally, the CAB would retain the authority to reexamine the purchase and make appropriate changes to the agreement as might become necessary as the company's business environment changed.

This unique 1968 LTV historical and management review film presents a fantastic overview of the massive size and scope of the business that LTV had grown itself into. There is an interview of founder Jim Ling and approximately two-thirds of the way through the film there is a portrait of Braniff Chair Harding L. Lawrence and a review of Braniff's importance to the LTV conglomerate:

https://t.co/NZIMYynG3q…

LTV was given the choice of either selling Braniff and Okonite (a wire and cable producing entity) or its controlling interest in Jones & Laughlin. The Justice Department filed the suit against LTV in 1969, and the agreement to sell Braniff was announced on February 19, 1970 with full divestiture of Braniff effective on August 2, 1971. LTV owned approximately 55-percent of Braniff stock with the remainder owned by the public.

LTV owned Braniff just two days short of four years with the purchase of the airline and its then parent company Greatamerica Corporation on August 4, 1967. The CAB stated they could find no reason for preventing the merger on October 20, 1967, and fully approved the merger on November 17, 1967, with the stated stipulations. Braniff's shares as a result of the LTV sale of the airline went to the general public. Braniff would for the first time since the early 1960s become an independent public company once again.

During its ownership by LTV, Braniff International saw the implementation of a number of unique passenger service conveniences including the famed Jetrail Carpark System at Dallas Love Field. The unique people mover monorail system whisked passengers from Braniff's new Terminal of the Future to the Outer Parking Lot high above the congested terminal dropoff area on Cedar Springs Road.

Photo: Two of the ten Jetrail Air Coaches are traveling northbound on the Inner Rail continue to the Braniff Terminal of the Future. The plush Air Coach is painted in 1967 Alexander Calder/Harper and George Orange, which was one of five colors selected by Mr. Chuck Ax, the interior designer for the Jetrail project. The Dallas architect firm of Pierce Lacey designed the infrastructure for the unique monorail system.

text:
India's food delivery & quick commerce war is just getting started. 🍔⚡

Flipkart is set to enter food delivery after aggressively expanding Flipkart Minutes in quick commerce.

Look at the battlefield today:

• Eternal → Zomato + Blinkit
• Swiggy → Food Delivery + Instamart
• Zepto
• Flipkart Minutes (+ Food Delivery soon)
• Amazon Fresh / Amazon Now
• JioMart
• BigBasket
• Several regional & niche players

Almost every large consumer-tech company now wants a share of India's high-frequency spending.

But here's the interesting part...

Food delivery is still essentially a duopoly between Eternal (Zomato) and Swiggy. Building a nationwide restaurant network, delivery fleet, customer loyalty, and profitable logistics is much harder than launching another app.

Quick commerce, on the other hand, has become a full-scale capital war where everyone is investing billions in dark stores, faster deliveries, and customer acquisition.

Competition will likely mean:
✅ Better offers for customers
✅ Faster innovation
✅ Lower delivery times

But for companies, it also means:
❌ Higher cash burn
❌ Margin pressure
❌ A tougher road to profitability

As investors, don't just ask "Who is entering?"

Ask "Who can survive this price war and still generate sustainable cash flows?"

In the long run, market leadership is built not by discounts, but by execution.

text:
I consider myself one of the lucky ones.

I didn’t struggle to get my first international job. In fact, I wasn’t even looking for one when the opportunity found me.

Here’s the summary:

• I was in my lab in Germany 🇩🇪 at the start of the second year of my MSc, running experiments.

• A PhD student forwarded an email to everyone in the lab about a student event in the Netherlands 🇳🇱 tagged “Best of Tech Course”, organised by one of the world’s leading semiconductor lithography companies.

• I thought I’ll probably learn something new. I submitted a video application.

• I got selected and attended the program online (I can’t remember why it wasn’t held onsite in the Netherlands).

• During the meet-and-greet session, I was paired with a hiring manager from the Optics team, which aligned perfectly with my MSc in Optics and Photonics.

• He noticed my teaching experience in Nigeria, together with my Physics and Optics background, and felt I’d be a good fit for his team.

• He shared a link to an opening and encouraged me to apply if I was interested.

• I applied on a Saturday. HR called me for the first interview on Tuesday.

• After a few rounds of interviews over the following months, I got the offer.

They relocated me from Germany 🇩🇪 to the Netherlands 🇳🇱, sent a relocation company to pack all my belongings, paid for my flight ✈️ , and even put me in a five-star hotel for my first two months for free.

Looking back, I was lucky. But I also realized that luck often comes from simply showing up.

If I had ignored that random email because I was “too busy,” none of this would have happened.

text:
U really CAN just do things and get $ 

BUT… u have to be honest on who you are first 

what I mean is if u suck dealing with uncertainty? 

or u just hate managing clients in general 

don’t start a freelance or agency operation to begin - or just stay small scale to maintain your sanity (lol)

if u legit aren’t build for that then a W2 or single client / low volume service biz is best 

U might even be better off in a closing role 

it’s not a one size fits all thing 

u could thrive in a high output outbound agency or freelance environment 

u might suck at that but have a nack for closing deals & thrive on a HTS offer 

or u may even climb the corporate ladder in sales etc quickly & stack your cash that way 

Exit later.. plan accordingly with some investments & skills to fall back in fractional work style 

Point is…

Yes, imo cold call agency is best model atm due to competition in all other channels 

+ low start up fees, and low complexity if you sell SMB 

But don’t get stuck in 1 lane 

I’m actually far, far more experienced at closing deals 

I’m only going to take on several more cold call agency clients 

Build out my team to help fulfil a lot of the work 

and I’m looking into part time closing / AE roles for B2B services offer and training offers 

Where I’ll make anywhere from $1.5k to $5k commission per deal closed and it’s usually 1-2 call close - fast sales cycle 

Not dealing with corporations with 20 decision makers 

More suitable for my own lifestyle and flexibility 

But my skill set and path may be different to many ppls

I can hop on calls with people interested in something /qualified

and close at up to 2x the rate as most people who try the same thing 

Ppl beside me fail and get fired 

While I end up being referred all the good inbound leads & demos / zoom calls 

sales & biz in general is NOT fair or the same for each person 

u have to find out what your thing is 

your own skills & strengths 

my belief of a good route is:

- cold calling local biz + freelance sites to start cold call agency 

- get basic sales skills 

- leverage basic sales skills to apply for closing roles (fractional)

- I do NOT suggest a biz unless highly SELF driven 

I personally don’t want to work for large companies ever again at this point in time 

A AE role or BDR at a tech company pays well good stability 

But you have no flexibility, and when you are free - you are expected to drive your own pipeline basically 

Im first and foremost I am business person

 I don’t like being controlled preferably 

I have sold millions of dollars in products & services over the years in my own businesses with no micro management 

My own genius is not in doing all of the work - I know how to create the whole system 

I know how to build teams, sell, market, manage paid ads, go viral on social media 

you’ve seen it here on X: top 1% reach in sales twitter in last 14 days 

I’m far more talented and skilled to just sit on phone calls all day 

But I lost a business due to a bad partnership a few years back 

Had to start again and basically start from scratch which was heart breaking tbh 

what I’m saying is you need to figure out what YOUR strengths & weaknesses are 

what do you want to do that suits you best?

are u ok with stress & uncertainty? 

or do you prefer order & consistency in income? (salary) 

don’t listen to anyone who says you must start a business 

or MUST get a W2 job first etc 

or contract freelance is the best 

the TRUTH?

It’s not a one size fits all 

It’s about what path works best for yourself

text:
Denver Broncos 2026 Fantasy Deep Dive

Most people still view the Broncos through the lens of “Sean Payton + elite defense + Bo Nix growth.” That is directionally correct, but the more interesting 2026 fantasy edges sit in the addition of Jaylen Waddle, Nix’s continued dual-threat identity after ankle surgery, the high-play-volume environment created by one of the league’s best defenses, and a running back room that remains a true committee with multiple paths to relevance. This is an ascending offense with more mouths to feed than last year.

The QB Reality
Bo Nix enters Year 3 fully healthy after fracturing his right ankle in the playoffs and undergoing two surgeries (including a follow-up for bone spurs). He has been a full participant in camp and has repeatedly stated he will not curtail his mobility — “I’m going to roll… that’s when I feel at my best.” His scrambling and designed runs remain a meaningful part of his fantasy floor and ceiling.

The offense ranks among the higher-play and higher-pass-volume units in the league thanks to the elite defense. Nix is a mid-to-late round QB1 with weekly upside when the rushing production and efficiency align. He is not in the absolute elite tier yet, but the supporting cast upgrade and system continuity make him one of the more appealing options in that range.

Scheme Continuity with a New Voice
Sean Payton remains the head coach, but he has handed primary play-calling duties to OC Davis Webb (promoted from quarterbacks coach). Webb has emphasized that this is still a Sean Payton offense with only minor tweaks. Expect continued motion, timing routes, play-action, and an emphasis on yards after the catch.

The big schematic development is the addition of speed packages designed around Jaylen Waddle. The Broncos traded significant capital (including a first-round pick) to acquire him, and the staff has a clear vision for using him both outside and in the slot to create mismatches.

Running Back Room – True Committee
This is not a workhorse situation. J.K. Dobbins is the nominal lead back and has been healthy in camp so far, but his career injury history remains a constant concern. RJ Harvey brings strong receiving skills and touchdown production from his rookie year. Rookie Jonah Coleman has generated positive early buzz and profiles as a capable three-down contributor who could push for snaps.

The result is a committee that makes every individual back harder to trust as a weekly starter. Dobbins has the clearest path to early-down and goal-line work if healthy. Harvey offers the better PPR floor via targets. Coleman is the high-upside handcuff/lottery ticket. Draft one if the price is right, but do not over-invest in the room.

Tight End – Secondary Role
Evan Engram returns but saw a reduced snap share in his first year in Denver. Adam Trautman and younger options (including Justin Joly) compete for residual work. This is not a high-priority TE room for fantasy. Engram is a deeper-league streamer at best unless the target distribution shifts meaningfully.

Wide Receivers – The Waddle Effect
The addition of Jaylen Waddle is the single biggest change. He brings elite speed, yards-after-catch ability, and the capacity to stretch the field both vertically and horizontally. Early indications and coaching comments suggest he will be a featured piece — potentially the top target or a true co-WR1 alongside Courtland Sutton.

Courtland Sutton remains the big-bodied, contested-catch, red-zone threat who has been Bo Nix’s most trusted target the past two seasons. His overall target share may dip with Waddle in the mix, but the efficiency and touchdown upside should keep him as a strong WR2/flex.

Troy Franklin, Marvin Mims Jr., and Pat Bryant battle for the WR3 role and residual snaps. The top two (Waddle and Sutton) are the clear fantasy priorities. The depth provides insurance but limited standalone weekly value in standard leagues.

The Bigger Picture Edges

- Elite defense creates positive game scripts and high overall play volume — a quiet positive for the entire offense.
- Nix’s confirmed intent to continue running after the ankle surgeries preserves his dual-threat fantasy profile.
- Waddle’s arrival gives the passing game a true speed element it previously lacked and should open things up for Sutton and the rest of the skill group.
- The RB committee limits individual ceilings but creates multiple handcuff and flex options if injuries hit.
- Play-calling transition to Webb is a mild unknown, but the system foundation remains Payton’s.

Draft approach summary:

- Bo Nix: Solid mid-to-late round QB1. Dual-threat upside + improved weapons.
- Jaylen Waddle: High-end WR2 with WR1 upside. The biggest new piece in the offense.
- Courtland Sutton: Reliable WR2/flex. Red-zone work and chemistry with Nix remain strong even with competition.
- J.K. Dobbins / RJ Harvey: Late-round committee plays. Prefer Harvey slightly in PPR for receiving work; Dobbins if you want early-down volume and believe in the health.
- Jonah Coleman: Deep sleeper / handcuff with three-down potential.
- Evan Engram and the rest of the skill group: Depth or streaming only.

The Broncos offense has more fantasy-relevant pieces than last year thanks to Waddle, but the target distribution is more competitive and the backfield remains split. The highest-conviction plays are Nix (for the dual-threat floor), Waddle (for the new explosive element), and Sutton (for the proven chemistry and red-zone role). Treat the running backs as situational rather than set-and-forget.

text:
An 83-year-old math problem with a $500 bounty was solved in a 25-page paper by a UCLA professor who has won every major prize in mathematics.

The paper was posted for free on his blog in September 2015. The lecture explaining it is on YouTube.

Every top hedge fund on earth has tried to hire him for seven figures. He teaches undergraduates at UCLA instead.

His name is Terence Tao. He is 49. Fields Medal 2006. He started college at nine, got his PhD at twenty, and became a full professor at twenty-four.

In 1932, Paul Erdős posed a question any teenager can understand.

Take an infinite sequence of plus and minus ones. Add them up along any fixed step. Every second entry, every seventh, every hundredth. Erdős conjectured the partial sums must eventually grow arbitrarily large no matter how cleverly the sequence was arranged. He offered $500 for a proof.

Some of the sharpest minds in number theory spent 83 years trying and failed.

In February 2015 a group of computer scientists ran a distributed proof for a special case. The output was a 13-gigabyte log file. Largest computer-generated math proof in history at the time.

Terence Tao read the result and thought about it for six months.

In September 2015 he posted a paper that solved the whole conjecture. He had noticed the discrepancy problem was equivalent to an old unproven statement about the Liouville function called the Chowla conjecture. He handled the technical connection in 25 pages.

The Erdős discrepancy problem was closed. Erdős had been dead nineteen years.

"For a really hard problem, you need to be okay with being stuck for months. You need to enjoy being stuck."

That is Tao explaining his method in almost every interview. Most mathematicians hate being stuck. He treats it as the job.

Retail traders spend their careers trying to beat known problems for small money. Tao spends his trying to close ones nobody has ever solved, for nothing but the answer.

The lecture is free. The paper is free. The blog he writes on has been free since 2007.

Almost every serious math result of the last thirty years has passed through his desk. Almost nobody watching this video will attempt the discrepancy problem tonight.

The math is free. The willingness to work on problems that have never been solved is much rarer than intelligence.

text:
The Nat Gas trade is where the memory trade was one year back, and nobody seems to be noticing. Here’s the hidden truth nobody is telling you, and what I’m buying (save this)

The US is heading into a historic natural gas supply deficit in 2028 and nobody is ready for what’s coming.

Current production sits around ~110-112 Bcf/d of natural gas per day, and the market can add up a further ~20 Bcf/d of new supply through additional drilling across the key basins of Appalachia, Haynesville, and the Permian which brings the total max deliverability of natural gas to ~132 Bcf/d.

But that max deliverability figure is the ceiling, not a promise. It assumes producers can optimally run their drilling operations, and more important, the infrastructure to deliver that gas gets built. This is where the argument breaks. It took the United States 10+ years to build exactly one interstate gas pipeline, the Mountain Valley Pipeline between Appalachia, and the Mid-Atlantic capable of transmitting ~2 Bcf/d.

The other bottleneck even before a millimetre of gas is available for transmission sits at the processing stage. At this leg of the natural gas value chain, raw gas extracted upstream off the gas-bearing rock is processed to get rid of contaminants to extract pure methane. The processing equipment deployed today is operating at max capacity, and any new buildout will take a minimum of ~2-3 years before any real capacity addition impacts the gas supply available for sale.

Gas already accounts for >40% of the US power generation requirements. Stack the total current and projected demand addition in comparison to the ~20 Bcf/d potential supply headroom, and it's clear why the nat gas trade is both immediate and convex. The primary demand forces come from two sources, LNG exports, and power demand from AI data centers.

The US produces ~112 Bcf/d and plans to scale it further by ~20 Bcf/d (a base growth of ~18%). However, take into account LNG exports which today are ~15 Bcf/d and are projected to hit the mid-30s Bcf/d by 2030 so exports as a % of total production go from roughly 13% to a number that will eat away the entire excess production even before a singular unit is available for the energy demand from AI compute workloads which is projected to add anywhere between ~5-15 Bcf/d of net new demand with no source to fulfill it. This is what makes this a demand side convex opportunity much like the memory trade of 2025.

Critics argue the world isn’t heading for a natural gas supply crunch. The lazy argument is that gas is abundant, and quote the flat forward price curve at the Henry Hub, the official delivery point for the NYMEX natural gas futures contract as evidence. Data shows the current spot price for gas is ~$2.63, and average across calendar years 2027 (~$3.35), 2028 (~$3.6-3.8), 2029 (~$3.7-3.9), and 2030 (~$3.7-3.9) shows that the market is pricing gas essentially at the same level in 2030 as it did in 2028.

Most physical gas today trades at the Henry Hub spot/monthly index price, not at a fixed future price. So when the deficit does indeed hit, the spot prices run to ~$8-10, and the bulk of gas eventually re-prices to spot. This is what the market is missing, and is exactly the whole trade.

So to close, the bottleneck is not gas. The US has plenty of it, and current prices reflect this excess. The problem is the bottlenecks around processing and transmission which makes the whole setup so convex.

As an investor I’m always on the lookout for such opportunities, and looking at the natural gas value chain closely enough reveals the actual names primed to capture the maximum upside.

The first name is Expand Energy (EXE), the largest US gas producer at 7.48 Bcf/d, operating at a breakeven cost below $3, sitting at 0.5x leverage, and generating ~$343m of FCF and ~$522m of net income last quarter. Trading at 5x trailing, and 4x forward EBITDA it is the cheapest large-cap gas producer in the US. The reason it's the best positioned play moving into the 2028 convexity is because its 2028 book remains open. What this means is it sells into new demand at rising spot prices rather than a locked forward price of ~$3.50 today. The current multiples don’t capture this, and both its cash flows and multiples will re-rate aggressively when that curve eventually wakes up.

Its close twin Range Resources (RRC) comes in second place. It sits on more than 30 years of premium, low cost Marcellus inventory with only 0.5x leverage. It earned $195m last quarter and the reason it belongs here is exactly the same as EXE. 95% of its 2028 production is unhedged meaning just like EXE, it too will capture higher cash flows, and see its multiples re-rate aggressively selling into demand in that rising price curve.

The next one on my radar is Kinder Morgan (KMI) which runs the largest gas network in the US. It moves ~40% of the natural gas consumed in the US and sits as the toll booth operator in the exact bottleneck the thesis posits. The most recent quarter saw the company print a record $2.2B of quarterly EBITDA on a $9.6B project backlog that is 92% gas and about 60% tied to power generation, so the backlog itself is the AI buildout. At ~12x forward EBITDA, 3.6x leverage and a 3.7% yield, it captures the rising volume of gas that has to move through a constrained system. The catch is that a toll road earns on throughput, not on the gas price, so the upside is real but still capped.

The last name on the record is directly tied to the rising demand for gas from AI data centers. Williams (WMB) owns Transco, the largest volume gas pipeline in the US, and is the backbone carrying Gulf Coast gas into the highest demand markets including Virginia, the biggest data center cluster on the planet. It is also the only midstream name building power directly for AI: Socrates, 400 MW of dedicated off-grid gas generation for a Meta data center, live by year end, and a 750 MMcf/d Transco expansion to feed the Virginia load. Management guides FY26 EBITDA at ~$8B+ with ~$7B of power-focused capex. It owns the physical link between the gas and the data center, which is the cleanest demand pull in the chain. Just like KMI, Williams is a beneficiary of this demand, but doesn’t directly benefit from gas price increase like the producers, and as such offers a steady, but not asymmetric upside.

To close, the whole trade is to long the cheap gas producers into a rising demand curve, and flat forward price curve about to get ripped, EXE and RRC are the whole trade.

One honest caveat, because this is not the memory trade in one important way. Gas supply is short cycle meaning that where memory had three makers and multi-year fabs capping supply, a gas producer can drill and complete a well in months, and Permian associated gas grows regardless of the price, since it comes up as a byproduct of oil drilling, adding several Bcf/d of price-insensitive new supply right into the deficit window.

So the flat curve is not only complacency, it is also a bet that any 2028 tightness gets drilled away. This trade works only if three things hold: producer capital discipline stays intact, the processing and pipeline bottlenecks stay tight, and LNG demand shows up on schedule. The day a large producer breaks ranks and floods supply at $6 gas, the thesis weakens into rising supply. I am betting the curve is asleep, not efficient, and that is the other side of the trade you need to know and factor before dropping a penny into any of the names above.

- mathematician at NASA
- Her hometown offered no public schooling for Black children past 8th grade 
- Her family had to move 120 miles just so she could attend high school
- Was so gifted with numbers she skipped multiple grades
- she Was attending high school by age 13 
- Became one of the first Black women accepted into West Virginia University's
- Left the program after a year to raise her three daughters
- Years later, a relative told her NASA's predecessor was hiring Black women to do math 
- she applied immediately
- Was segregated from her white colleagues, forced into separate bathrooms and dining areas
- Widowed in 1956, left raising her daughters alone while carrying a brutal workload
- Kept working anyway as NASA raced to catch up after the Soviets launched Sputnik 
- In 1960, became the first woman in her division credited as an author on a research report
- she Hand-calculated the trajectories for America's first crewed spaceflights
- Verified, by hand, the same orbital math a computer had just produced for John Glenn's flight .. because he wouldn't fly until she confirmed the numbers herself
- Did the calculations that helped bring Apollo 13 home safely after it nearly ended in disaster
- Received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015

The company operates primarily across core sectors including Water & Wastewater Infrastructure (STPs, WSSPs, sewerage networks), Roads & Highways, Electrical Transmission, and Urban Infrastructure. text:
Like the wise words my old co-worker use to say that his mother use to say….

“Life’s a bitch… and then you die.”

And I should clarify, it was the end of 2024 and 2025 was when everything happened all at once.

So in the order of things, my spouse and I were still living at my mom’s she started dating again and the guy moved in… Well, it started to become a problem. We were living in the basement (it has an exposed basement and nice) but basically he was pushing my mom to get us to move out. 

So because he also wanted to get ride of the cats (we had 3 at the time) we weren’t going to let that happens so we were taking them with us. Since renting was almost just as much as a mortgage on a house and we couldn’t find a place where you could rent and have pets we decided to buy a house (we wanted to buy anyway) eventually we found one we really liked and at that time houses where FLYING off the market before they where even reaching the listing. Eventually we found out that people from out of state where buying houses with cash without even inspecting them so they where just tossing money at them which is why they where going so fast. 

We rushed to the bank got approved and put an offer on the  night before the guy was going to accept another deal, so we quite literally got the house at the 11th hour and 59 minutes. The next morning we found out our offer was accepted! A few hours later we got into our car and that’s when we found our car was pretty much dead. Pistol rings were destroyed and it was burning all the oil in minutes, causing it the seize up die. That was July of 2024.

In September we moved in the house and sold our dead car to a mechanic who fixed them and put the money towards our wedding. 

October we got married. (We had the wedding planned since 2022, because of COVID all venues were backed out like crazy)

Found out in like LATE December we were going to have a kid. So we needed to worry about getting another car, and bought a used one late February. A month later my truck had major problems and got that fixed by early April. 

Now comes early July! We had the garage setup for a rummage sale! We wake up, get dressed open the garage aaaaaaaaaand the back right corner caved in. As we were trying to clean up a huge thunder storm roller through so we rushed to clear out the garage otherwise more could have been damaged. 

My mom offered to pay for it because my Daughter was due September.

 Mid-August rolls around and we found out that we are NOT getting short term disability for maternity leave because work did not file the paper work so we got no help there. 

September rolls around, our daughter is born and tried to file for some financial assistance, to which financial assistance told us we where not eligible because we quote “make to much.”  

Had to take on more debt over the winter, until maternity leave was over and now here we are in 2026, and my current battle is looking for a few job while trying to get ahead AND still fighting with the city/bank to get things squared away with my taxes. I think we got it all fixed and now I’m waiting for the mortgage company to send out our refunds. 

It has been a very, VERY chaotic adventure! 😅

text:
Tale Tale — The Steam That Remembered the Mountains

The pups had spent all morning wandering the desert, where the summer sun painted every stone with heat.

By afternoon, Salty Desert Dawg smiled and said, "Today we learn that water has more than one language."

The pups looked puzzled.

"Out here," he said, "we know water as rain, rivers, and wells. But today, we will meet water as steam."

An old healer welcomed them to a traditional temazcal, a humble dome of earth and stone. Nearby rested bundles of rosemary, eucalyptus, chamomile, pericón, hierba santa, and fresh basil. Their fragrance drifted through the warm air before a single stone had been touched.

"Every plant," the healer said softly, "has spent its life learning from the sun, the soil, the wind, and the rain. Today it shares a little of that wisdom."

The glowing volcanic stones were sprinkled with herbal infusions.

A cloud of fragrant steam rose into the darkness.

The pups breathed slowly.

The scent of rosemary reminded one of his grandmother's garden.

The eucalyptus opened another pup's breath after weeks of dusty trails.

Chamomile seemed to quiet thoughts that had been barking too loudly.

No one hurried.

Inside the warm darkness, every heartbeat sounded a little clearer.

After the final round of steam, the healer used fresh herb branches to gently fan the warmth across tired muscles. It wasn't punishment.

It was encouragement.

"Wake up," the herbs seemed to whisper.

"You've carried enough."

Outside, beneath the shade of an old mesquite tree, cool water waited alongside warm herbal tea.

Then came the massage.

Strong but careful hands worked tired shoulders, sore hips, and weary backs that had carried many miles across the Chihuahua desert.

The pups watched in amazement.

"The body remembers," said Salty Desert Dawg.

"So does kindness."

He explained that many traditions understand healing as more than fixing pain. Sometimes people need warmth after cold seasons of life. Sometimes they need rest after long battles. Sometimes they simply need someone to remind their body that it is safe to let go.

The smallest pup looked toward the desert mountains.

"So the herbs healed everyone?"

The old Dawg smiled.

"The herbs offered their gifts."

"The steam opened the door."

"The hands offered comfort."

"But healing..." he said, placing a paw over his heart, "...is something we also choose by accepting the gift."

As the sun began to set, the desert breeze felt different against their skin.

Not because the wind had changed—

but because they had.

Walking home beneath the wide Chihuahua sky, each pup carried the scent of mountain herbs, the warmth of stone, and a quiet lesson that would last long after the steam had disappeared.

For some wisdom is written in books.

Some is written in deserts.

And some... rises silently with the steam before settling gently into the heart.

Full English translation of the official statement by Rachid Khalfi, spokesperson for Morocco’s Ministry of the Interior, on the recent events at the crossing points leading to Ceuta and Melilla:

"In the wake of the events that recently took place at the crossing points leading to the cities of Ceuta and Melilla, the Ministry of the Interior confirms that the various data collected and analyzed have shown that these events were not the result of circumstantial or spontaneous factors. Rather, they resulted from the interaction of several interlocking factors, foremost among them the malicious exploitation of the digital space, the dissemination of misleading information, the role of human trafficking networks, and erroneous interpretations of legal and administrative data. These aimed to create the illusion of the possibility of easy access to the European space without legal consequences.

Aware of the nature of these developments and their indicators, the public authorities, from the earliest stages, activated a proactive and comprehensive approach. This was based on the early monitoring of various indicators, raising the levels of vigilance and mobilization, enhancing the readiness of the various security services and territorial authorities, and intensifying land and sea surveillance. This enabled control of the course of events, the protection of lives, the preservation of public order, and the securing of the borders, while strictly adhering to the provisions of the law and respecting the principle of proportionality in intervention.

The precise statistical data available to the competent authorities, based on the monitoring and field tracking systems adopted at the points of departure of those participating in these irregular crossing attempts, made it possible to determine the actual number of those involved. This amounted to approximately 40,000 people heading toward the city of Ceuta and about 1,135 people heading toward the city of Melilla.

All the people who managed to reach Melilla were returned immediately.
This tally is based on precise statistical and field data obtained through approved technical mechanisms for monitoring and tracking, making it the authoritative reference, in contrast to some circulating figures that are not based on reliable data or objective foundations.

In this context, the recent decisions issued by the Spanish judicial authorities regarding the restriction of the possibility of applying the procedure of immediate return to certain irregular migrants intercepted at sea stood out in particular. These decisions, accompanied by erroneous interpretations and misleading circulation, led to the reinforcement of a conviction among some aspiring crossers of the possibility of avoiding immediate return. This contributed to the emergence of a single pattern of irregular migration attempts, consisting of crossing by swimming, as the means that some believed offered greater chances of escaping immediate return.

These events have so far resulted in the recording of one accidental death following a fall from a rocky area adjacent to the city of Ceuta, in addition to 10 deaths by drowning. This reality reveals that the short distance separating the two sides—less than seventy meters—and the relative shallowness of the depth, which in some points does not exceed a little more than two meters, generated among a number of participants a misleading sense of the ease of crossing. This led them to underestimate the scale of the risks and to undertake attempts that ended, in some cases, with tragic consequences.

As for what is being circulated regarding the recording of other deaths in the city of Ceuta, the Moroccan authorities continue, within the framework of official channels of cooperation and coordination with their Spanish counterparts, to verify the accuracy of these data, as well as the actual number of the persons concerned, their identities, and their nationalities, with a view to completing the required legal, administrative, and humanitarian procedures.

It should also be noted that the competent Public Prosecutor’s Office has, within the framework of its legal powers, opened judicial investigations into the various acts and facts related to these events, with the aim of determining all the circumstances, uncovering responsibilities, and applying the legal consequences in accordance with the provisions of the law.

While renewing its affirmation that the management of the migration phenomenon can only take place within the framework of a comprehensive approach based on shared responsibility, effective solidarity, and burden-sharing, the Ministry of the Interior stresses that the Kingdom of Morocco will remain, as its partners have always known it, a reliable and responsible partner, committed to strengthening international cooperation and coordination in the field of combating irregular migration and human trafficking. At the same time, it will spare no effort in taking all necessary measures to protect public order, safeguard border security, and ensure the safety of persons and property, within the framework of the rule of law and respect for the Kingdom’s national and international commitments."

text:
You don’t need to be a rocket scientist to figure out that no one in this generation, your children’s generation, your grandchildren’s generation or great grandchildren’s generation will live on another planet. 

It’s just not logically viable. 

The obstacles aren’t just technological, they’re economic and logistical. Mars offers no obvious abundance of resources that justifies relocating civilization there, and recreating even a fraction of Earth’s infrastructure would come at an astronomical cost. In fact, to build anything close to what we’ve already built on planet Earth will cost at least 1 billion times more to do on Mars.

To break it down for you further here are the valuable assets Mars has:

•  Significant water ice, especially near the poles and beneath the surface. Water can be converted into drinking water, oxygen, and hydrogen fuel.

• Mars is rich in iron oxide (rust), which gives the planet its red color. Iron could potentially be used to manufacture steel.
Martian rocks contain silicon, which could be used to produce glass, ceramics, and potentially solar cells.

• Mars contains aluminum, an important material for lightweight construction.

• Magnesium is present and could be used in metal alloys and manufacturing.

• Titanium has been detected in Martian basalt and could be valuable for aerospace and structural applications.

• Mars contains sulfur, which could be be used in industrial processes and fertilizer production.

• Calcium is present and could be used to make cement and other construction materials.

•Mars’ atmosphere is approximately 95% carbon dioxide (CO₂), which could be converted into oxygen, methane fuel, and other useful products for a Mars settlement.

• Scientists believe Mars may contain rare earth elements, but there is currently no evidence of economically recoverable deposits.

 There is currently no evidence that Mars possesses resources valuable enough to justify exporting them to Earth. And with current or foreseeable technology, the cost of mining and transporting materials from Mars would far exceed their market value on Earth.

In fact, most experts believe Martian resources would primarily be used in situ (on Mars) to support any future settlement, rather than being exported back to Earth.

Wake up people. It just isn’t happening. And you should be thankful. Now go and make sure planet Earth is healthy. You’re welcome.

text:
Bloomberg’s funniest mistake is imagining that China is 1980s Japan and today’s EU is the United States.

It is neither.

China is not an export-dependent client economy waiting for a foreign master to rewrite its industrial policy. Exports now account for a far smaller share of China’s GDP than during the pre-2008 peak, while China produces nearly one-third of global manufacturing output.

Yet Bloomberg’s argument is:

Europe lost industrial competitiveness, therefore China must reduce production.
Europe accumulated a trade deficit, therefore China must sacrifice its own industries.
Europe threatens protectionism, therefore Beijing must offer “goodwill.”

What goodwill did the United States offer when it produced roughly half of the world’s manufactured goods after World War II?

Nobody called American industrial dominance “overcapacity.”
Nobody demanded that Washington dismantle its factories to protect weaker competitors.

Western production was called strength.
Chinese production is called damage.

This has never been about capacity.
It is about who is permitted to possess it.

Europe hollowed out its own industrial base, subordinated its energy and foreign policy to Washington, and spent decades worshipping neoliberalism. Now it wants China to pay the funeral expenses.

China may lose sales in a trade rupture.
Europe will lose access to the industrial ecosystem it failed to build and can no longer cheaply replace.

China is not Japan.
Brussels is not Washington.

And European decline is not a Chinese policy obligation.

And Johnson's point isn't that Trump got new intel. It's that there was no new intel. Iran didn't beg, didn't blink, didn't offer anything. Which means whatever changed Trump's mind, it wasn't Iran.

Iran now knows it controls the Strait, and there's nothing the U.S. can do about it short of accepting Iran's terms. A user fee, basically, like a cover charge at the door. 

Johnson doesn't think that's some far-off outcome, but already the deal on the table.

He says Iran now considers the U.S. so politically compromised heading into the midterms that they're weighing preemptive strikes even without a new American attack. That's a different war than the one everyone's been covering.

If Iran's already convinced Washington is too weak and too distracted to enforce a red line, does it matter what Trump decides next?
