text:
Parents of the Classes of 2027 and 2029, Here’s What You Need to Know About the Future of NCAA Division I Athletics
College sports at the Power 4 level is changing faster than at any point in decades. If your son or daughter is a rising junior or sophomore (or about to enter that window), the landscape they will recruit into looks different from the one current seniors are navigating.
What’s happening financially
Top athletic departments face permanent higher costs: direct revenue sharing with athletes, NIL support, facilities, and coaching. Many are turning to outside capital.
•  LSU is reportedly closing a deal for $100M+ upfront in exchange for a share of future media rights.
•  Utah already completed the first major single-school private equity partnership and created a commercial company around its athletics business.
•  The Big 12 struck a private capital partnership that gives the conference and its schools access to significant capital without giving up ownership.
This is not fringe activity. It is becoming a competitive necessity for programs that want to stay at the highest level. Money is flowing more heavily toward football (and to a lesser extent men’s basketball) media rights and commercial assets.
What’s happening in Washington
Congress is advancing the bipartisan Protect College Sports Act. The goal is national rules on NIL, transfers, eligibility, and revenue sharing, plus limited antitrust protection so schools and conferences can enforce standards. It also includes language intended to protect women’s sports and Olympic/non-revenue sports from being cut. The bill has White House support and recent backing from major conferences, though final passage and exact language are still moving.
What this means for your athlete
1.  The gap between the top and everyone else will likely widen. Programs with strong media rights and new capital will have more resources for facilities, staffing, NIL support, and recruiting. Mid-majors and lower-resource Power 4 schools will feel more pressure.
2.  Football drives the money. Non-revenue sports (including baseball, softball, soccer, track, etc.) will still exist at most schools, and federal legislation is trying to protect them. But internal prioritization inside athletic departments will follow the revenue. Ask specific questions about how each program funds its non-football sports long-term.
3.  Academics and the “right fit” matter more, not less. The professionalization of the top end makes the high-academic pathway and developmental programs even more valuable for many athletes. Not every player needs (or will get) the highest-dollar Power 4 offer. Strong academic institutions that treat athletics as part of the educational experience remain excellent options and often provide better long-term outcomes.
4.  Transparency and control questions are real. When outside investors have a claim on future media revenue, incentives can shift. Good programs will still prioritize the student-athlete experience, but parents should ask: Who ultimately controls decisions on coaching, facilities, and sport sponsorship?
5.  Recruiting timeline and evaluation stay critical. The 2027 and 2029 classes will still be evaluated on talent, character, academics, and projected development. The difference is that the financial resources available to programs will vary more widely. Visit campuses, talk to current athletes and parents in the specific sport, and look at roster continuity and academic support — not just the newest facility renderings.
Bottom line for parents
The old model is gone. Direct athlete compensation and outside capital are here. Federal legislation is trying to put guardrails around the chaos. Your job is the same as it has always been, just with more variables: find the place where your child can develop as an athlete and a student, graduate on time, and leave with options. The loudest money is not always the best long-term fit.
Stay informed, ask hard questions !

text:
Who is paying a heavy price? China? It is Panama itself.

A year ago, the Mulino administration was painting a grand vision, planning to transform the ports at both ends of the canal into a global logistics hub. However, the chain reaction following the ousting of the Chinese port operator is now exacting a heavy toll on this Central American nation.

Panama’s initial decision was driven by clear geopolitical calculations: the hope that distancing itself from the major Eastern power would secure Washington's long-term favor and thereby increase its own leverage in canal affairs. But what is the situation now?

Following a visit to Beijing by a Panamanian delegation last month, Panama’s Acting Foreign Minister (Deputy Foreign Minister) Hoyos confirmed that they are seeking China's understanding to reach an agreement on extending the maritime shipping pact; however, China has yet to formally approve the agreement.

Furthermore, safety inspections on Panama-flagged vessels at Chinese ports—which include seven of the world's top ten ports—have intensified significantly. Since March of this year, the number of Panama-flagged ships detained in Chinese ports has risen steadily, triggering a wave of shipowners switching flags; a large number of vessels have re-registered under flags such as Liberia or the Marshall Islands. Data from Clarksons Research indicates that Panama’s share of the global fleet has shrunk by 3.3% this year, marking a significant loss among major flag states.

Once credibility is damaged, repairing it is no overnight task. The fallout from the change in port ownership has extended beyond just ship registration, creating a combined impact through both financial and legal pressures. Regarding the financial chain, relevant Chinese authorities communicated their concerns to the international shipping giant that took over the port operations following the incident. Meanwhile, negotiations for new Chinese investments in Panama have largely stalled, and customs clearance efficiency for bilateral agricultural trade has declined.

The Panamanian government had originally hoped that ousting the Chinese firm would quickly pave the way for European and American capital to fill the void. The reality, however, is that while new backers have yet to materialize, the confidence of existing clients has already been shaken. Various projects previously planned under the "Belt and Road" cooperation framework—such as port expansions and logistics parks—are currently frozen, with stakeholders adopting a "wait-and-see" approach. Another layer of pressure stems from the legal front: the original port operator, CK Hutchison, has formally initiated international arbitration proceedings, seeking damages of up to approximately $2 billion from the Panamanian side. This legal battle is expected to drag on for years; regardless of the outcome, the ultimate financial burden will likely fall upon Panama's public treasury.

Where, then, is the reliability of allies? Washington has repeatedly pushed—and even pressured—Panama to take action regarding the port issue, loudly proclaiming a need to prevent other nations from "controlling" the canal. Yet, when Panama faced the resulting backlash, U.S. expressions of support proved hollow and ineffective. While U.S. officials accused the major Eastern power of "weaponizing port state control," such accusations lack substantive grounding within international maritime rules and failed to offer Panama any tangible protection against risk.

A more profound impact lies in the precedent set regarding the spirit of international contracts. By forcibly altering a commercial contract that had been in effect for nearly three decades—citing political reasons—Panama has effectively heightened the political risk associated with long-term concession agreements across Latin America. Any nation signing similar agreements in the future will now be compelled to re-evaluate the stability and enforceability of such contracts.

text:
Tucked inside a New Hampshire office park, Phoenix Tailings uses electricity to extract critical minerals from mining waste. These minerals are vital for key U.S. weapons systems, including missiles currently used in the Iran war.

This process could help the U.S. reduce its reliance on China for processing these materials. The Trump administration is pushing for more domestic production, but building a new factory will take up to a year and a half.

Phoenix Tailings recently secured a $500 million Pentagon loan to expand its operations. The company, which began as a backyard lab eight years ago, is the latest to receive such government support.

The urgency for these minerals has increased as the Iran conflict depletes stockpiles of munitions like Tomahawk missiles and THAAD interceptors. Meanwhile, the White House is demanding faster production and banning military contractors from sourcing critical minerals from China.

Anthony Balladon, co-founder of Phoenix Tailings, acknowledged the challenge of replenishing stocks and scaling up production within the required timeframe. The company is actively working to boost its capacity.

While the U.S. accelerates efforts to build domestic supplies independent of China, establishing new mines and scaling production across the industry will take years. Extracting minerals from existing mine waste offers a stopgap, though it will require multiple companies to meet growing demand.

Phoenix Tailings uses raw materials from traditional mining waste, recycled magnets, and disk drives. The company, based in Woburn, Massachusetts, plans to build a larger facility to supply the defense, aerospace, and automotive industries.

Balladon refers to this planned expansion as the "freedom facility," designed to ensure the Western Hemisphere is free from Chinese influence in the rare-earth sector.

At their current facility, technicians in hazmat suits oversee a chemical process that uses electricity to remove oxygen, producing a metal used for extremely strong permanent magnets. These magnets are crucial for fighter jets, missiles, radar systems, and drones.

Critical minerals play an essential role in defense systems; a $150 million weapon is useless without $20,000 worth of these materials, according to Balladon.

The defense sector heavily relies on samarium, needing 50 to 100 tons annually, yet U.S. capacity is currently very limited. Phoenix Tailings is one of the few companies producing this metal, currently making about 200 kilograms a year. They aim to scale to 5 tons soon and reach a 120-ton capacity by next year or 2028.

Other U.S. magnet makers are also seeking alternatives to China. Arnold Magnetic Technologies, for instance, now sources samarium from an abandoned mining site in La Rochelle, France. Solvay, the company processing the French dirt, restarted operations after China weaponized its near-monopoly during a trade war.

For Arnold Magnetic Technologies, paying more for Solvay’s samarium is manageable since it represents a small portion of a weapon system's total cost. The surge in magnet demand has also benefited the company.

However, concerns remain regarding other minerals, like tungsten, where China controls roughly 80% of the global mine supply. A Pentagon deadline of Jan. 1, 2027, has raised fears that the U.S. won't be ready to operate without China-sourced tungsten.

Until domestic production increases, the Pentagon will have to rely on existing inventories, recycling, and limited non-China sources.

The ongoing Iran war has further depleted U.S. military stockpiles, raising concerns about potential diminished firepower in a future conflict with China. A recent analysis warned it could take at least three years to replenish supplies of certain interceptors.

President Trump recently issued an executive order requiring that critical materials for military equipment be sourced domestically or from allied nations.

Major defense contractors like Lockheed Martin say they are continuously assessing their global supply chains to ensure access to these critical materials.

Despite the challenges, Balladon expressed confidence that U.S. companies can achieve these goals with the right support and industry partnerships.

text:
That's a weak, fluff letter.    It looks like it could have been written by the colleges themselves. 

Here's a far better letter:  

Send this letter, and we'll be impressed. =================================  

from: alan@studentloanjustice.org to:  alan_garber@harvard.edu cc: lawrence_summers@harvard.edu date:  Apr 14, 2026, 2:25 PM  subject:  Offer to pay for the return of bankruptcy rights to student loans.  

Alan,  I am the nation’s first student loan activist, wrote the first published book to be critical of the federal student loan program (The Student Loan Scam, Beacon Press), and have pursued student loan justice for 21 years. My grassroots group now has 1.4 million members across the country.  

Alan: I am disgusted by the collective failure of college presidents in this country to address the unprecedented removal of constitutional bankruptcy rights from student loans. Please don’t pretend to be unaware of this shocking usurpation of the citizens' rights. We both know that all college heads- including you- are very aware of it.   

You may NOT be aware that uniform bankruptcy rights were called for in the Constitution (ahead of every right in the Bill of Rights) as a direct result of a debtor’s rebellion that happened in Western Massachusetts shortly after The Revolutionary War, but it’s true.  Today, 37 of the 43 million federal student loan borrowers are hopelessly underwater on their predatory college debt- It has become a destabilizing, national threat.  

Alan: I urge you strongly to publicly call for the return of standard bankruptcy rights to student loans, and also that the wealthiest colleges in the nation (whose cumulative endowments now approach $1 Trillion in value) pay at least half the cost of the $6 Billion/year in discharges that will result.  

This is the solution that will be most beneficial, and least costly to all parties involved.   It is a very small price to pay considering the alternatives, which could well involve the evaporation of federal loan support for all the colleges, civil unrest, and other horribles one might imagine when the pitchforks and the torches come out.  

These have actually already begun, See the story of Justin Mohn, or the Nelson family of Broken Arrow, Oklahoma for two recent examples (I will paste graphics below).  

Like it or not, Alan.  Fair or unfair, Harvard is the face of the Academy, and the citizens’ rage against this national threatening loan scam will be increasingly- and justly- turned against the colleges who have profited so immensely from it, with Harvard being chief (and most visible) among them.  

I know this is the least-cost, most stabilizing solution available. I also see the coming storm. I strongly urge you to take this very good advice. Larry Summers has recently called for the return of bankruptcy rights to the loans.  You need to make a similar call while in office, not after you leave. I am cc’ing this letter to him.  I consider this letter confidential.  

Come July, if I hear nothing from you and you take no noticeable, public action toward the end I suggest, I will reconsider that status.  I hope to hear from you in a good-faithed, constructive way.    

I am at your beck and call should you require an expert briefing.  

Godspeed-  Alan Collinge  alan@studentloanjustice.org  (202) 594-1120

text:
She was just ten years old when a stranger walked up to her on the street in broad daylight and cut her hair. Her crime was simple: too many strands of hair were slipping out from under her hijab.

When she went to the police for help, they offered no justice. Instead, they told the young girl that it was her own fault.

That little girl was already a chess prodigy in Iran. 

At seven years old, she had won her very first national championship, proudly receiving her trophy while wearing a princess dress and a tiara. As she grew into her teenage years, her incredible talent on the board only shone brighter. 

Dorsa Derakhshani went on to win the Asian Youth Chess Championship three times and earned the prestigious titles of Woman Grandmaster and International Master.

Yet, her brilliant mind could not protect her from a strict system that cared more about enforcing a piece of clothing than celebrating her intellect. Dorsa lived under constant surveillance and suffocating rules, well aware that one small misstep could lead to arrest or worse. Looking back on her childhood, she often reflects, "The blame is always put on the woman."

The turning point came in 2017. Dorsa traveled to Gibraltar to compete in an international tournament, choosing to play without wearing a hijab. 

The reaction from her homeland was swift and harsh. At eighteen years old, the Iranian Chess Federation banned her from the national team. Her career in her home country was stripped away simply because she chose to play the game with her hair uncovered.

Refusing to let this setback destroy her spirit, Dorsa made a life-altering decision. 

At nineteen, she packed everything she owned into six suitcases, took her passport, and left her homeland behind. She landed at Saint Louis University in the United States after earning a full chess scholarship. 

She was completely alone in a foreign country, far from her family and without any safety net.

The pressure was immense, and the fear of failure weighed heavily on her mind. 

"If I fail at university, no one will take care of me," she remembered thinking during those uncertain first months.

She did not fail. 

Instead, she built an extraordinary new chapter for herself. 

Today, Dorsa is pursuing her medical degree at the University of Missouri while continuing to compete on the university chess team. She plans to use the same steady, strategic hands that once moved chess pieces across a board to perform operations and save lives as a surgeon.

The pain of leaving her roots behind remains real, and she misses Iran deeply. However, she understands the dangerous reality of returning under the current government. 

"I have love for my country, but I will not return until the regime has changed," she shares softly. "If I go back, they will put me in prison somewhere, and no one will ever hear from me again."

Dorsa’s journey from a young girl punished for showing her hair to an inspiring future surgeon proves that true strength comes from standing firm in who you are. 

She stepped away from a life of restrictions to create a future defined by freedom, purpose, and unconditional compassion. 

Dorsa once used her mind to win chess matches; now, she is using it to heal people. Though she remains far from the country she loves, she has created a peaceful and meaningful life on her own terms. 

She reminds us that true victory isn't about defeating an opponent—it's about holding onto your freedom, your dignity, and your dreams.

text:
🚨 SCAM WARNING 🚨

at 1:16am i asked a recruiter how to verify he was real.

he said, i can send message from official account. or maybe just follow you?

he offered to prove himself using the account i was asking about. he followed me, i followed back, nothing was verified, and it felt like something had been.

he had come into my x dms that night, recruiting for content and marketing at a podcast company. min-ji, head of scouting at a vc called theforms. i don't open links in x dms, a shortened calendly link caught me once and i only worked out where it went afterwards, so i moved him to telegram where i can read a full url before i touch it.

theforms[dot]ventures has a real site. team page, headshot, lee min-ji, navy suit, bio about spotting founders long before the market catches up, previously at okx ventures. under the photo, two icons, x and telegram, both pointing back at the account messaging me. the loop closes on itself and never touches anything outside it.

the bio never names one company he found. in venture, deals are the entire cv.

then i scrolled, and the firm had two heads of scouting. one woman, one man, same title, same page. nobody writes that by hand. you get a duplicate like that when profiles are generated in bulk and dropped on a template without anyone reading the output, which is also how a man ends up carrying a woman's name.

i kept going because i wanted to see the link.

he took my details, then said once i join the workspace we can discuss compensation. that's the lever. the money sits behind one more door, and the door needs you to walk through it.

then it came. sites[dot]google[dot]com/view/zbo-iyji-hex/workspace, an access code, hak-hjak-80hk-9j1k, a contact address at web3blockwave[dot]info.

i didn't open it, and i didn't need to. google workspace does not live at sites[dot]google[dot]com/view/. that's the free site builder anyone can spin up in two minutes, and the google in front buys trust the page never earned. no real invite is gated behind a code you type into a page. the code is theatre, it makes an empty room feel locked. even the slug is working, zbo-iyji-hex reads as a meet code at a glance.

pages like that run clickfix. an invented error, session expired, certificate expired, then instructions to fix it, open your terminal and paste this. the page already wrote the command into your clipboard while the error held your eyes. nothing downloads, so nothing gets scanned, you type it in yourself, and when it asks for your password that's not your wallet, that's keychain, session cookies, ssh keys, everything. north korean crews built a version of this aimed specifically at people who work in crypto.

fake vc firms aren't new, fortune documented two of them running this exact play in 2016. what's new is the price. domain, thirty dollars. bios, free and generated, which is why there are two of the same job. headshots, free. team page, one afternoon. the first thing in that chain that costs real money is a workspace that actually works, and they never had one.

so stop asking whether something looks real. looking real is free now, it tells you nothing. ask what the first expensive thing is, and go check whether it exists.

and don't memorise my version. mine came as a job. yours might come as a podcast booking, a partnership, a grant, a bug bounty, an airdrop, an investor intro. the story is whatever gets you to move. the link never changes.

three things worth keeping.

- no site needs your terminal. not google, not microsoft, not your bank, there is no legitimate version of that instruction.

- verification only counts through a channel they didn't hand you.

- if the money sits behind a link, the link is the product.

it will keep getting better than this. we'll keep hunting them down. it could be any account that messages you next, so stay safe out there.

text:
Southpaw Lou Brouillard (left), the former Welterweight Champion, wins a 10-round split decision over Jimmy McLarnin (right), on August 4, 1932, at Yankee Stadium.

The referee and one judge voted for Brouillard, the other judge for McLarnin, all three scoring it 6-4 in rounds. 

The New York Times reported that Brouillard "pounded and battered McLarnin through ten rounds of primitive fighting to gain a decision that met with the undivided support of the onlookers."

In unofficial scoring, the Brooklyn Times Union also scored it clearly for Brouillard. The New York Daily News scored it 5-4-1 for McLarnin. The Brooklyn Daily Eagle scored it 6-3-1 for Brouillard. The Brooklyn Citizen gave seven rounds to Brouillard.

Brouillard had won the title from Young Jack Thompson in October of 1931 but lost it in his first defense, as had become somewhat of a tradition in the welterweight division by this point, to Jackie Fields in January of 1932.

McLarnin, a future two-time Welterweight Champion, would respond to this loss with a three fight winning streak that culminated in his May of 1933 1st-round TKO of Young Corbett III to capture the Welterweight Title for the first time.

His first reign would be short-lived as he would lose the title, one year later, to Barney Ross via 15-round split decision at "The Graveyard of Champions" (The MSG Bowl in Long Island City, New York); where no champion in any weight class would ever sucessfully defend his title.

Also going on during this era was what some sportswriters of the day referred to as "The Jinx of the Welterweight Title", as that belt would change hands an incredible twelve times in five years; for many years during the 20th Century, reporters would comment on the so-called jinx that each Welterweight World Champion faced every time he defended his title for the first time. 

Young Corbett III, for example, reportedly was the seventh welterweight champion in succession to lose possession of the title in defending it for the first time. 

His successor, McLarnin, also lost the title in his first defense, to Barney Ross. Then Ross lost his first defense to McLarnin, who in turn once again lost the welter title back to Ross on his first defense, after having won the title from Ross. (By then the papers were saying this was the 12th time the jinx had continued. Somewhere along the line the total number had become distorted.) 

It would take the great Henry Armstrong to end this jinx. 

McLarnin, as stated above, would regain the title from Ross, via another split decision, and then lose it again in his first defense to Ross.

McLarnin would split two ten-round decisions with Tony Canzoneri following his loss of the title a second time and, then, retire after posting a 10-round decsion win over Lou Ambers in November of 1936 in his final career bout.

Jimmy McLarnin, the "Belfast Spider", 55-11-3 with 21 KO wins, has been referred to as the greatest Irish boxer of all time.

In 1996 Ring Magazine voted McLarnin the fifth-greatest welterweight of all time.

Despite many offers, after winning his final two bouts over excellent fighters in Tony Canzoneri and Lou Ambers, Jimmy McLarnin would never return to the ring.

text:
Man arrested for gathering scrap. Assaulted by police, leads to 1 million dollar lawsuit.

​A scrap metal misunderstanding turned into a major internal investigation and a $1 million federal lawsuit after Eugene Police officers took 41-year-old Jehoshaphat Commandest into custody in Oregon.
​
Police responded to a property on River Road following a report of unauthorized material removal from a demolition site. While the property owner reported the activity, Commandest had been informed by a neighbor—who was previously invited to clear the site—that he could collect scrap boards and metal.

When officers arrived, Commandest explained he believed the site was abandoned and offered to return everything immediately.

Although Commandest cooperated and allowed officers to place him in handcuffs without resistance, the situation escalated rapidly as Officers Stephen Lahm and Lindsey Collier escorted him to the patrol vehicle.

Dashcam footage shows an altercation while Commandest was restrained against the hood of the cruiser, including the use of a Taser.
​
​The resisting arrest charge against Commandest was dismissed, and he later resolved the trespass charge in December 2025.

​A formal complaint led to an investigation by the Eugene Police Auditor’s Office, which sustained findings that Officer Lahm’s use of force violated department policy.

​Officer Lahm resigned from the Eugene Police Department and was placed under state professional-standards review.

​ In July 2026, Commandest filed a federal lawsuit against the city, the department, and the involved officers alleging excessive force, negligence, and severe physical injuries resulting from the incident in the amount of 1 million dollars.

text:
Leo Frank Trial Anniversary: 

State’s Case Against Leo Frank As It Stands After Week’s Testimony Is Shown Here

Photo-diagram of court room in old city hall building, where Leo M. Frank, superintendent of the National Pencil factory, is on trial for his life charged with the murder of Mary Phagan. Although the available seats are taken soon after court convenes, the crowd waits without all day for some weary spectator to give up a seat. On the second floor the many witnesses await their turn for a grueling examination by attorneys on either side.

Atlanta Journal

August 3rd, 1913

Most Important Points State Sought to Prove Are That Mary Phagan Was Killed Shortly After Entering Factory—That Crime Was on Second Floor, and That Frank Was Not in His Office at the Time He Saw He Gave Her the Pay Envelope

An entire week has been given over to the trial of Leo M. Frank, charged with the murder of Mary Phagan, and so far the state has not shown or attempted to show any direct connection on the part of the defendant with the crime. Solicitor Dorsey has worked systematically to weave a chain of circumstantial evidence about Frank.

Those who have watched the progress of the trial day by day are impressed with the fact that he has endeavored by the introduction of circumstantial evidence to pave the way for the testimony of James Conley, the negro sweeper, who will be the climax witness for the state and upon whose evidence the case against Frank will largely stand or fall.

The state swore but twenty-six witnesses when the trial began Monday afternoon, but up to date it has called thirty and the indications are that still others are to be put upon the stand. The defense has not put up a single witness and can not do so until the state rests its case. However, Attorneys Rosser and Arnold, counsel for Frank, have administered severe cross-examinations to the more material of the state's witnesses and in many instances have succeeded in minimizing the evidence given by them on their direct examination.

The state has sought to show by its witnesses:

First. That Mary Phagan was murdered within an hour after she left her home just before noon on April 26 to go to the pencil factory for her pay.

Second. That she was rendered unconscious by a blow upon the back of the head and that she died from strangulation.

Third. That she was murdered on the second or office floor of the factory and that her body was taken to the basement on the elevator.

Fourth. That no one saw her enter or leave the factory and that Frank was the only person who saw her while she was there.

Fifth. That at the exact hour Frank has stated that the girl came into his office he was himself absent from the office, although he claims not have left it from about 11 o'clock until 12:30 and 1 o'clock.

Sixth. That the girl was not criminally assaulted, although she had suffered some kind of violence five or ten minutes before her death.

Seventh. That about 1 o'clock, several minutes after the murder was committed, a negro was seen sitting on a box on the first floor near the foot of the stairs.

Eighth. That on Sunday morning Frank was very nervous and excited and that he would not look upon the face of the dead girl when he was taken to the undertaking establishment.

DR. HARRIS' TESTIMONY.

The most significant evidence so far offered by the state was the testimony of Dr. H. F. Harris, secretary of the state board of health, and Monteen Stover, a fourteen-year-old girl, who formerly worked at the pencil factory.

Dr. Harris made a post-mortem examination on the body of Mary Phagan a few days after her death. He testified that she had undoubtedly died from strangulation produced by the tightly-drawn cord around her neck; that the blow on the back of the head undoubtedly rendered her unconscious; that she had died within from a half to three-quarters of an hour after having eaten some cabbage and bread; that she had not been criminally assaulted but that she had suffered some kind of violence between five and ten minutes before death.

Dr. Harris explained that the cord had left a deep indentation in the girl's neck which was badly contused and swollen; that the blow on the back of the head had caused a slight hemorrhage beneath the skull, but not sufficient to kill; that he had examined the contents of the stomach and found pieces of cabbage and bread which were almost totally undigested; that his examination of the organs of the body convinced him that no criminal assault had been made upon the child, but that the dilated and inflamed blood vessels satisfied him that external violence had been committed, and that the condition of the inflammation caused him to believe it occurred not more than ten minutes before her death.

A bottle containing the undigested cabbage taken from Mary Phagan's stomach was tendered by Dr. Harris, as were two other bottles containing partially digested cabbage, which he said he had taken from the stomachs of two healthy normal men an hour after they had eaten it.

Dr. Harris was too ill to finish his testimony, and the defense had no opportunity to cross-examine him. He will doubtless be recalled this week.

MONTEEN STOVER'S EVIDENCE.

Monteen Stover testified that she went to the pencil factory for her pay at 12:05 o'clock on Saturday, April 27; that she stepped into the outer office where she could have a good view of Frank's private office; that she saw no one in either office; that she sat on a bench outside the office until 12:10, when she went back home.

A statement made by Frank to the detectives was read to the jury. In it Frank says Mary Phagan came to his office about 12:05 or 12:10; that he gave her her pay envelope and that she then went out.

In their cross-examination of several witnesses Attorneys Rosser and Arnold brought out the fact that it would be almost impossible for a person to see into Frank's private office from the outer office when the safe door was open; that the door was so large that it practically cut off all view into the inner office. It is presumed that the defense will later attempt to show that the safe door was open at the hour the Stover girl says she looked into Frank's office.

DR. J. W. HURT.

The testimony of Dr. J. W. Hurt, the coroner's physician who performed the autopsy on Mary Phagan's body, Sunday morning following the murder, differed in several important particulars from that of Dr. Harris in his testimony. He agreed with Dr. Harris that the girl came to her death by strangulation, but admitted on cross-examination that the only accurate way to prove this was by an examination of the lungs, which he had not made. He also agreed that the blow on the head was delivered before death and produced unconsciousness, but admitted on cross-examination that such blows frequently result in concussion of the brain and in death.

Dr. Hurt corroborated Dr. Harris in the latter's statement that the girl had not been criminally assaulted, but differed with him as to her having undergone external violence. Dr. Hurt says he never found any indications of violence and that the dilated and inflamed blood vessels could have resulted from natural causes.

He would not attempt to estimate how long the cabbage had been in the stomach, but admitted that mastication had a great deal to do with digestion and that some persons digested food sooner than others.

MRS. J. W. COLEMAN.

Mrs. J. W. Coleman, mother of Mary, testified that the girl left her home at 11:45 to go to the factory, and just prior to leaving she partook of a meal consisting of cabbage and bread.

Attorney Rosser developed from Mrs. Coleman that it was two blocks to the car line from her home and that she had no way of knowing how soon Mary caught a car.

George Epps, a newsboy, swore that he boarded the car with the girl at Olive street and Bellwood avenue at 10 minutes to 12 and that they left the car at Marietta and Forsyth streets about 12:10. He was not sure of the latter time, as he judged it by the sun. The girl, he said, walked on across the Forsyth street viaduct toward the factory, two blocks away.

The presence of blood spots on the second floor of the factory, near the girl's dressing room was testified to by R. P. Barrett, a machinist at the factory; Mell Stanford, another factory employe, Detectives Starnes and Black, Mrs. George W. Jefferson, also a factory employe, and Chief Beavers. Dr. Claude A. Smith, city bacteriologist and chemist, testified that he had made an analysis of the stain upon chips taken from the floor and found that it was blood.

Barrett swore that he had found hair upon the handle of his turning lathe in the metal room; that it was not there Friday when he stopped work, and that no girls worked in the factory on Saturday. He also testified to having found a pay envelope under Mary Phagan's machine.

Attorneys Rosser and Arnold brought out from a number of witnesses that paint spots, both red and dark, could be found in all parts of the factory and that it was not an uncommon thing to find blood spots around the women's dressing rooms and toilets of factories where large numbers of women were employed.

WHAT DARLEY SAID.

One of the State's witnesses, N. V. Darley, general manager of the pencil factory, stated on cross-examination that about 175 pay envelopes were scattered over the factory on every pay day, and that lengths of cord, similar to that found around Mary Phagan's neck, could also be found all over the factory; that it was frequently carried to the basement in the trash. He declared further that order blanks and tablet paper of the character upon which the notes found by the body were written, could be picked up in all parts of the factory, and that pencils were everywhere plentiful.

Both Darley and E. F. Holloway, the day watchman, testified that the switch box on the elevator was unlocked on Sunday morning, and Holloway recalled under cross-examination that he had left it unlocked the day before.

Mrs. J. Arthur White stated that she was at the pencil factory from 12:30 to about 1 o'clock on the day of the murder and that as she walked down the stairs to leave she saw a negro sitting on a box on the first floor a few feet from the staircase.

In his affidavit Conley claims that it was just before 1 o'clock that Frank called him up to aid in disposing of the body. Conley's statement has not yet been produced in court.

FRANK'S NERVOUSNESS.

Among the witnesses who swore that Frank was very nervous on Sunday morning when he was brought to the factory were Detective John Black, Detective J. N. Starnes, W. W. Rogers, a bailiff, and Darley.

Upon cross-examination practically all of these witnesses admitted that they had never seen Frank before and knew nothing about his natural demeanor. Some of them said he was not very much more nervous than others at the factory that Sunday, and Darley declared that on two former occasions he had seen Frank fully as nervous and excited—once just after he had seen a child run over by a street car and once after Frank and a pencil factory official had quarreled.

Detectives Black and Rogers did not think that Frank had looked upon the dead girl's face when taken to the undertaking establishment, but neither would swear positively that he had not. Black admitted that Frank was between him and the body and that he had seen the face.

Pinkerton Detective Harry Scott testified that Frank had told him that he had not left his office from the time he returned from Montag Bros., about 11 o'clock, until about 1 o'clock, when he went upstairs to tell Mrs. White that he was going to lunch and lock the front door, and that she had better leave if she wished to get out before he returned at 3 o'clock.

THE STATE'S WITNESSES.

A list of the witnesses so far introduced by the state follows: Mrs. J. W. Coleman, mother of Mary Phagan; George Epps, a newsboy; Newt Lee, the negro night watchman at the factory; Police Sergeant L. S. Dobbs, who found the notes in the basement beside the body; Detective J. N. Starnes, W. W. Rogers, a bailiff; Miss Grace Hix, an employe at the factory, who identified the dead girl; Detective John Black, J. M. Gantt, former ship[p]ing clerk at the factory, who testified that Frank was nervous and jumped when he encountered him at the factory door about 6 o'clock the day of the murder; Pinkerton Detective Harry Scott, Miss Monteen Sttover [sic], R. P. Barrett, Mell Stanford, Mrs. George W. Jefferson, who saw the blood on the metal room floor and who swore no paints were ever kept in the metal room; Detective B. B. Haslett, who said he saw Frank in his office on Monday morning and that he was nervously pacing back and forth; William A. Gheesling, the undertaker, who embalmed the body; Dr. Claude A. Smith, E. F. Holloway, Mrs. J. Arthur White, N. V. Darley, Call Officer W. F. Anderson, who responded to Newt Lee's call for thhe [sic] police to come to the factory Sunday morning amout [sic] 3 o'clock; Dr. H. F. Harris, G. C. Febuary, stenographer tto [sic] Chief Lanford, who identified a statement made by Frank to the chief; Albert McKnight, husband of the cook at the Frank home, who swore Frank reached his home on the day of the murder about 1:30, remained but a few minutes and left without eating luncheon; Helen Ferguson, who testified that she asked Frank for Mary Phagan's pay on the Friday before the murder, but that he didn't give it to her; Detective R. L. Waggoner, who rode to police station in the automobile with Frank on Tuesday following the murder and who swore he was nervous; Dr. J. W. Hurt, Police Chief James L. Beavers and Patrolman Lassiter, who with some of the other officers, swore that he saw a trail in the basement, leading from the elevator to the body which indicated that the dead girl had been dragged.

text:
You step into the palengke with a bayong tucked under your arm. The fish goes in first, followed by leafy vegetables, a few kilos of rice, ripe mangoes, and fresh bread. The bag stretches but never tears. 

When you get home, you rinse it, leave it under the sun to dry, and use the same bag again on your next market trip. No pile of crumpled plastic bags. No overflowing trash bin. Just one sturdy bag doing what it has always done.

Today, that simple routine has become surprisingly rare.

The humble bayong is more than just a nostalgic symbol of old-fashioned market days. It is one of the most practical and sustainable alternatives to single-use plastic bags ever developed. Generations of Filipinos practiced a zero-waste lifestyle without even realizing it, relying on woven bags made from buri, pandan, abaca, or rattan for everyday shopping.

Every time someone chooses a bayong over a disposable plastic bag, they prevent another piece of plastic from entering the waste stream. A typical plastic shopping bag may be used for only a few minutes before being discarded, yet it can remain in the environment for centuries. In contrast, one sturdy bayong can serve its owner for years, replacing hundreds—if not thousands—of disposable bags over its lifetime.

That difference matters.

Plastic bags do not simply disappear after they are thrown away. They eventually break down into tiny microplastics that contaminate soil, rivers, and oceans, where they can be ingested by fish, wildlife, and ultimately humans. Traditional bayongs, on the other hand, are made from natural plant fibers that decompose without leaving behind toxic residues.

The bayong also proves that sustainability does not have to sacrifice durability. Designed for busy market days, it can carry kilos of vegetables, rice, fish, meat, and fruits without easily tearing. While a plastic bag often gives way under heavy weight, a properly woven bayong becomes even more dependable with regular use.

Another advantage is its circular life cycle. Traditional bayongs are crafted from renewable materials harvested locally, often by artisans using weaving techniques passed down through generations. Their production requires far less energy than manufacturing plastic bags, which depend on fossil fuels and industrial processing. When a woven bayong finally reaches the end of its useful life, it naturally decomposes instead of remaining in landfills for generations.

Even maintenance is simple. A bayong can be rinsed after carrying fish or meat, dried under the sun, and used again. Instead of reaching for fresh plastic bags every shopping trip, one reusable bag can safely serve countless visits to the market.

Modern versions have also emerged. Across many public markets, woven plastic-strip bayongs have become increasingly common. While these are not biodegradable, their exceptional durability still offers an environmental advantage because they are reused repeatedly instead of being discarded after one trip. One bag that lasts for years is still far better than hundreds of flimsy plastic bags that quickly become trash.

Reviving the bayong is not simply about bringing back a familiar Filipino icon. It is about rediscovering a practical solution to one of today’s biggest environmental problems. The Philippines has always had a culture of reusing, repairing, and making things last. The bayong is proof that sustainable living is not a foreign concept—it has always been woven into Filipino life.

The next time you head to the grocery or the palengke, consider leaving the plastic behind. A bayong may look like a bag from the past, but it might just be one of the smartest choices for the future.

(✍️: Top Dagohoy)

text:
I came home from work with a headache. My boyfriend said I was "letting him starve" because I refused to cook for him... even though the kitchen was full of food.

I'm 21, he's 26.

When I got home close to midnight, I asked him to warm up my leftover Chinese food because I wasn't feeling well.

While my food was heating up, he started wandering around the kitchen saying he was hungry.

I suggested eggs, noodles, frozen meals, rice, even canned fish with vegetables. We had plenty of food at home.

He rejected every single idea.

Then he asked if he could use my credit card to buy food from a nearby gas station.

I said no.

Money has been tight, and I've been doing everything I can to keep us afloat. I even helped him get a car a few months ago.

Then he asked me to cook for him.
I told him I was exhausted and had a headache. I even offered to wash the dishes and cook the rice if he'd prepare the meat.

He refused.

Instead, he sat on the couch saying I was "letting him starve."

I finally told him,

"You're not starving. You're choosing not to cook when you're perfectly capable of feeding yourself."

Now he says I was selfish and uncaring.

Was I wrong?

text:
A Threads post accusing Puregold of denying a senior citizen discount has generated outrage online. But a closer look at both the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) rules and the photos uploaded by the poster tells a very different story.

The post presents itself as a consumer rights exposé. In reality, it leaves out crucial information that completely changes the context.

THE BIGGEST OMISSION: THE ITEMS WERE ALREADY ON PROMO

The most glaring problem with the post is that it never tells readers that some of the featured products were already under store promotions.

Yet the photos themselves reveal exactly that.

One pack of Calla detergent clearly carries a “Buy 1 Get 2nd at 25% Off” promo sticker. Another Green Cross soap box prominently displays a FREE promotional offer.

Under the DTI-DA-DOE Joint Administrative Order No. 24-02, senior citizens are not entitled to stack discounts on grocery purchases.

Instead, they are given a choice:

* take the 5% senior citizen discount, or
* avail of the store promotion, whichever provides the greater benefit.

In this case, a 25% promotional discount is obviously worth far more than a 5% senior citizen discount.

Presenting the transaction as if the discount was illegally denied—while leaving out that the products were already on sale—creates an incomplete and potentially misleading narrative.

NOT EVERYTHING IN A GROCERY IS A “BASIC NECESSITY”

The post also repeatedly claims that items such as detergent, soap, toothpaste, and similar household products should automatically qualify for the senior citizen grocery discount.

That is not how the law works.

Radar checked and was informed that DTI does not grant 5% discount on every supermarket purchase.

Only products classified as Basic Necessities and Prime Commodities (BNPCs) qualify.

For example:

Covered

* Laundry detergent soap
* Bath soap
* Rice
* Fresh meat
* Fresh vegetables
* Bread
* Cooking oil
* Sugar
* Eggs

Not automatically covered

* Fabric conditioner
* Soft drinks
* Snacks
* Alcoholic beverages
* Luxury or specialty products
* Various household items outside the BNPC list

One of the products highlighted in the post is fabric conditioner.

Fabric conditioner is not classified by the DTI as a basic necessity entitled to the 5% grocery discount.

Simply buying it inside a supermarket does not make it eligible.

THE LAW IS PRODUCT-BASED—BUT STILL HAS LIMITS

The Theeads post is correct on one point.

The DTI indeed states that eligibility depends on the product classification, not merely on whether an item carries a premium brand.

A branded bath soap, for example, can still qualify because regular bath soap is listed as a prime commodity.

However, that does not mean every branded household product automatically becomes discount-eligible.

The product must first belong to one of the categories recognized under the BNPC list.

PROMOTIONS ARE NOT A VIOLATION

The post suggests that giving only a promotional discount instead of the senior discount is illegal.

The DTI rules say otherwise.

For BNPC grocery purchases already under a promotional sale, senior citizens are entitled to choose whichever discount is higher. The law does not allow both discounts to be applied simultaneously.

A 25% promotional offer therefore already exceeds the statutory 5% grocery discount.

BE CAREFUL WITH VIRAL “FACT-CHECKS”

Consumer rights deserve to be protected, and businesses should absolutely be held accountable when they violate the law.

If a store incorrectly classifies products, refuses valid discounts, or charges prices different from shelf tags, consumers have every right to question it and file complaints.

But that same standard should apply to other click bait or rage bait social media posts.

In this case, the post omitted visible details from its own photos—particularly the promotional stickers—and blurred the distinction between products that are legally covered by the DTI’s Basic Necessities and Prime Commodities list and those that are not.

The result is a narrative that encourages outrage while leaving readers without the complete legal picture.

Knowing consumer rights also means knowing their limits. A missing fact can completely change the story.

text:
I graduated from the University of Ilorin and attended my convocation on 21 October 2024.

I was over the age limit for NYSC, so I couldn't serve.

Like many fresh graduates, I had no work experience. I just wanted someone to give me a chance.

On 15 November 2024, I got a call with a job offer to work as a Production Accountant at a rice factory.

I didn't even apply for the role. I was recommended.

But the recommendation wasn't the end of the process.

I still had to write a test and go through an interview. Thankfully, I performed well and earned the offer.

The salary wasn't what I had hoped for, but it was about twice the NYSC allowance, so I accepted it. I saw it as an opportunity to gain experience rather than wait for the "perfect" job.

Just 11 days later, on 26 November 2024, I resumed work.

Looking back, that decision changed everything. That first opportunity gave me the experience I needed to move on to better opportunities.

PS: There's definitely an element of luck in getting a first job. Sometimes it's an application. Sometimes it's a recommendation. But when the opportunity comes, you still have to be prepared enough to prove you deserve it.

text:
Collected my NYSC certificate 7 May 2008 in Sokoto (after serving 3 month extension. POP was 14 Feb 2008)

Ran to Offa next day. Spent two days to dira with parental prayers lol. 

Then proceeded to Lagos to continue my job search. Applied to almost every company I can think of (over 100 if I counted before, during after service). There was hardly top company in Nigeria I didn't send application email to. 

Sent CV to Oando general career email on 25 May 2008. 

Three days later, got email from them inviting me for job test for the position of Fixed Asset Accountant. They had seen ICAN first stage pass (& prize I won) on my CV and felt I should be able to do the job despite needing 3 years' experience. 

Scared, I emailed them to say I wasn't qualified. No response. 

I showed up still. Saw 5 other candidates on that day. Marked there and then. Our scores communicated. I scored 73%. Highest. Passed. 

Invited for interview. 3 of us on that day. Passed that one too.

Invited for final chat with COO. Passed. 

Got offer. 

Everything happened in quick succession because they needed to fill that role. It wasn't even a general graduate trainee recruitment. It was for a specific role where the holder moved to another department and they needed to fill urgently. 

Resumed 16 June 2008 and began my oil & gas journey from there. 

PS: I will say there is an element of luck (like everything in life), because my CV (sent to the general recruitment email on their website) was so timely and what if I didn't start ICAN during my NYSC! The role was also not publicly advertised. They just needed to fill the role urgently.

At about 6 PM EDT last Saturday, August 22, 2026, World Crisis Radio posted a strategic analysis on X at @WebsterGTarpley (and soon after on https://t.co/V3jowoiMhO), which was headlined “World War CRINKs in Sight… Consider This a War Warning!... September-October a Potential Time Frame for Russian Provocation against NATO Members Poland and/or Baltic States… As Putin’s Long-Awaited Test of NATO Cohesion Nears, Trump Telegraphs Total Appeasement.” This estimate was supported by a summary of Russia’s state-sponsored terrorism against the NATO alliance in Europe and also in the United States over July and August 2026. The point was also that NATO governments and news media had failed to educate public opinion about the seriousness of a war danger growing out of the military, political, financial, and economic crisis of the Putin dictatorship in the Kremlin, and that these governments and news media had an urgent obligation to do everything possible to inform their publics. The Wall Street Journal wrote on Wednesday: “The surprise visit by the director of the Central Intelligence Agency to Moscow this week was to deliver a warning to Russia not to attack NATO countries, according to people briefed on the visit. (WSJ, Aug. 26, 2026 6:10 pm)
For our part, we are proud to have anticipated events when so many others failed to recognize them after the fact.
In particular, we had stressed that around July 4, the United States government had informed President Nawrocki of Poland that Russia was planning a large scale provocation in the not-too-distant future for the purpose of testing the cohesion and resilience of NATO under crisis conditions. For several months, countries on the northeast flank of NATO had been calling attention to the growing danger of some aggressive Russian provocation in the Baltic area. The Baltic states, Poland, and Sweden had been among the most explicit in this regard. One option for this aggressive testing was that the Russian forces would find a way to violate the territory of a Baltic country like Poland, Estonia, Latvia, or Lithuania, or perhaps Finland, either claiming to be lost through faulty geolocation, or to provide urgent help to the victims of a Russian helicopter or other aircraft that had just crashed by mistake in NATO territory. Or, Putin might send in his little green men along the lines of what he had done in seizing Crimea in 2014. At the time of these reports, it was immediately evident that this strategy would depend on the speedy intervention of Trump and his staff to block NATO’s article 5 mutual defense committment and forbid any armed response to such a blatant Russian incursion, and instead to demand an impotent offer of negotiations with Moscow to solve the question. In those talks, it was expected that Russia would demand a cutoff of all aid from NATO to Ukraine as the price for getting Russian troops out of NATO territory. This role of Trump as the enforcer of appeasement, disunity and defeatism in the West represents the indispensable hinge of the entire Russian scheme. True to form, Trump dismissed the Ratcliffe mission as “semi-routine,” and assured reporters that Russia would not attack anybody.

Around August 7, reports indicated that the US intelligence community had revised its notion of the possible timeframe for these events, and was now regarding them as plausible for any time starting with the autumn of 2026. Fall 2026 will arrive in the northern hemisphere on Tuesday, September 22 at 8:04 PM EDT. So, the new CIA timeframe meant that the acute war danger would begin on September 22. Putin’s window for provocation and aggression was set to open in a matter of weeks.
This analysis is the only one that can explain the urgency of Ratcliffe’s visit to Moscow. Ratcliffe was being sent in to tell the Kremlin: “We know what you’re planning, and we’re not going to let you get away with it. So don’t do it.” (Daily Telegraph)
Early on the following Tuesday morning, August 25, 2026, CBS News reported that CIA Director Ratcliffe had visited Moscow for talks with Kremlin officials: “A U.S. military plane landed at an airport in Moscow, Russia, on Tuesday, and CIA Director John Ratcliffe was among those on board. Charlie Dagata reports.” It was later reported that Ratcliffe had departed the Russian capital about eight hours later.
It also became known that the United States had requested that Ukraine suspend its drone and missile attacks against Russia for the duration of Ratcliffe’s visit. The Kyiv government had agreed to stop firing at the Moscow area for that limited time, but made no commitments about suspending attacks on the rest of Russia. Ratcliffe met with Alexander V. Bortnikov, the chief of the Russian Federal Security Service or FSB, which inherited many of the functions of the Cold War era KGB.
Ratcliffe had flown in on a four-engined C-17 transport aircraft, rather than on a smaller executive jet. It was speculated that the large aircraft had been used to transport a roll-on roll-off conference capsule, which features a full array of secure communications in the equivalent of a SCIF, an environment which is impervious to all outside monitoring. It was widely noted that the last time a CIA director had visited Moscow was on the eve of Putin’s February 22, 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which started the current war. This was William Burns, who was sent to warn Putin that the United States was well aware of his preparations for invading Ukraine, and that the Russian dictator should not start this militaristic adventure. At that time as now, the US intelligence community had been loudly announcing to the world what Putin was doing in the attempt to cut through the complacency and skepticism that were still strong in many quarters.

WHAT WAS RADCLIFFE’S MISSION?

The world then wanted to know what had been Radcliffe’s assignment in Moscow. To answer this question, it was necessary to be aware of the massive context of Russian state-sponsored terrorist activities, especially in Europe, against the background of Putin’s Ukraine war. As we stressed last week, the controlled and corrupt corporate and public media, especially in the United States, had imposed a virtual embargo on vital information about this Russian onslaught. In the resulting context of ignorance, speculation was rife: was it about Russian aid to Iran? Was it about Russia’s possible exemption from the latest round of US sanctions against Tehran? Was it an attempt to restart diplomacy to get a cease-fire in Ukraine? Was it an attempt to restart negotiations about the Ukraine war by sending in Witkoff and Kushner for another round of diplomatic charades?
As we showed last week, Russian state terrorism (formerly known as hybrid warfare) in Europe had escalated this summer to outrageous proportions. A Russian warship had conducted live fire exercises in the English Channel. Three drones, clearly Russian, loaded with explosives had turned up at the airport in Leipzig-Halle in Germany, a key nodal point for NATO’s military and other assistance to Ukraine. (Chancellor Merz is about to formally accuse Russia as the guilty party.) Important ammunition factories had been blown up in Bulgaria and just south of Rome, Italy. Drone violations had also been registered by Romania, Latvia, and other NATO members. A large explosion hit the petroleum facilities in the port of Rotterdam, Netherlands, which is Europe’s largest. A gasoline pipeline nexus near Tulsa, Oklahoma also exploded. In Toledo, Ohio, a factory specialized in enabling the recycling of used equipment was also hit. This came after water systems and sewage treatment facilities in at least seven American states were disturbed by cyber hacking widely attributed to Russia’s CRINKs partner, Iran.

On the Ukrainian battlefield, ballistic missiles from North Korea were arriving, giving the Russians the equipment they desired for their winter 2026-2027 campaign to demoralize the Ukrainian people by attacking civilian infrastructure. The North Korean missile question is by itself enough to establish the urgency of the moment.
It was in this atmosphere that Ratcliffe, considered the most – or the only – pro-Ukrainian member of the cabinet -- visited the Kremlin. After reviewing a number of source reports about the content of Ratcliffe’s dialogue with the Russians, it is possible to establish one overriding main theme and a number of subsidiary issues.
The overriding object of Ratcliffe’s visit was unquestionably to solemnly warn the Kremlin that their preparations for testing NATO were known to the United States, and that this country would not tolerate any Russian attack on NATO members. As a source of the London Daily Telegraph summed it up, the message was: “We know what you’re planning, and we’re not going to let you get away with it. So don’t do it.” (Daily Telegraph) In short, no attacks by Russia on NATO countries. No testing of NATO. NATO, as Russians might say, is ready to administer a decisive rebuff to any attacker.
A corollary to this main issue reported by some sources is that Ratcliffe told Bortnikov that the United States will honor Article 5 of the North Atlantic Pact, which provides for mutual defense among the members of the alliance, a provision often summed up as an attack on one is an attack on all.  Of course, the main confusion on this point had been produced by Trump himself. So, if this point was in fact convincingly made by Ratcliffe, this would be an exceedingly positive development. As some observers have noticed, Trump’s power appears to be dwindling as he approaches his final phase as lame duck, which is likely to begin with the November Congressional elections, especially if his MAGA supporters lose big in the way many public opinion polls are now predicting. If Trump wants to be seen as a friend of NATO Europe, the best way to do that would be to order immediate shipments to Kyiv of Patriot and THAAD ABM interceptors, plus a generous shipment of Tomahawk cruise missiles, Army ATACMs, and the like--at once.

Another important aspect of Ratcliffe’s message is widely thought to have been an attempt to reveal to Putin (who can be safely assumed to have been listening to the conversations in his nearby suite even if he was not present in the room with Ratcliffe) the grim and dire condition of his Russian realm, including the astronomical Russian losses on the battlefield, and the drastic cut in Russia’s ability to export oil and petroleum products as a result of Ukraine’s summer drone offensive, which has severely damaged or destroyed a large part of Russia’s oil refineries, storage tanks, pipelines, pumping stations, and tanker terminals. The assumption here is that Putin’s courtiers or palace guard are deliberately gaslighting the paranoid and isolated dictator, somehow limiting his ability to understand how disastrously his war has been going.

This part of the briefing therefore tried to establish the reality of the Ukraine war debacle, in effect urging Putin and his retainers not only to stop the war, but also to drop plans for a massive draft call of hundreds of thousands of Russian men, which will soon be unavoidable if Putin wants to keep attacking with his human wave frontal assaults. Another component of this part of the presentation could well have been an account of the ongoing crisis of panicked withdrawals from the Russian banking system by depositors of all kinds, starting with its two flagships, Sperbank and VTB Bank. VTB has been especially hard hit because of its reliance on its business with the leading online retailer Wildberries, more than half of whose shipment centers and warehouses have been hit. If Wildberries goes under, so will VTB Bank.

In short, Putin needs to imitate Red Army General Boris Gromov, who on Feb. 15, 1989 led his defeated forces out of Afghanistan across a bridge over the Oxus River and into then-Soviet Uzbekistan, putting an end to the Soviet-Afghan War.
A third important point in Ratcliffe’s briefing to the Russians was very likely a demand that Russia stop supporting its CRINKs ally Iran with intelligence and satellite imagery, advanced Russian drones, drone components, TNT, and spare parts for Russian-made weapons systems. Iran earns foreign exchange by selling Russia cheap ballistic missiles for use against Ukraine.  Ukraine, it should be noted, helped the US by launching missile attacks against Iranian freighters in the Caspian Sea, which were carrying military equipment for Iran.
Little or nothing about the Russian reply to these points has come to the surface so far.

COUNTDOWN CALENDAR

When might Putin test NATO? Russia’s national elections for the state parliament or Duma are scheduled to be completed by September 20. Putin has been anxious to avoid antagonizing public opinion before these elections, not because they are free and fair, but because popular discontent might find some means of expressing itself in the context of voting. Once the elections and related events are completed, Putin evidently believes he will be free to take unpopular steps.

A second consideration is the beginning of autumn. The first full day of autumn will be September 24, and with it is likely to come increasing danger.

Putin’s program of mobilization and conscription - As Ratcliffe himself had pointed out before this week’s trip to Moscow, the average combat life of a Russian draftee thrown into the fighting front is thirty-five minutes. Russia has routinely been losing 1000 soldiers per day in killed, wounded, missing, and captured. This adds up to losses of 7000 per week and 30,000 per month. Russian army losses currently exceed recruitment, so the force is shrinking. Putin therefore desperately needs manpower. He has been extremely reluctant to attempt a mass mobilization or levée en masse because of the potential for mass discontent, draft riots, or armed resistance. Putin wants especially to avoid antagonizing the elite oligarchs or nomenklatura in Moscow and St. Petersburg, who have been largely spared personal sacrifice during the conflict. Putin’s watchword has been to keep the Ukraine war a distant phenomenon, with only propaganda news reports reaching the vast majority of urban Russians. This is now impossible thanks to Kyiv’s long-range drone attacks.

According to Ukrainian intelligence sources, Putin’s plan is to draft 300,000 new conscripts during the remaining months of 2026, and then to follow that up with another 300,000 draftees in 2027, for a total of 600,000 new soldiers available as cannon fodder for the Russian army. Some women might be targeted. If mass resistance to this draft call should materialize, elements of the Russian oligarchical elite might support an effort to eliminate Putin.
We read: “According to Ukrainian intelligence findings, the General Staff of Russia has already formulated a mobilization blueprint targeting 600k personnel, apportioned at 300k per year. The influx is primarily designated to replenish combat units deployed in Ukraine and staff formations currently undergoing organization.
“Moscow is adjusting domestic legislation and expanding oversight of military conscription registries. Russian authorities are institutionalizing recruitment pipelines for convicted felons — including individuals serving sentences for severe crimes — while considering recruitment mechanisms for select categories of female prison inmates.
“In addition, recruitment quotas are being established across Russian security and law enforcement agencies, including the Ministry of Internal Affairs, the Federal Bailiff Service, the Federal Penitentiary Service, and the Investigative Committee. Conscript training cycles are projected to last between 15 and 60 days depending on prior experience, with a portion of personnel slated for training at proving grounds in Belarus.” (The New Voice of Ukraine)

Military assistance from North Korea (DPRK)-Ukrainian President Zelenski has warned repeatedly that dictator Kim of Pyongyang is in the process of sending some 50,000 of his troops to Ukraine. A previous North Korean troop contingent of about 12,000 arrived in Ukraine early in 2025 and played a role in the reduction of Ukraine’s Kursk salient. It is estimated that about half of the North Koreans were killed, wounded or captured in the process, and the division involved was later sent back to North Korea. Observers described the North Korean soldiers as better armed than the Russians, but lacking in helmets.

North Korea ballistic missiles-Reports from earlier in August indicate that North Korea has sent the Russians Hwasong-11C (KN-30) and 120 KN-23/KN-24 short-range ballistic missiles with six launchers and ninety North Korean military personnel now in Russia’s western Voronezh region [opposite Kharkiv and north of Donetsk]. “The KN-30 is the western designation for North Korea’s Hwasong-11C. It is an enlarged version of the Hwasong-11 family and belongs to the short-range ballistic missile category. The missile uses a solid-propellant engine and is launched from a mobile ground-based launcher.
“The KN-30 could also provide Russia with a higher-payload ballistic missile option than its Iskander-M system. North Korea has claimed that the missile can carry a warhead of up to 2.5 tons, although that figure has not been independently verified. By comparison, the Iskander-M's 9M723 ballistic missile is generally assessed to carry a warhead of around 480–700 kg.” (Times of India on MSN). The result is that madman Kim can now hit targets in central Europe.
Putin’s plan to get Belarus into the war - Putin is actively pressuring Belarus dictator Lukashenko to enter the war. At the beginning of the conflict, Putin was able to use Russian troops he had massed along Ukraine’s northern border in Belarus under the cover of military exercises to attempt the quick conquest of Kyiv, but this thrust was defeated. Right now, the total subservience of Belarus is even more necessary, since in addition to the attempt to envelop Kyiv from the north as well as the east, Putin is heavily focused on seizing the Suwalki corridor, a 40-mile-wide land chokepoint along the border between Poland and Lithuania. This narrow gap is all that separates Belarus from the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, which was historically the province of East Prussia with its capital in Königsberg. The only land connection between Poland to the south, and the NATO Baltic states of Lithuania, Latvia, and Estonia to the north crosses the Suwalki corridor. If Putin could seize this narrow tract of land between Belarus and Kaliningrad, NATO’s task of defending the three Baltic states would be critically threatened.
Lukashenko has up to now resisted Putin’s pressure to commit to war, but Russia and Belarus are both parts of a “union state” or confederation, and Putin’s capability of eliminating the Minsk dictator with a coup is real.
Putin also wants the Belarus armed forces under his command. Belarus has a population of about 9 million, and a standing army of 45,000 with 289,000 in the reserves, plus 110,000 paramilitaries. They have 500 tanks, 100 combat aircraft, and 80 helicopters. Putin is eager to acquire this extra supplement for his aggression.
More bounties and signing bonuses for convicts and criminals- Putin’s desperation tactic of recruiting convicts out of prison and signing up members of criminal gangs from the Russian underworld has been running out of steam because of the extremely high mortality rates at the Ukrainian front. Although this effort may not appear promising, Putin is determined to increase convict recruitment by further increases in bounties and signing bonuses.

Confiscation of property-Putin has recently signed a decree (ukaz), which establishes that any property owner who fails to provide for the defense and upkeep of such property risks having the property seized by the Kremlin. The property can then be sold to a third party, with the proceeds going to Putin’s treasury in Moscow. According to Michael Clarke of Sky News, Putin might also attempt to sell confiscated property cheaply to win back his estranged supporters in the oligarchy, or otherwise to acquire new allies through such largesse.

Forced loans subtracted from bank deposits - One of the factors contributing to the massive withdrawals of deposits or panic runs on Russian banks has been the nationwide fear that the Kremlin is planning to seize the contents of bank accounts in whole or in part to fund a forced loan by the Russian people to finance the continuation of the Ukraine war. Something similar was done in Cyprus in 2013. Any funds which Putin could acquire in this process could of course be used to finance the hopeless Ukraine conflict.

Forecast: This analysis suggests that Putin might begin his attack on NATO towards the last week in September or the beginning of October. The other constraining factor worth mentioning is the so-called rasputitza or rasputitsa, the period of October rains common to Western Russia, Ukraine, Belarus, Lithuania, and Poland. These October rains make any unpaved road impassable for tanks, armored personnel carriers, artillery, or other vehicles. In some cases, this sticky mud can become a foot deep, or even more. Some historians have speculated that it was this mud which saved Moscow from conquest by the Wehrmacht in 1941. If Putin wants to grab the Suwalki corridor, he will need to do it before the rasputitza rains get going. Last week, NATO combat aircraft quickly surrounded the Kaliningrad exclave in a much-needed show of force, reminding us that alliance strategy in case of war very likely includes an attempt to preempt Putin’s plans by seizing this isolated Russian territory along the southern Baltic.

WHAT PUTIN’S TEST OF NATO MIGHT LOOK LIKE

Since Putin’s dangerous experiment in “testing” NATO could come at virtually any time, let’s review a number of possible scenarios for this op using a list suggested by the London Daily Telegraph.

Crimean variant-A first option would attempt to duplicate Russia’s 2014 seizure of Crimea by deploying street provateurs backed up by elite Russian commandos in uniforms with no insignia who refuse to talk to the press, but who then unmask and reveal that they are Putin’s soldateska, followed by a referendum. This might work in areas like Narva in Estonia, or Daugavpils in Latvia, where Russian minorities nurse grievances against pro-Western governments. But little green men will not fool anybody, and alerted local troops will probably open fire before Trump can interfere to save them.
Option 2:  Conventional attack on Baltic littoral states with a wave of drones and an attempt to cut off NATO help by capturing the Suwalki gap plus the Swedish island of Gotland in the Baltic opposite the Gulf of Finland. Polish and Lithuanian forces would be joined by a German armored brigade in Lithuania and a UK battle group in Estonia.
Option 3: Incursion-A Russian helicopter develops engine trouble and makes an “emergency landing” in Lithuania just across the border from Kaliningrad. Russian troops say they have to enter NATO territory to rescue their comrades. Will anybody fall for this?
Option 4: False flag-The Russians send a heavy-duty drone with Ukrainian markings into Warsaw, and Poles are killed. Russian agents try to foment a Polish-Ukrainian conflict to split NATO. Short of a high-profile assassination, not effective.
Option 5: Russian sabotage in Europe-This also would have limited effect after so many previous attacks, since the shock effect has worn off.
Option 6: Cyber attack-This could cause chaos if health care, finance, water, electricity, gasoline, or communications are hit, but NATO may not be tested.
Result: all these scenarios lead to likely escalation. Deterring Putin will take deeds, not just words. But appeasement will not work.
