text:
Bijan Robinson just became the highest paid running back in NFL history. Up to $75 million, with a record $51 million guaranteed.

Three years ago, the NFL had collectively decided running backs weren't worth paying at all.

And the guy who saw it coming lost everything trying to stop it.

Rewind to 2018.

Le'Veon Bell is the best running back in football. Three time All Pro. The Steelers franchise tag him for a second straight year at $14.5 million.

Bell doesn't want the tag. He wants a long term deal, because he can do math. He knows exactly what another 400 touch season does to a running back's body and to his next contract.

So he does something nobody in his position had ever done.

He doesn't show up. All season. And when the deadline passes in November, he officially forfeits every dollar of that $14.5 million.

An entire year of his prime. Gone. For nothing.

He got destroyed for it. Called selfish, soft, a quitter, a guy who abandoned his teammates in a playoff race.

Here's what he actually said at the time: "A lot of people call me selfish, but I'm really not." He said he was doing it for the guys behind him.

He'd said it even more directly a year earlier: "I want to set standards for all the other running backs behind me."

Then the worst case scenario happened.

Bell signed with the Jets for less guaranteed money than Pittsburgh had already offered him. He was never the same player. His career was basically over by 2021.

He gave up $14.5 million and got nothing. The lesson the league took from it was that running backs have zero leverage, and that even the best one alive can be replaced by James Conner in a week.

Then the market completely collapsed.

By July 2023, Saquon Barkley, Josh Jacobs and Tony Pollard were all franchise tagged at roughly $10.1 million, the LOWEST tag number of any position on the field. Offense or defense. Below every other job in football.

So the running backs got on a Zoom call.

Austin Ekeler organized it. Barkley, Nick Chubb, Derrick Henry, Josh Jacobs and Christian McCaffrey all joined. The best backs in the world, on a video call, trying to figure out how to stop their own position from becoming worthless.

Ekeler's public words on how they were being treated: teams act like they are "discardable widgets."

And the call accomplished nothing. Chubb said it out loud afterward: "Right now, there's really nothing we can do."

Chubb also explained the cruelest part of being a running back better than anyone ever has. They're the only position where production is used AGAINST you. Run for 2,000 yards and the next year teams say you're worn down.

Now here's the timing that makes this whole thing.

That Zoom call happened in July 2023.

Three months earlier, in the April 2023 draft, the Atlanta Falcons had used the 8th overall pick on a running back out of Texas named Bijan Robinson.

And they got absolutely roasted for it. Taking a running back that high, in that market, was treated as one of the dumbest picks in modern draft history. Analytics people called it malpractice. Running backs don't matter. You can find one in the fourth round.

Then the pendulum swung back.

Saquon Barkley ran for 2,005 yards and won a Super Bowl in Philadelphia. Derrick Henry turned Baltimore's offense into a nightmare. Teams remembered that it's actually pretty hard to win when nobody can run the ball.

And today, Bijan Robinson reset the entire market. $51 million guaranteed. $37 million at signing. The most any running back has ever gotten.

Le'Veon Bell will never see a dollar of it.

He sat out a season to make a point that the market wasn't ready to hear, lost $14.5 million and his prime, and got called selfish for it.

Seven years later, the guy Atlanta got mocked for drafting just got paid like a franchise quarterback.

Bell was right. He was just early.

Follow @thesportsontap, we post a story like this every day.

My sister sun dries these & pack in zip lock pouch to u.k. It is not just a leaf. It's green gold. The importance of many native things are realised more when someone from outside took so much effort to take them along. 
The same leaf that we keep aside in our plates. The same leaf that we ignore max but it continues to offer what it has to. 
The curry leaves. I often see in local vegetable shops many ask for this as it is given free here in southern India. When u chk in super markets or online it comes wit price tag. Since it's free in local shops ppl take it, refrigirate, spoil until it decays , throw. Or use it in tempering but finally lands in ur dustbin. 
It's time we teach from young the magnificence of this leaf. Traditionally we make Curry leaves thogayal(semi solid mixture of dal,chilly& curry leaves), curry leaves kuzhambu (gravy) , curry leaves powder - always super hit at my home & of course in tempering. At my home the tempered leaves are mostly wasted. So we often resort to gravy & chutney. 
 We also use the powder for dosai, idly , mixing with rice etc. Now restaurants also have curry leaves idli, rice, dosai etc.. 
Include them somehow  in ur recipes. And finally when you accompany it with curd rice.. you will be in heaven. Try it.

text:
𝗘𝗫𝗣𝗟𝗢𝗥𝗘 𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗧𝗔𝗚𝗘

𝗕𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗟𝗨

𝗪𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘 𝗔 𝗧𝗘𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘 𝗛𝗢𝗡𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗘𝗗 𝗔 𝗙𝗔𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥, 𝗔 𝗧𝗔𝗡𝗞 𝗛𝗢𝗡𝗢𝗨𝗥𝗘𝗗 𝗔 𝗠𝗢𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥, 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗦𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡𝗦 𝗣𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗘𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗟𝗜𝗙𝗘 𝗢𝗙 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

At Basaralu, three brothers transformed remembrance into two institutions.

They consecrated Mallikārjuna in their father’s name and created a tank in their mother’s name.

One sustained worship. The other sustained water, cultivation and settlement life.

The principal inscription also describes the temple from its foundation to the summit of its tower, praises its coloured decoration and recalls narrative scenes from the Bhārata and other works. The architecture standing today gives material form to that written celebration.

Basaralu, Mandya Taluk, Mandya District, Karnataka.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗕𝗔𝗦𝗨𝗥𝗜𝗩𝗔̄𝗟̣𝗔 — 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗘𝗧𝗧𝗟𝗘𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗡𝗔𝗠𝗘𝗗 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗗𝗦

The inscriptions call the settlement Basurivāḷa, represented as Basurivāl in B. Lewis Rice’s Roman edition. That historical place-name survives in modern Basaralu.

The three securely published records appear in Epigraphia Carnatica, Volume III, Mandya Taluk, as Nos. 121, 122 and 123. They document the foundation of Mallikārjuna, a second endowment two years later and the appointment of temple managers during the reign of Narasimha III.

The earliest record belongs to Hoysala Vīra Narasimha II. Its date is Śaka 1157, Jaya, Vaiśākha śuddha 2, Monday, under Rohiṇī—corresponding to 1235 CE in Rice’s edition.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗙𝗢𝗨𝗡𝗗𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗗

𝗘𝗣𝗜𝗚𝗥𝗔𝗣𝗛𝗜𝗔 𝗖𝗔𝗥𝗡𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗖𝗔, 𝗩𝗢𝗟. 𝗜𝗜𝗜, 𝗠𝗔𝗡𝗗𝗬𝗔 𝗡𝗢. 𝟭𝟮𝟭

Śaka 1157, Jaya, Vaiśākha śuddha 2 — 1235 CE

A central clause reads:

“Tamma tandeya hesara Mallikarjuna-devaram Basurivalol su-pratishteyam madi…”

𝗧𝗥𝗔𝗡𝗦𝗟𝗔𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡

“Having duly installed Lord Mallikārjuna at Basurivāḷa in the name of their father…”

Tamma taṇḍeya hesara records that the consecration was made in the father’s name.

Mallikārjjuna-dēvaraṃ identifies the deity.

Basurivāḷoḷ fixes the act at the settlement now called Basaralu.

Su-pratiṣṭheyaṃ māḍi records the proper installation of the deity.

The record then states that the brothers caused a tank to be made in their mother’s name and a temple in their father’s name. Family memory was expressed through both sacred architecture and a water resource serving the surrounding landscape.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗜𝗛𝗔𝗥𝗔 𝗗𝗔𝗡̣𝗗̣𝗔𝗡𝗔̄𝗬𝗔𝗞𝗔 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗛𝗜𝗦 𝗕𝗥𝗢𝗧𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗦

The inscription traces the family through Chikka-Hadevaḷḷa and Malleya Nāyaka.

Malleya Nāyaka and Gujjale had three sons:

Siṅgeya Nāyaka
Māreya Nāyaka
Harihara

The mother’s name appears as Gujjale in Rice’s published translation; the associated reservoir is widely remembered as Gujjavve Kere.

The record praises all three brothers, while presenting Addāyada Harihara Daṇḍanāyaka as the leading figure. 

He served Vīra Narasimha II as a minister and military commander and is celebrated through a sequence of courtly titles.

It also recalls his confrontation with Seuna forces, placing the patron within the political and military world of the Hoysala kingdom. Yet the Basaralu foundation is expressed through family memory.

The brothers installed Mallikārjuna in their father’s name.

They created the tank in their mother’s name.

Worship and water became parallel forms of remembrance.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗜𝗡𝗦𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗗𝗘𝗦𝗖𝗥𝗜𝗕𝗘𝗦 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗘𝗠𝗣𝗟𝗘

EC III, Mandya No. 121 offers a contemporary literary description of the building.

Rice translates the passage as praising a temple that shone from its foundation to the pinnacle, carried varied coloured decoration and contained spaces adorned with ancient stories from the Bhārata and other works. Its brilliance is compared with Mount Meru enriched by the art of a goldsmith.

The surviving temple still presents an extensive narrative and divine sculptural programme. The inscription confirms that storytelling, colour, workmanship and visual abundance shaped the thirteenth-century understanding of the foundation.

At Basaralu, text and architecture illuminate one another.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘 𝗦𝗛𝗥𝗜𝗡𝗘𝗦 — 𝗢𝗡𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗠𝗜𝗡𝗔𝗡𝗧 𝗧𝗢𝗪𝗘𝗥

The Mallikārjuna temple is a trikūṭa, a three-shrined composition organised around a shared navaraṅga.

Its exterior, however, is dominated by a single complete tower.

The principal western shrine possesses an antarāla, śukanāsi and superstructure. The northern and southern sanctums open into the common hall without corresponding towers.

The visitor therefore experiences three sanctums within, while one principal vimāna defines the exterior.

The axial sanctum houses the Mallikārjuna liṅga. Nandi faces the principal shrine from the east.

Lathe-turned pillars organise the navaraṅga and support carefully composed ceiling bays, including a directional scheme associated with the Aṣṭadikpālas.

The temple stands upon a jagati whose projections guide movement around the building and provide the level from which its sculptural sequence can be read.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗩𝗜𝗠𝗔̄𝗡𝗔 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗛𝗢𝗬𝗦𝗔𝗟𝗔 𝗖𝗥𝗘𝗦𝗧

The principal vimāna rises through diminishing, richly articulated tiers.

Its śukanāsi projects before the tower as an architectural continuation of the sanctum. Above it appears the Hoysala royal emblem of Sala confronting the animal represented in dynastic tradition as the tiger.

The inscription places Harihara’s foundation within Hoysala kingship through its royal genealogy, regnal setting and patron’s service. The crest gives that political affiliation visual form upon the building.

Royal authority appears in the record.

Dynastic identity appears in stone.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗗𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗘𝗫𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗜𝗢𝗥

The exterior belongs to the fully developed phase of Hoysala architectural ornament.

Projecting eaves divide the elevation into ordered zones. Miniature towers occupy the intermediate register. Larger divine figures appear below, while horizontal sculptural bands encircle the basement.

The lower courses bring together elephants, horsemen, lions, narrative scenes, makaras, kīrtimukhas and haṃsas.

Elephants establish the visual foundation. Horsemen evoke movement and martial power. Lions express strength and authority. Narrative bands carry sacred stories, while makaras, kīrtimukhas and haṃsas complete the sequence with protective and auspicious imagery.

The bands follow every projection and recess of the walls. Sculpture responds to the plan rather than functioning as an independent layer of decoration.

Architecture creates the rhythm.

Sculpture makes that rhythm visible.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗦́𝗜𝗩𝗔 𝗔𝗡𝗗 𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗪𝗜𝗗𝗘𝗥 𝗦𝗔𝗖𝗥𝗘𝗗 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗟𝗗

The larger wall panels present a predominantly Śaiva programme enriched by Vaiṣṇava, Śākta and other divine forms.

Among the major compositions are dancing Śiva, Gajāsuramardana, Tripurāntaka, Hara-Gaurī, Durgā, Mahiṣāsuramardinī, Sarasvatī, Hayagrīva and Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa.

Attendants, guardians, musicians, dancers and celestial beings complete the larger images and sustain the movement of the sculptural wall.

Narrative courses include episodes associated with the Rāmāyaṇa, Mahābhārata and Bhāgavata traditions. The story of Prahlāda receives particularly detailed treatment.

The programme gives visible form to the inscription’s praise of a temple adorned with stories from the Bhārata and other works.

The walls were created to be read as well as seen.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗦𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗡𝗗 𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗗 — 𝟭𝟮𝟯𝟳 𝗖𝗘

EC III, Mandya No. 122 belongs to the reign of Hoysala Vīra Somēśvara.

Harihara Daṇḍanāyaka granted two villages—Bēbi and Teraṇi, described as hamlets of Basurivāḷa—to support Mallikārjuna.

The endowment served the deity’s aṅga-bhoga, ceremonial worship, vessels, lamps, festivals including Caitra and Pavitra, food-giving and the repair of damaged or ageing parts of the temple.

The wording presents the foundation as a continuing institution. Consecration required an economic structure capable of sustaining daily service, periodic celebration, charity and architectural care.

The record also states that Chikka-Jiya went to Parvata and brought Mallikārjuna. It records a further grant of wet land below Basaralu’s old tank and dry land near temple property at Hadavaḷanahaḷḷi.

Parvata is generally understood as Śrīparvata. The inscription securely records Chikka-Jiya’s journey and his connection with Mallikārjuna; the precise institutional context remains open to closer study.

The record was composed by Chidānanda, son of Paramaprakāśa-Yogīśvara, whom it praises as a true poet and an embodiment of Brahmanical learning.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗧𝗛𝗜𝗥𝗗 𝗥𝗘𝗖𝗢𝗥𝗗 — 𝟭𝟮𝟲𝟵 𝗖𝗘

EC III, Mandya No. 123 belongs to the reign of Hoysala Narasimha III.

Dated Śaka 1191, it records that Hariyanna and Narasiṅgadeva, identified as the sons of Addāyada Hariyanna, were appointed sthānikas of Mallikārjuna’s temple at Basurivāḷa, with lands assigned for the deity’s service.

A sthānika held recognised responsibility within the local administration and service of a religious institution.

The three records reveal successive layers of temple life.

The first documents construction, consecration, water infrastructure and initial land support.

The second enlarges the endowment and lists the services it maintained.

The third identifies those entrusted with formal responsibility for the institution.

Basaralu’s inscriptions preserve more than a founding event. They show how a temple was financed, administered and carried forward.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗕𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗟𝗨 𝗜𝗡 𝗧𝗛𝗥𝗘𝗘 𝗗𝗢𝗖𝗨𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗘𝗗 𝗠𝗢𝗠𝗘𝗡𝗧𝗦

𝟭𝟮𝟯𝟱 𝗖𝗘

Harihara Daṇḍanāyaka and his brothers consecrate Mallikārjuna in their father’s name, create a tank in their mother’s name and establish land support for the deity.

𝟭𝟮𝟯𝟳 𝗖𝗘

Harihara grants Bēbi and Teraṇi for worship, festivals, food-giving and repair. The record also names Chikka-Jiya’s journey to Parvata and his connection with Mallikārjuna.

𝟭𝟮𝟲𝟵 𝗖𝗘

Hariyanna and Narasiṅgadeva are appointed sthānikas of the temple, with lands assigned for Mallikārjuna’s service.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

𝗪𝗛𝗬 𝗕𝗔𝗦𝗔𝗥𝗔𝗟𝗨 𝗠𝗔𝗧𝗧𝗘𝗥𝗦

Basaralu brings inscription, architecture, sculpture, family memory, water management and institutional history together within one coherent landscape.

The records preserve the settlement’s historical name, identify the brothers responsible for the foundation and explain why the temple honoured their father while the tank honoured their mother.

They describe the visual splendour intended by the patrons, record the lands that supported worship, festivals, food-giving and repair, name Chikka-Jiya’s connection with Parvata and document the appointment of temple managers.

The temple adds its own evidence.

Three sanctums are gathered beneath one dominant tower.

The royal crest places the building within the Hoysala political world.

The sculptural walls give visible form to the inscription’s reference to the Bhārata and other narratives.

At Basaralu, a father’s memory became a temple.

A mother’s memory became a reservoir.

Their sons transformed remembrance into institutions that served deity, water, land and community.

That is the enduring importance of Mallikārjuna at Basaralu.

Declan Rice

Hybrid engine (No 6/No 8). Press-resistant, progressive carrier, chance creator and aggressive ball-winner. Demands the ball, drives through midfield and links defence to attack. Would give Arteta a dynamic, high-energy midfielder who can dictate tempo while covering large distances and adding goal contributions.

Martín Zubimendi

Deep-lying tempo controller and press-resistant pivot. Excellent scanning, short-to-long progressive passing, and positioning between the centre-backs. Frees Rice to push forward, improves build-up against high presses, and adds defensive solidity + occasional goals from midfield. Acts as the calm “brain” that keeps Arteta’s possession structure secure.

Ethan Nwaneri

High technical ceiling: close control, dribbling in tight spaces, shooting from distance, and goal threat. Can play as right/left attacking midfielder, inverted winger or even false 9. Offers unpredictability and finishing ability when Arteta needs a creative spark or rotational option in the final third. Still developing the full tactical discipline required.

Myles Lewis-Skelly

Versatile, press-resistant and progressive. Strong technique, box-to-box engine and composure on the ball. Originally a midfielder, converted to left-back by Arteta but now also used as a left-sided No 8. Offers inversion from full-back, progressive passes from the half-space, and energy in transitions — perfect for Arteta’s fluid left side.

Martin Ødegaard

Technical reference and creative hub. Elite vision, line-breaking passes, close control, set-piece quality and tempo control. Operates mainly as right-sided No 8 / advanced playmaker. Physical, duel-winning and highly adaptable. Strong in the air, good timing of runs, and capable of playing No 8, deeper midfield or even false 9/striker. Flair, dribbling, shooting volume and creativity. Excellent 1v1 ability, ability to receive on the half-turn, and capacity to produce magic moments. Best as a central No 10 or left-sided attacker. text:
The ancient civilizations of Mesoamerica left behind a rich artistic legacy that continues to captivate and intrigue modern scholars and enthusiasts. Among the myriad of themes that Mesoamerican art explored, one aspect stands out as both fascinating and provocative: human sexuality...

From the seductive curves of ceramic vessels to the intricate murals adorning temple walls, the depictions of sexuality in Mesoamerican art offer a window into the intimate realms of desire, fertility, and spirituality. This was a natural aspect of ancient belief and can tell us a lot more about the everyday lives of ancient Mesoamericans.

Sexuality and eroticism were recurring themes in Mesoamerican art, reflecting the diverse cultures and beliefs of the region. Artworks from ancient civilizations such as the Maya, Aztec, and Olmec often depicted sexual imagery and explored various aspects of human sexuality.

In these ancient cultures, nudity and sexuality were not seen in the same light as they are today. In modern and near-modern history, explicit eroticism and nudity was often seen as taboo and inappropriate. But in ancient cultures it was not so. Fertility and sex played a huge role in the everyday lives of many ancient civilizations, including Mesoamericans. There were numerous deities connected with virility, fertility, childbirth, and so on. With that being said, it should not come as a surprise to realize that a lot of Mesoamerican gods, murals, sculptures, and beliefs revolved around explicit nudity and sexuality.

Of course, it goes without saying that many Mesoamerican cultures held fertility in high regard and believed it to be closely tied to the cycles of nature. After all, life back then was not a certainty, and the people prayed to the gods of fertility to secure offspring, as well as good yield.

Sexual imagery often represented the act of procreation and the creation of life. Phallic symbols, depictions of copulation, and images of male and female genitalia were common motifs in Mesoamerican art, particularly in pottery, sculptures, and murals. Knowing that this was a focal point of all their lives and their future as well, the Mesoamericans did not shy from these depictions.

As a result, many Mesoamerican cultures produced a significant amount of erotic pottery. These ceramics featured explicit sexual scenes and depicted various sexual acts, including intercourse, masturbation, and oral sex. Sex meant offspring, life, and new generations. So these people embraced it fully. Erotic pottery was often associated with ritual and fertility, believed to bring blessings and ensure abundance. That is why today, archaeologists often stumble upon ceramics painted with the most explicit sexual scenes - all of which simply celebrate the art of creating new life.

Some Mesoamerican cultures, such as the Aztecs, even had sacred prostitutes who were considered an integral part of religious ceremonies. In Aztec society, sacred prostitutes were known as "cihuapipiltin" or "quetzalli." These women held a significant position and were considered representatives of the goddess Xochiquetzal, who was associated with fertility, beauty, and female sexuality. The cihuapipiltin were chosen for their physical beauty and trained in various arts, including singing, dancing, and weaving. Sexual motifs were also present in the adornments and attire of these sacred prostitutes.

But maybe someone offers him $1 Billion for his best game worn jerseys in his collection and he makes the move. text:
A $500,000 check written in 2004 turned into more than a billion dollars by 2012. The same man watched his own hedge fund fall from $7 billion to about $350 million.

His name is Peter Thiel. He is 58.

He co-founded PayPal in 1998 and sold it to eBay in 2002 for $1.5 billion. Two years later he became the first outside investor in Facebook, taking 10.2 percent for half a million dollars.

Then Clarium Capital, his global macro fund, peaked above $8 billion in 2008 and posted three straight losing years. Investors who stayed lost 65 percent from the peak. By 2011 the fund held roughly $350 million.

So the man teaching you how to think about competition has been on both sides of being wrong in public.

The framework fits on a napkin. Perfect competition destroys profit, so build the thing nobody else can offer. Start with a market small enough to dominate, then widen. Look for proprietary technology ten times better than the alternative, network effects, scale economics, and a brand people ask for by name. Value the last mover, not the first.

"Competition is for losers."

That is the title he put on a Wall Street Journal essay in September 2014, adapted from the book he wrote out of a Stanford class he taught in 2012. A student named Blake Masters posted his notes from that class online for free, and the notes went viral before the book existed.

at the board it's simple. one company sold for $1.5 billion, one check compounded two thousand times, one fund down ninety-five percent from peak assets. the same brain produced all three.

no magic. concentration into an idea almost nobody shares, held long enough to be measured.

here is where it lines up with every founder reading this. you already know your product is a slightly better version of something people already buy.

you will still call the crowded market validation, raise on comparables, and describe five competitors as proof of demand in the same deck where you claim to be different.

the class notes are free. the essay is free. this talk is free.

what nobody can sell you is the willingness to answer his actual question in writing: what important truth do very few people agree with you on.

That willingness is the edge, and it costs an honest page, not another pitch deck.

afternoon. Four or five people were waiting for the darshan of Acharyal in the Matham. Meenakshi Patti prostrated to the sage with her granddaughter and got up. Swamiji looked at her and laughed. Paati was wondering if she should tell Periyavar about the chain that she found.

Swamiji foresaw her. "Today you should have completed your Pancha Sankyopachara pradakshina in order. But then, it was not completed because of some object that came to the hand of your granddaughter! That sudden delight did not allow you to do more than four pradakshinas. You came hurriedly, thinking that Kamakshi has given you Her full blessings. What, am I right?"

Patti was shocked. She became insensate, and swallowed her words as she spoke: "Swamigal shouldn't mistake me. Once that object came to the hand of my granddaughter, I assumed that Ambal Herself had dropped it for my granddaughter to take. In that sudden delight I totally fogot that I had to make one more pradakshina."

Periyava said relentlessly, "Did you forget only that? Did you not forget to get the chain weighed at Rangu Patthar's shop? Or get the severed portion melted in the furnace to rejoin it." He clinched His talk with the words, "Let it go. When you weighed it, was it exactly eight sovereigns?"

Patti and her granddaughter were stunned. "All you said now is the truth, Periyava!" said Patti.

Swamiji asked her calmly, "Tell me in fairness. To whom does that chain belong?"

"To Ambal Kamakshi."

"Tell me yourself, can you take it secretly and pack it inside the edge of your sari?"

"A mistake... nothing else but a mistake! Periyava should forgive me. I have done it out of ignorance." Patti was genuinely repenting. She placed the double-stringed sovereign chain on the brass plate that was found before Swamiji, her hands shaking. Swamiji laughed.

It was now two in the afternoon. Swamiji asked Meenakshi Patti and her daughter to sit before him. It was at that time that Ambujam Ammal, wife of Needamangalam Ganesa Iyer, who had taken leave in the morning, came back full of sorrow and prostrated to the sage. Her eyes were shedding tears profusely. Swamiji saw this and said affectionately, "Adada, why do you shed tears Amma?"

Ambujam Ammal wiped her tears and replied, "It is like this, Periyava. Two months ago when I did the five days seva in the Kamakshi Amman temple I prayed to Ambal earnestly that I would offer Her my eight-sovereign double-stringed chain if she united my daughter and son-in-law, who were then separated. Ambal has united them. I went to the temple to offer my chain. It slipped from my neck and fell down somewhere. I searched everywhere thoroughly but the chain could not be found. What can I do now, Periyava?" She started wailing.

Swamiji turned his face to Meenakshi Patti and looked meaningfully. Patti prostrated to Him and got up briskly. She took the double-stringed sovereign chain from the brass plate before the sage in her hand. She turned to Ambujam and said holding up the chain, "Amma Ambujam. Check if this is the double-stringed chain you lost."

Ambujam took the chain from her hand and checked. "The same, the same chain, Patti. How did it come here?" Patti narrated everything that happened to them in one breath.

Ambujam Ammal hugged Meenakshi Patti. "Patti, you don't worry at all! I am informing you this before our Acharyal. I shall arrange for a new double-stringed chain in eight sovereigns for your granddaughter! Her marriage will be performed grandly. This double-stringed I have prayed to offer to Ambal. This evening I shall take you and your granddaughter Kamakshi to the jewellery shop in this down and get her an eight-sovereign double-stringed chain. In addition, I shall give you five thousand rupees for the marriage expenses."

Swamiji was sitting as the Pratyaksha Kamakshi, witnessing this scene. Everyone prostrated to Acharyal. He looked at Meenakshi Patti and said, "Today you and your granddaughter have not done the five pradakshinas.

back. Told me something, feeling sad. Looking at the way you have come now with a large banana bunch, it seems that your problems would have been solved by the grace of Kamakshi, right?"

Ambujam prostrated again and said, "True, Periyava. My only daughter, Mythili was made to stay away from her husband's home for the last three years. Two months back I came running to you, reported this humiliation and wept. It was you who advised me to do “Pancha Sankya Upacharam” (five circumambulations and five prostrations for five days) and perform abhishekham (ablution) and worship in the Kamakshi Amman temple of this town. I completed them with extreme care, and what a wonder, fifteen days back, my son-in-law Radhakrishnan who works in Jamshedpur Tata Steel Plant came over himself and took his wife Mythili back with him. It's all that Kamakshi's grace and your blessings, Periyava!" Tears of joy filled her eyes as she spoke.

Swamiji said, "Besh, besh, very glad. Let the dampati rest in prosperity! By the way, where did you get such a big bunch of bananas? Looks massive!" Swamiji's laughed heartily.

Ambujam said smilingly, "This bunch was harvested from our own banana bed, Periyava; which is why it is so big!" She spoke with humility.

Showing happiness, Swamiji ordered her, "Alright, only Amma Kamakshi has united your daughter and son-in-law. So you offer this big banana bunch to Her and distribute the fruits to the devotees who visit the shrine."

Ambujam said, "No no, Periyava. Let it remain in this sanctum. I have another identical bunch to offer to Ambal. Now I seek your leave to have a darshan of Ambal, complete my prayers and get back here." She prostrated.

"Besha! After completing your prayers you must take food in the Matham and then only should get back to your place. Remember it!" Swamiji gave her His consent to leave Him.

There was not much crowd in Kamakshi Amman temple on that day. It was eleven in the morning. As it was later than usual, Meenakshi Patti hurried to the temple with her granddaughter. She halted at the shop selling archana packs, and told her granddaughter, "Hey Kamakshi! Today is the day of completion. So we shall do everything in five numbers as told by Acharyal. What you do, get five archana packs with five coconuts, five bananas, betel leaves, nuts, etc. and come back running!" and gave her the required money.

The granddaughter bought the things as ordered. Patti performed the archanas to Ambal and prayed Her with tearful eyes, 'Amma Kamakshi, I am completely depending on You only! I have no refuge except You and Swamigal. Only You should arrange for the eight-sovereign double-string chain and complete my granddaughter's marriage in a fitting manner.' As Patti sobbed, her granddaughter was also moved and wept. Then they started going round the inner couryard from left to right. They were on their fourth round.

"Patti... Patti... Patti!" Meekakshi Patti looked back at the loud call from her granddaughter and chided her angrily, "Why are you crying so loudly? What have you lost to raise such a noise?"

"Nothing lost Patti, but something gained! Please come here, I shall show you!" She took her grandmother to a corner, opened her right palm and showed her something. It was a severed, double-stringed chain with a front.

"Where did you find that?" Patti asked with surprise. Her granddaughter said, "As I was coming behind you with a bowed head, my eyes fell on this chain. I took it at once, and no one has noticed me! This chain is severed Patti. Check if it is genuine gold or just a gold-plated one."

Patti took the chain in her hands to estimate its weight. She said, "Looks like sovereign, Kamakshi! May be eight or eight-and-a-half sovereigns. This has been granted to us by Kamakshi Herself backed by the blessings of Periyava. Alright, let us go out first!" She packed the chain inside the edge of her sari and hurriedly came out, forgetting to complete her fifth circumambulation.

Located in Chaoyang, Liaoning province, the Niuheliang site is one of the most important archaeological sites of the late Neolithic Hongshan culture and offers a remarkable glimpse into the early development of Chinese civilization. More than 5,800 years ago, this mountain landscape was home to a grand ceremonial complex of altars, a goddess temple, and stone-built tombs, reflecting a highly organized ritual tradition. Recent discoveries, including large rammed-earth platforms and newly identified ritual features, have further highlighted Niuheliang's role as the core area of an early regional polity. Today, visitors can still sense the spiritual world of a society that revered Heaven, honored its ancestors, and treasured jade, preserving the legacy of one of the origins of Chinese civilization.

Fair assessment, and I can’t help but deeply respect your concern to protect the glory and sufficiency of Christ’s sacrifice. That is the right instinct for any true believer, and I believe you are a brother. I want to make it clear that I (and any genuinely faithful dispy) don’t believe any ritual, prophecy, or interpretation could undermine or diminish the finished work of Christ. It is complete, final, untouchable. It would be impossible.

I’d like to simply offer one observation to consider. In Acts 21, Paul took part in temple purification rites that involved offerings after the cross. It served a purpose, everything written does, even if some things aren’t as clear.

And if Paul didn’t undermine the Ultimate Sacrifice, then I don’t think the belief in future memorial sacrifices (which no true believer claims are atoning) should automatically do so either. The cross remains complete and sufficient, no matter our interpretation.

text:
What Happens After Isaiah 53?

Everyone knows Isaiah 53.

The suffering Servant.

The Man of Sorrows.

The One who was "pierced for our transgressions" and "crushed for our iniquities."

But very few people keep reading.

And that's a shame.

Because what happens after Isaiah 53 may be one of the most breathtaking prophetic progressions in all of Scripture.

Isaiah 53 answers how God can forgive sinners.

The chapters that follow answer how God remains faithful to every promise He has ever made.

Rather than jumping from one proof text to another, let's simply keep reading Isaiah.

Watch what happens.

The horizon keeps expanding.

Not away from Israel.

Outward through Israel.

Because God's promises don't disappear.

They unfold.

❖ Isaiah 53 — Redemption

The Servant bears our sins.

"He was pierced for our transgressions..." (53:5)

"My righteous Servant will justify many..." (53:11)

Redemption is accomplished.

But Isaiah isn't finished.

The cross was never God's finish line.

It was His foundation.

❖ Isaiah 54 — Restoration

Immediately, the spotlight turns to Zion.

"With everlasting lovingkindness I will have compassion on you." (54:8)

"My covenant of peace shall not be removed." (54:10)

The nation is restored.

God's covenant faithfulness has not failed.

The promises made to Zion remain the promises made to Zion.

God keeps His word.

❖ Isaiah 55 — Invitation

Then the circle grows wider.

"Come, everyone who thirsts..." (55:1)

"I will make with you an everlasting covenant, My steadfast, sure love for David." (55:3)

The blessings secured by the Servant are now freely offered.

The invitation reaches everyone who will come.

God's grace expands without canceling His promises.

❖ Isaiah 56 — Gathering

Then Isaiah does something remarkable.

Foreigners who join themselves to the LORD are welcomed.

Eunuchs once excluded receive "a name better than sons and daughters."

Then comes one of Scripture's greatest declarations:

"My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples." (56:7)

But don't miss the very next verse.

"The Lord GOD, who gathers the outcasts of Israel, declares, 'I will gather yet others to him besides those already gathered.'" (56:8)

The order matters.

First, the outcasts of Israel are gathered.

Then others are gathered alongside them.

Not instead of them.

The circle simply becomes larger.

This was never God's backup plan.

Fourteen centuries before Isaiah, God told Abraham:

"In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed." (Gen. 12:3)

The blessing promised through Abraham was always meant to reach the nations.

Jesus affirmed Isaiah's vision.

When He cleansed the Temple, He did not quote Isaiah 53.

He quoted Isaiah 56.

"My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations." (Mark 11:17)

The Court of the Gentiles—the very place where the nations were meant to seek Israel's God—had become a marketplace.

Jesus wasn't abandoning Isaiah's vision.

He was defending it.

Paul later confirms the same pattern:

"Christ became a servant to the circumcised to confirm the promises given to the patriarchs, and in order that the Gentiles might glorify God for His mercy." (Rom. 15:8–9)

Paul doesn't describe God's promises as transferred.

He describes them as confirmed.

If we wanted Isaiah himself to summarize this entire progression in one verse, he already did:

"It is too small a thing that You should be My Servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob and to restore the preserved ones of Israel; I will also make You a light for the nations, that My salvation may reach to the ends of the earth." (Isa. 49:6)

Restore Israel.

Reach the nations.

That is exactly where Isaiah takes us after chapter 53.

Notice the progression.

The Servant.

Zion.

Everyone who thirsts.

Foreigners.

All peoples.

And finally...

"All flesh shall come to worship before Me, declares the LORD." (Isa. 66:23)

Isaiah's vision keeps growing wider.

Nothing is replaced.

Everything expands.

A faithful Servant.

A restored Zion.

An everlasting covenant.

A welcomed world.

A gathering of the nations.

A worshiping creation.

One faithful God.

The New Covenant is not the story of God changing His mind.

It is the story of God keeping His word.

So...

What happens after Isaiah 53?

The rest of the story.

text:
On behalf of the entire worldwide mission of Jagadguru Kripalu Yog and the Jagadguru Kripalu University, we offer our deepest gratitude to Smt. Droupadi Murmu, Hon’ble President of India, for graciously inaugurating Jagadguru Kripalu University and blessing this historic occasion with her esteemed presence. We also extend our heartfelt thanks to Dr Hari Babu Kambhampati, Hon’ble Governor of Odisha; Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha; Shri Suryabanshi Suraj, Hon’ble Minister for Higher Education; and all the distinguished dignitaries who honoured the occasion with their presence and encouragement.
The distinguished dignitaries were warmly received at the University Administrative Building by Swami Mukundananda, Founder and Chairman of Jagadguru Kripalu University. The University is situated in Banara Panchayat of Cuttack District
The Hon’ble President formally inaugurated the campus by cutting the ceremonial ribbon at the Admin Building and unveiling the commemorative inaugural plaque.
The dignitaries then joined the members of the Jagadguru Kripalu University Board for a commemorative group photograph, capturing this landmark moment in the institution’s history.
In keeping with the Indian tradition of nurturing nature, the Hon’ble President, together with the Governor, the Chief Minister, and Swami Mukundananda, planted a sacred Peepal sapling, symbolizing growth, wisdom, and the flourishing future of the institution.
The inaugural ceremonies continued with the offering of floral tributes at the statue of Jagadguru Shree Kripalu Ji Maharaj, paying tribute to the visionary spiritual master whose inspiration gave birth to the university.
Following these ceremonies, the dignitaries proceeded to the main auditorium, where thousands of attendees, including distinguished guests, public representatives, academicians and devotees, had assembled with great enthusiasm to witness this historic occasion.
The formal function commenced with the Master of Ceremonies welcoming the Hon’ble President, the Hon’ble Governor, the Hon’ble Chief Minister, Swami Mukundananda, and the other dignitaries to the dais. The entire gathering then rose in unison for the rendition of the National Song and the National Anthem, followed by the ceremonial lighting of the lamp (Dweep Prajwallan).
Swami Mukundananda then delivered the inaugural address, presenting the vision and mission of Jagadguru Kripalu University.
Following his address, Swami Mukundananda presented commemorative mementos to the Hon’ble President of India, the Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, and the other distinguished dignitaries. Each dignitary was presented with a beautifully crafted idol of the Trimurti: Lord Jagannath, Lord Balabhadra, and Devi Subhadra, along with a specially minted commemorative coin featuring the iconic Jagadguru Kripalu University building on one side and Jagadguru Shree Kripalu Ji Maharaj, Founder Acharya on the other. These commemorative gifts symbolized the university’s deep roots in Odisha’s sacred cultural heritage and its enduring commitment to preserving India’s timeless spiritual traditions while advancing excellence in higher education.
The gathering was subsequently addressed by the Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, followed by the Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, Dr Hari Babu Kambhampati.
The Hon’ble Chief Minister of Odisha, Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, described the inauguration of Jagadguru Kripalu University as the beginning of a transformative journey for higher education in Odisha. He noted that the university would serve as a world-class centre for learning, research, innovation, and character-building, integrating modern disciplines such as Artificial Intelligence, Cyber Security, Healthcare Sciences, and Business Management with India’s timeless spiritual values. Reaffirming the Government of Odisha’s commitment to quality education and skill development, he assured the university of the State Government’s continued support in its journey to nurture future-ready youth and contribute to the vision of a prosperous and developed Odisha.
The Hon’ble Governor of Odisha, Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, observed that Jagadguru Kripalu University embodies a vision of education that goes beyond degrees and careers. He remarked that true education must cultivate wisdom, integrity, compassion, and a spirit of selfless service alongside academic excellence. Paying tribute to Jagadguru Shri Kripalu Ji Maharaj and appreciating the efforts of Swami Mukundananda, the Governor said that the university would harmoniously blend India’s spiritual heritage with modern education, research, and innovation, preparing future leaders committed to the service of society and the nation.
The ceremony culminated with the inspiring keynote address of the Hon’ble President of India, Smt. Droupadi Murmu, who expressed confidence that Jagadguru Kripalu University would integrate India’s ancient cultural and spiritual heritage with modern education and emerge as a powerful institution dedicated to the service of society and the nation. She emphasized that education is the foundation of character building and nation-building, and urged universities to nurture youth with knowledge, values, integrity, and compassion. Appreciating JKU’s vision of promoting research, innovation, entrepreneurship, and holistic development, she conveyed her best wishes for the university to become a leading centre of excellence contributing to Viksit Odisha and Viksit Bharat.
The historic inauguration concluded with the audience once again standing together for the rendition of the National Song and the National Anthem.
We express our sincere appreciation to the Government of Odisha, the district administration, the police and security personnel, volunteers, and every individual who worked tirelessly behind the scenes to ensure the seamless planning and successful execution of this historic inauguration.
Our heartfelt thanks also go to the thousands of devotees and guests who travelled from near and far to be a part of this momentous occasion. Your enthusiastic participation, warmth, and support transformed this inauguration into a truly memorable celebration.
As Jagadguru Kripalu University embarks on its journey, we seek the continued blessings, goodwill, and support of all. Together, let us strive to build an institution that nurtures knowledge with wisdom, excellence with values, and leadership with selfless service for the benefit of society, the nation, and humanity.

text:
Lily Tomlin fell in love with Jane Wagner within minutes of seeing her in a New York hotel room in March 1971. More than five decades later, she still calls Jane the greatest love of her life.

Lily was already becoming one of America’s most distinctive comedians when a friend introduced her to Jane, a gifted writer from Tennessee. Lily had admired Jane’s television special about a neglected boy and wanted her help developing material. Yet work was not the first thing Lily noticed. “A friend brought her to my hotel room, and I tell you, in two minutes, I fell in love with her.” Jane wore hot pants, knee-high stretchy boots, and a small backpack. Lily left for Chicago soon afterward, but returned to New York and arranged their first date.

Their romance quickly became a creative partnership. Jane understood the feelings hiding beneath Lily’s characters, while Lily could turn Jane’s most delicate observations into movement, voices, and laughter. Lily once explained that they viewed people and the world in similar ways. Jane could put those feelings into words, and Lily could give them a body onstage. It was not simply writer and performer. Each woman completed an artistic sentence the other had started.

Lily’s praise for Jane was never casual. “She writes satirically but tenderly, and she loves farce and black comedy and broad slapstick. When you put all this together...” That combination became the emotional heartbeat of their work. Jane did not write jokes merely to earn applause. She found lonely people, overlooked women, wounded children, and outsiders, then allowed Lily to make audiences laugh before realizing their eyes were wet.

Their masterpiece together was the one-woman Broadway production “The Search for Signs of Intelligent Life in the Universe” (1985). Jane wrote a universe of characters and Lily inhabited them with astonishing speed and humanity. The performance brought Lily a Tony Award, but years later, while accepting a lifetime achievement honor, she made her private truth public in one unforgettable image. Jane, she said, was the person whose shoulders allowed her to stand tallest.

Love beside the spotlight was harder. In 1975, Lily was offered a TIME cover connected to publicly coming out. She declined because she wanted recognition for her work, not to be turned into a symbol chosen by someone else. She and Jane were living together, and people in their industry knew. Still, the language around them softened romance into friendship. At one workplace, someone even suggested that they arrive in separate cars because people were talking. Lily refused. They had already spent enough energy creating their lives. They would not waste more pretending they were strangers.

Jane later remembered finding each other as an ecstatic period, both creatively and personally. Her words reveal why their relationship lasted. They were not protecting only romance. They were protecting a shared imagination. Success never belonged entirely to one woman. Lily carried Jane’s language before audiences, while Jane gave Lily material that could be hilarious, wounded, strange, and compassionate at once. Their admiration became a daily form of devotion.

On December 31, 2013, after 42 years together, they married privately at a friend’s Los Angeles home. There were no carefully prepared wedding rings. Lily searched through their own jewelry because she felt they needed something to exchange. The moment was simple, almost improvised, and perfectly suited to two women who had already built a marriage in everything but name.

Lily later named Jane as the greatest love of her life and one of the writers who touched her most. That answer held romance, gratitude, and more than half a century of shared work inside a few words. Jane had loved the woman behind the voices. Lily had loved the woman behind the words.

They spent decades proving that love can whisper and still endure.

text:
Full translation of League related parts:

Part 1.
(In school, Xiaoyao showed great ability in math but became discouraged after students accused him of cheating. After being diagnosed with diabetes, he moved off-campus and lived alone with little parental supervision. He started playing League and reached No.7 in KR server.)

“A lot of teams added me on KR server, asking me if I was Chinese and interested in playing professionally.

I was intrigued.

I could never fit into the school system. In the eyes of a high school teacher, between a student that got 140 in math and 30 in English, and a student that got 80 in both, they would simply prefer the latter. Even though I was good at math, I couldn't force myself into learning subjects that I was not interested in.

I wanted a life of freedom. I dreamed of making money on my own, going wherever I wanted — supporting myself by playing games.

After a long discussion with my mom, I eventually dropped out and left on my own.

I finally had the freedom I wanted. It took me a while to realize that this wasn’t real freedom at all.

Part 2.
Many teams tried to recruit me, offering me a monthly salary around 5K RMB (740 USD) — the standard rate for an amateur player. One team offered me 8K RMB (1.2K USD), so I immediately joined them. I’d never seen that kind of money before.

The way people talk about professional gaming online, it sounds incredibly glamorous. But when I arrived, it was basically a shady internet cafe. They took away my ID as soon as I got there, gave me 7 RMB (1 USD) per day, and had me boosting other people's accounts all day.

I called a cab and ran away. I went to Anhui first, and then was recruited by another organization in Shanghai — by one of the top teams in China.

I’d always imagined it would be glamorous, living in a fancy villa and dating beautiful women. In reality, it was just a bunch of people crammed into a house playing video games.

We would wake up around noon and start playing till 2 or 3 AM every day. We probably got 1 day off every month. Every player came in with an esports dream. By the end, they were all sick of it. It was extremely tedious.

Most people there were used to shouting, screaming, and swearing. I was never yelled at, but I saw it happen to other players.

Some kids genuinely loved the game; they thought they were "the best in the world" before coming here. Then they realized that good players were everywhere. People in the industry wouldn't comfort you, saying things like "It's fine. Keep trying. I will give you time to grow." No. They would only say "If you can't play well, just get out of here." Some 18 or 19 year old kids were kicked out after just a few days.

Apart from the competitive pressure, the real issue was money.

My family stopped giving me money a long time ago. I was on an academy team, with no reputation or fans, making 6K RMB (900 USD) a month. The team would give out bonuses of tens of thousands RMB if you reached top 10 in the server — but that wasn't a regular income. Between the cost of living in Shanghai, treatment for my diabetes, and my online girlfriend asking me to buy her things, I couldn’t afford my living expenses.

Everyone depended on income from the "gray areas."

By that, I don't mean eloboosting — although there were rules prohibiting pro players from boosting, there was no real punishment even when someone was caught, so it doesn’t count.

The real "gray area" was playing "grudge matches" for other people. People get into fights for many reasons. For example, one person stole the other person's girlfriend, so they would arrange a League match, with each side putting down 20K RMB (3K USD). The winner takes the money, and the loser has to apologize publicly.

Our managers always knew where to find those matches and would send us to play. The winner usually didn’t end up keeping the money, so we split the money with the manager.

When I first joined the academy team, I was consistently among the best players there — my goal was to become a Worlds champion. I didn't think this was unrealistic. My home province, Hubei, had produced international champions before, like Clearlove and Jiejie.

At the time, I thought the manager valued me because I was performing well. He often took me to bars and karaoke lounges, paid for a few female hostesses, and ordered bottles of alcohol. A single night would cost 10-20K RMB (1.5-3K USD) but he would pay the bill.

Only later did I realize that I was being "set up".

I’d never been to places like that before — at first, I didn't know what to do. I just thought "Why are all the women in this bar so beautiful?". They surrounded me, praised me, and told me what an amazing player I was. I believed every word of it. I enjoyed it.

Later, whenever one of them would ask me to buy her something, I’d do it without hesitation. In reality, I barely had any money. I was only pretending to be generous.

At the time, I only had one goal: I had to make money. I had to make big money. I was born to be extraordinary. I had to make a name for myself.

But you couldn't make that much money in legitimate ways. After that, whenever the manager asked me to matchfix, I immediately agreed.

I eventually realized that those were their usual tricks. First, they’d good relationships with you by treating you to meals, even taking you to "massage parlors" — because "only people who had been through 'that' together could truly be brothers". Once a bond was formed, they would take you to drinking, to play Texas Hold'em, to gamble and spiral you into debt.

Even the few pros who later became famous were only 18 or 19 when they played on academy teams — they were extremely susceptible. Eventually, they ended up agreeing to matchfix to repay their debts.

It wasn’t only our team. Many organizations operate this way. The academy system was a money-losing system that existed to develop players. Within the entire esports industry, only Tier 1 League was profitable. In the past, Tier 2 organizations could promote to Tier 1 based on their performance. By the time I entered pro play, this was no longer possible. Tier 1 spots could only be purchased. The owners and managers, unable  to make any money, began directing their players towards matchfixing.

Of course, some people were capable of refusing. One of my friends told me that he played this game to make a name for himself — he wouldn't give up his dream because of some temporary difficulties.

I couldn't. I couldn't resist the temptation. Soon, my health condition began to deteriorate. Because of my diabetes, I needed to use the bathroom every 10 or 20 minutes. I couldn't make it through the entire game. I gave up on myself. I just wanted to make as much money as possible, leave Shanghai, and move to somewhere where I might be able to eat more healthily.

I’m still in contact with that friend with an esports dream. Absurdly, he recently told me, “I really regret not matchfixing back then.” In the end, he didn’t succeed as a pro player. As he got older and his mechanics declined, he couldn’t find any opportunities. He made no money and had no name recognition. He simply became a nobody.

Part 3.
I matchfixed for about 2 years. The coaches and managers would organize it for the entire team. They would usually reach an agreement with the bookmaker and then tell us to lose on purpose. A fixed game could pay us around 50K to 200K RMB (7.5K to 30K USD), which meant each person would receive around 20K to 50K RMB (3K to 7.5K USD) after being split among 6 or 7 people. The betting markets were overseas, so the authorities had no way of taking them down.

As time went on, and my health got worse, I couldn’t compete. Instead, I helped my teammates place bets. Everybody pooled in some money and divided the earnings, because they didn't trust an outsider with this job.

Over those 2 or 3 years, I made about 4 million RMB (600K USD), without ever being caught.

In the end, it was my “esports dream” that ruined me.

I was upset that I couldn't compete on stage playing the PC game, so I decided to switch to Wild Rift. The games were shorter, which allowed me to use the bathroom in between matches.

I adapted well on Wild Rift. After a month, I reached rank 1 on the CN server.

I didn’t realize, however, that the only reason I was never caught matchfixing before might’ve been that my previous manager was “professional.” I switched teams to play Wild Rift, and I continued to fix matches. I was reported after only one month.

In the middle of a series, the manager walked over to give me the news: “You can’t compete anymore. Start thinking about how you’re going to repay us.” He told me to return that month’s salary. According to the contract, if I was banned, the company had suffered a financial loss.

At that moment, it felt like everything in my life had collapsed. I wanted to die.

I tried every possible way to appeal. Many people were banned for a month but for me, it was a whole year. I wanted to see if I could reduce my punishment.

They told me they could unban me if I told them everything, so I confessed to it all. They banned me permanently.

I wasn’t even allowed to stream the game — I didn’t only participate in matchfixing, I also placed bets, which was technically gambling.

Later, I learned that the person who reported me was another player who got caught for matchfixing. The league told him that his punishment would be reduced if he reported other people, so he ratted me out. What an asshole. But that's how society works.

At the time, I blamed a lot of people. People who reported me. People who introduced me to matchfixing. I even blamed my mother — I believed that she was responsible for my diabetes. She lived overseas until I was in 4th grade. Throughout my childhood, my family rarely cooked at home for me and my diet has always been unhealthy. If I didn't have diabetes, my life would have been much better.

There was nothing I could do. I returned home in disgrace.

I had no plan. I was depressed. I just wanted to start a small eloboosting studio. At that time, Douyin/TikTok wasn't that popular. Even without much promotion, I could still earn about 20K RMB (3K USD) a month living in my small city, while spending half of my time working and the other half playing around.

The money I made from matchfixing was never taken away. To be honest, I had enough money to live comfortably for the rest of my life.

But because money came so easily for me, I had no sense of caution. People I had known for a few days would ask to borrow a few thousand RMB, and I would just give it away without much thought.

Then I met a guy who ran his own business. He drove an expensive car. He was ugly looking, but his girlfriend was really pretty. I particularly admire people like that. I thought he must have something special; some quality that entices beautiful women to date him. He asked to borrow money from me a couple of times, and he paid me back. He owned a couple of stores, and appeared legitimate. I gradually trusted him more and more.

Eventually, he borrowed about 2 to 3 million RMB (300K to 450K USD) in total and he couldn't pay me back. Then I found out that he’d been gambling in Macau.

He told me that he would take me to Macau so we could gamble and win our money back. He had already borrowed all of my money, so this was my last chance. I borrowed hundreds of thousands of RMB from my mom, and put together a total of around 1 million RMB (150K USD). We went, and we lost everything. My studio was shut down. I rented out my apartment. I didn't even have a computer.

My mom didn't say much. She told me that from now on, we were total strangers and she no longer had a son.

I can still blame others for my experiences in Shanghai. Now, I only have myself to blame.”

(Afterwards, he moved to Wuhan and starting doing food delivery. He has to work long hours to afford housing, food, and insulin. He feels  trapped in poverty. Still, he refuses to answer people who asked him for access to gambling or matchfixing. He believes that lessons can only be learned through experience. Now he finds comfort in literature and hopes that his life eventually improves.)

text:
$CIFR $SLNH

Texas Tightens the Queue – and Raises the Value of Controlled Power

Cipher Digital’s second-quarter call offered a useful read-through for Soluna’s Kati 2 project and the broader Texas data-center market.

Texas’ latest intervention delays clarity around Batch Zero, but it does not halt development. Cipher CEO Tyler Page framed the Governor’s directive as an extension of the batch process’s original purpose: separating credible projects from speculative load requests.

“They need a way to determine who is serious.”

Cipher said its relevant sites have funded deposits, secured land, completed water work and submitted the required studies and attestations. Page expects a stricter review could reduce the amount of load that ultimately remains in the queue, strengthening the relative position of developers that have already committed capital and completed the necessary work.

The more consequential signal came from the tenant side.

Historically, Page said, final interconnection approval was the dividing line before tenants engaged seriously. That threshold is beginning to move.

“We have had tenants interested in the sites awaiting Batch Zero.”

Cipher has already held lease discussions around Colchis, its planned 1 GW campus, even though the ERCOT process remains underway. Page also raised the possibility of a condition-precedent structure.

In practical terms, a tenant deal can be negotiated and potentially signed before the ERCOT process is fully concluded, with certain obligations remaining conditional on final interconnection approval, financing or other development milestones.

That distinction is important. Cipher did not claim that ERCOT approval had become unnecessary. It showed that commercial execution no longer has to wait for every regulatory step to finish. Tenant negotiations, design, legal work and financing preparation can advance in parallel with the grid process.

The strongest read-through came from behind-the-meter generation.

Page said sites capable of producing their own power had become more valuable following the Texas intervention.

“Any sites where we’re producing our own generation… are also now more valuable.”

Cipher is primarily evaluating natural-gas-based generation. Management described the opportunity as “potentially enormous” and said its potential could exceed the rest of the company’s current portfolio.

Soluna’s architecture is different. Kati 2 starts with colocated renewable power and is being developed around a broader hybrid system that can include grid supply, on-site gas and potentially battery storage. The underlying principle is the same: when the grid cannot provide sufficient certainty on the required schedule, developers capable of bringing more of the power solution to the site gain leverage.

Cipher’s comments support a more precise reading of Kati 2’s development path.

Final interconnection approval, shovel-ready development and tenant execution are connected, but they are not the same milestone. The ERCOT process remains important, yet it does not automatically stop design, permitting, financing preparation or tenant work.

Texas is not making controlled power less valuable. It is increasing the premium on projects backed by real land, real studies, real capital and a credible plan to serve large loads without placing the entire burden on the grid.

For Soluna, that strengthens the strategic logic behind Kati 2: not as a way to bypass ERCOT, but as a more resilient path from power to compute.

A recently unearthed clip from a 2024 episode of The State of Belief podcast highlights this problem.
Talarico appeared alongside another guest, Texas state Representative Salman Bhojani, who is a Muslim. This kind of interfaith dialogue, it doesn’t water down your tradition; in fact, it strengthens it. It brings out new flavors and new colors.”

text:
Korean vs China: Memory war 👇

Samsung and SK Hynix are pushing custom HBM to lock in big-tech customers and shape next-generation standards.

As AI chips move beyond GPUs into ASICs and NPUs, customer requirements are diverging. 

The Korean firms are adjusting base-die structures, optimizing interfaces, and combining foundry and packaging capabilities to deliver memory tailored to specific AI systems.

Samsung plans to leverage its dual memory-and-foundry strength to offer integrated logic, memory, and advanced packaging solutions. 

SK Hynix is expanding beyond pure supply into joint design partnerships with AI customers. 

The shift means competition is moving from pure volume toward who can design memory that fits a customer’s AI architecture.

China is pursuing a different route. Restricted access to advanced HBM and leading-edge processes has pushed Chinese players toward 3D IC, chiplet, and hybrid-bonding approaches. 

Instead of matching high-end HBM directly, they are stacking existing memory or using packaging techniques to boost system performance. 

Some industry voices see China as relatively advanced in certain 3D stacking methods and note that highly customized DRAM may be more economically viable for Chinese producers than for the volume-focused Korean model.

Questions remain about how far vertical stacking can scale given heat, power delivery, and yield challenges. 

Still, the broader trend is clear: as AI semiconductors diversify, customer-specific memory is gaining weight over purely standard products.

Which approach do you see as more durable for the next phase of AI memory demand?

text:
how to sell an ai offer, on a discovery call, including the cold DM that gets you there:

cold DM: “saw [specific thing about their business] — built a quick breakdown of how we could fix [specific problem] for you, no strings. want it?”

lead with the specific use case, never “ai” as a category. nobody buys “ai.” they buy the problem it solves.

discovery call:

- “walk me through the manual process right now.” get them to describe the pain in their own words before you mention automation at all

- “how much time/money is that actually costing you a week?” make the cost concrete, not abstract

- “what have you tried already, ai or otherwise?” find out if they’re skeptical from a bad past experience, that changes your whole approach

- “if this got automated tomorrow, what would you do with that time back?” 

get them picturing the outcome, not the tool

the pitch, once you’ve discovered: name the specific outcome, not the tech. “this frees up 10 hours a week” beats “we build custom ai workflows” every time. 

nobody’s buying the model. they’re buying their time back.

close on the outcome, not the build.

 Underperformance is Real 📉

Unlikely. Despite leadership churn, the RBI issued an explicit clarification in 2026 confirming "no material governance or conduct concerns," calling it a "sound, professionally run board." This claim hits home. High private sector attrition (~25%), aggressive sales targets, and post-merger tech friction have impacted branch experience, leading to a surge in RBI Ombudsman complaints. Retraining staff and balancing cross-sell pressure with service quality is urgent.

Nvidia pays new grads about $198k, Amazon about $178k - by senior level though, Amazon is ahead by nearly $90k

New grads tend to fixate on the number in their offer letter. A more useful metric might be how much room there is to grow inside the company.

So we compared entry level software engineer comp to senior comp* across companies to see where the differential is largest. @OpenAI, @LinkedIn and @databricks lead, all between 2.4x and 2.6x.

This framing probably only applies to bigger tech companies. At an earlier stage startup you’re betting on the startup itself growing, and that trumps everything else.

But at a large company, knowing how you’ll grow internally is pretty useful. Especially if you plan to be there long term.

* 3rd level, L3 on https://t.co/q2NOapsdJO’s leveling standard, used to normalize scope and responsibility across companies

SpaceX is not “govt funded” in the sense of free money, grants, or subsidies that simply pad Elon’s net worth. The large majority of what people call “government funding” is competitive, fixed-price contracts for actual services the U.S. government needs and buys:
•  Cargo and crew transport to the ISS
•  National security / NRO / Space Force launches
•  Starshield (secure government constellation)
•  Artemis Human Landing System work
These are services delivered. NASA and the DoD pay for results (rockets that fly, astronauts that return safely, satellites that reach orbit). SpaceX repeatedly won them because it offered the lowest price and the highest reliability after the Shuttle retired and Soyuz became the only alternative. That is the opposite of a handout.

text:
As anticipation continues to build for Christopher Nolan's upcoming The Odyssey, historians, archaeologists, and ancient warfare enthusiasts are debating one key question: What would the real Odysseus have looked like?

A striking reconstruction by Greek armor maker Katsikis Dimitrios (HellenicArmors) presents an answer grounded in archaeological evidence rather than cinematic interpretation. The recreation depicts Odysseus wearing authentic Mycenaean Bronze Age armor, based on surviving archaeological finds from the Late Bronze Age—the period in which the Trojan War is traditionally believed to have taken place.

According to the latest research of Professor St. Papamarinopoulos, the fall of Troy occurred around 1218 BC, while Odysseus is believed to have returned to Ithaca approximately 1207 BC after his legendary ten-year journey. If these dates are accepted, the king of Ithaca would have been equipped not with later classical Greek armor familiar to modern audiences, but with the sophisticated bronze panoplies used by Mycenaean warriors.

The reconstruction features the characteristic bronze cuirass, protective shoulder guards, helmet, greaves, and large shield associated with Mycenaean elite soldiers. Such equipment closely resembles famous archaeological discoveries, including the Dendra Panoply, one of the oldest nearly complete suits of armor ever found.

For many historians, this type of reconstruction highlights an important distinction between historical reality and cinematic storytelling. While filmmakers often adapt costumes for dramatic effect or visual appeal, archaeological evidence suggests that the heroes celebrated in Homer's epics belonged to a very different military culture from the one commonly portrayed in popular media.

As Christopher Nolan prepares to bring The Odyssey to the big screen, discussions surrounding historical authenticity continue to grow. Reconstructions like this offer audiences a glimpse into how the legendary king of Ithaca may have truly appeared—a Bronze Age warrior shaped by the world of Mycenaean Greece rather than the later image of the classical Greek hoplite.

Whether Nolan's version ultimately embraces historical accuracy or artistic interpretation, the debate has already sparked renewed global interest in Mycenaean civilization and the archaeological legacy behind one of history's greatest epic tales.

#archaeohistories

text:
Robert Duvall was 65 when a closed flower shop changed the final three decades of his life. 

In Buenos Aires in 1996, he went looking for flowers, found the shop shut, and walked toward a bakery instead. 

Years later, he still sounded amazed by the accident behind everything that followed. 

“The flower shop was closed, so I went to the bakery. If the flower shop had been open, I never would’ve met her.” 

Luciana Pedraza was 24, and an ordinary detour had just become their love story.

One small change of plans.

One life-changing meeting.

Luciana's friends recognized the famous actor. They knew he loved Argentine tango and urged her to invite him to a party.

She almost didn't.

Later, she admitted she barely knew who he was. But she handed him her card anyway.

And he showed up.

To Luciana, he wasn't an Oscar winner.

He was simply Bobby.

As they spent time together, they discovered another surprise. Both were born on January 5, exactly 41 years apart.

The age gap worried Duvall.

Luciana's father turned it into a joke, asking whether he should call Duvall his son or his father.

Tango soon became the heartbeat of their relationship.

They danced together everywhere life took them, even at a White House state dinner honoring Argentina's president in 1999.

One invitation had become a lifelong rhythm.

Their partnership reached the screen.

Duvall cast Luciana beside him in *Assassination Tango*. They later worked together again, trusting each other on camera just as they did in life.

Away from Hollywood, they chose something quieter.

They married in 2005 and divided their lives between Argentina and Virginia. One offered tango, cafés, and family.

The other offered horses, open fields, and peace.

When Duvall turned 90, he summed up his happiness in the simplest way.

"My wonderful wife... She takes care of me."

Luciana became part of every chapter that followed. She encouraged his work, kept him active, and stood beside him through the passing years.

Public attention never defined them.

Their everyday life did.

Robert Duvall died peacefully at home on February 15, 2026, at 95.

Luciana's farewell wasn't for a legend.

It was for the man she called everything.

Sometimes the biggest love stories begin because one ordinary door happened to be closed.

text:
Filipino filmmakers Lav Diaz and John Torres are set to bring their latest works to two of the world’s most prestigious film festivals, marking a strong showing for Philippine cinema on the global stage.

Diaz returns to the La Biennale di Venezia, set for August 26 to September 5, with “Makikiraan Po (Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors),” which will screen in the out-of-competition section. The selection comes two years after his last appearance at the festival and coincides with the 10th anniversary of his Golden Lion win for “Ang Babaeng Humayo,” as announced by producer Hazel Orencio.

Written and directed by Diaz, the film is set in 1617 during the Spanish colonial period in Las Islas Filipinas. It centers on Padre Enciso, a friar and encomendero who enforces brutal rule while pursuing the construction of a marble church altar.

He assigns his son, Dungwen, to lead a perilous mission transporting the materials across bandit-ridden terrain, where they face the feared marauder Baribari. At the same time, a local healer, Babayeng Intimatandog, defies Enciso by sustaining indigenous Malay traditions, setting up a clash between colonial authority and native belief.

The cast includes Bart Guingona, Ronnie Lazaro, Isabel Sandoval, Christian Bables, Yul Servo Nieto, Bong Cabrera, Rafa Siguion-Reyna, Sri Arjhay Babon, Necias Pataunia, and Daniel Palisa. The film is produced by Monty Blencowe and Bianca Balbuena-Liew.

Meanwhile, Torres is set to premiere his latest feature, “The Remotes” (2026), at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), which will run from September 10 to 20. The film will screen under the Wavelengths section and marks his narrative debut after years of working in experimental cinema.

The film marks his narrative debut after years of working in experimental cinema.

Written by Torres and Do Dayao, “The Remotes” follows a grieving detective whose investigation into a strange case pulls him into a web tied to a sinister navigation app. As the probe unfolds, the technology leaves both physical and psychological damage in its wake, blurring the lines between reality and perception.

The film stars Alchris Galura, Gabby Padilla, Julia Richards, and Enchong Dee. Torres is expected to attend two public screenings at the TIFF Lightbox and participate in post-screening Q&A sessions. 

Backed by Los Otros, it is produced by Torres, Sherad Anthony Sanchez, and Shireen Seno.
La Biennale di Venezia, the world’s oldest film festival, and TIFF, one of the most influential platforms for contemporary cinema, are both key launchpads for international exposure. 

Selections in their official programs signal strong artistic recognition and offer Filipino filmmakers wider visibility, critical attention, and potential global distribution.

(✍️: Marinel Cruz)

text:
Atiku Abubakar’s economic promise will not be reform by surprise. It will be reform with consultation, notice, preparation and protection for ordinary Nigerians.

No trader will wake up to discover that a sudden policy has doubled transport costs. No manufacturer will lose an entire investment because government changed currency, fuel or tax rules overnight. No family business will collapse because officials announced a major reform without explaining how citizens will survive the transition.

Nigeria needs bold decisions, but boldness without preparation becomes punishment.

An Atiku and Amaechi administration will consult workers, manufacturers, farmers, transporters, professionals and state governments before implementing policies with nationwide consequences. It will publish timelines, explain expected effects and create temporary support for vulnerable households and businesses.

Atiku understands that economic confidence depends on predictability. Investors will commit capital when rules are clear. Businesses will hire when costs can be planned. Families will adjust when government communicates honestly and provides enough time to prepare.

Rotimi Amaechi will bring the implementation discipline required to ensure that reforms move from announcement to responsible delivery.

The APC removed critical economic supports without adequate preparation, then asked Nigerians to endure the consequences while officials celebrated theoretical gains.

ADC will offer a different leadership culture.

Reforms will be bold, but they will also be humane. Decisions will be decisive, but never careless. Nigerians will understand what is changing, why it is changing and how government will protect them during the transition.

Atiku will rebuild confidence. Amaechi will coordinate implementation. ADC will govern with courage, competence and compassion.
