text:
LETTERS FROM STOCKHOLM

THE FIVE-MINUTE WARNING: WHAT ADELEKE SHOULD HAVE READ AT ILE-IFE

By Kio Amachree | Worldview International

He was singing. That was his offence.

On 7 December 2025, at the tenth coronation anniversary of the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, the Governor of Osun State stood at the podium doing what the whole of Nigeria knows him for. Before him sat former President Olusegun Obasanjo, serving and former governors, senators, and the traditional rulers of Yorubaland. And the wife of the President of the Federal Republic — an unelected citizen, newly installed that day as Yeye Asiwaju Gbogbo Ile Oodua — rose from her seat, walked to the podium of a sitting Chief Executive of a Nigerian state, and told him: five minutes, or I switch off this microphone.

Twice she went up. The world watched.

Dele Momodu called it what it was — the public disgrace of a Governor before a global audience, in his own state. Mrs Tinubu called the outrage a "needless controversy."

It was not a controversy. It was a disclosure.

WHAT THE GESTURE ACTUALLY MEANT

Read the choreography, not the words. A woman who holds no office recognised by the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria overruled a man who holds one of the highest offices that Constitution creates — and did it reflexively, in public, without hesitation, in front of the assembled political class of the South West. Reflex is the tell. Nobody rehearses that. It comes from an internalised belief about where authority actually resides.

Momodu diagnosed the motive precisely: the objective is that every governor, North, East, West, should join the APC, so that one man may be emperor in word and in deed. Anyone who declines is an enemy.

Adeleke declined. He left the PDP on 2 December 2025 and took the Accord Party ticket rather than walk into the tent. And in his own words at the time, he was almost deferential about the man whose wife had just silenced him: "I believe our president is a democrat. He's been in this position before. When he was in opposition, I learned a lot from him."

That was the error. He was reading a rulebook the other side had already put down.

THE BILL ARRIVES: 5 AUGUST 2026

Ten days before the polls, we have the answer to what the five-minute ultimatum was foreshadowing.

By letter dated 5 August 2026, referenced 3000/EFCC/ABJ/HQ/PFS/TA/OSUN/VOL.17/666, signed by Assistant Commander Adenike Babalola for the Director of Investigation, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission directed First Bank to place a Post-No-Debit restriction on the Osun State Government Statutory Allocation account, number 2017170947. This is a salary account. The wages of Osun's workers, frozen in the final fortnight of a governorship campaign.

The Commission says it has been investigating since March 2026, alleging fraudulent handling of Ecology Funds, Intervention Funds and FAAC allocations to the tune of eleven billion naira, and that it acted because of movements of funds since 2 August. Fine. Let those allegations be tested — in court, with evidence, on the record. Corruption in Osun is not to be excused because the accuser is compromised.

But note the timing, and note the asymmetry. The Governor has directed the State Attorney-General to challenge the order at the Federal High Court in Osogbo, and has asked the EFCC Chairman a simple question: show the proof, publicly. He further alleges that over sixty Accord members have been arrested and moved to Abuja without charge, that the local government system has been deliberately paralysed, and that party members have been killed.

Osun votes on Saturday 15 August 2026 — a date INEC itself shifted from 8 August under the new Electoral Act 2026. Campaigns close at midnight on 13 August. In 2022, Adeleke took the state by 403,371 votes to Gboyega Oyetola's 375,027 — a margin of roughly 28,000. In a contest that tight, a state government without access to its own salary account is not a state government. It is a hostage.

This is not anti-corruption. It is anti-corruption's uniform, worn to a robbery.

THE LESSON FOR EVERY MAN CURRENTLY CHEERING

To those in Osun and beyond who are applauding this week's federal manoeuvre, I offer a single observation.

Power exercised as personal property cannot be inherited by institutions — only seized by individuals. A system in which a President's wife may silence a Governor, in which an agency's letterhead may substitute for a court order, and in which a son with no elected office moves through Aso Rock with the standing of a minister, is not a strong system. It is a brittle one. It has no internal mechanism for succession, no rule to appeal to, and no restraint but loyalty — and loyalty, in Nigerian politics, has the shelf life of a market tomato.

The men now being trained to break the rules on the President's behalf are, by that very training, being taught how the rules are broken. They will not forget the lesson when their own turn comes.

So I will say it again, as I have said before: the danger to this presidency is not the opposition. It is the circle. It is the ambition sitting at the table, nodding. When the succession question turns from theory into schedule — and the open speculation about a dynastic handover has made that inevitable — the knives will come from inside, because inside is where the knives have been sharpened.

WHAT MUST HAPPEN NOW

Let this be plain, and let it be lawful. The removal I call for is the removal every constitutional democracy provides:

That the Federal High Court in Osogbo determine, urgently, whether the EFCC has any statutory power to freeze the statutory allocation account of a federating state, and set the order aside if it does not.

That the EFCC publish its evidence, or withdraw. An agency that acts against a sitting state government ten days before a poll has forfeited the presumption of good faith and must earn it back in public.

That INEC's leadership, and the security services deployed to Osun, understand that the whole world will be reading the returns from 3,763 polling units across thirty local governments on 15 August.

That the National Assembly cease its slumber and legislate a clear bar on the freezing of subnational treasuries within ninety days of an election.

And that the voters of Osun — all 2,339,233 of them — answer this at the ballot box. Not in the streets. Not with blood. With their thumbs.

Nigeria does not need another strongman removed by force. It needs one removed by law, and the precedent that follows.

The First Lady gave a Governor five minutes. The Nigerian people have given this administration four years. Only one of those clocks matters.

Kio Amachree writes from Stockholm.

⚡️Chinese private capital is beginning to reach the same conclusion Chinese state capital reached first:

The domestic financial system no longer offers a clean store of confidence.

Property no longer carries the old inevitability.

Equities remain exposed to policy.

Deposits preserve nominal value while losing strategic optionality.

Capital controls limit escape.

Gold becomes the asset that sits outside every one of those traps while remaining locally accessible.

That is why this matters more than fourteen days of ETF inflows.

Chinese households are searching for a form of wealth that the property cycle cannot impair, corporate governance cannot dilute, monetary policy cannot quietly erode, and geopolitical escalation cannot strand inside another country’s jurisdiction.

Gold satisfies that demand better than anything else available at scale.

The state is doing the same thing from the sovereign side.

The central bank wants reserves that cannot be frozen.

The household wants savings that cannot be trapped inside a failing domestic asset regime.

One is protecting national optionality.

The other is protecting personal optionality.

Both arrive at gold.

That convergence reveals the actual transition.

Gold demand is spreading from institutions protecting against geopolitical fracture to households protecting against institutional fragility.

Once both layers begin buying for the same underlying reason, price sensitivity changes.

Buyers stop asking whether gold is cheap.

They ask how much exposure they can afford to remain without.

That creates a structurally different market.

Corrections attract allocation rather than destroy belief.

Higher prices validate the thesis rather than exhaust it.

Demand becomes reflexive because the rising price confirms the loss of confidence that caused the buying.

The deeper meaning reaches beyond China.

The global monetary system is fragmenting into two layers.

Financial assets remain the primary tools for growth and yield.

Neutral collateral becomes the insurance layer beneath them.

Gold is being repriced because the insurance layer was too small for the amount of political, monetary, and sovereign risk now moving into it.

China is central because it contains enormous trapped savings, a damaged property engine, limited external escape routes, and a state openly reducing dependence on foreign reserve claims.

The Catechism of the Catholic Church teaches that purgatory is a state of final purification for those who die in God’s friendship but who still need to be purified before entering the fullness of heaven. It is not a second chance at salvation, nor is it the same as hell. Those in purgatory are already saved; they are being prepared to see God face to face.

Here are the key Catechism passages:

CCC 1030 – What is Purgatory?

“All who die in God’s grace and friendship, but still imperfectly purified, are indeed assured of their eternal salvation; but after death they undergo purification, so as to achieve the holiness necessary to enter the joy of heaven.”

Meaning: Even forgiven Christians may still have lingering attachments to sin or the temporal effects of sin. God’s love completes their purification.

CCC 1031 – Biblical Foundation

The Catechism points to:

1 Corinthians 3:13–15 – A person’s work is tested “as through fire,” yet the person is saved.
2 Maccabees 12:44–46 – Judas Maccabeus offers prayers for the dead, showing belief that the dead can benefit from our prayers.

The Catechism also notes that the Church’s teaching is rooted in Sacred Tradition, drawing especially from early Church councils such as the Council of Florence and the Council of Trent.

Two prisoners — one of them a former member of Comando Vermelho, a major Brazilian criminal organization — received the sacraments of Christian initiation (baptism, Eucharist, and confirmation) on Sunday, July 26, at the Gameleira 2 maximum-security state menʼs penitentiary in Campo Grande, Brazil.

Both men received the sacraments after two years of catechesis provided by the prison ministry of the Archdiocese of Campo Grande.

“What is the primary objective of prison ministry? Education, celebration, and life in the faith,” explained Said Brandão Sayd, the ministry’s coordinator, in an interview with ACI Digital, the Portuguese-language sister service of EWTN News.

“Our principal goal is to have a Catholic community within the prison — to ensure that people, even amid all those difficulties, receive the Church’s help and can effectively leave that place or live there in a state of grace,” he added.

The sacraments were administered by Father Álisson Muryel, the ecclesiastical adviser for the prison ministry in the Archdiocese of Campo Grande, an area that, according to Brandão, has 11 prisons and nearly 10,000 inmates. The ministry is “present in all the prisons,” he said.

Without going into details regarding the personal information of the prisoners who received the sacraments, Brandão noted that one of them is single and “due to leave soon.”

“He wants to rebuild his life; he wants to do it differently,” Brandão said.

The other man, “who is staying longer,” is in “a stable relationship but wants to receive the sacrament of marriage.”

The coordinator explained that “in the second half of the year,” they are going to “prepare him for this sacrament.”

Brandão told ACI Digital that there is a team of catechists, supported by a parish, at every prison in the archdiocese. “Our meetings always follow this pattern, prioritizing catechesis,” he said. “Above all else, the Catholic Church needs to go in there [into the prison] and proclaim the message,” he added.

According to Brandão, it is not enough simply to “offer a hug” or “be deeply concerned about human rights, important as that is ... But if you don’t speak about Jesus in there, who will?”

“Without that, there is no conversion,” he affirmed.

According to Brandão, there are prisons where the pastoral team is able to be present every week, while in others, due to scheduling restrictions, meetings take place every two weeks.

“Since it is organized by cellblock, the blocks cannot be mixed. So, we go in, visiting two blocks one week, another two the next, and carry out the work there in that way,” Brandão explained.

Through this process, the inmates follow a program lasting one or two years, depending on the frequency of the monthly catechesis sessions.

During the meetings, they work on the four dimensions of the faith: the creed, the commandments, prayer, and the sacraments. That period of preparation, Brandão noted, is intended to ensure the inmate “is aware of what he is receiving, and embraces it ... it is a great responsibility to prepare them so they understand what the faith is.”

However, Brandão pointed out, providing good catechesis is pointless without the sacraments, and that is why a monthly Mass is held at the prison. At Gameleira 2, Mass is celebrated once a month in one of the four cellblocks. “So, each block has three Masses a year,” he explained.

Mass is preceded by a time of confession for those who have already received the sacraments of baptism and the Eucharist.

After the prisoners are released from the correctional facility, pastoral care workers encourage them to continue attending a parish near their homes.

“We do not know what is happening in each person’s heart, but the Word is reaching them, and the Gospel is being proclaimed,” Brandão concluded.

Most signed job offers aren't employment contracts in the US and he'd almost certainly be at-will, so the new employer can go "Aww jeez, guess we're not hiring anymore :(" and not a whole lot happens.

In some states like California, he might be able to get unemployment despite resigning since leaving for a huge wage increase, relying upon that when turning in his two weeks, then having it yanked away last moment can be viewed as good cause so they'd possibly get some benefits. It'd be tough, though. Resigning and getting unemployment is almost always an uphill battle and will end in failure. He could very easily be denied if he's in a state that doesn't care about that reasoning or because the state read the job offer and said "oh, it says at-will and it can be rescinded at any time, retard."

He could sue for promissory estoppel because he reasonably expected that job to work out, but I don't know how much that'd pay out if it would pay anything at all. My guess is that if that lawsuit was at all scary to the new employer, then they'd have just let the hire go through and make up a reason to at-will fire him in the first month because that'd make the potential lawsuit go away fast.

He's in a nightmare scenario. Hopefully he built up some savings.

Holy fucking shit! Dark truth.💔

"Whatever AI model and corresponding prompt produced, Tuesday’s image failed the film, never mind the man. 

Its “Patton” wears a bare helmet where the starred, lacquered one should sit; 

its “MacArthur” smokes a generic English briar in place of a corncob so famous that the Missouri Meerschaum Company, in business since 1869, still sells a model in his name.

The insignia belong to no army in particular, though a few belong to a very particular army: 

the “Patton” figure’s red collar tabs and red-piped shoulder boards run closer to Soviet pattern than to anything the U.S. Army has ever issued, and the star-shaped order screwed flat to the center figure’s chest sits the way Moscow pinned its decorations, where American orders hang from ribbons.

What we see is a texture called “WWII general” with celebrated names captioned on top; the past worn as costume rather than consulted as record.

History kept better notes than the AI model was able to reproduce. Of all the commanders in the American pantheon, Trump’s caption reaches for the two most famously at war with civilian control of the military. 

Truman relieved MacArthur in April 1951 for public insubordination over Korea, and the firing became a constitutional lesson learned by every officer: generals answer to elected civilians. 

Patton, brilliant in the field and unemployable at peace, slapped two hospitalized soldiers in Sicily and spent his last years testing a chain of command that finally stopped indulging him.

Both men carry a darker credential. 

In July 1932 MacArthur, then-Army chief of staff, commanded the eviction of the Bonus Army — thousands of destitute veterans camped in Washington, D.C. — and by most accounts pressed the operation far further than Hoover had authorized, even ignoring his command to stop the assault. 

Then-Major George S. Patton led the cavalry, and infantry followed with tear gas. That morning District police, attempting to clear a downtown camp, had opened fire, killing William Hushka, a Lithuanian immigrant, and mortally wounding Eric Carlson of Oakland, both veterans of the war; their deaths gave Hoover his justification for calling in the Army.

The veterans and their families were driven out under threat of severe violence, and their camps and belongings were burned. 

As documented by Paul Dickson and Thomas B. Allen, authors of The Bonus Army, 55 veterans were injured and 135 were arrested. One veteran’s wife miscarried. Another’s malnourished 4-year-old son died.

Less than two weeks after the evacuation, 3-month-old Bernard Myers, the son of a bonus marcher from Pennsylvania, died in a Washington hospital. His parents said the infant’s health had deteriorated after he inhaled tear gas.

Countless marchers suffered injuries at the hands of the soldiers, and many lost their possessions in the fires. Yet for all the protesters’ sacrifices and efforts, a divided Congress did not pass the legislation granting them immediate compensation for their war service. As the veterans disbanded and settled in camps across the country, their campaign seemed a complete failure.

In other words, flanking Trump in his AI-generated fantasy are the two officers most famously associated with insubordination and the two most storied soldiers on the scene the last time the Army attacked an encampment of American civilians in the capital.

Tuesday’s image tramples the Constitution’s intentional subordination of the military beneath the office now borrowing its clothes.

Images like this one get waved through as jokes, yet the levity holds more weight than it admits. Because the composite is self-evidently fake, it carries built-in deniability while still performing all the same symbolic work. 

Nothing here was offered as fact, so there is nothing to  fact-check. Trump depicting himself as a WWII general cannot be  debunked, only objected to, and the objection itself is the product."

text:
A Living Experiment in Human Conversation

In the middle of an attention economy engineered for fragmentation, speed, and outrage, one sustained experiment quietly demonstrates another possibility.

Every week, an Army veteran known as FamousInMyPhone hosts what is believed to be the world's only one-person, 24-hour marathon Space on X. For more than a year—and across more than eighty consecutive episodes—he has remained live on the microphone for an entire day and night.

People from every continent join. Some stay for ten minutes. Others remain for many hours. Together they share conversation, music, lived experience, quiet reflection, humor, and simple human presence.

There are no talking points. No hidden agenda. No ideology to sell. No debate stage.

Only respect, curiosity, and an open invitation to witness our shared humanity.

This is not a performance.

It is a living record.

What It Looks Like in Practice

A typical marathon begins on a Wednesday morning and continues until the following morning.

Listeners arrive from Tokyo, Lagos, São Paulo, rural America, Australia, and small towns across Europe. Someone shares the story of losing a parent. Another plays a song that shaped their youth. A veteran speaks honestly about the transition back into civilian life. A young person from another continent asks sincere questions and unexpectedly stays for hours.

Strangers who entered as anonymous usernames gradually become familiar voices.

People who never intended to speak often discover they have something worth saying.

The conversations wander naturally—from philosophy and science to music, recovery, travel, books, family, faith, and everyday life—but they consistently return to the same foundation: listening before judging.

Unlike so much of modern social media, there is no reward for outrage, performance, or tribal identity.

The only enduring expectation is simple human respect.

Over twenty-four uninterrupted hours, something unusual begins to emerge.

Time itself becomes part of the conversation.

The pace slows.

Trust develops naturally.

Strangers become companions.

The result is something remarkably rare online: an attention sanctuary—a place slow enough for genuine listening, long enough for unexpected friendships to form, and open enough that anyone may arrive or leave without pressure or obligation.

Why Consistency Matters

Most online platforms reward speed, conflict, and constant novelty.

These weekly marathon Spaces demonstrate the opposite.

The same host simply shows up.

Week after week.

Hour after hour.

Holding the microphone open for whoever arrives.

That consistency has already carried the project into Guinness World Records territory for sustained one-person marathon broadcasting, with formal recognition currently being pursued.

Yet the greatest achievement is not the possibility of a record.

text:
In the midst of an attention economy designed for fragmentation, one sustained experiment quietly demonstrates another possibility.

Every week an Army veteran known as FamousInMyPhone hosts what is believed to be the world's only one-man 24-hour marathon Space on X. For more than a year, across more than eighty consecutive episodes, he has remained live on the microphone for a full day and night, bringing together people from every continent through conversation, music, stories, and simple human presence. There are no talking points, no hidden agenda, and no ideology to sell.....only respect, curiosity, 
and an open invitation to bear witness to our shared humanity.

This is not performance. It is a living record!

In a medium that rewards speed, outrage, and brevity, these marathon Spaces create an attention sanctuary—slow enough for genuine listening, long enough for strangers to become companions, and open enough that anyone may come and go freely.

Through remarkable consistency, the project has entered Guinness World Records territory, with formal recognition currently being pursued. Yet the true achievement is not the record itself. It is the weekly demonstration that respectful, high-integrity communication across borders remains possible when one person simply shows up and faithfully holds the space.

A vision naturally follows: ethical support that matches the long view of the experiment. Imagine a single gift offered purely as an expression of six years of gratitude....

not an investment, 
not a purchase, 
not an attempt to gain influence. 

No equity. 

No ownership. 

No expectation of financial return.

Only the practical freedom for the work to continue exactly as it already does: free, respectful, agenda-less, and open to all.

Complete independence is essential.

The host remains entirely free to continue, adapt, or end the project according to his own judgment. 

Any gift would carry no claim upon the conversation, no privileged voice in the room, and no subtle obligation. 

It would be gratitude expressed in a way that protects rather than possesses.

Such support is uncommon because it asks for genuine humility: the strength to give without seeking control. The Spaces neither depend upon nor wait for such generosity. 

They continue each week regardless. Existing avenues already allow contributions of any size from those who simply wish to help sustain the work.

For those who recognize the quiet power of sustained, respectful human gathering, the invitation is simple. Join a Space. Listen. Participate if you wish. Support only if it genuinely moves you.

If you are someone capable of offering meaningful long-term support, and you understand the value of preserving independent, worldwide dialogue, please contact FamousInMyPhone directly. 

Serious inquiries are welcome.

Time wasters, proposals seeking control, or offers that compromise the independence of the project are respectfully declined.

Ultimately, this living experiment remains what it has always been: a weekly reminder that when given enough time, patience, and goodwill, people from every corner of the world can still meet one another beyond the noise. 

The invitation is not merely to support a project, but to honor a practice that quietly demonstrates a better way to communicate—through presence, patience, freedom, and our shared humanity.

text:
August 5 Saint Oswald of Northumbria, Saxon King who planted first Cross in Bernicia, through which many miracles were obtained.
605 - 642
Patronage: Zug, Switzerland
.
The English Saxon kingdom of the Northumbers was founded by Ida in 547. After his death the northern part called Bernicia was preserved by his children; but Deira, that is, the southern part, comprising Yorkshire and Lancashire, was occupied by Ælla or Alla, and after his death was recovered by Ethelfrid, grandson of Ida, who ruled the whole kingdom of the Northumbers twenty-four years. He being slain in battle by Redwald, king of the East-Angles, in 617, his sons Eanfrid, Oswald, and Oswi took refuge among the Scots, where they were instructed in the Christian faith, and received the sacrament of regeneration. In the meantime, Edwin, the son of Alla, reigned seventeen years over both kingdoms; but in 633 was killed fighting against the united forces of Penda the Mercian, and Cadwalla, king of the Britons or Welch, a Christian by profession, but a stranger to the maxims of his religion; in his manners a barbarian, and an implacable enemy to the English Saxons. Upon this revolution the three sons of Ethelfrid returned from Scotland; and Eanfrid, the eldest, obtained the kingdom of the Deira, whilst Osric, cousin-german to Edwin, was chosen King of Bernicia. Both these princes loved the glory of men more than God, and apostatized from the faith which they had embraced; but were both slain the same year by Cadwalla; Osric in battle, and the other soon after by treachery. Hereupon Oswald was called to the crown, both of Deira and Bernicia, he being the son of Ethelfrid, and nephew of Edwin, whose sister Acca was his mother. He was also the brother of Saint Ebbe the Elder, and  nephew of Saint Ethelreda.
.
This prince had embraced the faith with his whole heart, and far from forsaking Christ, as his unhappy brothers had done, to court the favour of his subjects, he had no other view than to bring them to the spiritual kingdom of divine grace, and to labour with them to secure a crown of eternal glory.
.
At that time Cadwalla ravaged all the Northumbrian provinces, not as a conqueror, but as a cruel tyrant, laying every thing waste with fire and sword, at the head of a vast army, which he boasted nothing could resist. Oswald assembled what troops he was able, and being fortified by faith in Christ, marched confidently, though with a small force, against this mighty enemy, who had by that time proceeded as far as the Picts’ wall. Oswald gave him battle at a place called by Bede Denis-burn, that is, the brook Denis, adjoining to the Picts’ wall on the north side. Being come near the enemy’s camp, the evening before the engagement, the pious king caused a great wooden cross to be made in haste, and he held it up himself with both his hands whilst the hole dug in the earth to plant it in was filled up round the foot. When it was fixed, Saint Oswald cried out to his army: “Let us now kneel down, and jointly pray to the Omnipotent, and only true God, that he would mercifully defend us from our proud enemy; for he knows that we fight in a just war in defence of our lives and country.” All the soldiers did as he commanded them. The place where this cross was set up was called in the English tongue Hevenfelth, that is, Heaven’s field, by a happy omen, says Bede, because there was to be erected the first heavenly trophy of faith; for, before that time, no church or altar was known to have been raised in the whole kingdom of the Bernisians. This cross of Saint Oswald remained afterwards very famous. Bede tells us, that to his time, many cut little chips of it, which they steeped in water, which being drank by sick persons, or sprinkled upon them, many recovered their health. He adds, that after the death of King Oswald, the monks of Hexham used to come to the place on the day before the anniversary of his death, there to watch the night in prayer, reciting the office with many psalms for his soul, and the next morning to offer the victim of the holy oblation. A church was built on the spot some time before Bede wrote, who mentions that one of the monks of Hexham, named Bothelm, then living, having broken his arm by falling on the ice as he was walking in the night, and having suffered a long time much anguish from the hurt, was perfectly cured in one night by applying a little of the moss which was taken off from this cross, and brought him. The learned Alcuin, in his poem on the bishops and saints of York, published by Mr. Thomas Gale, at Oxford, relates how the pious king, no ways daunted at the multitude and ferocity of his enemies, encouraged his soldiers to a confidence in Christ, and exhorted them to implore his protection prostrate with him on their faces before the cross which he had set up. This author likewise adds an account of several miracles wrought down to his time in 780, at the relics of Saint Oswald, and at this cross; or by chips cut from it infused in water, by drinking which, many sick were cured, even in Ireland, and other distant countries. So great was the veneration of the people for this cross, that the abbey of Durham used for its seal, during several ages, this cross on one side, and on the reverse the figure of Saint Oswald’s head, as Mr. Smith exhibits it from several ancient records. Almighty God was pleased to bless the king’s faith and devotion by granting him and his small army a complete victory over Cadwalla, who was killed in the battle, and his forces, with those of his allies, entirely routed.
.
Saint Oswald, after giving thanks to God, immediately set himself to restore good order throughout his dominions, and to plant in them the faith of Christ. By his ambassadors he entreated the king and bishops in Scotland to send him a bishop and assistants, by whose preaching the people whom he governed might be grounded in the Christian religion, and receive baptism. Aidan, a native of Ireland, and a monk of the celebrated monastery of Hij, was chosen for the great and arduous undertaking; and by his mildness soon repaired the mischief done by another monk sent thither before him, whose harshness had alienated many from the sweet law of the gospel. The king bestowed on Aidan the isle of Lindisfarne for his episcopal seat; and was so edified with his learning and zeal, that this great prince, before the bishop could sufficiently speak the English language, would be himself his interpreter, and explain his sermons and instructions to the people.
.
Oswald filled his dominions with churches and monasteries, and whilst he was governing his temporal kingdom, was intent only to labour and pray for an eternal crown. He very often continued in prayer from the time of matins (at midnight, to which he rose with the monks) till day-light; and by reason of his frequent custom of praying or giving thanks to our Lord at all times, it is said that wherever he was sitting he would have his hands on his knees turned upwards towards heaven. Bede says that he reigned over Britons, Picts, Scots, and English. The kingdom of Northumberland was then extended as far as the Frith of Edinburgh; but by this expression of Bede some other provinces of the Picts, and others in Wales must have paid homage to him. Penda, the Mercian, being one of the allies of Cadwalla, and, according to Malmesbury, present at his defeat, Mercia also paid him a kind of submission; and so great was his power, that all the other kings of the heptarchy acknowledged a certain dependence; whence Adamnan, abbot of Hij, in the life of Saint Columba, styles him emperor of Britain.
.
Wonderful were the humility, affability, and charity of this great king amidst his prosperity; of which Bede gives us the following instance. One Easter-day whilst he was sitting down to dinner, an officer, whose business it was to take care of the poor, came in, and told him there was a great multitude of poor people at his gate desiring alms. Whereupon the king sent them a large silver dish full of meat from his own table, and ordered the dish to be broken into small pieces and distributed among them. Upon this Saint Aidan, who happened to be at table, taking him by the right hand, said: “Let this hand never corrupt.” Bede adds, that this arm being cut off from his body after he was slain, remained incorrupt till his time, and was then kept, being honoured by all with due veneration, in the church of Saint Peter, at the royal castle of Bebbaborough, (so called from Bebba, a former queen,) now Bamborough in Northumberland. Simon of Durham, and Ingulphus testify that this arm was afterwards kept at Peterborough.
.
When Saint Oswald had reigned eight years in great prosperity, Penda, the barbarous Pagan king of Mercia, who nine years before had slain the pious King Edwin, uncle to Saint Oswald by his mother, but had been vanquished by our saint in the beginning of his reign, found means again to raise a great army and invade the Christian dominions of our holy king. Saint Oswald met him with an inferior force, and was killed in the battle that was fought between them. When he saw himself surrounded with the arms of his enemies, he offered his prayer for the souls of his soldiers. Whence it became a proverb: “O God be merciful to their souls, said Oswald when he fell.” He was slain in the thirty-eighth year of his age, of our Lord 642, on the 5th of August, in a place called Maserfield. This seems to have been at Winwick in Lancashire, where is a well still called Saint Oswald’s, which was formerly visited out of devotion; and that this territory was called Maserfelte, appears from an old inscription in Winwick church. Nevertheless, Oswaldtry, that is, Oswald’s cross, a market town, seven miles from Shrewsbury, is supposed by some to have also been formerly called Maserfelth; and Capgrave, Camden, and others think this the place where Saint Oswald was slain; for, he might before this, say they, when he defeated Penda, have added that part of Shropshire to his kingdom. The famous church of Saint Oswald there stands without the New gate. Leland in his Itinerary says it was once a monastery; this must have been in the Saxon times; but soon after the Norman conquest this church of Oswaldtry or Oswald’s cross, was a parish when it was given to the monastery of Shrewsbury, to which it afterwards belonged, and was impropriate. See Tanner in his Monastic history; who says the town called Album Monasterium or White-minster, was not Oswaldtry, but Whit-church, which was once a monastery. The church of Oswaldtry was probably so called from Saint Oswald’s cross, of which it was probably possessed; but Winwick in Maserfelth in Lancashire more justly claims the honour of his martyrdom. The inhuman tyrant caused the saint’s head and arms to be struck off, and fixed on poles; but Saint Oswald’s brother and successor Oswi took them away the year following, and carried the arms to his own royal palace, and sent the head to Lindisfarne. The head was afterwards put in the same shrine with the body of Saint Cuthbert, and with it translated to Durham, as Malmesbury and others assure us. The rest of Saint Oswald’s body was translated by his niece Osfrida, wife of Etheldred, king of Mercia, to the monastery of Bardney in Lincolnshire. During the Danish irruptions these relics were removed, by the care of Edilred, king of the Mercians, to Gloucester, where Elfleda, countess of Mercia, and daughter to king Alfred, built the church of Saint Peter. The monument erected to Saint Oswald there, is still to be seen in a chapel of this cathedral between two pillars; but part of the relics were translated to the abbey of Saint Winoc’s Berg in Flanders, in 1221, and deposited there with great solemnity by Adam, bishop of Terouanne. The barbarous king Penda, after he had slain five pious kings, Edwin, Oswald, Sigebert, Egric, and Annas, turned his arms against Oswi, who tried in vain to soften him by presents and the most favourable proposals. Seeing himself rejected by man, he turned his gifts into prayers, and bound himself by vow, in case he should be victorious, to consecrate to God his daughter Enfleda, then only one year old, and give with her twelve portions of land (each of which was sufficient to maintain ten families) to build and endow monasteries. God heard his vow, and Oswi, with an inferior army, defeated and slew the tyrant near Loyden, now Leeds in Yorkshire, in 655. The place of this battle was called Winwidfield or Field of Victory; situated on the river Winuaed, now Aire. With Penda, who was then eighty years old, of which he had reigned thirty, fell thirty commanders of royal blood.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor St. Oswald of Northumbria, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon him. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to him by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St.  Oswald of Northumbria might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
Passing on my best wisdom, pt 5

How to get your first 1,000 email subscribers (quickly).

You ever read those posts about how to get your first 100 subscribers? They all suck, but I can't resist them. I'm always looking for someone to tell me something actually good.

The advice is usually boring. 

"Start out by texting your friends" lol so dumb. Your friends don't want to subscribe to your email list. They'll probably razz you about it too.

Well, I wanted to leave something ACTUALLY good out there on the Internet. This is the best tip and literally my go to move everytime I start a new list in a new market.

GIVEAWAYS!

But wait there are some nuances to pull it off right. 

Do it wrong and you get a bunch of coupon moms or online casino grandmas on your email list that never buy nuthin.

Do it right and you'll pull 1,000 new buyers onto your list in a few days, maybe even a few thousand.

PRO TIP #1: The prize is the filter

This is the most important tip I can give you. My friends and I tested this to death and we used to giveaway iphones, ipads, flat screen TVs. 

Oh they'll attract ALOT of subscribers alright, but they'll never be interested in what you actuall sell.

Also, there is a point of no return. After $500 prize value it doesn't seem like the pull is any better than a $5,000 prize.

Unless your name is Russell Brunson and you're giving away corvettes and Ferrari's, that's a whole different game.

For my company Adskills, we did a giveaway where we offered an entire year of SEMRush for free. Huge value and totally relevant. This keeps the casino grandmas away lol

PRO TIP #2: Cover your legals

This gets into sweepstakes and lottery laws and you can get in trouble. Just ask AI to help you. Basically, don't ask them to pay, make sure it's truly randomized, no employees or family can win, and make sure all the rules and drawings are public. 

People get kinda crazy when they lose these things and they can go on the war path if they smell collusion. Just be cool, don't be tricky.

ALWAYS ALWAYS ALWAYS ACTUALLY GIVE THE PRIZE AWAY AT THE END. LoL can't believe I have to say that.

PRO TIP #3: Go viral with referral links

No one will EVER share your giveaway IF they think that by sharing it reduces their chance to win.

Why would I tell my 5 friends if that means 5 more people that might win instead of me? So use a referral link system that gives them an extra ticket to win for each person they refer... BOOM!

Now your market becomes a promotional army for you. Just get the first 100-200 people to join the giveaway, show them how to earn more ways to win with referrals, and watch them go to work.

Even better use a leaderboard to show them who's in the lead with the most "tickets to win." They'll go hard trying to beat each other in referrals.

(Do all that BEHIND the giveaway registration, don want people feeling like it's too hard)

PRO TIP #4: Turn it into sales

I find that 2 weeks is long enough to get a lot of promo time in and referrals, and not so long that people lose interest.

When you annouce the winner you're going to say "But first, I have a price for everyone so stay tuned..."

Then you announce the winner of the prize to everyone who subscriber. And you say "To make sure everyone walks away feeling like a winner from this we're making our product 50% off for the next 24/48/72 hours only, use promo code such and such."

Do the biggest discount you can handle. Make it a big deal. Do it just on the front end product and have 1-click upsells already lined up behind it.

When you do all of this right the entire industry is going to see and feel the splash you just made in their pond. 

You're going to get at minimum a few hundred subscribers if you mess everything up, but likely a few thousand subscribers if you only mess up a little.

And then you're going to create a table rush effect of sales by offering all these new leads a big discount on your product.

Congratulations, you've just entered a new market, have thousands of leads, and your first customers.

Send me a Christmas card with all your new money.

text:
Passing on my best wisdom, pt 4

How to sell high ticket WITHOUT phones. 

Recently I wrote about Russell Brunson, and mentioned I interned with him.

Well how I got that internship is I cold called his affiliate manager and closed him on letting me talk to Russ and then I closed Russ on letting me come out and work for free for 30 days. 

If you think that’s easy, just let me know when you’ve pulled it off. I’ll be here, forgive me if I don’t hold my breath. 

I was able to do this because prior to all this Internet marketing stuff I was an award winning salesman. I started door to door selling motivational posters to businesses and then moved to tire shop packages. 

After that I worked in a boiler room operation that sold timeshares. And finally landed in warehouse equipment sales where I specialized in semi-truck warehouses. 

Almost a decade ago I ran my own sales floor where I had 5 sales guys and a sales manager. We did millions in sales. 

And then I decided I never want to sell by phone, ever again. 

I tell you all of that so you can understand my level of experience with selling. My reason for not selling over the phone has nothing to do with skill or fear. 

It’s about time. 

Aintnobodygottimefodat!!!

Well, chumps do, but hey chump on if you love chumpin! 

Here’s what I figured out…

1. It’s not 1996 anymore. 

Consumers today know more about the car they are going to buy than the salesman does. The Internet connected consumer doesn’t require a lengthy call to explain the product. 

2. All of the psychological elements of a phone sales call can happen with a video, the right questions on a web form, and a good email follow up series. 

I’ve sold 5 figure consulting, services, coaching, masterminds, businesses, and licensing deals all without ever picking up a phone. 

You need 3 things…

1. Irresistible bait.

This is a case study, video, or report of some kind that your market is desperate to get access too. For example, one of mine was “How I scaled from $5,000/day to $65,000/day” back when everyone was stuck at $5,000/day caps on Meta ad accounts. 

Imagine I had free protein bars at a bodybuilding gym, easy right.

You gotta know what your market will jump through hoops to get. Do the work. Read lots of Reddit and FB groups. 

But it can’t just be exciting, it’s also got to attract the right person and make them more likely to buy from you. The $65k scaling trick, was to get them to hire my ad agency. 

Once I offered 10 books everyone has to read, got lots of leads, but no one bought because they were busy reading 10 books now!

Make sure your bait attracts the right fish. 

Ok, step one, get their attention. The hard work is done. You’ve got the fish on the hook, now you just have to real them in and not let them spit the hook out. 

2. The psychological web form.

You’ve probably seen something like this because I’ve taught this a lot and it’s kind of become best practice now. 

Before me, form questions were basic info like business size and budget size etc.

I used forms to ask people psychologically baited questions. For example, “Why is now all of a sudden the right time for you to (insert result).”

That question uses NLP and forces them to 1. think about the life event (kid, new job, new house, laid off) that is making this now urgent for them 2. Subconsciously, agreeing they need this right now.

Your form questions should get them to write out what’s blocking them from the result, why they need the result now, and what their life will be like after the result.

That’s an entire sales call in a single web form. The buyer sells themselves in the answering.

3. Scarcity.

You have to take away their time to “think about it.” You’re in or you’re out, let me know right now or I have another customer to move on too. 

Through the video and email follow up they should have access to all the details they need. Now it’s time to decide.

Right now.

text:
Mixed bag with $OPEN. Lots for the long-term AI bulls to like. Also lots of the short-term execution bears to like. I'd say the quarter offered encouraging evidence that the current AI strategy is working, but also offered little proof that the grander AI market-maker vision is ready for prime time.

The headline results were weak. Revenue fell 44% year over year to $883 million, contribution profit and adjusted EBITDA missed estimates, and homes sold dropped 46%, explaining the stock's post-earnings crash. Underneath those numbers, however, AI-driven efficiencies are emerging. Homes acquired jumped 149%, contribution margin reached a two-year high of 5.8%, operations cost per acquisition fell from $8,400 to $3,000, underwriting productivity more than doubled, required pre-offer home visits plunged from over 80% to below 20%, and Opendoor's AI sales assistant is converting three times better than in January at one-third the cost.

That is genuine progress. It mostly proves AI can make Opendoor a better iBuyer. The transformational thesis, that Opendoor can evolve into a capital-light, AI-powered market-maker connecting buyers and sellers without owning every home, remains largely conceptual, with the third-party marketplace still unlaunched and no concrete economics provided. If Opendoor ultimately builds that platform, the enormous housing market could support genuine 10X, and perhaps even 100X, upside. I don't think there's a higher upside "investable" stock in the market right now.

Until that vision produces measurable revenue, profits and capital efficiency, the market is unlikely to award the talk. Only walk will cut it. And right now, we don't have that. So... the stock, for all its long-term potential, will likely remain stuck in neutral in the short-term.

text:
Cowboy Conversations | Tony Lindsay QB '96-2000 For Tony Lindsay, the showdown with Colorado wasn't just another football game. It was personal.  

Growing up in the Denver area, Lindsay dreamed of becoming a Buffalo. Colorado was the school he wanted to play for. But the scholarship offer never came. In fact, the Buffaloes showed very little interest.  

One coach on Colorado's staff, however, believed in him—Bob Simmons.  

When Simmons became Oklahoma State's head coach, Tony Lindsay was one of the first players he called.  

Instead of wearing black and gold, Lindsay became Oklahoma State's quarterback. And when the nationally ranked Buffaloes came to Stillwater on Homecoming of 1997, he finally had the opportunity to prove they had made a mistake.  

Leading up to the game, Lindsay talked with his dad every day, counting down the hours until kickoff. Seeing his family before the game made the moment even more meaningful.  

Then the ball was kicked.  

"It didn't matter what the weather was. It didn't matter who was there. It was just us on that field against them."  

Late in the game, disaster struck.  Lindsay lost a fumble and was convinced he had cost Oklahoma State the victory.  

But on Colorado's very next possession, Maurice Simpson intercepted a pass, giving the Cowboys another chance.  

What happened next became Oklahoma State football history.  

Bootlegging to his right, Lindsay broke one of football's cardinal rules by throwing back across his body. But he never questioned the decision.  

"My thing with Lonzo—it didn't matter who was around him. He's open."  

Trusting All-American tight end Alonzo Mayes to make a play, Lindsay lofted the football toward the middle of the field.  

Mayes came down with it, and Lewis Field erupted.  

"He comes down with the catch... and all else is history."  

The kid who grew up dreaming of playing for Colorado instead authored one of the most iconic plays in Oklahoma State football history—against the very program that never gave him a chance.  

🎥 Watch Tony Lindsay relive the game-winning touchdown, the emotions of facing his hometown school, and one of the greatest victories of his Cowboy career in this edition of Cowboy Conversations. #GoPokes #OkState

OK, now that Silver is taking off, I will try to do some more deep dives on some of my favorite companies.

This one may be a little more under the radar to some, but to me it is one of the top tier Silver mines.

Silvercorp Metals:

Silvercorp Metals Inc. (SVM) derives approximately 69% to 72% of its net revenue from silver, making it a primary silver play. The company has over 236 million ounces of silver in measured and indicated resources across its core Chinese properties. It is already an established producer. However, its massive new growth asset—the El Domo project in Ecuador—is slated to enter commercial production in mid-2027.

An analysis of Silvercorp's revenue mix, asset base, pipeline timelines, and risk profile reveals the following breakdown of its current position.

Revenue Mix & Metal Diversification

Silvercorp operates primary silver mines, but its ore bodies are polymetallic. Silver represents 72% of its annual revenue. Over the 17-year life-of-mine plan at its flagship district, silver is projected to normalize at 69.3% of net revenue.

The remaining revenue is generated by a mix of other metals extracted from its mines:

Lead and Zinc: Significant industrial byproducts from the primary Ying Mining District and Gaocheng (GC) Mine.

Gold: A minor contributor in China, but poised to scale up significantly via global pipelines.

Copper: Will become a major revenue driver once the El Domo project goes live.

Ounces in the Ground (Silver Resource Base)

Recent independent technical updates outline a substantial resource base in China:

Ying Mining District: Contains 198 million ounces of silver in Measured & Indicated (M&I) resources.

Gaocheng (GC) Mine: Holds 38.3 million ounces of silver in M&I resources.

Total Core Silver Base: 236.3 million ounces of silver (excluding additional inferred resources and secondary silver credits from overseas projects).

Production Timeline

Silvercorp is not a pre-revenue exploration company; it has a long history of active production and profitability in China.

Current Operations: Active and generating cash from the Ying and GC underground mines.

El Domo (Ecuador): Construction began in 2025, and first commercial production is strictly on schedule for July 2027.

Tulkubash (Kyrgyzstan): Recently acquired gold projects are entering the early stages of engineering and construction.

Jurisdictional & Location Risks

China-Centric Regulatory Footprint: Most operating cash flow originates in China. This exposes investors to sudden regulatory shifts, national environmental policies, and geopolitical friction. For instance, operations were voluntarily suspended in June to implement mandatory state underground safety upgrades.

Ecuador Regulatory Friction: While the El Domo Project is a high-margin copper-gold deposit, Ecuador is historically an emerging mining jurisdiction with localized community resistance and environmental court challenges. Silvercorp relies on an Investment Protection Agreement with the state to shield capital execution.

Financial & Price Leverage

Silvercorp features a high operational and price leverage to silver, meaning its bottom line moves aggressively with spot market fluctuations.

During market rallies, its adjusted net income surged by 303% year-over-year off a 183% spike in realized silver prices.

Conversely, its cash costs are profoundly offset by industrial metal credits. At Ying, the cash cost per ounce of silver after by-product credits hovers at a negative $0.94/oz, insulating the company from collapsing into losses during broader market downturns
Core Investment Thesis: Pros & Cons

Positives:

Negative Cash Costs: Strong by-product credits shield operating margins.

Debt-Free Growth: Extensive expansion into Ecuador and Kyrgyzstan is fully funded by internal cash.

Long Mine Horizon: Core Chinese assets possess a visible, approved 15 to 17-year operational runway.

Negatives:

Jurisdiction Clustering: Vulnerable to the geopolitical policies of China and Ecuador.

Grade Dilution: Transitions to more mechanized shrinkage mining have driven higher ore dilution and lower localized head grades.

Non-Cash Volatility: Net income often gets skewed by paper-heavy derivative charges on convertible notes.

Is it a good investment?

Silvercorp is widely regarded by mining analysts as a fundamentally sound, high-tier vehicle for silver bulls. It offers a rare pairing of an elite, debt-free balance sheet, consistent free cash flow generation, and a major multi-year production expansion profile. However, investors must be willing to accept the sovereign risks tied to its operating regions.

text:
The box score from his sophomore season at TCU takes about ten seconds to read. Four appearances all year. Three starts. Every one of those starts at designated hitter.
​
Which is a strange line for a young man who had been, not long before, arguably the finest all-around athlete in the state of Utah.
​
At American Fork High School he lettered four years in baseball and earned first-team all-state as a junior and again as a senior. He batted .610 as a junior with thirteen doubles and seven triples. He hit eleven home runs as a senior and drove in eighty-six across his final two seasons.
​
Utah handed him its Gatorade Player of the Year award. In 2021 the state named him Mr. Baseball.
​
He was, in those same years, one of the best football players in Utah. He caught passes for 1,142 yards, eighth in the state, and picked off six throws as a defensive back.
​
BYU offered him a football scholarship at wide receiver. He was already committed to BYU for baseball. Utah State had offered on the football side, and Nevada, Nebraska, and UCLA were all making calls.
​
He chose the diamond. Baseball ran in the family, his father having coached the American Fork program to multiple state championships. On the first of February, 2022, he signed with TCU.
​
Nobody would second-guess that. It was the sport he was built for and the path everyone around him could plainly see.
​
But careers rarely follow the scouting report. The seasons in Fort Worth did not open the door everyone assumed the bat would open.
​
On Wednesday, BYU released its fall camp roster. Among the newcomers at wide receiver was a young man who had been offered a scholarship at that exact position, by that exact program, and had said no.
​
He is listed as a senior, the classification reflecting years spent in a different uniform entirely. He has come home to Provo to play the game he set down after high school.
​
Most people get one shot at the road not taken. Once in a great while, somebody gets to walk back to the fork and take the other one.
​
His name is Fisher Ingersoll.
​
Now you see the whole picture.
​

text:
The tale of the tape is the first thing a college coach reads, and his read five foot eight. In a sport that confuses height with ability, that number closes doors before anyone watches the film.
​
In October of his junior year, his 247Sports page carried a single scholarship offer. By the time the class was graded out, the Composite ranked him the 199th running back in the cycle.
​
He committed to a Big 12 program in January regardless. Then the signing class was announced, and he was not in it.
​
That is usually where the road forks. A young man takes the next-best offer, or none at all, and the commitment becomes a line in a forum thread nobody revisits.
​
Meanwhile his senior year was coming apart in a different direction. His starting quarterback fractured a hand mid-game, and the offense had to be rebuilt on a Thursday.
​
So the tailback learned a second job. Wildcat snaps. Option keepers. Slot receiver. His coach used him wherever that week's problem happened to be.
​
At SoFi Stadium in October, Palos Verdes decided a five-foot-eight quarterback could not beat them through the air. He scored on runs of fourteen and twenty-one yards, then dropped a sixty-one-yard touchdown pass over the top of them.
​
His team won it 40-14, claimed the Bay League championship, and stood at 9-1 with an undefeated Crean Lutheran squad waiting in the first round of the Division 2 playoffs.
​
They won that one 34-17. Then Chaparral, 19-16. The season ended in the semifinal at 11-2.
​
The Los Angeles Times, covering him that November, put a finger on what the star ratings never weighed: he had given up his own numbers so his team could win, and it had worked.
​
The final line was 4,030 rushing yards, 48 touchdowns, and 791 yards receiving.
​
On Wednesday, BYU opened fall camp in Provo. Somebody read the roster and found a name on it that had not been there before. Number 20. True freshman. Running back.
​
No press conference. No hat on a table. In a program holding to a 105-man limit, he had earned a spot and taken it.
​
He walks into a room that already holds LJ Martin, the preseason Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year, and returning letterman Sione Moa. The Cougars open September 5 against Utah Tech.
​
His name is Journee Tonga.
​
Now you see the whole picture.
​

text:
A college offensive lineman is good enough to play three different interior positions at a high level — and he still has to win his starting job all over again, every single year.
​
In high school, he anchored an offense that averaged 409.9 yards a game, recording 62 pancake blocks in a single season alone — a stat reserved for linemen who simply refuse to lose their matchup.
​
He was a low three-star prospect, the 33rd-ranked recruit in his entire state, with only two reported offers to his name: his hometown program and one other in-state school.
​
He originally committed to that other school — then left for two years, serving a full-time mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Tonga and Oakland, California.
​
He came home a different person with a different plan, and chose his hometown program instead of the one he'd first picked.
​
Playing time didn't come easily at first. He appeared in barely a handful of games combined across his first two seasons on campus.
​
Then everything clicked. In year three, he started six games and played in ten, finally putting real proof on tape.
​
His own head coach later summed up what makes him valuable in five words: "Sonny Makasini is a complete lineman."
​
He can play left guard, center, or right guard — whichever alignment the staff needs on a given series, without ever missing a beat.
​
Off the field, he's an Eagle Scout who still serves as an assistant clerk in his local church congregation, and unwinds the same way a lot of his teammates do — playing video games. Three of his own uncles played college football before him.
​
Even with all of that behind him, every single offseason still brings a fresh competition for the exact same starting job, this year against a new arrival with a remarkable story of his own.
​
His name is Sonny Makasini.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

text:
A high school defensive back intercepted the ball sixteen times in his career — and personally scored more touchdowns off those turnovers than most teams' actual running backs scored all season.
​
Five of his sixteen career interceptions, he returned all the way to the end zone himself.
​
That was just the defensive side. He also racked up 148 career tackles, while adding real offensive production of his own — 612 yards and seven touchdowns on the ball as a runner and receiver.
​
He was fast enough to matter well beyond football. As a freshman, he broke a district 400-meter record that had stood for 25 years, and as a junior he ran the 100 meters in 11.09 seconds.
​
He played varsity basketball too, averaging nearly 13 points, 4 assists, and better than a steal and a half a game as a junior.
​
He was named his conference's Two-Way Player of the Year, plus regional and league MVP honors in the same season.
​
Analysts compared his upside to past BYU safety standouts and predicted whole programs would end up regretting they never made a real push for him.
​
And still, his real offers numbered barely a handful — BYU, one Power Conference school, and his in-state option.
​
In his own words on why the versatility mattered more to him than any single position: "I just love being an athlete. I love all three aspects of the game."
​
He signed with BYU, then left before ever playing a college snap — serving a full-time mission for The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints in Houston, Texas.
​
When he finally took the field, the position everyone had projected for him changed. Coaches and analysts had long pegged him for safety.
​
He's now a cornerback, developing on the opposite side of the coverage shell from where scouts once had him penciled in.
​
His name is Cannon DeVries.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

text:
Every time this BYU wide receiver ran a route in high school, the headline led with somebody else's name first — one that already belonged to the NFL.
​
He's the youngest of five brothers, and every one of them played wide receiver at the same school before him.
​
Three of those brothers made it to the NFL. One of them, right now, is considered one of the best receivers in all of professional football.
​
In his own right, he was one of the most heavily recruited wide receivers in the state — 974 receiving yards and 9 touchdowns his senior year, with a signature performance in the state semifinals: 13 catches, 195 yards, and a touchdown that set up the game-winning field goal.
​
Recruiters noticed too: scholarship offers arrived from seven different programs — Utah, Utah State, Washington State, Oregon State, Hawaii, UNLV, and San Diego State — each one betting he could be more than a family name on a roster.
​
He picked the same school his brothers had, anyway.
​
As a true freshman in his first fall camp, he made an acrobatic, tipped-ball catch that observers immediately compared to one of the most famous plays his own brother ever made — in that same jersey, on that same field.
​
Asked what it's like carrying that name onto the field every day, he didn't dodge the question. His answer: "I want to embrace it."
​
By his own account, he calls his brothers constantly for advice, leaning on family that has already walked the exact road he's on now.
​
By his third spring on campus, coaches had started describing real, visible growth — no longer just the little brother trying to keep up in the receiver room.
​
Last season, he stood on the sideline for BYU's Big 12 Championship game appearance against Texas Tech — a stage no one in his family had reached in quite the same way.
​
He wears No. 0 — a number BYU fans have started to associate with him specifically, not simply with the last name stitched above it.
​
His name is Tei Nacua.
​
Now you see the whole picture.
​

text:
For two straight years, a Utah running back did something that should have been impossible to overlook. Almost everyone overlooked it anyway.
​
As a sophomore, he cleared 1,000 rushing yards. As a junior, he came up just short of it again.
​
Two workhorse seasons from a kid in Lehi, Utah — and the phone barely rang. The offers that came in were real, but modest: Utah State, San Diego State, San Jose State, UNLV, Weber State, Sacramento State.
​
Ten scholarship offers by his senior year. Not one from a Power Conference program.
​
So he answered the only way a running back knows how. He kept carrying the ball.
​
Senior season: 577 rushing yards, 10 touchdowns, through six games. Add 224 receiving yards and three more scores through the air. That's 8.2 yards every time he touched it.
​
He was named his high school's team MVP and All-Region — for the second year the numbers had been too big to explain away.
​
Analysts who watched the tape started reaching for a comparison: the tall running style, the receiving threat out of the backfield, the trust in pass protection — all echoes of a BYU great who went on to the NFL.
​
Then, at last, a Power Conference program noticed. It wasn't a surprise pick from across the country. It was the school half an hour from his own house.
​
He picked it anyway — turning down the exposure of a bigger conference stage for a program he'd grown up watching, with a head coach and a running backs coach he trusted from the first conversation, and a shot to stay close to the family that had watched every one of those 1,000-yard seasons in person.
​
He committed on social media, thanking his coaches by name, tagging the program's recruiting staff, closing with the hashtag every BYU commit reaches for.
​
Before he ever suited up, he showed up to watch the season opener — and stood for a photo with the program's all-time leading rusher, a back who's since gone on to play in the NFL.
​
This fall, he steps onto that same field for the first time, not as a fan in the stands but as a true freshman with a roster spot and a number of his own.
​
His name is Devaughn Eka.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

text:
Shea Charles wanted to join Leeds. Leeds are the ones who walked away, twice over, first on Charles himself, then on an alternative target too. Fulham are the club left picking up a pursuit nobody else wanted to finish.
Leeds had three separate bids rejected by Southampton across the summer, the third worth around £23 million, before publicly drawing a line and confirming they wouldn't go any higher. That wasn't hesitation born of disinterest. Charles was genuinely Leeds' top midfield target, and he wanted the move to Elland Road. The 49ers ownership group simply refused to get dragged into a bidding war once Fulham entered the picture, a financial discipline the club has now applied twice this window, having also stepped back from a separate midfielder, Morita, despite making a contract offer first.
Fulham's own path here hasn't been smooth either. Their opening £24 million bid was rejected outright, with Southampton holding firm at over £30 million despite Fulham believing a £25 million package would get it done. What's shifted since is Fulham's willingness to add bonuses on top of an improved £25 million offer rather than simply repeat the same number, while Southampton, a Championship club with only a year left on Charles's contract, still needs this sale to happen at some point this summer regardless of how long the standoff runs.
The framing that Charles wants Fulham specifically "for the chance to play in the Premier League" undersells what actually happened. He wanted Leeds, in the Premier League, and that specific move collapsed because his own preferred suitor decided £2 million wasn't worth the fight. Fulham isn't the destination Charles chose first. It's the destination still standing once his first choice chose not to compete.

text:
Mini-Bernie column, which is just one example of the kind of stuff I'll be writing on a subscriber platform like Substack .... 

There are many "It is time!" calls for the #STLCards to promote power-hitting prospect Joshua Baez from Triple A Memphis. No, I don't think it's time. Not yet. And there's a good reason for that. 

The Cardinals are holding off to maintain Baez' MLB rookie eligibility for 2027. Which makes sense. By doing so, they could be in line for a draft-choice bonus if he wins NL Rookie of the Year. 

By waiting another 10 days or so, the Cards can still bring Baez to the majors this season to gain some experience, and I expect this to happen. But the timing is important. I realize that many of you are familiar with the reasons for holding off, but this is just for those who aren't familiar with the process. It's a little confusing so I wanted to clarify. 

The Explanation 

--- The earliest date the Cardinals can promote him is August 15, and they could wait to Aug. 16 or 17. That's because they'll have to manage his playing time so he does not exceed 130 official at-bats. He reaches 130 at-bats before the end of the 2026 regular season, then his rookie eligibility for 2027 expires. 

--- Securing rookie eligibility into 2027 means staying at or below two MLB thresholds. 

(1) An active roster limit of 45 days.  Under current MLB rules, days spent on the active Major League roster during September count toward the 45-day threshold. 

The '26 regular season ends on Sunday, September 27. The period from September 1 through Sept 27 accounts for 27 active roster days.

 Promoting Baez on Aug. 15 puts him at exactly 44 active roster days by season's end. Even if the club added him to the 26-man roster on Aug. 14, Baez would reach the 45-day limit by the end of the season and that's OK -- he wouldn't exceed the 45-day threshold.

(2) A limit of 130 at-bats. Promoting Baez at mid-August keeps the Cardinals clear of the exceeding the 45-day roster limit, but the number of at-bats is an entirely different threshold. (Note: it is literally based on at-bats. Not plate appearances, which include walks and sacs and other things.) 

Based on the current schedule, including today's game at NYY, the Cards have 48 games remaining. If they promoted Baez after the Aug. 15 game, the Cardinals would have  39 games left. 

Hypothetically: if Baez is promoted in time for the Aug. 16 game and plays every remaining contest as a starter, averaging 3.5 to 4 ABs per contest -- it's a problem. 

If he averaged 3.5 at-bats over the final 39 games, he would reach 136 at-bats and lose rookie status regardless of his service time. 

That's an easy obstacle to work around, simply because Baez won't be in the lineup for every game. The Cardinals would just have to manage his playing time to stay under that 130 at-bat limit. 

If, however, the Cardinals want to start Baez in every game, give him unrestricted playing time, and disregard his number of ABs -- this would mean delaying his promotion. There's no reason for that to happen. 

Here's what I'm thinking

The Cardinals open a three-city, 11-game road trip on Aug. 14 that takes them to Wrigley Field for 3, Cincinnati for 5 and Philadelphia for 3. If he's put on the roster on Aug. 14, he'd still avoid crossing the 45-day limit. That's good! The big guy could take aim at the LF Wrigley bleachers, take advantage of the driving range and the Par 3 course otherwise known as Great American Ball Park, and play in another hitter-happy environment in Philly. 

The challenge becomes keeping him at 130 or fewer at-bats. Starting Aug. 14, the Cardinals have 41 scheduled games remaining on their schedule. 

If Baez averaged 3.5 at-bats over the 41 games, that would put him over 130 at-bats. Obviously, his playing time would have to be spread out to prevent that. But based on that average of 3.5 ABs per game, he could still start and play 35, 36, games. If his average is 3.8 at-bats per game, they'd have to dial it back to 33 games. If he averaged 4.0 at-bats per game, he could start no more than 32 games. 

Also: just because Baez starts a game, he doesn't have to finish it. And he doesn't have to start a game; he can still be used as a pinch-hitter or a guy who enters the fray later and gets a couple of at-bats. There are many ways -- easy ways -- to keep him at 130 at-bats or fewer. 

Just wanted to offer the various scenarios. But it seems rather simple and easy to put Baez on the roster before that three-city road trip, monitor his number of at-bats, and still have him start a lot of games from Aug. 14 through Sept. 27. 

Thanks for reading this.
