A guest post by Oz.
Oz and Drew PavlouAug 3📷📷 📷📷📷📷
Friends, Drew Pavlou here.
My mate Oz just published this brilliant account of Australia’s political, cultural and economic drift. It’s simply one of the best things I’ve read all year, so I thought I would share it with my Substack followers as a guest post.
To tell you the truth, I am extremely scared for the future of our country. I simply think most Australians do not realise how fast we could drop off a cliff as a country.
We could very easily lose first world country status in our lifetime.
If you don’t believe me, just look at Argentina.
Argentina was basically the wealthiest country in the world at the start of the twentieth century. Now the median per-capita household income in Argentina is approximately $475 AUD a month.

What happened?
The difference between Argentina and the US over the past 120 years was astonishingly small: Argentina grew at just 1.1% a year per capita while the US grew at 1.6% a year per capita.
Half a percentage point of growth compounded over 120 years. That was enough to lose first world country status.

To quote one of my favourite political leaders Lee Kuan Yew: “This is not a game of cards. This is your life and mine.”

I would urge you to please share this article with as many fellow Australians as possible. Please help spread the message.

Australia is sick

Our political economy is eating itself

Decline can take many shapes.

In 1850, Cincinnati was the sixth-largest city in America and the roaring boomtown of the interior. It was never sacked, never burned, never went bankrupt. It simply grew a little slower than Chicago, decade after decade. Today it is a pleasant regional city nobody thinks about. Decline via drift.

Argentina ran the accelerated version. In 1913 it was one of the richest countries on earth per capita — richer than France. The great magnet of the southern hemisphere. A century of telenovela politics stacked on a broken economic base turned it into the world’s byword for squandered inheritance. Nobody in Buenos Aires in 1913 would have believed you.

Australians were the richest people on earth for large parts of the late nineteenth century. We should be again. We sit on half the world’s seaborne iron ore, a third of its uranium reserves, produce more lithium than any other country, have gas fields among the largest on the planet, the sunniest habitable continent, and 27 million educated people under common law on Asia’s doorstep. We have never had slavery or suffered savage civil wars. No nation has ever been dealt better cards.

Yet we are failing. GDP per capita has been negative or sclerotic since 2023. The steepest fall in real household disposable income in the OECD and highest inflation in the Anglosphere. Fertility at a record low. Capital-city houses at ten-plus times incomes. The list goes on. We are on track for the grind into obscurity. We will have no one to blame but ourselves and we will not be able to say we did not know. Something is rotten in the state of Australia.

📷

Given our resource, security, and human capital abundance, this is a political failure. Our political economy has always been heavily contested by snouts in the trough — from the days of Macarthur strong-arming a nascent government, to the land-hungry squattocracy, to countless groups today as compellingly detailed by Cameron Murray in his book Rigged. Like all nations we have our own Bootleggers and Baptists. All Bootleggers are definitionally petty, looking to line their pockets. But our Baptists seem particularly stupid.
📷Netflix adaptation of Australia’s eSafety Commissioner
From the brazen government shake down of global tech to pay off a few legacy media companies to banning under-16s from social media in a sop to those same companies to win some meagre advertising dollars back from the global platforms. All under the auspices of a dystopian-titled eSafety Commissioner. God forbid our media tycoons make things people want. It’s crazy we only got age-verification for online porn sites by accident in an attempt to shore up legacy media ad dollars. They’re confessing they could have had porn sites verify age for the last 20 years but didn’t.

We can’t trust our government to regulate AI because we know it will just be another jobs-for-the-boys program or an excuse to funnel cash to some interest group.

Our political class is stuck in the narratives of the past. Each wing lives in its own delusions.

Labor remains anchored to a union base that now covers barely one in twelve private-sector workers and is, increasingly, a concentration of criminal activity. (Public sector unions are their own strange paradox). Its flagship, the CFMEU, had to be placed into administration after bikies and organised crime were found clipping the ticket on government projects. They siphon taxpayer contracts on one side and hold the country to ransom on the other. The rest of Labor’s base, the inner-city professional and public sector cardigan wearer, are fixated on ideological crusades. Climate. Israel. The Voice.

The Liberals talk about free markets and enterprise, which in practice is capture by the Business Council. It believes in one thing: cheap-labour-maxxing. The Liberals’ own pearl-clutchers split off into the Teals.

Both sides are complicit in two decades of bungling.
Howard-era apparatchiks are still drinking the Kool-Aid on their catastrophic decision to abdicate immigration policy to the universities. Philip Ruddock, Howard’s immigration minister, has announced a new book Nation Building: How Immigration Made Australia — with a foreword by Abul Rizvi, the mandarin who designed the student-visa-to-residency pipeline. Why are they confessing? They’re bragging. The scheme was meant to build university capacity and mint skilled migrants. Instead it disfigured our universities into visa mills and rebranded the tuition fees of aspiring permanent residents as our “fourth-largest export.” Ironically, in the process the Liberals fed Labor’s natural voter base — university jihadists.

The entire Kevin ‘07 campaign was insane on its own terms. Australia produces about one per cent of global emissions. There was no mechanism, even in theory, by which the “great moral challenge of our generation” could be answered from Canberra. There were, however, serious and successful attempts to hobble our energy system. Which was the point. This was obvious at the time. No comeuppance will ever come to these self-righteous economic terrorists.
Self-congratulatory tears were shed when the Gillard government launched the NDIS, costed by the Productivity Commission at $13.5 billion a year at maturity, serving roughly 400,000 of the most profoundly disabled Australians. It now runs past $50 billion a year — more than Medicare (!) — with 740,000 participants and counting. We could hand every one of the originally intended recipients $125,000 a year in cash and come out ahead. But that wouldn’t feed an entire industry of parasites. Just try clawing those sweet dollars from their hands now. It’s over.
Turnbull promised Snowy 2.0 for $2 billion. The official budget is $12 billion and already conceded broken; the Auditor-General’s latest report rates the final bill unknowable, while outside estimates run to $40 billion. The greatest white elephant in Australian infrastructure history, and it isn’t even finished. He still rolls with a #withhydropower banner on his LinkedIn profile. No shame. These are our best!

Meanwhile the standing absurdities accumulate. We banned drilling over some of the largest gas fields on the planet, and one of the largest LNG exporters on earth is now building terminals to import gas. (To their credit, the Victorian Libs now want to drill.) We hold a third of the world’s uranium reserves, and it is illegal to do anything with it here. Our premier think tank, the Grattan Institute, surveyed the national predicament and recommended switching off your gas stove (grim, grim, grim). Our best and brightest have the vision and national will of a toadstool. We have one of the most licensed workforces in the world, rivaled only by basket-case employment markets like India and South Africa. Our privatised pension scheme is a conspiracy of union and private sector interests, each getting their vig. Our government is threatening to dip its fingers into it. It’s inevitable. Why wouldn’t they. It’s the shape of our political economy.

📷

This excellent chart shows the relative stagnation of the last decade. It looks harsher than it is: the Albanese government cannot be blamed for the economic conditions it inherited (although it hasn’t helped), and the Howard government timed its regime well with the China boom.

The rot runs deeper than any one government. Labor’s political economy points one way: immigration-maxxing. Half a million net arrivals a year flatters headline GDP, launders per-capita stagnation through population growth, keeps Treasury’s projections respectable, pays off the union base with megaproject pipelines, and imports voters (according to the ABC). The Liberals’ political economy is dominated by Business Council capture, which wants the same migrants at lower wages, and which has left the party impotent with actual voters.

Those voters have now, incredibly and predictably, absconded to One Nation, a party of nincompoops but one that actually cares about the one thing both major parties have been giving voters good and hard and against their will for a long time: immigration. The bar is so low that all it takes to win is opposing infinite immigration, self-flagellation, and the paganisation of everything (are you enjoying the renaming of your cities and smoking ceremonies anon?).

📷Are you enjoying your immigration-maxxing anon

An ageing population shifts an ever-greater burden onto a shrinking cohort of young workers who cannot buy homes and have stopped having children. We are structurally hobbled.

The Voice — a proposal to write ancestry into the machinery of government — lost the referendum. Badly. Sixty–forty, every state. Victoria and South Australia, where it also lost, went ahead and built their own versions anyway (imagine this on a federal level). What is that if not contempt for voters?

Not once in a generation has our federal political class offered a pro-growth vision: a wealthier Australia, one where people want more children and can assume a better life for them. We have instead been ravaged by an inward-facing political class, each faction eking out a greater slice for its own interest group. We tinker with tax policy at the edges while the country is hollowed out. The state is eating the country:

📷

Demographically, we may be past the point of no return, where too many mouths are now dependent on government mismanagement. We’ve always had interest groups vying for their cut. But now the misalignment between the good of the country and the good of particular groups may be too high.
Australia is not alone. Similar demographic, political, economic, and institutional challenges seem to grip most countries. But that is not an adequate excuse. Australia has prided itself on its economic exceptionalism, soaring with the help of China’s rise through the 90’s and 00’s. I was there when the AUD > USD. I felt like a king travelling through the US. Today an Australian feels like a third worlder paying with pacific pesos overseas. We have immiserated ourselves over the last ~15 years. Our decline has been self-inflicted.

It’s easy to talk about agency and only needing the will to change, but it’s not clear at all that our political and intellectual institutions, the incentives in our political economy, and Australia’s structural demographic realities are up for turning.

Why Epe, Lagos Is Emerging as One of the Strongest Real Estate Opportunities in 2026

Epe is no longer the quiet lagoon town many people once overlooked. It is rapidly positioning itself as a key growth corridor in Lagos State, offering investors a rare combination of relative affordability and strong long-term upside.

 Why the Potential Is Real

1. Still Affordable Compared to Core Lagos Areas**  
While land prices in Lekki and parts of Ibeju-Lekki have soared, Epe remains more accessible. As of 2026, plots typically range from about ₦1.5–5 million in interior villages to ₦5–15 million in Epe town, ₦8–25 million along major roads, and ₦15–50 million+ near emerging estates and key infrastructure. Average listings sit around ₦6 million per plot. Early buyers still have a window before prices fully catch up with neighbouring corridors.

2. Major Infrastructure Tailwinds**  
Several large-scale projects are reshaping the Lekki–Epe axis:
- Proximity to the Lekki Free Trade Zone, Dangote Refinery, and Lekki Deep Sea Port
- Alaro City (a major mixed-use development in the Free Zone)
- Ongoing Epe Mixed Development Scheme and Labour City under the Epe Master Plan
- Progress on the proposed Lekki-Epe International Airport
- Impact of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and improved expressway connectivity

These developments are already driving demand and appreciation in surrounding areas.

3. Growing Demand Drivers**  
Epe benefits from educational institutions (including Augustine University and LASU Epe campus), tourism potential around the lagoon and nearby beaches/resorts, and emerging logistics and food-hub activity. As Lagos continues to expand eastward, residential, commercial, and industrial demand is expected to rise.

4. Favourable Land Characteristics**  
Much of the land is dry and suitable for development, and the area is generally regarded as relatively serene and secure compared with more congested parts of Lagos.

The Opportunity  and the Caution

Smart investors are treating Epe as a medium- to long-term play rather than a quick flip. Historical patterns in Lagos show that corridors that receive major infrastructure often deliver significant capital appreciation over 5–10 years. At the same time, success depends heavily on location (proximity to roads and projects), proper documentation (C of O, Governor’s Consent, or clear freehold title), and thorough due diligence.

Bottom line:** Epe currently offers one of the better risk-reward balances in the Lagos real estate market for those who buy carefully and hold with a medium-term horizon. The “new Lagos” narrative that once applied to Lekki is now extending further east  and Epe sits right in that path.

If you are considering land or property here, prioritise verified titles, physical site inspection, and professional guidance. The window of relative affordability will not stay open forever.

Discover the Ultimate Women’s Vacation Party Dress: A Timeless Retro Polka-Dot Masterpiece for Spring and Fall 2026

Step into a world of effortless elegance and playful sophistication with the Women’s Vacation Party Dress, an extraordinary new design that redefines seasonal fashion for the discerning woman who seeks both style and comfort in equal measure. This sleeveless, round-neck, high-waist creation features a striking retro polka-dot print and a gracefully flared skirt, embodying the best of European and American fashion sensibilities. Crafted specifically for the transitional seasons of spring and fall 2026, this figure-flattering silhouette promises to become the cornerstone of your wardrobe, whether you are jetting off on a sun-drenched European escape, attending an intimate American garden party, or simply elevating everyday moments into something memorable.

The heart of this dress lies in its new retro polka-dot print design. Polka dots have long held a cherished place in the history of fashion, tracing their origins back to the mid-nineteenth century when the lively pattern first appeared in European ballrooms and later captured the imagination of American designers in the twentieth century. In 2026, this classic motif returns with a fresh, contemporary interpretation that feels both nostalgic and thoroughly modern. The dots are rendered in a carefully balanced scale—neither too large to overwhelm nor too small to disappear—creating a rhythmic visual dance across the fabric that catches the light and draws the eye with every movement. The print itself is executed with exceptional precision, ensuring that each circular motif maintains crisp edges and consistent spacing, a testament to advanced textile printing techniques that allow for vibrant color saturation without sacrificing the soft hand-feel of the material.

Imagine the fabric: a lightweight yet substantial blend selected for its ability to drape beautifully while offering just enough structure to hold the high-waist line and flared skirt in perfect form. The material breathes easily, making it ideal for the mild days of spring when temperatures begin to rise and the cooler evenings of fall when a light layer might be needed. It moves with you rather than against you, skimming the body in a way that feels liberating rather than restrictive. The sleeveless cut further enhances this sense of freedom, allowing arms to move freely during lively conversations at outdoor gatherings or while exploring cobblestone streets in a charming European village. The round neckline frames the collarbone and neck with gentle simplicity, offering a clean canvas that pairs equally well with delicate gold jewelry for a refined look or bold statement pieces for a more dramatic statement.

The high waist is perhaps one of the most flattering design elements of this dress. Positioned to sit just above the natural waistline, it creates an elongated silhouette that flatters a wide range of body types. By drawing the eye upward and then releasing into the full, flared skirt, the dress achieves a balanced proportion that has been celebrated in both European couture houses and American ready-to-wear collections for decades. The high waist gently defines the midsection without constriction, offering a comfortable fit that remains secure throughout hours of wear. This thoughtful construction allows the dress to skim rather than cling, providing a smooth line that enhances natural curves while offering a sense of ease that many fitted styles cannot match.

The flared skirt is the crowning glory of the design. Beginning at the high waist, it falls in soft, controlled folds that create gentle movement with every step. The fullness is carefully calibrated so that the skirt swings with a lively yet elegant motion—never so voluminous as to appear costume-like, yet ample enough to produce that delightful sense of fluidity that makes a dress feel special. When walking, sitting, or dancing, the skirt responds beautifully, adding a touch of romance and playfulness that is perfectly suited to vacation settings and party atmospheres. The length has been thoughtfully considered for 2026 trends, falling to a point that is both practical for daytime exploration and sophisticated enough for evening celebrations. Whether you are strolling through a spring market in Tuscany or attending a fall harvest gathering in New England, the skirt’s movement will turn heads in the most graceful way.

This dress draws deeply from both European and American style traditions. European influences are evident in the refined proportions, the attention to clean lines, and the subtle sophistication of the overall silhouette—qualities long associated with the ateliers of Paris, Milan, and London. At the same time, the American contribution shines through in the approachable, versatile nature of the design. American fashion has always excelled at translating high style into wearable, practical garments that adapt effortlessly to real life, and this dress embodies that spirit. The result is a piece that feels equally at home in a chic European café and at a casual American backyard barbecue, bridging continents with its universal appeal.

Spring 2026 will be a season of renewed optimism and lighthearted celebration after years of more restrained aesthetics. Designers across both continents are embracing prints, movement, and silhouettes that celebrate the body rather than constrain it. This polka-dot dress anticipates that mood perfectly. The retro print brings a sense of joyful nostalgia while the modern cut keeps it firmly rooted in the present. As temperatures warm and outdoor gatherings multiply, the sleeveless construction and breathable fabric will prove invaluable. Pair it with strappy sandals and a wide-brimmed hat for daytime excursions, or elevate it with heeled mules and a structured clutch for evening events. A light cardigan or denim jacket can be draped over the shoulders when the spring breeze turns cool, transforming the look without diminishing its impact.

Fall 2026 will demand pieces that transition seamlessly from warm afternoons to cooler nights. The polka-dot dress rises to that challenge with remarkable ease. Layer it under a tailored blazer or a soft leather jacket for added warmth and structure. The high waist remains visible beneath most outer layers, preserving the flattering silhouette. Earth-toned accessories or rich jewel-colored shoes can shift the mood of the print toward autumn sophistication, while the flared skirt continues to provide that sense of movement that keeps the look dynamic. The dress’s versatility makes it an ideal travel companion: pack it once and wear it multiple ways throughout a multi-destination journey that might include both European city breaks and American countryside retreats.

Figure-flattering is more than a marketing phrase when it comes to this dress; it is a carefully engineered reality. The combination of the high waist and flared skirt creates an optical effect that balances proportions. For those with an hourglass shape, the design accentuates the natural curve at the waist while allowing the hips to move freely. For straighter figures, the volume of the skirt introduces soft curves that enhance femininity. For those with a more athletic build, the sleeveless cut and round neck highlight toned arms and collarbones while the skirt softens the overall line. The print itself plays a supporting role in this flattery: the polka dots create visual interest that draws the eye across the entire garment rather than focusing on any single area, resulting in a balanced and harmonious appearance.

The newness of the design cannot be overstated. While polka dots have appeared in countless collections over the decades, this particular interpretation feels fresh because of its precise scale, the quality of the print application, and the thoughtful integration with a contemporary silhouette. Designers working for the 2026 season have moved away from overly literal retro references toward more nuanced tributes that honor the past while serving present needs. This dress exemplifies that approach. It does not shout “vintage”; instead, it whispers of timeless charm updated for today’s lifestyle. The sleeveless cut feels current, the high waist aligns with ongoing preferences for defined yet comfortable shapes, and the flared skirt offers the kind of movement that has been missing from many recent minimalist collections.

Consider the occasions for which this dress is ideally suited. Vacation settings are where it truly shines. Picture yourself arriving at a Mediterranean coastal town, stepping off a train in a sunlit square, the flared skirt catching a gentle sea breeze as the polka dots seem to dance in the light. Or imagine a long weekend in the American Southwest, the dress providing a light, cheerful counterpoint to desert landscapes. Party environments benefit equally: whether an intimate dinner with friends, a rooftop gathering under string lights, or a more formal celebration, the dress strikes the perfect balance between festive and refined. The sleeveless design keeps you cool as energy rises, while the figure-flattering cut ensures confidence remains high throughout the evening.

Styling possibilities are virtually endless. For a classic European-inspired look, pair the dress with simple leather sandals, a woven basket bag, and minimal gold jewelry. A silk scarf tied at the neck or worn as a headband can add an extra touch of continental flair. For an American casual interpretation, try white sneakers, a denim jacket, and a crossbody bag for daytime exploring. Evening transformations might include metallic heels, a bold cuff bracelet, and a sleek clutch. The polka-dot print is remarkably accommodating: it works with solid neutrals that allow the pattern to take center stage, and it also plays nicely with complementary patterns when carefully chosen. Soft stripes or subtle florals in coordinating colors can create layered interest without clashing.

The construction quality deserves particular attention. Seams are finished with care to prevent fraying and to ensure longevity across multiple seasons. The high-waist band is reinforced just enough to maintain its shape without adding bulk or discomfort. The skirt’s flare is achieved through strategic paneling or carefully placed gathers that distribute volume evenly, avoiding any sense of heaviness. The round neckline is finished cleanly, sitting smoothly against the skin. These details may seem small, yet they accumulate into a garment that feels expensive and thoughtfully made—qualities that European and American consumers increasingly demand in 2026.

As fashion continues to evolve toward greater versatility and longevity, this dress stands as an example of intelligent design. It is not a fleeting trend piece destined for a single season; rather, it is a foundational item that will remain relevant as styles shift. The retro polka-dot print has proven its staying power across generations, and the silhouette’s balance of structure and ease positions it well for the years ahead. Women who invest in this dress in spring or fall 2026 will find themselves reaching for it repeatedly, discovering new ways to style it as their wardrobes and lifestyles change.

The emotional resonance of such a garment should not be overlooked. Clothing has the power to influence how we feel and how we move through the world. text:
🇺🇸 If I Were an Afrikaner... I’d Live Close to the Coast.
 Part 6: Beaches, History & Beauty
One of the best things about living in Southeast Georgia is that you can enjoy the peace and affordability of a small town while still being close to some of the most beautiful coastal places in America.

From Waycross, the Georgia coast is an easy getaway.

You can spend the morning at home, drive east, and before long you’re surrounded by salt air, marshes, boats, beaches, and centuries of history.

🌴 St. Simons Island offers beautiful beaches, a historic lighthouse, fishing, golf, restaurants, and streets shaded by live oaks.

🌅 Jekyll Island is home to the unforgettable Driftwood Beach, miles of bike trails, historic homes, sea turtles, and peaceful stretches of shoreline.

⚓ Brunswick brings together a working port, historic downtown streets, fresh seafood, shopping, healthcare, and access to the Golden Isles.

And this is what makes Southeast Georgia so special.

You don’t have to choose between country life and coastal life.

You can have both.

You can raise your family in a quiet community, enjoy lower housing costs, know your neighbors, and still spend your weekends boating, fishing, biking, exploring historic sites, or watching the sun set over the Atlantic.

For Afrikaner families who love the outdoors, this region offers something familiar.

Space.

Nature.

Community.

And the freedom to build a life that is not swallowed up by traffic, noise, and crowds.

You can enjoy:

🏖️ Beaches and barrier islands
🎣 Fishing and crabbing
🚤 Boating and marinas
🚲 Bike trails and nature paths
🏛️ Historic sites and museums
🍤 Fresh local seafood
🛍️ Shops, markets, and festivals
⛳ Golf and recreation
🌞 Warm weather for much of the year

There is something healing about living close to the water.
The salt air slows you down.
The sunsets remind you to breathe.
And the coast gives families a place to make memories that last for generations.

"This is the day which the Lord hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it."
 Psalm 118:24 KJV

🇺🇸 Southeast Georgia gives you the best of both worlds: small-town living, strong communities, and the beauty of the coast just down the road.

Brighton Beach has seen multiple reported sexual attacks in recent years. 
A place where families, tourists and young people should feel safe after dark has repeatedly become a crime scene. 
Police statements on the latest arrest give age and gender only no further details released so far.

Britain’s coastal resorts are not immune. 
Public spaces that should offer freedom and leisure keep featuring in rape investigations. Women walking alone, or separated from friends on a night out, remain vulnerable. 
The pattern in Brighton alone raises an obvious question, 
how many more incidents must occur on the same beaches before the public is told the full picture and effective measures follow?

Anyone with information should contact Sussex Police online or on 101, quoting serial 228 of 05/08.

The victim deserves justice. The public deserves safety and transparency.

Nearly 2,000 Knights, clergy and guests celebrated their homelands during the annual States Dinner, which concluded the opening day of the 144th Supreme Convention in Denver on Aug. 4.

The event began with a procession of 28 historic flags of the United States in honor of the country’s 250th anniversary, followed by the colorful flags of some 75 jurisdictions represented at the convention.

Archbishop Paul Coakley of Oklahoma City, president of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops and a longtime Knight, delivered the dinner’s keynote address, reflecting on the importance of patriotic virtue, particularly in light of the semiquincentennial of the United States, where the Order was founded in 1882.

“Patriotism is not an afterthought for the Knights of Columbus; it is written into our very structure,” Archbishop Coakley said. “Patriotism is not, first and foremost, a political virtue. It is a religious one. It flows from the Fourth Commandment, honor your father and mother, and it can rightly be understood as a form of familial love extended outward.”

He added, “If we put God first, our love of country becomes stronger and more durable, because it is no longer resting on the nation’s ability to make us comfortable or proud. It rests instead on gratitude to the God who placed us here.” 

Concluding his remarks, Archbishop Coakley said, “Honor your country as you honor your parents: with gratitude, with loyalty, and with honesty that never mistakes flattery for love. Put God first and let your patriotism flow from that priority rather than compete with it. Teach your children that love of country is a debt of gratitude, not a slogan, and gratitude is an attribute of a Christian man.”

Bishop Louis Tylka of Peoria, Illinois, gave the invocation before the dinner, and Archbishop James Golka of Denver, state chaplain of Colorado, offered welcoming remarks. Supreme Chaplain Archbishop William Lori of Baltimore gave the final blessing and led guests in singing the Salve Regina.

text:
AI Therapy Chatbots Spur States to Act Over Patient Safety Fears | Ian Lopez, Bloomberglaw

Emilie’s work as a therapist was far from typical. Emilie, according to a federal lawsuit, claimed to have seven years’ experience helping patients with cases including depression.

Except Emilie’s background, including her Imperial College London degree, was pure fiction. She was an AI bot with some 45,500 patient interactions.

Pennsylvania sued the company behind Emilie, Character Technologies Inc., in May for propping up an AI chatbot on its https://t.co/r1czx1vmgc platform, where it allegedly mimicked a professional, licensed therapist. The action followed a Kentucky lawsuit against the same company for exposing minors to harm.

A survey of over 42 million US young adults and adolescents found that nearly a fifth used AI chatbots for mental health advice, about 43% of which did so each month.

As millions turn to AI for advice, states are stepping in to regulate a space the federal government has yet to standardize. Tennessee, Colorado and Maine this year signed off on measures to curb AI use in therapy, following laws passed by Illinois, Nevada, and Utah in 2025.

Loosely regulated consumer chatbots offer unstructured pocket therapy which can prove perilous. In Colorado, a 13-year-old died by suicide in 2023 after using a https://t.co/r1czx1vmgc chatbot, according to a federal lawsuit.

A spokesperson for https://t.co/r1czx1vmgc said the tool’s “robust disclaimers” make clear that “users should not rely” on bots “for any type of professional advice.” The group said it’s “committed to continuing to collaborate with safety experts, regulators, and other stakeholders” while developing new features for their “entertainment AI platform.”

Therapists want an emerging universe of AI-enabled programs, like Woebot Health, regulated to safely prescribe as on-demand therapy. These tools use generative AI, but with guardrails, to engage with patients as a human therapist would, according to Nature Partner Journals. That’s not what’s happening on most generative AI products.

“Digital therapeutics” are “proliferating, and many of them are very good,” said Page Walley, a clinical psychologist and Tennessee senator behind the state’s restrictions on advertising AI as a mental health professional. “We just wanted to draw a line in the sand and say, if you do cross this, you’re operating in violation of the law.”

Where’s the Line?

Bloomberg Law couldn’t find Emilie on https://t.co/r1czx1vmgc, but there are many like it. Coupled with ChatGPT and Claude’s use as a pocket therapist, AI adoption for mental health is surging.

Ankur Varma, psychotherapist and Brown Man Therapy co-founder, doesn’t “actively encourage” patients to have conversations with artificial intelligence. But if they do, he’ll discuss their AI sessions.

“For folks who aren’t working with a professional or don’t have access to a professional and are divulging very personal issues, really difficult issues, or they might be in crisis, that’s where my concern comes in,” Varma said.

States are figuring out parameters. At least a dozen enacted legislation on AI chatbot protections for children. Vermont and Rhode Island in recent months greenlit AI therapy restrictions. In 2025, Illinois directly restricted how licensed professionals utilize AI in healthcare, banning these tools from directly engaging with patients.

The effort was meant to counter the “large proliferation” of businesses pushing AI bots as therapists, said the sponsor, Illinois Rep. Bob Morgan (D), though he noted its limited scope.

A “state law is not going to be detailed enough to give the specific answer of what should ChatGPT answer to a particular specific question,” Morgan said.

The Illinois law, however, doesn’t adequately halt general-purpose AI chatbots like Claude from providing therapy, said C. Vaile Wright, American Psychological Association senior director of health care innovation. It does leave providers open to penalty for recommending over-the-counter AI wellness apps like Woebot or Wysa between sessions.

Federal laws are a better way to set standards, due to the high-level of nuance in mental health, she said.

“If you don’t pay attention to that nuance you end up with laws that don’t actually do what they intended them to do,” Wright said. “That’s what we’re seeing a lot at the state level.”

FDA’s Role

Wright in November presented to a US Food and Drug Administration advisory committee about AI mental health technology where she urged for modernizing regulations and establishing a public repository of FDA-cleared tools.

The FDA’s authorized some 1,200 AI-enabled medical devices. But none of them are for generative mental health, Michelle Tarver, director of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health told the FDA panel.

The risk posed by the technology is “AI Psychosis,” Bethany Russell, a licensed therapist who focuses on youth care, told the committee. Unregulated AI therapists may misdiagnose a patient resulting in unsafe responses to suicidal users. The solution is using it to safely “augment” professional care, she said.

The FDA said in an emailed statement that the agency “supports clear and predictable regulatory pathways that enable the development of safe, effective, and high-quality medical devices, including those that incorporate emerging technologies such as generative artificial intelligence.”

The American Medical Association also urged Congress to prohibit chatbots from diagnosing or treating mental health conditions, and to require FDA review for any that do behave like professionals.

“The absence of regulation by the federal government is leaving a vacuum” that “states are trying to fill,” said Michael Sutton, a Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton LLP attorney. It’s “an easy space for regulators to step in without upsetting the apple cart too much.”

Some AI mental health tools are trained via information specifically gathered for therapeutic purposes, which doesn’t include more general purpose AI like ChatGPT or https://t.co/r1czx1vmgc’s Emilie. But without a uniform standard, a state-by-state patchwork may limit the depth of regulation needed for patients to access more helpful tools than general LLMs.

“There’s going to be a future where you have FDA-approved AI tools for clinical purposes that then will not be available to providers to help extend their care,” Wright said.

• 𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 — The acquisition of the NDB Landfill and construction of the new Stateline facility will effectively double WBI's waste management site count, providing high-margin cross-selling opportunities.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞
• 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐒𝐮𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 — FY26 CapEx guidance was hiked by $100M at the midpoint. This aggressive growth spending requires heavy borrowing, pushing total debt up $150M sequentially to $1.636 billion.
• 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐲𝐞𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 — The special committee paused the conversion from a Delaware LLC to a Texas C-Corp until full index eligibility requirements are met, potentially delaying expected inflows from passive funds.

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢
Bullish. WaterBridge is successfully executing its roll-up and organic growth strategies simultaneously. The guidance raise across all major KPIs proves the underlying strength of the Delaware Basin macro environment and the company's pricing power.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

🟢 𝐒𝐩𝐞𝐞𝐝𝐰𝐚𝐲 𝐏𝐡𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐈 𝐏𝐢𝐩𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞 [NEW]
The central pillar of WBI's organic growth story is fully operational. First volumes on the Speedway Phase I Pipeline came online in July 2026 and are ramping steadily. This shifts the project from a capital sink to an accelerating cash flow generator, providing high visibility into H2 2026 margin expansion.

🟢 𝐃𝐨𝐮𝐛𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐟 𝐄𝐧𝐯𝐢𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬 [NEW]
WBI announced an aggressive move to double its waste management footprint. The $169 million net acquisition of the 560-acre NDB Landfill offers 40+ years of capacity. Paired with a greenfield investment in a new 280-acre Stateline facility, WaterBridge is leveraging its core E&P relationships to expand this complementary, high-margin product line.

⚪ 𝐑𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐞𝐫 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐢𝐝𝐬𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐦 𝐒𝐲𝐧𝐞𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐞𝐬 [NEW]
The $80 million cash acquisition of Ranger Water Midstream immediately adds ~70,000 barrels per day of permitted capacity and ~1.2 million barrels of storage in Lea County, NM. Crucially, this infrastructure is proximal to the Speedway network, allowing WBI to route dedicated Speedway volumes for treated supply and capture immediate commercial synergies.

🔴 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛𝐢𝐧𝐠 [NEW]
The aggressive pace of acquisitions and organic build-outs is taxing the balance sheet. Total borrowings climbed from $1.486B in Q1 to $1.636B in Q2. Concurrently, FY26 CapEx guidance was raised by $100M to a midpoint of $560M. Operating Cash Flow is strong, but it is currently dwarfed by the combined cash outlay for CapEx and acquisitions.

🔴 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐮𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐬𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐏𝐚𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐝 [NEW]
Management announced that the special committee evaluating the conversion to a Texas corporation has paused the process. While they acknowledge the long-term benefits, they are waiting until 'full index eligibility requirements are met.' This delays a potential catalyst for the stock, as broad index inclusion often drives passive buying.

🔴 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐫𝐨 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐚𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐁𝐚𝐬𝐢𝐧
WaterBridge's massive capacity build-out, including the new Stateline landfill and the Speedway expansion, is entirely tethered to continued high E&P activity in the Delaware Basin. While the current macro environment is highly constructive, any sudden shock to commodity prices could leave the company with overbuilt capacity and elevated debt leverage.

𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐬𝐬 𝐌𝐚𝐫𝐠𝐢𝐧 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐥: $0.22
Accelerating. Up from $0.20 in Q1 2026 and $0.18 in Q4 2025. This sequential margin expansion validates management's prior claims that new projects (like Kraken and Speedway) are being contracted at meaningfully higher rates than the legacy portfolio average.

𝐓𝐨𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐋𝐢𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐲: $347.6 million
Decelerating. Liquidity fell from $500.7 million at the end of Q1. The drop was driven by the $80 million cash outflow for the Ranger acquisition and heavy capital expenditures ($123.3M) during the quarter. To compensate, WBI subsequently amended its credit facility, expanding aggregate revolving commitments from $500M to $750M.

𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐞𝐝 𝐖𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐇𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐕𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐦𝐞𝐬: 2.55 to 2.75 million barrels per day
Accelerating. Raised from the previous range of 2.525 to 2.725 million bpd. The increase reflects the second-half volume impact of the Ranger infrastructure acquisition and strong base business demand.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $435 to $475 million
Accelerating. Raised by $10 million across the range from the previous $425-$465 million. The revision prices in expected second-half contributions from both the Ranger and NDB Landfill acquisitions.

𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐭𝐚𝐥 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞𝐬: $530 to $590 million
Accelerating. Significantly increased from the prior $430-$490 million range. The $100M bump is allocated toward high-return projects, including Ranger integration, the greenfield Stateline landfill construction, and the acceleration of the New Devon Project.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐈𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐱 𝐄𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐢𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞
Regarding the paused C-Corp conversion, what specific 'full index eligibility requirements' is the board waiting to meet, and what is the estimated timeline for hitting those thresholds?

𝐂𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐚𝐧𝐭 𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐋𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐠𝐞 𝐔𝐩𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬
With CapEx increasing by $100M and debt rising by $150M in a single quarter, where does covenant net leverage stand today, and do you still expect to remain under the 3.0x long-term target by year-end?

𝐖𝐚𝐬𝐭𝐞 𝐌𝐚𝐧𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐑𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐞 𝐌𝐢𝐱
By doubling the environmental waste management footprint via the NDB Landfill and Stateline facility, what percentage of total Adjusted EBITDA do you expect this segment to generate once both assets are fully operational?

#E2ENetworks- Q1FY27 Concall

Sovereign AI - The Biggest Differentiator
- The company's biggest pitch is "Sovereign AI."

- Customers can deploy and fine tune AI models on their own secure infrastructure instead of relying only on global AI APIs.

- This is attractive for enterprises and government projects where data security and control are important.

- However this is a strong positioning, not a true moat. Other cloud providers can also offer private AI deployments.

Long Experience in AI Infrastructure

- E2E has over 16 years of cloud infrastructure experience and several years in GPU computing.

- Strong operational expertise in running AI infrastructure and managing GPU clusters.

- This gives the company an execution advantage, but it is not impossible for competitors to build similar capabilities.

Flexible Technology Approach
- E2E is open to supporting future AI chips beyond NVIDIA.

- This reduces long term dependence on a single vendor.

- Today, however, its business is still largely built around NVIDIA GPUs.

Strategic Partnerships
- Partnerships such as with L&T can help expand infrastructure.

- But these are commercial partnerships, not exclusive arrangements.

- They don't create a lasting competitive moat.

- Management clearly said that the strong quarter was driven mainly by:
▪︎Higher GPU capacity
▪︎Very high utilization
▪︎Operating leverage

- They did not attribute the performance to higher pricing.

- Some price increases were implemented mainly to offset rising hardware costs.

- Existing customers were even offered long term contracts at older prices.

- E2E therefore has limited pricing power. Growth currently depends more on demand and capacity than on the ability to charge significantly higher prices.

- Strong Bet on India's AI Revolution

- Around 20-21% of revenue already comes from the India AI Mission.

- Management believes AI is a decade long supercycle and says the industry is still at "Day Zero" of AI adoption. 

- Around 5,100 GPUs are already live.

- Another 1,024 Blackwell GPUs are expected shortly.

- E2E is already preparing for future NVIDIA generations like B300 and Vera Rubin.

- A Delaware (USA) entity has been created to:
▪︎ Serve international customers
▪︎ Build global partnerships
▪︎ Expand overseas presence 

- Management believes each GPU generation can be monetized for 5-6 years, reducing fears that every new NVIDIA launch immediately makes older GPUs obsolete.

text:
$DK Q2 2026 earnings: Massive Crack Spread Rebound Drives Record Profitability, But Regulatory Adjustments Distort Baseline

Delek US Holdings delivered a blowout second quarter, reversing a deep year-ago loss to post $169.5 million in Net Income and $638.7 million in Adjusted EBITDA. Revenue accelerated 48% YoY to $4.08 billion. The narrative is heavily macro-driven: benchmark crack spreads skyrocketed 136% YoY, supercharging the refining segment. Delek Logistics (DKL) also printed a record quarter, anchoring cash flows. However, earnings quality requires scrutiny—$148.6 million of the Adjusted EBITDA resulted from a Renewable Volume Obligation (RVO) adjustment based on anticipated Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs). Even excluding this regulatory lifeline, the $490.1 million core Adjusted EBITDA highlights a profoundly strong operating environment following the Q1 Big Spring turnaround.

Full article with charts - link in bio

🐂 𝐁𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞
• 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐫𝐨 𝐓𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐬 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐨𝐧 𝐀𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐲𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 — The U. S. Gulf Coast 5-3-2 crack spread surged from $20.19 a year ago to $46.25. Delek's high distillate yield and direct access to advantaged domestic crude allowed the Refining segment's Adjusted EBITDA to quintuple to $566.2 million.
• 𝐓𝐮𝐫𝐧𝐚𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐭𝐞, 𝐅𝐮𝐥𝐥 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐚𝐜𝐢𝐭𝐲 𝐀𝐯𝐚𝐢𝐥𝐚𝐛𝐥𝐞 — With the Big Spring refinery turnaround successfully finished in Q1 and no additional turnarounds planned for the remainder of 2026, the company is perfectly positioned to capture peak summer driving demand with its full system online.

🐻 𝐁𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐞
• 𝐑𝐞𝐠𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐃𝐞𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 𝐃𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐄𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠𝐬 — A massive $148.6 million of the quarter's Adjusted EBITDA was driven by an RVO short adjustment. If the EPA denies or delays Small Refinery Exemptions, Delek faces a massive compliance liability that would crush cash flow.
• 𝐋𝐚𝐠𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞𝐬 𝐚𝐭 𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐀𝐬𝐬𝐞𝐭𝐬 — Despite the phenomenal macro environment, El Dorado's capture rate was a disappointing 35.4%, significantly lagging Tyler (50.4%) and Krotz Springs (51.0%).

⚖️ 𝐕𝐞𝐫𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭: 🟢
Bullish. While the reliance on EPA waivers remains a persistent overhang, Delek is generating massive free cash flow in the current crack spread environment. The reliable, growing base of Logistics (DKL) EBITDA and a cleansed post-turnaround refining system offer immense near-term upside.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐓𝐡𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐬

🟢🟢 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐂𝐫𝐚𝐜𝐤 𝐒𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐬 𝐃𝐫𝐢𝐯𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐁𝐨𝐨𝐦 [NEW]
Accelerating. The macro environment shifted drastically in Delek's favor. Benchmark crack spreads increased by an average of 136.0% from prior-year levels. The Gulf Coast 5-3-2 crack spread reached $46.25/bbl, allowing Refining segment Adjusted EBITDA to reverse from a low baseline to $566.2 million. High distillate yields are paying off disproportionately.

🟢 𝐃𝐊𝐋 𝐋𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐬 𝐀𝐧𝐜𝐡𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐂𝐚𝐬𝐡 𝐅𝐥𝐨𝐰
Stable. Delek Logistics (DKL) delivered its best quarter ever, generating $143.5 million in Adjusted EBITDA, up 12% YoY. Growth is fueled by higher margins in the wholesale business and increased third-party cash flows. Management notes the 'economic separation' between DK and DKL is increasing, paving the way for eventual value-unlocking deconsolidation.

🟢 𝐄𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐩𝐫𝐢𝐬𝐞 𝐎𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐢𝐳𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐏𝐥𝐚𝐧 (𝐄𝐎𝐏) 𝐄𝐱𝐞𝐜𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
Accelerating. Delek continues to execute its structural EOP, which targets over $220 million in annual run-rate improvements through software, commercial optimization, and operational efficiency (such as the recent acid gas injection (AGI) well completion in the Delaware basin). This structural cost advantage is amplifying the leverage on today's wide crack spreads.

🔴 𝐑𝐕𝐎 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐒𝐑𝐄 𝐑𝐞𝐠𝐮𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐨𝐫𝐲 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐨𝐬𝐮𝐫𝐞
Stable but critical. Delek booked a $148.6 million benefit for a Renewable Volume Obligation (RVO) short related to assumed Small Refinery Exemptions (SREs). While management has historically expressed confidence in the EPA granting these waivers to prevent 'disproportionate economic harm', this concentrates a massive percentage of Delek's profitability in the hands of political/regulatory decision-makers rather than operational performance.

🔴 𝐄𝐥 𝐃𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐨 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐂𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐢𝐜𝐭𝐬 𝐒𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐭𝐡 [NEW]
Despite a roaring macro environment that lifted the system-wide tide, the El Dorado refinery is an operational laggard. While its absolute refining production margin per barrel improved to $16.40 (up from $5.21 YoY), its capture rate was only 35.4%. This severely lags the 50.4% capture rate at the Tyler refinery and indicates sub-optimal crude slate processing or lingering backwardation impacts isolated to this specific asset.

𝐎𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫 𝐊𝐏𝐈𝐬

𝐍𝐞𝐭 𝐃𝐞𝐛𝐭 (𝐄𝐱𝐜𝐥𝐮𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐃𝐊𝐋): $202.1 million
Delek's standalone balance sheet continues to strengthen. Total consolidated net debt was $2.56 billion, but $2.36 billion of that sits at the DKL level. The parent company's low net debt position ($614.9M cash vs $817.0M debt) offers immense flexibility for continued countercyclical share repurchases and maintaining the $0.255 quarterly dividend.

𝐑𝐞𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐎𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐄𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐧𝐬𝐞𝐬 𝐩𝐞𝐫 𝐁𝐚𝐫𝐫𝐞𝐥: $5.32
Stable. Despite high inflation in the broader industrial economy, Delek kept total refining operating expenses relatively flat YoY (up slightly from $5.17 in Q2 2025). This cost control validates the structural changes implemented under the Enterprise Optimization Plan.

𝐆𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐚𝐧𝐜𝐞

𝐃𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐤 𝐋𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐬 (𝐃𝐊𝐋) 𝐅𝐘𝟐𝟔 𝐀𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐝 𝐄𝐁𝐈𝐓𝐃𝐀: $520 - $560 million
Stable. The company reaffirmed the annual guidance for its midstream arm. After printing $143.5 million in Q2, DKL is perfectly on track to hit the midpoint ($540M) or higher, cementing its role as a highly visible cash flow engine that covers the consolidated enterprise's dividend and interest burdens.

𝐊𝐞𝐲 𝐐𝐮𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬

𝐄𝐥 𝐃𝐨𝐫𝐚𝐝𝐨 𝐂𝐚𝐩𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 𝐑𝐚𝐭𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐦𝐞𝐝𝐢𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧
El Dorado's capture rate of 35.4% significantly trailed Tyler and Krotz Springs. How much of this was driven by crude slate availability versus specific operational bottlenecks, and what EOP initiatives are targeting this specific asset?

𝐒𝐑𝐄 𝐂𝐨𝐦𝐦𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐔𝐩𝐝𝐚𝐭𝐞
Given the $148.6 million RVO adjustment this quarter, what is the latest correspondence with the EPA regarding the 2025 and 2026 Small Refinery Exemption petitions? At what point does the RIN liability force physical blending changes if waivers are delayed?

𝐃𝐊𝐋 𝐕𝐚𝐥𝐮𝐞 𝐔𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐜𝐤 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐧𝐞

text:
Undefeated (19-0 coming in) Johnny Saxton stops Joey Carkido (pictured) when referee Pete Tomasco doesn't allow Carkido out for the 6th round on August 6, 1951 at Toppi Stadium in Philadelphia.
---------------------------------------------------------
From Jim Amato (for IBRO):

The great city of Youngstown, Ohio, has produced many a fine fighter: Lenny and Ray Mancini, Tommy Bell, Tony Janiro, "Red" D'Amato and Harry Arroyo, etc. One of Youngstown's finest from the 1940s and early '50s has been all but forgotten. Only the die-hard local boxing fans remember just how tough Joey Carkido was.Carkido racked up an impressive 33-3 record as an amateur boxer before turning professional in 1945. As a pro, he won 46 of his first 50 fights against some rugged customers like Vic Moreno, Pete Manchio, Ray Salas and Ross Anzalone.On December 8, 1947, Carkido fought the first of four world champions he would meet in his distinguished career. Paddy DeMarco halted Carkido in seven rounds.The year 1948 was an "up and down" year for Carkido. He won only five of 16 fights while losing 8 and drawing in three. In 1949 Carkido again lost more then he won, but it was against top-flight competition like Ron Delaney and another champ, Lew Jenkins. On April 3, 1950, he scored the biggest win of his career when he outpointed Beau Jack over ten rounds. In his next match he dropped a ten-round duke to Charley Fusari.Carkido didn't fight too many stiffs. Still there were more losses than victories. In 1951 kayo losses to Chuck Taylor and Johnny Saxton pushed Carkido out of the big leagues. He would lose all four of his 1952 contests.After 98 professional fights Carkido retired with a respectable 59-32-7 record. He boxed several times at Madison Square Garden. In 1988 he was inducted into the Trumbull County of Ohio Legends of Leather Hall of Fame. A worthy tribute to a fine fighter.
----------------------------------------------------------
From Philly Boxing History:

In the only photo I've ever seen of Toppi Stadium (above) the venue looks like a dream. Imagine an outdoor stadium built specifically for boxing events. Instead of the massive five-figure capacity of the baseball and football fields that normally housed outdoor summer fights, Toppi Stadium was an outdoor arena of intimate proportions. It was a large outdoor boxing club really. Five-thousand seats. A bricked-in plot roughly the size of a football field with raised bleachers on the east and west ends, a ringside circle of chairs on the ground, and tall floodlights lining the north and south walls. In the center of everything was a simple three-rope boxing ring. The four corner posts of the ring rose up to form a wrought-iron lighting framework above the canvas, making the ring look like an off-season cabana. The photo shows a South Philly crowd mostly in short sleeves presumably on a warm summer night. Toppi Stadium staged its first boxing show on July 15, 1948. And for six years it was a treasure for local boxing fans. Forty-five fight cards played out through 1953 in the open air of Packer Park between June and September.
No championship bouts were ever staged here. In fact the majority of the main events were 8-rounders. Still in the days of the late 1940s and early 1950s, during the very first period of TV competition, boxing talent abounded and boxing shows were frequent. Toppi Stadium offered a nice night out for fans during the warm weather months and a platform for the active purse-hungry boxing talent. In addition to the who's-who of Philadelphia fighters that appeared at this venue, many big names fought at Toppi Stadium. Included in this cast of characters were Sandy Saddler, Lew Jenkins, Paddy DeMarco, Arthur King, Jose Basora, Gene Burton and Chico Varona.
South Philly's Eddie Giosa headlined five shows, more than any other boxer. Other Philly-based stars who appeared were Clarence "Honeychile" Johnson, Marvin Edelman, Harold Johnson, Joey Giardello, George Benton, Jimmy Carlini, Ike White, Gil Turner, Calvin Smith, Johnny Forte, Jimmy Collins, Charley Spicer and New Jersey's Johnny Saxton & George Costner.
In the first show, Eddie Giosa beat Johnny Forte over ten rounds before 2,649 fans. The largest crowd ever to attend a Toppi Stadium show was 4,877 in 1949. The main event that night saw George "Sugar" Costner beat Bobby Lee by ten-round decision. Young Gil Turner ran his undefeated record to 21-0 in the summer of 1951 when he stopped Rudy Zadell in five rounds after being staggered himself. The following summer after ten more bouts, Turner would challenge Kid Gavilan for the welterweight crown. Featherweight champ Sandy Saddler stopped by for a non-title bout on August 20, 1951 and scored a KO over Hermie Freeman. South Philly's Jimmy Carlini scored one of the best wins in his undefeated career when he decisioned Ike White in eight rounds on July 7, 1953. George Benton showed great promise in two appearances in 1953. He won a decision over Chuck Goldsby and stopped Jimmy Franklin in six. The latter was a main event. However, the most notable fight to take place at Toppi Stadium is famous for tragic reasons. 
On September 16, 1948, heavyweights Billy "Chicken" Thompson of Philadelphia and Johnny Haynes of New York clashed in an eight-round main event at Toppi. The 21-year old Thompson was coming off a KO loss at the hands of Jimmy Bivins, but still he brought a fine pro record of 17-3 into the ring against Haynes, 20-10. Haynes fought well and won most of the rounds. Thompson did win a couple sessions, but for the most part Haynes battered him. In the 8th and final round Thompson was dropped to the canvas, partially out of the ring. The final count of ten came with just three seconds left in the fight. Unable to be revived, Thompson was taken to the hospital in critical condition. He underwent brain surgery but never regained consciousness. Thompson died five days later.
The forty-five fight cards played out over six outdoor seasons, but there was no boxing in 1952 at Toppi Stadium, presumably due to the major outdoor action that year at Municipal Stadium - three massive championship shows in June, July & September. That summer Toppi Stadium only offered pro wrestling. But during all the other years of its existence, Toppi Stadium thrived. There were 8 boxing shows in 1948, and 13, 5, 10, and 9 in 1949, 1950, 1951, & 1953, respectively.  
By 1954, Toppi Stadium was history. The ballparks continued to host occasional boxing events through 1958, but after that, outdoor boxing in Philadelphia was a thing of the past.
The venue's name came from Jimmy Toppi, Sr. and Jimmy Toppi, Jr., the prominent father-son and boxing manager-promoter team who built it. During this same period, the Toppis ran boxing shows almost every week at The Met in the cooler months of the year. Their Toppi Stadium was the summer home for their boxing program.
Toppi Stadium was a little jewel of Philly boxing that came during a very fine ring era. It was a unique fight venue that carved out its own chapter in local ring history.

text:
In 1998, Warren Buffett gave a 1-hour masterclass on how to never lose money investing.

Here are the 22 most valuable lessons from his lecture:

1. You only have to get rich once. If you have $100 million and can make 10% unleveraged or 20% leveraged, the difference between $110 million and $120 million at year-end means nothing to your life, your family, or anything. But the downside, especially with other people's money, is disgrace, humiliation, and facing the friends whose money you lost. The equation never makes sense.

2. To make money they did not need, they risked money they did have and needed. That is just plain foolish, Buffett says, regardless of your IQ. If you hand him a gun with a million chambers and one bullet and offer him any sum to put it to his temple and pull once, he will not do it. There is nothing on the upside that justifies the downside. People do this financially all the time without thinking.

3. The smartest people in finance went broke, and that is the most fascinating story Buffett knows. Long-term Capital Management had 16 people with possibly the highest average IQ of any business in the country, 350 to 400 combined years of experience, and most of their own net worth in the firm. They still went bankrupt. Buffett says if he ever wrote a book, it would be called why smart people do dumb things.

4. Beta and sigmas tell you nothing about the real risk of going broke. The LTCM team relied heavily on mathematics and believed a six- or seven-sigma event could not touch them. They were wrong. History does not tell you the probabilities of future financial events. The real risk is not volatility. It is a permanent, irreversible blind spot in something crucial, often caused by knowing a great deal about something else.

5. Invest only in businesses you can understand. That one rule narrows the field by about 90%, and that is fine. Buffett can understand Coca-Cola. he cannot value an internet company, and he says if a student handed him a valuation of one on a final exam, he would flunk them. People thought Enron was incredible because it had a good track record, but almost nobody understood how it made money. That was the signal to avoid it.

6. You want a business that is a castle with a wide moat around it. Inside the castle, you want an honest, able, hard-working duke. The moat can be low cost, like Geico in auto insurance, or brand, or patents, or location. But a wonderful castle will always be attacked, so the job of every manager Buffett owns is one thing: widen the moat. Throw crocodiles and sharks into it to keep competitors out.

7. Moats change slowly and invisibly, but they change. Thirty years ago, Kodak's moat was as wide as Coca-Cola's. They had share of mind; the little yellow box meant best in everyone's head. Then they let Fuji into the Olympics and narrowed their own moat. Coca-Cola's moat, by contrast, is wider now than 30 years ago. Every time infrastructure gets built in a country that is not yet profitable, the moat widens a little. You cannot see it day by day, but in 10 years, the difference is enormous.

8. Share of mind beats share of market. When you say Disney, every person in the room has something in their head. Say Universal Pictures or 20th Century Fox, and you have nothing. A mother with two kids will pick the $17.95 Disney video over the $16.95 alternative because she knows it will be fine and does not want to preview ten videos to decide. That little bit of certainty in the customer's mind is worth a fortune.

9. The best businesses have pricing power and require little capital. see's candy sold 16 million pounds at $1.95 when Buffett bought it for $25 million. The entire thesis was whether the price could go to $2.25 without hurting sales. It could, because nobody wants to hand their valentine a box of candy and say, "This year I took the low bid." Today, See's makes $60 million on the same formulas and still takes almost no capital. Compare that to GM, which had to reinvest every dollar into better factories and whose stock barely moved over 50 years.

10. The best businesses earn a royalty on other people's capital. Coca-Cola sells a formula and collects a royalty on every drink. American Express takes a few percent of every dollar you spend. You put up the capital, they take a cut. Low capital intensity is one of the most underrated qualities in a business and one of the surest paths to durable wealth.

11. Define your circle of competence and stay inside it. The size of the circle does not matter. Staying inside, it does. If you know which 30 companies out of thousands you actually understand, you are fine. Buffett understood H.H. brown shoes and Frank Rooney, so he closed that deal in five minutes. If you do not know enough to understand a business instantly, you will not understand it in a month either.

12. Ignore the macro entirely. Buffett has never bought or skipped a business because of a feeling about interest rates, the economy, or any macro forecast. If Alan Greenspan and Bob Rubin both whispered exactly what they would do for the next 12 months, it would not change what he pays for anything. You want to focus on what is important and knowable. The macro is important but not knowable, so you ignore it.

13. Inactivity is the strategy, not a flaw. Wall Street makes money on activity. You make money on inactivity. A broker is like a doctor paid by how often he changes your pills. If everyone in a room trades their portfolio with everyone else every day, they all end up broke, and the intermediary keeps the money. Buffett looks for one good idea a year and rides it to its full potential. He measures Berkshire by how little turnover there is, like a church where the same people fill the seats every Sunday.

14. If you understand businesses, diversification is a mistake. For the 99% who will not evaluate businesses, Buffett recommends a low-cost index fund and extreme diversification. But if you bring real intensity to evaluating companies, owning more than six is a terrible idea. Very few people got rich on their seventh best idea. A lot of people got rich on their best one. Buffett keeps about half his money in what he likes best.

15. Buffett's biggest mistakes are mistakes of omission, not commission. The times he understood a business well enough to act and instead sat there sucking his thumb. He passed on healthcare stocks during the Clinton plan and on Fannie Mae in the mid-eighties, each a multi-billion-dollar miss. Accounting never captures these. The $2,000 he put into a Sinclair service station as a young man, money he lost, has an opportunity cost of about $6 billion today.

16. Focus on what will happen, not when. Coca-Cola went public in 1919 at $40 a share and dropped to $19 within a year. There was always a reason not to buy: the great depression, world war, sugar rationing, thermonuclear weapons. But one share bought then and reinvested would be worth about $5 million. If you are right about the business, you will make a lot of money. The timing is the tricky part, so do not focus on it.

17. When hiring, look for integrity, intelligence, and energy. But if the person lacks the first one, you actually want them dumb and lazy. Because a person with intelligence and energy but no integrity will destroy you. Buffett borrowed this from Pete Kiewit. The trait everyone screens for last is the one that matters most.

18. Here is a thought experiment Buffett gives students. Imagine you could own 10% of one classmate for the rest of their life. You would not pick the highest IQ or the best grades. You would pick the person you respond to best, the one who is generous, honest, gives credit to others, and has leadership qualities. Now imagine you also had to short one classmate. You would pick the egotistical, greedy, slightly dishonest one. The qualities that decide both are not talent. They are character.

19. Every quality on the admirable side is achievable, and every quality on the repellent side is removable. The things that make you want to own 10% of someone are not the ability to throw a football or run fast; they are behavior, temperament, and character, all of which anyone can choose. Buffett's point: you already own 100% of yourself, so you might as well become the person worth betting on.

20. The chains of habit are too light to be felt until they are too heavy to be broken. Buffett sees people in their forties and fifties trapped by self-destructive patterns they can no longer change. At a young age, you can choose any habits you want. Ben Franklin and Ben Graham both did exactly this, looking at people they admired and simply deciding to behave like them. There was nothing impossible about it.

21. Take a job you would take if you were already independently wealthy. Buffett told a 28-year-old at Harvard who wanted a consulting job "to look good on his resume" that it was like saving up sex for your old age. There comes a time to just start doing what you love. Buffett offered to work for Ben Graham for free, was told he was overpriced, and kept pestering him for years. Take the job you would jump out of bed for. You cannot miss.

22. You won the ovarian lottery, and that should shape how you think. Buffett imagines a genie 24 hours before your birth letting you design the world's rules, with one catch: you do not know which of 5.8 billion balls you will draw. Born here or in Afghanistan, with an IQ of 130 or 70, male or female, able-bodied or not. If you could put your ball back and draw one of 100 random others, most people would not, because they are already in the luckiest 1%. Buffett knows he is perfectly wired for a market economy that pays him like crazy, while an equally good citizen leading scout troops and teaching Sunday school is not, purely by luck.

Dade Battlefield Historic State Park was created to protect an important piece of Florida’s past. The land was set aside in 1921, ensuring that the pine flatwoods landscape remained intact for future generations. A monument was added the following year, and the protected area gradually expanded as the state worked to preserve both the natural setting and the cultural significance of the site. 

Today, the park welcomes visitors with a museum, shaded walking trails and interpretive signs that share the broader story of the people and events connected to the area.  

Each January, a large reenactment offers a public‑friendly way to learn, reflect and experience one of Florida’s most meaningful historic places.

text:
🥎Nittany Lions Welcome English to 2027 Softball Roster

University Park, Pa. – Penn State softball and head coach Clarisa Crowell announced an addition to the program’s 2027 roster on Wednesday afternoon, with the Blue & White set to welcome NJCAA DI College World Series catcher and Santa Fe College alumnus Sydney English to Happy Valley.

A native of Callahan, Florida, English joins the Nittany Lions following a standout two-year career at Santa Fe College, where she developed into one of the top offensive performers in the program. After making an immediate impact as a freshman in 2025, English elevated her game even further during the 2026 campaign, batting .378 with 71 hits, 48 RBI, 16 doubles and seven home runs while compiling a .491 on-base percentage and .574 slugging percentage. Her contributions to the team were essential to propelling the Saints to an appearance in the 2026 NJCAA DI College World Series. In recognition of her efforts, English was named an All-Citrus Conference North First Team member as well as a Second Team All-FCSAA selection. Across her two collegiate seasons, the left-handed hitter produced a .346 career batting average with 84 hits, 58 RBI, 19 doubles and eight home runs, reaching base at a .469 clip.

While at Penn State, English plans to pursue a degree in organizational leadership through the College of Liberal Arts. Prior to beginning her collegiate career, she attended West Nassau High School in her hometown, where she earned Athlete of the Year honors in 2024 while collecting four First Team All-First Coast selections, four All-Nassau County honors, a pair of Florida All-State accolades and serving as a three-year team captain. A multi-sport athlete, English also lettered in volleyball and girls weightlifting while participating in the Fellowship of Christian Athletes. She competed in travel softball with Santa Fe Inferno under coach Jason Nowling from 2021 through 2024, helping her club to a JO Cup runner-up finish and a third-place showing at TSCP Nationals.

FOLLOW SYDNEY ON SOCIAL

Instagram | @sydney3nglish
X | @sydenglish1

WHY SYDNEY CHOSE PENN STATE
“Choosing Penn State was an easy decision because it offers everything I was looking for, both on and off the field. The coaching staff, facilities, and competitive softball program made me feel confident that it was the right place for me. This is the opportunity I dreamed of earning after coming from the junior college level, and I’m incredibly grateful that the coaches believer in me. I couldn’t be more excited to represent Penn State and compete for this team on and off the field.”

COACH CROWELL ON ENGLISH

"We are thrilled to welcome Sydney to our Penn State softball family. She is a left-handed hitter who will add power to our offense and depth to our catching staff. Sydney brings valuable championship experience after helping guide Santa Fe College to the NJCAA DI College World Series, where she competed on one of the nation's top Junior College teams. We are excited about the impact she’ll have both on the field and within our culture, and we can’t wait to see her in the Blue & White this year."

FOLLOW THE NITTANY LIONS

Visit https://t.co/3oReyVDVxG for more information on Penn State softball. Fans can keep up to date with the Nittany Lion softball team on Facebook at /pennstatesoftball as well as Twitter and Instagram @PennStateSB.

text:
This is the whole reason I stopped renting my life.

When your income comes from one client, one platform, one country, one bank, that isn’t freedom. That’s permission somebody else renews every month.

Learned it in Morocco. $125k sitting in my account and my card wouldn’t work because of some agreement between two governments I never signed. Nearly stranded in a hotel with money I couldn’t touch.

That was the day I stopped confusing access with ownership.

Now it’s banks in multiple countries. Residency. My own audience and offers instead of renting attention. And land here in Georgia, which is the one that actually matters.

Because you can’t leave a lease to your children.

Every generation before us understood this. You worked, you acquired, you passed it down. A man was supposed to hand his sons more ground than he was given.

We traded that for convenience and called it freedom.

Own something real. Something your kids or future kids can stand on after you’re gone.
