text:
We Have Nowhere Else To Go

Letters from Stockholm

By Kio Amachree

There is a phrase that has followed me my entire life, spoken in markets and ministries alike, half in admiration and half in warning: power is sweet. It is one of the most dangerous sentences in our national vocabulary. It contains, in three words, the whole disease.

Because in Nigeria power has never been widely understood as a trust, something borrowed briefly from other people, to be handed back intact. It is understood as a harvest. A season. Your turn. And when a man believes it is his turn, he does not govern. He gathers.

I write this from Stockholm, and I want to say plainly what the distance has made unbearably clear to me. We are not being destroyed by our enemies. We are being destroyed by the people we trusted, and by a culture that still, even now, congratulates them.

The Arithmetic of Contempt

Look at the numbers, because the numbers do not lecture. They simply state.

The 2026 Appropriation Bill went to the National Assembly at 58.18 trillion naira. It came back at 68.323 trillion naira and was signed into law on 31 March 2026. Ten trillion naira, added by legislators, to a budget already running a deficit of roughly forty six per cent, money the country does not have and must borrow, with debt financing revised upward to some 29.2 trillion naira.

What did that ten trillion buy?

The civic monitoring group Tracka went through the documents line by line. It found 15.13 billion naira allocated for thirty nine sport utility vehicles, and 947.7 billion naira for 2,579 so called empowerment projects. Together, 962.83 billion naira, more than the combined 960.27 billion naira allocated to seven federal ministries: Trade and Investment, Housing, Women Affairs, Justice, Livestock Development, Aviation, and Petroleum Resources.

Of those 2,579 empowerment projects, only seventy have a clearly identified location. Seventy. The rest is money released into fog.

Then there is the small matter of the Presidential Foreign Intervention Promotion Council, to which 1.3 billion naira was appropriated in the 2026 Act. It does not exist. A phantom body, funded from the sweat of people queuing for kerosene.

And the Almajiri and Out of School Children Education Commission, an agency created for the poorest children in the Federation, was found carrying a 1.4 billion naira road project in Ogun State, part of some 8.4 billion naira in road allocations inserted into the budget of a body with no road building mandate whatsoever. Femi Falana, SAN, called it what it is: budget padding. He also said the quiet part aloud, that it persists because the President allows it.

This is not incompetence. Incompetence is accidental. This is design.

In June 2026 the Federal High Court in Lagos, Justice Yellim Bogoro presiding, declared the National Assembly's 110 billion naira vehicle and allowance scheme unlawful, 40 billion naira for 465 bulletproof SUVs and 70 billion naira in support allowances, in a suit brought by SERAP against the Senate President and the Speaker. The court held that spending public money on luxury vehicles while millions cannot eat was a failure to prioritise the national interest.

The National Assembly's response was to explain that the Land Cruisers are for constituency work.

That is where we are. Not shame. Not resignation. Explanation.

Darkness in the Capital, and Dry Taps in Maitama

On the morning of 23 January 2026 the national grid collapsed. Not partially. Total generation fell to zero megawatts. Every one of the eleven distribution companies, Abuja, Benin, Eko, Enugu, Ibadan, Ikeja, Jos, Kaduna, Kano, Port Harcourt and Yola, recorded nothing. Four days later it happened again. It had happened on 29 December 2025. It has happened, in one form or another, year after year after year.

And yet in Aba, Abia State, a city of some nine hundred thousand people, the lights stayed on. Geometric Power's 188 megawatt plant, its own distribution network, its own smart meters. An island of ordinary competence in an ocean of national failure, proving definitively that this is not a curse, not a climate, not a colonial inheritance. It is a choice, and other Nigerians have made the opposite choice successfully, in Nigeria, with Nigerians.

Now consider water. In January 2026 the Abuja Electricity Distribution Company disconnected the FCT Water Board from power over unpaid bills. The FCT Administration, the government of the Federal Capital Territory, could not pay its electricity bill. The Lower Usuma Dam stopped operating. Taps went dry across the capital of the Federal Republic.

By March, residents of Ushafa, Bwari and Dutse had gone weeks without water. By May, communities along the Airport Road corridor, Lugbe, Aco Estate, Goza and Sauka, reported taps dry for months. This August, residents of Wuse Zones 1, 2 and 3 and Wuse II are appealing publicly to the Minister after nearly three weeks without supply, buying from vendors at prices that rise every day.

All of this in a city where a 470 million dollar Greater Abuja Water Supply Project was commissioned with cameras and speeches in June 2025.

We have mastered the ribbon and forgotten the pipe.

A Young Woman Died, and the Country Still Does Not Know How

On 27 June 2026, Mary Habila, twenty six years old, died inside the compound of the country home of the Minister of Works in Uburu, Ebonyi State.

I make no accusation. I do not know what happened in that room, and neither does anyone else outside it, and that is precisely the point. The Director of Public Prosecutions advised that a post mortem was essential, noting there was no evidence she was unwell before her sudden death. The police insisted on it. The Minister has publicly stated he supports an autopsy, described her as being like a daughter to him, and offered his account of a nosebleed. Her family, citing cultural reasons, opposed the examination, and were reduced to petitioning the Inspector General of Police to release their daughter's body for burial.

Weeks passed. Photographs circulated. Nothing was settled.

That is the scandal. Not a verdict, but the absence of any machinery capable of producing one. A young Nigerian woman can die in proximity to power in this country and the state cannot reliably tell her mother why. Two months later, we still do not have a clean, credible, independent answer. In a functioning republic that answer would have taken eleven days and would not have depended on who the deceased happened to be standing next to.

And she is not alone. On 26 April 2026 in Effurun, Delta State, Mene Ogidi, twenty eight, was restrained on the ground and shot at close range by an Assistant Superintendent of Police. We know his name only because a stranger held up a phone. How many have no stranger, and no phone?

What the Abuse Costs, Measured in Children

Nigeria has 18.3 million children out of school, the highest number on earth. UNICEF puts the figure of children and adolescents without access to formal schooling or digital learning at more than 28 million. Only about twenty seven per cent of children between seven and fourteen have basic reading skills. And in this same 2026 budget, education's share fell from the previous year.

Between June 2025 and May 2026, more than 14,500 people died in conflict related violence, placing Nigeria fourth in the world on the Global Terrorism Index. On 26 April 2026 gunmen took twenty three children from an orphanage near Lokoja.

Set that against 15.13 billion naira for thirty nine motor cars.

That is the exchange rate of our governance. That is what a stolen trust actually purchases: a generation that cannot read, in a country that cannot protect them, financed by debt they will inherit.

The Door Behind Us Is Closing

Here is why I am writing this now, and why I am writing it with urgency rather than elegance.

For sixty years, the escape valve for Nigerian ambition has been departure. When the country failed you, you left. Europe took you. America took you. That door is closing, and it is closing fast.

In February 2026 the European Union voted to allow the deportation of asylum seekers to safe third countries with which they have no connection whatsoever. In June the Pact on Migration and Asylum came into force, and a further agreement legalised return hubs outside the Union and the detention of minors. Germany's Interior Minister has spoken of commissioning return hubs before the end of this year, with African countries under discussion. The Netherlands has already concluded an arrangement with Uganda.

Meanwhile a word that was fringe when I first heard it, remigration, the mass deportation of non white people regardless of citizenship status, now appears in far right manifestos across Europe and has its own annual summit, most recently on 30 May 2026.

I live in Europe. I have watched this hardening arrive year by year, in the tone of a bus driver, in the language of a parliamentary debate, in the way a policeman looks at a boy in Rinkeby. Africans are being made the symbol of everything Europe fears about itself.

So understand what this means. The diaspora is not a permanent exit. It is a shrinking room. Whatever passport we carry, whatever tax we pay, whatever decades we have given, there is one country on this earth that can never deport us, and it is Nigeria.

That is not sentiment. That is strategy. We have precisely one homeland, and men who cannot pay an electricity bill are running it into the ground.

There Will Be No Break Up

Let me be unambiguous, because I know where this argument usually goes.

Nigeria will not break up. It is not going to happen. I say this not as a loyalist but as a realist. Every serious model of dissolution ends the same way, not in three or six orderly republics, but in a decade of contested borders, stranded minorities, collapsed currency, ruined trade, and armed men filling the vacuum. And the people who would suffer most are precisely those who suffer most now. The Niger Delta child, the Almajiri, the market woman in Onitsha, the widow in Maiduguri.

Break up is the fantasy of men who imagine they would be on the winning side of it. There is no winning side of it.

The work is not secession. The work is repair. We must improve the Nigeria we actually have, for children who will actually live in it, learning honestly from what we got wrong. Anything else is a daydream that costs blood.

What Must Be Done

I do not believe in complaint without prescription. So let me state a minimum programme, modest, specific, and achievable within a single term by any government that wanted to.

One. Consequence, not recovery. Asset recovery figures are announced with fanfare every year while politically exposed persons are almost never convicted. Recovery without prosecution is simply a tax on theft. Nigeria needs a genuinely independent prosecutorial office for public sector corruption, with security of tenure, budgetary independence from the National Assembly it must investigate, and a published register of every case above one billion naira with its status updated quarterly.

Two. Kill the padding. Every insertion into an agency budget by a legislator should be published, by name, with the sponsoring member identified, within seven days of insertion. Sunlight costs nothing. It is the cheapest reform available to us and the one most fiercely resisted, which tells you exactly how well it would work.

Three. Replicate Aba, do not repair the grid. Nigeria should stop pretending it will fix a national transmission system it has failed to fix for forty years. Decentralise. Licence and finance municipal and regional generation on the Geometric model, city by city, with guaranteed cost reflective tariffs and ring fenced revenues. Twenty Abas would transform this country faster than any single federal project.

Four. Autopsy as a right. No death occurring on the premises of a public official should be closed without an independent forensic post mortem conducted outside the jurisdiction where the official holds influence, with the report published. Not to persecute anyone. To protect everyone, including the innocent official, who is entitled to be cleared by evidence rather than by silence.

Five. Diaspora as instrument, not remittance machine. Nigerians abroad send home tens of billions of dollars a year and are treated as an ATM with a voice they are not permitted to use. Diaspora voting, diaspora bonds tied to audited municipal water and power projects, and a standing diaspora accountability office with real reporting powers. We have engineers at Sweco and AFRY, lawyers in the Inns of Court, physicians in Houston, financiers in Zurich. Use us, or lose us permanently to societies that are already deciding they no longer want us.

To My Brothers and Sisters Abroad

I am driven by something I cannot fully explain and have stopped trying to. Call it inheritance. My father served this country when service still meant something, when a Nigerian could stand in a room in New York or London and be the most serious person in it. I have spent years now setting down a record of what is being done to that inheritance, and I will go on doing it.

But I cannot do it alone, and neither can any of us.

To every Nigerian in Stockholm, London, Houston, Toronto, Johannesburg and Dubai, the fight is not optional any longer, and it is not charity. It is self defence. The clouds over Nigeria are darkening, Europe is bolting its doors, and the men holding our trust are buying tyres for bulletproof convoys while a nurse's family begs for her body and a child in Sokoto has never held a book.

Enough. Write. Document. Petition. Fund the journalists. Name the accounts. Support the courts when they rule against the powerful, as one did in June. Refuse the invitation to celebrate the man who has made it without asking what he made it from. That celebration, that quiet, cultural, universal Nigerian applause for the successful thief, is the deepest root of the whole catastrophe, and it lives not only in Abuja but in our own living rooms in the diaspora.

Power abused is not sweet. It is a slow poison, and we have been drinking it for sixty five years while calling it wine.

We have one country. There is no other. Let us behave, at last, like people who know it.

Kio Amachree is Founder and President of Worldview International.

text:
Heavyweight Wayne Bethea (pictured) runs into a wrecking ball named Charles "Sonny" Liston on August 6, 1958 at Chicago Stadium, getting TKO'd 69 seconds into round one.

The AP reports:

"Sonny Liston of Philadelphia slammed New York's Wayne Bethea with a quick barrage of heavy rights and lefts for a 69-second TKO victory Wednesday in a scheduled 10-round heavyweight bout in Chicago Stadium. Liston dropped Bethea for the first time in his career with a savage series, starting with an explosive right to the jaw. Bethea wobbled back into action after a mandatory eight count, but then was sent reeling helplessly across the ring under another furious assault by Liston. Referee Bernie Weissman mercifully called it a TKO in 1:09 of the opening round."

UPI reported that Wayne Bethea had lost 7 teeth during the one-round fight.

Sonny Liston's trainer, Jimmy Wilson, 54, died the night before this bout in Philadelphia due to a heart condition.

"It was in the bag - I could see it in your eyes." - Tony Vone, Bethea's co-manager stated, accusing referee Bernie Weissmann of improprieties while stopping the fight prematurely in Liston's favor.

Immediately after this fight Frank Gilmer summoned Tony Vone, Bethea's co-manager, to a hearing to explain his accusations levelled at referee Bernie Weissmann. On September 18th, finding no evidence of improprieties in Weissmann's actions and the fact that Vone did not appear, Gilmer revoked Vone's corner license with the state of Illinois.

"I can say right now when a boxer is hit and turns completely around and makes no effort to face his opponent and staggers off to the side and gives every appearance of not having his faculties, there is nothing a referee can do but stop the fight to protect the fighter from possible injury. If I had been the referee, I'd have done the same thing Weissman did." Gilmer would state in response to Vone's charges.

Immediately after this bout, International Boxing Club President Truman Gibson said he would offer Heavyweight Champion Floyd Patterson a $250,000 guarantee to meet Liston in Chicago.

Patterson would stop Roy "Cut And Shoot" Harris in a title defense on the 18th and then choose to defend his title against Brian London (coming in off a points loss to Henry Cooper in January) next, in May of 1959.

Liston would wait over four years, scoring fourteen straight wins, before getting a title shot.
----------------------------------------------------------
Wayne Bethea would win two in a row following his 1st round TKO loss to Sonny Liston in August of 1958.

Though he managed a run of solid wins early in his career - triumphs over Julio Mederos, a fading Ezzard Charles, Jimmy "The Spoiler" Slade, and Joe Bygraves - Bethea would drop two bouts on split decisons to Zora Folley (Dec, 1956 and Jan 1957) followed up a few fights later by a loss to Harold Johnson by decision that put him in the category of "tough fighters to fight that never seemed to get a decision."

The losses to Nino Valdes (UD10) and Liston (TKO10 in 1958 cemented his status.

He'd only be stopped once in his 28-18-4 (11 KO's) career, by the formidable Liston, and in addition to Miteff, Valdes and Folley he'd drop a handful of decisions to a "Who's who?" of late 1950's/early 1960's contenders such as Eddie Machen, Cleveland Williams, Karl Mildenberger and Henry Cooper.

Long forgotten is that his ring finale ended in tragedy, on October 14th of 1963, when Ernie Knox died of a subdural hematoma on the brain just two days after he was KO'd in the 9th round, at the Baltimore Coliseum, by Bethea.

A grand Jury would investigate Knox's death as his autopsy showed that he weighed only approximately 153 lbs (at his autopsy) which meant that his weigh-in tally of 178 lbs could not have been correct.

The Medical Examiner testified that Knox's weight could not have changed more than 3-6 lbs between the end of the bout and his autopsy. After reporting that "no fraud" was found in the death of Knox, the jury urged the state to enact tighter regulations for control of boxing.

The jury suggested that all weigh-ins be held only on official scales of the state athletic commission and examining physicians or a member of the commission directly supervise the weigh-ins.

text:
ICE turned migrant detention into the FBI's largest DNA pipeline in 2025, cataloguing toddlers alongside asylum seekers in a permanent criminal database built for crimes nobody committed.

Georgetown Law's Center on Privacy and Technology estimates ICE added roughly 919,908 new DNA profiles to the FBI's Combined DNA Index System in 2025 alone, confirmed by a Wired investigation into internal records. That single-year haul followed a 2020 Justice Department rule that stripped DHS of its exemption from mandatory DNA collection, converting immigration detention into a direct feed for federal forensic databases. DHS is now the largest single source of new genetic profiles in the country's criminal DNA system, with detainee profiles in CODIS topping 3.3 million.

Georgetown identified 492 children under 14 whose DNA reached the FBI between January 2025 and January 2026, including four-, five-, six-, and seven-year-olds, despite DHS policy setting the collection age at 14. Congressional visitors to the Dilley family detention center found families confused about why their children were being tested, with no explanation offered. Researcher Stevie Glaberson described the program as compelled collection of sensitive information on the chance it might someday help solve a crime.

Once entered, a profile stays searchable by law enforcement nationwide against crime-scene evidence indefinitely. Refusing the swab is itself a federal crime, with prosecutions already secured in 2025. Four Americans detained during a protest outside an Illinois ICE facility say their DNA was taken though charges were later dropped. A military veteran swabbed after a raid at his workplace says no one told him what would happen to his genetic material. One person swabbed, US citizen Dana Briggs, put it plainly: her family's biological profile is now government property.

This is the imperial boomerang, imperialism abroad and fascism at home, biometric colonization run through a law-enforcement label. Israel sorts and catalogues Palestinians through the same logic, treating a population as permanent suspects because of Judeo white supremacy. Pissrael's sugar daddy is just following suit with its white supremacy. They even to twin out on crocodile surrounded death camps. What more is it going to take for people to rip these motherfckers out root & stem?

text:
WHEN 200 MILLION PEOPLE WANT TO BREAK YOUR NECK, DO NOT HAND THEM THE ROPE

Letters from Stockholm

By Kio Amachree

The ancient Greeks gave us a word for what we witnessed at the State House on 28 July 2026. The word is hubris. And they gave us a second word for what always, without exception, follows it. That word is nemesis.

Standing before the Catholic Bishops of Nigeria, men of God who came in peace, Bola Ahmed Tinubu chose to boast. Anybody who wants to take the job from me would have to try, he declared. All is fair in politics and war. I will not roll out a red carpet or give anyone a leash to tie around my neck.

Read those words again. Study them. This is not the language of a servant of the people. This is the language of a man who believes the Presidency of Nigeria is his personal property, a trophy to be defended by any means, fair or foul. All is fair, he says. Nigerians should take careful note of that phrase, because a man who tells you that all is fair in politics is telling you in advance what he intends to do to your votes.

The Greeks understood something that this man, in all his years, has never learned. Hubris was not merely arrogance. It was a crime. It was the overstepping of boundaries by mortals who believed themselves beyond accountability, beyond consequence, beyond the reach of justice. And the Greeks taught that nemesis, retribution, follows hubris as surely as night follows day. The temple at Delphi carried two warnings carved in stone: Know thyself. Nothing in excess. The Book of Proverbs says it even more plainly. Pride goes before destruction, and a haughty spirit before a fall.

Every fallen strongman in history believed he was the exception. Every single one. They dismissed their critics, surrounded themselves with flatterers, mistook fear for love and silence for consent. And every single one discovered, always too late, that the people they held in contempt had been keeping accounts all along.

And what, exactly, is the record of this man who now speaks of leashes and red carpets? Let us not deal in insults. Let us deal in documents. The United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois, in 1993, ordered the forfeiture of 460,000 dollars traced to accounts connected to him in a proceeding arising from a federal heroin trafficking investigation. That is not my opinion. That is the public record of the American courts, a record I am pursuing to this day through FOIA litigation before Judge Beryl Howell in Washington. His academic history collapsed under subpoena in Chicago in 2023 in full view of the world. His declared identity, his age, his qualifications, his very biography, dissolve under the mildest scrutiny. This is the man lecturing Catholic bishops about wrestling his opponents to the finishing point. A man whose entire public life is a certificate that cannot be produced and a forfeiture that cannot be explained now demands that 200 million Nigerians accept his intellectual dishonesty as statesmanship.

And under his watch? Hunger in the villages. Massacres in Kaduna. A currency in ruins. Young Nigerians fleeing in their millions through any airport that will have them. Yet the man's chief preoccupation, delivered to bishops who came to speak of the suffering of the flock, is the security of his own tenure.

Here is my counsel to him, offered freely, as one who has watched power rise and fall on four continents. Do not tempt fate. Do not lecture a hungry nation about your grip on power. When 200 million people are aggrieved, when they have buried their children, lost their savings, and watched their patrimony looted before their eyes, the very last thing a wise man does is stand before them and speak of necks and leashes. Because the imagery cuts both ways, sir. When 200 million people want to break your neck, you do not hand them the rope.

Nemesis is patient. She kept her appointment with Abacha. She kept her appointment with Mobutu, with Marcos, with Ceausescu, with every strongman who ever mistook a moment of power for permanence. She has never once missed an appointment in the whole of recorded history.

January 2027 is coming. The Nigerian people are keeping accounts. And no red carpet, no leash, and no boast delivered to bishops will alter the arithmetic of a nation that has finally had enough.

I remain, as always, watching from Stockholm.

Kio Amachree is Founder and President of Worldview International, Stockholm.

text:
Looking back at your political rise, has being gay net-helped you or net-hurt you?

I’m probably too close to it to be somebody who can really say. I know that there were times when I thought it would be the end of my political career, or that I wouldn’t have one at all. And then there were many times when I felt I could walk into a room or walk into the state and have it not matter at all, and obviously what I would like to get to–

At times where it helped too?

I mean, it definitely helped people recognize or care about what I was trying to do in a different way.

It gave you a newness. You were something different, right?

I mean, I was something different in lots of ways, right? I was the mayor from Indiana in his 30s.

And not Indianapolis!

And not in Indianapolis, no, the fourth largest city in Indiana. But, yeah, I’d like to think there are a lot of different dimensions to the newness of what I had to offer. But I think it helped explain … so much of my story then and now is about belonging. And it can sound a little touchy-feely. I actually think the hunger for belonging is a huge part of what drives the Trump-Vance energy too

EXCLUSIVE: Federal Probe Reveals How Hamas Bullies and Coerces Gaza Aid Groups,  Diverts American Aid Dollars to Their War Effort | Adam Kredo, Washington Free Beacon

Hamas officials routinely bullied and intimidated employees of U.S.-funded NGOs operating in Gaza in order to control their operations, according to a confidential probe by American investigators that was obtained by the Washington Free Beacon. The probe reveals that Hamas threatened to sic its fearsome police force on aid workers and even tried to access the NGOs' private employee data as the terror group moved to establish outposts at hospitals and redirect aid to meet its needs.

The June investigatory report by the U.S. Agency for International Development (USAID) inspector general's office, an independent law enforcement entity separate from the largely defunct USAID, provides definitive proof that Hamas is interfering in aid operations and threatening workers on the ground. In one case, Hamas Ministry of Interior personnel "attempted to obtain employee data" from a U.S.-funded NGO and, in another, ordered a humanitarian group "to provide material support to some specific families that they had identified." In the second case, Hamas officials warned that failure to comply with their order would result in "the police" shutting down the group's aid operation.

Hamas's police force is instrumental in repression—maintaining political control and crushing dissent—inside Gaza. The Free Beacon previously reported that the Hamas police installed makeshift torture chambers at Gaza hospitals.

The June 24 report, which was privately transmitted to Congress and obtained exclusively by the Free Beacon, describes a situation on the ground in Gaza that Hamas and its international allies have vehemently denied for years: Aid operations are subject to strict oversight by Hamas personnel who are often stationed at sensitive humanitarian sites, such as hospitals and aid depots. The USAID inspector general obtained clear evidence of "interference by Hamas operating as the de facto authority" during the course of its investigation into the group's activities.

The USAID inspector general, as part of this probe, instructed nine NGOs late last year to produce a list "with the dates and descriptions of attempts by Hamas to interfere with staffing or other operational decisions." It also asked the nonprofits to list all "interactions with Hamas," including with Hamas elements in the Gaza Health Ministry, which Hamas controls. Six of the nonprofits provided all of the information requested, while three made clear that they had not received U.S. funding. By contrast, the United Nations is stonewalling the same investigation into its staffers' ties to Hamas, with at least six U.N. agencies failing to provide the USAID inspector general with identical information about staffing and interactions with Hamas, the Free Beacon first reported on Thursday.

"The USAID inspector general's investigation in Gaza is helping unveil the extent to which Hamas terrorists actively coerced aid organizations to impede, coerce, and divert U.S. taxpayer-funded aid," a senior State Department official briefed on the investigation told the Free Beacon, noting that this is the first federal probe of its nature. "Quite a contrast from the international community's dismissive insistence that Hamas was never, ever, at fault."

Hamas has been repeatedly caught meddling in aid operations and diverting humanitarian supplies to its militant wing. The USAID inspector general, in December 2025, warned "federal agencies, nongovernmental organizations (NGOs), and U.N. agencies of the risk of aid being diverted to Hamas and other U.S.-designated terrorist organizations." The notice included "credible allegations of Hamas interference, diversion, and theft of humanitarian aid in Gaza, as well as allegations of smuggling contraband into Gaza through humanitarian aid shipments." In other documented cases, Hamas operatives infiltrated dozens of U.S. and U.N.-affiliated aid groups in Gaza, embedding personnel into senior positions to direct humanitarian operations on the ground and ensure the groups served Hamas's interests, according to internal security documents published last year by the Free Beacon.

While none of the six NGOs included in the inspector general's most recent June probe—Mercy Corps, International Medical Corps (IMC), Save the Children Federation, Action Against Hunger (AAH), Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development (ACTED), and Project Hope—reported any "involvement with or interference by the militant wing of Hamas," they admitted to being pressured by the group's Gaza government to provide information on their staff and permit potentially Hamas-linked Gazans to patrol their aid sites. There is little distinction between Gaza's Hamas-controlled government and its armed wing, which both work in tandem to enforce a strict police state that includes interference in aid operations. The humanitarian groups themselves are not suspected of any wrongdoing by the inspector general, which was focused primarily on Hamas's activities.

"Concerns about Hamas exploiting humanitarian aid sent to Gaza go far beyond" the U.N. Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA), the terror-tied aid organization that is at the center of the USAID inspector general's investigation, the senior State Department official said. "The 'see no evil, hear no evil' posture in avoiding holding Hamas responsible for widespread theft, diversion, and interference of aid delivery in Gaza must end. The facts speak for themselves, even if inconvenient for some."

IMC, for instance, reported that in January 2024 the Hamas Ministry of Interior asked it to "allocate a dedicated booth or tent so Gazan personnel could always be present at a field hospital in Meraj," a rural area in southern Gaza. Hamas is known to take a particular interest in hospitals and medical facilities, where they station their operatives, maintain underground command centers, and even conduct violent interrogations on Gaza civilians in their torture chamber, the Free Beacon exclusively reported in June.

By August 2024, the Hamas Ministry of Interior instructed IMC "to suspend activities until it received approval" from the Gaza government, a tactic the terror group has repeatedly employed to gain greater leverage over aid groups and intimidate them into compliance. The same month, IMC was told to "register all expatriate medical staff and share license information and professional details for all national healthcare workers" operating in Gaza.

While the Hamas Ministry of Interior ultimately waived this request, it stipulated to IMC that "national medical staff in Gaza were only allowed to work in non-ministry health facilities for up to 24 hours per week," essentially limiting the time Gazan staff could spend outside Hamas-controlled institutions.

Project Hope, meanwhile, reported in January 2025 that "two unarmed individuals" with the Hamas Ministry of Interior credentials "attempted to obtain employee data," but were told by the aid group that this information cannot be shared. The USAID inspector general's report does not say whether Hamas retaliated against Project Hope, but details other instances in which the terror group threatened to shutter aid operations or dispatch its police force for noncompliance.

ACTED—a Paris-based group that has run humanitarian projects in Gaza since at least 2007—reported that on at least two occasions in 2025 "an individual claiming to be part of the [Hamas] 'Ministry of Social Development'" contacted the organization to obtain a copy of its beneficiaries list detailing where aid is delivered.

"The individual also asked ACTED to provide material support to some specific families that they had identified," according to the USAID inspector general report. "In April 2025, the individual again contacted multiple ACTED staff, stating that if the company did not provide the requested information, the police would stop ACTED's ongoing work."

ACTED additionally reported that the Hamas Ministry of Economy requested to "inspect a warehouse containing aid commodities" in November 2025 and, in the same month, stopped two of its employees to demand information about the organization. Hamas organs continued pressuring the group through January 2026, when the Ministry of Interior's Institutional Investigations Unit demanded information about ACTED's Gaza programs.

The encounters disclosed by ACTED and the other Gaza aid groups that spoke to the inspector general paint a vastly different picture of Hamas's activities than those disseminated by the international community, which has repeatedly claimed that Israel is the party responsible for blocking aid to needy Gazans.

The USAID inspector general unearthed evidence in August 2025 that Hamas "commandeered U.N. aid trucks," embedded terrorist operatives in "U.N. agencies or at U.N. facilities," and ensured humanitarian goods were "directly delivered to Hamas officials," the Free Beacon first reported at the time. The Gaza operations manager of the U.S.-funded World Vision charity, Mohammed el Halabi, was convicted by an Israeli court in 2022 of diverting tens of millions of dollars in aid to Hamas's armed wing.

UNRWA, however, claimed as recently as July 2025 that it "received no specific allegations regarding any diversion of humanitarian aid it distributes in the Gaza Strip by Hamas or other armed groups." UNRWA's former commissioner general, Philippe Lazzarini, claimed in a July 2025 X post that there is "no proof of aid diversion in Gaza" and that such claims "were only aimed at tarnishing the reputation of the humanitarian community." A spokesman for the U.N. Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs told Fox News in September 2025, "we do not have evidence of systematic aid diversion from the U.N. to Hamas."

Hamas's own internal security documents offer further proof that the terror group kept close tabs on dozens of NGOs working in Gaza, tracking which officials were friendly to the terror group and who was "affiliated with the Hamas movement." The U.S.-registered Catholic Relief Services, for instance, hired a Gaza director whom Hamas identified as a member of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

The U.N. only acknowledged the problem publicly in July of this year, when its deputy special coordinator for the Middle East peace process, Ramiz Alakbarov, admitted in the face of mounting evidence that the terror group is "targeting and abusing humanitarian operations" in a systematic fashion.

Sen. Chuck Grassley (R., Iowa), who has been tracking the issue as chairman of the powerful Senate Judiciary Committee, told the Free Beacon that while allegations around Hamas's interference with aid operations have been swirling for years, "these newly reported [USAID inspector general] documents prove it."

"Terrorists routinely harassed aid organizations that receive American taxpayer dollars," Grassley said. "The documents raise serious concerns about the United Nations' failure to admit interference from Hamas and even more questions about where American aid is ending up." Congress, the senator added, "should follow up on this new information to ensure taxpayer dollars are not the victim of waste, fraud and abuse."

The senior State Department official who spoke to the Free Beacon reached a similar conclusion, saying that the overwhelming evidence compiled by the USAID inspector general provides proof that "Hamas is not the innocent, angelic bystander that many in the international community would have us believe." Rather, the source said, "the facts in the USAID IG's investigation reveal Hamas' systemic attempts to thwart, divert, and obstruct aid intended for those in need."

Those claims are supported by documents from Hamas's own interior ministry. NGO Monitor, an international watchdog group, published a series of internal Hamas documents showing that the terror group considers hospitals and other civilian sites to be a key node in its terror infrastructure. This comports with evidence produced by Israel showing that hospitals, schools, aid depots, and other civilian strongholds are routinely exploited by Hamas.

A second U.S. official involved with the Board of Peace, a Trump-created international organization established to oversee Gaza's reconstruction, said it is abundantly clear that "NGOs operating in Gaza have been exploited as instruments of the Hamas terrorist organization" and that "some of them have even been complicit and let this happen."

"The Board of Peace will not tolerate this model of service delivery under its mandate," the official added. "The people of Gaza deserve humanitarian assistance that is transparent, accountable, and free from terrorist influence. We must, and will, do better for them."

A State Department spokesman told the Free Beacon that it wholly rejects "Hamas's shameful use of civilian organizations to generate illicit financial support for its military wing." The spokesman said that every U.S. dollar is "subject to various oversight measures including counterterrorism vetting, monitoring, and oversight procedures to prevent" diversion to Hamas and other terror groups.

text:
The Persistent Folly of Government-Run Grocery Stores

The idea of government-run grocery stores keeps resurfacing whenever food prices rise or “food deserts” make headlines. Politicians promise lower prices, better access, and an end to corporate “greed.” It sounds compassionate. In practice, it is one of the more reliably stupid ideas in public policy—repeatedly tested, repeatedly failing for the same fundamental reasons.

The Core Problem: Incentives and Knowledge

Private grocery retailers operate on razor-thin margins, typically 1–3 percent (sometimes as low as 1–2 percent after all costs). Success depends on relentless efficiency: precise inventory management, sophisticated logistics, supplier negotiations based on volume, responsive pricing, and ruthless cost control. Profit-and-loss accounting provides continuous feedback. Stores that waste money, stock the wrong items, or ignore customer preferences shrink or close. Those that serve people well expand.

Government ownership removes that feedback loop. Managers answer to politicians and bureaucracies rather than customers and investors. There is no residual claimant who personally benefits from efficiency or suffers from losses. Losses are socialized onto taxpayers. Political priorities—union contracts, local hiring quotas, favored suppliers, or “equity” metrics—crowd out operational competence. Without market prices and residual ownership, rational economic calculation becomes far harder. This is the classic knowledge and incentive problem that has plagued state enterprises for generations.

History Is Not Kind

Large-scale experiments are unambiguous. Soviet-era stores were legendary for empty shelves, long lines, and chronic shortages of basic goods even as the regime claimed abundance. Venezuela’s Mercal network under Chávez offered heavily subsidized prices that looked great on television—until shelves emptied, black markets flourished, corruption in procurement exploded, and the system required ever-larger subsidies while delivering less reliable supply. Mexico’s long-running state grocery chain has been plagued by losses, disrepair, and corruption for decades without solving affordability.

Smaller U.S. experiments follow the same pattern. Erie, Kansas took over its local store and promptly lost money almost every month (only one profitable month in 2022, with annual losses in the six figures). Baldwin, Florida’s city-run market ran consistent operating deficits and closed in 2024. Kansas City’s Sun Fresh, after millions in public funds, became known for sparse shelves, odors, and heavy losses before its decline. Multiple stores funded through federal Healthy Food Financing or state programs never opened, closed quickly, or required ongoing subsidies. Rare “successes” are usually tiny rural operations in places with no competition, heavy ongoing support, or effectively privatized management.

Military commissaries are the main counter-example often cited. They deliver real discounts, but they serve a captive, defined population, receive large direct appropriations, operate with institutional logistics support, and are not expected to compete in open commercial markets. Scaling that model to ordinary civilian neighborhoods is not the same thing.

Why “Just Sell Cheaper” Doesn’t Work

Proponents claim government stores can forgo profit and taxes to cut prices 20–30 percent. Grocery margins are already so thin that eliminating the profit slice buys only a couple of percentage points at best. Achieving large discounts requires either massive ongoing subsidies (taxpayers covering the gap) or cutting corners on quality, variety, labor, or maintenance. Subsidized low prices create excess demand, leading to shortages, rationing, or secondary markets—exactly what happened with Mercal. Centralized procurement often proves less agile than private chains that move billions of dollars of product weekly.

text:
At thirteen years old, Misty Copeland was sleeping on the floor of a motel room she shared with her mother and five siblings.

No one looking at her life then would have imagined she was destined to make history.

Born on September 10, 1982, in Kansas City, Missouri, Misty's childhood was marked by instability from the very beginning. Her father left when she was only two years old, leaving her mother, Sylvia, to raise six children on her own. 

The family moved constantly, searching for affordable places to live. Home could be a motel one month, a cramped apartment the next, or a borrowed room with relatives or friends. Money was always scarce. Meals were never guaranteed. Privacy simply didn't exist.

As if poverty wasn't enough, one of her mother's relationships became abusive, exposing the children to fear and violence that no child should ever have to experience.

By the time Misty was thirteen, the family was living in a single room at the Sunset Inn in San Pedro, California.

Six children.

One room.

Misty slept on the floor, never knowing how long they would stay before having to move again.

School became the one place where she could breathe.

While attending San Pedro High School, she joined the school's drill team. Her coach quickly noticed something unusual. Misty moved with incredible balance, grace, and natural control.

"You should try ballet," the coach suggested.

The idea seemed impossible.

Misty had never taken a ballet class. She didn't own ballet slippers. Ballet belonged to another world, one filled with expensive lessons, elegant studios, and girls whose lives looked nothing like hers.

Still, she decided to attend a free class at a local Boys & Girls Club.

She borrowed a pair of ballet shoes.

She stepped up to the barre.

And almost immediately, everyone could see she had extraordinary talent.

Within months, her instructors realized they were witnessing something incredibly rare.

Most professional dancers begin training before they are six years old.

Misty was already thirteen.

Yet her natural ability rivaled students who had spent years in the studio.

One of her teachers offered to train her for free.

But there was another challenge.

Her unstable home life made serious training nearly impossible. Constant moves, overcrowded living conditions, and emotional stress threatened to derail her progress before it had truly begun.

So her teacher's family made an extraordinary offer.

They invited Misty to live with them.

For the first time in her life, she had her own bedroom.

She had regular meals.

She had stability.

Most importantly, she finally had the chance to focus completely on dancing.

She trained for hours every day, pushing her body to catch up with dancers who had started years earlier.

Her progress was astonishing.

Within just two years, she was winning competitions and performing at a level that few believed possible.

But as her talent grew, so did the obstacles.

She was repeatedly told that her body wasn't right for ballet.

She was considered too muscular.

Too curvy.

Too different from the traditional image of a ballerina.

Behind many of those criticisms was an unspoken reality.

She was also Black in an art form where very few dancers looked like her.

During this period, a painful custody dispute erupted between her mother and the family she was living with.

Eventually, Misty returned home, once again leaving behind the stability she had finally found.

Even so, her talent could no longer be ignored.

She earned scholarships, won prestigious competitions, and at eighteen joined the American Ballet Theatre in New York, one of the world's most respected ballet companies.

She was one of the few Black dancers in the company.

The criticism didn't disappear.

People continued to question her body, her background, and the fact that she had started dancing so late.

Misty refused to let any of it define her.

She kept training.

She kept performing.

She kept proving people wrong.

In 2007, she was promoted to soloist.

Then, in 2015, she made history.

At 32 years old, Misty Copeland became the first Black female principal dancer in the 75-year history of the American Ballet Theatre.

It was a milestone that reached far beyond ballet.

She wasn't simply achieving a personal dream.

She was opening a door that had remained closed for generations.

Misty continued breaking barriers throughout her career.

She became the first Black woman to perform the lead role in Swan Lake for the company.

She spoke openly about discrimination, unrealistic beauty standards, and the lack of diversity in classical ballet.

Instead of hiding what made her different, she embraced it.

Her strength became her signature.

Her story became her message.

She also dedicated herself to inspiring the next generation by writing books, mentoring young dancers, and creating opportunities for children from backgrounds like her own.

Reflecting on her journey, she once said,

"I didn't see anyone who looked like me in ballet. I want to be the person I needed when I was young."

From sleeping on a motel floor to standing on one of the world's greatest stages, Misty Copeland's journey is a reminder that talent can emerge from the most unlikely places.

She was told she started too late.

She was told she had the wrong body.

She was told she didn't fit the image of a ballerina.

She proved every one of those voices wrong.

More importantly, she changed what the world believed a ballerina could look like.

The little girl who once wondered where her family would sleep each night grew into the woman who inspired countless others to believe they belonged, too.

Sometimes changing your own life changes an entire generation.

Misty Copeland did both.

text:
Zohran Mamdani is launching five government-run grocery stores in NYC with 30% discounts on essentials funded by $70 million of taxpayer money.

Sounds wonderful. Cheap food for areas that need it. 

Who could object?Anyone who understands the economics, history and game theory.

 Here’s why kind-sounding ideas can be dangerous ideas:

1. It’s a marketing campaign, not a food policy. Five stores won’t feed a city of 8.5 million. They exist to produce a spectacle - a photo of Mamdani holding a loaf of cheap bread and a grin that says “see socialism works.” The stores are the ad but the the product he’s selling is collectivism and more state control… which doesn’t work. 

2. The maths is predatory. Grocers run on 1–3% margins. Mamdani is discounting 30% … over ten times the entire profit margin of potential competitors. Tax payers fund rent, property tax and supply and offer no penalty for a business that’s losing money. That kills any hope of competition that would naturally transform demand and supply dynamics for real. 

3. It corrupts price signals and creates an arbitrage economy. Prices are data. They tell farmers what to grow, distributors what to ship, entrepreneurs where to invest. Subsidise the price and you corrupt the data ... and create a guaranteed profit for anyone with a shopping trolley. People will stockpile non-perishables, clear the shelves, and resell at market price, pocketing the taxpayer subsidy as personal margin. Venezuela ran this exact experiment: price-controlled stores bred a professional class of resellers, and the subsidised goods ended up on the black market anyway. The discount doesn’t reach the needy. It reaches the fastest to grab and resell the stock. 

4. It’s proven to fail at scale. Kansas City tried a municipal grocery store and it burned through millions and ended in empty shelves. The Soviet Union tried it with an entire nation. In 1989, Boris Yeltsin visited an ordinary supermarket in Texas and was so staggered by the abundance available to regular working people that he later admitted it shattered his faith in the Soviet system. A random capitalist grocery store did more to end communism than any weapon ever built. The well sticked grocery-store is a miracle of capitalism not state control. 

5. There’s no feedback loop. When a private store fails, it closes. When a government store fails, it gets a bigger budget. A failure becomes the argument for more funding. Losses don’t kill a failed experiment in a state run program… They feed bigger budgets. Watch and be prepared to see the $70m budget become $100m in no time.

And the punchline: New York just published a tender asking private operators to actually run these stores. Even the socialist experiment needs capitalists to work the tills. The actual profits will go to government contractors- watch as Accenture suddenly becomes a leading grocery story Labour hire company. 

Markets aren’t the enemy of ordinary people. They’re the greatest anti-poverty machine ever discovered. Break the machine and everyone eats worse - especially the people you promised to help.

The only problem is that by the time it proves to be anothet failed socialist initiative there will have been millions of Tik Tok views of Mamdani pretending it works and spreading socialist propaganda to young people who are weaponised against their own interests.

JUDGE: SHORT-BARRELED RIFLE, SUPPRESSOR NFA REGISTRATION SCHEME UNCONSTITUTIONAL

BELLEVUE, Wash. — Aug. 5, 2026 — A judge for the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas has ruled that the remaining registration scheme for short-barreled rifles and suppressors in the National Firearms Act (NFA) is unconstitutional in Jensen v. ATF, a case supported by the Second Amendment Foundation (SAF).

Since 1934, the NFA required anyone who wished to purchase certain classes of firearms, including silencers and short-barreled rifles, to pay a $200 tax and register the firearm with the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), purportedly drawing from Congressional authority to levy taxes. Through the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill, however, the tax on these arms was eliminated but the registration requirement was left in place. SAF and its partners have filed three lawsuits challenging the remaining registration requirements, because without the tax, Congress’ reliance on their taxing power is no longer justifiable.

“The basis for each lawsuit challenging the NFA registration scheme is the same – without the tax, the remaining requirements for the affected arms under the NFA have no constitutional basis,” said SAF Executive Director Adam Kraut. “And today the first court to rule on the issue has agreed with us. We’re eager to continue this fight and leave major portions of the NFA in the dustbin of history. A big win is a great way to kick things off.”

SAF itself is a named plaintiff in NFA lawsuit Brown v. ATF and is backing two additional challenges – Roberts v. ATF and this case, Jensen v. ATF. Plaintiffs in Jensen are SAF sister organization – Citizens Committee for the Right to Keep and Bear Arms, FPC Action Foundation, Texas Rifle Association, Hot Shots Custom and three individuals.

“The removal of the $200 tax in the One Big Beautiful Bill offers the best opportunity to remove the NFA registration requirements that we’ve had in almost a century,” said SAF founder and Executive Vice President Alan M. Gottlieb. “We are thrilled the court ruled in our favor and look forward to other jurisdictions following suit in our remaining NFA cases. This ruling will set a precedent we can now argue in courts across the country to allow Americans to exercise their Second Amendment rights without fear of being placed on some government registry.”

For more information visit https://t.co/cRbddY8WzX.

The Second Amendment Foundation (https://t.co/ZXluFDjbJV) is the nation’s oldest and largest tax-exempt education, research, publishing and legal action group dedicated to safeguarding and promoting the fundamental rights of individuals enshrined in the Second Amendment of the United States Constitution. SAF engages in aggressive legal action to ensure the principles of armed self-defense, personal liberty, and the ownership of arms are defended, secured, and restored. Through public education initiatives, SAF teaches the importance of the Second Amendment to promote a society that values and exercises the right to keep and bear arms.

text:
Bail: A Constitutional Right, Not an Automatic Entitlement

Donda Attorneys Inc 
Servant Leaders for Justice

One of the most misunderstood areas of our criminal justice system is bail. Many people believe that being arrested automatically means being denied freedom until trial, while others believe bail is a right that must always be granted. Neither view is correct. Bail sits at the intersection of two constitutional values that our law must carefully balance: the presumption of innocence and personal freedom on the one hand, and the interests of justice and public safety on the other.

The Constitutional Basis

Section 35(1)(f) of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 provides that everyone who is arrested for allegedly committing an offence has the right "to be released from detention if the interests of justice permit, subject to reasonable conditions." This is a foundational right, but it is not unqualified — the right is to have release considered fairly against the interests of justice, not to unconditional release.

The Constitutional Court has affirmed that this framework balances an accused person's right to liberty against society's interest in the proper administration of justice. Bail is best understood as a constitutionally guaranteed process, not a guaranteed outcome.

Where the Criminal Procedure Act Comes In
The Criminal Procedure Act 51 of 1977 (sections 60 and 61) gives practical effect to section 35(1)(f), setting out how applications are brought and, for serious offences, where the burden shifts from the State to the accused.

Schedule 1, 5 and 6 Offences

Schedule 1 (e.g. common assault, minor theft) — bail is usually a formality.

Schedule 5 (e.g. culpable homicide, robbery with aggravating circumstances) — accused must show the interests of justice permit release.

Schedule 6 (e.g. premeditated murder, gang rape, organised firearm offences) — accused must show exceptional circumstances, a significantly higher threshold.

What the Court Actually Weighs (s60(4))

-Flight risk (ties to community, travel documents, employment)
-Risk of interfering with witnesses or evidence
-Risk of committing further offences on bail
-Risk to public order / confidence in the justice system
-Personal circumstances and preliminary strength of the State's case

A bail hearing is not a trial — the court assesses risk, not guilt.

Conditions of Release

Commonly: reporting to a police station, surrendering a passport, no contact with witnesses/complainant, staying within a defined jurisdiction, curfews. Breach can mean forfeiture and re-arrest.

Why This Matters for You

The schedule a charge falls under shapes strategy from day one — what evidence to lead, what undertakings to offer, and how quickly to act. At Donda Attorneys Inc., our criminal law practice regularly handles first appearances and contested bail applications across Schedule 1, 5, and 6 matters.

text:
Fascinating treatment of the law's division, touching on both the "dead" and "deadly" distinction of the ceremonial law, as well as the general equity of the political/civil law of Israel, concluded by a standard treatment of the natural/moral law in the Reformed tradition: 

XIII. As the Law is divided in various ways, it is chiefly described as either positive, which flows solely from the most wise will of God and lasts only for a time; or natural, which, flowing from the nature of God or man, holds always and equally for all. 

XIV. God gave a positive law concerning the fruit of the tree of knowledge before the fall; and after the fall, he gave not a few, both under the Old and under the New Testament. For the commands of baptism and of the Supper belong here, which, having been given in the church, last to the end. Also, the prohibition of blood and of things strangled, which pertains only to the beginnings of the New Testament, Acts 15:20, 29, 'that ye abstain from meats offered to idols, and from blood, and from things strangled, and from fornication'—namely, that for a time, until Christian liberty was fully demonstrated, relief might be given in a small matter to the weakness of certain brethren. For elsewhere it is taught that under the New Testament all distinction of foods has been abolished, 1 Corinthians 8:8, 'meat commendeth us not to God'; 1 Corinthians 10:25– 26, 'whatsoever is sold in the shambles, that eat, asking no question for conscience sake'; Colossians 2:16, 21, 'Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, … Why are you submitting to decrees: ‘Touch not; taste not; handle not.'

XV. Under the Old Testament, there was chiefly a twofold positive law, the forensic and the ceremonial. The former, which is also called the political law, is that according to which the commonwealth of Israel was to be administered by the command of God in times of peace and of war. It contains statutes concerning magistracy, marriages, servants, inheritances, etc., and the penalties to be inflicted upon transgressors even of the moral law. This law is distinct from the moral law, yet not opposed to it, except perhaps in certain exceptions from the common law. It is in many respects implicit in both the moral and the ceremonial law. Its chief end was the good order of the commonwealth. Nor does it continue today except in its common and moral foundations, since in other respects it was accommodated to that time, that people, and that land.

XXII. The moral law, which is also called the Decalogue and the natural law, is: that which, written on the heart of man in his integrity and in part still remaining after the fall, and afterwards comprehended summarily by Moses in the Decalogue, constitutes the most holy, immutable, most perfect, and perpetual rule of all conduct of soul and body. 

XXIII. This law was written on the heart of man at the first creation, as the image of God given to him teaches, and the remnants after the fall show, Romans 2:14–15, “For when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law, these, having not the law, are a law unto themselves: which shew the work of the law written in their hearts.” Also to this end, that man might then attain to eternal life through the keeping of the law, Romans 8:3, “what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh."

XXIV. Remnants of the inscribed law are naturally still in man, Romans 1:19–20, “because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them … through the things that are made”; Romans 2:14–15, “for when the Gentiles, which have not the law, do by nature the things contained in the law”; Ephesians 5:29, “for no man ever yet hated his own flesh.” Hence flows the law of nature and the original law of nations, which the libertines in vain trace back entirely to tradition or to human arbitrariness. Although conscience, in many of its acts, can often be suffocated by the habit of sinning, and God often gives men over to a reprobate mind by supernatural judgment, Ephesians 4:19, “who being past feeling have given themselves over unto lasciviousness, to work all uncleanness with greediness.” The Jews call these common rights the precepts of the Noachides, though they do not establish them well at seven. The end of this natural law, moreover, is the external restraint of men and their greater ἀναπολογησία [inexcusableness].

text:
DID YOU KNOW??

Copenhagen is pioneering a revolutionary concept in urban green space called a "Parkipelago", a collection of roaming, artificial floating islands that move around the city's harbor.

​Designed by Australian architect Marshall Blecher and Danish design studio Fokstrot (Studio Fokstrot), these mobile wooden islands are free for anyone to use for kayaking, stargazing, swimming, picnics, and fishing. Walk with me 👇🏾👇🏾 

1. How Copenhagen's Floating Islands Work:
​The project, officially named Copenhagen Islands, started with a single 215-square-foot prototype island named CPH-Ø1 (from Ø, the Danish word for "island").

A. ​Natural & Recycled Construction: Built by hand in Copenhagen's boatbuilding yards using traditional techniques, the platforms are clad in sustainably sourced timber and buoyed by recycled plastic bottles.

B. ​Growing Real Trees: The prototype features a full-sized linden tree growing directly at its center, with root systems contained in a submerged tank beneath the wooden decking.

C. ​Seasonal Migration: During the summer, the islands drift separately to encourage urban water exploration. During winter or large festivals, they can be latched together to create a floating "supercontinent" for markets, concerts, and lectures.

2. Ecology Above and Below the Waterline:
​Far from just being pretty platforms for humans, the floating parks double as dual-environment ecosystems:

A. ​Above Water: Planted with endemic grasses, bushes, and trees, the islands offer isolated urban sanctuaries for local seabirds, ducks, swans, and pollinators away from city noise.  

C. ​Below Water: The submerged undersides serve as artificial reefs, providing anchor surfaces for seaweed, mussels, and barnacles, which in turn attract native fish and marine life. 

​SUMMARILY! 
​As sea levels rise and urban waterfronts gentrify, Copenhagen’s floating "parkipelago" presents a flexible, climate-resilient vision for public parks, proving that a city's green spaces don't have to be rooted on solid ground to thrive. That Sci fi future is looking closer than ever it seems? 😅

Hopefully you've learnt something new today?

text:
MAKING EUROPE GREAT AGAIN: European values dilemma 

I. THE PHILOSOPHICAL PROBLEM

Europe's crisis is not primarily economic or military but firstly a crisis of foundational confidence. Post-1945 European identity was built on renunciation: renunciation of nationalism, of military power projection, of civilizational self-assertion. This was a rational response to catastrophe. It also left Europe without a positive account of what it stands for, only a negative account of what it refuses to repeat.

A civilization organized around avoiding its past cannot generate the confidence required to shape its future. This is the philosophical starting point: Europe needs a positive telos, not just a set of prohibitions.

Three intellectual traditions offer competing answers, and any honest account of European renewal has to engage all three rather than pick one and pretend the others don't exist.

II. THREE COMPETING VISIONS

Liberal universalism (Kant, Habermas): Europe's purpose is to model post-national governance — rules-based order, human rights, supranational institutions — as a template the rest of the world eventually adopts. The EU itself is the philosophical project made concrete. Strength comes from moral and institutional authority, not military power.

Civilizational particularism (Herder onward, echoed in later conservative thought): Europe's purpose is to preserve and renew distinct national and cultural traditions — language, history, religious inheritance, local self-government. Strength comes from rooted identity, not abstraction. This view treats the liberal universalist project as identity-erasing.

Republican realism (Machiavelli, de Gaulle's tradition, and contemporary "strategic autonomy" thinkers): Europe's purpose is sovereign capacity — the ability to act, defend itself, and set its own terms rather than depend on the US security umbrella or foreign supply chains. Strength comes from hard power and self-sufficiency, not persuasion or purity.

These are not fully compatible. A serious "make Europe great again" argument has to state which of these does the load-bearing work, because they point to different institutions, different budgets, and different foreign policies.

III. THE PRACTICAL TRANSLATION

Whichever philosophical frame is chosen, several problems are frame-independent and have to be solved regardless:

Demographics: Europe's median age is rising and birth rates sit well below replacement across most member states. No cultural renewal survives population collapse. This forces a choice between family policy investment, immigration, or managed decline and evasion of the choice is itself a choice.

Energy and industrial base: European manufacturing competitiveness has eroded relative to the US and China, worsened by post-2022 energy costs. Sovereignty claims are hollow without industrial capacity behind them.

Defense capacity: Reliance on US security guarantees is incompatible with claims of strategic autonomy. This is a budget line and a procurement policy.

Institutional coherence: 27 states with veto rights cannot execute a unified civilizational project at the speed the 21st century requires. Either integration deepens in specific domains (defense, energy, capital markets) or "Europe" remains an aspiration rather than an actor.

IV. THE HONEST CONCLUSION

There is no philosophy-first shortcut. A civilization recovers confidence by acting successfully, not by first resolving its metaphysics and then acting. The Marshall Plan-era recovery, the founding of the Coal and Steel Community, the Single Market for example did not wait  for philosophical consensus. They were concrete, narrow, achievable commitments that generated confidence as a byproduct of success.

The realistic path is to pick a small number of concrete domains like energy grid integration, joint defense procurement, capital markets union and execute them competently, and let the civilizational narrative follow the results

text:
Lindsay Clancy Trial- Day 7

Before the next witness testified the Commonwealth advised the court that the parties had agreed to admit a demonstrative chart identifying both the generic and brand names of several medications that had been discussed throughout the trial. The chart was intended solely to assist the jury in following the testimony regarding the various medications.

The Commonwealth then called Dr. Justin Brower a forensic toxicologist with NMS Laboratories in Pennsylvania. Dr. Brower testified that NMS is a nationally accredited reference laboratory that receives forensic clinical and postmortem toxicology cases from all 50 states. He holds a PhD in organic chemistry and previously served as a laboratory supervisor and forensic toxicologist for the North Carolina Office of the Chief Medical Examiner before joining NMS Laboratories.

Dr. Brower explained that his role was not to perform the initial testing but to conduct the final review of every aspect of a case including the raw analytical data the reported drug concentrations and the overall accuracy of the toxicology report. He testified that NMS received a blood sample in April 2023 and was specifically asked to quantify four medications that the Massachusetts State Police Crime Laboratory could not quantify.

Those medications were lamotrigine also known as Lamictal mirtazapine also known as Remeron quetiapine also known as Seroquel and trazodone. Dr. Brower testified that lamotrigine is commonly prescribed for seizure disorders and bipolar disorder mirtazapine and trazodone are antidepressants and quetiapine is an antipsychotic that is also frequently prescribed in lower doses for insomnia.

He testified that lamotrigine mirtazapine and trazodone were all within therapeutic concentrations. He stated that quetiapine appeared only slightly elevated but was not at a level he would consider toxic or consistent with an intentional overdose. He explained that in overdose deaths involving quetiapine he would typically expect concentrations much closer to 10000 nanograms per milliliter whereas Lindsay’s measured approximately 1800 nanograms per milliliter.

The Commonwealth also questioned Dr. Brower regarding the previously identified benzodiazepines. He testified that diazepam commonly known as Valium along with its metabolites nordiazepam oxazepam and temazepam appeared to be at therapeutic or even subtherapeutic concentrations. He explained that lorazepam also appeared to fall within or slightly below the therapeutic range.

Throughout his testimony Dr. Brower repeatedly emphasized the limitations of toxicology. He explained that numbers on a laboratory report cannot by themselves determine how a specific person was affected by medications. Toxicology must be interpreted alongside the person’s medical history the surrounding circumstances clinical findings and other investigative information. He testified that he was provided none of that information and knew nothing about the facts of this case when he reviewed the blood sample.

The Commonwealth also asked whether the combination of these medications could reduce a person’s breathing. Dr. Brower testified that several of the medications are central nervous system depressants and in sufficiently high concentrations or combinations could suppress respiration. However based solely on the concentrations observed in this case he was not willing to offer an opinion that the medications caused someone to stop breathing. He testified that additional clinical information would be necessary before reaching such a conclusion.

Finally Dr. Brower explained that Narcan would have no effect on any of the medications identified because Narcan only reverses opioid overdoses and none of the medications detected act on opioid receptors.

text:
Saw this on a FB WI page. 

FYI. 

Wisconsin's Friday fish fry traces back to Catholic canon law dating to 1249, when the church forbade eating meat on Fridays as a way of commemorating Jesus's crucifixion. That religious practice traveled to Wisconsin directly with waves of German and Polish Catholic immigrants who settled the state through the 1800s, and it found unusually fertile ground here for a simple practical reason: Wisconsin's abundance of freshwater lakes, rivers, and Great Lakes shoreline made fish genuinely cheap and plentiful, an easy, affordable substitute for meat that most other regions couldn't offer as readily.

By the mid-19th century, Milwaukee's Jones Island neighborhood had become a real center of freshwater commercial fishing on Lake Michigan, and fish had already worked its way into the city's regular lunch rotation well before it became a formal Friday-night institution. What actually turned it into a statewide social ritual, though, wasn't religion alone. It was Prohibition. When alcohol sales became illegal from 1920 to 1933, Wisconsin taverns needed some other way to keep customers walking through the door, and serving cheap fried fish dinners became the workaround. Some establishments reportedly offered fish free with the purchase of a beer, served discreetly enough to skirt the law, blending the Catholic tradition with Wisconsin's deep German brewing culture into a single Friday night ritual.

The tradition kept evolving well past Prohibition's end. Post-World War II meat rationing gave fish another practical boost, and by the 1950s and 60s, Wisconsin's iconic supper clubs had begun offering all-you-can-eat and family-style fish fries, pulling the tradition out of strictly Catholic households and into a genuine statewide staple enjoyed regardless of religious background. Even after the Catholic Church loosened its rules in 1966, limiting the meatless requirement to Fridays during Lent alone, Wisconsin's habit of "going out for fish" on Friday nights had already become too ingrained to fade with the rule change.

Today the tradition runs through polka halls, church basements, VFW posts, and rooftop restaurants overlooking Lake Superior alike, with regulars debating fiercely over cod versus perch versus walleye, beer batter versus breading, and whether the sides, coleslaw, rye bread, tartar sauce, potato pancakes, measure up. Parishes like St. Sebastian in Milwaukee still run some of the largest fish fries in the state entirely on volunteer labor, treating it less as a fundraiser and more as an actual community homecoming. Nearly 175 years removed from the medieval church law that started it, and a full century removed from the Prohibition-era tavern owners who turned it into a business strategy, the Wisconsin Friday fish fry remains exactly what it became somewhere along the way: less a religious obligation than a genuine, deeply local weekly ritual nobody needs a reason to keep showing up for.
