text:
The Red-Green Alliance Is Real, and Israel Is Only Its First Target

The Muslim Brotherhood has partnered with the Democratic Socialists of America. This is a fact.

For years, anyone who pointed to the growing convergence between the Muslim Brotherhood's American affiliates and the Democratic Socialists of America was accused of paranoia. That accusation is becoming harder to sustain. The evidence, organizational, financial, and electoral, now points to a working alliance between Islamist advocacy networks and America's fastest-growing socialist movement, built on a shared and explicit hostility toward Israel and the democratic Western order that supports it.

Israel may be the alliance's most visible target, but it is not its only target. Both movements reject central foundations of Western democracy, including national sovereignty, liberal pluralism, traditional institutions, and the legitimacy of the existing constitutional order. Their ideologies are different, but their immediate political objective is increasingly the same: weaken the institutions, values, and alliances that sustain the democratic West.

Two Movements, One Enemy

The Muslim Brotherhood's founding project was never secretive about its goals: the establishment of Islamic governance and the destruction of the Jewish state, which its founder, Hassan al-Banna, and his successors have framed as both a religious and civilizational obligation. The Democratic Socialists of America, for its part, has made anti-Zionism a formal plank of its platform, with chapters nationwide endorsing boycotts, divestment resolutions, and rhetoric that treats Israel's very existence as the root injustice in the Middle East. When two movements independently arrive at the same enemy, cooperation is not a conspiracy theory. It is a strategy.

But Israel is only the point where their hostility is most clearly aligned. The deeper target is the Western democratic system Israel represents and depends upon: constitutional government, free societies, national self-determination, religious pluralism, and a strategic alliance led by the United States. Israel is attacked not only as a Jewish state, but also as a frontline member of the democratic West.

That strategy has a name among researchers who track it: the Red-Green Alliance, a term first used to describe the fusion of radical leftists, the "Reds," and Islamists, the "Greens," in Britain, where secular socialists in the Stop the War Coalition partnered openly with the Muslim Association of Britain, an organization with documented Brotherhood lineage, to build the Respect Party. The American version of this alliance has matured quickly, and it is no longer confined to protest coalitions. It now runs through fundraising, formal caucuses, and electoral machinery.

Following the Money and the Organizing

The infrastructure is visible to anyone willing to look. DSA formally organized a Muslim Caucus in 2021 to fuse Islamist-adjacent organizing directly into the socialist apparatus. The Council on American-Islamic Relations, an organization named as an unindicted co-conspirator in the largest terrorism-financing prosecution in American history, has directed political action committee money toward democratic socialist candidates, most notably New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose winning coalition drew explicitly on both DSA's organizing muscle and the Muslim American Society, a group researchers have long linked to the Brotherhood's ideological network in the United States.

This is not incidental overlap. A recent report on Mamdani's rise describes his coalition as a "strategic convergence" between socialist and Islamist organizing networks, echoing the same red-green pattern that reshaped British politics two decades ago. Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed offers another data point: his campaign's super PAC has drawn its largest single contribution, $300,000, from his own father-in-law, a founding committee member of the Islamic Society of North America, another organization named in the Holy Land Foundation terror-financing case. El-Sayed's direct campaign has separately collected more than $115,000 from CAIR-affiliated donors, including an official who publicly praised Hamas after October 7.

Shared Rallies, Shared Language

The clearest evidence of the alliance is not financial. It is rhetorical. Since October 7, DSA chapters and Islamist advocacy groups have appeared side by side at the same rallies, used the same slogans, and issued the same condemnations of Israel's right to defend itself. DSA's national leadership formally censured its own congressional endorsees for insufficient hostility toward Israel, while CAIR chapters organized turnout for the same demonstrations. This is coordination in practice, whatever language either side uses to describe itself.

The shared rhetoric also extends beyond Israel. Western institutions are routinely described as colonial, oppressive, illegitimate, or structurally corrupt. Police, borders, national identity, religious traditions, capitalism, and the constitutional system itself are presented not as institutions to reform, but as structures to dismantle. Israel serves as the central rallying point because it allows both sides to unite around a common enemy while advancing a much broader attack on Western legitimacy.

Defenders of this alliance insist that it is simply "coalition politics," with two groups that have overlapping short-term interests joining forces on specific issues. That framing understates what is happening. Coalition politics does not typically involve one partner's largest donors sitting on the founding committees of organizations tied by federal courts to Hamas financing, nor does it typically produce joint electoral machines that install allied officials in the nation's largest city.

Israel Is the Front Line, Not the Final Target

The fixation on Israel can obscure the larger ideological struggle. Israel is targeted first because it is a Jewish, democratic, Western-aligned nation surrounded by hostile movements that reject its legitimacy. But the same political forces also challenge the legitimacy of the United States, Europe, and the broader democratic order.

The Red-Green Alliance does not require socialists and Islamists to agree on religion, economics, personal freedom, or the future structure of society. It requires only that they cooperate against the institutions they both seek to weaken. Their long-term visions may be incompatible, but their short-term enemies are the same: Israel, American power, Western national identity, and liberal democracy itself.

Why This Should Alarm Supporters of Western Democracy

The danger of the Red-Green Alliance is not abstract. It represents the mainstreaming of anti-Zionist and, in some cases, Islamist-sympathetic politics within the activist base of one of America's two major political parties. As DSA-backed candidates win primaries and general elections with Islamist organizational support behind them, the political cost of supporting Israel within the Democratic coalition rises accordingly. What began as an unlikely pairing between secular Marxists and religious Islamists has become a durable electoral bloc, and its foreign-policy consensus is unmistakably hostile to the Jewish state.

But the threat does not end with foreign policy. As this alliance gains influence, hostility toward Israel becomes a gateway to hostility toward the broader Western system. Democratic institutions are weakened, extremist rhetoric is normalized, and movements fundamentally opposed to Western values gain greater access to political power.

Supporters of Israel and Western democracy who dismiss this convergence as coincidence are ignoring the money trail, the organizational overlap, and the shared enemies that bind these movements together. Israel is the immediate target, but the larger struggle is over the future of the democratic West. The alliance is not hidden. It is simply, for now, underestimated.

text:
Senators demand crackdown on wildfire "prediction markets" | Cyrus Farivar, Policy - Ars Technica

Several US senators have written a letter to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC), inquiring about the agency’s “plans to crack down on prediction markets” that offer “contracts for individuals to bet on wildfires.”

“Offering bets on destructive wildfires threatens to minimize communities’ suffering, all so the rich and powerful can profit,” wrote the group of senators, who represent Oregon, California, Nevada, Minnesota, and New Hampshire.

The document specifically cites that Polymarket hosted bets in January 2025 on the wildfires in Los Angeles, and it mentions another website which specifically accepts “simulated bets” exclusively on California wildfires.

“There’s also the heightened risk—according to state and local fire officials—that individuals could be tempted to commit arson in order to make sure their bets are successful,” the letter continues. “By offering contracts on fires, prediction market sites run the risk of encouraging people to influence fires that have already started, creating additional concerns around public safety and insider trading.”

The public letter, which was issued Monday, comes as active wildfires continue to burn in significant parts of the Pacific Northwest. On Tuesday, the Spokane County Sheriff’s Office announced the arrest of an arson suspect who is believed to have started one of the blazes currently threatening Spokane, Washington, and the surrounding area. Several hundred buildings have already been destroyed, and approximately one quarter of the city’s population has recently been ordered to evacuate.

The CFTC did not immediately respond to Ars’ request for comment.

Kalshi is one of the major prediction markets. Kalshi spokesperson Elisabeth Diana told Ars by email that the company does not allow such wildfire markets “because they create perverse incentives.”

But its primary rival, Polymarket, has taken a different approach. A spokesperson for Polymarket told Ars in an emailed statement that the company does not “profit from outcomes,” adding that people “come to Polymarket for information.”

“While we are not blind to the risks, removing these markets does not prevent a tragedy but makes the most accurate information less accessible to the people who need it most,” he wrote.

In the same email, the spokesperson also noted “on background”—a condition to which Ars did not agree—that “Polymarket does not currently have any markets on wildfires and has not for some time.”

The spokesperson declined to respond to Ars’ follow-up questions about whether Polymarket was claiming that, by definition, it provides “the most accurate information” to people experiencing a wildfire.

Perverse incentives

For their part, wildfire experts say that they are appalled by the mere existence of prediction markets that allow for trading on these disasters.

“[Such markets] could create a perverse incentive for arson or other destructive activities,”

Michael Gollner, a professor at the UC Berkeley Fire Research Lab, emailed Ars. “We should not focus our energy on monetizing the outcome of devastating natural disasters. Instead, we should focus our efforts on mitigating these events with targeting investments before they start so that our communities can become more resilient.”

Riva Duncan, the president of Grassroots Wildland Firefighters, a nonprofit organization made up of current and former federal wildland firefighters, said her community is “pretty disgusted” by these betting markets.

“To think there are people hoping to make money off tragedy is beyond comprehension,” she emailed Ars. “They should ask some of the folks in Spokane who just lost their homes how they feel about it.”

19 Charged for Allegedly Defrauding Medicaid, Getting Paid While in Prison, Vacationing, or Dead | Janice Hisle, The Epoch Times

At times when Pennsylvania home healthcare aides were supposed to be helping people, they instead were “hospitalized, working at other jobs, and even in jail,” Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald told reporters Aug. 4 in Philadelphia.

Often, the aides worked with co-conspirators who would bill Medicaid for services that were never rendered, he said, announcing 19 defendants were charged in the latest “fraud takedown.”

The new cases involve alleged home-healthcare schemes that netted in excess of $4 million, said McDonald, who heads the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division. The cases were brought as a result of cooperation among multiple federal and state law-enforcement agencies.

McDonald also announced that his agency’s Northeast Healthcare Strike Force is expanding to Philadelphia, to “place dedicated fraud prosecutors right here to further root out the fraud in Pennsylvania.”

Investigations revealed blatant patterns of deliberate conduct, not honest mistakes, he and other officials said.

For example, a healthcare company “billed for an aide that was dead—600 clock-ins in a year, to the tune of a total of $225,000 in Medicaid billings,” U.S. Attorney David Metcalf said, adding that other aides claimed to be working “while jet-setting across the Caribbean and Europe.”

McDonald also noted a case that intertwined several alleged fraudsters in the same family.

Conspirators claimed work hours for their son during a timeframe when police were citing him for marijuana possession. On another occasion, that same aide “billed Medicaid for a full day of in-home care for his father … [while] the father was not home at all; he was in a courtroom—watching a different relative get sentenced for defrauding this same program.”

After widespread Medicaid fraud drew national attention in Minnesota late last year, President Donald Trump launched various fraud-fighting measures. He appointed Vice President JD Vance to head an anti-fraud task force. He also created McDonald’s new fraud-focused division in the Justice Department.

Those efforts have started only recently but are paying off, said Scott Brady, executive director of the White House Fraud Task Force.

“We’ve already stopped tens of billions of dollars in fraud, and we’ve already indicted and convicted hundreds of fraudsters,” he said, noting he is among native Pennsylvanians who consider it “personal” to fight fraud in the Keystone State.

McDonald said the home healthcare program helps honest Americans receive care with dignity, “from those they trust the most.” But when “deceitful opportunists” take advantage of it, the program “becomes a money tree, a gravy train for criminal fraudsters.”

“The era of getting rich off the backs of our programs for our sick, elderly, and disabled is over,” McDonald said.

‘Everybody Is Doing This’

Metcalf highlighted the case of Sean Murray, who was being held on prior federal drug charges in the Federal Detention Center in Philadelphia. The prison is adjacent to the federal building where officials were speaking to reporters, Metcalf and other speakers noted.

Murray, 58, was indicted on one count of healthcare fraud and nine counts of wire fraud.

Instead of providing healthcare services, as claimed, he was elsewhere, Metcalf said.

“He was at the gym. He was at the massage parlor. He was on a cruise, and at worst, he was packaging narcotics to run his drug trafficking operation,” the prosecutor said, adding, “In a jail call that was recorded in August 2024, Sean Murray boasted about how easy of a racket it was.”

The Epoch Times was unable to immediately reach Murray’s lawyer, Gina Amoriello, for comment.

The case against Philadelphia-based Benevolent Home Health Care, the company whose founders allegedly billed for the deceased healthcare aide, was tied to an alleged drug trafficker, Metcalf said.

The drug suspect is married to one of the company’s founders, Metcalf said. During a drug raid, the husband purportedly stated, “Hold on, I need to clock out of my shift.”

“And when the agents asked what he meant by that, he said, ‘Everybody is doing this. If that’s a problem, you'd have to arrest the whole city,’” referring to healthcare-billing schemes, said Metcalf. “That is shocking, and it illustrates the extent of the problem that we’re dealing with here: ‘Everybody is doing this.’”

The Epoch Times received no immediate response to a phone message left for Benevolent; the drug suspect allegedly tied to the company was identified only as “Miss Williams’s husband” during the news conference and in a subsequent news release.

Then, “While this man was in the prison behind me, the company and Miss Williams billed him for home care services … a federally charged narcotics trafficker, literally sitting behind bars in the federal detention center, was still being billed for home care services,” Metcalf said.

Such brazen fraud cases “make a mockery of your tax dollars,” Metcalf said, but said, “it ends today.”

“If ‘everybody is doing it,’ it takes everyone to stop it,” he said. “This is going to take the total force of the United States government and our state partners.”

Beyond Fraud, Waste, and Abuse

Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday called defendant Ashley Griffin “quite the magician” and said sarcastically that she “had some very ‘productive’ days.”

A personal care attendant for 13 different agencies in several counties, Griffin claimed to have worked “more than 24 hours in a single day—more than 1,000 times … and, for one day, she submitted 126 hours of work,” Sunday said.

During more than three years, she claimed more than 64,000 work hours “for services that she absolutely could not have possibly done,” Sunday alleged, amounting to Medicaid payments of more than $1.2 million.

The Epoch Times was unable to immediately identify an attorney who might offer comment on behalf of Griffin, 27.

“These [cases] might be half-comical, if they weren’t unbelievably serious criminal acts causing a tremendous amount of harm,” Sunday said, calling the cases a public health threat. In the past, some Medicaid patients have died after failing to receive the help they needed.

Dr. Mehmet Oz, administrator of the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, said: “These fraudsters are stealing our trust, and that’s a much more difficult thing to replace.”

The doctor said he diagnosed a deeper pathology too: “This is not fraud, waste, and abuse by itself. This is corruption.”

“When ‘everyone is doing it,’ which is maybe the most important quote from this press conference,” the implication is that “if you’re not part of the corrupt system, you’re a fool,” Oz said. “That’s how countries collapse.”

Primary Archetype: Floor General / Pass-First Creator

Sydney Youngblood enters the 2029 evaluation cycle as an advanced lead guard with early national visibility, Nike EYBL experience, and a growing Division I market. Her value is not built on scoring volume alone. The stronger signal is her ability to organize possessions, control pace, and create functional offense without forcing the game.

Youngblood projects as a primary on-ball creator who balances distribution with selective scoring. She plays with poise, changes speeds effectively, and uses the middle of the floor with purpose. Her mid-range pull-up and floater package give her solutions when defenses contain the rim or play conservative ball-screen coverage. She can generate her own offense, but her natural identity remains team-oriented.

The processing profile is the foundation of the projection. Youngblood appears comfortable reading help defenders, advancing the ball early, and keeping teammates involved. She does not need extended isolation sequences to influence the game. Her value comes from creating advantages, extending them, and making the next correct read.

Defensively, the statistical sample remains incomplete, but the competitive infrastructure is significant. Boo Williams and the Nike EYBL environment consistently expose guards to speed, physicality, and pressure. Youngblood’s stated objective of becoming a complete two-way guard aligns with the next stage of her development. Continued growth in point-of-attack defense, screen navigation, and physical strength will shape her eventual collegiate role.

At 5’9”, she possesses functional positional size for either guard spot. The next evaluation phase should focus on three-point consistency, turnover control under increased usage, and how her decision-making holds against older EYBL competition.

The offer sheet reflects meaningful market trust. Mississippi State and Pittsburgh establish high-major recognition, while Old Dominion, Howard, UMBC, William & Mary, Queens, and Hampton demonstrate broad regional and system-level interest.

The Beechum Verdict: Youngblood projects as an early-cycle high-major trajectory guard whose strongest assets are pace, processing, leadership, and connective play. Her ceiling will depend on continued physical development and shooting growth, but the current foundation supports a multi-year collegiate lead-guard projection.

text:
Harrier “Elevator Ride”: The Legendary Farley Takeoff

Developed by legendary British test pilot John Farley, the “Farley Takeoff” was one of the most spectacular demonstrations ever performed in the Harrier jump jet.

Unlike a conventional takeoff, Farley would first establish the aircraft in a steady hover at approximately 100 feet (30 m) above the ground.

From there:
✔️The Harrier remained supported entirely by its vectored engine thrust.
✔️Farley would smoothly pitch the aircraft’s nose to around 60° while still hovering.
✔️Once stabilized, he would apply maximum power.
✔️The aircraft would then accelerate into an extremely steep climb before transitioning to normal forward flight.

To spectators, it looked as though the Harrier was riding an invisible elevator before suddenly launching skyward.

The maneuver was never part of normal RAF or Royal Navy operations.

Investigations and flight testing had shown that:
✔️The maneuver required exceptional precision and experience.
✔️Any loss of engine thrust or compressor instability while hovering at low altitude could leave little or no chance of recovery.
✔️It offered no operational advantage over approved short takeoff or vertical takeoff procedures.
✔️Service pilots were therefore prohibited from performing it outside of specialized test flying.

The Harrier’s unique Rolls-Royce Pegasus engine, with its vectored-thrust nozzles, made this remarkable demonstration possible. 

While often described as a “rocket climb,” the aircraft remained under normal engine power throughout the maneuver, the dramatic appearance was created by thrust vectoring and expert handling rather than any rocket assistance.

Few pilots ever possessed the skill to perform the Farley Takeoff, and it remains one of the most iconic Harrier demonstrations ever flown.

text:
This post today by DSTL is very interesting. It offers us a glimpse of work ongoing to plan out how to carry out mine countermeasures operations from the future 3 "motherships" to be acquired from Norway. https://t.co/4UgaqLlQti

Points of interest include: 

1) the ship model itself. It is understood the new ships will come specifically through Norway's Standardized Vessel project, but the model is vastly different from the (specified at the time to be "purely indicative", admittedly) CGI posted by the Salt-Kongsberg team when it was selected by Norway to deliver the design of the new vessels (2 designs planned, a Medium and Large). The model used by DSTL is an offshore vessel pure and simple, so I'm not sure what to think of it. 

At this stage, the design of the Standardized Vessels should be getting clearer (in the Autumn the plan is to begin the new competition to decide which yard is going to build them, with the aim to start build next year; the general shapes ought to be clear by now...?) so you'd hope this activity is being carried out on a model which has some relationship to the actual thing. 
Either the Standardized (Large) is going very, very OSV COTS or the UK is buying from Norway but perhaps not actually from the Standardized Vessel proper, but straight from Vard's civilian products...? 

The Royal Navy has been clear for a while that it wants one thing from the new mothership: SPACE. 1000 square meters of deck space to embark drones and payloads and have the freedom to change and mix and evolve over the years, rather that build perfect little motherships like the Netherlands-Belgium-France ones which are sized almost to the centimeter around the current USVs and payloads. 
The RN wants to embark more USVs and have room to adapt. 

2) The payload itself. The models and payloads mapped out on the deck are all coherent with MHC equipment already in service or with things known to be, to some extent or another, planned. 

Most notable is the embarkation of a full 4 USVs, of which 3 are of the MMCM kind (blue ones) and one ARCIMS/SWEEP (the single purple one). The blue containers supply further clues: we can see labels TSAM 1 and TSAM 2, and MuMNS 1 and 2: TSAM being the Thales towed, variable depth sonar for locating the mines, and MuMNS the Saab ROV used to dispose of them. Two ROVs (the yellow little shape) are visible parked outside of their containers. The purple containers hold the SWEEP gear and probably SEA CAT UUVs for use on the ARCIMS USV. 

4 USVs would mark a further expansion in MHC Block 2 plans: a 3 USV config was the plan the last time meaningful information emerged. 

3 USVs are what is currently embarked on RFA LYME BAY for the potential Hormuz mission: 2 MMCM types (1 UK, 1 french) and 1 ARCIMS. 

Astern there are at least 3 containers labeled "UAS" and we see models shaped like the S-100 PEREGRINE rotorcraft drone. 

At present MHC has no Air Element, but the addition of UAS has long been part of MHC Block 2 plans. The UAS can be useful for anything from Search to re-broadcast to control drones over greater distances. 
3 UAS per MHC system was the indicative size of complement in known MHC Block 2 plans, and that's exactly what we see on the model.

text:
Yusuf Puts It In Writing: Britain's Marines Will Land On French Beaches "Anyway"

Reform's Operation Fortress plan has spent the past 24 hours moving from a policy document into something closer to a live diplomatic incident, and Zia Yusuf's own Substack post today, published under his own name rather than relayed through a spokesperson, confirms the parts of it that mattered most were never really in doubt.

The headline commitment is now on the record in his own words. If France agrees to accept returns, migrants will be disembarked in French ports. If France doesn't agree, Yusuf writes, they will be "landed on the beaches anyway." That single sentence resolves any ambiguity left in the original document, which had only hedged towards this scenario in its legal appendix. It is now the stated position of Reform's prospective Home Secretary, a role Yusuf assigns himself directly in the closing line of the post, published in his own voice rather than attributed to him by others.

The French government's actual objection is worth stating precisely rather than paraphrasing loosely: officials have called the plan "a violation of French sovereignty," a quote Yusuf includes and then dismisses, framing Paris's objection as reluctance to give up what he describes as a lucrative arrangement funded by British taxpayers. Mocking a formal sovereignty objection from a NATO ally, rather than addressing it, is a striking way to respond to exactly the kind of diplomatic friction the plan's critics warned it would produce.

The other major development is Tony Abbott's public endorsement. Unlike Brigadier Litster, whose service record checks out, or the still-unverifiable Commander Chris Grace and John Cail, Abbott is not a minor or unconfirmed figure. He is the former Australian Prime Minister who actually implemented Operation Sovereign Borders, the precedent Reform's document leans on throughout. His endorsement gives the plan a credible, internationally recognised voice it didn't have before, and it will likely feature heavily in Reform's response to critics who've focused on the document's weaker sourcing elsewhere.

None of this resolves the substantive problems already identified: the mismatch between Australia's total exclusion policy and Reform's version, which offers no equivalent deterrent; the ECHR compliance claim that only holds for as long as Britain remains a member; the operational capacity questions raised by a retired Royal Navy commander on the BBC's own airwaves. What today's post does is remove any remaining doubt about intent. Reform is not proposing a contingency it hopes never to use. It is proposing, in writing, from the man who would run the Home Office, to put armed personnel on an ally's beaches regardless of whether that ally agrees.

text:
This person had a signed job offer, put in their two weeks, worked out their notice, and then the company rescinded the offer 3 days before their start date.

Now they're unemployed with rent due. This should be illegal.

Here's what almost nobody in that thread knows. In many states, it basically is.

The doctrine is called promissory estoppel. A company that makes you a promise it knows will cause you to resign owes you when you resign and get burned. The offer letter alone means little in an at-will state. Your resignation is what creates the liability.

A woman in Nebraska quit an 11-year job for an offer that got revoked the day before her start date, because an owner's wife didn't want her hired. The state supreme court made the clinic pay.

In California, Joseph Toscano quit a piano retailer on a promise from Greene Music. They yanked the offer two weeks later. A court hit them for $536,833.

And the damages come from the job you gave up. Your old salary. Your tenure. Your benefits. The entire life you dismantled because they told you to.

The part that should make this person feel better. HR's email saying the position was "eliminated due to restructuring" is a signed admission the rescission had nothing to do with them. That's the first exhibit in a demand letter.

Most of these never reach a courtroom. One letter from an employment lawyer, and a company staring at its own words tends to find months of severance for someone who never worked there a single day.

Companies rescind casually because they think the downside is zero. It isn't.

text:
Mapping monsters: new data release reveals all-sky views of supermassive black holes

The Sloan Digital Sky Survey has released Data Release 20, marking a major expansion of its fifth-generation mapping campaign. For the first time, the public dataset includes optical spectra collected by the BOSS instrument at Las Campanas Observatory in Chile. Combined with ongoing observations from Apache Point Observatory in New Mexico, this delivers a true all-sky spectroscopic view of the cosmos.

The full release contains more than 3.3 million optical spectra of roughly 500,000 galaxies and 1.5 million stars. Within it, the Black Hole Mapper program has grown dramatically—three to four times larger than in the previous release—contributing about 1.1 million spectra focused on half a million distinct objects.

A standout feature is the SPIDERS program, which pairs SDSS optical spectroscopy with X-ray maps from the eROSITA space telescope. This effort has produced precise optical identifications and distance measurements for approximately 200,000 X-ray sources, creating the largest uniform follow-up catalog of its kind. Most of these targets are active galactic nuclei and quasars powered by accreting supermassive black holes, along with galaxy clusters and active stars.

The combined X-ray and optical data offer fresh insights into how black holes grew across cosmic history. Researchers found a surprisingly high density of extremely luminous active galactic nuclei at high redshifts near redshift 6, showing that rapidly growing giant black holes were common during the era known as cosmic dawn. At the same time, soft X-ray-selected objects account for only a small fraction of the total black-hole mass in the local universe. This suggests that 70 to 90 percent of black-hole growth occurred either behind thick clouds of gas and dust or during periods when X-ray emission was suppressed.

To study the extreme environments near accretion disks that cannot be imaged directly, SDSS-V employs time-domain spectroscopy. Reverberation mapping involves collecting repeated spectra over time to measure light-travel delays between the central disk and surrounding gas clouds, providing geometric mass estimates for distant black holes. The All-Quasar Multi-Epoch Spectroscopy program further monitors changing-look quasars, potential binary black holes, and powerful gas outflows. The unexpected diversity of these spectra required extensive visual inspections to identify unusual objects missed by automated systems.

These advances are made possible by the Robotic Focal Plane System installed on the 2.5-meter telescopes at both observatories. All Data Release 20 products are freely available to the public through the project’s science and catalog archive servers, along with updated web tools and Jupyter Notebook tutorials designed to support multi-wavelength research worldwide.

text: you can beleive what you want as faith. but cannot state faith as facts.there is no contemporary 1st-century documentary or archaeological proof that Thomas the Apostle journeyed to India. Historians evaluate the tradition based on later texts, regional trade routes, and material gaps. Zero 1st-Century Records: No Roman, Greek, Jewish, Persian, or Indian state records from Thomas's lifetime mention him.Silent Canonical Texts: The New Testament offers no details on Thomas's later life or travels.Late Attestation: The earliest written narrative linking Thomas to the East is the Acts of Thomas, an apocryphal text composed in Edessa (Upper Mesopotamia) around the early 3rd century—at least 130 to 150 years after his supposed death.The Indo-Parthian ConfusionThe King Gondophares Connection: The Acts of Thomas names an actual historical king, Gondophares, who ruled the Indo-Parthian Kingdom (modern Afghanistan, Pakistan, and parts of Northwest India) in the 1st century.Geographic Disconnect: Historians note that the text places Thomas in the northern/northwestern realm of Gondophares, which does not match or support the separate local oral traditions of South India (Kerala and Mylapore/Tamil Nadu) that emerged centuries later. Trade,  Archaeological findings—such as Roman coins and pottery found along the Malabar coast—prove extensive maritime trade between the Roman Empire, the Persian Gulf, and South India during the 1st century.Alternative historians suggest that early Christian communities in South India (the Saint Thomas Christians) likely originated or were influenced later via East Syrian/Persian Gulf merchant migration and trade networks rather than a direct, single-man apostolic mission

And it’s the reverse when you come in, Nobunaga, ESPECIALLY amongst we Irish. You always refuse the first two offers of refreshment and always accept the third even if you don’t want anything.

“Ah! As I live and breathe. Look who it is! Let me put the kettle on.”

“Oh, no, I just popped in to say hello and see how everyone is doing. I’d hate for you to go to any trouble.”

Minutes pass with more conversation, then:

“Are you sure I can’t get you anything? A bit of cake maybe?”

“Oh, that’s a grand offer, but there’s need to go to any bother on my account.”

Mire minutes pass with more conversation, then:

“Right when you came up the drive, I was headed to the kitchen to put the kettle on and have a wee bit of cake myself. Won’t you join me?”

“Well, if you’re having some anyway, a spot of tea and a bit of cake would be welcome, but just a small piece.”

The host wants to be treated with respect, not like a hotel or a restaurant and also doesn’t want the hospitality ultimately refused. That’s one of the worst insults you could give.

The guest wants the host to know that the hospitality is appreciated and is neither presumed nor taken for granted.

It’s a delicate dance with rules we learn by osmosis as children when visiting our great-aunts, our grandparents, and our parents’s friends.

Williams opined that “it’s entirely possible you could see these connected in this decision” because “it’s really kind of hard to separate the magazine out from the firearm to the extent that an AR-15 comes with a standard magazine; it’s generally a 30-round magazine.” He furthermore noted these guns’ wide use among the American public.

From the article:

The U.S. Supreme Court is gearing up to weigh another big Second Amendment issue in its upcoming term — a matter legal specialists say will greatly affect Americans’ constitutional rights.

During a Tuesday Federalist Society forum, Notre Dame Law School Professor Haley Proctor and American Suppressor Association General Counsel Michael Williams offered viewers a sneak preview into what’s at stake in Viramontes v. Cook County and Grant v. Higgins. The pair of consolidated cases — which deal with the legality of laws banning AR-15s and similar semiautomatic firearms — will be heard by the high court in its October 2026 term.

The two panelists began by laying the foundation of the Supreme Court’s existing Second Amendment jurisprudence, which included a discussion of its 2022 NYSRPA v. Bruen decision. In Bruen, the majority (6-3) recognized that Americans have a constitutional right to carry firearms outside the home for purposes of self-defense.

The Bruen ruling established a two-step test lower courts are to use when assessing restrictions on firearm possession. The majority said courts must first assess whether the regulated conduct is covered by the Second Amendment’s plain text, and if so, determine if that regulation is consistent with the nation’s “historical tradition of firearm regulation.”

Turning to Viramontes and Grant, Williams observed how the 2nd and 7th Courts of Appeals effectively failed to properly adopt Bruen‘s two-step framework when considering the challenges to the respective laws.

In Viramontes, Williams noted that the 7th Circuit “essentially stops the argument at step one” by analogizing AR-15s to “automatic weapons” like M-16s, which it found are “presumptively not covered by the Second Amendment” under existing SCOTUS precedent. Meanwhile, in Grant, he said that the 2nd Circuit focused more on the second step by accepting Connecticut’s “historical analogues” regarding bans on “certain types of knives” and “machine guns,” and started “to slip closer and closer” to a framework rejected by the Supreme Court in Bruen.

The attorneys also considered the possibility that the Supreme Court may address the lawfulness of restrictions on gun-magazine size in its decision. The sole question agreed to by the justices is whether the Second and 14th Amendments “guarantee the right to possess AR-15 platform and similar semiautomatic rifles.”

Williams opined that “it’s entirely possible you could see these connected in this decision” because “it’s really kind of hard to separate the magazine out from the firearm to the extent that an AR-15 comes with a standard magazine; it’s generally a 30-round magazine.” He furthermore noted these guns’ wide use among the American public.

Proctor expressed uncertainty on whether the high court will handle the magazine issue in Viramontes and Grant, “especially now that there is a circuit [court] split” on the question. She noted there’s always a chance, however.

“One possibility is that they decide Viramontes and send it back to the lower courts to try again with the standard capacity magazine bans,” Proctor said. “What … separates these out is the question of the definition of arms. … [Wolford v. Lopez] shows pretty well that the [Bruen] step-one questions are fairly well-settled. But that is still one area in the magazine cases where lower courts are trying to crack open the step-one analysis. And we see that in the back-and-forth in the 9th Circuit’s decision on large-capacity magazines in the Duncan case.”

“So, hopefully we’ll get some sort of clarification in Viramontes even if the court doesn’t take up the magazine issue on how the arms analysis is meant to proceed,” she added.

In Wolford, the Supreme Court ruled 6-3 that Hawaii’s “vampire rule” restricting concealed-carry holders’ ability to carry on private property open to the public to be unconstitutional. The majority held that the state’s gun control “regime” — which was adopted to seemingly sidestep Bruen — “hobble[d] what the Second Amendment protects: the right of Americans to carry arms for self-defense as they go about their daily lives.”

While signaling the Supreme Court would likely deem the AR-15 restrictions in Viramontes and Grant to be unlawful, Proctor and Williams indicated they wouldn’t be surprised if states with these laws effectively try to circumvent a positive ruling. Williams compared such behavior to the “mass resistance” among Southern states to the high court’s Brown v. Board of Education (1954) decision nuking state-enforced segregation.

“There’s a Supreme Court case that comes out; a certain number of states do not like that outcome; and they’re doing everything in their power to get out from under it, with a little bit of help from some lower courts who haven’t quite wrapped their minds around this test and this issue yet. … But it would be frankly shocking to me if there were not attempts by these states after … a likely, hopeful victory here for AR-15s to get around by just making it difficult,” Williams said.

Towards the end of the panel, the two participants also flagged several gun-related issues that are likely to come down the Supreme Court’s pipeline in the coming years. Proctor highlighted legal battles over bans on firearm possession for 18 to 20-year-olds and felons, while Williams pointed to existing restrictions on suppressors and remaining commerce clause questions involving gun regulation.

A date for oral arguments in Viramontes and Grant has not been announced.

text:
The idea that being a decent person involves controlling the kinds of thoughts you allow yourself to think can easily be met with resistance. If virtue depends on limits to what is thinkable, and a certain free-thought ideal celebrates no limits, then the potential conflict between freethinking and virtue is obvious. And if the choice is offered between thinking whatever you like and being virtuous, then it’s perhaps no surprise that some will opt for absolute freedom of thought. Freedom, for artists and thinkers in this tradition, is the ultimate value – and, as a result, virtue is depicted as restrictive and square. What emerges is an anarchic freethinking ideal that cherishes humour and shock appeal. You can find it in punk music and in the cartoon series South Park, and baked into the founding libertarian ethos of the web. 

Concern about virtue and innocence, especially if we use these now faintly archaic terms, is something that’s easy to mock, particularly in cultures that celebrate what’s edgy and savvy. The Irish wit Oscar Wilde’s response to the Society for the Suppression of Vice was to joke that he and his mother had ‘founded a society for the suppression of virtue’. And we know what Wilde (and later followers in his footsteps) objected to: po-faced moralisers, killjoys, unthinking enforcers of traditional morality. Judgments of sexual morality, moreover, can be notoriously difficult. If the image you are looking at is disturbing, is it because it is explicit and unfamiliar to you, or is it because it is wrong? When are you looking at a problem, and when is the problem you?

That people can be ethically mistaken is not, however, a good reason for having no ethics at all. And the fact of fallibility does not take away the basic tension identified above: between virtues that by their nature restrict thought and imagination and the prevailing spirit of the internet that encourages the idea that everything should be viewable and thinkable. The idea that freedom and freethinking might cause problems for virtue didn’t start with the internet but, as with so much else, the internet intensifies the situation. If, as the Irish playwright George Bernard Shaw wrote, virtue is insufficient temptation, then the internet makes sure we are never lacking. (link below)

$TLN KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM TALEN ENERGY Q2 2026 EARNINGS CALL

The Talen Energy Q2 2026 call provides a materially constructive read-through for existing dispatchable generation, merchant nuclear, integrated power retailers, transmission developers, electrical-equipment suppliers and selected Appalachian natural-gas producers. PJM scarcity has moved beyond a theoretical load-growth narrative and is now visible in realized dispatch, forward spark spreads, capacity-auction outcomes and bilateral contracting interest. The most important strategic change is that time-to-power, grid location and access to existing generation are becoming more valuable than undeveloped land or long-dated new-build generation plans. The principal negative read-through is that this scarcity is attracting increasingly aggressive regulatory intervention, including capacity-price caps, backstop procurement and potential load-curtailment structures. The most differentiated implication is locational: incremental data-center load in a generation-surplus zone can generate direct contracted revenue while also improving the realized price of the broader generation portfolio through basis compression. Consequently, power producers with existing low-cost assets, available interconnection capacity and credible paths to long-term contracts are positioned to outperform, while hyperscalers without secured power and providers dependent on behind-the-meter solutions face greater execution and valuation risk.

INDEPENDENT POWER PRODUCERS AND WHOLESALE POWER MARKETS

PJM SCARCITY IS NOW A MONETIZABLE EARNINGS TAILWIND RATHER THAN A LONG-DATED INVESTMENT NARRATIVE (READ-THROUGH 1)

Affected companies and impact: Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG: US) — Positive, High; Vistra Corp. (VST: US) — Positive, High; NRG Energy, Inc. (NRG: US) — Positive, Medium-High; Talen Energy Corporation (TLN: US) — Positive, High.

Supporting call evidence: Talen reported that West Hub spark spreads had increased by nearly 50% from the prior year, that the last 3 PJM base residual auctions cleared at the applicable price cap, and that the same auctions would have cleared above $500/MW-day without the cap. Management also stated that long-term energy and capacity forwards were approaching or exceeding the approximately $80/MWh level previously discussed for hyperscaler contracts. Bilateral capacity bids were reportedly being observed at cap-level economics into the early 2030s, although management appropriately cautioned that these markets remain thin.

The transmission mechanism is direct. Higher forward energy prices raise the value of unhedged generation, while wider spark spreads increase the margin earned by gas and coal assets after fuel costs. Elevated capacity prices provide a high-margin, largely fixed revenue stream independent of actual energy production. Low-variable-cost nuclear assets benefit disproportionately because nearly all incremental energy-price appreciation converts into gross margin. Constellation therefore represents the clearest public-market beneficiary. Vistra and NRG also benefit through competitive generation portfolios, although their integrated retail books can offset or defer part of the immediate wholesale upside.

The near-term trading catalyst is continued upward revision to forward earnings and free cash flow estimates as sell-side models incorporate stronger PJM curves, higher capacity revenue and improved plant utilization. The next PJM capacity auction and any further strengthening in 2027-2029 forward prices could produce additional estimate revisions. The longer-duration fundamental shift is a sustained increase in the replacement value and strategic value of existing dispatchable generation. New generation remains expensive, slow to permit and difficult to interconnect, while load growth is materializing faster than incremental firm supply. Existing assets should therefore retain structurally higher scarcity rents than were embedded in historical valuation frameworks.

The principal limitation is regulatory. Capacity-price caps and backstop procurement can prevent the full economic scarcity signal from reaching generators. Nevertheless, even capped pricing is already supporting materially higher cash generation. The evidence supports a higher normalized earnings base for PJM merchant generators, not merely a weather-driven cyclical spike.

LONG-TERM POWER CONTRACTS ARE BECOMING A CREDIT-AND-DURATION PRODUCT RATHER THAN A SIMPLE PREMIUM-PRICE PRODUCT (READ-THROUGH 2)

Affected companies and impact: Constellation Energy Corporation (CEG: US) — Positive, High; NRG Energy, Inc. (NRG: US) — Positive, High; Vistra Corp. (VST: US) — Positive, Medium-High; Talen Energy Corporation (TLN: US) — Positive, High; https://t.co/SpqvHNUxpK, Inc. (AMZN: US), Microsoft Corporation (MSFT: US), Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL: US), Meta Platforms, Inc. (META: US) and Oracle Corporation (ORCL: US) — Negative, Medium, through higher power-procurement costs.

Supporting call evidence: Management stated that wholesale energy and capacity prices were now approaching or exceeding the approximately $80/MWh level previously associated with long-term hyperscaler PPAs. Talen also described “renewed interest in long-term contracts in the C&I space” and an expanding customer universe that now includes hyperscalers, co-location providers, neo-cloud companies and large commercial and industrial users. The existing AWS arrangement is expected to increase long-term contracted gross margin from approximately 10% in 2028 to approximately 35% as the contract approaches full ramp. An additional approximately 2 GW of similar contracts could increase contracted gross margin to approximately 60% beyond 2030.

The positive read-through for generators is not that every future PPA will carry an unusually large premium to current merchant pricing. That premium is likely compressing because the merchant alternative has appreciated materially. The value of a new contract increasingly comes from revenue durability, counterparty credit, reduced earnings volatility, improved financing terms and the potential to lower the seller’s cost of capital. A long-tenor agreement with a highly rated technology counterparty can support a higher valuation multiple even when the contract price is only modestly above the prevailing forward curve.

Integrated generation and retail companies are particularly advantaged. NRG, Constellation and Vistra can combine generation, retail load management, structured hedging and credit capabilities to offer customers customized long-duration products. This expands the contracting opportunity beyond one-off hyperscaler transactions and creates a pathway to convert volatile merchant gross margin into recurring infrastructure-like cash flow.

The negative transmission mechanism for technology and C&I buyers is higher procurement cost. As wholesale alternatives rise, generators have less incentive to accept low fixed-price contracts. Buyers must either pay more, accept greater curtailment risk, fund new capacity, provide stronger contractual protections or delay the load. The near-term catalyst is the announcement of new power contracts and disclosure of price, tenor, capacity obligations and commencement dates. The longer-duration shift is a transfer of bargaining power toward owners of existing generation and transmission-ready sites.

DATA CENTERS AND DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE

SECURED POWER AVAILABILITY IS BECOMING A RELATIVE COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE AMONG HYPERSCALERS (READ-THROUGH 3)

Affected companies and impact: https://t.co/SpqvHNUxpK, Inc. (AMZN: US) — Positive, High, on a relative basis; Microsoft Corporation (MSFT: US), Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL: US), Meta Platforms, Inc. (META: US) and Oracle Corporation (ORCL: US) — Negative, Medium, where equivalent near-term power has not already been secured.

Supporting call evidence: Management observed that hyperscalers were seeking projects capable of delivering power “exactly in ’28” and stated that as the industry approaches 2027, “’29 becomes the new ’28.” Talen emphasized that the AWS campus adjacent to Susquehanna is already being built and that the broader issue is increasingly a matter of customer prioritization and resource allocation rather than a single regulatory bottleneck. Management characterized successful contracting as “a matter of when, not if,” but acknowledged that even the hyperscalers are struggling to accelerate construction schedules.

The transmission mechanism is through data-center deployment timing. Compute capacity cannot be monetized until the site has sufficient power, transmission access, cooling, permits and equipment. A hyperscaler with an energized or contractually secured power position can deploy servers sooner, capture customer demand earlier and reduce the risk that committed capital remains stranded in unfinished facilities. Amazon’s existing relationship with Talen and the approximately 2 GW Susquehanna-linked contract create a relative advantage because a meaningful portion of future campus power has already been identified.

For hyperscalers without comparable arrangements, the risk is not necessarily a reduction in long-term artificial-intelligence infrastructure demand. The more likely outcomes are project delays, geographic relocation, greater use of co-location providers, higher contracted power costs or a shift in capital spending from server equipment toward site-enabling infrastructure. Reported capital expenditure can remain high even as the timing of revenue-generating compute deployment slips.

The near-term trading catalysts are new site announcements, PPA disclosures, project delays and changes in management commentary regarding data-center energization schedules. The longer-duration fundamental shift is that power procurement becomes a strategic capability comparable with semiconductor procurement and network architecture. Technology companies with direct generation relationships, utility commitments and scalable grid-connected sites should receive a relative execution premium. Companies that announce large data-center capital budgets without commensurate power visibility face increasing risk that nominal investment does not translate into timely capacity growth.

LOCAL DATA-CENTER LOAD CAN CREATE A PORTFOLIO-WIDE BASIS BENEFIT THAT EXCEEDS THE DIRECT VALUE OF THE PPA (READ-THROUGH 4)

Affected companies and impact: Talen Energy Corporation (TLN: US) — Negative, Medium-High, near term from current basis; Positive, High, longer term from normalization; PPL Corporation (PPL: US) — Positive, Medium-High, longer term through load and network investment.

Supporting call evidence: Talen stated that the historical PPL discount to West Hub had been approximately $9/MWh but had widened to approximately $20/MWh. Management attributed the move to transmission work south of Talen’s generation and the PPL zone’s position as a large net exporter. The company identified 2 mechanisms for compression: completion of transmission upgrades and additional load within the PPL zone. Management also provided a highly material sensitivity: every $1/MWh improvement in zonal basis across the portfolio would equate to approximately $1 of adjusted free cash flow per share. The current 2027 and 2028 outlooks reportedly use existing widened basis marks and do not assume normalization.

The near-term negative mechanism is straightforward. Generation in an export-constrained zone realizes a lower local power price than generation priced directly at West Hub. A West Hub hedge can protect the broad commodity price but does not fully hedge the PPL locational discount because farther-dated zonal products and financial transmission rights are less liquid. The widened basis therefore creates a real earnings drag even when broader PJM prices rise.

The longer-term positive mechanism is more powerful and less widely appreciated. A new data center located inside PPL reduces the amount of surplus generation that must be exported. That supports local prices across the entire generation fleet, not only the MW sold under the new contract. A single load agreement can therefore create 2 sources of value: direct contracted margin and indirect basis improvement on remaining merchant output. Management summarized this relationship by stating that “nothing solves basis like load.”

This is a potentially significant multiplier for Talen and a broader strategic signal for generators evaluating powered-land development. The most valuable site may not be the site that commands the highest standalone real-estate value; it may be the site that creates the greatest uplift in the realized price of the surrounding generation portfolio.

The near-term catalysts are completion of transmission outages, evidence of narrowing cash and forward PPL basis, and binding load commitments. The longer-duration shift is the increasing integration of generation strategy, data-center siting and nodal or zonal power-market economics.

FRONT-OF-THE-METER GRID SOLUTIONS ARE LIKELY TO CAPTURE THE MAJORITY OF LARGE-SCALE DATA-CENTER POWER DEMAND (READ-THROUGH 5)

Affected companies and impact: Quanta Services, Inc. (PWR: US) — Positive, High; Eaton Corporation plc (ETN: Ireland) — Positive, High; Powell Industries, Inc. (POWL: US) — Positive, Medium-High; Bloom Energy Corporation (BE: US) — Negative, Medium, relative to expectations for behind-the-meter power as the dominant long-term architecture.

Supporting call evidence: Talen repeatedly stated that it is not pursuing behind-the-meter structures. Management said that the preferred long-term solution is “front of the meter, grid connected,” with or without incremental capacity, and described grid power as “the primary preference of our customers.” Management further argued that combining existing baseload energy with new capacity is more reliable, durable and less expensive than a behind-the-meter solution.

The positive transmission mechanism for grid suppliers is a larger infrastructure requirement for each data-center campus. Front-of-the-meter solutions require substations, high-voltage interconnection, protective relays, transformers, switchgear, power-distribution systems, controls and utility-grade transmission work. Quanta benefits from engineering and construction demand; Eaton and Powell benefit from electrical distribution and switchgear requirements.

The negative read-through for Bloom Energy is relative rather than absolute. Behind-the-meter fuel cells and other on-site generation can still provide bridge power, resilience, backup capability or a solution in regions with insufficient grid capacity. However, Talen’s customer discussions indicate that large customers generally prefer to retain grid access and use new on-site or adjacent capacity as a supplement rather than as the sole long-term supply architecture. This limits the probability that behind-the-meter systems displace the grid as the dominant solution for multi-hundred-MW and GW-scale campuses.

Talen is not a neutral observer because its strategy is explicitly built around front-of-the-meter assets. Nevertheless, management’s repeated reference to customer preference gives the commentary greater evidentiary value than a purely theoretical competitive assertion.

The near-term catalysts are the design of newly announced hyperscaler campuses and the mix of utility interconnection, on-site generation and battery capacity specified in those projects. The longer-duration shift is toward hybrid grid architecture rather than complete grid bypass. That favors incumbent utilities, transmission contractors and electrical-equipment manufacturers over single-technology behind-the-meter providers.

REGULATED UTILITIES AND TRANSMISSION INFRASTRUCTURE

PPL AND AEP OHIO APPEAR POSITIONED AS RELATIVE WINNERS IN THE DATA-CENTER LOAD-LOCATION COMPETITION (READ-THROUGH 6)

Affected companies and impact: PPL Corporation (PPL: US) — Positive, Medium-High; American Electric Power Company, Inc. (AEP: US) — Positive, High; Exelon Corporation (EXC: US) — Positive, Medium; Dominion Energy, Inc. (D: US) — Positive, Medium.

Supporting call evidence: Talen described PPL as a zone with approximately 2 times as much generation capacity as current load and available transmission capacity within the zone. Management cited the AWS campus and other large data-center developments as evidence that the region can absorb incremental demand. AEP Ohio was characterized as business-friendly, data-center-friendly and already established as a major data-center hub. PJM demand was forecast to increase by more than 17% through the end of the decade. Transmission work between PPL and the BGE and Dominion load pockets was also identified as an active system investment.

The regulated-utility transmission mechanism is a larger rate-base opportunity. Data-center connections require transmission extensions, substations, distribution upgrades and reinforcement of the surrounding grid. Utilities can earn regulated returns on approved infrastructure investment, while sustained load growth can improve fixed-cost absorption and support broader system modernization.

AEP has particularly strong exposure because Ohio combines established data-center development, a large transmission footprint and proximity to existing generation. PPL benefits from a generation-surplus service territory that can accommodate load, while Exelon and Dominion participate through the downstream load pockets and associated transmission requirements.

The positive read-through is conditional on regulatory treatment. Large load additions create concerns regarding cost allocation, reliability and whether residential customers will subsidize data-center infrastructure. Management explicitly described data centers as a political issue and noted that elections and ratepayer-protection pledges are influencing policy. Utilities that secure contracts requiring large-load customers to fund dedicated infrastructure and capacity obligations should outperform utilities that assume substantial upfront cost with uncertain cost recovery.

The near-term catalysts are utility load-service agreements, interconnection approvals, tariff structures and regulatory rulings on cost allocation. The longer-duration shift is higher transmission and distribution capital expenditure in regions capable of combining available power with favorable permitting and utility cooperation.

PPL CONGESTION CONFIRMS THAT TRANSMISSION SPENDING IS AN ECONOMIC NECESSITY, NOT A DISCRETIONARY GRID-MODERNIZATION THEME (READ-THROUGH 7)

Affected companies and impact: Quanta Services, Inc. (PWR: US) — Positive, High; MYR Group Inc. (MYRG: US) — Positive, High; Hubbell Incorporated (HUBB: US) — Positive, Medium-High; Eaton Corporation plc (ETN: Ireland) — Positive, Medium-High; Powell Industries, Inc. (POWL: US) — Positive, Medium-High.

Supporting call evidence: Management stated that PPL basis had widened to approximately $20/MWh and directly linked the discount to transmission outages and upgrade work limiting southbound power flows. The work is part of a broader system upgrade between the PPL region and the BGE and Dominion load pockets. Management also said that additional transmission has already been approved and that the constraint will be addressed through both network investment and new local load.

The transmission mechanism is unusually visible. Congestion is already creating a material economic penalty for generators, while growing load in southern PJM raises reliability requirements. This creates a clear financial incentive for utilities and PJM to advance transmission projects. Unlike discretionary modernization projects, these investments are supported by observable basis differentials, reliability needs and large-load commitments.

Quanta and MYR are the most direct beneficiaries through engineering, procurement, construction and maintenance of transmission lines and substations. Hubbell benefits from grid hardware, connectors and utility components. Eaton and Powell benefit from medium- and high-voltage electrical equipment, power distribution and control systems required at both utility and customer interconnection points.

The near-term catalyst is conversion of approved projects into contractor backlog and equipment orders. The current work also creates temporary operational disruptions, meaning earnings benefits for generators may lag contractor revenue recognition. The longer-duration fundamental shift is a multi-year transmission build cycle driven simultaneously by data centers, generation-location mismatch, aging infrastructure and grid reliability.

The call also indicates that transmission expansion will not eliminate the value of local generation. Even after network upgrades, very large data-center loads will require both increased transfer capability and incremental firm capacity. Transmission contractors and equipment suppliers should therefore benefit under both the “build more generation” and “move existing generation more efficiently” scenarios.

"The economy's doing great,"  they keep saying

So houses are cheap now, right?

Fuck no. The last time the economy was great, American houses went up 18.8% in a single year

And when rates get cut, the same thing happens again, because a rate cut is not a discount. It is a bidding war with more ammunition

Do the arithmetic yourself, it takes two minutes

Today: $410,700 house, 20% down, 6.66%. Principal and interest about $2,110 a month

Cut the rate to 5.66% and change nothing else. That same $2,110 now finances about $364,000 instead of $328,000

You did not get a cheaper house. You got $36,000 more borrowing power, and so did every other buyer in your city, on the same day, bidding on the same short supply

2021 is the receipt. Rates hit 2.65%, prices rose 18.8% in twelve months, houses sold in four days with inspections waived, and everyone who was "waiting for a better rate" was priced out permanently by the better rate

The rate is a payment discount. The price is an auction. Auctions eat discounts

So here is what you actually do, and this is the part nobody explains

BUY THE PRICE, RENT THE RATE. Price is permanent. A rate is a phone call in a future year. You cannot refinance a purchase price

MAKE THE SELLER BUY YOUR RATE DOWN INSTEAD OF CUTTING HIS PRICE. One point is 1% of the loan and buys roughly a quarter point off the rate. On a $328,000 loan that is $3,280 per point. A seller who will not drop $10,000 off his asking price will very often pay $10,000 in closing costs, because his listing price is his ego and the credit is invisible. Conventional loans allow seller concessions of 3% with less than 10% down and up to 6% with more, so ask for the maximum

ASK FOR A 2-1 BUYDOWN BY NAME. Seller funded, your rate drops 2% year one and 1% year two. On that loan it is about $420 a month back in your pocket in year one while you renovate

BUY IN THE FROZEN PART. Existing sales are running about 4.09 million a year, near multi decade lows. Nobody is showing up. I bought a house in Ohio for $61,000 last quarter that would have had six offers in 2021. It got none. I was the only person who called

Purchase $61,000, repairs $28,400, appraised $148,000, rents $1,275, payment $612

Everybody in the market is praying for the exact event that will take their house away from them

The boring part is the part where you buy

text:
In July 2026, Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) set a grim historic milestone: capturing over 51,000 human beings in a single month. Averaging more than 1,600 arrests every single day, the federal deportation machine has reached an unprecedented scale.

What the corporate press frames as a mere administrative "policy shift" is, in reality, a brutal domestic campaign. Fueled by bipartisan funding and corporate greed, the U.S. state apparatus is deploying military-grade surveillance, private concentration camps, and forced tracking devices against working-class communities.

Stripped of Legal Status, Shackled with Trackers
The human toll of this machine is clearest in towns like Springfield, Ohio, where hundreds of Haitian immigrant workers have been targeted following the Trump administration’s sudden revocation of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for over 300,000 Haitians on July 27.

These workers—who have lived, paid taxes, and raised families in the U.S. for years—were stripped of their legal right to work and drive virtually overnight. Under the guise of routine "check-ins," DHS issued summonses ordering workers to report to ICE field offices. Upon arrival, hundreds were fitted with GPS ankle monitors and placed under effective house arrest, forbidden from traveling more than 75 miles from their homes.

Imperial Hypocrisy on Display
The ideological justification for revoking TPS relies on a staggering contradiction:

The U.S. State Department maintains a "Level 4: Do Not Travel" advisory for Haiti due to armed gang warfare, political collapse, and extreme violence, barring American citizens from visiting.

Simultaneously, the administration claims Haiti is "safe enough" to deport over 300,000 workers back into that exact warzone.

This isn't an oversight—it is the raw logic of national origin discrimination. It punishes victims of decades of U.S. imperial intervention in Haiti while treating human beings as disposable labor to be extracted and discarded at will.

A Expanding Dragnet: Airports, Workplaces, and Homes
The record-breaking 51,000 arrests in July were not achieved through standard law enforcement procedures; they were carried out through aggressive surveillance and dragnet tactics across everyday public spaces.

Airport Raids: TSA data is now fed directly to ICE to track and seize travelers at security checkpoints, capturing between 20 and 40 people daily at U.S. airports.

Unmarked Patrols: Masked agents in unmarked vehicles conduct aggressive traffic stops, grabbing workers outside their homes and workplaces.

Administrative Traps: Routine immigration check-ins are weaponized. Immigrants who attend risk immediate arrest or shackling; those who miss them are branded as fugitives.

Nearly 68,000 immigrants are currently caged across the country—the majority inside overcrowded facilities managed by private prison corporations like GEO Group, generating millions in profit off human suffering.

Neglect, Torture, and Death Behind Bars
Inside these private detention centers, basic human rights are nonexistent. Since January 2025, an immigrant worker has died in ICE custody approximately every 10 days—a mortality rate nearly four times higher than in recent years.

The Death of Edwin Jeovanny López Cornejo
In early August, 43-year-old Edwin Jeovanny López Cornejo, a Salvadoran worker and father who had lived in the U.S. for 20 years, died inside New Jersey’s privately operated Delaney Hall detention center. Seized outside his home on his way to work despite holding a valid work permit, Edwin was imprisoned for six weeks.

Despite suffering from severe chronic medical conditions, his family's pleas for adequate treatment were ignored. After collapsing inside his cell, he died at a local hospital. ICE did not even bother to inform his family; hospital staff had to make the call. His story is far from unique: over 88% of those held at Delaney Hall have zero criminal record.

State Sanctioned Violence: Worms and Force-Feeding
Contaminated Water: At the Adelanto ICE Processing Center in California, detained workers released footage showing live, worm-like organisms swimming in their limited drinking water supply, leading to widespread stomach illnesses.

Judicial Torture: When prisoners launch hunger strikes to protest dirty water, medical neglect, and indefinite detention, federal courts routinely grant emergency orders authorizing involuntary force-feeding—a painful procedure involving nasal tubes widely recognized by international bodies as physical torture.

Why the Political Class Won't Save Us
While Democratic politicians occasionally offer performative critiques of Trump's rhetoric, the infrastructure driving this repression is thoroughly bipartisan.

When state police were deployed in New Jersey to crush protests outside Delaney Hall, it was ordered by Democratic leadership. The political establishment does not oppose the border regime—they manage it. The machinery of deportations, border militarization, and private caging receives multi-billion-dollar bipartisan budget increases year after year.
