DETAILED SUMMARY
THE "SYNODAL CHURCH" IS NOT THE CATHOLIC CHURCH 

00:04 MODERNISM’S PATH TO THE DESTRUCTION OF ALL TRUE RELIGION AND ITS FULL BLOOM IN THE SYNODAL CHURCH

Fr. Jenkins begins by recalling the teaching of St. Pius X that modernism leads inevitably to the destruction of all that is religion, of all true religion, and ultimately to a kind of pantheism. He observes that this process is no longer theoretical or distant. It is happening openly before our eyes as modernism reaches full bloom in the synodal church associated with Leo and Francis. In that entity, all religions are effectively being canonized.  

He turns immediately to the concrete document that embodies this development: the final document on synodality. It was approved by the bishops of the Novus Ordo in synod on 26 October 2024 and presented to Francis. Francis approved it and declared it magisterial, making it part of the ordinary magisterium of the synodal church as of 24 November 2024. The document therefore functions as a magisterial decree. It sets the stage for the systematic development and implementation of its ideas throughout the synodal structure.  

Fr. Jenkins compares the text to works such as Mein Kampf or Das Kapital. It sits on the shelf. Very few people have actually read it, largely because it is almost impenetrable. Yet whether people read it or not is secondary. What matters is that those charged with its execution now simply implement it according to the instructions they receive, turning the blueprint of synodality into lived reality.

01:48 THE SYNODAL CHURCH IS NOT THE CATHOLIC CHURCH BUT THE ANTI-CATHOLIC CHURCH PAR EXCELLENCE

Fr. Jenkins states the central thesis without qualification or softening. The synodal church of Leo and Francis is not the Catholic Church. In fact, the whole of Vatican II was directed toward founding the synodal church, building upon the synodal structures first created under Paul VI. The Catholic Church is not the synodal church, and the synodal church is not the Catholic Church.  

More precisely, the synodal church is the anti-Catholic Church. Many anti-Catholic movements exist in the world, yet this one occupies a unique and especially dangerous position. It attacks the very root of the virtue of faith in the soul. That is why St. Pius X declared modernism the most dangerous enemy the Church has ever faced: it does not merely contradict particular doctrines; it destroys the very idea and concept of faith itself.  

Consequently, Fr. Jenkins describes the current project as the anti-Catholic faith carried to the extreme. This is what is being constructed in Rome at the present moment. Even while those who desire the traditional faith are being excommunicated, all other religions are exalted. The final document itself speaks of building what it calls the “Church of Churches.”  

03:09 THE FINAL DOCUMENT AS A FORENSIC CRIME SCENE AND THE FALSIFICATION OF CHRIST

Scott observes that the phrase “Church of Churches” appears in the final document. Fr. Jenkins confirms that the intention is precisely to construct such a multi-religious entity. Scott then mentions a recent article reporting that the Vatican is inviting representatives of other religions to participate in synods and offer input. Fr. Jenkins replies that this direction was already contained in the final document itself.  

He explains that he had earlier read Francis’s 2015 text announcing the synodal church, but he had never actually read the final document on synodality until a few days before the conversation. He began reading it then and found it anything but a pleasant experience for a Catholic. For a Catholic the text is an atrocity. Reading it is comparable to examining a forensic crime scene—bloody, evil, and wicked. The document reveals an intentional effort to murder the faith and to murder the Church.  

en Christ Himself is targeted. The authors effectively place Him back in the tomb and fabricate a false Christ. Christ is falsified within the document; what emerges is an impostor Christ. Fr. Jenkins notes that he has progressed a little more than one-third of the way through the text. That portion is the most significant because it treats the theology and the spiritual foundation of the synodal church. The subsequent parts simply apply that foundational theology.  

05:03 THE ABSOLUTE CORRESPONDENCE BETWEEN SYNODALITY AND THE MODERNISM CONDEMNED IN PASCENDI

Fr. Jenkins draws a direct and total parallel. When one reads St. Pius X’s encyclical Pascendi Dominici Gregis of 8 September 1907, which condemns the errors of the modernists, one finds that the pope deals carefully with the theological and philosophical underpinnings of modernism. The correspondence between those underpinnings and the theology and philosophy of synodality is absolute.  

St. Pius X condemned modernism as the synthesis of all heresies and the most dangerous enemy the Church has ever faced. Synodality is simply modernism under a new name. Therefore the synodal church was already condemned by the Catholic Church during the reign of St. Pius X. He condemned it hook, line, and sinker—from beginning to end, in all of its principles and in all of its conclusions. He condemned it absolutely and in the most solemn and firm terms. No more penetrating or all-inclusive condemnation is possible.  

06:34 SYNODALITY AS THE STINKING DEATH-FLOWER OF MODERNISM IN FULL BLOOM

Anyone who recognizes that synodality is modernism sees it as the ultimate flower of that heresy. It is a stink-weed that required a hundred years to bloom. When the flower finally opens, it smells of death. It smells of rotting flesh. Fortunately such flowers do not endure for long.  

This is modernism. This is the flower of modernism, now bearing the name synodality. People are not obliged to face the reality if they prefer not to, yet anyone who truly wishes to understand what synodality is must grasp that it is modernism come to full bloom—and that it stands under the Church’s formal condemnation. There is no question about this.  

Those who continue to wring their hands and ask “What is synodality? We cannot figure it out” need only read Pascendi and the final document on synodality. Neither text is easy. Both are completely vacuous. As one reads the errors condemned by St. Pius X, clear understanding is progressively drained from the mind because the teachings are so bizarre. By the time one finishes absorbing modernist principles, nothing remains of the Catholic faith. That is precisely what St. Pius X warned against, and it is exactly what the synodality document achieves.  

08:24 THE PERSISTENT DISMISSAL OF MODERNISM DESPITE CLEAR CONDEMNATION

cott raises a pointed historical and contemporary question. If modernism is so dangerous, why has it been so easily dismissed by so many? St. Pius X was the first pope-saint in five hundred years—a great man, a great saint, and a great pope. He called modernism the synthesis of all heresies and the greatest enemy the Church has ever faced, already present in the very life-veins of the Church.  

Yet within only a couple of years after his death, much of his work was dismantled. The vigilance committees he established were done away with. The Oath against Modernism was eventually suppressed. Even good bishops, priests, and popes seemed to dismiss or “poo-poo” the danger. Contemporary Catholic books written by excellent priests of that era often treated modernism as merely another heresy in a long historical line that the Church had always overcome and would overcome again. The same dismissive attitude persists today among some who still possess the faith. Certain Catholic groups refuse even to use the word “modernism” or to call the error out by name.  

10:23 THE NECESSITY OF SAINTLY FAITH AND THE DECEPTIVE NATURE OF THE MODERNISTS

Fr. Jenkins answers that it takes the mind and the faith of a saint to feel the proper horror at heresy. Ordinary good will is not sufficient. After St. Pius X’s death in 1914, the horrors of the First World War absorbed the attention of the entire world from 1914 to 1918. In that distraction, modernists were able to consolidate their positions.  

Benedict XV replaced the staunch anti-modernist Cardinal Merry del Val with a less vigilant Secretary of State. Modernism continued its advance under Benedict XV, under Pius XI (despite that pope’s personal bravery against the Bolsheviks at the Miracle of the Vistula), and under Pius XII. St. Pius X had already warned that the modernists are bold and audacious. They change everything and recognize no sacred boundaries, yet they present themselves as innocent and pious.  

They possess what Fr. Jenkins calls “multiple personalities.” In one context they will deny a doctrine such as the Virgin Birth; in another they will appear to affirm it. They redefine terms so that the same words no longer carry the traditional Catholic meaning. Their conception of God mirrors the same disorder: a deity capable of contradictorily manifesting in every religion. Without the insight and grace of a saint, even well-intentioned people succumb to the pious exterior and fail to recognize the underlying destruction of the faith.  

17:27 THE DUTY TO EXPOSE THE NOVUS ORDO AND THE SYNODAL CHURCH OUT OF LOVE

The dialogue turns to the practical question of why so much time and effort are devoted to exposing the Novus Ordo and its synodal development. The answer is straightforward: the Novus Ordo is modernism triumphant. It is the worst enemy the Church has ever faced because it destroys the very concept of faith.  

The motive is not hatred or bitterness but love—love for Christ, love for the Church, and love for souls. Fr. Jenkins employs a vivid analogy. The situation is like a building already on fire, filled with the flames of error, heresy, blasphemy, and sacrilege. People inside are distracted or asleep. It would be criminal not to shout “Fire!”  

19:00 GENUINE CARE FOR THE MEMBERS OF THE SSPX AND THE CALL TO REJECT ALL COMPROMISE

Fr. Jenkins expresses genuine concern for members of the Society of St. Pius X, many of whom have nowhere else to go and whose families are divided. He has friends among its priests. Loyalty to Archbishop Lefebvre’s original intention—to preserve tradition without compromise—remains essential.  

The SSPX should not seek reinstatement in the synodal “Church of Churches.” Any threatened excommunication should be met with a clear declaration that the synodal entity is not the Catholic Church but the modernism already condemned by St. Pius X, an enemy that seeks to eradicate traditional faith and worship. Confrontation, not negotiation, is required.

26:39 THE PARALLEL WITH POLITICAL COWARDICE AND THE CLEAR CHOICE

The same pattern of avoidance appears in politics—in Congress, Britain, and Germany—where few will stand up and say certain policies are simply wrong. Traditional Catholics face the same temptation.  

The same pattern of avoidance appears in politics—in Congress, Britain, and Germany—where few will stand up and say certain policies are simply wrong. Traditional Catholics face the same temptation.  

29:00 MODERNISM AS THE GREAT APOSTASY

The discussion closes by linking modernism to the Great Apostasy. In his first encyclical of 1903 St. Pius X already feared “times of great apostasy” both in the world and inside the Church. Modernism is the definition of that apostasy: the denial of all the truths of the faith.  

The true Catholic Church cannot be overcome by the gates of hell (Matthew 16:18). The present synodal entity has been overcome by hell and therefore cannot be the Catholic Church. Actual popes must be Catholic; the current leader of the counterfeit cannot be an actual Vicar of Christ. Listeners are urged to contemplate these realities, study the relevant texts, and hold fast to the traditional faith without compromise.

text:
I moved to Manchester thinking life in the UK would be all work and no fun.

Surprisingly, it turned out to be the little things that made me happiest.

Every Saturday morning, I’d walk to the local bakery, grab a hot sausage roll and a coffee, then head to the park. People would be walking their dogs, kids would be playing football, and older couples would be feeding the ducks. Nobody seemed to be in a rush.

A few months after moving in, my next door neighbor, Emma, invited me over for a barbecue in her garden. I barely knew anyone on the street, but by the end of the evening, I had met almost all of my neighbors. We laughed, shared food, and talked about everything from football to travel.

One Sunday, my car wouldn’t start. Before I could even think about calling for help, my neighbor across the road came outside with jumper cables.

He smiled and said, “Happens to all of us.”

Ten minutes later, my car was running again.

I offered him £20 for helping me, but he refused.

He said, “Just help someone else when they need it.”

That simple moment stayed with me.

Life in the UK wasn’t about doing something exciting every day. It was the routine that made it special, morning walks, friendly chats with neighbors, weekends in the park, fish and chips on a Friday night, and knowing there were people around who genuinely looked out for each other.

It made me realize that happiness doesn’t always come from earning more money or chasing bigger dreams.

Sometimes, it comes from living in a place where ordinary days feel peaceful, and where simple acts of kindness become part of everyday life.

text:
Mule deer are already using California’s first wildlife overpass, even before construction is complete.

Just 15 hours after crews left the site for the day, cameras recorded three mule deer walking across the new bridge over U.S. 97 in Siskiyou County, near the Oregon border.

These animals became the first officially documented users of California’s first overcrossing built by Caltrans specifically to reconnect wildlife habitat divided by a state highway.

A bobcat and other species have also been observed on the structure while workers finish the surrounding fencing and remaining details.

The bridge measures roughly 100 feet long and 140 feet wide (30 by 43 meters). It spans one of Northern California’s most hazardous highway corridors for wildlife.

Between 2015 and 2020, more than 50 deer and 16 elk were killed near this location. Collisions with large animals also endanger drivers, especially at highway speeds.

The crossing offers a safer passage for mule deer, elk, black bears, mountain lions, gray wolves, and other wildlife traveling between habitats separated by the road.

The bridge itself forms only one component of a larger system.

Caltrans is installing approximately 2 miles (3.2 kilometers) of fencing that stands 8 feet (2.4 meters) high. This fencing directs animals toward the bridge and keeps them off the roadway. Special exits allow any animals that enter the highway corridor to leave safely.

A wildlife tunnel is also under construction nearby, providing an additional safe route beneath U.S. 97.

The project’s estimated construction cost is $15.1 million. Researchers from the UC Davis Road Ecology Center and Caltrans are monitoring the site with about 100 cameras to record which animals use the crossing and to guide improvements in future projects.

The deer’s quick appearance is an encouraging result. They required no guidance or training. As soon as a safer path became available, they used it.

text:
“The Murder 4 Hire- Gone Wrong”

In the winter of 1980, in the quiet Pittsburgh suburb of Upper St. Clair, a successful real estate executive named Gregory J. Holub found himself trapped in a bitter divorce. His marriage to Nancy Lee, his college sweetheart of more than two decades, had crumbled. They shared a large home on Williamsburg Circle, two teenage sons, and assets that would later be valued near a million dollars…art, antiques, real estate, rare coins, and more. Nancy had filed for divorce that summer. 

Gregory, a vice president for corporate planning at Merrill-Lynch Realty, decided the cleanest solution was not the courts.
That December he placed a discreet classified ad in The Pittsburgh Press. It read…. “Mercenary. Person or Service required in high risk….high reward situations.  Must be adventurous. Cool and systematic in applying unconventional solutions.” 

Fifty-one people answered. One of them was Walter Lion, a retiring Marine sergeant from nearby Coraopolis who thought the notice might lead to overseas pipeline work or something similarly adventurous.
Instead, the conversations turned dark. 

Over the phone Gregory offered ten thousand dollars for a single job….the killing of his wife. The murder, he explained, was to be the first in a possible series. It was scheduled for a precise hour between five and six o’clock on a Tuesday afternoon at the International Art Gallery in McMurray, where Nancy worked as a saleswoman. 

The date chosen was her forty-eighth birthday. He gave detailed instructions on how to do it and how to get away.
Lion went to the authorities. Investigators from the state attorney general’s office recorded the calls. When the tapes were played for Nancy, she recognized her husband’s voice without hesitation. 

In February 1981 Gregory was arrested and charged with solicitation, criminal attempt, and conspiracy to commit murder. A judge set bond at a quarter of a million dollars. Prosecutors noted that an investigation continued into whether anyone else had been involved in the scheme.

The criminal case moved slowly. In November 1981, Criminal Division Judge John W. O’Brien refused defense requests to dismiss the charges, rejecting arguments that newspaper coverage had blown the matter out of proportion. 

He also denied a bid to place Gregory in the Accelerated Rehabilitative Disposition program, which would have allowed a first offender to avoid a full trial and eventually clear the record. Trial was scheduled for early the following year on the charges of criminal attempt and solicitation to commit homicide.

Meanwhile the divorce proceedings, handled by Common Pleas Judge Gene Strassberger, froze every joint asset. Nancy found herself living on a monthly welfare check of a few hundred dollars inside a house that had once symbolized their prosperity. 

The home grew shabby; the legal battle seemed endless. She told reporters it was like a nightmare and that she would eventually repay the welfare money once the assets were released.

Gregory was eventually convicted on the solicitation charge and sentenced to five to ten years in prison.  A divorce decree followed in 1984, with the economic issues left to be sorted separately. The plot never reached the gallery floor.  Nancy survived. 

The newspaper ad that was meant to solve one man’s problems instead became the public record of how far he was willing to go, captured in wiretapped conversations and identified by the very voice of the woman he wanted silenced.​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​

text:
"The Catholic high school in Pittsburgh was two blocks from Forbes Field.
As soon as the last class was over, I was really excited about the Pirates and I just walked as quickly as I could over to Forbes Field."
Anthony Jerpe.
While fans at Forbes Field waited nervously for their Pirates to bat in the bottom of the ninth, Anthony Jerpe had to go home and help his family with dinner.
Anthony Jerpe took off through a side entrance and made his way around the back side of the outfield wall at Forbes Field.
He turned the corner near the left-field fence, strolling alongside some cherry trees, when he heard a loud sound and saw it:
A baseball soaring over his head. It landed right next to him.
Jerpe stood frozen at first, but then, seeing nobody else was nearby, ran over to get it.
"I picked it up and I thought:
"Well, somebody just hit a home run."
I didn't know whether it was Mickey Mantle or Yogi Berra or Clemente:
I had no idea.
The last person I thought in the world would do that was Bill Mazeroski."
Jerpe walked over to a cop who was standing by the Forbes Field left-field gate to see what had happened.
The eighth-grader suddenly began to realize this was very likely a momentous home run ball he'd found.
"There was this loud roar and I thought:
"Man, something good must've happened." Bill Mazeroski’s famous game-winning home run landed just a few feet away.
Jerpe picked it up and, as the area quickly swelled with delirious fans, he was rushed by team officials to the victorious Pirates’ clubhouse where he offered the ball to Mazeroski:
Who declined, saying the memories were enough.
"In the clubhouse there was so much hollering going on, but Maz said something back to me.
I think what Maz said was:
"It's OK, kid, you can keep it."
Jerpe hung onto the ball and kept it in his room until, next spring, when he and his friends needed a ball to play in a nearby field.
An errant hit took the Mazeroski ball into a side area full of tall grass and weeds;
After a frantic one-hour search, the kids never found the ball.
It's estimated that had Anthony Jerpe held onto the precious memento for 50-plus years, he could had sold it for up to a million dollars."
"Bill Mazeroski"

text:
While nuclear families are increasingly common, large joint family households sharing a single kitchen remain a traditional norm.

Under the 1854 Muluki Ain (the national legal code), Magars were categorized as Namasinya Matwali which is "Non-enslavable Alcohol-Drinkers", a middle-tier rank shared with the Gurungs, positioned below the "twice-born" Tagadhari but above enslavable groups.

Magars occupied a "doubtful order" in the hierarchy, below Kshatriya status and denied the sacred thread, yet considered superior to Vaisya or Sudra.

Despite not wearing the sacred thread, Magars are served by Brahmin priests, and higher "twice-born" will accept water from Magar hands, reflecting a status one source explicitly frames as "pani chalne jat" ("castes from whom water is accepted, but not rice"), i.e., functionally respected but formally subordinate.

Dominant Magar clans, such as Thapa, Rana, Bhujel, and Budathoki have historically pursued Sanskritization, adopting Brahmanical dietary restrictions and employing Brahmin priests to gain elevated status while some Rana-descended and other elite Magars were historically absorbed into Thakuri or "honorary Chhetri" status.

To gain exemption from two customary state prerogatives, aputali (the state's right to escheat/confiscate property when there is no heir) and fines for adultery (chak-chakui), Magars were required to pay a special tax called the Salami levy, assessed by household classification.

For Magars of the Barhapanthi and Atharapanthi sub-groups, this levy was collected at half rates, since only the aputali obligation (not chak-chakui) was remitted for them.

Like other hill communities, Magars traditionally practiced sino-eating, consuming the flesh of cattle that had died of natural causes. 

In 1810, the state offered to remit associated fines if Magars agreed to revere Brahmans and supply hides to the government munitions factory (Megjin).

text:
Arsenal signing £75m Bruno Guimaraes transfer will make Mikel Arteta's side unstoppable.

The Gunners' Premier League rivals should fear the worst. Fresh from their long-awaited Premier League title win, an £75m deal for the Newcastle skipper promises to be transformative for an Arsenal side who already have the opportunity to build a dynasty next season.

It's been one of the summer's most protracted transfer sagas, but there is now an air of inevitability about Arsenal completing a sensational swoop for Newcastle's talismanic captain, Bruno Guimaraes.

After one rejected bid and a lot of smoke and mirrors, the Gunners are finally closing in on a deal worth £75 million ($101m) for the 28-year-old Brazil international midfielder, who wants to make the move despite the Magpies' reluctance to sell.

Not only will this be a transformative transfer for Arsenal, but it promises to have significant consequences for the rest of the Premier League as Mikel Arteta looks to build an era of dominance in north London.

Should Arsenal get the Bruno deal done, as anticipated, then you would be hard pressed to find a more balanced midfield in the whole of Europe.

Even individually, Guimaraes is one of the finest central midfielders on the planet. Not only does the Brazilian run tirelessly and bite into tackles, but he also has the composure and vision to pick out a pass in the final third, and the shooting ability and attacking nous to find the back of the net - reflected in his 15 goal contributions in the Premier League alone last season, the most productive of his career to date.

Bruno's importance to Newcastle is underlined by the fact that the Magpies have won just two of the 16 matches he has missed since arriving from Lyon in January 2022. Their 1.8 points per game ratio with him in the team falls to 0.7 without him, per Opta.

The 28-year-old was at his creative best for Brazil at the World Cup this summer, where he was arguably the Selecao's most important player alongside fellow Arsenal target Vinicius Jr, racking up four assists in four games before Carlo Ancelotti's side was dumped out in the last 16. Only France dynamo Michael Olise registered more.

Crucially, he is another on-pitch, Premier League-proven leader for the Gunners, too, bringing plenty of experience and know-how to what is still a relatively young squad as he enters his peak years.

When you combine Bruno's all-round capabilities with the running and defensive work of Declan Rice, and the guile and creativity of Martin Odegaard or Eberechi Eze, then Arsenal's new-look midfield becomes an incredibly daunting prospect for any opponent.

It's likely that Guimaraes will slot in alongside Rice and behind Odegaard as a box-to-box No.8, adding a fresh dimension to what is already a formidable midfield unit, pushing higher than the likes of Martin Zubimendi or Myles Lewis-Skelly would.

While he should offer plenty going forward, the Brazilian actually outperformed Arsenal's existing options in a variety of defensive metrics last season; he won more individual duels per 90 than any of Arsenal's current central midfielders (6.1), and he also won more tackles per 90 (1.6). In terms of recoveries, only Rice (5.2 to his 5.0) made more, per Opta.

We shouldn't forget the Gunners' strength in depth, either, with the likes of Zubimendi, Lewis-Skelly, Mikel Merino and wonderkid Max Dowman to come off the bench. This is a squad that is set up to challenge on multiple fronts once again.

Arsenal boss Arteta has been open about wanting to take a squad that can already call themselves Premier League champions to an even higher plane, which is certainly reflected in the serious pursuits of both Guimaraes and his compatriot Vini Jr.

Speaking in an in-house club interview last week, the Spanish tactician said: "A lot is happening. We all know about the context of this transfer window. From ownership to the board, the sporting director, myself, we know that we want to take this club to a different level.

"That is going to require a better squad, better individuals. We have identified where we have opportunities to grow and to improve and to evolve our game and what is going to be needed to achieve that. Hopefully very soon we can start to put things in a very concrete way."

Arteta expanded on that point in his press conference following the friendly victory over Girona. "We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see it. The transfer market and our opponents, what we are doing, we won't sit still. And we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

Asked why he was so keen to strengthen, the former midfielder added: "Because the margins are very small. And because we want to get better and the level is going to increase, we need to increase the competition internally. We need to make sure we identify the things that we don't have in the team, to have bigger margins. And that's the way we have to think."

According to The Athletic, the north Londoners believe that even being at the table for a player of Vinicius' calibre is a marker of their progress.

Arsenal's stability already gave them an edge over their Premier League rivals next season, and Bruno could be the addition that helps them pull away

text:
The Story of Sudāmā and Sri Krishna
A poor devotee, who was made the richest in the whole town by Sri Krishna.

In the city of Dwārakā, Lord Kṛṣṇa lived in royal splendour as the king of the Yadus. Among His childhood friends from the gurukula of Sage Sāndīpani was a poor Brahmin named Sudāmā (also called Kucela). Sudāmā was a man of pure heart, learned in the Vedas, and completely devoted to Kṛṣṇa, yet he lived in extreme poverty. His clothes were torn, his house was broken, and he and his wife often went hungry.

One day Sudāmā’s wife, unable to bear their children’s hunger any longer, gently requested him to go and meet his old friend Kṛṣṇa. She said, “He is the Supreme Lord Himself, and He loves you. If you simply go to see Him, He will surely help us.”

Sudāmā felt shy about asking for anything, but he agreed to go just to have the darśana of his beloved friend. His wife managed to collect a small quantity of flattened rice (poha / aval) by begging and tied it in a piece of cloth as a humble gift for Kṛṣṇa.

The Meeting
Sudāmā walked all the way to Dwārakā. When the palace guards saw the poorly dressed Brahmin, they hesitated, but Kṛṣṇa, who was seated with Queen Rukmiṇī, immediately rose and ran barefoot to receive him. Sri Krishna embraced Sudāmā with great love, seated him on His own throne, and personally washed his feet. Rukmiṇī fanned him and served him like a servant.

Kṛṣṇa laughed and talked with Sudāmā about their childhood days in the gurukula, recalling how they had once gone to collect firewood and been caught in the rain. Sudāmā felt completely at home, yet he was too embarrassed to mention his poverty or to offer the small packet of flattened rice. Kṛṣṇa, who knows the heart of every being, snatched the packet Himself, opened it with delight, and ate a handful of the humble offering with great pleasure. He was about to take more when Rukmiṇī gently stopped Him, saying that with one handful He had already given Sudāmā more wealth than he could ever need.

The Transformation
Sudāmā spent the night in the palace in a state of pure bliss, still not asking for anything. The next morning he took leave and began walking home, feeling that the darśana of Kṛṣṇa was itself the greatest gift. He wondered what he would tell his wife.

When he reached the place where his broken hut had stood, he stopped in astonishment. In its place stood a magnificent palace, lavish mansion filled with riches and his wife came out dressed like a queen, surrounded by attendants. By the grace of the small offering of flattened rice accepted by the Lord, Sudāmā had been given Massive wealth.

Yet Sudāmā remained completely unchanged in heart. He and his wife used their new prosperity in the service of the Lord and of others. They continued to live with the same humility and devotion, understanding that the real gift was not the wealth but the loving friendship of Kṛṣṇa.

The Teaching
This story shows the intimate, personal love of Lord Viṣṇu (Kṛṣṇa) for His pure devotee. The Lord does not look at the material value of an offering — He looks at the love with which it is given. A handful of flattened rice offered with devotion brought the highest prosperity, yet the greatest treasure was the Lord Krishna’s loving embrace and remembrance.

text:
SDSU leads international research collaboration to broaden understanding of sex workers' health

San Diego State University led an international collaboration published in The Lancet Public Health, one of the world's leading public health journals, that offers the most comprehensive synthesis of evidence on sex workers' health in more than a decade.

Published July 24, the four-paper series brings together two years of research and collaboration among SDSU, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, the Global Network of Sex Work Projects (NSWP) and sex workers from diverse geographic settings. Together, the partners developed a body of evidence to inform future research, policy and practice while advancing health equity.

The collection expands how researchers understand sex workers' health by examining not only HIV and sexually transmitted infections, but also mental health, reproductive health, violence, stigma, discrimination, workplace safety, access to healthcare and the broader social conditions and structural determinants such as laws and policies that can influence health. 

“This landmark international collaboration demonstrates the power of research to reshape an entire field,” said Amy Bonomi, dean of SDSU's College of Health and Human Services. “By challenging conventional approaches to understanding health among sex workers, Dr. Goldenberg and her colleagues have created a framework that will influence future research, inform policy, and strengthen public health practice around the world to improve the health and lives of sex workers.”

Led by Shira Goldenberg, associate professor in the Division of Epidemiology and Biostatistics in the School of Public Health and co-director of the SDSU/UCSD Joint Doctoral Program in Public Health, the project represents a sustained international effort to better understand the factors that shape the health and well-being of sex workers around the world. A defining feature of the work was its partnership with NSWP, an advocacy group for the rights of female, male, and transgender sex workers with member organizations in five continents.

FILM STUDY THESIS

Josephine Pinnock enters this evaluation as an ascending Northeast guard with the size, handle, and cognitive profile to manage meaningful offensive responsibility. Her value is rooted less in recruitment momentum and more in her ability to create advantages, operate through ball-screen actions, and solve possessions with the ball.

Pinnock functions most naturally as a lead or combo initiator. She changes pace, manipulates defensive angles, and maintains vision when pressure compresses the floor. Her 5’11” frame allows her to see over smaller defenders, while her handle gives her access to the middle of the floor and secondary passing windows. She projects as more than a connective guard because she can initiate actions rather than simply extend advantages created by others.

The upward trend in Pinnock’s evaluation comes from increasing role clarity. Her film suggests a guard becoming more comfortable organizing offense, making early reads, and controlling possession tempo. The most portable traits are her pick-and-roll feel, read-and-react processing, positional size, and ability to create for teammates without relying entirely on athletic separation.

The next analytical layer is production verification. Shooting efficiency, assist-to-turnover performance, usage, and scoring durability remain unresolved. Those variables will determine whether her current creation profile translates into dependable primary-guard production or settles into a secondary initiator role.

Defensively, Pinnock’s size supports credible multi-matchup value. Her defensive value is tied to awareness and positioning as much as physical tools.

Positive Direction provides her independent-club environment rather than a shoe-circuit designation. That context places greater weight on direct film evaluation and performance against identifiable competition.

Pinnock holds multiple Division I offers, with Syracuse and Stony Brook representing the latest additions to her recruitment. Those offers confirm increasing market recognition but do not independently establish projection level.

THE BEECHUM VERDICT

Pinnock’s evaluation is moving upward because her primary traits have clear collegiate utility. She currently projects as a mid-major-caliber initiator with Power Four upside. Shooting efficiency, turnover control, and sustained production under pressure remain the decisive evaluation variables.

text:
Per request, I’m sharing my thoughts on this week’s Torah portion today so people don’t miss it. I’ll be sharing it again tomorrow before Shabbat. 🙏 

This week, we read the profound Torah portion of Re’eh, which literally means “See.”

The portion begins:

“See, this day I set before you blessing and curse: blessing, if you obey the commandments of the ETERNAL your God that I enjoin upon you this day; and curse, if you do not obey the commandments of the ETERNAL your God, but turn away from the path that I enjoin upon you this day and follow other gods, whom you have not experienced.”

This is the source for the concept of free choice.

God created the world with free choice. He presented us with the user guide for life, the Torah, but it is in our hands whether to follow it or not.

That is the literal explanation of those few verses.

However, enough literature has been written about these verses that there could be entire books devoted just to those first few words.

Let’s examine some of those ideas.

Let’s start with the very first word: Re’eh.

The word is written in the singular form. “You (an individual) should see…”

But then, strangely, the verse continues in the plural: “…I set before you (in the plural) blessing and curse…”

That is strangely inconsistent. Why start by speaking to the individual and then continue by speaking to the collective?

This is a question that pretty much all the commentators on the Torah ask, and everyone offers their own unique answers.

One answer that deeply resonated with me is that when you, as an individual, choose to behave morally, your words and actions can impact the collective.

We often think, “I am just one person. I can’t really make a difference.”

The Torah, and specifically this first verse—and even more specifically, that first word, “Re’eh”—teaches us that one person, when choosing the right path, has the potential to affect many, and even the world.

All major events throughout history started with one person.  

Another interpretation of that first verse comes to answer the question: What exactly is the Torah referring to when it says it can be a blessing or a curse?

One answer is the word “Anochi,” which means “I.”

The idea is that the sense of self can be a blessing or a curse.

If you have no self-confidence at all, it’s a curse. If you have too much ego, it’s also a curse. But if you have self-awareness and belief in yourself, that is the greatest blessing.

So what exactly is the blessing or the curse? The word Anochi—the sense of self.

Another idea that I thought of can also be an answer to that same question.

Where else do we see the word Anochi? The answer is, of course, the Ten Commandments. They begin with that word.

“Anochi Hashem Elokecha” — “I am your God.”

So what can be a blessing or a curse? Faith in God, and what you do with it.

If you use that faith to lead a moral and ethical life, if you spread God’s word and teach His Torah, then your faith is a blessing.

If, however, you use your religiosity to judge others and put them down, if you use your observance to act holier than thou and insult others, then you are misusing the Anochi, and it becomes a curse.

That’s my interpretation.

Moving on…

Yet another interpretation of what God is talking about when He says it can be a blessing or a curse is a different word in that same verse: Hayom, which means “today.”

The obvious question is why that word appears in the verse at all.

“See, this day I set before you blessing and curse…”

What does the word “today” add here? It could have simply said, “I set before you blessing and curse.”

So what does the word “today” teach us?

The answer is that the idea of the present—the here and now—can be either a blessing or a curse.

If you have the mindset of living in the present and that motivates you to take advantage of every moment, if it makes you more present, then it’s a blessing.

But if your whole life is guided by the letters YOLO—“You Only Live Once”—and that mindset leads you to a life of extravagance, a life lacking morality or meaning, then the idea of “today” becomes a curse.

Another word to pay attention to in that first verse is Noten, which means “to give.”

“See, this day I give you blessing and curse…”

Why is it in the present tense? God gave us the Torah and its commandments in the past. Why is the verse written in the present?

Because the choice of following the right path, which leads to blessing, or choosing the wrong path, which leads to curse, is not a choice we made only in the past.

It is a choice we make every day of our lives. It is a choice in the present, not the past.

What we’ve done in the past is in the past. Every day we choose our path, and it is never too late to recalculate the path we choose. That’s why it’s written in the present tense—because it’s a choice we make every single day.

And on that note, let’s move on from that first verse. I’d just like to point out that everything we’ve learned so far came from that one verse. That’s how rich the Torah is.

A few verses later, the Torah says:

“…if you do not obey the commandments of the ETERNAL your God, but turn away from the path that I enjoin upon you this day and follow other gods, whom you have not experienced.”

In other words, the Torah is saying, “If you leave God’s path, you will worship other gods.”

The obvious question is: Really?

If I am not an observant Jew, does that automatically mean that I will worship other gods?

Aren’t there millions of non-observant Jews? Do they worship other gods?

The answer is profound.

The verse is not meant to be taken literally—that if you don’t follow the Torah, you will literally end up worshipping other gods.

What it means is that, as human beings, we all have a need for spirituality. If that need is not filled with God, we will fill it in other ways.

We absolutely see this clearly today.

Those who live unholy lives become “activists” for some movement or some new fad.

As humans, we crave purpose and meaning, and if you don’t get that purpose from holiness and from letting God into your life, you will almost certainly end up with something else that replaces religion.

Today, there are countless examples of this phenomenon, and due to the risk of insulting someone, I won’t name them all—but I will mention two obvious examples.

The pro-Palestine movement. It’s become a religion for millions around the world. These are morally bankrupt people who lack true meaning, so they fill that void with this ideology.

The same is true for BDS, BLM, and so many other modern-day religions that have captured the hearts and minds of millions of young people across the West.

If, the Torah teaches us, we don’t make room for God in our lives, that vacuum will be filled with something far less holy.

Later on in the portion, there is a strange verse that says:

“…but look only to the site that the ETERNAL your God will choose amidst all your tribes as God’s habitation, to establish the divine name there. There you are to go…”

The verse is, of course, referring to the Temple in Jerusalem. It’s telling us to go there to worship God. What’s strange is that it doesn’t specify the place.

It tells us to go to the site, to the place, but it doesn’t say what that place is.

Why?

The answer is in the last few words of that verse:

“Leshichno Tidreshu Uvata Shama,” which literally means, “You shall seek out His presence, and there you shall come.”

What that means is that the Torah doesn’t specify the place because, if you want God in your life—if you want to find and connect to God—you must seek Him out.

What’s the place where you’ll find God? Anywhere you sincerely seek Him.

If your heart is open to God, He will show up for you. If your heart is closed to God, you’ll never find Him.

It doesn’t specify the place because that is up to you and how much you seek God in your life.

The last two words also speak volumes.

“Uvata Shama” — “There you shall come.”

Why doesn’t it say, “There you shall go”?

The answer is that God is not telling you to go somewhere to find Him. He is telling you that He is awaiting your arrival. He is waiting for you to seek Him out. He is welcoming you to come to Him, not to go somewhere else.

That is why another verse in the Prophets says, “Shuvu Elai Veashuva Aleichem.” God promises us, “Return to Me, and I will return to you.”

If you take that first step and seek out God, He will welcome you with open arms.

And finally, one last beautiful thought I read.

A verse later in the portion says:

“You are children of the ETERNAL your God. You shall not ‘Titgodedu.’”

That last word is explained as meaning that we, the Jewish people, should not be divided into hostile factions, but rather remain one people.

That makes sense, but what doesn’t make sense is the connection between the beginning of the verse and the end.

“You are God’s children. Don’t make sects.”

What is the connection?

Furthermore, don’t we already have different groups? Don’t we have Ashkenazi Jews and Sephardic Jews? Don’t we have Hasidic Jews and more modern Jews?

So how do we reconcile that?

The answer is that so long as we know we are God’s children, it is perfectly legitimate to have different types of Jews.

Like a parent and his or her children, every child has a unique personality and different strengths. So long as they are part of the same family, and that family is what unites them, it is okay for each child to have their own traits.

God is saying here: “As long as you know that you are My children, it’s okay to have different types of Jews. But if you don’t realize that you are My children, then there is a prohibition against creating sects.”

That is the connection between the two parts of the verse.

I know I’ve shared this analogy multiple times, but it deeply resonates with me, and it is especially relevant here.

Like a coloring book, you have to color within the lines. But within those lines, you can express yourself however you want.

The same is true for our relationship with God. So long as we know He is our Father, so long as we know the Torah is here for all of us, and so long as we live within that framework, we can make Torah our own and color it with whatever colors we choose.

Shabbat Shalom.

text:
1. The Sufficiency and Divine Efficacy of the Written Word of God (Sola Scriptura)

Holy Scripture is the supreme, perfect, and clear norm of faith and life, immediately divinely inspired (theopneustos) by the Holy Spirit. It does not require unwritten traditions, the consensus of the Fathers, or the magisterial judgment of the Pope to possess divine authority or to generate saving faith (You too would agree that it is, at baseline, the Holy Infallible Word of God).

Because God is the primary author of the sacred letters, Scripture is autopiston (self-authenticating). It possesses an innate, supernatural power to enlighten the eyes, convert the soul, and convince the human conscience immediately, working through the Holy Spirit. The scriptures themselves teach their own clarity and sufficiency:

Psalm 119:105: "Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path."

2 Timothy 3:15-17: The sacred letters "are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus" so that "the man of God may be perfect, thoroughly furnished unto all good works."

Isaiah 8:20: "To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them."

Divine faith does not rest on the human authority of any church or bishop, but is generated supernaturally by the Holy Spirit through the Word itself. Therefore, Holy Scripture is the canonical, normal, and directive judge to which all human teachers, councils, and decrees must be subjected and by which they must be measured.

2. The Headship of Christ

The Roman Papacy claims an absolute, unchecked monarchical power over the universal Church, declaring the Roman Pontiff to be the visible head and ecumenical vicar of Jesus Christ on earth. Under this theological framework, there are absolutely no checks on his authority. The Pope is asserted to be an infallible judge whose sentence can be retracted by no one, while he alone can retract the sentences of all, and he is to be judged by no mortal. This absolute power effectively treats the Pope as if he is the Church, claiming the authority to establish laws that bind the conscience, to formulate new dogmas, to change the substantials of the sacraments, and to institute new forms of worship.

By claiming to be the visible, universal head of the Church, the Papacy literally usurps the unique, untransferable headship of Jesus Christ. The Church is a mystical body that can have only one Head, Husband, and Foundation. If there were another head besides Christ, the Church would be two-headed, and would be said to be the body of another than Christ.

No body can have multiple heads of the same order and respect without monstrosity. The true head of the Church must be perpetually present, bestowing life, motion, and spiritual sense upon its members. One mere mortal man cannot perform these functions for the universal Church diffused throughout the world. Furthermore, Christ explicitly prohibited such monarchical domination among His ministers:

"The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them, but you shall not be so." (Luke 22:25–26)

Likewise, Saint Peter himself forbids pastors to lord it 
over those entrusted to them:

"...neither as being lords over God's heritage, but being examples to the flock." (1 Peter 5:3)

Yet, the entire reality of the Church is restricted into a single office of the Roman Pontiff. The Pope is made the sole, living, and infallible organ of the Holy Spirit. Holy Scripture is not the word of God without the exposition of the Pope. Traditions are not divine without the determination of the Pope. The Church is not infallible without the direction of the Pope. Councils are mere conventicles without the confirmation of the Pope. The Fathers are not Fathers without the reception of the Pope. The consensus of the faithful is not valid without the consent of the Pope. Right reason in the articles of faith is not right without the consent of the Pope. Therefore, none of these are worth anything. The Pope alone is all things; with him excluded, all things are fallible. You see that in every contest, it must finally come to the judgment of the Pope, so that he alone may be wise, and the rest may flutter about like shadows. Meaning, there is no objective standard left by which the Pope's teachings can be measured or corrected. If Scripture itself derives its canonical authority as far as we are concerned from the Pope’s determination, the written Word of God cannot be used to check him. The Pope has effectively locked himself in a chamber of absolute, self-authenticating power.

This absolute, unchecked, and self-deifying power is the precise definition of the Antichrist prophesied in 2 Thessalonians 2:4, who "opposes and is raised above all that is called GOD, or that is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of GOD, showing himself as if he were GOD". For he sits, and shows himself as if he were God, by arrogating to himself divine power, or supreme and monarchical power over the entire church, the power of making laws by which the consciences of Christians throughout the entire church are bound. His ability to unilaterally remit sins, impose satisfactions, make new articles of faith, and depose secular rulers is a direct usurpation of the prerogatives belonging to God alone.

This unchecked elation is so manifestly contrary to the Gospel that even Gregory the Great warned that anyone who claimed such universal, unchecked authority over other bishops was the forerunner of the Antichrist:

"I confidently say because whoever calls himself universal priest, or desires to be called, runs before Antichrist in his elation."

3. Christ is the Sole, Present, Sufficient Head

The true Church of God does not need a visible, earthly monarch because Jesus Christ, the God-man, is its perpetual, living, and omnipresent Head. God the Father "gave him to be head over all things to the church, which is his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all" (Ephesians 1:22-23).

Christ promised His real, personal presence to His Church until the end of the age (Matthew 28:20). He is not an absent Lord who requires a deputy to rule in His stead. Just as a physical head is never separated from its body, Christ is perpetually joined to His members, directly bestowing spiritual life, salvation, and the gifts of the Holy Spirit upon them.

The Church, in its true and formal sense, is the spiritual assembly of those who truly believe and are sanctified by the Holy Spirit. Its proper, infallible, and sufficient marks are the pure preaching of the divine Word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments instituted by Christ. Wherever these marks are present, Christ Himself is present, ruling His Church through His Word and Spirit, and not through an earthly hierarchy of personal domination.

4. Sola Fide

A sinner is justified before God, absolved from sin, reconciled, and reputed as righteous, freely by His grace, solely on account of the vicarious satisfaction and merit of Jesus Christ. This righteousness is received through faith alone, without any confluence of human works, virtues, or preceding dispositions.

Scripture establishes this truth in the clearest terms:

Romans 3:28: "We conclude therefore that a man is justified by faith without the works of the law."

Romans 4:5: "But to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness."

Galatians 2:16: "Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but through faith in Jesus Christ..."

So constantly are these exclusive particles (such as without works, without the law, freely, by grace), it must be logically deduced to be by faith alone. For what else is it to be justified without the law, without works, not of the law, not of the works of the law, for faith to be imputed for justice without works, than to be justified by faith alone?

Faith does not justify through its own intrinsic dignity, value, or love, as if it were a work of our own. Rather, it justifies purely as a receptive instrument  that lays hold of the promise of grace and the perfect merit of Christ. Good works are not the cause or condition of justification, but are the necessary, inevitable fruits and consequences of a faith that is already justified.

5. Salvific Assurance

Lutheranism asserts that a Christian can and ought to be entirely certain of their present state of grace and justification with an infallible, divine certainty of faith.

This certainty does not rest upon an introspective examination of one's own works, moral worthiness, or transient emotional states, which would indeed render salvation conjectural and unstable, but rather upon the objective, immutable promise of God in Christ Jesus

As Martin Luther says:

"If we doubt that we are in grace, that we please God on account of Christ, we deny that Christ redeemed us, we simply deny all his benefits... For he who doubts concerning the grace of God toward him, must necessarily also doubt concerning the divine promises, and by consequence concerning the will of God..."

6. Real Sacramental Presence Without Rationalism

The true substantial body and blood of Jesus Christ are really, substantially, and orally present "in, with, and under" the consecrated bread and wine, received by both the worthy and the unworthy. The bread remains bread, and the wine remains wine, yet they are sacramentally united to the true body and blood of Christ. We also hold that the primary purpose is that of what Christ said "For the forgiveness of sins". A point unfortunately anathematized by Trent.

7. Genuine Catholicity and Historical Continuity

I know you might ask, "Where was your church before Luther?" But we say: The Lutheran Church is not a new sect, but the genuine continuation of the ancient, apostolic, and truly Catholic Church, cleansed of medieval abuses and errors.

I've been seeing your posts for a long time, so I know you care about not throwing away 2,000 years of Church History for a 16th-century reformation. However, the Lutheran Church specifically was a conservative reformation. We did not seek to overthrow the Church, but simply to restore it to purity. We retain the historic Western Mass (the Kyrie, Gloria, Credo, Sanctus, and Agnus Dei), the historic lectionary, the liturgical year, crucifixes, vestments, and sacred music. We did not reduce the Sacraments to mere symbols. We hold strictly to Christ's words: "This IS my Body." "This IS my Blood." We even retain the historic practice of private confession and holy absolution.

Consider this as well: In the fourth century, during the height of the Arian struggle, the true Christians who defended the divinity of Christ were labeled "Homoousians" by their opponents. Is one therefore able to conclude that the teaching of the homoousia (that the Son is of the same substance as the Father) was not previously known, believed, or confessed by the Church? Of course not. Nicaea did not invent a new doctrine, it simply defined and defended the ancient apostolic truth against a contemporary error.

In the exact same way, the term "Lutheran" or the confession of Sola Fide was not the creation of a new religion in 1517. It was the explicit defense of the ancient Gospel when human traditions and papal merit systems threatened to obscure Christ. 

You do not have to abandon the historic liturgy, the Real Presence, or the rich heritage of the Church Fathers to have peace with God. You do not have to trade 2,000 years of history for modern, low-church evangelicalism. Confessional Lutheranism offers you the fullness of Catholic liturgical and sacramental life, freed from the crushing anxiety of Purgatory, human merit, and papal tyranny, and anchored entirely in the objective, finished work of Jesus Christ.
