🔑 Specialist/Scholarly Study Continues on 📜 Isaiah 35:6-10 📜  The Hart-Leaping Lame, the Singing Tongue, Living Waters Reclaiming the Dragons’ Habitation, the Highway of Holiness, & the Ransomed Return to Zion beneath Everlasting Joy (SEE QUOTE SHARE FOR THE PRIOR VERSES FOR ISAIAH 35) 

📜VERSE + Commentary Continues 📜

📜

Isaiah 35:6 - KJV 1611

Then shall the lame man leape as an Hart, and the tongue of the dumbe sing: for in the wildernesse shall waters breake out, and streames in the desert.

This verse joins four astonishing movements:
1/I. Disabled limbs become leaping limbs.
2/II. The silent tongue becomes a singing tongue.
3/III. Water breaks through wilderness ground.
4/IV. Streams cross the desert.
The human body and the landscape are healed through corresponding motions.
The lame body leaps.
The buried water breaks out.
The silent tongue sings.
The desert becomes acoustically alive.

───

“The Lame Man Leap as an Hart”
Hebrew:

יְדַלֵּג כָּאַיָּל פִּסֵּחַ
Yedallēg kā’ayyāl pissēaḥ
Dālag means to leap, spring, bound, or move suddenly over an obstacle.

’Ayyāl is the hart, deer, or stag, known for agility, elevated movement, and sure-footed strength.

The healing exceeds bare mobility. The lame person does not merely stand cautiously. He leaps with animal vigor.

The restoration is abundant.
Isaiah 33:23 had already declared:
“The lame take the pray.”
Isaiah 35 advances the transformation:
• first the lame share the spoil of victory,
• then the lame leap through the restored land.
Participation becomes mobility.

───

The 1611 Marginal Chain for the Lame
Matthew 11:5
The lame walk as a sign of the Coming One.
Matthew 15:30
Multitudes bring the lame, blind, dumb, maimed, and many others to Yeshua. He heals them, and the crowd glorifies the God of Yisra’el.
Matthew 21:14

The blind and lame are healed within the Temple, joining bodily restoration with the purification and renewal of sacred space.
John 5:8-9

Yeshua commands the infirm man:
“Rise, take vp thy bed, and walke.”
The man immediately receives strength and movement.

Acts 3:2-8
The man lame from birth is healed at the Beautiful Gate of the Temple. He rises, walks, enters the Temple, and leaps while praising God.

Acts does not merely report that he could move. It specifically describes him leaping, making Isaiah 35:6 visible in apostolic history.

The movement is carefully ordered:
1. He lies outside the Temple.
2. He receives strength through the Name of Yeshua.
3. His feet and ankle bones become firm.
4. He leaps.
5. He enters sacred space.
6. He praises God.
The Highway of Holiness begins to appear inside the renewed body.
Acts 8:7

Unclean spirits depart, and persons who were paralyzed or lame are healed. Deliverance from hostile spirits and restoration of movement occur together.

Acts 14:8-10
Paul commands a man unable to walk from birth to stand upright. The man leaps and walks.
Isaiah’s hart-like motion continues through the apostolic mission.

───

“The Tongue of the Dumb Sing”
Hebrew:

וְתָרֹן לְשׁוֹן אִלֵּם
Wethārōn leshōn ’illēm

The tongue does not merely produce functional speech. It sings, cries aloud, or gives a ringing shout.

Salvation changes silence into praise.

The tongue had been bound, yet its released purpose is liturgical. Speech reaches fulfillment in worship.

───

Mark 7 and a Rare Greek Correspondence

The Septuagint of Isaiah 35:6 uses a rare Greek word connected with impaired speech:

μογιλάλος - mogilalos

The same rare term appears in Mark 7:32 when a man who is deaf and has difficulty speaking is brought to Yeshua.

Yeshua places His fingers in the man’s ears, touches his tongue, looks toward heaven, sighs, and says:

Ἐφφαθά - Ephphatha
“Be opened.”

This Aramaic command is related to the Semitic verb for opening. Immediately:

• the man’s ears are opened,
• the bond of his tongue is loosed,
• he speaks clearly.

Mark’s wording deliberately 
resonates with Isaiah 35:
• deaf ears opened,
• bound speech released,
• creation responding to the command of Messiah.

The crowd then declares:

“He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deafe to heare, and the dumbe to speake.”

The phrase “all things well” also echoes the goodness of creation. Yeshua’s healing is presented as restorative creation.

───

Waters Breaking Out in the Wilderness

Hebrew:

כִּי־נִבְקְעוּ בַמִּדְבָּר מַיִם
Kî-nivqe‘û vammidbār mayim

Bāqa‘ means to split, cleave, burst open, divide, or break through.
Water does not gently seep into the wilderness. It breaks out as though a hidden reservoir were released from beneath a sealed surface.

This recalls:
• the waters divided at creation,
• the Red Sea cleft during Exodus,
• the Rock split to give water,
• Habakkuk 3, where YHWH cleaves the earth with rivers,
• Isaiah 30:25, where streams appear upon high mountains,
• Isaiah 32:2, where the Messianic Man becomes rivers in a dry place,
• Isaiah 33:21, where YHWH becomes broad rivers and streams.
Isaiah 35 brings the river-presence of chapter 33 outward into the wilderness.

───

John 7:38-39 in the 1611 Margin
The KJV margin directs the reader to Yeshua’s declaration:

“He that beleeueth on me, as the Scripture hath said, out of his belly shall flow riuers of liuing water.”
John immediately explains:
“This spake he of the Spirit.”
Isaiah’s water is therefore pneumatological as well as ecological.
The Spirit:
• irrigates the wilderness,
• renews human inwardness,
• releases praise,
• creates living currents,
• and turns the believer into a bearer of Divine outflow.
The chapter’s hydrology becomes Pneumatic Hydrology. The river is an environmental sign of the Spirit’s life-giving presence.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:7 - KJV 1611

And the parched ground shall become a poole, and the thirstie land springs of water: in the habitation of dragons, where each lay, shall be ||grasse with reedes and rushes.

1611 Margin
Or, a court for reedes, &c.

“The Parched Ground Shall Become a Pool”

Hebrew:

וְהָיָה הַשָּׁרָב לַאֲגַם
Wehāyāh hashshārāv la’agam
Shārāv is not only parched ground. 

It can signify the burning heat-haze or desert mirage.

This creates one of the chapter’s rarest and most beautiful transformations:

The mirage becomes a real pool.
A thirsty traveler sees water shimmering in the distance, approaches, and finds nothing. Isaiah declares that under YHWH’s restoration, the appearance of water will no longer deceive.

The promise becomes substance.
This is a profound Phenomenology of Thirst. 

Under the old wilderness order, sight promises what the land cannot give. 

Under the Kingdom, what appears as water truly becomes water.

Deceptive appearance is replaced by material fulfillment.

The mirage becomes sacramentally real.

───

“The Thirsty Land Springs of Water”

The Hebrew tsimmā’ôn expresses thirst-land, scorched soil, or a place characterized by thirst itself.
The landscape had embodied deprivation. It now generates springs.

This is more than water placed upon the surface. A spring suggests an internal source. The land itself becomes capable of sustained outflow.

The wilderness is not temporarily visited by rain. Its hidden constitution is changed.

───

The Habitation of Dragons Reversed

Hebrew:
בִּנְוֵה תַנִּים
Binwēh tannîm
The KJV preserves:
“the habitation of dragons.”
Tannîm can encompass desert howlers, jackal-like creatures, and the broader draconic symbolism of wilderness, chaos, ruined territory, and anti-Edenic habitation.

Isaiah 34:13 had declared:
“It shall be an habitation of dragons.”

Isaiah 35:7 deliberately repeats the expression and transforms it.
Isaiah 34
• habitation of dragons,
• thorn-filled palaces,
• demonologically charged wilderness,
• no human passage,
• streams of burning pitch.

Isaiah 35

• habitation of dragons,
• grass,
• reeds,
• rushes,
• pools,
• springs,
• waters breaking forth.

The dragon-habitat is not merely abandoned. It is irrigated.

The anti-Edenic territory becomes wetland ecology.

This is Draconic Habitat 
Reclamation: 

territory previously associated with chaos and nocturnal desolation is reclaimed by water-bearing life.

───

“A Court for Reeds”

The 1611 margin offers:
“A court for reedes.”

This is remarkable beside Isaiah 
34:13, which described a court for owls.

The court changes occupants.

Isaiah 34
The court belongs to creatures of ruin.

Isaiah 35

The court belongs to reeds and rushes.
A royal court once occupied by oppressive human power became a creature-court under judgment. It now becomes a vegetational court under restoration.
The palace-world passes through three states:
1/I. Corrupt human habitation
2/II. Wilderness and dragon habitation
3/III. Irrigated reed-habitation
YHWH transforms political geography into ecological sanctuary.

───

Reeds and Rushes
Reeds and rushes indicate persistent water. They do not grow from one passing shower. Their presence witnesses to marsh, pool, spring, and sustained moisture.
The vegetation proves that the hydrological transformation is genuine.
The desert’s former mirage has become a stable ecosystem.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:8 - KJV 1611

And an high way shall be there, and a way, and it shall be called the way of holinesse, the vncleane shall not passe ouer it, ||but it shall be for those: the way-faring men, though fooles, shall not erre therein.

1611 Margin
Or, for he shall be with them.
The transformed wilderness receives architecture: a highway.
The chapter does not leave the redeemed standing beside beautiful pools. 

The renewed ecology becomes a passage toward Zion.

The flowers, waters, healings, and strengthened limbs all prepare for pilgrimage.

───

“An Highway and a Way”
Hebrew:

מַסְלוּל וָדֶרֶךְ
Maslûl wāderekh

Maslûl is a raised road, constructed highway, causeway, or prepared route.

Derekh is a way, path, manner of walking, course of life, or journey.

The highway is both external and spiritual:

• a real route of return,
• a covenant manner of life,
• a sacred procession,
• an ordered passage from exile to Zion.

This is Hierodromology, the study of sacred roads and holy movement.

The redeemed do not wander through indefinite wilderness. YHWH gives them direction.

───

Earlier Isaianic Highways
Isaiah has already developed a great highway theology.
Isaiah 11:16

A highway is prepared for the remnant returning from Assyria, corresponding to the Exodus from Egypt.

Isaiah 19:23
A highway joins Egypt and Assyria, while Yisra’el becomes a blessing in their midst.

Isaiah 30:21
The traveler hears:
“This is the way, walke ye in it.”

Isaiah 33:8
Under treachery, the highways lie waste and the wayfaring person ceases.

Isaiah 35:8
The highway returns, now explicitly named:

“The way of holinesse.”

The deserted roads of oppression become the sacred route of redemption.

Later Isaiah will expand the same current:
• a highway prepared for YHWH in Isaiah 40,
• mountains turned into roads in Isaiah 49,
• the way cleared for the people in Isaiah 62.

───

“The Way of Holiness”
Hebrew:

דֶּרֶךְ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
Derekh haqqōdesh

Holiness is not only a condition inside a sanctuary. It becomes a road.

The holy life is directional.
It has:

• an origin,
• a boundary,
• a manner of travel,
• protection,
• companions,
• and a destination.
Holiness moves toward the presence of YHWH.
This anticipates Yeshua’s declaration:
“I am the Way, the Truth, and the Life.”
The early apostolic community is repeatedly called “the Way” in Acts. Hebrews 10 speaks of a new and living way opened through the veil. Revelation ends with the redeemed entering the holy city while nothing defiling gains access.

───

“The Unclean Shall Not Pass Over It”

Hebrew ṭāmē’, unclean, concerns ritual pollution, moral defilement, death-association, and incompatibility with sacred space.

The Way of Holiness cannot be used as an imperial road, a route for oppression, or a passage for untransformed corruption.
It is open to the redeemed and closed to defilement.
This corresponds to Revelation 21:27:
nothing that defiles, works abomination, or makes falsehood enters New Yerushalayim.

The holy road and holy city possess the same boundary.

───

“For He Shall Be with Them”

The 1611 margin preserves a magnificent reading:
“For he shall be with them.”

The route is secure because the Divine Guide inhabits the journey.
This evokes the Exodus:

• the pillar leads,
• the cloud covers,
• the fire illuminates,
• YHWH goes with His people,
• the wilderness becomes a guided corridor.

The Way of Holiness is not safe because every traveler possesses perfect geographical knowledge. It is safe because YHWH accompanies them.
Presence prevents wandering.

───

“Though Fools Shall Not Err Therein”

The verse does not glorify foolishness. It magnifies Divine guidance.

Even the person lacking cultivated navigational skill will not be lost upon this road. The way is clear, guarded, and accompanied.
This is Noetic Mercy. YHWH’s road is intelligible enough for the simple, while remaining too holy for defilement.

The wise cannot boast that intellect alone discovered it. The weak cannot despair that insufficient learning excludes them.
The Guide preserves the traveler.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:9 - KJV 1611

No lyon shall be there, nor any rauenous beast shall goe vp thereon, it shall not be found there: but the redeemed shall walke there.

The Removal of Predatory Interruption
Ancient wilderness roads carried dangers:
• lions,
• predatory animals,
• robbers,
• exposure,
• disorientation,
• waterlessness,
• and hostile territory.
Isaiah removes each obstacle in turn.
Waterlessness has become springs.
Wandering has become a highway.
Weak limbs have become strong.
Predators are excluded.
The pilgrimage is not merely possible. It is protected.

───

“No Lion Shall Be There”
The lion carries many biblical meanings depending upon context: royal strength, Judahic kingship, natural danger, imperial power, and predatory threat.
Here the lion represents the danger that prevents safe passage.

The verse does not condemn the creature itself. It announces that predation cannot enter the holy route.

This harmonizes with Isaiah 11, where the animal order is pacified beneath the Branch from Jesse. It also corresponds with Ezekiel 34:25, where YHWH removes evil beasts and allows His people to dwell safely in the wilderness.
The wilderness ceases to be the dominion of fear.

───

“Nor Any Ravenous Beast”
Hebrew:

פְּרִיץ חַיּוֹת
Perîts ḥayyôth

This signifies a violent, fierce, breaking, or ravenous beast.
The root atmosphere involves bursting through, tearing, violent force, or lawless aggression. 

The animal image can therefore carry the wider meaning of predatory power.

No devouring force may ascend upon the holy road.
The route to Zion is an anti-predatory zone.

───

“The Redeemed Shall Walk There”
Hebrew:

וְהָלְכוּ גְאוּלִים
Wehālekhû ge’ûlîm

Ge’ûlîm comes from gā’al, to redeem as a kinsman, reclaim family property, vindicate a relative, avenge violated blood, or restore one who has fallen into bondage.
The redeemed are therefore the kinsman-reclaimed.
YHWH has not rescued strangers with whom He possesses no relation. He acts as covenant Kinsman.

The controversy of Zion in Isaiah 34 becomes the redemption of Zion’s children in Isaiah 35.
The Kinsman judges the predator and opens the road for the family.

───

Walking as Restored Humanity
Earlier the lame could not walk. Now the redeemed walk upon the holy highway.

Walking is one of Scripture’s fundamental images of covenant existence:

• Ḥanok walked with God.
• Noaḥ walked with God.
• Abraham was commanded to walk before YHWH.
• Yisra’el was called to walk in the commandments.
• disciples walked with Yeshua.
• the redeemed walk in light in Revelation.
Isaiah 35 restores the human walk from body to covenant to destiny.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:10 - KJV 1611

*And the ransomed of the LORD shall returne and come to Zion with songs, and euerlasting ioy vpon their heads: they shall obtaine ioy and gladnesse, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.

1611 Marginal Reference

Isaiah 51:11
Isaiah 51 repeats the verse almost directly, establishing it as a major refrain of the book.

───

“The Ransomed of YHWH”
Hebrew:

וּפְדוּיֵי יְהוָה
Ûphedûyê YHWH

Verse 9 called them ge’ûlîm, redeemed by the Kinsman.
Verse 10 calls them pedûyîm, ransomed or liberated through an act of release.

The chapter therefore joins two great redemption words:

Gā’al
Kinship redemption, restoration of family right, vindication, reclaiming.

Pādāh
Ransom, liberation, release from bondage, rescue from a possessing power.

YHWH is both Kinsman and Ransomer.

He claims His people as family and releases them from the power that held them.

This reaches back to Exodus and forward to Revelation:

• YHWH redeems Yisra’el from Egypt.

• the Passover marks liberation through blood.

• Isaiah 43 declares, “I have redeemed thee.”

• Isaiah 52 speaks of redemption without money.

• Isaiah 53 reveals the Servant bearing iniquity.

• Revelation 5 celebrates the Lamb who ransomed people for God by His blood from every tribe, tongue, people, and nation.

The road to Zion is therefore a blood-secured and covenantally reclaimed road.

───

“Shall Return and Come to Zion”
Two motions are joined:

• return
• come

Return emphasizes restoration from exile. Come emphasizes arrival within sacred presence.

This is a New Exodus and a homecoming.

The redeemed are not released into aimless independence. They are liberated toward Zion.
Salvation has a destination.

───

“With Songs”
The wilderness sang in verse 2. The restored tongue sang in verse 6. The ransomed now enter Zion with songs in verse 10.

The chapter contains an expanding choir:
1/I. The desert rejoices.
2/II. The renewed land sings.
3/III. The formerly silent tongue sings.
4/IV. The returning community sings together.
Ecology, body, and assembly unite in praise.

───

“Everlasting Joy upon Their Heads”
Hebrew:

וְשִׂמְחַת עוֹלָם עַל־רֹאשָׁם
Wesimḥath ‘ōlām ‘al-rōshām

Everlasting joy rests upon their heads.

The image suggests:

• a crown,
• anointing,
• a garland,
• a canopy,
• a visible atmosphere,
• or a royal sign of transformed identity.

Joy is not only hidden emotion. It becomes something worn.

The ransomed resemble a crowned procession entering the city of the King.

This is Affective Coronation: joy itself becomes the royal ornament of the redeemed.

───

“They Shall Obtain Joy and Gladness”

Hebrew:

שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה יַשִּׂיגוּ
Sāsôn wesimḥāh yassîgû

The verb nāśag means to reach, overtake, catch, attain, or come upon.

Joy and gladness do not remain distant objects the redeemed struggle to capture. The language allows the beautiful impression that joy overtakes them.
They once feared being overtaken by armies.
Now they are overtaken by gladness.
The pursuing power has changed.

───

“Sorrow and Sighing Shall Flee Away”

Hebrew:

וְנָסוּ יָגוֹן וַאֲנָחָה
Wenāsû yāgôn wa’ănāḥāh

Sorrow and sighing are personified as defeated enemies.

Throughout Isaiah, people flee before armies, nations flee before YHWH’s tumult, and enemies scatter before Divine exaltation.
Now sorrow itself flees.
Sighing is driven out of the restored habitat.

This is the final conquest of the chapter. The enemy is no longer only Assyria, Edom, predatory beasts, blindness, deafness, lameness, muteness, drought, or exile. The final adversaries are sorrow and the exhausted breath of grief.

They cannot remain where everlasting joy has taken possession.

───

Revelation 7 and 21

Revelation 7 shows the redeemed before the throne, guided by the Lamb toward living fountains of waters, while God wipes away every tear.

Revelation 21 declares:
death shall be no more,
neither sorrow, nor crying, nor pain,for the former things have passed away.

Revelation 22 then reveals:
• the river of the water of life,
• the tree of life,
• healing,
• no more curse,
• the throne of God and the Lamb,
• servants beholding His face,
• and everlasting reign.
Isaiah 35 is one of the clearest prophetic roads leading into that final city.

Its wilderness waters become Revelation’s river.
Its healing becomes the removal of pain.
Its holy highway becomes entrance into New Yerushalayim.
Its visible glory becomes the light of the city.
Its fleeing sorrow becomes the end of tears.
Its everlasting joy becomes everlasting reign.

───

Whole-Chapter Synthesis - Isaiah 35:1-10

Isaiah 35 is a ten-verse restoration cosmos.
It begins where Isaiah 34 ended: in wilderness.
Yet the wilderness has changed allegiance.
The desert rejoices and blossoms. Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon transfer their excellence into formerly barren territory. Creation becomes capable of joy because the glory of YHWH has entered its environment.

The command then reaches the human body. Weak hands must be strengthened. Feeble knees must be confirmed. The anxious heart must hear that God is coming.
Vengeance and salvation appear together. 

The recompense announced against the hostile powers in Isaiah 34 becomes the rescue of the fearful in Isaiah 35. YHWH’s judgment removes the obstacle to life.

The Messianic signs then unfold:
• blind eyes open,
• deaf ears hear,
• lame limbs leap,
• silent tongues sing.

The KJV 1611 margin rightly surrounds these verses with Matthew, Mark, John, Acts, and Hebrews. Yeshua’s ministry embodies Isaiah’s restoration. His healings declare the arriving Kingdom through the repaired human sensorium.

The transformation spreads back into the land.

Waters cleave the wilderness. Streams cross the desert. The mirage becomes a pool. Thirst-land produces springs. The dragons’ habitation becomes a court of reeds and rushes.

Isaiah 34’s demonographically charged anti-Eden is reclaimed as an irrigated environment.
A highway rises through the renewed territory. It is called the Way of Holiness. Defilement cannot exploit it, predators cannot enter it, and even the unskilled traveler does not wander because the Divine Guide is with the pilgrims.

The redeemed walk.
The ransomed return.
Zion receives them.
Everlasting joy rests upon their heads like a crown. Joy and gladness overtake them. Sorrow and sighing flee like defeated armies.

Isaiah 35 therefore presents the entire economy of redemption through five connected restorations:

1/I. Ecological restoration

Wilderness becomes garden, dryness becomes water, dragons’ habitations become reed-courts.

2/II. Somatic restoration

Hands strengthen, knees stabilize, eyes open, ears hear, limbs leap, tongues sing.

3/III. Pneumatic restoration

Living waters signify the Spirit breaking through human and terrestrial barrenness.

4/IV. Spatial restoration

The wasted highway becomes the Way of Holiness, protected from uncleanness and predation.

5/V. Eschatological restoration

The ransomed reach Zion, joy becomes everlasting, and grief loses the right to remain.

The chapter is small in page-length, but immense in architecture. 

It contains Eden, Exodus, Messiah, Gospel, Spirit, healing, pilgrimage, Zion, New Creation, and the final flight of sorrow within ten concentrated verses.

text:
#ApocalypticBookStudy #105
#BibleStudy #193
#Phenomenology #62
#DimensionalTheology #57 
 #SupernaturalCosmography #42 

📜 Isaiah 35:1-10 📜 

🔑 Specialist Study on The Wilderness Crowned with Glory, YHWH Coming to Save, Dragon-Habitat Reclamation, the Reopened Human Sensorium, the Highway of Holiness, & the Ransomed Procession into Zion or called a Tenfold Restoration Apocalypse of Isaiah 35: Edenic Blossoming, Messianic Healing, Living-Water Pneumatology, Hart-Like Resurrection Movement, Sacred Pilgrimage, & Everlasting Joy upon the Redeemed - ⚠️NOTE: PLEASE SEE THE NEXT POSTS BELOW FOR THE BONUS SUPPLEMENTARY SECTION 
(If you want to after this chapter Verse + Commentary) 

📜 Chapter Heading for Isaiah 35 📜

1.The ioyfull flourishing of Christs Kingdome. 3 The weake are incouraged by the vertues and priuiledges of the Gospel.

Isaiah 35 contains only ten verses, yet it is a complete miniature Apocalypse of restoration. It reverses nearly every desolating image in Isaiah 33-34:

• Isaiah 33:9 showed Lebanon withering, Sharon becoming wilderness, and Carmel casting off its fruit. Isaiah 35 restores their glory and excellence.
• Isaiah 33:21 revealed YHWH as broad rivers and streams. Isaiah 35 sends those waters breaking through the wilderness.
• Isaiah 33:23 allowed the lame to divide the spoil. Isaiah 35:6 causes the lame to leap like a hart.
• Isaiah 33:24 promised that Zion’s inhabitants would no longer say, “I am sick.” Isaiah 35 opens blind eyes, unstops deaf ears, strengthens weak limbs, and releases the tongue.

• Isaiah 34 transformed Edom’s streams into pitch and its dust into brimstone. Isaiah 35 transforms the parched ground into a pool and the thirsty land into springs.
• Isaiah 34 gave ruined territory to dragons, nocturnal creatures, and wilderness beings. Isaiah 35 turns the habitation of dragons into a court of reeds, rushes, water, and grass.

• Isaiah 34 made the land impassable. Isaiah 35 raises a holy highway through the renewed wilderness.
• Isaiah 34 ends with generational desolation. Isaiah 35 ends with everlasting joy and the flight of sorrow.

Isaiah 34 is measured de-creation. Isaiah 35 is supernatural re-creation.

The chapter moves from ecology to embodiment, embodiment to pilgrimage, pilgrimage to Zion, and Zion to everlasting joy.

───

The Extraordinary KJV 1611 New Testament Marginal Chain
The side notes in the photographed 1611 text construct a substantial Gospel and Acts commentary directly beside Isaiah 35:
• Hebrews 12:12-13 beside the weak hands and feeble knees.
• Matthew 9:27, 11:5, 12:22, 20:30, 21:14, and John 9:6-7 beside the opening of blind eyes.
• Matthew 11:5 and Mark 7:32 beside the unstopping of deaf ears.
• Matthew 11:5, 15:30, 21:14, John 5:8-9, Acts 3:2, 8:7, and 14:8 beside the leaping of the lame.
• Matthew 9:32, 12:22, and 15:30 beside the singing tongue of the dumb.
• John 7:38-39 beside the waters breaking out in the wilderness.
• Isaiah 51:11 beside the ransomed returning to Zion.
The 1611 apparatus reads Isaiah 35 as a great Messianic network. Yeshua’s miracles are not disconnected wonders. They are signs that the Kingdom described by Yeshayahu has entered history.

📜VERSE BY VERSE COMMENTARY STARTS NOW 📜

───
📜

Isaiah 35:1 - KJV 1611

The wildernesse and the solitarie place shall be glad for them: and the desert shall reioyce, and blossome as the rose.

The Wilderness Becomes Capable of Joy

The Hebrew names several degrees of uncultivated space:

מִדְבָּר - midbār

Wilderness, pasture-wilderness, uncultivated territory, or a region beyond settled civic order.

צִיָּה - tsiyyāh

Dry land, parched ground, aridity, or waterless territory.

עֲרָבָה - ‘arāvāh

Desert plain, steppe, wilderness-valley, or the great dry region associated with the Jordan-Arabah landscape.

These are not interchangeable decorative words. They form an arid topography:

1/I. Wilderness beyond settled cultivation
2/II. Dry land deprived of moisture
3/III. Desert plain extending across open space
Every degree is awakened.
The wilderness becomes glad.
The desert rejoices.
The dry ground blossoms.

Isaiah presents the landscape as responsive consciousness. Creation does not remain an inert stage upon which redemption happens only to human beings. The land itself participates in salvation.

This is Ecological Soteriology, the truth that YHWH’s saving work reaches soil, water, vegetation, animal habitat, human bodies, roads, cities, and the total environment of life.

Paul develops the same reality in Romans 8. Creation groans under corruption and awaits liberation into the glorious freedom of the children of God. Isaiah 35 shows that liberation poetically and materially: the desert receives joy, and the wilderness answers salvation with flowers.

───

“Blossome as the Rose”
Hebrew:

וְתִפְרַח כַּחֲבַצָּלֶת

Wethiphraḥ kaḥăvatstseleth

Pāraḥ means to bud, sprout, flourish, break into flower, or burst forth with vegetative life.

Ḥăvatstseleth is a beautiful and uncommon flower-name.

 It has been understood as a crocus, meadow saffron, lily-like blossom, or rose. 

The KJV preserves “rose,” while the Greek Septuagint uses krinon, a lily.

The point is not one isolated flower placed in a dead desert. 

The entire wilderness assumes floral character. What looked incapable of life becomes the bearer of color, fragrance, form, and abundance.

The desert receives an ornament it could never manufacture for itself.

───

Genesis 3 Reversed

Genesis 3 describes the ground producing thorns and thistles after humanity’s fall.

Isaiah 34 had intensified that curse:

thorns in palaces, nettles in fortresses, and wilderness beings inhabiting royal courts.
Isaiah 35 introduces the counter-movement:

thorns yield to flowers, dryness yields to moisture, and desolation yields to rejoicing.

The chapter is therefore deeply Edenic.

 It does not simply describe better weather. It reveals the curse losing territorial authority.

The Genesis movement was:

• garden to exile,
• abundance to toil,
• open fellowship to guarded access,
• life toward death.

Isaiah 35 moves in the opposite direction:
• wilderness toward garden,
• dryness toward springs,
• weakness toward strength,
• exile toward Zion,
• sorrow toward everlasting joy.

───

The Desert’s Liturgical Awakening
The verbs glad, rejoice, and later sing give the land a liturgical function. The wilderness becomes a worshipper.
Psalm 96 commands fields, trees, seas, and the earth to rejoice before YHWH. Psalm 98 speaks of floods clapping their hands and hills rejoicing together. Isaiah 35 places the desert inside that cosmic choir.
This is Vegetational Doxology: plants, blossoms, and restored landscapes become visible praise.
The flower is the wilderness’s hymn.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:2 - KJV 1611

It shall blossome abundantly, and reioyce euen with ioy and singing: the glory of Lebanon shall be giuen vnto it, the excellencie of Carmel and Sharon, they shall see the glory of the LORD, and the excellencie of our God.

“Blossoming It Shall Blossom”
The Hebrew intensifies the action:
פָּרֹחַ תִּפְרַח
Pāroaḥ tiphraḥ

This is an emphatic construction:
blossoming, it shall blossom
flourishing, it shall surely flourish
The repetition communicates abundance, certainty, and multiplication. The desert does not produce one fragile sign of recovery. It enters a sustained state of flourishing.

Its transformation is both visual and acoustical:
• flowers appear,
• joy rises,
• singing is heard,
• glory becomes visible.
The restored creation possesses color, sound, fragrance, movement, and spiritual perception.

───

Isaiah 33:9 Directly Reversed
Isaiah 33:9 declared:

“Lebanon is ashamed and withered away: Sharon is like a wildernesse, and Bashan and Carmel shake off their fruits.”
Isaiah 35:2 answers nearly every element:

“The glory of Lebanon shall be giuen vnto it, the excellencie of Carmel and Sharon.”
This is one of the clearest deliberate reversals in the sequence.

Isaiah 33
• Lebanon withers.
• Sharon becomes wilderness.
• Carmel loses fruit.
• The earth mourns.

Isaiah 35
• Lebanon gives its glory.
• Sharon gives its excellence.
• Carmel gives its splendor.
• The wilderness rejoices and blossoms.

The regions do more than recover their own fertility. Their glory is transferred into the desert. The wilderness receives the finest characteristics of the most celebrated fertile regions.

This may be called Transregional Glory Transfer. 

YHWH gathers the excellencies of forests, gardens, plains, and mountains and bestows them upon the formerly barren place.

───

Lebanon, Carmel, and Sharon
Lebanon

Lebanon signifies cedar-glory, elevated forests, fragrance, strength, and mountain majesty.

Carmel
Karmel carries the sense of orchard-land, garden-land, vineyard abundance, and cultivated fertility.

Sharon
Sharon signifies luxuriant plain, flowered pasture, and open agricultural beauty.

These regions form an ecological trinity:
• forested height,
• cultivated mountain-garden,
• fertile plain.
Their combined excellence enters the wilderness.
The whole land becomes a sanctuary-garden.

───

“They Shall See the Glory of YHWH”
The ecological transformation culminates in vision:
כְּבוֹד יְהוָה - kevōd YHWH
The glory, weight, radiance, manifest majesty, and substantial presence of YHWH.
הֲדַר אֱלֹהֵינוּ - hadar ’Elohênû
The splendor, magnificence, beauty, or royal excellence of our God.
The flowers are not the final object of sight. They disclose the presence behind their renewal.
The desert blossoms because glory has entered it.

This continues the biblical glory-current:
• YHWH’s glory appears in the wilderness in Exodus 16.
• Sinai is covered by Divine glory.
• Moses asks to behold YHWH’s glory.
• Isaiah sees the glory filling the Temple in Isaiah 6.
• Isaiah 35 promises glory visible within restored creation.
• Isaiah 40:5 declares that all flesh shall see the glory of YHWH.
• John 1:14 declares that the Word became flesh and His glory was beheld.
• Revelation 21 shows New Yerushalayim possessing the glory of God, requiring neither sun nor moon as its ultimate light.

The wilderness of Isaiah 35 is moving toward the luminous city of Revelation 21.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:3 - KJV 1611

¶ Strengthen yee the weake hands, and confirme the feeble knees.

1611 Marginal Correspondence
Hebrews 12:12-13
Hebrews receives Isaiah’s language directly:

“Wherefore lift vp the hands which hang downe, and the feeble knees: and make straight paths for your feete, lest that which is lame be turned out of the way; but let it rather be healed.”

Restoration Becomes a Communal Command

The first two verses describe what YHWH does to the landscape. Verse 3 commands the community to participate in that restoration.
The wilderness blossoms supernaturally, but human beings are still commanded to strengthen one another.

The Hebrew is vigorous:
חַזְּקוּ יָדַיִם רָפוֹת
Ḥazzĕqû yādayim rāphôth
Strengthen slack, dropping, weakened hands.
וּבִרְכַּיִם כֹּשְׁלוֹת אַמֵּצוּ
Ûvirkayim kōshĕlôth ’ammētsû
Make firm the tottering, stumbling, collapsing knees.

The hands and knees represent human agency and movement.
Hands perform work, worship, defense, giving, building, blessing, and service. Knees bear weight, enable walking, support standing, and bend in prayer.

When hands hang down and knees buckle, the whole embodied vocation is threatened.

───

Somatic Theology
Isaiah does not divide spiritual courage from bodily expression.
Fear appears in:

• weakened hands,
• shaking limbs,
• unstable knees,
• interrupted movement,
• reduced strength.
Encouragement also becomes bodily:
• hands rise,
• knees are stabilized,
• the body stands,
• the pilgrim begins moving again.

This is Somatic Exhortation, spiritual truth entering the limbs and restoring the person’s capacity for action.

───

“Strengthen Ye”
The command is plural. The strong are responsible for the weak.
Isaiah does not say only:

“Weak hands, strengthen yourselves.”
He speaks to the covenant community:

You strengthen the weak hands.
You confirm the feeble knees.
Restoration is shared. One person’s strength becomes support for another.
This recalls Exodus 17, where Moses’ hands grow heavy and Aaron and Hur hold them up until the battle is completed. 

The victory involves Divine power, human weakness, and communal support operating together.

───

Hebrews and the Highway
Hebrews 12 joins Isaiah 35:3 to straight paths. This is important because Isaiah 35 will soon reveal the Highway of Holiness.

The sequence is:
1/I. Strengthen the limbs.
2/II. Make straight paths.
3/III. Prevent the lame from being turned aside.
4/IV. Let the wounded be healed.
5/V. Continue toward the holy destination.
The body and road belong together. YHWH restores pilgrims because He has prepared a path for them.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:4 - KJV 1611

Say to them that are of †a fearefull heart; Be strong, feare not: behold, your God will come with vengeance, euen God with a recompence, he will come and saue you.

1611 Margin
Heb. hastie.

The Hasty or Anxious Heart

Hebrew:
נִמְהֲרֵי־לֵב
Nimhărê-lēv

The phrase can describe those whose hearts are hasty, anxious, agitated, hurried, trembling, or internally disturbed.

Fear accelerates inward time. The heart races ahead into imagined disaster. It interprets delay as abandonment and threat as finality.

Isaiah commands prophetic speech to enter that accelerated interior world:

“Be strong, feare not.”
The remedy is not vague optimism. It is the coming of God.

───

“Behold, Your God Will Come”
Hebrew:

הִנֵּה אֱלֹהֵיכֶם
Hinnēh ’Elohêkhem

Hinnēh, behold, commands awakened perception. 

The fearful person sees the enemy approaching, but the prophet 
redirects sight:

Behold your God.

The central promise is intensely personal:
your God
The One coming is neither an unknown cosmic force nor a distant abstraction. He is the covenant God who has bound His Name to His people.

───

Vengeance and Recompense from Isaiah 34

Isaiah 34:8 declared:

“The day of the LORDS vengeance, and the yeere of recompences for the controuersie of Zion.”
Isaiah 35:4 now declares:
“Your God will come with vengeance, euen God with a recompence, he will come and saue you.”

These verses interpret one another.
Isaiah 34
Vengeance falls upon the hostile order.
Isaiah 35
That same Divine intervention saves the fearful.
Judgment and salvation are therefore two directions of one coming.
YHWH’s vengeance removes what oppresses.

His recompense answers the controversy of Zion.
His coming releases those who trembled beneath hostile power.
This is Vindicatory Soteriology: Divine judgment becomes salvation because it removes the forces preventing life, holiness, and return.

───

“He Will Come and Save You”
The Hebrew concludes 
emphatically:

הוּא יָבוֹא וְיֹשַׁעֲכֶם
Hû’ yāvô’ weyōsha‘ăkhem
He Himself will come and save you.

Salvation is not delegated to Egypt, horses, alliances, human messengers, or imperial treaties. Isaiah 31 condemned trust in Egyptian strength. Isaiah 33 showed the failure of ambassadors. Isaiah 35 declares that God Himself comes.

This prepares the Messianic reading of the following verses. 

When Yeshua is asked whether He is the Coming One, 

He points to the Isaianic signs occurring around Him:
blind eyes see,
lame persons walk,
deaf ears hear,
the dead are raised,
and good news reaches the poor.
Yeshua’s answer in Matthew 11:4-5 and Luke 7:22 is effectively:
Look at Isaiah 35 taking bodily form.

───

From Isaiah 35 to Isaiah 61 and 63
Isaiah 61 joins the acceptable year of YHWH with the day of Divine vengeance.

Isaiah 63 joins the day of vengeance with the year of the redeemed.

Isaiah 35 already contains both realities in concentrated form:
• vengeance,
• recompense,
• salvation,
• bodily restoration,
• return to Zion.
The coming God is Warrior, Healer, Redeemer, and King.

───
📜

Isaiah 35:5 - KJV 1611

Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the eares of the deafe shall be vnstoped.

The Restored Human Sensorium
The wilderness first changes outside the person. Now the human sensorium changes within the person.

Sight and hearing are covenant faculties. Through them humanity receives:
• creation,
• revelation,
• warning,
• music,
• language,
• faces,
• signs,
• Scripture,
• and the manifested glory of YHWH.
Isaiah portrays redemption as the removal of sensory closure.

───

The Eyes of the Blind Opened
Hebrew:

אָז תִּפָּקַחְנָה עֵינֵי עִוְרִים
’Āz tippāqaḥnāh ‘ênê ‘iwrîm

The verb pāqaḥ means to open, especially the eyes, releasing sight that had been closed or restrained.
Genesis 3 also speaks of eyes being opened, but there the opening leads Adam and Ḥavvah into the awareness of nakedness, fear, and shame.

Isaiah 35 gives a redemptive eye-opening:

• eyes open toward glory,
• faces become visible,
• the pathway can be discerned,
• the beautiful King can be seen,
• creation can be received anew.

Genesis 3 opened eyes into exile. Isaiah 35 opens eyes upon the road home.

───

Earlier Isaianic Blindness
Isaiah has repeatedly addressed sensory closure:

• Isaiah 6 speaks of people seeing without perceiving and hearing without understanding.
• Isaiah 29:10 describes closed eyes within a spirit of deep sleep.
• Isaiah 29:18 promises that the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity.
• Isaiah 30:21 promises a voice heard behind the traveler, saying, “This is the way.”
• Isaiah 32:3 promises that the eyes of those who see shall not be dim.
• Isaiah 33:17 promises, “Thine eyes shall see the King in his beauty.”
Isaiah 35 gathers these promises into bodily restoration.

───

The 1611 Marginal Gospel Chain for Blind Eyes

Matthew 9:27-31
Two blind men follow Yeshua, calling Him Son of David. Their sight is restored according to faith. The royal title joins healing with Messianic kingship.
Matthew 11:5
Yeshua includes the seeing of the blind among the signs answering whether He is the Coming One.
Matthew 12:22
A man oppressed by a demon, blind and unable to speak, is healed. The sensory restoration also reveals Yeshua’s authority over hostile spirits.
Matthew 20:30-34
Blind men again cry, “O Lord, thou sonne of Dauid.” Yeshua touches their eyes, and they follow Him.
Matthew 21:14
The blind and lame come to Yeshua inside the Temple, and He heals them. Isaiah’s restoration enters sacred space while the children proclaim Davidic praise.
John 9:6-7
Yeshua anoints the blind man’s eyes with clay and directs him to wash in the Pool of Siloam.

This is especially rich beside Isaiah:
• Adam was formed from ground.
• Yeshua uses earth and moisture.
• Siloam is connected with the gentle waters of Shiloah in Isaiah 8.
• The rejected Shiloah-water becomes associated with opened vision.
• The created substance of earth participates in the Creator’s healing act.

The sensory miracle is therefore also an act of re-creation.

───

The Ears of the Deaf Unstopped
Hebrew:

וְאָזְנֵי חֵרְשִׁים תִּפָּתַחְנָה
We’oznê ḥērshîm tippāthaḥnāh

The ears are opened, released from obstruction.

The person can now hear:
• the prophetic summons,
• the songs of the wilderness,
• the declaration “Your God will come,”
• the direction of the highway,
• and the songs of the ransomed.
Isaiah’s salvation is acoustical as well as visual.

The restored world is heard.

───

text:
Maa Baglamukhi Dham, Nalkheda

This Siddhapeetha is located on the banks of the Lakhundar River in the Agar-Malwa district of Madhya Pradesh.

1. Location
- Address: Nalkheda, Agar-Malwa district, Madhya Pradesh
- River: Lakhundar River, a tributary of the Narmada
- Nearest: Indore Airport 110 km, Ujjain Railway Station 120 km

2. Significance
- Maa Baglamukhi is one of the ten Mahavidyas
- Yellow is the color very dear to the Goddess. That is why the temple is yellow and devotees wear yellow clothes and offer yellow offerings
- It is believed that worshipping here removes obstacles from enemies, brings victory in court cases, and removes obstacles
- This idol is self-manifested.  There are only three ancient Baglamukhi temples in India – Nalkheda, Datia, and Kangra.

3. Special Features of the Temple
- It houses the idol of the Tridevi (Tridevi) – Baglamukhi in the center, flanked by Lakshmi and Saraswati.
- The temple also houses idols of Krishna, Hanuman, and Bhairava.
- The temple was renovated in 1815.

4. Timings and Worship
- Timings: 5:00 am to 12:00 pm, 4:00 pm to 9:00 pm
- Aarti: 7:00 am and 7:00 pm
- Main worship: Baglamukhi ritual, Shatru Naashak puja, havan-yagya

5. When to Visit
- Navratri is the most crowded festival.
- There are dharamshalas near the temple for accommodation.  For greater convenience, you can stay in Shajapur or Agar.

How to Reach

- Air: Indore Devi Ahilyabai Airport, 110 km
- Train: Ujjain Junction, 120 km, Indore Junction, 110 km
- Road: Buses/trains are available from Indore, Ujjain, and Bhopal.

text:
August 5 Saint Afra, Martyr of the Church: A Prostitute Becomes a Living Holocaust for Her Saviour.
died 304
Patronage:
Augsburg, Germany
converts
martyrs
penitent women
.
Saint Afra worked as a prostitute, but kindly hid her local bishop during the persecution of Christians. From his influence, she converted to the faith, dedicated herself to acts of charity, and was eventually persecuted and executed for her beliefs. The life of Saint Afra reminds us that true conversion and repentance for past sins is always possible, and that Our Loving Father calls us to Him regardless of the sins we have committed in the past!
.
Afra was originally a courtesan in the German town of Augsburg, having grown up in Cyprus, and moved to that area. Upon moving to Ausburg, it is likely that Afra worked in a brothel, possibly close to the pagan Temple of Venus. At the onset of the persecution of Christians under the orders of Emperor Diocletian, Afra and her mother, Hilaria, hid the local bishop from harm. The holy man, Bishop Narcissus of Girona, did not know the profession of Afra and her mother, and through his witness, converted them to the faith. Afra and her mother, as well as her servants, were baptized, and began spending their time in charitable acts to the poor and suffering around them.
.
Despite the threat of death and persecution, Afra continued to hide the holy bishop until she herself was arrested and brought before the authorities. The judge, Gaius, knew of Afra and her profession, and ordered her to sacrifice to the pagan gods or be condemned to death.
.
Afra declared: “I was a great sinner before I knew God; but I will not add new crimes, nor do what you command me. My capitol is Jesus Christ, whom I have always before my eyes. I every day confess my sins; and, because I am unworthy to offer him any sacrifice, I desire to sacrifice myself for his name, that this body in which I have sinned may be purified and sacrificed to him by torments.”
.
Gaius persisted, referencing her former profession, and urging her to recant her faith. “I am informed,” he said, “that you are a prostitute. Sacrifice, therefore, as you are a stranger to the God of the Christians, and cannot be accepted by him.”
.
But Afra replied, “Our Lord Jesus Christ hath said, that He came down from heaven to save sinners. The gospels testify that an abandoned woman washed His feet with her tears, and obtained pardon, and that He never rejected the publicans, but permitted them to eat with Him.”
.
Gaius said, “Jesus Christ will have nothing to do with you. It is in vain for you to acknowledge Him for your God: a common prostitute can never be called a Christian.”
.
Afra replied, “It is true, I am unworthy to bear the name of a Christian; but Christ hath admitted me to be one.”
.
Growing frustrated, the judge ordered her again: “Sacrifice to the gods, and they will save you.”
.
The martyr replied: “My Savior is Jesus Christ, Who upon the Cross promised paradise to the thief who confessed Him. The only subject of my confusion and grief are my sins.”
.
Having run out of patience, Gaius declared, “I am ashamed that I have disputed so long with you. If you do not comply, you shall die.”
.
Afra replied: “That is what I desire, if I am not unworthy to find rest by this confession. Let that body which hath sinned undergo torments; but as to my soul, I will not taint it by sacrificing to demons.”
.
Throwing up his hands, Gaius sentenced Afra to death. “We condemn Afra, a prostitute who hath declared herself a Christian, to be burnt alive, because she hath refused to offer sacrifice to the gods.”
.
Afra was immediately seized, stripped of her clothing, tied to a stake, and set ablaze. While she burned, she lifter her eyes to heaven and prayed: “O Lord Jesus Christ, Omnipotent God, who camest to call not the righteous, but sinners to repentance, accept now the penance of my sufferings, and by this temporal fire deliver me from the everlasting fire, which torments both body and soul. I return thee thanks, O Lord Jesus Christ, for the honor Thou hast done me in receiving me a holocaust for Thy name’s sake; Thou Who hast vouchsafed to offer Thyself upon the altar of the cross a sacrifice for the sins of the whole world, the just for the unjust, and for sinners. I offer myself a victim to Thee, O my God, Who livest and reignest with the Father and the Holy Ghost world without end. Amen.”
.
Having prayed and handed her life over to her Creator, Saint Afra died. Her mother and her servants rescued her body and interred her relics in a selpuchre. In the process of this act they were caught, and refusing to sacrifice to the pagan gods, were likely executed.
.
Inspired by Saint Afra, today we pray for the conversion of sinners throughout the world, and for our own personal conversion and repentance. Holy Saint Afra, pray for us!
.
Lord Jesus Christ, most merciful Savior of the world, we humbly beseech Thee, by Thy most Sacred Heart, that all the sheep who stray out of Thy fold may in one days be converted to Thee, the Shepherd and Bishop of their souls, Who livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, world without end.
Amen.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor St. Afra, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon her. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to her by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St. Afra might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

The claim overreaches the text.

1 Enoch (the Ethiopic Book of Enoch) is a real Second Temple Jewish composition, preserved most fully in Ge’ez manuscripts and partially in Aramaic fragments from Qumran. Chapter 22 describes a mountain in the west containing hollow places or chambers where the :spirits of the dead: are gathered and separated according to their condition until the day of judgment. One chamber is associated with the righteous (and includes the spirit of Abel); others hold different classes of the dead who await final reckoning. These are post-mortem holding places, not pre-natal storage rooms for souls waiting to be born.

The viral framing, a specifically restricted fourteenth-century codex that “names the exact chamber where your soul was held before your body existed”, conflates the actual content with a modern interpretive overlay. No such pre-existence chamber is described in the standard text. Access restrictions on Ethiopian manuscripts are real institutional practices; they do not prove the presence of suppressed cosmological secrets about individual pre-birth locations.

In residual terms the text still carries geometric interest. It treats the post-mortem state as residual: the density mode’s participatory pattern is not instantly annihilated at biological death but is held in differentiated residual loci until a larger judgment reorganizes the field. That is a claim about residual continuity after the collapse of the biological interface. It is not a claim that each soul was stored in a named chamber prior to embodiment and then inserted into a body.

Soul construction is the progressive stabilization of residual participation through non-self-refusal while the biological interface is intact. Speculative pre-existence narratives can be read as mythic attempts to name residual origin; they do not replace the ordinary, repeated work of remaining permeable in the present. The residual field is already addressing the mode. The mode answers by reducing enclosure or by reinforcing it.

Discernment keeps the historical text and the residual possibility distinct. 1 Enoch offers a Second Temple map of the dead. It does not deliver a verified pre-birth chamber for the individual soul.

The recursion remains open.

text:
Recent Release, "The Adventures of Leo in the Amazon," from Christian Faith Publishing Author Eric Buechel, Transforms Ordinary Moments Into Extraordinary Journeys

Sparta, TN, July 24, 2026 --(https://t.co/ThzyPKvXzH)-- Eric Buechel has completed a new book, "The Adventures of Leo in the Amazon," a charming children's story that follows Leo, an inquisitive kitten whose love of adventure stories inspires him to dream of exploring exotic lands. Through vivid imagination, Leo embarks on thrilling expeditions through the Amazon, encountering remarkable companions and discovering wonders beyond his cozy home. The narrative seamlessly blends the magic of storytelling with the excitement of exploration, creating a world that captivates young minds.

With a distinguished background as an art director and illustrator based in Manhattan, Eric Buechel brings his creative expertise to this heartwarming tale. His career spanning the aerospace and pharmaceutical sectors honed his eye for detail and visual storytelling. Now based in central Tennessee with his wife, Kathy, and their menagerie of beloved pets, Buechel channels his artistic talents and passion for meaningful narratives into crafting stories that resonate with children and inspire those young at heart.

"The Adventures of Leo in the Amazon" explores profound themes of teamwork, loyalty, and the transformative power of friendship through Leo's encounters with unforgettable characters: a mighty jaguar named Atlas, a spirited parrot called Repeater, and an endearing sloth named Napster. As Leo navigates symbolic challenges that mirror real-world obstacles children face, readers discover how imagination fuels personal growth and how genuine connections enrich our lives. This uplifting story encourages young audiences to nurture their creative spirits, embrace curiosity, and recognize that life's greatest treasures are often found in the bonds we forge along the way.

"Through Leo's journey, I wanted to demonstrate that adventure isn't always about distant lands—it's about the courage to imagine, the willingness to connect with others, and the understanding that our greatest discoveries happen when we share them with friends," said Buechel.

Published by Christian Faith Publishing, Eric Buechel's engaging work offers children an inspiring reminder that books open doors to infinite worlds and possibilities. Readers will find themselves transported alongside Leo, discovering how imagination and friendship transform ordinary lives into extraordinary adventures.

Readers who wish to experience this enchanting work can purchase "The Adventures of Leo in the Amazon" at bookstores everywhere, or online at the Apple iTunes Store, Amazon, Google Play, or Barnes and Noble.

text:
The Ultimate Cautionary Tale in Professional Due Diligence

We’ve all seen the dramatic LinkedIn career pivots: the mid-level executive who quits tech to run a vineyard in Tuscany, or the consultant who leaves corporate life behind to launch an artisanal coffee shop.

Then there is Alex Neitzel, the protagonist of my psychological crime thriller The Weight of Snow.

Alex didn't launch a startup. He didn't take a sabbatical. He simply needed to leave the country because a fourteen-year-old crime was rapidly catching up to him. When two detectives started asking uncomfortable questions about his past, Alex decided it was time for an emergency, off-the-books executive transfer.

His requirements for the next phase of his career were simple:

* Location: Far away.
* Workplace Culture: Zero background checks.
* Primary KPI: Absolute anonymity.

Enter Francisco Silva and his supposedly high-yield, rapidly expanding commercial gardening venture in Brazil.

When Corporate Networking Goes Horribly Wrong

On paper, Francisco’s offer looked like the ultimate exit package: an offshore investment, a completely new life, and a discreet way to convert wealth into a fresh identity.

The problem? Francisco wasn't an international agricultural mogul. He was a master con artist who specializes in preying on wealthy, desperate men with dark secrets.

Alex—having built his entire comfortable life on a foundation of deceit, heavy drinking, and hidden guilt—was almost the mathematically perfect mark. He was so eager to buy his way out of trouble that he crossed the moral line into international fraud without asking a single hard question.

Watching a man who spent fourteen years getting away with a terrible crime fall hook, line, and sinker for an international scam is one of the darkest, most ironic twists in the entire book.

The Anatomy of an Unraveling

A great review by Likely Story breaks down this exact dynamic, exploring how Alex's desperation blinds him to the trap he's walking into. As the reviewer put it:

"Watching a man who built his entire life on deception get spectacularly deceived himself was probably my favorite twist in the story."

Beyond the botched Brazilian deal, the review dives into the broader thematic core of The Weight of Snow: the toxic ripple effects of guilt on Alex’s children, the tension of knowing the killer's identity early on, and why running halfway around the world to the Akatarawa Forest can't free you from your own past.

If you enjoy fast-paced psychological thrillers featuring morally complex characters, dysfunctional family drama, and protagonists who make catastrophically bad life decisions, you can read the complete review below:

👉 Read the Full Review on Likely Story: https://t.co/TVepTVpzHr.

The Weight of Snow is available now. Have you ever read a thriller where you were secretly rooting for the protagonist to get outsmarted? Let me know in the comments below!

The core of this discovery lies in the X chromosome, which carries intelligence-related genes; since women possess two X chromosomes and men only one, mothers are twice as likely to pass these traits to their offspring. 

Furthermore, these maternal genes are specifically programmed to activate in the cerebral cortex, the brain's sophisticated center for memory, language, and complex reasoning. In contrast, genes inherited from the father tend to influence the limbic system, which governs more primal functions and physical development.

While these genetic insights emphasize the mother’s biological impact, researchers underscore that intelligence is not determined by DNA alone. The quality of early caregiving and the nurturing environment provided by both parents remain crucial factors in a child's cognitive growth. This study highlights a fascinating genetic blueprint where mothers provide the foundation for complex thought, while fathers support other vital developmental systems. Ultimately, this research offers a deeper understanding of how our cognitive abilities are shaped, reinforcing the powerful biological and environmental bond between a mother and her child.

text:
The Importance of Persistent Challenges

I used to measure my self-worth by how productive I felt on any given day. My identity was tied entirely to visible progress toward my long-term goals. While that’s still somewhat true, I’ve managed to find a proxy that keeps me grounded even when all else is in stalemate.

During college/early years of my career, I realized that very few professional metrics offer immediate clarity of progress. Working on deals felt like planting seeds in the dark and I constantly questioned whether it's amounting to anything meaningful.
To break out of that loop, I began leaning into smaller, self-contained pursuits like drawing, sports, restauranting, diving into history/tech, and running. Among all of them, building a consistent running routine turned out to be the highest-leverage decision I’ve ever made.

What makes running distinct is its objective clarity. Metrics like pace, heart rate, cadence, and recovery scores mapped directly to my physical effort. When work felt abstract, running provided instant proof of progress. It became a form of therapy. I never expect to be the best in my city or even my building, but because it offers a persistent, measurable challenge entirely disconnected from my career.

That drive led me to sign up for the Sydney Marathon. This is my second marathon overall, but my first World Major. To push myself further, I set a target time of sub-3:45. Balancing serious marathon training with an undefined venture role that requires constant travel meant running had to be integrated into my life. To hold myself accountable, I started documenting every single session. I’ve posted daily updates for the past two months on Instagram, and now I’m bringing that log over to Twitter as well. Why not?

text:
The New Space Race Is between SpaceX and China.

This time, America isn't competing against one government-run space program. In many ways, it is one company—SpaceX—competing against China's rapidly growing industrial ecosystem.

Love Elon Musk or hate him, SpaceX has accomplished something extraordinary. It has revolutionized rocket launches, dramatically lowered costs, built the world's largest satellite constellation with Starlink, and become the backbone of much of America's access to space.

Today, more than 10,000 Starlink satellites orbit Earth. SpaceX launches more rockets than anyone else and has become indispensable to NASA, the Pentagon, and U.S. intelligence agencies. Through Starshield, its military division, SpaceX is helping build next-generation communications, surveillance, and defense capabilities.

Space is no longer just about exploring Mars.

It's about controlling communications, navigation, intelligence, missile defense, AI infrastructure, and eventually the economic activity of Earth orbit and the Moon.

But here's what many investors may be overlooking.

China has learned from every industry it has entered.

First came solar panels.
Then batteries.
Then drones.
Then electric vehicles.
Now space.
China isn't trying to build one giant SpaceX. It is creating an entire ecosystem of competing launch companies, satellite manufacturers, AI developers, and aerospace startups backed by one of the world's largest manufacturing bases.
If history repeats itself, China won't necessarily invent everything first. It will improve manufacturing, reduce costs, scale production, and compete aggressively across the global market.
That's exactly what happened with electric vehicles.
Many investors assume SpaceX's valuation can only keep climbing. Maybe it can—but there are real risks that deserve attention.

A valuation exceeding $2 trillion assumes SpaceX will continue dominating launch services, satellite internet, and future space infrastructure for many years.

But what happens if:

• China builds reusable rockets that are almost as good but significantly cheaper?
• Chinese satellite constellations offer competitive global internet service?
• Countries decide they don't want to rely on a single American company for critical communications?
• Governments diversify their launch providers instead of depending so heavily on one company?
• Increased competition puts pressure on launch prices and satellite margins?

History shows that technology leaders don't always remain dominant forever.

IBM was once considered untouchable.
Nokia dominated mobile phones.
BlackBerry ruled smartphones.
Intel seemed impossible to challenge.
Even Tesla is now facing intense global competition.

SpaceX still has enormous technological advantages, incredible engineering talent, and years of experience. None of that should be underestimated.

But China's greatest strength has never been a single breakthrough.
Its strength is relentless manufacturing, rapid iteration, scale, and the ability to mobilize enormous resources around strategic industries.
The next decade may not determine who reaches Mars first.
It may determine who controls the infrastructure of the 21st century—from satellites and communications to navigation, AI, and the future economy in space.
This isn't just another technology story.

It may become one of the most important geopolitical and investment stories of our lifetime.

text:
If you wanna read my take on this summer's hottest blockbuster...

I saw Christopher Nolan’s "The Odyssey" at Yonge and Dundas — or Sankofa Square, depending on which layer of Toronto’s civic memory one chooses to invoke.

It was an appropriate place to encounter one of our civilization’s oldest stories of homecoming. The square is itself an act of interpretation. Its new name comes from an Akan idea often translated as “go back and get it”: retrieve what should not be lost and use it to build a better future.

That is also what every adaptation of a classic attempts.

I first read "The Odyssey" in “The Western Tradition”, a Great Books course at the University of Toronto premised on the idea that Western civilization is a conversation carried on across centuries. A year later, in a second-year English course, we read Virgil’s "Aeneid".

I was taught to see Aeneas fleeing Troy with his father, Anchises, on his back and his young son before him: the past carried as a duty, the future leading him onward. Aeneas bears history’s weight while trying to found something new.

Odysseus appears to travel in the opposite direction. Aeneas leaves a destroyed home to build another. Odysseus spends ten years trying to return to the one he already has. Or, as Joyce would put it, “Longest way round is the shortest way home”.

Yet one pleasure of returning to these works is realizing how little their stories remain confined to the books whose titles we remember. Much of what we think of as the story of "The Odyssey” comes from the wider cycle surrounding the Trojan War and from later poets and dramatists who rearranged the tradition.

The Trojan Horse appears in "The Odyssey", but not as the sustained dramatic episode modern audiences imagine. The version embedded in our cultural memory owes at least as much to Virgil’s account of Troy’s destruction in "The Aeneid". Nolan’s incorporation of Sinon, who persuades the Trojans to bring the horse inside their walls, owes more to Virgil than Homer.

Odysseus himself changes from writer to writer: hero, liar, strategist, criminal, survivor and damned counsellor of fraud.

There has never been only one Odysseus. No story of consequence is ever told only once.

This is why arguments over whether Nolan has been “faithful” to Homer miss the point. We cannot unlearn Virgil, Aeschylus, Dante, Tennyson, Joyce or the countless painted, staged and filmed Odysseys that shape what we expect the story to contain.

Nolan has gone back and retrieved the parts he wants.

His Odysseus is not simply Homer’s endlessly adaptable, boastful and morally elusive man. He is a modern Nolan protagonist: a brilliant man forced to confront what his brilliance has wrought. The Trojan Horse becomes more than the stratagem that wins a war. It is a violation that corrupts the victory itself.

Like Nolan’s "Oppenheimer", Odysseus can change history but cannot control what follows. Modern audiences prefer great men chastened by guilt and capable of recognizing the suffering their ambition caused.

But Nolan’s more interesting departure comes at the end. Odysseus returns to Ithaca, destroys the men who have occupied his household and reunites with Penelope. Yet he does not resume his throne. He and Penelope leave. Telemachus is left to govern.

The homecoming becomes a transfer of power.

In that sense, Nolan has made "The Odyssey" into an "Aeneid" in reverse. Odysseus returns from Troy only to discover that restoration is impossible. The old king may reclaim the palace, but the future belongs to the son, to the next generation.

This is also the political truth at the heart of every promise to restore a country, institution or community.

“Again” may be the most powerful word in modern democratic politics. It promises that disorder is temporary, decline reversible and home still waiting exactly as we left it. We will restore prosperity, recover common sense, rebuild trust, take back control or return civic life to an earlier age of competence and civility.

The politics of restoration is powerful because it disguises change as return.

But no one returns to an unchanged Ithaca.

Odysseus has been away for twenty years. Telemachus has grown into adulthood. Penelope has preserved the household through intelligence, caution and her own capacity for deception. Even after the suitors are killed, their families demand vengeance and Ithaca approaches civil war.

Victory does not settle the question of legitimacy. It merely creates the circumstances in which the question must be answered.

That lesson matters as the United States approaches the 2028 election. A post-Trump America cannot be created simply by reinstalling a pre-Trump politics. Defeating one leader or movement will not by itself repair weakened institutions, civic habits and public trust. The question is what is rebuilt and toward what end. The United States needs not a homecoming alone but rather a second reconstruction.

Every institution constructs a story about its origins and the moment before everything supposedly went wrong. Communities require continuity, but restoration is always an act of interpretation.

We decide which past to recover, which inheritance to carry and which parts to leave behind. We call the result a return because that is less frightening than admitting we are founding something new.

Homer understands that killing the suitors is not enough. Odysseus must still be recognized. Penelope tests him by ordering that their marriage bed be moved. Odysseus knows this is impossible because he built it around a living olive tree.

His strength does not establish his identity. Nor does his victory. He is recognized because he remembers how the household was built.

That is a better account of political legitimacy than the triumphal restoration promised by so many would-be homecomers. Authority cannot merely announce that it has returned. It must show that it still understands the people and foundations that kept the community alive in its absence — and recognize that those people have changed, too.

The meaning of Sankofa is not that we should go backward. It is that we may have to return to retrieve something necessary for moving forward.

There is an irony in encountering that idea in a public square whose new name replaced the one by which generations knew it. The city sought to elevate a concept about learning from the past even as it rewrote the past. One need not defend every inherited commemoration to worry about public memory being treated as a blackboard to be wiped clean.

Joyce called history “a nightmare from which I am trying to awake”. Faulkner replied, in effect, that the past is never dead; "it is not even past". Sankofa offers a third possibility: the past is neither a destination nor merely a burden. It is something from which we retrieve wisdom, identity and obligation.

Perhaps that is the connection between Aeneas and Odysseus. The founder and the homecomer are engaged in the same political work. Each must decide what can be saved from the ruins, what must be carried and what future should inherit it.

Aeneas carries his father and leads his son. Nolan’s Odysseus finally yields Ithaca to his son.

No one simply returns home. The traveller has changed. The household has changed. Even the story of the home has been rewritten by those who preserved it.

We go back and get what we need. Then, carrying the past without being imprisoned by it, we make the home anew.

5. Troy Nyhammer🇳🇴 (19/8/2006)

• The Bømlo native has enjoyed an impressive 2026 season so far, establishing himself as one of Tromsø’s most exciting young attacking players. Still only 19 years old, Nyhammer has already contributed with 3 goals and 2 assists for a Tromsø side looking to close the gap on Norwegian football’s two dominant forces, Viking and Bodø/Glimt. 

• Having the ability to operate both as a winger and as a striker, he provides versatility in the final third and has shown signs of becoming a valuable attacking weapon at the highest level of Norwegian football.

• While many young wide players rely primarily on pace and direct running, Nyhammer offers a more complete profile. He is comfortable receiving the ball in different areas of the pitch, capable of creating from wider positions while also possessing the physical qualities needed to compete closer to goal. His ability to contribute both as a creator and as a finisher makes him an intriguing modern forward profile.

• His underlying numbers highlight a player with a unique skill set. Among forwards in similar leagues, Nyhammer ranks in the 100th percentile for aerial duels won, showing his ability to compete physically despite his age. He also ranks highly for his quality on the ball, sitting in the 89th percentile for successful crosses, 84th percentile for big chances created, and 87th percentile for accurate long balls. 

• These numbers underline a player who is not only involved in finishing attacks, but also in creating opportunities for those around him.

• One of Nyhammer’s biggest strengths is his ability to influence the game in multiple phases. His aerial ability gives Tromsø an additional outlet when progressing the ball, while his crossing and passing range allow him to create danger from wider areas. He has shown an ability to recognize spaces and deliver quality passes into dangerous areas, something that separates him from many young attackers who are still primarily focused on individual actions. His versatility also allows Tromsø to adjust his role depending on the opponent, whether that means starting wide and attacking inside spaces or playing closer to the box as a striker.

• Still only 19 years old, Nyhammer is far from the finished product. Like many young attackers, consistency and decision-making in the final third will continue to develop with more experience. Playing regularly at Eliteserien level, while also gaining exposure in European competition, will provide valuable learning experiences that should accelerate his progression.

• With more minutes against stronger opposition, Nyhammer has the tools to continue developing into a highly interesting attacking prospect. His combination of physical strength, creativity and technical quality gives him a profile that stands out, and if his development continues on its current trajectory, he could become the latest young Norwegian attacker to make the step towards a higher level.

text:
Alternative Asset Tokenization season

Tokenization is starting to reach assets most investors have never been able to access directly.

Real estate income. Private credit. Gold. Art. Watches. Even graded Pokémon cards.

Now the tokenized asset does three things:

→ Produces income from real underlying assets.

→ Settles and transfers onchain.

→ Becomes usable collateral in DeFi.

That is why tokenized alternatives matter to the world of finance, you’ll see the impact real soon.

This part of the RWA market interests me because the addressable market is much larger than what is currently onchain.

Global alternatives and private-market AUM could exceed $30T by 2030.

Meanwhile, current onchain value remains small:

→ Tokenized credit: ~$6.93B

→ Tokenized commodities: ~$7.46B

→ Tokenized real estate: ~$203M 

The gap is huge, but each asset class requires a different structure.

[1] Real estate tokens usually represent equity in an SPV that owns the property.

Investors receive rental income and part of the final sale proceeds.

@Reental_co + @lofty_ai already offer access to individual US properties from around $50 + also distributes rental income daily.

[2] Commodities use a more direct model.

One PAXG represents one fine troy ounce of gold held in a London vault.

@tethergold | XAUT and @KinesisMonetary provides a similar claim on allocated physical gold.
Investors gain onchain exposure without managing storage themselves.

[3] Collectibles are where the concept gets more interesting.

@Courtyard_io stores physical cards, comics and watches, then issues an NFT for each item.

The holder can trade the NFT or burn it to receive the physical asset.

@Collector_Crypt applies the same model to graded Pokémon cards on Solana.

Its cumulative volume passed $1B in May 2026, and some card NFTs can already be used as collateral to borrow USDC.

These 2 interesting protocols i’m watching as well = @4KProtocol @freeportmarkets

[4] Private credit is the category I’m watching most closely.

The global private credit market is estimated at $1.5T-$2T, while only around $6.93B is currently tokenized.

The products also have clear cash flows from interest and principal repayments.

Apollo’s ACRED provides tokenized access to an existing diversified credit fund.

Janus Henderson’s JAAA gives eligible investors exposure to AAA-rated CLO tranches.

@maplefinance's syrupUSDC and syrupUSDT deploy stablecoins into institutional loans and other strategies.

Some of these assets can already be posted as collateral in onchain lending markets.

Eligible ACRED holders, for example, can use sACRED on @Morpho or Drift Institutional to borrow USDC.

That is the point where tokenization becomes more useful to me.

The asset can generate income, settle onchain and support additional financial activity after issuance.

Still, I would never evaluate these products by token supply or TVL alone.

A token does not remove the risks attached to the underlying asset.

It only changes how ownership, cash flows and transfers are managed.

I think tokenized treasuries proved that regulated financial assets can operate onchain.

Alternative assets are the next serious test.

If the legal rights, custody and secondary liquidity work, crypto could open access to a major part of the financial market that has historically been limited to institutions and wealthy investors.

That is a much bigger RWA thesis than putting another asset ticker onchain.

text:
I think you pretty much hit the nail on the head.  I've been a Utah member most of my life, except for 4 years in New Orleans and 4 years in Phoenix.  

Let me offer an additional thought...

In Utah, you see church members - even ward members - everywhere!  We see each other at church, at McDonald's, at the mall, at the grocery store, at UPS, at work, at school assemblies, at sporting events, etc. etc. etc.

Over time, interacting so often tends to result in a "sameness" in members that you don't see so much elsewhere.

It's like tossing a bunch of rocks into an enclosed tumbler.  Eventually, all the edges get knocked off, and they end up looking a lot alike.

And, over time, the "sameness" can be perceived as "rightness" or "correctness" - the right way to look, the right way to act, the right way to dress, to think, to talk...

But, we're a global church now.  There's nothing "wrong" with the "Utah way," it just doesn't necessarily fit all nations, kindreds, tongues, and people around the world.

Doctrine shouldn't be compromised, but there are a fair number of practices that are quasi-policy, custom, habit, and culture that get ingrained over the generations in the rock tumbler that is Utah.
