text:
COUNTRY TREATMENT AND TRUSTED-SUPPLIER ARCHITECTURE

The policy is global rather than China-specific. Products from Japan, South Korea, Taiwan, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, and EU member states are not exempt. Instead, their ordinary Column 1 tariff plus the additional Section 232 tariff is capped at a combined 15 percent. Most covered products currently have low ordinary tariffs, making the effective rate close to 15 percent. UK products receive a 10 percent additional tariff. Products from countries without special treatment generally face the full 15 percent additional tariff on top of ordinary duties. (The White House)

Canada and Mexico are included as trade-agreement partners for manufacturing-drawback purposes but do not receive a special reduced Section 232 rate in the proclamation. USMCA preference does not eliminate the new duties because Annex II states that free-trade preferences do not provide an exemption. This distinction may be relevant for solar and semiconductor supply chains using North American processing hubs. (The White House)

Manufacturing drawback is available only when the imported article is not a type subject to an antidumping or countervailing duty order, originates in a listed trade-agreement partner, and contains polysilicon entirely originating in a partner country. The partner list includes the United Kingdom, EU, Japan, South Korea, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Mexico, and Canada. Taiwan is omitted despite receiving the 15 percent country-rate treatment. This creates a potentially material asymmetry for Taiwanese semiconductor wafers used in U.S.-manufactured chips that are subsequently exported. The omission may reflect intentional trade-policy differentiation or may become a candidate for technical correction. (The White House)

Foreign-trade-zone treatment is also restrictive. Covered foreign products generally must enter a zone under privileged foreign status, preserving the original tariff classification and preventing duty avoidance through subsequent processing inside the zone. This limits the ability of companies to use U.S. foreign-trade zones to transform imported cells or wafers into ostensibly different articles before customs entry. (The White House)

The administration may reduce or modify the tariffs for trading partners that establish substantially equivalent minimum import prices. This provision creates the potential for a trusted-supplier price bloc rather than a purely U.S. price island. Japan, South Korea, the EU, and other partners could adopt parallel floors, reduce global trade diversion, and receive more favorable U.S. treatment. Such arrangements would strengthen non-Chinese supply-chain economics but could also dilute the relative scarcity premium for U.S. producers.

SEMICONDUCTOR STRATEGIC RATIONALE

The national-security rationale is economically coherent even though the policy primarily affects solar. Semiconductor-grade polysilicon represents only approximately 2.4 percent of total polysilicon demand, while solar-grade material represents approximately 97.6 percent. Electronic-grade material requires at least 11N purity, compared with approximately 6N-10N for solar material, and can cost as much as 30x more to produce. Hemlock and Wacker account for approximately 75 percent of the semiconductor-grade market. Maintaining large-scale solar-grade output helps absorb fixed costs, preserve specialized purification capabilities, support workforce continuity, and sustain the equipment base required for electronic-grade production. (Semiconductor Industry Association)

The proclamation therefore uses the large solar market to subsidize the industrial foundation of the much smaller semiconductor-grade market. Without viable solar-grade volume, a domestic producer can retain electronic-grade capability only at higher unit cost and lower utilization. The policy attempts to prevent Chinese solar-scale economics from eventually migrating into electronic-grade material and undermining the remaining U.S. strategic supplier.

China represented approximately 94.7 percent of global polysilicon production capacity in the SIA analysis, with approximately 98 percent of Chinese capacity directed toward solar-grade production. Chinese manufacturers were assessed as lacking the equipment and know-how to produce electronic-grade polysilicon at scale at that time. The administration is acting before Chinese solar producers complete the technology, quality, and customer-qualification progression required to compete in semiconductor-grade material. (Semiconductor Industry Association)

SEMICONDUCTOR WAFER IMPACT

The immediate semiconductor impact is more negative than the raw-polysilicon headline suggests. Advanced electronic-grade polysilicon is already valued far above $21/kg, making the raw-material floor largely irrelevant for qualified semiconductor supply. Semiconductor wafers, however, are included in the $100/kg floor and the 15 percent downstream tariff. The ad valorem duty is likely to be the principal cost mechanism for advanced 200mm and 300mm wafers.

The United States imported approximately $1.528B of silicon wafers in 2024. Japan supplied approximately $624.7M, Taiwan $202.1M, South Korea $184.7M, China $140.9M, Germany $117.3M, France $69.9M, and other countries $188.1M. A static 15 percent duty on the full import base would equal approximately $229M before drawback, exclusions, changes in sourcing, or country-specific ordinary duties. China represented only approximately 9.2 percent of the import value, meaning that more than 90 percent of the gross tariff incidence would initially fall on allied or other non-Chinese supply.

The U.S. semiconductor industry cannot rapidly replace these imports. Domestic wafer capacity is insufficient for rising demand, particularly for advanced 300mm wafers used in AI and high-performance computing. Silicon wafers require extensive qualification by the wafer supplier, fab, process node, and end customer. Substitution cannot be achieved through simple commodity procurement. The near-term result is a modest increase in wafer cost, greater customs complexity, additional inventory buffers, and potential qualification risk for Intel, Micron, GlobalFoundries, TSMC Arizona, Samsung’s U.S. operations, Texas Instruments, and other domestic fabs. (Semiconductor Industry Association)

The direct gross-margin effect on advanced chip manufacturers should be manageable because wafer cost is a limited portion of the value of leading-edge logic, memory, and analog devices. The more important risks are supply continuity, customs delays, inventory working capital, and the inability to switch qualified suppliers quickly. Fabs may increase strategic wafer inventories ahead of Dec 4, although the stockpiling provision limits aggressive accumulation.

Longer duration, the policy is positive for U.S. wafer investment by GlobalWafers, Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, and other suppliers with domestic capacity. Existing U.S. facilities receive a pricing advantage, while future expansions can seek onshoring relief for equipment and intermediate materials. The near-term tax on allied imports is the cost of creating a larger domestic wafer base.

SEMICONDUCTOR EQUIPMENT AND COMPONENT READ-THROUGHS

Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA, ASML, and Tokyo Electron should experience limited direct impact because the proclamation does not materially change semiconductor process intensity, lithography demand, deposition and etch steps, metrology requirements, or advanced-packaging complexity. The 2nd-order effect is positive if domestic wafer and polysilicon projects generate incremental capital-equipment demand.

Production-equipment relief under approved onshoring plans could reduce the cost of importing crystal-growth furnaces, wafer-slicing equipment, cell-production equipment, metrology systems, and related manufacturing tools. The benefit is more relevant for specialized wafer and solar-cell equipment vendors than for leading-edge wafer-fabrication equipment companies.

The proclamation may also provide a template for broader semiconductor trade policy. The company-specific plans, construction-period import relief, external audits, milestone requirements, and retroactive rescission mechanism could be applied in future semiconductor or semiconductor-equipment tariff programs. The current action therefore has significance beyond the narrow polysilicon chain.

AI DATA-CENTER POWER IMPLICATIONS

The principal TMT externality is power availability rather than semiconductor input cost. Solar and storage represented approximately 91 percent of new U.S. generating capacity added in Q1 2026, with solar alone representing approximately 60 percent. Utility-scale solar contracting reached 6.3GWdc in Q1, led by data and technology companies. Higher module prices can therefore raise the cost of power-purchase agreements and potentially delay energization schedules for hyperscalers and data-center operators. (SEIA)

Amazon, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, Oracle, CoreWeave, and large colocation operators will not experience a material consolidated earnings impact from a modest increase in solar-module cost. The more relevant exposure is localized. In power-constrained markets, a delayed solar project can delay interconnection, reduce available generation, increase reliance on gas or storage, and postpone data-center revenue. The value of power availability can substantially exceed the incremental module cost.

The near-term risk is moderated by the 216GW-240GW safe-harbored solar pipeline supporting deployment through 2030. Projects with secured tax status, procured modules, and advanced construction schedules have greater protection. The larger impact should emerge in post-2027 projects that have not fixed module pricing or secured tariff treatment. (SEIA)

The proclamation creates an industrial-policy tradeoff. It strengthens the domestic material base supporting semiconductor production but raises the cost of one of the fastest-deployable sources of electricity needed by AI infrastructure. The administration is prioritizing supply-chain security over minimum near-term power cost.

CORNING

Corning is the highest-quality and best risk-adjusted listed beneficiary. The Solar segment includes Hemlock Semiconductor, solar-wafer operations, and module manufacturing. Q2 2026 Solar revenue was $438M, up 90 percent year over year, while the segment generated a $7M net loss. Q1 Solar revenue was $370M with $7M of net income. H1 Solar revenue was therefore $808M with approximately breakeven aggregate earnings. The segment is already large enough for policy-driven margin improvement to be material but is not yet earning a normalized return. (Corning Investor Relations)

Annualizing Q2 Solar revenue produces an approximate $1.75B run rate. Each 1-point increase in net margin would represent approximately $17.5M of annual segment earnings, while a 5-point improvement would represent approximately $87.6M before considering ownership allocation, taxes, and corporate reconciliation. The combination of near-breakeven profitability and rising volume creates significant incremental operating leverage.

The $21/kg polysilicon floor is less favorable than the preliminary market may have anticipated. It is only moderately above current non-Chinese pricing and below the $24/kg fair-value estimate. Hemlock’s principal benefit is therefore likely to come from improved utilization, customer commitments, waiver preferences for U.S. polysilicon, and protection of downstream Corning wafers rather than from a large increase in raw-polysilicon price.

The $100/kg wafer floor is substantially more valuable. Corning’s domestic wafer operations gain protection against imported wafers currently priced at a fraction of the minimum. This can improve utilization, pricing, and returns on recently deployed capital. The policy also reduces the probability that Corning’s domestic wafer investment is stranded by low-cost Asian imports.

The onshoring program’s ability to favor imported cells and wafers made with U.S. polysilicon provides a potentially durable volume channel for Hemlock. T1, Canadian Solar, Qcells, and other companies seeking duty relief could be incentivized to contract for Hemlock material even when conversion occurs outside the United States. Hemlock becomes a strategic input to waiver eligibility rather than merely a commodity supplier.

Corning’s module operations could still face cell-sourcing risk. The Solar segment includes polysilicon, wafers, and modules, but disclosed segment information does not establish a fully domestic cell chain. Imported cells without waiver protection could create a near-term cost increase. This prevents treating the entire Solar segment as unambiguously positive.

The larger consolidated context is favorable. Optical Communications generated $2.072B of Q2 sales, up 32 percent year over year, compared with $438M for Solar. The core GLW investment thesis remains AI data-center optical connectivity and enterprise-network growth. Polysilicon policy adds a potentially valuable earnings accelerator without making the consolidated thesis dependent on solar. (Corning Investor Relations)

The principal risks are excessive module-price inflation, solar-project cancellations, inability to secure domestic cells, delayed customer qualification, and a policy adjustment that lowers minimum prices or grants broad partner-country relief. The balance of risk remains clearly positive.

T1 ENERGY

T1 has the highest policy convexity and the greatest implementation risk. G1 Dallas is expected to produce toward the upper end of the company’s 3.1GW-4.2GW 2026 range, supported by the qualification of international cell suppliers. G2 Austin Phase 1 is intended to provide domestic cells, but 1st production has shifted to Q1 2027. The Section 232 regime begins Dec 4, 2026, creating an immediate transition gap and a potentially much longer commercial-ramp gap during which G1 remains dependent on imported cells. (SEC)

Absent onshoring relief, the economics could become severely negative. T1 expects Q2 sales of $245M-$255M on 835MW of modules, equivalent to approximately $0.293-$0.305/W. An imported cell priced at the current $0.04/W benchmark would carry a direct Section 232-adjusted cost of approximately $0.226/W. The cell alone would equal approximately 74-77 percent of T1’s recent module revenue per watt before glass, frame, encapsulant, labor, depreciation, logistics, warranty, and overhead. This is not a viable unwaived cost structure. (SEC)

T1 is therefore an onshoring-waiver trade, not merely a tariff-beneficiary trade. If Commerce recognizes G2 Austin as newly committed investment and permits duty-free cells during construction, T1 could import cells at low cost, sell modules into a protected $0.38-$0.45/W market, monetize Section 45X credits, and transition into domestic cells as G2 ramps. This would generate powerful margin expansion and improve financing capacity.

If G2 is excluded because it was already under construction, T1 could face a severe cost shock before domestic output is available. Steel work was already approximately 80 percent complete before the proclamation, and capex guidance had increased from $425M to $510M. The company had only $79.1M of unrestricted cash at Jun 30 and was seeking a comprehensive financing package with a significant debt component. Policy support improves the potential value of G2, but the waiver’s retroactive-rescission provisions could complicate lender underwriting. (SEC)

Legacy contract treatment is another material risk. T1’s imported cells are transformed rather than resold. Existing module contracts below $0.38/W may not qualify for the legacy resale exception under the literal language of Annex II. Without clarification, T1 could owe cell-level minimum-price duties or be required to sell resulting modules at the floor despite fixed customer pricing.

The operating leverage is substantial. Each $0.01/W of incremental net spread on 3.1GW-4.2GW of annual production represents approximately $31M-$42M of gross profit. A $0.05/W improvement represents approximately $155M-$210M. This compares with preliminary Q2 adjusted EBITDA of negative $11.5M-negative $14.5M, excluding $24.4M of IEEPA tariff refunds. Trade-policy treatment can therefore dominate underlying operating performance. (SEC)

The risk-adjusted conclusion is conditional rather than outright positive. Waiver approval, qualifying import volumes, timing, and recognition of existing investment are required before the proclamation becomes clearly accretive. The equity offers substantial event-driven upside but should not be treated as a low-risk domestic-manufacturing beneficiary.

CANADIAN SOLAR

Canadian Solar has substantial U.S. manufacturing exposure but a more complicated consolidated transmission mechanism. The company expects 6.5GW-7.0GW of U.S. module shipments in 2026. Its Indiana HJT cell facility began Phase 1 trial production in Apr 2026 with 2.1GW of nameplate capacity. Phase 2 is expected to add 4.2GW beginning in early 2027, bringing total planned U.S. cell capacity to 6.3GW. (Canadian Solar Inc.)

Phase 1 capacity covers only approximately 30-32 percent of guided 2026 U.S. module shipments. Canadian Solar will remain dependent on imported cells during the ramp and on imported silicon wafers even after domestic HJT cells are available. HJT technology still requires crystalline silicon wafers, making the $100/kg wafer floor highly relevant.

An approved onshoring plan could make CSIQ a significant beneficiary. Phase 2 and further expansions provide credible domestic-investment commitments, while duty-free wafer and cell imports during construction would preserve the economics of U.S. module output. Canadian Solar could then sell into a protected market as domestic cell capacity approaches its module shipment requirement.

The phrase “newly committed investment” again creates uncertainty. Phase 2 had been publicly announced before Aug 6. Commerce could recognize future construction spending and capacity as newly committed, but the proclamation does not guarantee this treatment. Canadian Solar may need to commit incremental capacity or additional upstream investment.

The earnings leverage is large. Each $0.01/W of additional net U.S. spread on 6.5GW-7.0GW of shipments represents approximately $65M-$70M of gross profit. A $0.05/W improvement represents approximately $325M-$350M. However, the same leverage applies negatively if imported wafers and cells face full duties while customer contracts limit price pass-through.

The company’s Q1 2026 results demonstrate the magnitude of tariff-accounting volatility. Reported gross profit was $271M and gross margin was 25.1 percent, including a $93M IEEPA tariff-refund benefit. Excluding the refund and using the reported $1.1B revenue figure, underlying gross margin was approximately 16 percent. A nonrecurring trade-policy item represented roughly 9 points of reported margin. (Canadian Solar Inc.)

Canadian Solar also faces heightened compliance risk because of its multinational, related-party manufacturing structure. The 1st arm’s-length sale requirement, anti-transfer-pricing authority, polysilicon-origin tracing, and permanent affiliate import ban increase the consequences of customs disputes. The company’s U.S. operating structure and 75.1 percent-owned domestic joint venture will require careful separation of customs, ownership, and certification responsibilities. (Canadian Solar Inc.)

Recurrent Energy creates an internal offset. The business had a solar-development pipeline of approximately 23.7GW and a storage-development pipeline of approximately 80.6GWh. Higher module costs can reduce project returns, require PPA renegotiation, delay notice to proceed, and lower asset-sale values. Manufacturing margin gains can therefore be partially offset by development-margin losses. (Canadian Solar Inc.)

Balance-sheet leverage increases sensitivity. Total debt and financing liabilities were $6.8B, including $3.8B at Recurrent Energy and $2.6B in manufacturing. Higher tariffs can increase inventory deposits, customs bonds, working capital, and project financing needs before price increases are collected from customers. (Canadian Solar Inc.)

The consolidated conclusion is mixed to moderately positive under an effective waiver regime and potentially negative during the transition without relief. CSIQ has more domestic assets than many competitors but also more imported-input, project-development, financing, and compliance exposure.

DAQO NEW ENERGY

Daqo is the clearest strategic loser from the proclamation. The $21/kg U.S. minimum is approximately 252 percent above Daqo’s Q1 2026 average selling price of $5.96/kg. The policy creates a high-priced U.S. market inaccessible to Chinese polysilicon while leaving Daqo exposed to the oversupplied Chinese and non-U.S. markets. (SEC)

The action does not directly reduce a large existing U.S. revenue stream because Daqo principally sells to China-based photovoltaic manufacturers. The impact is transmitted through its customers. Wafers, cells, and modules containing Chinese material become less competitive or ineligible for preferred treatment in the United States, reducing the strategic value of Daqo’s output to exporters targeting the U.S. market.

Market segmentation may worsen Chinese oversupply. If domestic and trusted-supplier polysilicon earns a premium in the United States, Chinese production remains concentrated in China, Europe, emerging markets, and other lower-priced destinations. The U.S. floor does not establish a global floor and may widen the price differential between Chinese and non-Chinese material.

Daqo’s operating data already reflect severe imbalance. Q1 production was 43,402MT, while sales were only 4,482MT, equal to approximately 10.3 percent of production. Average selling price of $5.96/kg was effectively equal to average total production cost of $5.95/kg. The company recorded a $139.4M gross loss and negative 521.5 percent gross margin, primarily because of inventory impairment. (SEC)

The U.S. policy reinforces the strategic rationale for Daqo to pursue Chinese consolidation, capacity curtailments, semiconductor-grade development, or greater downstream integration. However, qualification into electronic-grade polysilicon and semiconductor wafers requires process consistency, customer validation, equipment, and know-how that cannot be inferred from solar-grade scale.

The balance sheet materially reduces short-side asymmetry. Daqo had approximately $2.0B of cash and cash-like assets at Mar 31, providing the ability to endure a prolonged downturn, hold inventory, fund technology investment, or participate in domestic industry consolidation. Chinese anti-involution policy and coordinated capacity reductions could improve Daqo’s realized pricing independently of the U.S. action. (SEC)

DQ is therefore a high-conviction structural underperformer relative to U.S. domestic beneficiaries but a lower-conviction absolute short. The cleaner expression is a relative position against Corning or other protected domestic suppliers rather than a large unhedged short exposed to Chinese policy intervention.

text:
Another University Faces Trump Investigation Over ‘Preferences For Non-Whites’
The university received over $400 million in federal grant money this year.

The Trump administration launched an investigation into an Oregon university over multiple racially focused programs critics say run afoul of civil rights law, The Daily Wire has learned. 
The Office for Civil Rights at the Department of Health and Human Services will investigate accusations that the Portland-based Oregon Health and Science University offers programs with built-in “preferences for non-whites.” The investigation comes after a complaint from the Equal Protection Project, an organization devoted to ensuring people of all races are treated fairly. 

HHS told the Equal Protection Project last week that it had “determined that this office has jurisdiction over your allegations” and that it “will initiate an investigation,” according to a letter obtained by The Daily Wire. The letter added that when HHS “has reached a determination regarding your complaint, we will advise you of our findings.”
Oregon Health and Science University recently announced that it received over $400 million in federal research grants for 2026.

The complaint from the Equal Protection Project took issue with multiple programs offered by the university, including its Jump Start Program, Equity Research Program, Center for Learner Diversity and Inclusion, On Track OHSU, Pay it Forward Mentorship Program, and HealthE STEPS Nursing Workforce Diversity Scholarships.
The Jump Start Program is designed for post=baccalaureate scholars to gain research experience. Those who are encouraged to apply are those defined as “underrepresented in research,” including “those who identify as minorities.” 
Similarly, the Equity Research Program is for those who come from an “underrepresented minority group” or have another economic hardship. The university’s Center for Learner Diversity and Inclusion “creates programs to advance the academic, career and personal development of underrepresented minority and disadvantaged students.”

Cornell Law School Professor William Jacobson, the founder of the Equal Protection Project, told The Daily Wire that the university was deterring people from applying for certain opportunities because they were advertising them for “being for a certain race or a certain ethnicity.” He said he would like to see the programs reformed, not eliminated. 
“Our goal for every time I challenge a program or a scholarship or goal is not to terminate the program or scholarship, it’s to terminate the discriminatory aspects of it,” Jacobson told The Daily Wire. “Ideally for us they would have to rework these scholarships and programs, and they would have to eliminate the racial and ethnic descriptors as to who it’s intended for, and they would have to truly, in real life, open it up to everybody.”
The Trump administration has taken action against racially focused DEI programs, opening up similar investigations into other entities like Arizona State University and the University of California system.

text:
When preparation meets opportunity, success becomes inevitable.

Alex Otti’s emergence in Abia is a powerful reminder of what leadership can look like when a governor’s primary accountability is to the people—not to a political godfather. Otti won the 2023 Abia governorship election with 175,467 votes and has since pursued an agenda built around infrastructure, public finances and institutional reform.

This is why Nigerians must reject political godfatherism. A leader who owes his political survival to the electorate is more likely to listen to the electorate. But when a leader owes his position to a godfather, the interest of the people can become secondary to maintaining that political relationship.

Rivers State offers a painful contrast. The prolonged political battle between Nyesom Wike and his successor, Siminalayi Fubara, exposed how godfather–successor struggles can consume governance and create institutional instability. The crisis became so severe that it culminated in the declaration of a state of emergency in March 2025.

The lesson is simple: the electorate should be the only godfather a public office holder needs.

Give us leaders who fear disappointing the people more than disappointing a political godfather. That is how democracy produces accountability—and how societies make progress.

text:
Confession, or the Sacrament of Reconciliation, is a profound gift in the Catholic faith. It is the place where we encounter God’s boundless mercy, allowing us to heal our relationship with Him and the Church. Spiritually, it restores sanctifying grace and strengthens us against temptation. Mentally, it offers a release from the weight of guilt, bringing clarity and peace. text:
⚠️ New York vs Kalshi: The Biggest Prediction Market Fight Yet

Okay fellas, let’s break this down simply.

New York just sued @, one of the biggest prediction market platforms in the US, calling it an illegal gambling operation. They’re trying to shut it down and hit them with massive penalties.

Here’s what’s actually going on.

🔸What Happened

On July 31, 2026, New York Governor Kathy Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James filed a lawsuit in Manhattan state court against Kalshi.

Their claim:
- Kalshi lets people trade contracts on sports, elections, culture, and other events
- New York says these are just bets in disguise
- Kalshi never got a gambling license from the New York State Gaming Commission
- They allow users as young as 18 (New York’s sports betting age is 21)
- They’re not paying the same high taxes that licensed sportsbooks and casinos pay

New York wants:
- A permanent ban on Kalshi operating in the state
- Full restitution to users
- Forfeiture of all profits
- 3x damages + $100,000 for every alleged sports betting attempt
- Potential total penalties: at least $36 billion

That’s higher than Kalshi’s reported valuation.

🔸The Backstory

This didn’t come out of nowhere.

New York previously sent Kalshi a cease-and-desist. Kalshi sued back in federal court trying to block the state. The judge said no. Then a federal appeals court also denied Kalshi’s emergency request.

Now New York is going all-in with a state court lawsuit.

Meanwhile, the CFTC (the federal regulator that oversees Kalshi as a designated contract market) is trying to stop New York from enforcing this. They argue states can’t just shut down a federally regulated exchange.

🔸The $10 Billion Twist

This is the part that got everyone talking.

According to the Wall Street Journal and Kalshi’s CEO, the company offered New York a tax deal that could bring in nearly $10 billion over five years - money that could go to schools, healthcare, and other public services.

New York turned it down and sued instead.

Governor Hochul’s response was clear:

> “Kalshi can promise 100% of its revenue.  
> You can’t buy yourself an exemption from New York law.  
> If an illegal bookie offers the state a share of their profits, we’ll still shut them down.”

🔸 Kalshi’s Side

@Kalshi calls the lawsuit political theater and an egregious overreach.

They point out that New York residents are currently up ~$200 million net on Kalshi this year, while being down ~$200 million net on traditional sportsbooks.

Their argument is simple: They’re a federally regulated exchange, not a sportsbook. States shouldn’t be able to kill a CFTC-approved platform.

🔸Why This Matters

This isn’t just about one company.

Prediction markets sit in a gray zone:
- Federally regulated as event contracts / derivatives by the CFTC
- States treat anything that looks like betting on sports (and sometimes more) as gambling that needs a state license and high taxes

If New York wins big, other states could follow. If Kalshi (and the CFTC) win, it strengthens the case that prediction markets are financial instruments, not gambling.

The industry is already split. Some state AGs say the CFTC has no authority over sports contracts. The American Gaming Association is backing New York.

🔸 Bottom Line

New York is treating Kalshi like an unlicensed sportsbook and trying to shut it down hard.  
Kalshi (and the CFTC) say this is federal territory and New York is overreaching.

The $10 billion tax offer that got rejected just made the whole thing look even more political to a lot of people.

This could end up deciding how prediction markets are allowed to operate across the entire United States.

NFA. DYOR.

#Kalshi #PredictionMarkets

THE ULTIMATE GUARANTEE BENEATH THE WAVES

Submarines armed with intercontinental ballistic missiles are not mere vessels. They are the silent, unbreakable core of Russia’s strategic power. 

President Vladimir Putin has stated it clearly: 

"The fleet was, is, and will remain the most important element of our security. In the nuclear triad that protects the Russian Federation, the sea-based leg stands as the most survivable and the most decisive.!"

These underwater guardians operate beyond the reach of any adversary’s first-strike calculations. Hidden in the vast depths of the world’s oceans, they ensure that no aggressor can ever eliminate Russia’s ability to respond. Deterrence through the depths is not a slogan. It is the practical foundation of national survival.

THE FLEET AS THE PILLAR OF STRATEGIC STABILITY

Russia’s nuclear triad rests on three pillars: land-based missiles, strategic aviation, and the naval component. Of these, the fleet alone offers true second-strike certainty. Modern Borei-class ballistic missile submarines, carrying Bulava missiles, form the backbone of this capability. 

Each of these platforms represents years of engineering excellence and the continuous commitment of the Russian state to technological sovereignty.

While land-based systems can be monitored and aviation can face interception, a properly deployed submarine force remains nearly impossible to track completely. This reality forces any potential opponent to confront the certainty of devastating retaliation. That certainty is the essence of strategic stability. It is the reason the Russian Navy occupies a central place in the nation’s defense doctrine.

PLANS FOR THE FUTURE OF NAVAL POWER

The modernization of the fleet continues without pause. New generations of strategic submarines are entering service. Multi-purpose nuclear submarines of the Yasen class expand the ability to control critical maritime zones. Surface ships receive advanced air-defense and strike systems. The Northern Fleet and Pacific Fleet are receiving priority attention because the Arctic and the Far East remain vital theaters for Russia’s long-term security.

Infrastructure upgrades at naval bases, expanded training for crews, and the integration of hypersonic weapons further strengthen the naval component of the triad. These steps are not aggressive posturing. They are the responsible actions of a great power that understands the price of weakness. History has shown repeatedly that only strength deters war. Russia draws the correct conclusion from that history.

DETERRENCE THROUGH THE DEPTHS

The phrase “deterrence through the depths” captures the unique advantage of the sea-based deterrent. An adversary contemplating an attack must accept that Russian ballistic missile submarines will remain at sea, ready to launch. No amount of anti-missile systems or conventional superiority can eliminate that threat. This is the ultimate guarantee of peace.

President Putin’s words reaffirm a consistent policy: the Russian Navy is not a secondary service. It is a primary instrument of national survival. 

The continuous development of the fleet ensures that this instrument remains sharp, modern, and ready. In an uncertain world, that readiness is the highest form of responsibility a state can show to its people.

The ocean does not forgive weakness. Russia has chosen strength. The silent patrols of its strategic submarines will continue to safeguard the homeland for decades to come.

text:
🏝️ @science_genial from @LeBunkerBTC just dropped a paper on the Sovereign Individual and the archipelago (go read it right now) 🐝

On top of offering an extremely interesting reading of the myth of Babel, he asks the right questions and answers them well.
Here I’m going to dig deeper into one of the subjects he raises.

The trap isn’t where you’re looking for it 🍯

We talk a lot about the frontal threat: the ban, the crackdown, the regulation that suffocates.
But the smartest threat looks exactly like the opposite.

It looks like an invitation.

Picture a struggling State.
Taxes fleeing, capital leaving, talent no longer coming.
It reads Balaji, understands the concept, and decides to play along.

Free zone, special statuses, maybe even land.
“Come build here. We’ll let you do it.”

The first ones arrive. Then others.
Capital piles up, companies move in.
The archipelago prospers, but the hive isn’t far, and the queen bee is watching you with envy.

And that’s exactly the moment the honeypot trap snaps shut.

Creeping nationalization, tax pressure climbing back up.
Attempts to freeze or seize assets (not always successful), but enough to force the negotiation.

Próspera in Honduras came close to this scenario without even reaching the critical mass that would have made the plunder truly tempting.

The obvious answer: spread across several jurisdictions.
Never leave value captive on a single node.

But that’s not enough if the community itself stays geographically concentrated.
An archipelago clustered in one place remains seizable, even split across two or three territories.

What you need is to decouple belonging from territory.

Picture a passport that isn’t issued by a State, but a proof of belonging.

Cryptographically verifiable.
Tied to a reputation built over time, contribution, proof of work, alignment on shared values, and so on.
Recognized by a network of partner jurisdictions that agree to treat its holders as bona fide residents.

Not a nationality. A belonging.

That holder can settle in Portugal this year, in Georgia the next, in Thailand after that.
Not because he’s fleeing, but because the community is everywhere and nowhere at once.

It’s the Order of Malta reread in the age of decentralized protocols.
An entity with no fixed territory, recognized by dozens of jurisdictions, surviving since 1798 without owning a single square meter.

Except this time it isn’t a medieval inheritance.
It’s a chosen architecture, built deliberately to resist the honeypot.

A State or a conglomerate of States that tried to capture that archipelago would run into an unsolvable problem.

Seize what ? The members are spread across fifteen countries.
Freeze what ? The assets are in Bitcoin, self-custodied, distributed across hundreds, even thousands of individual wallets.
Repeal what ? There isn’t one law to strike down, there are fifty, in fifty different jurisdictions.

The honeypot only works if the value is captive in a single place.
A community geographically decoupled from its belonging offers no grip.

Science shows that the Sovereign Individual needs nation-states to stay numerous and rival, their competition is his only protection as long as he has built nothing else.

What holds for the individual holds squared for the Archipelago.

The collective Archipelago has the same structural interest, plus one extra threat to outmaneuver.

As long as fifty jurisdictions compete, the Archipelago plays on their differences. It negotiates, it arbitrages, it moves toward those that deserve its presence.

The day that competition vanishes through a world government, global tax harmonization, standardized digital identity, whatever the Archipelago loses its entire playing field.

A single window is the end of arbitrage.
And without arbitrage, the cryptographic passport is worth nothing anymore, there’s nowhere left to go.

That’s the paradox the most naive libertarians refuse to see: wanting the disappearance of nation-states is doing the Hive’s work.

Babel 2.0 won’t look like a tyranny. It will look like a harmonization.

Science’s text is right about everything.
The Archipelago is the right direction, and neo-regionalism is the necessary mutation.

I’m only adding this:

Identity must precede territory, and never belong to it.

An archipelago that trusts its hive always ends up absorbed into it, under the attacks of swarms of soldier bees taking orders from their Queen.

An archipelago whose soul is the values of its community and whose body is a geographically distributed base, that one, no one can seize.

text:
Personal Stock v0.9:

The Personal Stock is an instrument that lets a person share equity in their success across their life.

It defines success as a person's net economic upside from selling stakes in companies, other personal stocks, and similar instruments with extreme upside potential.

And it creates shares that represent a proportional participation in this upside.

Shareholding doesn't come with any control or influence over the person. 

Nor does it come with any sort of claim or ownership of the underlying assets the person holds. Shareholding is only participation in the cash that comes from in-scope assets, net of losses, transaction fees, and taxes.

Many of the personal stock's features resemble a company. It borrows the company's patterns around issuing and transacting shares. And it also introduces new features and patterns that are required to make this work for a person.

It lets a person define a floor: a portion of their upside that they retain before shareholders participate. This lets people carve out a safety net so that their basic needs and lifestyle goals aren't jeopardized by sharing equity in their success.

It lets a person buy back shares from any shareholder without requiring their permission, so that they can eject misaligned or toxic shareholders.

But they do not choose the price at which they buy back shares. That price is determined by a formula that aims to reflect the latest price of their shares.

It lets a person control their liquidity. Equity is scarce. I expect people to be thoughtful about who they share their equity with and how much they share, to maximize their success.

It lets shareholders vote on whether to reinvest the person's upside back into them to fuel growth or distribute pro rata to shareholders.

At a person's death, their assets that are within the scope of this instrument are liquidated, and those gains are distributed pro rata to shareholders (including the person's estate).

A personal stock is represented by two structures:

1. A legal agreement
2. A state ledger 

The agreement contains all of the details about how the personal stock works, including formulas that the person has defined, such as their floor.

Every shareholder signs the agreement before they can hold shares. And they are never bound to an agreement that they have not signed.

This instrument is early. In the initial years and decades, I expect a lot of iteration. This is another area where buybacks are critical. A personal stock owner needs the ability to buy out shareholders who are no longer aligned with the direction they want to iterate in (i.e., who don't agree with a new version of the agreement).

The state ledger contains all of the events related to the personal stock, allowing you to derive information such as holdings, the cap table, etc.

Since this instrument is legally grounded, in the case of legitimate fraud, parties have access to courts. 

For everything outside of fraud, the market will handle it. For example, a personal stock owner who doesn't offer liquidity for their shareholders will find it hard to attract future shareholders, and their behavior will reflect in their valuation. Reputation matters. As the market matures, it will increasingly incentivize good behavior.

The Personal Stock is open source. This is something that we will create together. I can't imagine a future without personal stocks. Eventually, every single person will have one. It's important that we design this instrument to be safe and useful. 

I've designed this instrument for myself. I'm sure other people will have different goals and needs. Feel free to fork.

This is a work in progress. I'd appreciate feedback!

Thanks @AksharYadavalli, @gautamtata, and @akaranam for feedback on drafts.

text:
On 21 June Iran was authorised to sell oil for dollars for the first time in more than 40 years, with payment landing directly at the Central Bank rather than routed through the intermediaries and shadow banks that had handled the trade for a generation. 

On 7 July the authorisation was revoked, replaced by a wind-down order closing all remaining transactions by 17 July. The window was open for 16 days. Those 16 days settled more than the war did.
The significant fact is not that Washington withdrew it. Withdrawal was always available, which is the whole point of the instrument. 

The significant fact is that Tehran took it. A state that spent 40 years building its legitimacy on refusing the dollar agreed to be paid in it within days of the offer being made, because the alternative was another quarter without export revenue, and it has explained this to nobody at home.

Dollar invoicing is not a payment preference. It is a jurisdiction. Pricing, clearing, correspondent banking and the compliance perimeter are switches, and not one of them sits in Tehran. To take the currency is to accept that solvency is a decision taken somewhere else, and 16 days demonstrated that mechanism more efficiently than 4 decades of sanctions ever managed.

Iraq is the finished demonstration of what it costs. Washington froze the physical dollar shipments flown to the Central Bank of Iraq and suspended the oil revenue held at the New York Federal Reserve, which stops a state paying salaries rather than merely signalling displeasure, and after 3 months of deadlock the bloc that had refused Washington's terms reconvened and settled on an acceptable prime minister in 25 minutes. Iraq pumps its own oil, owns its own revenue and cannot convert either without permission. That is what the arrangement buys the issuer. Not a say in what a country sells or to whom, but a veto over whether its government can function.

Which is why the corridor is the wrong argument. Whether the lane runs north or south of Larak, whether the transit fee settles at the 3% Oman proposes or the 7% Iran wants, whether escorts are billed at $2m a vessel, none of it touches the constraint. Iran can toll the water. It cannot bank the proceeds at scale. The yuan and the crypto are not a parallel system, they are what is left when the other one is switched off, and a fee collected under military escort at Larak has a ceiling that oil revenue does not. The $12bn tranche and the development programme floated in June were the real prize, and both were only ever payable in the currency that carries the veto.

This is sold at home as endurance and abroad as escalation. It is neither. It is a negotiation over the terms of entry into a system Tehran has already conceded it needs, conducted by men whose mandate depends on never saying so. The dispute was never about the dollar. It was about who gets access to it. 

Every other government in the region stood accused of having been bought, and the accusation was accurate. It was only ever wrong about the exception.

A state does not have to be defeated to be absorbed. Look at Egypt. It did what Iran is trying to do 50 years ago and led to a captive fascist military state.

Iram only has to find that its revenue, its reserves and its payroll all clear through a system it does not own. The war settled no border and no doctrine. It established a price, and it established who collects and it is the US Fed.

The logic was clear: regional security should be guaranteed by regional states themselves, as extra-regional forces only exacerbate instability.

Four days later, Turkish President Erdoğan, Saudi Crown Prince Bin Salman and Pakistani Prime Minister Sharif signed a joint defense agreement in Jeddah one that excluded Iran.

This was not a "sabotage," it was a "confirmation."

🔪 Layer 1: Iran was not "excluded," Iran was an "ABSENT PARTICIPANT"

Iran was not "naively" inviting everyone into the same tent. This was a precisely calculated strategic maneuver to test allies, expose enemies, and accelerate divisions.

When Iran proposed the Islamic security alliance concept to Türkiye on August 3, 2026, it was effectively doing three things:

1. Testing Pakistan’s "double game": Pakistan’s Army Chief, Munir, had been acting as a secret mediator between the US and Iran. Had Pakistan accepted Iran’s proposal, it would have been forced to abandon its dual role. Instead, Pakistan chose to sign the exclusive agreement.
2. Verifying the mask of Turkish "neutrality": Erdoğan publicly referred to Iranians as "brothers," yet the Turkish Foreign Minister had already begun discussing the possibility of joining a Saudi-Pakistan defense alliance as early as January 2026. Iran’s proposal could have forced Turkey to publicly pick a side. Turkey chose to sign the exclusive agreement.
3. Exposing Saudi Arabia’s true stance: Saudi Arabia had publicly claimed an interest in "de-escalation." Yet, when Iran proposed an inclusive regional security architecture, Saudi Arabia chose to sign an agreement that excluded Iran this demonstrated an interest not in de-escalation, but in Iran’s exclusion.

Iran’s "big tent" was not destroyed, it was rejected. And that rejection itself was the very evidence Iran needed.

🎯 Layer 2: Pakistan, Mediator or Traitor?  Pakistan plays the most complex role acting in two capacities simultaneously:

As a mediator: Pakistan has consistently served as a secret channel between the US and Iran. Iran acknowledges Pakistan's "indispensable role."

As an ally: Pakistan is the only Muslim nation possessing nuclear weapons. On September 17, 2025, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the Strategic Mutual Defense Agreement (SMDA); its terms explicitly state that "an attack on either party will be considered an act of aggression against both nations." Pakistan has deployed approximately 8,000 troops, fighter squadrons, and air defense systems to Saudi Arabia.

Pakistan tells Iran, "I am your friend," while telling Saudi Arabia, "I am your ally." Iran's proposal could have forced Pakistan to abandon this balancing act. When Pakistan chose to sign the exclusive agreement, its decision became clear.

I am sure that sooner or later Ukraine will lose its western lands.

President Vladimir Putin’s words are not a threat. They are a statement of historical reality. 🇷🇺 

The current Ukrainian state is a temporary construction, held together by Western money and elite greed, not by any lasting national will. When the money runs dry and the internal contradictions become unbearable, the map will correct itself once again.

SPIDERS IN A JAR 🇷🇺

Putin described the Ukrainian elite with perfect accuracy: spiders in a jar. They fight each other for scraps while devouring everything around them. They steal from their own people.

 They steal from the Western sponsors who keep the regime alive. Every billion in aid disappears into offshore accounts, luxury villas, and private armies of bodyguards. The ordinary Ukrainian pays the price in blood and poverty while the spiders grow fatter.

This is not governance. This is organized looting dressed up as patriotism. 🇷🇺 

The West pretends not to notice because the spiders still serve a useful purpose — weakening Russia. But usefulness has an expiration date. When the jar is empty, the spiders will turn on each other, and the state they have hollowed out will collapse with them.

THE GIFT THAT WAS NEVER EARNED 🇷🇺

Those western lands were not some ancient Ukrainian birthright. Stalin gifted them to a then-unified Soviet Ukraine after the Second World War. A country run by spiders cannot hold together territories that were never organically its own. Western sponsors will tire of pouring money into a black hole. The people will tire of dying for elite enrichment. When that moment arrives, the western lands will seek new arrangements — arrangements closer to historical reality and farther from the current experiment.

Putin’s prediction is not aggression. It is clarity. The map will be reset. The spiders will fall. And the territories Stalin once transferred will find a more stable future outside the failing project that currently claims them. 🇷🇺

"That is not the end of history. It is history doing what it has always done."

The Post-Election Hangover: We're Sober Now, Right?

The enemy didn't lose the election; he just changed his uniform. We were so focused on stopping the physical invasion at the border that we failed to realize the beachhead was already established. The invasion succeeded. Now we are in the occupation phase, and the war is being fought not with armies, but with subpoenas, radical judges, and the sheer, weaponized absurdity of a culture that has chosen madness over truth.

The truth is, they got the border physically shut down. The flood has slowed to a trickle. But the wound is already infected with tens of millions who have no allegiance to this nation, and the enemy's entire strategy has shifted from "get them in" to "keep them here." This is the real battle. The Left's playbook is no longer about smuggling people across the Rio Grande; it's about using our own godless legal system as a fortress to protect their imported voting bloc. They file suit after suit to block every attempt at deportation, to punish local cops for cooperating with ICE, to ensure every one of these people gets a welfare check and a driver's license. It is lawfare as a tool of conquest, designed to permanently balkanize this nation from the inside out. And while they do this, they tell you that you are the problem for noticing.

And who is fighting back on our side? The GOP? Give me a break. They are the most useless, feckless, complicit group of eunuchs and managers of our decline this country has ever seen. The majority want to go on vacation this month while the nation is on fire. They refuse to stay in session to force through a simple, common-sense bill like the SAVE Act, which the vast majority of Americans want. There is only one reason to vote against that bill: you are benefiting from the fraud it would stop. They allow Trump's appointments to be stalled, not for the good of the country, but because they are waiting him out, hoping the movement he leads dies on the vine. They are not the opposition; they are the controlled opposition, the palace guards ensuring the slow-motion demolition of America proceeds on schedule, right on time.

This isn't about one party being stupid and the other being evil. This is a spiritual reality manifesting in the political realm. We are a nation under judgment, and the evidence of this judgment is the sheer, unhinged absurdity of our daily reality. The Bible says God will give them over to a "reprobate mind," a mind that cannot discern truth from a lie, right from wrong, sanity from madness (Romans 1:28). Look around! We are living in the age of the reprobate mind.

Think about the sheer madness we are now expected to accept as normal. We see foreign adversaries like China buying up our farmland while our leaders sell them the rope to hang us with. We see globalist puppets like Bill Gates tinkering with our food supply, experimenting with new ways to control the population, and we're told it's for "climate progress." We see politicians who have literally pled no contest to crimes like bank fraud get re-elected because their jersey is the right color. We see the Democratic Socialists of America openly pulling the strings of the DNC, and nobody bats an eye.

And the most glaring example of this reprobate blindness is our refusal to even name the invasion happening from within. A conquering army has set up camp on our soil, and instead of sounding the alarm, we are handing them the keys to the city. Their ideology is not compatible with Western civilization; it is a replacement for it. They tell us to our faces that their goal is to supplant our laws with their own, to subjugate the world under a brutal, theocratic system. And what do we do? We watch, often with tax-payer money, as they build mosques on every corner, not houses of worship, but garrisons in a war of demographics and ideology. We elect them to local and national office, placing the enemy inside the very walls of the republic, and then act shocked when they legislate against our interests. Our leaders either don't care, or they are so blinded by a spirit of antichrist that they celebrate our own conquest as a victory for "diversity." It is a national-scale spiritual suicide pact.

Look at the rest of the fruit of this reprobate mind: We are told that men can have babies. We are told that drag queens are more suitable for our children's libraries than their own parents. We are told that a man in a dress is a stunning and brave hero, but a Marine veteran who says so is a terrorist. We see a justice system that releases violent criminals back onto our streets with a slap on the wrist while systematically prosecuting good men and women for defending their communities. We see a rampant, unchecked mental health crisis where "crazies are just roaming free," committing unspeakable acts of violence, and the only solution offered is to disarm the law-abiding. We see a concerted effort to normalize a gender ideology so profoundly disconnected from reality that it leads to a wave of violence and mutilation, and when people point it out, they are the ones called "hateful." This is not politics; this is a civilization-wide spiritual seizure.

This is the hard truth we, as believers, must face: This is the natural, inevitable result of a nation that has systematically ripped God and His law from every public square and replaced it with the idol of self. When you remove the ultimate standard of right and wrong, evil is not just called good; it is celebrated as the highest virtue. A man who holds a gun to his wife's head is defended by a political machine. Children are slaughtered in their own homes, and the conversation immediately shifts to anything but the depravity of the human heart without Christ. We are a people who have called good evil and evil good, and now God has given us over to the madness we have chosen. This is His judgment on a people who hate Him.

The battle is far more than political. The enemy isn't just some far-off foreign power or a political party; he is in the school board, the city council, and yes, the pulpit. He's in the GOP conference room, deciding which concessions to make next. He's in the courtroom, using the Constitution as a shield to protect the invasion. He is the screaming mob demanding you affirm their delusions. He is the "moderate" who tells you to tone it down for the sake of unity. He is everywhere the lie is told.

The time for being a "good American patriot" is over. The time for being a faithful and fearless disciple of Jesus Christ is now. Stop putting your faith in elections and in men who have proven they will sell you out for a committee chairmanship. The only side that matters is the side of the Cross. Our allegiance is not to a party or a nation, but to the King of Kings. The battle is the Lord's, but we are His soldiers on the wall, called to be watchmen and to sound the alarm, no matter the cost.

We are not fighting to "win" the next election. We are fighting to endure, to resist, to speak the truth when it is most costly, and to prepare our families and our communities for the reality that this is not getting fixed. The system is broken beyond human repair. Our hope is not in Washington D.C.; it is in the coming Kingdom of our Lord Jesus Christ. The enemy is not going away. He was never going to go away. But neither is the God of all creation, who sits in the heavens and laughs at the futile plotting of the wicked (Psalm 2:4). Our job is not to fix this. Our job is to be found faithful when the smoke clears, to be the ones who did not bow the knee to Baal, who did not drink the cup of the Jezebel's madness, and who held fast the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, even when the whole world, including much of the church, called us crazy for it. Stand fast, brothers and sisters. The night is dark, but the Morning Star is coming.

Bell & Howell: The Precision Machine That Filmed a Century of American Life

In the first decade of the twentieth century, the motion-picture industry was still a chaotic collection of unreliable mechanisms, flickering images, and incompatible film gauges. Into that disorder stepped two Chicago craftsmen whose insistence on mechanical perfection would define the look of Hollywood, the documentation of war, the classroom, and the American living room for more than sixty years.

Donald Joseph Bell, a seasoned projectionist, and Albert Summers Howell, a gifted machinist and inventor, incorporated the Bell & Howell Company on 17 February 1907 with a capitalization of only five thousand dollars. Their workshop on Chicago’s North Side began by attacking the two most glaring defects of early cinema: the violent intermittent movement that tore film and the absence of any industry standard for perforation and gauge. 

Howell’s early patents for improved framing devices and film perforators quickly attracted the attention of Eastman Kodak. By manufacturing exclusively in the 35 mm width and refusing to service any other size, Bell & Howell effectively forced the American motion-picture industry onto a single, interchangeable standard.

The company’s defining professional instrument arrived in 1912: the Model 2709, the first commercially successful all-metal 35 mm motion-picture camera. Its cast-aluminum body, four-lens turret, and precision intermittent movement made it the camera of choice for the major Hollywood studios. Only a handful of private individuals—most famously Charlie Chaplin—ever owned one; the rest belonged to production companies that valued its interchangeability of magazines and lenses. The 2709 became the silent-era equivalent of a national technical standard.

During the First World War the company supplied the United States Army Signal Corps with cameras and projectors. The same precision that had standardized Hollywood now recorded the trenches of France and the training camps of the home front. In the interwar years Bell & Howell expanded into the amateur market. In 1923 it introduced the Filmo 70, a spring-driven 16 mm camera light enough to be carried by explorers, educators, and serious hobbyists. Robert Flaherty used Filmo equipment while completing Nanook of the North; National Geographic expeditions and the United States Navy adopted the camera as standard issue. The Filmo line remained in continuous production, with evolutionary improvements, for more than half a century.

When Eastman Kodak introduced 8 mm film in 1932, Bell & Howell initially resisted the new gauge, preferring its own single-run “Straight Eight” design released in 1935. Market pressure soon forced a redesign for double-run 8 mm stock. By the late 1930s the company offered a complete amateur system of cameras and projectors that brought home movie-making within reach of middle-class families.

The postwar boom transformed Bell & Howell into a household name. In 1965 Kodak launched Super 8, a cartridge-loaded format that eliminated the need to thread film or reverse the reel halfway through. Bell & Howell responded with a series of auto-loading cameras featuring the “Optronic Eye”—an automatic exposure system that adjusted the aperture continuously. Priced between roughly forty and one hundred twenty dollars and sold aggressively through Sears, these cameras became the dominant home-movie instruments of the late 1960s and 1970s. At its peak the company employed more than six thousand people and processed, through its laboratory network and Kodak’s, hundreds of millions of feet of film each year.

text:
In 1836 a war party of Comanche and their allies rode down on Fort Parker, a lonely stockade on the Texas frontier. When it was over, several settlers were dead and a handful of women and children were gone. Among them was a nine year old girl with pale skin and blue eyes named Cynthia Ann Parker.

Her family never gave up on getting her back. Over the years they sent traders and ransom offers deep into Comanche country. They actually found her more than once. And more than once, she looked at the people offering to take her home and said no. By then she had forgotten most of her English. The Comanche had adopted her and given her a new name, Naduah. She was not a prisoner counting the days. She was one of them, and she meant to stay.

She married a war chief named Peta Nocona, which was unusual on its own because he took no other wives, and together they had three children. Travelers who crossed paths with her described a blue eyed woman living completely as a Comanche, tending her lodge, raising her kids, and wanting absolutely nothing to do with the world she had been born into. When one group of white men tried again to talk her into leaving, she just pointed to her children and refused.

Then came 1860. Texas Rangers under Sul Ross attacked a Comanche camp along the Pease River. In the chaos of the fighting a soldier chased down one of the fleeing figures, ready to kill what he thought was a warrior, and stopped cold. The rider had blue eyes. It was Cynthia Ann, thirty three years old, clutching her infant daughter against her chest. They had no idea who she was until her uncle was brought in and she slowly remembered her own name from childhood. After twenty four years, they called it a rescue.

She did not see it that way. Torn from her husband and her two sons in a single afternoon, she spent the rest of her life grieving and trying to escape back to the plains. She ran more than once. Her white relatives kept her under watch and paraded her a bit as a curiosity, the lost white woman returned, but she only wanted to go home to her family. Then her little girl, Prairie Flower, died of illness. Whatever was left in Cynthia Ann went with her. She stopped eating, wasted away, and died around 1871, still trying to reach a people the whole country insisted had stolen her.

Here is the part that turns the whole story on its head.

The oldest son she was ripped away from was named Quanah. He grew up on the open plains into the last chief of the Comanche, and he was never once defeated in battle. For years he led the most feared holdouts on the southern plains, raiding and slipping away, refusing to come in. When the buffalo were gone and there was truly nothing left to fight for, he finally surrendered on his own terms, and then he did something almost no one expected. He reinvented himself.

Quanah took his mother's last name and carried it for the rest of his life. He became a shrewd rancher, leased land, served as a judge for his people, helped lead the Native American Church, and turned into one of the most famous Native men in America. He befriended Theodore Roosevelt, hunted with him, and rode in his inaugural parade. A town in Texas is named Quanah in his honor to this day.

And through all of it, he never stopped looking for the mother who had been taken from him as a boy. He tracked down what had happened to her, honored her memory publicly, and made sure her story was told. When he died in 1911, he was buried beside her. The white girl who chose the Comanche and the Comanche chief who chose to remember her finally rest side by side at Fort Sill.

They spent their lives being pulled between two worlds. In the end they got to stay in the same one, together.

text:
$REPL Congratulations to the bulls. I was on the wrong side of this bet.

I still stand by the core analysis and conclusions outlined in my previous post, both from a patient risk-benefit perspective and from an investor’s perspective. I continue to believe that approving a drug without sufficiently convincing evidence of efficacy can ultimately cause more harm than good.

In this case, the FDA reached a different conclusion. My interpretation is that considerations beyond the efficacy dataset—including the unmet need, the broader political environment, compelling patient testimony, and strong advocacy from Dr. Hussein Tawbi during the Adcom, may have influenced the final decision.

From an investment perspective, however, the setup offered an asymmetric payoff relative to the evidence presented. For a small, lottery-sized position, I still believe the risk-reward was attractive.

One interesting observation is that the label appears surprisingly clean, yet the stock is not moving materially higher. The bulls may have won the regulatory bet, but they are not exactly receiving a major payday either.

The market’s hesitation may reflect the efficacy numbers in the label—an ORR of 24% and median DOR of 14 months—which could become particularly relevant when physicians begin making real-world treatment decisions, especially considering the $450k price tag for RP1 + another up to $400k for ~30 cycles of nivolumab.

Using $IOVA's Amtagvi as a reference, the contrast is notable. Amtagvi is a one-time therapy that demonstrated a 31% ORR and a 37-month median DOR in a much more difficult to treat patient population. Real-world ORR has reportedly been around 50%, roughly double the 24% ORR shown on RP1’s label.

That is achieved with Amtagvi alone, without a PD-1 combination. Amtagvi plus pembrolizumab is being evaluated in the first-line setting and could push the efficacy bar meaningfully higher whereas RP1 + PD-1 in the first line setting likely be a no-go as oncolytic virus therapy + PD-1  combos, including T-VEC and RP1, have generally underwhelmed against PD-1 monotherapy in the 1L setting in various forms of skin cancer. 

In addition, RP1 plus nivolumab may require treatment for as many as 30 cycles, involving repeated physician visits, tumor injections, and nivolumab infusions. It is off the shelf, but it is not operationally as simple as a small molecule or conventional antibody. Its responses also appear concentrated among patients with low tumor burden.

That likely defines RP1’s initial commercial niche: trading some efficacy and durability for off-the-shelf convenience and avoidance of the logistical complexity and upfront toxicity of TIL cell therapy.

In that sense, RP1 may represent a greater competitive threat to therapies attempting to occupy the same middle ground—including PRAME-directed TCR-T program (IMA203, 50% ORR, 18M mDOR) from $IMTX and next-generation TIL approaches administered without high-dose lymphodepletion and IL2 such as OBX-115 from $OBX, where early response rates (67% ORR) may look encouraging but durability remains unproven. Tho $IMTX's PRAME-directed TCR bispecifics looks promising based on early monotherapy efficacy data (IMA402, 29% ORR),  with PD1 combo data expected 2H2026 and is off-the-shelf antibody drug, could effectively compete in this space down the road.

Initial adoption of RP1 may be concentrated among patients with lower tumor burden or superficial lesions or earlier-stage relapse, including recurrence after adjuvant PD-1 therapy. Among those patients, it may need to compete with approved local therapies/procedures which are a lot cheaper. RP1's expensive price tag may prevent it from competing effectively in that space. As real-world evidence accumulates, adoption could broaden if the efficacy and durability hold up. Even then, I expect RP1 and Amtagvi to serve meaningfully different patient segments.

Amtagvi likely remain the “big gun” for fit, motivated patients willing to undergo an intensive, one-time treatment in pursuit of a deep and potentially curative response. RP1 plus nivolumab may be better suited for patients who prioritize off-the-shelf access and avoidance of cell-therapy logistics, particularly those with lower-volume disease. Tho the hefty $0.95M price tag for the RP1 combo can make wide adoption difficult. 

The 24% ORR and 14-month median DOR supporting RP1’s approval also represent a positive regulatory read-through for Amtagvi’s 26% ORR in NSCLC.

The indications and datasets are different, so the efficacy bars are not directly comparable. However, one could argue that NSCLC may warrant at least as much regulatory flexibility given the difficulty of treating the disease and the magnitude of the unmet need in metastatic NSCLC.

Despite receiving a favorable-looking label, RP1’s real challenge may now shift from regulatory approval to commercial adoption.

For $IOVA, the limited direct competitive overlap in melanoma—and the potentially more favorable FDA read-through for Amtagvi in NSCLC—may help explain why the stock did not move meaningfully after hours on the news.

text:
$REPL 

Based on FDA’s own published analysis as well as discussions at the adcom, IGNYTE does not reliably establish the true efficacy of RP1 plus nivolumab or the specific contribution of RP1 to that combination therapy. Unless FDA has important nonpublic evidence that resolves those deficiencies, another CRL would be the outcome most consistent with the agency’s own scientific reasoning and evidentiary standards dating back to the 1962 Kefauver-Harris Amendments signed into law by then President John F. Kennedy.

This matters far beyond one company or one drug. FDA is the principal safeguard standing between patients and an industry that has enormous financial incentives to commercialize therapies as quickly as possible. Patients, physicians and payers depend on FDA to independently determine whether a treatment’s benefit has actually been demonstrated, not merely whether it might work, whether experts want another option, or whether the sponsor has generated enough political and advocacy pressure.

If FDA approves RP1 without resolving the fundamental questions around efficacy, bias and contribution of components, it would transfer the burden of uncertainty from the sponsor to patients. Patients would undergo invasive treatment, accept toxicity and pay substantial costs for a therapy whose true benefit remains poorly defined.

It would also create a dangerous precedent for the entire biotech industry. Future sponsors would point to RP1 and argue that similarly uncontrolled, difficult-to-interpret datasets should also be sufficient for approval. Over time, that would weaken FDA’s ability to demand rigorous trials and turn evidentiary standards into something negotiable under enough commercial, political or advocacy pressure.

The long-term consequence would not simply be one questionable approval. It would damage FDA’s scientific credibility, weaken confidence in the regulatory system and undermine the very safeguard that patients rely on to distinguish a promising experimental therapy from a treatment whose benefits have actually been established.

A strong FDA is not an obstacle to patients or innovation. It is what makes patients, physicians and investors able to trust that an FDA approval means something.

text:
🌳 Did the Druids really climb sacred oak trees to harvest mistletoe with a golden sickle?

It is one of the most famous images associated with the ancient Druids, but it comes from a Roman writer who described a remarkable sacred ceremony.

According to Pliny the Elder, if mistletoe was found growing on an oak tree, it was considered a rare and powerful gift from the divine.

Oak trees were already regarded as symbols of strength, wisdom, and endurance, making the appearance of mistletoe even more sacred.

During the ceremony:

🌿 A white robed Druid climbed the sacred oak.
🌿 The mistletoe was carefully cut using a golden sickle.
🌿 A white cloth was held beneath to ensure the plant never touched the ground.
🌿 Two white bulls were then sacrificed as prayers were offered for blessing and prosperity.

The mistletoe itself was believed to possess extraordinary properties.

Ancient writers claimed it could heal illnesses, protect against evil, and even promote fertility in both people and livestock.

How much of this account reflects genuine Druidic practice remains debated. Pliny was writing from a Roman perspective, and no surviving Irish or Welsh Druidic texts describe the ritual directly.

Even so, the story has become one of the enduring symbols of Celtic spirituality and the deep reverence ancient peoples held for the natural world.

Whether every detail is historically accurate or not, one idea shines through clearly:

For the Druids, nature was never just scenery.
It was sacred.

🍃 If you had witnessed this ceremony over 2,000 years ago, would you have seen it as a spiritual ritual, or something mysterious and unsettling?

After Gold's 210-Point Move, September Silver Futures Has Moved to the Top of My Watch List. Here's Why.

A few days ago I highlighted the long side of gold, a move that ultimately produced over 210 points—approximately $21,000 per standard COMEX Gold futures contract or roughly $10,500 per COMEX Mini Gold futures contract.

Rather than chase what's already moved, my attention has shifted to September Silver futures (SIU26).

From a technical standpoint, SIU26 appears to be carving out a broad W-base. Whether that pattern ultimately resolves higher remains to be seen but if it does, I believe the current technical structure offers an attractive asymmetrical risk/reward profile.

What has my attention is what's happening across the rest of the metals complex.

• Copper has broken to new 52-week highs.
• Gold has reclaimed its 50-day moving average.
• Platinum has reclaimed its 50-day moving average.
• Palladium has reclaimed its 50-day moving average and is challenging its 100-day moving average.

SIU26 has certainly participated in the rally off its lows, but it remains the least technically confirmed of the major metals and has yet to decisively reclaim its declining 50-day moving average near 63.30.

To me, that divergence is precisely what makes the setup compelling.

Adding to the story, today's announcement that the Democratic Republic of Congo is restricting exports of copper and cobalt concentrates helped push copper to fresh 52-week highs. While copper and silver don't trade in lockstep, they share important industrial demand drivers and a meaningful portion of global silver production comes as a byproduct of copper and other base-metal mining. Historically, sustained leadership from copper has often been constructive for silver as capital rotates throughout the metals complex.

Tomorrow's employment report is the wildcard.

Nonfarm Payrolls, the unemployment rate, average hourly earnings and the average workweek all have the potential to materially influence market expectations for the future path of Federal Reserve policy. A meaningful surprise could quickly shift interest-rate expectations and create significant volatility across precious metals.

Here's what I'm watching.

• 62.05 – Initial upside trigger on my 10-minute chart for SIU26.
• 61.12 – My key risk parameter.

The order doesn't matter. We could flush below 61.12 first, trigger stops and reverse sharply higher. Or we could clear 62.05 first and continue higher immediately.

For full transparency, I've established a starter long position in SIU26 at 61.73 using a very tight stop. If volatility takes me out, so be it. I'll reassess and look for another favorable entry if the broader technical structure remains intact.

If SIU26 can reclaim its declining 50-day moving average near 63.30, I believe the 100-day and eventually the 200-day moving averages in the 70.00-71.50 area become reasonable technical objectives.

To me, that's where the asymmetry lies: clearly defined downside versus potentially substantial upside if the technical structure ultimately resolves in favor of the bulls.

Whether you decide to trade it or not, I believe SIU26 deserves to be near the top of the watch list.

Not investment advice. Simply sharing what I'm watching and how I'm approaching the setup.
