Now that I've had a chance to fully digest $OPEN earnings I think it's hilarious that the bears are flexing because the stock is down ~15%. Here are some sobering thoughts:

1. A stock can move downwards for MANY reasons post-earnings and those may have NOTHING to do with the fundamentals of the company. Here are some reasons:
- Traders and capital allocators think there are better opportunities...*cough* like AI, Space and Memory 
- Capital allocators think that the fundamentals may be strong but looking to de-risk from high-beta and small cap stocks
- The market is deleveraging 

2. When in doubt, zoom out. The right way to measure @nejatian as a CEO is not using the meme $10 price that Opendoor was at when speculation and momentum was high. Everyone who has any understanding of fundamentals knows that it was drastically overextended. The right way to measure Kaz is the fact that the stock is currently trading around $3.50 when it was trading at around $0.70 the summer before he even arrived. After 3 quarters of his execution - the stock has secured a floor that was higher than the previous CEO. You may not think it goes much higher than today's valuation...but the market has priced in 3 quarters of his execution and definitively thinks he is a better exec than Carrie was. 

3. The only CEO I've ever seen move this fast and cut OpEx is @elonmusk - If you can't appreciate how fast Kaz moves...your expectations are untethered from reality. Name me one exec team that's cut marketing from 80 million to 5 million while increasing the acceptance of their offer....I'll wait. This is market making 101.

4. The guidance on the lower contribution margin for Q3, is the only meh part that I think disappointed bulls picked up on that is of merit. But again, if contribution margins are within 100-150 bps of this quarter, as long as acquisitions remain elevated then this business will do just fine.

5. If we think this is a multi-bagger in the next 5-10 years...freaking out over 10% after earnings is just dumb. It's a non-event. It's normal to see small caps swing back and forth. Volatility is the price of admission for owning high growth, high potential businesses. I don't know a single CEO as transparent about their business fundamentals as much as Kaz is. If you don't like the execution, position your portfolio accordingly. It's that simple. 

Me? I'm liking what I see.

text:
New Pacific Metals Analysis

I think this one flies under the radar a bit, but given it moved 23% in the last two days, I had to do a deeper analysis on New Pacific. Looking closely at it, New Pacific Metals Corp. (TSX: NUAG / NYSE American: NEWP) reveals that it is a world-class, pre-production asset generator controlling two of the largest undeveloped, open-pit silver deposits globally. The company is highly leveraged to the price of silver, shifting from a pure exploration play into a fast-advancing engineering and permitting phase.
Revenue Splits and In-The-Ground Ounces

Silver Revenue Percentage: 

The revenue profile is asset-dependent. The flagship Silver Sand Project is a 100% pure silver play, which is exceptionally rare in the mining industry. 

Conversely, their massive Carangas Project is a polymetallic system designed with a two-phase sequencing approach: Years 1–8 are heavily silver-dominant (averaging 15.5 million oz of pure silver per year), while an $8\text{M}$ tonne-per-year gold circuit initiates in Year 9 to turn it into a gold-dominant operation.

Silver Ounces in the Ground:

Across its consolidated portfolio, New Pacific holds approximately 400 million ounces of pure silver in the ground. The Silver Sand project alone hosts roughly 157 million ounces of total payable silver, while the newly updated Carangas PEA details an expected life-of-mine production of 195 million ounces of payable silver (or 339 million silver-equivalent ounces).

Other Metals in the Mines: Beyond pure silver, the company’s structural resource system holds massive secondary deposits of Gold (projected at 1.1 million payable ounces at Carangas), Zinc ( (1,453 million pounds), and Lead (941 million pounds).

Production Timeline and Location Risks

Production Timeline: New Pacific Metals is not yet in production. Management's current stated corporate objective is to advance environmental assessments, finalize community agreements, and migrate exploration licenses into definitive Administrative Mining Contracts. 

The baseline target is to reach a formal construction and final investment decision (FID) by late 2027 or early 2028. Silver Sand represents a more rapid, capital-efficient path to immediate production (13-year mine life), whereas Carangas represents a massive 19-year long-term growth pipeline.

Location Risks: 

All core operations are located in Bolivia (specifically the Potosí and Oruro Departments). Operating in Bolivia presents substantial jurisdictional country risk. Though the regulatory environment has shown signs of stability and illegal artisanal miners were successfully removed from Silver Sand, the country has a historical reputation for legal frameworks that shift unpredictably, resource nationalism, and intensive local community consultation processes required to secure long-term surface rights.

Investment Positives vs. Negatives

Positives

Massive Open-Pit Economics: Rare open-pit silver profiles yield incredibly low operating costs; Silver Sand boasts an elite LOM AISC of just US$10.69 per ounce.

Deep Institutional Backing: Major validation and technical oversight from primary producers Silvercorp Metals (28% equity) and Pan American Silver (11% equity).

Clean Balance Sheet: Zero debt and a comfortable $39 million cash runway allowing them to advance permitting without immediate, highly dilutive equity raises.

Negatives

Severe Jurisdictional Discount: Trading at a massive discount (roughly 25% of its multi-billion dollar spot NPV) solely due to investor hesitation over Bolivian country risk. Though this could also be viewed as a plus, given it is undervalued.

Heavy Near-Term Capital Costs: Building these sites requires combined initial capital expenditures exceeding US$1 billion, presenting a massive future funding hurdle.

Zero Immediate Cash Flow: As a developer, they are completely vulnerable to broader equity market cycles and cannot generate organic revenue until the end of the decade.

Is it a "Good" Investment?

text:
Reflections on My Namesake

I discovered a lot more about the man I was named after just a few weeks ago by reading his obituary after a chat with each of my parents. I didn't expect to feel so differently about my identity afterwards.

Stedman Fitzroy Matthew was born on Christmas Day of 1950 in Montserrat, West Indies, which happened to be his mother's birthday as well. He died at the age of 69 in San Francisco on July 30, 2020. The COVID-19 pandemic meant a small funeral. For my entire life up to that morning a few weeks back, the only things I knew about him were that he was a friend of my parents and that they liked his name; that was the full extent of information offered when I asked in my youth.

According to the obituary, Stedman was a regular on Fillmore Street, where I've lived since the spring of 2023. I knew my parents met building The Fillmore Center together in the late 1980s but I didn't know that my father met Stedman playing tennis in Alamo Square Park, a mere block west of my residence. I felt an unusual calling to that particular park when first searching for a place to live in the city and ever since, I've told many friends that it is my favorite park in the world. It seems now that there is narrative and spiritual resonance to accompany that feeling. That sense of consonance from the discovery reaches back and rearranges the history of how I felt about my name growing up.

Stedman was a stiff, strange, adult name to hand a kid, and it eventually made me quite shy. Every introduction followed a similar script: I'd say my name, the other person would say it back wrong or don a quizzical expression and ask me to repeat it, I'd say it again or twice or three times more, and then two days later at the same practice or classroom or party they'd have lost it entirely and we'd run the whole exchange from the top. I learned to say it quietly, which made it worse. What I concluded with the infallible logic of a lonely child was that no one wanted to know or remember me or bother staying connected to me.

My twin brother's name is Myles. He is named after Miles Davis and the name fits; he carries himself like he invented the concept of cool. Both of us would go on to perform a good deal of jazz music in childhood (ironically, I was the trumpeter). He arrived in the world with a famous referent he could hinge his identity to. In contrast, my parents never bothered to tell me even a small detail about the man I was named after, much less maintain their relationship with him. He died without knowing his friends' son shared his name. It mirrors the way I feel about the limits of their understanding of me: loving but at times selectively careless and without presence in some of the most important places for needs that connect to my identity in specific ways.

Being forgettable is survivable on its own but being the forgettable half of a matched set is different. There's a control subject standing next to you at all times and everyone can't help but run the comparison out loud. When you're a twin you often get to be half of one person at best, and I was routinely assigned the lesser half after a certain age (some people still do it). "Oh, you're The Other One." Later in adolescence, our bodies diverged. At age 17, my brother began medaling on Muscle Beach podiums as a competitive bodybuilder and the diminishment stopped being figurative. Most people incorrectly assumed I was the younger twin and many began calling me "the little one" or "the small one" to my face. They did it cheerfully, like how you'd use a nickname somebody had agreed to.

Something I only really worked out after learning more about my name recently was that I couldn't attribute any significance to it beforehand, and that basically allowed a lifetime of diminishment to leak into my self image, whereas a stronger sense of identity might have offered a protective wall of sorts.

The way I finally asked for more information again was a little silly. A friend posted something that encouraged me to ask my parents about their favorite colors, animals, flowers, and the like. Somewhere in that conversation the older question I'd been carrying since childhood surfaced.

My mother said she'd met Stedman a total of perhaps three times; her memory of him was impressionistic. Very tall (obituary said 6'7"), faithful and devout, intelligent, gentlemanly, and a calming foil to my father's more excitable friends.She said that being around him made her feel at ease. She was fuzzy on anything verifiable, so I'm glad I had three sources.

My father had a lot more. Once I got him talking, he didn't stop for an hour. He met Stedman playing tennis at Alamo Square Park somewhere between 1985 and 1989. The group played weekly (sometimes more) and it was competitive enough that people came out on Saturday mornings specifically to spectate. If it had rained overnight they'd pull off their shirts and squeegee the court with them so the matches could proceed.

There was a Brazilian guy in the group named Gabriel. He'd hit a couple of balls and have to sit down. He stopped showing up to tennis, moved across the bay to Oakland, and eventually died there. Nobody really ever asked after him as the AIDS epidemic began to crest in San Francisco; during the don't-tell years, the stigma did everyone's asking for them. My father learned about it years later from Stedman. He called it willful ignorance: "It just pains me whenever I think of it."

Stedman came down to Los Angeles once or twice after my parents relocated and stayed with them in the apartment the Northridge quake took in 1994. "Mom just loved him. Queen's English accent, a gentleman in every respect, cerebral, well-read, gentle." His last visit was before I was born. I asked my father then and there if Stedman knew I was named after him. He responded, "I would think not, because we just lost contact."

Decades passed and eventually another friend of my father's who was still in San Francisco ran into Stedman at a local church (ostensibly St. Dominic's Catholic Church, going by the obituary). My father indicated to the mutual friend that he'd like to reconnect if possible, but that friend never followed up. Eventually, my father just Googled him (you know, the way anyone could have on any one of the seven thousand preceding days) and found the obituary. "I just freaked out." He said what broke him was the outpouring of support from the congregation and all the visible evidence of an entire life he'd been out of contact with. Somehow I still never got to hear about this until I pried it out a few weeks ago.

I'm a little stuck on the fact that my parents gave me a name loaded with meaning but then never handed me the meaning, which feels like an act of carelessness or an erasure of that meaning. It stings in a specific way to be named after a man they let fizzle away without event until a search engine told them he'd been dead for a few years. I know my parents love me the way parents love children. I also sometimes feel like they don't really care quite enough to fully know me as a person. I've often felt spiritually discarded and abandoned by them in a forgot-to-bother way more so than an actively harmful one; like most people I introduced myself to growing up. The entire conversation was my father grieving that exact flaw in himself. He regrets the way he let close connections like Gabriel, Stedman, and others lose out to distance or inertia.

Knowing now that I've been living inside the footprints of my late namesake's life for years shifts something. I've said before that the Bay Area's ley lines are special and I feel that now more than ever. I feel like I'm in the right place at the right time to do whatever it is I am meant to with a sense of higher significance about it all. There are some rocks and bandages in the way right now but I'm well on my way down the path.

Stedman was the tallest person in just about every room he ever walked into, but the obituary doesn't remember him for it once. It remembers him for being gentle and formal and kind; for stewardship and holding things together on behalf of other people. "With his wealth of interests and knowledge and his immense, pure heart, he found delight in everyone." It's a funny legacy to leave to someone everyone called small once upon a time. Like the Stedman before me, my heart has always been enormous.

I was home recently and went out to a karaoke bar with my friend Diana, whom I've known for about twenty years. Partway through the night she recognized me aloud for being the friend who always shows up. She remembered better than I had that I've pulled up to wherever she happened to be in the world: LA, Davis, or even Barcelona just for a night where I slept outside on a sandy beach. She appreciated that I've always found a way to stay connected and come through and that helped me see some virtue of mine through another person's eyes.

If I'm remembered for one thing as I am today, I want it to be this characteristic. That no matter how much time and distance accumulate between me and someone who is a part of my story, that I'm here to hold and reattach the bond. I hope that anyone I've experienced a real connection to knows their place in my heart and knows they can stay there as long as they want to.

There's an album in a storage unit somewhere in Southern California that contains a photograph of Stedman with my parents. "Just the three of us." Both of my parents independently remember what they were wearing in it. My father doesn't want to scan it and send it over. He wants me to come down and look at it in person instead. I think we both agree that it would offer a welcome sense of closure.

I know I'm a little late, but so long Stedman. I guess I'll see you soon.

According to court documents, after learning of the diagnosis, the intended parents demanded that West undergo a late-term abortion, citing an abortion clause in the surrogacy contract. They threatened West with a $250,000 lawsuit for breach of contract if she refused.

West refused.

She offered to cut ties with the couple, assume responsibility for the child herself, or place him for adoption. Later, she offered to renounce parental rights if the couple would agree to allow the child to receive lifesaving surgery.

The article states that "the case demonstrates what happens when human beings, in this case an unborn baby boy, are commodified and sold in the marketplace like any other piece of property. It is fundamentally and necessarily dehumanizing. The California couple believes they have the right to snuff out this boy’s life and that the woman carrying him in her womb has no say in the matter. Every child deserves to be welcomed as a gift—not treated as the object of a contract. Every woman deserves to be valued for who she is—not for what her body can provide.

I was born again 50 years ago yesterday. At age 17, I was supposed to be in Florida at a baseball tournament, but a God ordained hand injury DQed that, detouring me to a booster sponsored Fellowship of Christian Athletes Conference at Central Michigan University, where this worldly Roman Catholic sinner was stormed by the gospel all week, and emotionally collapsed at the feet of an all forgiving Jesus at the last session on August 5, 1976.  
I remember arriving home and my dad asked me, "Well, how did it go?" I said, "Dad, I became a Christian this week."  He just stared at me, blinking with his one eye that wasn't patched, processing.  
Well, was it the real deal?  Time is the great revealer.  50 years!  The rest of that summer I devoured my Good News for Modern Man New Testament they'd given me, and I couldn't be silent about this Savior whose favor I couldn't earn by ceremonies and being good, but "paid it all on the cross." 

Amazing grace (how sweet the sound)
that saved a wretch like me!
I once was lost, but now am found,
was blind, but now I see.

Through many dangers, toils and snares
I have already come:
'tis grace has brought me safe thus far,
and grace will lead me home.

What a Savior!

Here's the gospel I believed that day 50 years ago:

Heaven cannot be earned by doing good works.  Eternal life will be enjoyed only by those who see the bankruptcy of their best efforts in God’s eyes, and humbly beg for His pardon and mercy that is found in Christ’s work alone.

“For all of us have become like one who is unclean, and all our righteous deeds are like filthy rags” (Isaiah 64:6).

“For by grace you have been saved through faith; and that not of yourselves, it is a gift of God; not as a result of works, that no one should boast” (Ephesians 2:8-9).

One sharp winter’s day a poor woman stood at the window of a king’s greenhouse, looking for a cluster of grapes, which she longed to have for her sick child.  She went home to her spinning wheel, earned a silver piece, and offered it to the gardener for the grapes.  He waved his hand and ordered her away.  She returned to her cottage, snatched the blanket from her bed, pawned it, and once more asked the gardener to sell her the grapes, offering him five shillings.  He spoke furiously to her, and was turning her out, when the princess came in, heard the man’s anger, saw the woman’s tears, and asked what was wrong.  

When the story was told, the princess said, “My dear woman, you have made a mistake.  My father is not a merchant, but a king; his business is not to sell, but to give;” and upon saying this, she plucked the cluster of grapes from the vine and dropped it into the woman’s apron.

 “Nothing in my hands I bring, simply to Thy cross I cling.”

Believe it and really live.

Speaking during an inspection of Section 4B in Ondo State on August 5, 2026, Umahi said construction is progressing across Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Akwa Ibom and Cross River, with several sections already substantially completed.

He said the project is creating thousands of direct and indirect jobs, improving security and opening new opportunities for commerce, agriculture and education.

“The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is already on sail. We have sailed past Lagos that my brother Donald Duke talked about.”

Umahi also defended the project’s revised alignment, explaining that the route was changed for engineering and economic reasons after the original coastal alignment encountered deep soil deposits and major ocean channels that would have significantly increased construction costs.

He urged Nigerians to offer constructive criticism while supporting projects that will benefit the region.

According to Umahi, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is committed to completing the highway and using infrastructure to transform Nigeria’s economy.

“Under President Bola Tinubu, this country shall be rebuilt.”

— Francis Nwaze, FIPMD
Senior Special Assistant to the Honourable Minister of Works (Media)
August 6, 2026

🌿🍒 𝗕𝗲𝘀𝘁 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗲𝗿𝗰𝗶𝗮𝗹 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗿𝗿𝘆 𝗚𝘂𝗮𝘃𝗮 𝗙𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗶𝗻 𝗞𝗲𝗻𝘆𝗮: 𝗔 𝗖𝗼𝗺𝗽𝗹𝗲𝘁𝗲 𝗙𝗮𝗿𝗺𝗲𝗿'𝘀 𝗚𝘂𝗶𝗱𝗲

Cherry Guava (Psidium cattleianum), also known as Strawberry Guava, is one of the most promising rare fruit crops in Kenya. It is prized for its sweet, aromatic fruits, adaptability, ornamental value, and increasing demand among homeowners, fruit enthusiasts, and commercial growers.

If you're planning to invest in Cherry Guava farming, choosing the right location is one of the most important decisions you'll make. The right climate, altitude, rainfall, and soil conditions directly influence tree health, fruit quality, yields, and long-term profitability.

This comprehensive guide explores the best regions for commercial Cherry Guava farming in Kenya, the environmental conditions the crop thrives in, and practical tips for establishing a productive orchard.

🌍 𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝗟𝗼𝗰𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗠𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀

Even though Cherry Guava is known for being adaptable, commercial production performs best where environmental conditions closely match the crop's natural requirements.

Choosing a suitable region helps:

✅ Increase fruit yield
✅ Improve fruit sweetness and quality
✅ Reduce disease pressure
✅ Lower irrigation costs
✅ Improve flowering and fruit set
✅ Extend orchard lifespan

☀️ 𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗮𝗹 𝗚𝗿𝗼𝘄𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

Before selecting a location, understand the crop's preferred conditions.

🌡 Temperature

Cherry Guava performs well in warm to mild climates.

Ideal range:

✔ 18°C–28°C

It can tolerate warmer temperatures if adequate moisture is available.

🌧 Rainfall

The crop grows best where annual rainfall is moderate and well distributed.

Recommended:

✔ 800–1,800 mm annually

Where rainfall is unreliable, supplementary irrigation is beneficial.

🏔 Altitude

Cherry Guava adapts well to many elevations.

Recommended range:

✔ 800–2,200 metres above sea level

Higher elevations often produce fruits with excellent flavour and colour.

🌱 Soil

The tree thrives in:

✔ Deep soils
✔ Fertile soils
✔ Well-drained soils
✔ Loamy soils

Avoid waterlogged areas, as prolonged wet conditions can increase the risk of root diseases.

🧪 Soil pH

Ideal soil pH:

5.5–6.8

Slightly acidic soils generally support healthy nutrient uptake and vigorous growth.

🌿 1. Central Kenya

Central Kenya offers many of the conditions Cherry Guava prefers.

Suitable counties include:

✔ Kiambu
✔ Murang'a
✔ Nyeri
✔ Kirinyaga

These areas typically provide fertile soils, moderate rainfall, and favorable temperatures.

🌄 2. Eastern Highlands

Several highland areas in Eastern Kenya are suitable for Cherry Guava production.

Examples include:

✔ Embu
✔ Meru
✔ Tharaka Nithi (cooler zones)

The combination of altitude and well-drained soils supports healthy orchard development.

🌳 3. Rift Valley Highlands

Parts of the Rift Valley have excellent conditions for commercial orchards.

Suitable areas include:

✔ Nakuru
✔ Nandi
✔ Uasin Gishu (warmer locations)
✔ Elgeyo Marakwet (selected zones)

Farmers should choose sites with good drainage and moderate temperatures.

🌱 4. Western Kenya

Western Kenya receives relatively high rainfall, making it suitable where drainage is adequate.

Potential counties include:

✔ Kakamega
✔ Bungoma
✔ Vihiga
✔ Busia (well-drained sites)

Proper orchard management helps reduce disease pressure in wetter environments.

🌴 5. Selected Coastal Areas

Cherry Guava can also grow in some coastal locations.

Commercial success depends on:

✔ Reliable irrigation where necessary
✔ Well-drained sandy loam soils
✔ Good orchard management

Avoid low-lying sites prone to flooding.

🌞 6. Semi-Humid Areas

With irrigation, Cherry Guava can be cultivated successfully in several semi-humid regions.

Consistent moisture is especially important during establishment and fruit development.

🚫 𝗥𝗲𝗴𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀 𝗥𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗶𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗘𝘅𝘁𝗿𝗮 𝗖𝗮𝗿𝗲

Some locations may require additional management rather than being unsuitable.

These include areas with:

⚠ Prolonged drought
⚠ Poor drainage
⚠ Heavy clay soils
⚠ Frequent flooding
⚠ Strong salinity

Such challenges can often be mitigated with proper site preparation, irrigation, drainage improvements, and soil management.

💧 𝗜𝗿𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀

Commercial orchards benefit from reliable water supplies.

Recommended systems include:

✔ Drip irrigation
✔ Micro-sprinklers
✔ Water harvesting
✔ Mulching to conserve soil moisture

🌿 𝗦𝗼𝗶𝗹 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗽𝗮𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Before planting:

✔ Conduct a soil test.
✔ Correct soil pH if necessary.
✔ Incorporate well-decomposed organic manure.
✔ Prepare sufficiently sized planting holes.
✔ Improve drainage in heavy soils.

Many highland regions provide:

🍒 Better fruit colour
🍒 Enhanced flavour
🍒 Vigorous tree growth
🍒 Consistent flowering
🍒 Reduced heat stress

These factors contribute to higher-quality produce suitable for premium markets.

“WE HAVE SAILED PAST EPE”: UMAHI CLARIFIES DONALD DUKE’S OPINION AS TINUBU’S LAGOS-CALABAR COASTAL SUPERHIGHWAY ADVANCES ACROSS STATES

The Honourable Minister of Works, Senator Engr. David Umahi, CON, has clarified opinion arising from the opinion expressed by former Cross River State Governor, Donald Duke, that the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway would may not go beyond Epe, explaining that construction has already progressed beyond the area and is advancing steadily across several states.

Speaking during an inspection of Section 4B of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway in Ondo State on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, the Minister explained that the Renewed Hope flagship infrastructure project of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is making steady progress, creating thousands of jobs, improving security and opening new opportunities for commerce, agriculture and education.

Recalling Donald Duke’s opinion on the project, Umahi pointed out that the facts on the ground have now answered every doubt. “So the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is already on sail. And then so we have sail past Lagos that my brother Donald Duke talked about.”

The Minister explained that construction is progressing simultaneously across several state, “We are also on sail at Ogun, 28KM, on sail at Ondo, 52KM, all by two. We are already on sail in Calabar, 27km, and the Akwa Ibom, the first section of Akwa Ibom is about 47km. Those jobs are over 60 percent done. And we are on sail in the longest section of this Lagos-Calabar, that is at Akwa Ibom, 180km by two.”

Umahi emphasised that the coastal highway is not just about connecting communities but about transforming lives through employment, improved security and economic prosperity. “Roads are source of employment. We’ve counted over one thousand people within this section employed by HITECH. It is creating a lot of direct and indirect jobs. It is also solving the problem of insecurity. Because anywhere we are working, we have a lot of security people working along the corridor. We have the local people that are also helping, and they have their vigilante, they have their local security, and so it is helping. It is opening a lot of corridor for commerce, for agriculture, for education.”

The Minister maintained that constructive criticism remains welcome, provided it is accompanied by practical alternatives. “So if you want to criticize us, I’ve said it, criticize us constructively and offer alternatives.”

Umahi further explained that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu remains fully committed to delivering the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway, expressing confidence that the project will be completed. “According to the words of President Bola Tinubu, he said this project will be done. With God on his side, it will be done.”

The Minister urged the people of the Niger Delta to support and defend the transformational project, describing it as one that will reshape the economic future of the region. “It is up to Niger Delta people to open their mouth and defend these projects. Of course, they should defend the project. They should defend the president. They must have to vote for the president to complete this project.”

Umahi maintained that opposition to the coastal highway does not reflect the interests of the Niger Delta people. “Those who are attacking the coastal highway, they don’t have love for the Niger Delta people.”

The Minister described the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway as one of the most transparent and economically prudent infrastructure projects ever undertaken in the country. “And this project is the most prudent project I’ve ever seen. When the Deutsche Bank people came to finance the first section, they said that the construction was in perfection. They said the design was in perfection, but the procurement, the cost was undervalued. And that’s why when they put it in the market, it was oversubscribed by 100m US dollars. And that is our bragging right as Minister of Works.”

text:
“WE HAVE SAILED PAST EPE”: UMAHI CLARIFIES DONALD DUKE’S OPINION AS TINUBU’S LAGOS-CALABAR COASTAL SUPERHIGHWAY ADVANCES ACROSS STATES

In a statement by @FrancisNwaze1, Senior Special Assistant (Media) to the Honourable Minister of Works, Senator Engr. David Umahi, CON, has clarified remarks by former Cross River Governor Donald Duke suggesting the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway might not extend beyond Epe. During an inspection of Section 4B in Ondo State on Wednesday, 5 August 2026, the Minister stated that construction has already advanced well past Lagos and is progressing simultaneously across multiple states.

Nwaze reported that Umahi highlighted ongoing work of approximately 28 km in Ogun, 52 km in Ondo, 27 km in Calabar, about 47 km on the first Akwa Ibom section (over 60% complete), and the longest stretch of 180 km in Akwa Ibom. The dual-carriageway project is generating thousands of jobs—more than 1,000 people employed by HITECH on the inspected section alone—while enhancing security along the corridor and creating opportunities for commerce, agriculture and education.

The Minister explained that the route alignment was revised purely for engineering and economic reasons. The original coastal path encountered soft soils as deep as 50 metres and would have required three major bridges of roughly 3.5 km each across ocean channels, making it technically difficult and prohibitively expensive. The adjusted alignment follows President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s directive to minimise large water crossings while ensuring the project remains achievable and of high quality.

Umahi described the highway as one of the most transparent and cost-effective infrastructure projects undertaken in Nigeria. He noted that Deutsche Bank officials found the design and construction to be of excellent standard and that the first section was oversubscribed by $100 million when placed on the market. He welcomed constructive criticism that offers practical alternatives, reaffirmed the President’s commitment to completing the project, and urged the people of the Niger Delta to support and defend it as a transformative initiative for the region’s economic future.

The Minister also commended HITECH Construction Company for its professionalism, quality of work and positive relationship with host communities.

THREE US MIDDLE EAST ALLIES SIGN A MUSLIM DEFENSE PACT AND AMERICA IS NOT IN IT

A new Muslim defense pact among Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan will be signed this Friday in Jeddah, and Washington is not invited.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will meet in the Saudi coastal city to sign a trilateral defense agreement, according to Reuters and AFP sources.

Turkey is formally joining the pact that Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed in September 2025, an agreement whose core clause declares that an attack on one country is an attack on both.  That language is a copy of NATO's famous Article 5.

The timing says everything.  

The United States and Iran are at war.  The Strait of Hormuz is closed.  Houthi missiles wounded Saudi civilians near the Yemen border this same week.

One simple headline, three complicated countries

The Israeli press describes the pact as an effort to contain Iran.  That is true, but only for one of the three signers.

In reality, this is a story about foreign policy motives that do not match.  A simple way to remember the three actors: the rich one, the bellicose one, and the poor one.

Saudi Arabia is the rich one.  Turkey is the bellicose one.  Pakistan is the poor one.  Each country signs the same paper this Friday for a completely different reason.

The rich one: Saudi Arabia wants protection it can trust

Riyadh's motive is the straightforward one.  A senior Saudi official said this week that the kingdom expects attacks "from north and south."

The Saudis have learned that hosting American bases does not guarantee American protection.  

Iranian drones burned Saudi oil facilities in 2019, and Washington responded with words.  

Israel struck targets in Doha, the capital of neighboring Qatar, in September 2025, and Washington offered only a mild complaint.

Less than two weeks after that strike in Doha, Riyadh signed the pact with Pakistan.  The Saudis reportedly did not even inform Washington before signing.

A Reuters journalist asked whether the pact obliges Pakistan to extend its nuclear umbrella over Saudi Arabia.  The senior Saudi official gave a chilling answer: the agreement "encompasses all military means."

The bellicose one: Erdogan collects alliances like an empire collects provinces

Turkey's motive is the complex one, and readers of this site already know the pattern.

Ankara keeps a military base and a defense pledge in Qatar.  Ankara holds naval and port rights in Somalia until 2034.  Turkish troops operate in Libya.  Turkish drones arm a dozen African states.  

Last week, as we informed our readers, Turkey also announced it was raising military readiness over Cyprus, and blamed Israel for it.

Turkish analyst Goktug Caliskan described his country's strategy with unusual honesty, calling Ankara "a unique geopolitical hybrid": a NATO member with NATO-grade weapons that speaks the language of the Global South.

That is the game.  

Turkey keeps the protection and technology of NATO while it builds a parallel network of Muslim alliances.  

Erdogan enjoys the benefits of both clubs and offers loyalty to neither.

The poor one: Pakistan sells the one thing it has

Pakistan's motives come in order of urgency: money, India, and relevance.

The first motive is money.  Pakistan survives on international rescue loans, and Saudi Arabia is becoming its largest external financier, with more than six thousand million dollars in loans and deposits this fiscal year.  

The pact formalizes Pakistan's oldest export: soldiers and deterrence in exchange for cash.

The second motive is India.  After the military crisis between India and Pakistan in May 2025, the pact changes the calculations of any future war.  

An Indian strike on Pakistan could now be interpreted as an attack on Saudi Arabia, a kingdom where two and a half million Indian citizens work and send money home.

Former Indian Foreign Secretary Kanwal Sibal called the pact a "grave misstep" by Saudi Arabia and warned it was "strategically most adventurous."

The third motive is relevance.  This agreement seats a nearly bankrupt state at the center of Middle East geopolitics, while India, one of the largest economies on earth, is left outside of the agreement.

Why Israel is nervous, and why Washington should be

Are these three countries reliable American allies?  

Officially, yes.  Turkey sits in NATO.  The United States has officially designated Pakistan a major non-NATO ally.  Saudi Arabia is a top buyer of American weapons.

Yet these three American partners just built their own Article 5, and America is not in it.

Georgetown professor Gregory Gause argues the pact is a message to Washington: if the United States cannot restrain Israel from striking its Middle East partners, the Saudis will turn to other security providers.

For Israel, the concern is more direct.  Erdogan calls Zionism a genocidal ideology and shelters Hamas figures on Turkish soil.  

This Friday, that same Erdogan gains a seat in a pact standing next to the only nuclear arsenal in the Muslim world.

Pakistani Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar was asked about the idea of a broader joint Muslim security force.  Dar answered: "Why not?  What's wrong with that?"

The lesson America First already taught

None of this happened by accident.  

It happened because years of weak American foreign policy taught the region a lesson: American protection is not guaranteed, especially in one of the most turbulent regions of the world.

Allies who doubt American protection will buy protection somewhere else.  

Some will buy it from Pakistan.  Others will buy from Beijing, which already supplies most of Pakistan's weapons and has replaced Washington as Saudi Arabia's main trade partner.

President Trump has an opening to reverse this drift, and the tools exist: stronger written defense commitments for the Gulf, delivered from a position of strength, not apology.

Peace Through Strength is not a slogan.  

It is the only policy that keeps allies from writing their own Article 5.  

America can still be the umbrella of protection that the free world trusts, and this Friday in Jeddah is the reminder to act.  🇺🇸🇸🇦🤝 #MuslimDefensePact #SaudiArabia #Turkey

Speaking during an inspection of Section 4B of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway in Ondo State on Wednesday, August 5, 2026, the Minister explained that the Renewed Hope flagship infrastructure project of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is making steady progress, creating thousands of jobs, improving security and opening new opportunities for commerce, agriculture and education.

And we are on sail in the longest section of this Lagos-Calabar, that is at Akwa Ibom, 180km by two.”

In a July 31 interview on the CBC News program Morning Live with guest host John Northcott, retired American diplomat Gina Abercrombie-Winstanley was interviewed for eight minutes on the topic of the Israel-Hamas conflict in Gaza.

Abercrombie-Winstanley has served as the chief diversity and inclusion officer of the United States Department of State under the Biden administration, as well as ambassador to Malta, a European microstate with a population smaller than Brampton, Ontario.
The caption on screen informed viewers that she was the former deputy director for Iran affairs, though nowhere in her official biography lists any such title or responsibility, and it is unclear on what basis CBC made such a claim.

Abercrombie-Winstanley’s comments were rife with falsehoods and misinformation. At one point, claiming that aid is “very restricted” coming into Gaza, she told Northcott that “right now, 500 trucks per week pass into the Gaza Strip.”

In fact, according to COGAT, the agency coordinating aid into Gaza, the correct figure is roughly 600 trucks per day being permitted into the coastal territory. Despite her claim effectively reducing aid figures by some 85 percent, she was not challenged by Northcott, who permitted her false statement to stand unchallenged.

Near the end of the interview, she made another eyebrow-raising allegation, telling viewers that “five Israeli soldiers have been killed, over a thousand Palestinians, including many civilians have been killed daily since a ceasefire began.”

Once again, Abercrombie-Winstanley’s figure is not only false, but wrong to the power of roughly 300. In fact, since the ceasefire between Hamas and Israel took effect in October, 2025, an estimated 1,000 Palestinians have died in total, not daily.

If her outlandish allegation were correct, that would mean that some 300,000 Palestinians have been killed in less than a year, a figure that no legitimate body, even Hamas, claims to be the case.

Moreover, the (actual) figure includes hundreds of terrorist operatives (Israel claims 420), including individuals who participated in the October 7, 2023 massacres in Israel, as well as other active members of terrorist groups like Hamas, and represents a remarkably low proportion of civilian casualties, in particular given the intense urban combat environment.
This is not the first time that Abercrombie-Winstanley has made highly questionable comments on Canada’s taxpayer-funded broadcaster.

In February, 2025, she was interviewed by host Dwight Drummond, who failed to offer any challenge to her claims, and in fact muttered agreement. After castigating “both sides,” she soon launched into a rant casting unfounded aspersions on Israel’s identity, alleging that “the state and people of Israel have decided de facto that it is more important to have a Jewish state than a democratic state.”

In actuality, Israel is a liberal democracy with equal rights for all citizens, Jewish or not.

Gina Abercrombie-Winstanley’s falsehoods spoken during the July 31 interview on CBC News’ Morning Live were so preposterous and out of step with reality that it should have prompted an immediate correction from host John Northcott. Incredibly, none was forthcoming.

Consequently, HonestReporting Canada filed an official complaint with CBC News executives and requested an immediate on-air correction to be broadcast. On August 1, CBC News Network aired the following on-air correction orated by CBC Anchor Marianne Dimain:

“We’d like to clarify statements made in an interview yesterday with former U.S. Ambassador Gina Abercrombie-Winstanley. Referring to casualties in Gaza, she suggested over one thousand Palestinians have been killed per day since the ceasefire.  In fact, that reflects the total number of reported deaths since the ceasefire began. She also talked about the number of trucks entering Gaza.  Israeli officials state up to six hundred trucks enter every day. Humanitarian groups estimate that fewer than one hundred and fifty of them are strictly carrying humanitarian aid.”
Honest Reporting Canada

text:
1:03AM on a Thursday morning & I am back again here folks tippy tappin away on my laptop in the dark while some podcast drones away on the tele as the much needed background music to my magical, manic mind. Man when I was drinking I could sleep like a fucking baby. Now? It's just real amazing little 2 hour segments of small sleep. I wake up and beg for it to be morning, beg for it to be time to get the morning routine going but nope, its another 90 minute mini nap in the middle of the night with my mind spinning like a hamster wheel of hell with the devil hamster strung out on meth going a million miles per minute. Fun times, eh?

Got all my literature today and the stepwork, the real party, starts tonight with my sponsor and man that dude is a total bad ass by the way - but I did have to call him a few times yesterday, and I so desperately am looking forward to the work later today, the much needed dark, healing work that is about to begin... But no no Andy, don't get impatient with your recovery, because Ms. Kelly says that impatience is one of my relapse triggers. Awesome, great, cool, yay. But probably going to read Dr. Bob's Nightmare sometime between now and the 5am meeting to pass some much needed time off the corrupt clock because I hear that's a real fun one to read and I need some immediate inspiration.

I started to re-read Thompson's Hell's Angels again for the millionth time and ahhh the intro always hits like a powerful drug surging through my arteries, veins and capillaries providing some much needed writer's block relief: California, Labor Day weekend ... early, with ocean fog still in the streets, outlaw motorcyclists wearing chains, shades and greasy Levis roll out from damp garages, all-night diners and cast-off one-night pads in Frisco, Hollywood, Berdoo and East Oakland, heading for the Monterey peninsula, north of Big Sur... Love his work and yeah yeah Fear &  Loathing blah blah but what about his ESPN blogs in Hey Jude, especially the 9/11 recap, or the Caribbean Nightmare descent into madness that is the Rum Diary... Rum... And Coke... and coke. Mmmmm damn, we had some real good times there didn't we?

I've been by the famed and fortified Owl Farm in Woody Creek, Colorado seeking, looking, or even peeping, for a glimpse of what Hunter's life was like once upon a time there but nothing can be seen from the road, the sweet wide open road that brings such peace in times of need. I wanted to see that big ass red peyote fisted cannon his ashes were blown out of and boom, boom what a fabulous way to go out folks. Rumor has it that good ol' Johnny Depp, Captain Jack Sparrow himself, has it in storage somewhere in Paris if my source is accurate. Boom! Boom! Would love to be in those old, ancient, story filled, cobbled, gritty Parisian streets but first thing's first bud, we gotta get clean. Don't get too impatient like Ms. Kelly gleaned!

I have to get back out to West Texas soon after this shit is over and get back to Marfa and my beloved Chinati Foundation and get me some Flavin, some Judd and some John Chamberlin back in my little life to help ease this progressive, pitiful pain. Shit I think it's been a decade since I've been down in those spooky, foggy, purple-y, Marfa Light lit San Juan magical mountains.

3:02AM now and I am going to try to go back to sleep between now and the 5am but will probably find myself pacing around, with this magical, manic mind making my life more amusing. Oh yeah the 5am... Good god that meeting is poppin' off like a New York disco spilling out into the grimey Lower East Side streets at 5am with the finance bros, the fashion kids, and the glamorous gliterrati frantically looking for late night spots to keep the alcohol and drug fueled party going. I love the city man, the city that jump starts so many careers, the city that offers every vice you can consume, the city that is always alive, always busy and the city that never sleeps, just like me.

#Recovery #MentalHealth

text:
Oooof. Another sweaty, sleepless, manic filled night. After only sleeping for a few hours last night, almost having to go to the hospital yesterday, or at least thinking I needed to because I felt like I was going to fucking die, to what simply felt like "pulling off" what ended up being a very busy, very chaotic day of work, and THEN hitting a 5PM meeting, I crashed early and hard. Maybe 7PM? Wonderful, healing sleep - nature's nurse. Need it.

Now it's 4AM and I can't sleep so here I am typing away in the dark at my laptop with all of you, with the AC on blast because god knows it's hot outside and I can't wait to go for a walk and get a sweat going to get through this fucking stage of recovery. Need it.

If you know me, you know I like to understand things. Hell, pretty sure everyone likes to understand things but for some reason I am compulsive about it, I need it, I need to know. Why is my detox "delayed" - why did I not have these crazy nights a week or two ago? I'm 18 days in. What the fuck is going on? Frustration mounts and all the Internet research, Google, Ai, choose your weapon, etc, all seem to give similar but different answers - different than what I am actually experiencing. I want to talk to my sponsor about this, like right now, but its 4am man... Should I call him? I feel bad it. I don't know the rules yet. I don't. I just don't know and I want the knowledge. Need it.

Have a meeting here at 5am in 30 minutes, then off for a walk with a back pack full of waters for my unhoused friends down on the strip because I worry so much about them and want to help them so badly. Also added bonus the waters add weight to the backpack so I get a better work out in, not mad about that. Also you won't catch photos or videos of me passing these waters out on here, I'm not doing it for the clout. I'm doing it for me and for those in need. Need it.

But the routine is starting to stick and it feels good. Wake up, write, attend a meeting, walk with waters for service for the unhoused while not getting shanked, shower, then another meeting at 7am and then off to work and all the fun things that unravel there. Routine is good. Need it.

Welp, that's all from detox land for now. I'll have a documentary review coming here in a little while, it's about Sega vs. Nintendo which will be more light hearted than whatever the hell this is. But for now writing feels good and again very cathartic. And I really do need it.

text:
Outdated CPR training is putting women’s lives at risk.

Women who suffer cardiac arrest outside hospital are significantly less likely to survive than men, and one overlooked reason is that CPR training almost never accounts for female anatomy.

A Duke University analysis across 47 U.S. states found women are 14% less likely to receive bystander CPR. In the UK, the gap is similar: only 68% of women get CPR from bystanders compared to 73% of men, with many people citing fear of inappropriate touching or concern about injuring a woman’s chest.

The problem is compounded by the tools we train on. A global survey revealed that roughly 95% of CPR manikins are designed with flat chests; only one widely available model includes visible breasts. As a result, most trainees never practice the slight technique adjustments needed for women and often hesitate in real emergencies.

Research published in the Journal of Emergency Medical Services offers hope: when trainees used manikins equipped with realistic silicone breasts, they were almost twice as likely to feel confident performing chest compressions on a woman.

Experts say updating training manikins to represent both male and female anatomy could eliminate hesitation, close the gender survival gap, and save thousands of lives. https://t.co/y7KN8TxxQD

“I had the opportunity to play with my brothers, D-Wade and Chris Bosh, and one of the greatest, if not the greatest, to ever play the game.”

“Pat Riley told us there’s winning and there’s misery. Ain’t no in-between.”

“The rest of my life has been messed up since he said that because I can’t do the in-between. If I’m losing, I’m miserable.”

Dwyane Wade says LeBron James and Chris Bosh immediately agreed to take less money to keep Haslem in Miami.

“I told Bron and CB, ‘This doesn’t work without number 40.’”

“There was no hesitation.”

“Bron was like, ‘Done. Whatever we need, because this doesn’t work without 40.’”

“If UD ain’t here, this don’t feel right.”

“To their credit, they both gave back money to get him close enough to where he felt comfortable staying, because he still had a family to feed.”

text:
The Devastation Caused by Guardianship Abuse

I recently had the opportunity to visit a friend in Florida whom I met because of our shared guardianship nightmares.

Her father is 90 years old and is currently trapped in a guardianship. He immigrated to the United States from Guyana with nothing but a dream and built an extraordinary life through hard work and determination. He is the true definition of the American dream.

Today, his home is worth more than $1 million, and he owns additional income-producing properties that generate income each month.

Yet despite everything he worked a lifetime to build, he has lost control over his own life. He signed his pre-need directives multiple times to ensure he would never end up in this situation.

Florida law was supposed to protect exactly this. Under Florida Statute § 744.3045, a competent adult can name a preneed guardian the person they choose, in advance, to serve as their guardian if they ever become incapacitated. And under § 744.312, the court is required to consider the wishes the incapacitated person has expressed as to who should be appointed. These statutes exist for one reason: to honor a senior's own voice in decisions about their life, before anyone else's interests get involved. He did everything the law asked of him. It didn't matter.

My friend was forced to purchase the very home she grew up in despite already being on the title with her father under joint tenancy with right of survivorship — simply to save it from being sold by the guardian. The guardian sued her, using her father's own money, to force the sale of that home. In the end, the courts ordered her to pay a real estate agent more than $20,000 — for a house she already owned, that was never even listed on the market. She had to pay a stranger a five-figure fee to "sell" her a home that was already legally hers, just to keep the guardian from taking it. I visited that home. It wasn't just a house; it was a lifetime of memories.

She showed me her father's bedroom, preserved exactly as he left it. His wife, who courageously battled cancer for years before passing away, is still present in every corner of that room. Her wigs remain where she left them. Photographs of the two of them together line the walls, telling the story of a lifetime of love, devotion, and family.

She is successful, responsible, and has spent years sacrificing her own time, finances, and emotional well-being fighting simply to be part of her father's life.

Yet she was denied the opportunity to care for him.

Instead, custody was given to a son who could not pass a background check and who is now being paid to care for their father. A son who had been disinherited from his father's trust.

Think about that.

This father has more than enough money to remain in his own home with professional caregivers providing 24-hour care if needed. His daughter has repeatedly offered to care for him herself, asking for absolutely nothing in return except the chance to be with her father.

Instead, she has to fight just to see him.

How can a system that claims to protect vulnerable adults justify decisions like this?

When a guardianship strips a person of their rights, separates loving families, ignores capable family members, and enriches others while the protected person loses everything they worked a lifetime to build, it is no longer protection.

It is exploitation.

Stories like this are happening across America every single day. Guardianship should be a last resort, used only when absolutely necessary and with the least restrictive alternative in place. Instead, too often it has become a system that tears families apart, depletes estates, and leaves loved ones fighting the very people who claim to be protecting those they love.

That is not justice.

That is a complete disgrace.

text:
Friday morning headlines from #Georgia, 7 August

📍Eighteen years have passed since the August 2008 Russia–Georgia war over South Ossetia. On the Georgian side, 412 soldiers and civilians were killed, while 365 people died on the Ossetian side. Around 20,000 ethnic Georgians were forced to flee their homes. Georgia also lost control of another 125 villages in the Tskhinvali region (South Ossetia). After the active phase of the war ended, Russia recognized South Ossetia and Abkhazia as independent states. A timeline of the events, with photos and videos, is available here https://t.co/3jkjn0jKcD

📍Representatives of Georgia’s civil society issued a joint statement marking the 18th anniversary of the August war. They said Georgia’s defense capabilities are closely linked to the support of its international partners, and that Russia’s attempts to shift responsibility for its aggression onto Georgia harm the country’s national interests.

📍One year has passed since the Batumi City Court sentenced Mzia Amaghlobeli, founder of the popular media outlets Batumelebi and Netgazeti, to two years in prison for slapping a police officer who had insulted her. International organizations and diplomatic missions marked the anniversary. The OSCE Representative on Freedom of the Media, the British Embassy, and the International Press Institute called for her immediate release. The Georgian Young Lawyers’ Association (GYLA) said the European Court of Human Rights has registered a fourth complaint related to Amaghlobeli’s case. She was arrested in January 2025. Human rights groups say the case is politically motivated.

📍A court found opposition leader Nika Melia guilty of contempt of court and sentenced him to one year and six months in prison. Melia is already serving a sentence on other charges. However, the new sentence replaces the previous one, meaning his expected release date remains unchanged. He is due to be released in December 2026.

📍New charges have been filed in the case of the murder of young Tbilisi teacher Giga Avaliani. Prosecutors charged Nia Imnadze, the girlfriend of the main suspect, with incitement to intentionally inflict grievous bodily harm. Anastasia Beruashvili has also been charged with failing to report an especially serious crime. According to investigators, the suspects monitored Avaliani for several days before the attack and studied the route he usually took. The 28-year-old teacher died from injuries after a brutal beating in October 2025. More about the Giga Avaliani case here https://t.co/jWcURxKD2E

📍Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze made another statement about what he called Russophobia and a campaign against Russian tourists, which he claims is being carried out by certain groups in Georgia. According to him, false information is being deliberately spread on social media to create the impression that Georgia is unsafe for Russian tourists and to damage the country’s economy. Georgia’s State Security Service has opened an investigation under the article on sabotage. According to the agency, the campaign, allegedly coordinated from abroad and supported by certain individuals and organizations inside Georgia, used fake bot accounts to spread claims that Georgia poses a danger to Russian tourists, including false reports about the deliberate poisoning of their food.

📍According to Azerbaijani media, Baku has sent a diplomatic note to Georgia’s Foreign Ministry over what it says are unjustified delays faced by Azerbaijani truck drivers at Georgian border crossings, with some vehicles reportedly held for several weeks. In response, Georgia’s Foreign Ministry said the relevant agencies had begun an urgent review of the issue and were working on a solution. Azerbaijan’s embassy in Tbilisi also said the matter is being addressed jointly with the relevant Georgian authorities.

📍In Telavi, the main city of Georgia’s Kakheti region, which was recently hit by severe flooding and mudslides, all buildings located within a 10-meter zone around the Telavi Gorge will be demolished, local authorities said. The decision is based on an expert assessment. Residents affected by the measure will be offered alternative housing or financial compensation.

President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev now faces a historic choice:

Remain trapped between Putin’s declining Russian empire and Xi Jinping’s authoritarian China—or lead Kazakhstan toward sovereignty, prosperity and partnership with the democratic world.

Europe, America and the wider Free World should present Kazakhstan with a concrete strategic offer:

✅ A clear pathway toward OECD membership

Kazakhstan already cooperates extensively with the OECD and is working to implement OECD standards. The next step should be a formal accession perspective—conditional on economic reform, stronger institutions, anti-corruption measures, judicial independence and political liberalisation.

✅ Kazakhstan in an expanded EU Eastern Partnership

The European Union should create an Eastern Partnership Plus that includes democratic and reforming Central Asian countries.

Kazakhstan already has an Enhanced Partnership and Cooperation Agreement with the EU covering investment, trade, energy, raw materials and regulatory cooperation. This agreement should become the foundation for deeper European integration.

✅ A new NATO partnership

Kazakhstan has cooperated with NATO through the Partnership for Peace since 1994. NATO should offer a substantially upgraded partnership focused on military reform, officer training, interoperability, cybersecurity, border security and protection of Kazakhstan’s sovereignty.

The long-term objective must be clear: Kazakhstan should become a fully sovereign Western security partner, no longer dependent on Russia’s military structures.

✅ Major European and American energy agreements

The Free World should offer long-term contracts and investment for Kazakh oil, gas, uranium, critical minerals, renewable energy and hydrogen.

We should help Kazakhstan develop export routes across the Caspian Sea, Azerbaijan, Georgia and Türkiye—bypassing Russia completely.

European capital should finance pipelines, ports, railways, electricity connections, refineries and modern energy infrastructure.

Kazakhstan should receive:

• preferential access to European and American markets
• major infrastructure investment
• digital and artificial-intelligence partnerships
• cooperation in nuclear and renewable energy
• modern agricultural technology
• university and student-exchange programmes
• support for small and medium-sized enterprises
• integration into Western supply chains

✅ A strategic transport partnership

The EU, United States, Türkiye, Azerbaijan and Kazakhstan should jointly develop the Trans-Caspian Middle Corridor connecting Central Asia with the Black Sea and European markets.

Kazakhstan must become the central economic bridge between Europe and Central Asia—not merely a raw-material appendage of Moscow or Beijing.

But this offer must have clear conditions.

President Tokayev must:

🔹 end support for Putin’s war economy
🔹 fully enforce Western sanctions against Russia
🔹 prevent sanctions evasion through Kazakhstan
🔹 reduce dependence on Russian pipelines and military structures
🔹 defend Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity
🔹 release political prisoners
🔹 guarantee freedom of expression and political competition
🔹 strengthen the rule of law and independent courts
🔹 protect foreign investors and private property
🔹 gradually withdraw Kazakhstan from Russia-dominated organisations

Kazakhstan does not have to choose permanent isolation or submission.

The Free World must offer a serious alternative:

🇪🇺 European economic integration
🌐 OECD membership
🛡️ NATO partnership
⚡ Western energy investment
🚆 Trans-Caspian infrastructure
💶 Access to capital, technology and markets

President Tokayev, break with Putin’s Russia.

Choose sovereignty.
