What I’ve learned here is that there’s literally nothing anybody can say short of “everything is horrible and we’re all gonna starve to death” that will appease some people. Offering any type of solution, mitigator, or encouragement is condemned.

If you bring up how you couponed and ate out (maybe?) once a month and drove around in a car with no AC all summer in your 20s, you get told you “just don’t understand what kids these days go through.”

If you bring up how other generations weathered economic calamity throughout history and encourage people that they, too, have the power to survive this, you get told you want everyone to live like it’s the Great Depression and be happy about it.

If you tell someone it’s cheaper to make a burrito at home than DoorDash Chipotle, you get accused of demanding they live off rice and beans. (Which is ironic considering this whole thing started because someone was complaining about paying $20 for…rice and beans.)

If they scream that ground beef is $12 a pound and you point them to a store that has it for $5 a pound, you get told that’s subpar beef and would NEVER feed their family of eight, five of which are teen boys, what are you, a monster?!

If you agree that prices are insane and we have deep systemic problems that need fixing but that, in the meantime, perhaps people can save money with some simple changes, they just ignore you said the first part and accuse you of telling everyone to eat cake.

If you bring up those deep systemic problems and what it would take to fix them, everyone ignores that tweet because nobody *actually* knows how to realistically go about uprooting the welfare state, curbing government spending, getting the national debt under control, or dealing with foreign threats without spending money - most if not all of which would take the participation of our deeply broken Congress.

And in all of it, you get accused of sending a terrible political message to socialism-loving young people, and that the “correct” political message is to fuel mass hysteria over prices and let Iran have nukes so milk will magically come back down to 2005 prices. Which wouldn’t work because the issues are so much deeper than that and we’d wind up with egg all over our faces, but whatever.

They will find a problem with whatever you say because anything short of “you should be able to live at 23 without budgeting, penny-pinching, or sacrificing” (which literally no generation has ever done but okay) or “no one should have to give up a single creature comfort to buy food” is considered “bad political messaging” to the youths.

There’s no winning for anyone here because the point is not to have a conversation or to offer people hope. Many in the outrage mob don’t even see when someone is agreeing with them on the underlying issue but merely offering an alternate angle from which to approach it. They just want to be angry and they want everyone else to declare Doomsday with them and when someone doesn’t, they throw a fit.

Which, apparently, is considered GREAT political messaging.

Our nation has lost its soul.

Not that it hasn’t struggled since its bloody foundation. Perhaps that is the lesson: a world built on the blood of the innocent cannot stand forever, because eventually even the soil remembers.

The soil is sour.

I am reminded of the fall of the Aztecs and Rome.

When greed and fear overtook their leadership, when suffering became entertainment, death became policy, sacrifice became obedience, and control became culture, it changed who they were, soul-deep.

We are witnessing a pattern that has unfolded again and again throughout history.

Until humanity learns how to build a living world, one rooted in dignity, reciprocity, stewardship, and the protection of life, this will continue to be the result.

Empires consume themselves.
Living civilizations regenerate.
Nature left us the blueprint.
The ancestors left us a message.
The universe keeps repeating the pattern.

We simply forgot how to listen.

We forgot a language humanity once understood, a language carried through water, animals, trees, geometry, story, memory, and the living land.

There was a time when we walked hand in hand with Creation.

When we understood that we belonged to the universe instead of standing above it.

And oh, how we laughed.

This world must learn to laugh again.

To wonder again.

To love again.

How heartbreaking it is to watch human beings enslave themselves to systems, and to gods of money, domination, and extraction, that cannot create life, cannot heal what they destroy, and can never love them back.

But the living world is still here.

The pattern is still here.

The Garden is still possible.

So I will leave the light on.

Reporting from the Ark.

Watching.

Waiting.

Hoping to see you soon.

Good Health Is Good Business
Why the Greatest Investment You'll Ever Make Isn't in Your Business

By Lawrence Zolnowski
President & CEO | The Chamber Guy®

I want to ask you two simple questions.

If I could guarantee that your business would double over the next ten years...

Would you take that deal?

Of course you would.

Now let me change one part of the offer.

What if your health was cut in half during those same ten years?

Would you still take it?

For most of my life, I believed success was measured by building businesses, creating opportunities, growing organizations, and helping people succeed.

Today, I still believe all of those things matter.

But after meeting tens of thousands of business owners over the years, I've learned something even more important.

Without your health, every other success becomes harder to enjoy.

We Spend Our Lives Building Businesses...

...But How Much Time Do We Spend Building Ourselves?

Business owners are some of the hardest-working people you'll ever meet.

We're the first to arrive.

The last to leave.

We answer emails at midnight.

We skip vacations.

We postpone doctor's appointments.

We tell ourselves we'll slow down "after this project."

"After this quarter."

"After this year."

Then one day we realize something.

The business has grown.

The bank account has grown.

But our energy hasn't.

Our health hasn't.

Our relationships may not have either.

That isn't success.

That's simply surviving.

The Wealthiest Person in the Room Isn't Always the Richest

I've met business owners worth millions of dollars.

Some would gladly trade a portion of that wealth for one more healthy year.

One more pain-free day.

One more chance to travel.

One more opportunity to play with their grandchildren.

One more morning waking up full of energy.

Money can buy many things.

It cannot buy back time.

It cannot always buy back health.

That realization changes the way you look at success.

One Discovery Can Change Your Life

Never underestimate what one conversation can do.

One physician could identify a problem before it becomes serious.

One breakthrough treatment could restore your quality of life.

One wellness strategy could give you energy you haven't felt in years.

One nutrition change could improve every day that follows.

One referral could become your biggest customer.

One strategic partnership could transform your business.

One conversation could literally change your future.

Sometimes we are only one introduction away from a completely different life.

That's Why This Year's South Florida Health Expo Matters

People often think this event is only for doctors or healthcare companies.

It isn't.

It's for every person who believes life is worth living well.

It's for every entrepreneur who wants more energy.

Every executive who wants to perform at a higher level.

Every family that wants to live longer, healthier lives.

And every business owner looking to connect with one of the fastest-growing industries in South Florida.

Medical services.

Longevity.

Health & Wellness.

Preventative care.

Innovation.

Technology.

This isn't simply another trade show.

It's an opportunity to discover ideas that could improve your health, your business, or both.

The Hidden Secret Behind Our Sold-Out Expos

People often ask me why our expos continue to sell out.

Most assume it's because of the attendees.

The truth is...

The real magic happens before the doors even open.

We're the only business expo in Florida that dedicates three full hours exclusively to exhibitor networking.

No attendees.

No distractions.

Just business owners.

CEOs.

Founders.

Executives.

Decision-makers.

Meeting one another.

Building trust.

Sharing ideas.

Creating partnerships.

Many exhibitors tell me those three hours generate more business than the rest of the day combined.

Some meet future clients.

Others meet referral partners.

Some even build lifelong friendships.

That's our hidden secret.

Business doesn't just happen at our expos.

Relationships happen.

And relationships are where great businesses begin.

Why This Industry Matters So Much

South Florida is becoming one of America's premier destinations for health, longevity, wellness, and active lifestyles.

Successful people are investing in living better—not just living longer.

They're looking for answers.

They're looking for innovation.

They're looking for trusted professionals.

If your business serves people in any way—and almost every business does—this is an audience worth knowing.

Healthcare companies need marketing.

Technology.

Insurance.

Legal services.

Construction.

Real estate.

Printing.

Banking.

Transportation.

Professional services.

The opportunities extend far beyond medicine.

There Are Only About 15 Exhibitor Spaces Remaining

Don't wait.

Every year people tell us,

"I'll do it next year."

Many call back a few weeks later only to discover the show is sold out.

Before I Leave You With One Final Thought...

Twenty years from now...

Your children probably won't remember your biggest sale.

Your clients won't remember how many hours you worked.

No one will remember the email you answered at 11:30 at night.

But they'll remember whether you were healthy enough...

To take the vacation.

To play golf with a friend.

To dance at a wedding.

To hold your grandchild.

To enjoy the life you worked so hard to build.

That's why I believe...

Good Health Is Good Business.

Because the greatest investment you'll ever make...

Isn't in your company.

It's in yourself.

If you could improve just one area of your life this year—your health, your business, your finances, your relationships, or your work-life balance—which would you choose, and why?

text:
Two graduate students sat with Charlie Rose and explained why the world needed another search engine when Yahoo had already won.

Larry Page and Sergey Brin were in their twenties. Google was a few years old, running on money they'd raised while still enrolled at Stanford.

The market looked settled. Yahoo, AltaVista, Lycos, Excite. Portals stuffed with news, mail, weather, and directories, all trying to keep visitors on the page as long as possible.

Their answer was the opposite. A blank box on a white screen, designed to send you away as fast as possible.

The insight underneath was PageRank. Instead of counting words on a page, rank pages by how many other pages link to them, and weight those links by the authority of the sources.

They'd tried to sell it early on. The story goes that they offered the technology to Excite for around $1,000,000 and got turned down.

In the interview they're still explaining the basics. Why relevance beats volume. Why the fastest route off their site was the point.

Page has almost entirely disappeared from public view since, which makes the tape rarer every year.

Two students argued the winner of search had already been decided wrong, and they were right.

text:
Each of these coins began as a weighed metal blank, usually silver or copper alloy, placed between engraved dies and struck with a single hammer blow.

Greek mints used the octopus across several centuries and denominations. At Eretria, examples appear on silver staters, drachms and smaller fractions from roughly 500–465 B.C.; Syracuse later placed the animal on tiny silver litrai, some measuring about 12 millimeters and weighing less than a gram. 

The arms were compressed, curled or spread to occupy nearly every available part of the irregular flan. Because each coin was struck individually, differences in centering, pressure and die engraving made every impression distinct.

A coin’s image also helped identify its issuing city. Athens used the owl, Metapontum an ear of wheat and Kyzikos — a tuna. 

For maritime communities, the octopus offered a familiar local subject that could be recognized at a glance.

text:
I'm writing up an SOP template for https://t.co/PILY7FV23J members.

I'm thinking about adding a FAQ section that explains the Scriptural basis for church safety teams.

Here it is:

"""Are churches actually being targeted?"""

Violent attacks against American churches have increased seven-fold since 2018 (https://t.co/TFRu6BOVPP).

Since the days of the early Church, powers and principalities have delighted in seeing Christians "killed all day long...accounted as sheep for the slaughter" (Rom 8:36).

Christ instructed us to be armed ("...he who has no sword, let him sell his garment and buy one"; Luke 22:36), recognize evildoers ("...be wise as serpents"; Matt 10:16), and be ready to make the ultimate sacrifice for those we love ("greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one’s life for his friends"; John 15:13).

"""But shouldn't Christians be peaceful?"""

Some cite Jesus' charge to "turn the other cheek" (Matt 5:39), or how He stopped Peter from attacking the temple guard (John 18:11), as justification for Christian pacifism.

This argument ignores the intent, and even the content, of Scripture.

First, Christ's instruction to "turn the other cheek" was a refutation of personal revenge based on honor and pride—not a blanket prohibition of physical violence. Christ Himself fashioned a whip and assaulted merchants in the Temple of Jerusalem.

As for the second example, after Christ admonishes Peter in John 18:11, the verse continues: "Shall I not drink the cup which My Father has given Me?" Jesus stopped Peter only because it was His will to die to save us.

"""Am I even capable of protecting others?"""

First and foremost, God is in control: "Unless the Lord guards the city, the watchman stays awake in vain" (Ps 127:1).

Whereas it is paramount that we train hard ("a wise man will hear and increase learning"; Prov 1:5), God can and will perform amazing works through us according to His plans: "It is God who works in you both to will and to do for His good pleasure." (Phil 2:13).

"""But *how* can I protect my church?"""

Nehemiah 4:13–20 give us the blueprint. It not only covers what to do, but also embodies all the above lessons.

"I positioned men behind the lower parts of the wall, at the openings; and I set the people according to their families, with their swords, their spears, and their bows."

Nehemiah assessed his situation, found the weak points, and positioned armed men accordingly.

"And I looked, and arose and said to the nobles, to the leaders, and to the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awesome, and fight for your brethren, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your houses.”"

Notice the *order* in which Nehemiah gives his instruction.

First, "do not be afraid"—a common encouragement from God and His angels when speaking to us.

Second, he instructs his men to remember the Lord, who provides the real protection.

Third, he reminds his men what they fight for—not honor or pride or bloodlust, but for their families; for innocence.

"And it happened, when our enemies heard that it was known to us, and that God had brought their plot to nothing, that all of us returned to the wall, everyone to his work."

Those who want to harm Christians are cowards. They want a surprise attack, and become demoralized by a hard target. Nehemiah's men recognize the threat, but carry on.

"So it was, from that time on, that half of my servants worked at construction, while the other half held the spears, the shields, the bows, and wore armor; and the leaders were behind all the house of Judah. Those who built on the wall, and those who carried burdens, loaded themselves so that with one hand they worked at construction, and with the other held a weapon."

The workers and the protectors are one in the same. A church safety team is first and foremost a ministry. Our highest priority is to encourage others in the love of the Lord, and to offer protection as we do it.

"Every one of the builders had his sword girded at his side as he built. And the one who sounded the trumpet was beside me."

There's a clear leader and communication method.

"Then I said to the nobles, the rulers, and the rest of the people, “The work is great and extensive, and we are separated far from one another on the wall. Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, rally to us there."

"There is a response plan in case of attack."

Our God will fight for us.

Amen.

Putting the Nehemiah blueprint together:
1. Fear not. God is in control. Your enemies are cowards.
2. Remember who you are here to protect.
3. Know your weak spots, position the team accordingly.
4. Have a leader, a communication method, and response plans.
5. Above all, spread the love of God whenever you serve.

text:
Flowers are like the jewels of the earth, sparkling and dazzling in the bright sunshine, mimicking the colours of the heavenly home. Just as we plant a garden, so do we also lay stones as the foundations for a home. God also plants a garden and laid the foundations of the earth—a measuring rod of time as extensions into space. The earth as a place to dwell, and the garden as a place of growth, is like the temple and the sanctuary, the home for encountering heaven upon earth. As in nature, so too with us: like fractals repeating at different orders of magnitude, the body and soul are our dwelling place, the garden in our hearts.

We can use the example of a bud becoming a flower to show that the “distance” between them is what we call time—a measure of the difference between what was and what is—by using the same idea of a snapshot of “being” in the “now” and at different moments. This change over time is a transformation via energy/entropic pathways.

Regular actualisation of potentials occurs in a universe of constant motion and unfolding. By our beholding, this reality has become a normative expectation—yet the regularity itself is not created by our expectation; it rests on the stable whatness of the things involved. Thus we come to see that the world and all that lies beyond exists independently of the human mind, just as we expect the sun to rise each day.

The univocal part of “being” is its whatness; for example, an acorn is still oak, a sapling is still oak, and a tree is still oak—though none of these states of being are the same, they are held in the sameness of their identity as oak. Just as a human being’s identity is no less human depending upon its stage—only its actual being is different in each stage, therefore possessing being to a different degree and intensity.

Our personhood develops from the moment of conception, not just the unique DNA fingerprint formed, but at the gift of the soul. We are ensouled beings—body and soul are one, developing as one from the seed of our beginning implanted in the womb of our mother.

Because only mankind has consciousness, this means all else only by what belongs to nature in its being or sheer fact of existing is how the universal “whatever has breath” can praise (Psalm 150:6), or give glory to God. Therefore, as the term liturgy suggests a fitting response to the gift of being, with gratitude, this can only be beheld by mankind to God.

The interpretation of Genesis as simply liturgical offers a limited or narrow view of its meaning. Genesis teaches far more about the Creator and the relation of our being to Him than the right response to Him alone.

Liturgy is like the narrow path, or participation in the divine order, that allows humanity to recognise and respond to the God who created and loves us. Jesus says, “I AM the Way, the Truth, and the Life”; He is the path to the tree of Life and is the flaming sword of Truth—the Word of God made flesh, who lived and dwelt among us. In Christ, we have the right way to live, to breathe and move and have our being.

St. Irenaeus of Lyons said, “The glory of God is a living man”; that is the way humanity participates with the divine, listening and responding. This is to live as one who “walks with God,” existing in continuous communion with Him on the pilgrimage of our lives now and on into eternity.

text:
I pray there is a heaven for animals where they will always be safe and free. 🙏❤️✝️

In 1999, two elephants named Shirley and Jenny were reunited at The Elephant Sanctuary in Tennessee. This emotional reunion was significant as they had been companions in the circus 23 years prior.

This reunion not only marked a joyful moment for the elephants but also underscored the importance of companionship for elephants, especially those who have endured traumatic experiences in captivity.

After their reunion, The Elephant Sanctuary provided Shirley and Jenny with a loving environment where they could bond closely, resembling a mother-daughter relationship. The sanctuary offered individualized care, allowing them to live comfortably and independently in a natural habitat setting.

Circus elephants like Shirley and Jenny often suffer from chronic foot and joint disease, obesity, infertility, and severe psychological stress due to their confinement and the harsh conditions they endure. Many experience symptoms of depression and aggression, leading to a significantly shorter lifespan compared to their wild counterparts.

text:
Traces of Texas reader Natalie Morgan kindly shared this stupendous circa 1950 picture of Roy Orbison and the Wink Westerners. Besides Roy, the rest of the Westerners were Charles Evans on stand-up Bass, Billy Par Ellis on drums, Richard West on piano and James Morrow on electric mandolin. Shortly after this, in 1951,  Roy was 15 years old when he and the band began appearing on radio broadcasts from nearby Kermit, Texas. Mr. Lipscombe, who was the superintendent at Wink High School, was running for a position with the district Lions Club and offered the Westerners $200 to be the opening act when he was asked to speak --- a gig that led to Roy's trip to Chicago at the age of sixteen to appear at the National Lions Club Convention.  And the rest, as they say, is history. 

Thank you, Natalie! What an awesome shot!

text:
Kaito just showed its hand for InfoFi 2.0.  with Yu Hu front running the main announcement. 

The more interesting question from a creator point of view, isn’t what Kaito is building. It’s where you should position yourself based on your skills and size.

What Yu Hu is stating with? 

>Going big into AI, TradFi and crypto (last intentionaly).

My guess is that AI and StockFi will become priorities over the next six months, while crypto remains the focus now (low hanging fruit).

AI companies have much larger budgets than crypto ( we are still in a bear), while tech and finance have some of the highest CPMs out there. Bullish on the new Kaito positioning here from a business perspective.

However, crypto for now is the only proven industry this worked before. 70% AI and TradFI businesses targets by the beginning of 2027, are probably too ambitious and is all about the capacity to execute and market appetite. Similar to, “we are strong on X but we want to go on all other social platforms” ( it never really happened). Here is all about the team capabilities to execute vs just the wants. Reading more between the lines for now. 

Ok. What about the 4 solutions? Who are these for?

>Kaito Select - More for established creators. However, there will be “takeover campaigns” that could require loads of small and medium sized accounts, making this more inclusive. I see this more social vs anything else. Here I would pay attention to what type of projects will use this. 

>Kaito Invite

Pretty much exclusive. This will likely target the upper tier of creators and potentially offer more lucrative deals to attract top talent across AI, TradFi and crypto. Here will be interesting to see the budgets and if Kaito can bring similar type of deals the top creators get form marketing agencies. 

This could work in combination with Kaito Katalyst for projects and businesses that want access to the best possible creators.

We’ve seen something similar in the past, where a creator could have a paid deal while also participating in a leaderboard.

>Kaito Partner

Pretty much an affiliate marketing programme.

Here, having distribution channels like a Telegram GC will probably matter more. Simply pushing referral links on the timeline won’t move the needle much for most creators.

For Kaito, it’s good business because they can tap into new ways of bringing projects and businesses in as clients that need more bespoke solutions. See the Kalshi announcement.

>Kaito Katalyst

This is InfoFi 2.0 imo. For pre TGE projects, most will probably want low CPMs and social activity rather than retention, especially if the product is still in beta. Good chance for most people to complete on, tho let’s see how mindshare will be tracked and if leaderboards will be back. 

For post TGE projects, the focus will likely shift towards a combination of onchain and social activity. Here again, the onchain activity needs to be tracked and transparent. 

Overall this could be a great opportunity for small and medium sized creators, while most bigger size creators will not necessarily participate here, unless there is a conjunction with Select. 

Overall, plenty more opportunities for everyone. If you are planning to participate with Kaito, this time you should first try and understand how to position yourself vs just how many post and replies I can do in a day to climb a leaderboard. 

Now let’s see the execution @Punk9277

Gm Creators 🛠️

Rayls Enygma (by @RaylsLabs) is a privacy and security engine designed for blockchain networks. It allows banks and users to transfer assets, run smart contracts, and conduct financial activity with full data confidentiality, while keeping transactions mathematically verifiable on-chain and auditable for regulators.  

🔒 What is Rayls Enygma? 🏦

Imagine sending a locked box containing money to a bank. The bank teller can mathematically confirm you have enough funds and execute the transfer - without ever opening the box or seeing your private account balance.

Rayls Enygma  privacy-preserving framework designed to connect Traditional Finance (TradFi) with Decentralized Finance (DeFi) across EVM-compatible blockchains.  

Here is how the core tech works:

▪️ Zero-Knowledge Proofs: Advanced cryptography that proves a transaction is 100% valid without revealing who sent it, who received it, or the transfer amount.
▪️ Homomorphic Encryption: Computes encrypted data on-chain without needing to decrypt it first.
▪️ Programmable Auditability: Grants regulatory bodies "view keys" for selective disclosures so institutions maintain legal compliance without broadcasting private client data to the public.  

Privacy where you need it, compliance where required.

Rayls Enygma solves this exact trade-off. By pairing zero-knowledge proofs and homomorphic encryption with selective regulatory auditability, it offers the best of both worlds: strict enterprise privacy with verifiable on-chain transparency.

It gives banks and enterprise users the privacy required by law without sacrificing the trustless efficiency of decentralized finance.

Details:
Freezes all immigration to the U.S., except for temporary tourist visas, until the following conditions are codified into law:
  - Ending adjustment of status of the H-1B visa and scrapping the unconstitutional OPT program that displaces tech workers by allowing foreign graduates to work instead of returning home.

 - Birthright Citizenship: U.S. citizenship is bestowed upon minors only if one parent is a U.S. citizen or a green card holder, ending the practice of automatic citizenship.
 - Ending chain migration and the Diversity Visa Program, limiting entries to spouses and unmarried minor children, and ending the practice of admitting extended family members instead of nuclear family members or being picked based on mere luck.
 - Prohibiting the entry of Sharia Law adherents, Chinese Communist Party members, known or suspected terrorists, and members of Foreign Terrorist Organizations.
 - Baring noncitizens from accessing means-tested federal programs like SNAP, SSI, TANF, Medicaid, Medicare, WIC, federal student loans, and public housing.

Some of the bill details:
 - Replaces the H-1B visa lottery system with a wage-based selection process.
 - Requires employers to demonstrate good-faith efforts to hire American workers first.
 - Prevents companies that have recently conducted layoffs from hiring H-1B workers.
 - Ends the use of H-1B visas as a pathway to permanent residency.
 - Eliminates the Optional Practical Training (OPT) program to prioritize employment opportunities for American STEM professionals.
 - Builds on Rep. Eli Crane’s (R-AZ) End H-1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026, which proposes a three-year pause on H-1B visa issuances followed by comprehensive reforms designed to restore the program’s integrity and effectiveness.
--------------------

3⃣ H.R.8443 - End H–1B Visa Abuse Act of 2026:
Rep Eli Crane (R AZ-02) @RepEliCrane 
Bill Date: 4/22/2026
Press Release: https://t.co/7bBG7nvOIh
Bill Text: https://t.co/CVN2jtZ9uy
Bill Cosponsors: https://t.co/zNGVAdfUBv

Immigration Accountability Project's Summary Link: https://t.co/3BaG7wIUGe

Immigration Accountability Project's Summary:
  Sec. 1. Prohibits H-1B visas from being issued for a period of three years (this means the current crop of H-1Bs would rotate out of the country during the pause).

  Sec. 2. Reforms the existing H-1B program for when it comes back online by:
     - Requiring H-1B applicants to have a foreign residence to which they intend to return when their visa expires.
     - Reducing the cap on H-1B visas to 25,000 from 65,000, eliminating the existing exemptions to the cap, and limiting H-1B visas to a single term of three years (from the current double term of six years).
     - Codifying the Trump H-1B fee of $100,000 and extending it to all new H-1Bs and to those seeking permission to change employers (feel free to designate how this fee should be used).
     - Requiring employers seeking to import H-1Bs to attest that they are unable to find a qualified American worker, that bringing in an H-1B will not adversely affect American workers, that they have not laid off workers in the previous 12 months and will not lay any off in the following 12 months, and that they will pay the H-1B a minimum of $200,000 per year.
     - Requiring USCIS to distribute H-1B visas each year according to the highest wages offered by employers, rather than in a lottery system.
     - Barring H-1B workers from being employed by more than one employer at a time and barring third-party employers or staffing agencies (the so-called body shops) from employing H-1B workers.

  Sec. 3. Disallows H nonimmigrants (including H-1Bs, H-2A agricultural workers, and H-2B seasonal workers) from bringing their family members with them. (This would eliminate a lot of the costs generated by the spouses and children of the low-skilled workers, including education costs. It would also eliminate the problem of granting employment authorization to the spouses of H-1Bs, which takes more jobs from American workers.)

  Sec. 4. Prohibits the Federal Government from sponsoring or employing nonimmigrant workers.

  Sec. 5. Eliminates Optional Practical Training (OPT) in all its forms.

  Sec. 6. Makes nonimmigrant visas actually temporary by prohibiting nonimmigrant workers, including H-1Bs, from adjusting their status to lawful permanent residence. This means every nonimmigrant would have to return to their home country when the visa expires and apply for a green card from there.

  Sec. 7. Prohibits nonimmigrants from changing from one nonimmigrant status to another without leaving the United States first. This will prevent H-1B workers who lose their jobs from switching to student or tourist visas so they can remain in the United States while they try to find a new employer.

  Sec. 8. Establishes that all these changes are effective upon enactment.
--------------------

  Sec. 2. Suspending the Issuance of H-1B Visas Prohibits H-1B visas from being issued for a period of three years (this means the current crop of H-1Bs would rotate out of the country during the pause).

  Sec. 3. Restricting H Nonimmigrant Visas to Primary Workers (Note: This was Section 4 in the House version) Disallows H nonimmigrants (including H-1Bs, H-2A agricultural workers, and H-2B seasonal workers) from bringing their family members with them. (This would eliminate a lot of the costs generated by the spouses and children of the low-skilled workers, including education costs. It would also eliminate the problem of granting employment authorization to the spouses of H-1Bs, which takes more jobs from American workers.)

  Sec. 4. Necessary Reforms to H-1B Visa Requirements (Note: This was Section 3 in the House version) Reforms the existing H-1B program for when it comes back online by:
     - Requiring H-1B applicants to have a foreign residence to which they intend to return when their visa expires (ending dual intent).
     - Reducing the cap on H-1B visas to 25,000 from 65,000, eliminating the existing exemptions to the cap, and limiting H-1B visas to a single term of three years (from the current double term of six years).
     - Codifying the $100,000 fee (which Senator Sheehy's version renames to a "Tariff on the Importation of Labor" rather than the "Trump Fee") and extending it to all new H-1Bs and to those seeking permission to change employers (feel free to designate how this fee should be used).
     - Requiring employers seeking to import H-1Bs to attest that they are unable to find a qualified American worker, that bringing in an H-1B will not adversely affect American workers, that they have not laid off workers in the previous 12 months and will not lay any off in the following 12 months, and that they will pay the H-1B a minimum of $200,000 per year.
     - [New Sheehy Version Addition] Establishing strict mathematical definitions for an "H-1B-dependent employer" based on company size: companies with 25 or fewer employees are dependent if they have more than 7 H-1Bs; 26 to 50 employees require more than 12 H-1Bs; and 51 or more employees require H-1Bs to make up at least 15% of the workforce.
     - Requiring USCIS to distribute H-1B visas each year according to the highest wages offered by employers, rather than in a lottery system.
     - Barring H-1B workers from being employed by more than one employer at a time and barring third-party employers or staffing agencies (the so-called body shops) from employing H-1B workers.

  Sec. 5. Prohibiting Federal Employment of Nonimmigrant Visa Holders Prohibits the Federal Government from sponsoring or employing nonimmigrant workers.

  Sec. 6. Eliminating the Optional Practical Training Program Eliminates Optional Practical Training (OPT) in all its forms.

  Sec. 7. Prohibiting Adjustment of Status Makes nonimmigrant visas actually temporary by prohibiting nonimmigrant workers, including H-1Bs, from adjusting their status to lawful permanent residence. This means every nonimmigrant would have to return to their home country when the visa expires and apply for a green card from there.

  Sec. 8. Prohibiting Change of Status Prohibits nonimmigrants from changing from one nonimmigrant status to another. This will prevent H-1B workers who lose their jobs from switching to student or tourist visas so they can remain in the United States while they try to find a new employer.

  Sec. 9. Effective Date Establishes that all these changes are effective upon enactment.

Investing billions into Elon Musk’s SpaceX or contracting its Starlink network instead of backing Telesat was heavily debated, especially given that Starlink offered a proven, cheaper, and immediately available alternative. [1, 2]
However, the Canadian government bypassed a direct investment in SpaceX for several critical reasons: [1]

1. Digital Sovereignty and Geopolitical Volatility
•Musk's Erratic Behavior and Rhetoric: Tensions between Ottawa and Elon Musk spiked dramatically. Following bilateral trade friction and U.S. tariff threats, Musk sparked a national backlash by publicly stating "Canada is not a real country". [1]
•The Tariff Fallout: The political risk of relying on Musk became highly evident when Ontario Premier Doug Ford officially cancelled a $100-million provincial Starlink contract. The cancellation underscored the dangerous vulnerability of trusting critical infrastructure to an unpredictable foreign billionaire allied with protectionist U.S. leaders. [1, 2, 3]
•Foreign Legal Overreach: Leaving Canada’s sensitive military communications entirely on an American corporate network means Ottawa’s defense operations would remain structurally subservient to U.S. jurisdictional control and foreign regulatory compliance.

The Ultimate Irony: Canada is Still Paying SpaceX
Canada did not escape SpaceX's orbit entirely. While Canada refused to invest in SpaceX as an infrastructure provider, Telesat is still legally forced to buy its rocket services. Because SpaceX holds a near-monopoly on global orbital delivery, the Canadian satellites built in Montreal will ultimately be launched into space aboard SpaceX Falcon 9 rockets

text:
Smithsonian’s Leftist Director Declares History a ‘Prime Tool of Social Justice,’ Resurfaced Video Shows | David Lindfield, Slay News

A resurfaced presentation by the leftist director of the Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History is drawing fresh scrutiny after the museum recently defended its commitment to political neutrality before Congress.

Anthea Hartig testified during a series of congressional hearings last month examining allegations of ideological bias within the Smithsonian, insisting the institution operates according to principles of scholarship, independence, accuracy, and nonpartisanship.

But a February 2025 presentation to students at the University of California, Los Angeles paints a markedly different picture.

During the lecture, Hartig described “history as a practice” as “a prime tool of social justice” and outlined what she characterized as an “equity-based, justice-forward, community-driven and necessarily humble approach to public history.”

Congressional Testimony vs. Public Remarks

Appearing before lawmakers in July, Hartig emphasized that the museum does not advocate political positions.

“Our work is governed by the Smithsonian standards of scholarship, accuracy, independence and nonpartisanship,” she testified.

She added that “the museum does not take sides in America’s political debates,” explaining that its role is to preserve historical evidence so Americans can “draw their own conclusions.”

Yet in the UCLA presentation, Hartig offered a more activist vision of the museum’s mission.

“The United States’ long and violent racial history continues to be present in our reckoning,” she said.

She argued that true redress “should leverage responsibility,” involve “the act of correction,” and pursue “restorative justice through history.”

Later in the presentation, Hartig stated plainly that “history as a practice … is for me a prime tool of social justice.”

Museum Has ‘Moved Away’ from Earlier Vision

Hartig also contrasted the museum’s original mission with its current direction.

She described the museum’s 1964 opening during the Cold War as reflecting an attitude of, “We’re going to be the best and most technologically advanced country in the nation, and we’re going to show everyone how we did that.”

“We clearly have moved away from that,” she said.

Instead, Hartig promoted what she called the museum’s “bold new vision” of becoming “the most accessible, inclusive, relevant, and sustainable public history institution in the country.”

According to that vision, the museum aims to serve an audience reflecting “the full racial, class, gender, ethnic, and geographic demographics of the United States.”

Black Lives Matter Collection Highlighted

Hartig highlighted several initiatives that reflect the museum’s current priorities, including what she described as a Smithsonian-wide effort to collect artifacts documenting the Black Lives Matter movement.

She said the museum worked to “document and preserve and share objects focused on Black Lives Matter to show the history of the movement starting in 2012.”

Displaying photographs of protest signs outside the White House during the 2020 demonstrations, Hartig praised the exhibits as “phenomenal” and “incredibly poignant.”

The presentation itself opened with a land acknowledgment and included an image of an American flag bearing what appeared to be the words “Defund the Police,” which Hartig identified as being from a 2020 Black Lives Matter protest in Washington, D.C.

Another image showed a protest sign reading, “America – loving you is complicated.”

Praise for Anti-ICE Activists

Hartig also praised Tsuru for Solidarity, describing the anti-ICE activist organization as “a truly remarkable group.”

The organization identifies itself as a Japanese-American social justice movement seeking to end immigrant detention facilities and oppose what it describes as “racist, inhumane immigration policies.”

According to Hartig, the group collaborated with Black Lives Matter initiatives highlighted by the museum.

Push for ‘Language Justice’

Another initiative Hartig discussed was what she called a “proactive multilingual strategy to support language justice.”

She argued that everyone has the right to communicate in the language with which they are most comfortable.

Since 2019, she said, museum exhibitions, signage, and digital projects have been produced in at least English and Spanish, with additional languages incorporated depending on the community being represented.

‘We’re Under Attack’

Toward the end of the presentation, Hartig suggested the museum was facing criticism because of its approach to history.

“We’re under attack for speaking complicated truths,” she said, urging students to “raise your voices and speak them together.”

She concluded by describing historians as “tellers of stories and seekers of truths,” as well as “ambassadors of empathy and defenders of inalienable rights.”

The resurfaced remarks have renewed questions from critics about whether the Smithsonian’s leadership is advancing an ideological agenda despite assurances to Congress that the institution remains politically neutral.

text:
Only the strong survive.

Going into a new job with the attitude that you are going to hate your job is the loser’s mindset.

When I first moved out to California I lived with my mom and applied to lots of jobs but my first offer was for a minimum wage job labeling boxes and bottles and filling them with acids of various types for use making semi conductor chips in Sunnyvale. The job was four ten hour days per week, so I could still do job interviews on Fridays for a higher paying job.

But while I was working, I busted my ass and did the best job I could. I never missed a day of work, never was late and never exceeded the break times.

Having studied chemistry in college, I quickly realized some simple ways of increasing productivity without doing more work by suggesting methods that reduced cleaning tank and equipment between batches.

It wasn’t long until the increased productivity allowed the sales people to confidently increase sales of etchants and I was put in charge of the acid room and we were working seven days a week, ten hours a day to meet the demand, and with the California overtime laws, I was making good money.

It wasn’t too long before I was sent out to Connecticut to be operations manager for a new plant we were opening.

We’re in a golden age now, not the Great Depression.

text:
What began as an ordinary drive on a Utah highway quickly turned into a frightening experience when lightning struck Casey Pettus' truck. ⚡🚚 Although Casey escaped without injuries, his vehicle caught fire and was completely destroyed, leaving nothing but ashes on the roadside.

While he was grateful to be alive, losing a truck meant facing unexpected expenses, insurance claims, and the challenge of getting to work. Like many parents, Casey tried to stay strong for his family despite the stress.

Later that day, his 9-year-old son quietly approached him with a jar containing all of his savings. 💙 Without hesitation, he offered every dollar to help his father buy a new truck.

The child knew his savings wouldn't be enough to replace the vehicle, but that wasn't the point. He simply saw that his dad had a problem, knew money could help, and offered everything he had. It was an act of pure love, free from doubt or hesitation.

The touching gesture reminded everyone that kindness isn't measured by the size of the gift but by the heart behind it. ❤️

That day, Casey lost a truck to lightning, but he gained something far more valuable—a powerful reminder of unconditional love and generosity from his own son. Sometimes, the smallest hands carry the biggest hearts. 🫶⚡

With this entry from @TheCougChron co-founder @RealTStevenson, our America 250 Series has come to an end!

I want to take a moment to tell you a bit about this series and why it matters to me.

This was my first real project as Editor-in-Chief at The Cougar Chronicle, a role I started in mid-June.

On around June 23rd, I noticed that we didn't have an op-ed scheduled for the 4th of July. With it being the 250th anniversary, I sent a panicky message to the staff asking for someone to write something. Within 24 hours, I had 9 people volunteering.

I decided to full send it. I reached out to other colleagues and friends at TPUSA, College Republicans, BYU's Political Science department, and other organizations. I even sent out an email to state legislators who we had connections with. Before July even began, we had committed to an entire series. 

Our team kicked into high gear, which anyone knows is a feat for college students in mid-summer. Our editors got to work on drafts, our web designer built a section for it on our website, we designed new templates for social media, and we did all of this while juggling our pre-existing upload schedule.

By the end, we received 17 essays from 3 universities, 4 student organizations, both houses of the Utah State Legislature, representing writers of various ages and experience levels. 

Each of them turned out great. They look great, they feel professional, and they each offer something different. Soon, some of them will be appearing in our annual print edition!

And most of all, the content of these essays is some of the most uplifting, pro-America writing I've seen in a long time. Each one is a much needed whitepill that reminded me why I love this country and do what I do. If you haven't seen any of them yet, I'll link to our website page in the top comment. 

We did all of this with a small team of dedicated students, each of whom are either working, taking classes, or doing both. They truly are a fantastic group who love America and are eager to fight for her.

I have faith that the coming months will see The Cougar Chronicle shine at its brightest and produce the finest student journalism in the state. If you're not following, you should, because the best is yet to come!

If you're a student at any Utah or Church-owned university and you want to join the cause, DM me or comment below and we can get you involved!

If you'd like to support what we do, I'll also be dropping a link below where you can donate, which helps us do things like improve our website, launch our print-edition, create scholarship opportunities, and much more. 

So congrats to the @TheCougChron team for completing this Essay Series, and a huge thank you to all of the writers who contributed!

text:
He told his students to go to the windows.
Get out. Jump if you have to.
Then Liviu Librescu walked to the classroom door and pressed his body against it.
He was 76 years old. He weighed 140 lbs 
The gunman was in the hallway.
It was April 16, 2007. A Monday morning. Solid mechanics class at Virginia Tech, Room 204. Twenty-two students, most of them 19 or 20 years old.
At 9:45 AM, gunshots echoed through Norris Hall. Room by room, the shooter was working his way down the corridor.
Liviu heard it. He understood immediately.
He had survived the Holocaust. He had survived a labor camp. He had spent decades living under Communist oppression. He knew exactly what evil sounded like.
He told his students to escape through the windows. Second floor — it was a drop, but they'd survive. Then he walked to the door and held it shut with his body.
The shooter tried to force it open. It wouldn't move.
He fired through the door. Wood splintered. Bullets came through.
Liviu stayed.
Behind him, students were climbing out the windows. Dropping to the ground. Running. One by one, all twenty-two of them got out.
The shooter kept firing through the door.
Liviu held it shut until every student was safe.
Then the bullets killed him.
When police arrived, they found his body at the door.
All 22 of his students survived. Not one was injured.
Liviu Librescu was born on August 18, 1930, in Ploiești, Romania.
He was Jewish. In 1941, when he was eleven years old, Romanian authorities sent him and his family to a labor camp. His father died there. Liviu survived. When the war ended, he was fifteen.
He went back to school. Studied engineering. Earned a doctorate from the University of Bucharest.
But Communist Romania had no interest in allowing a Jewish intellectual to succeed. He was blocked from academic positions. Passed over for jobs he deserved. He applied to emigrate. The government kept refusing.
Finally, in 1978 when Liviu was 48 years old — Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin personally intervened. Romania let him go.
He had spent most of his adult life trapped in a country that didn't want him.
In Israel, he taught at Tel Aviv University. Published over 300 papers. Became an international expert in aeroelasticity — the science of how air flows over aircraft wings.
In 1985, Virginia Tech offered him a position. He moved to Blacksburg, Virginia. He taught there for 22 years. His students loved him — demanding but kind, high standards, genuine care.
He was still teaching full-time at 76. Still publishing research. Still showing up every Monday morning for solid mechanics.
April 16 was the first day of Passover — the Jewish holiday celebrating liberation from slavery and oppression.
Liviu Librescu died on the day his tradition sets aside to celebrate freedom.
He spent his entire life escaping death and oppression by luck, by persistence, by the intervention of others. And on his last morning, he chose to stand at a door so that twenty-two young people could have the future he had fought so hard to reach.
He could have run. He could have hidden. He could have climbed out a window with his students.
He chose to stay.
The Virginia Tech shooting killed 32 people that day — the deadliest school shooting in American history at the time.
Room 204 had zero casualties.
Because a 76-year-old Holocaust survivor held a door with his body until every student behind him was gone.
His funeral was held in Israel. Students from Virginia Tech flew across the ocean to honor him. The Israeli government awarded him the Star of David Medal posthumously. Virginia Tech named a scholarship in his memory.
His son said his father died the way he lived — protecting others.
A man who survived everything evil threw at him for 76 years.
On his last day, he made sure 22 kids survived too.
Professor Liviu Librescu. August 18, 1930 — April 16, 2007.
Holocaust survivor. Labor camp survivor.
302 published papers. 22 years at Virginia Tech.
22 students out the window.
He held the door.

My only duty was to care for the young master who had been bedridden for two long years.

I stood over his lifeless body. Beard grown wild. Skin pale. Completely forgotten by everyone in that house.

text:
Nepal’s Catastrophe and the Great Humanitarian Crisis

What struck Nepal on the 26th of August was seismic enough to shake the whole world. A torrent of water and mud swept across the Tibetan region and Nepal’s Rasuwa, along with other parts of the nation. The flood was caused by the collapse of a glacier and an ensuing ice-rock avalanche in the high Himalayas that triggered catastrophic flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border. The ice-rock avalanche struck the Lhende River valley, generating a seismic signal equivalent to an earthquake of magnitude 5.2.

The surge later fed the Bhote Kosi and then the Trishuli River, carrying the torrent towards the south of Nepal. The Trishuli River saw water levels rise by up to 9 metres in just 30 minutes during the flood. The Trishuli later joins the Narayani River, which enters India’s Bihar state, where it is called the Gandak River. Thousands have been evacuated and rescued in the Nepal-bordering states of India, and further concerns over rising water levels in the Gandak remain imminent. The flood also hit Indian workers engaged at the Trishuli-1 Hydroelectric Power Station in central Nepal, with 63 Indian workers from the project subsequently rescued, while hundreds of Indian nationals remained untraced across Nepal.

Countries and organizations across the world are assisting Nepal in overcoming this catastrophe. India has sent around 60 metric tonnes of Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) material, and the Indian Air Force is assisting the humanitarian effort on the ground. Organizations like the World Health Organization, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, and others are mobilizing funds and essential emergency supplies for Nepal. China has also mobilized its disaster management teams, with the matter receiving the personal attention of China’s top leadership. Chinese President Xi Jinping directed an all-out search-and-rescue effort, while Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited the flood-hit Gyirong area in Tibet, reflecting the severity of the incident on the Tibetan front.

As of 29 August, at least 669 people have been killed in Nepal and seven in Tibet, while nearly 3,000 people remain missing across Nepal and Tibet. The figures are expected to change as rescue teams continue to reach areas that remain cut off. According to Nepal’s Department of Tourism, 668 tourists from 34 countries were out of contact following the disaster.

Buddhist spiritual leader H.H. Dalai Lama said that he is praying for all those who have lost their lives and offered condolences to the bereaved and to all those affected by the tragedy. The danger is not over yet; warnings of further risk are threatening Nepal again, with authorities closely monitoring newly formed glacial lakes and the possibility of further flooding.

text:
Bangladesh and the Emerging “Mecca Pact”: A Strategic Opportunity Requiring Preparation

Speculation over Bangladesh’s possible association with the emerging “Mecca Pact” has generated strong reactions at home. Supporters view it as a potential strategic opening, while critics question its purpose, membership criteria, and geopolitical implications. Because the initiative is still developing and its formal conditions remain unclear, Bangladesh should avoid both premature enthusiasm and automatic rejection. The more important question is whether Dhaka can convert its geographic importance into durable strategic leverage.

Bangladesh occupies a sensitive position between South and Southeast Asia, facing persistent security pressures along both its eastern and western frontiers. The Rohingya crisis, instability inside Myanmar, cross-border incidents, and regional power competition all create long-term challenges. Relations with India are also complex, involving cooperation, asymmetry, border security concerns, water disputes, and competing political perceptions. These realities make national resilience—not rhetoric—the central requirement of foreign policy.

For Bangladesh, strategic relevance will depend heavily on state capacity. Military modernization should therefore focus on credible deterrence rather than prestige. A larger, better-trained force may be justified, but numerical expansion should be tied to doctrine, logistics, technology, command quality, and fiscal sustainability. Proposals for a half-million-strong army and doubling security services must therefore be evaluated against threat assessments, recruitment quality, recurrent expenditure, equipment availability, training capacity, and measurable operational requirements. Expansion should strengthen readiness and deterrence without creating an oversized payroll that crowds out essential development. Priority areas should include domestic UAV capability, precision weapons, missile research, naval modernization, air defense, secure military communications, cyber capability, and indigenous maintenance and production.

Intelligence reform is equally important. Modern security threats frequently operate below the threshold of conventional war through disinformation, covert influence, cyberattacks, economic pressure, political manipulation, and support for non-state actors. Bangladesh therefore needs stronger HUMINT, SIGINT, cyber intelligence, counter-intelligence, and inter-agency coordination, combined with legal oversight to prevent politicization and abuse.

Historical experience also suggests that frontier security and maritime power matter. Bengal’s past repeatedly demonstrated that weak defense invited external pressure, while stronger military organization improved territorial control and bargaining power. History should not be used mechanically, but it offers one durable lesson: sovereignty is more credible when supported by capable institutions.

Security expansion must, however, reinforce democracy rather than weaken it. Enlarging the police, BGB, Navy, Air Force, and Army may improve border management, public order, criminal investigation, and crisis response, but effectiveness depends on professionalism, accountability, training, and respect for law. A larger coercive apparatus without institutional reform could create new problems instead of solving old ones.

Financing modernization will require disciplined priorities. Bangladesh can review tax exemptions, inefficient subsidies, politically motivated projects, and poorly targeted spending, but defense expansion must remain compatible with education, healthcare, infrastructure, and economic growth.

Ultimately, Bangladesh should keep the door open to the Mecca Pact if participation serves national interests and if membership terms are acceptable. Even without immediate membership, a strong strategic relationship could be valuable. The broader lesson is clear: Bangladesh must upgrade education, defense, intelligence, technology, and governance so that geopolitical opportunity is matched by national capability.I can also make it more forceful and newspaper-op-ed style, while keeping the analytical structure and approximately the same length.

text:
LeBron James opened a public school in Akron in 2018.

They didn't take the best students. They went and found the WORST ones.

Two hundred and forty third and fourth graders who were significantly behind everybody else in the district. Kids in the bottom 25 percent of test scores in Akron Public Schools.

That was the entire admissions criteria. Be the kid nobody could reach.

Here's what those kids get.

Free tuition. Free uniforms. Free breakfast, lunch and snacks. Free transportation within two miles. A free bicycle and helmet.

A longer school day and a longer school year than any other school in the district.

Access to an on-site food pantry for their family.

And if they graduate high school, four years of college tuition is guaranteed. Originally at the University of Akron, and later Kent State came in and offered a second option, including a full year of room and board.

But here's the part that actually separates it from every other celebrity school.

The parents get help too.

Job placement services. GED classes. Adult education. The foundation treats the family as the unit that needs support, not just the child.

Because James understood something obvious that most school reform ignores. You cannot fix a nine year old's reading scores if his mother is about to lose the apartment.

He also built the I PROMISE Village, housing for students and families dealing with homelessness, domestic violence, or whatever else has gone wrong.

Now the honest part.

The school has not been a clean success. Test scores at IPS have been rough, and critics have pointed that out loudly. The school also receives regular public funding, and the district has been clear that taxpayers are part of the investment, not just LeBron.

Both of those things are true and worth saying.

But so is this. In its first year, 90 percent of those students met or exceeded their individual growth targets in reading and math, outpacing their peers across the district.

And the underlying program has grown enormously. The I PROMISE Network now supports more than 1,300 Akron students, all of whom have been guaranteed college scholarships if they hold up their end.

Which brings up the reason any of this exists.

LeBron James missed 83 days of school in fourth grade.

He was living with his mother, moving constantly, sometimes staying wherever they could. He has said plainly that he was one of those kids, the ones everyone gives up on.

A football coach's family took him in for a year and gave him a bed and a routine, and that's the year he started showing up.

He turned into the most famous athlete on the planet.

Then he went home and built a school for the version of himself that didn't get lucky.

LeBron James says Reebok offered him $10 million as a high school senior but his mom told him not to take the deal until he heard what the other companies had to offer even though they were broke.

“It’s me, my mom, and Maverick Carter at the end of the table. And he says, ‘If you don’t go talk to any other companies, this is yours.’”

“And I look at it… 10 million fucking dollars.”

“10 million!”

“I was a high school senior, man, that gave me a check for $10 million if I promise not to go see anybody else.”

“I told him I need a break. They stepped out. I need a fucking break. I can’t believe…”

“My mom looked at it, and me and my mom were living in an apartment and Section 8 housing in Akron.”

“And my mom looked at me, she said, ‘Son, trust your gut. If they’re offering you this, then who knows what the other companies may offer you.’”

“She’s like, ‘We ain’t got shit already, so it’s not like it changes our life at this moment.’”

“But I want you to trust your gut and do what you think is right.”

“So they came back in. Boom, I said, ‘Thank you. I would definitely like to continue our conversation, but I would be remiss if I did not take those other pitches from the other companies.’”

text:
Kendrick Lamar’s verse on Pusha T’s “Nosetalgia” (2013) remains one of his sharpest features‼️.

The title blends “nose” and “nostalgia”—looking back on the crack era through the sense most tied to memory‼️. Pusha raps as the young dealer. Kendrick answers as the Compton kid who lived the damage‼️.

Opening: Childhood Texture
 “You wanna see a dead body?  
 Instrumentals from my mama’s Christmas party  
Trouble’s on my mind  
 I still smell crime, my little brother cryin’”

He opens with the "Boyz n the Hood" line, then drops straight into sensory memory: Christmas music playing while crime and addiction hang in the air‼️. The Sega Genesis bars follow—

“Smokers repeatedly buying my Sega Genesis  
 Either that or my auntie was stealin’ it  
Hit the pipe and start feelin’ it…”‼️

showing how the habit reached into everyday objects‼️. Weed never hit like this; the high is different, heavier. “Quantum physics could never show you the world I was in” draws the line: this experience sits outside ordinary explanation‼️.

The Number Scheme⁉️
 “When I was ten, back when nine ounces had got you ten  
And nine times out of ten, niggas don’t pay attention  
 And when it’s tension in the air, nines come with extensions”‼️

Kendrick stacks 9s and 10s. The repeated figures add up to 87 (his birth year); 9 + 10 gives 19, completing 1987. He uses three 9s and six 10s, which quietly set up the later 36‼️. The measurements of the drug trade become the coordinates of his origin‼️.

Father and the Flip⁉️
 “My daddy turned a quarter-piece to a four and a half  
Took an L, started sellin’ soap fiends bubble bath  
Broke his nails misusin’ his pinky to treat his nose  
Shirt buttoned open, taco meat laying on his gold”‼️

His father cooked, then fell off and sold soap to fiends‼️. The physical details are unflinching. The child then offers to put him back on‼️:

“I said, ‘Daddy, one day, I’ma get you right with thirty-six zips  
 One thousand grams of cocaine…  
 Drop some ice cubes in it, Deebo on perimeter’”‼️

Thirty-six zips = a brick. “Ice cubes… Deebo on perimeter” works on multiple levels: the actual cooking process (ice to cool and form the hard edge), Ice Cube, and Deebo from "Friday"‼️. The father challenges him. Kendrick answers:

“Go figure, motherfucker, every verse is a brick  
Your son dope, nigga  
Now reap what you sowed, nigga”

Both verses on the song run 36 bars‼️. The track itself splits almost evenly in time. “Your son dope” means both excellence and the product itself‼️. The same material that wrecked the family is now his craft‼️. “Reap what you sowed” turns inheritance into something else‼️.

 “I was born in ’87, my granddaddy a legend  
 Now the same shit that y’all was smokin’ is my profession, let’s get it”

He names the year the numbers already encoded and completes the conversion: the dope they smoked is now his profession‼️.

The numerology, bar count, time split, sensory details, cooking references, and father-son dialogue all lock into one system‼️. He doesn’t just describe the environment that made him‼️he builds the verse so its form "is" that environment, then reclaims the central metaphor (the brick, the dope) as art‼️. That’s why the verse still holds up: technical precision and emotional weight in the same package‼️.

This is one of hip-hop best verse

text:
Akron (2015) is a sincere, understated indie romantic drama that offers a refreshing take on young love by treating a same-sex relationship as ordinary rather than fraught with external prejudice.

Directed by Brian O’Donnell and Sasha King, the film follows Benny (Matthew Frias) and Christopher (Edmund Donovan), University of Akron freshmen who meet during a casual football game and quickly fall for each other. 

Their romance unfolds with the full support of family and friends an uncommon and welcome choice that shifts the focus from coming-out struggles to the more universal challenges of intimacy and inherited pain. 

A long-buried family tragedy involving their mothers eventually surfaces, testing the couple’s bond and forcing difficult reckonings with grief, guilt, and forgiveness.

Frias and Donovan share genuine chemistry, making the early courtship scenes tender and believable. 

Supporting turns, especially from the mothers (Andréa Burns and Amy da Luz), add emotional weight without tipping into pure melodrama. The Midwestern setting feels lived-in and authentic, grounding the story in everyday realism.

At times the plot relies on convenient coincidences and the middle section loses some momentum as the past trauma dominates, leaving the resolution feeling slightly rushed. 

Still, the film’s gentle sincerity and refusal to sensationalize its characters’ sexuality remain its greatest strengths.

Clocking in at a lean 88 minutes, Akron is a modest, heartfelt effort that prioritizes emotional honesty over high drama. 

It’s a worthwhile watch for anyone seeking a quiet, hopeful story about love’s ability to confront and perhaps heal old wounds.

Experts and surveys note exactly this shift: 1950s middle-class life frequently meant a small house, limited or no college expectation, basic (or employer-tied) health coverage, and far less square footage and gadgetry. Measuring today’s costs against yesterday’s expectations produces an apples-to-oranges comparison. Lifestyle creep and status competition amplify the feeling that the old package is “not enough.”Media and GeographyCoverage disproportionately reflects high-cost, high-density metros where supply is inelastic, demand is strong (jobs, amenities, networks), and ratios are extreme. Those places dominate national conversation. In large parts of the interior and South, a more traditional version—owning a solid if unflashy home, raising a family, achieving reasonable stability—remains within reach of median earners on local incomes, especially with dual earners or moderate trade-offs on size/location.

Housing: The Core BenchmarkThe traditional post-WWII marker was a single-family home. National median home price relative to median household income was roughly 2.3× in 1970 (the modern low), hovered in the 2.7–3.5× range through much of the 1980s–1990s, and sits around 5.0–5.1× recently. Some measures put the current ratio near historic highs.housingalmanac.comThis is not uniform:Coastal and high-demand metros (San Jose, Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Honolulu, parts of the Northeast and West) often run 8–12×.

Many Midwest and Southern markets remain in the 2.5–4× range (e.g., places like Toledo, Akron, Pittsburgh, various Ohio/Indiana/Iowa cities). A substantial share of the country is still in territory closer to historical https://t.co/MSydlVaGdP

Homes themselves are not the same product. Average new single-family homes grew from roughly 1,200–1,500 sq ft in the 1950s–1970s to a peak near 2,400–2,500+ sq ft around 2015, and remain well above 2,000 sq ft today (even after recent modest shrinkage). They also typically include more bathrooms, central air, better insulation, appliances, and finishes that were uncommon or luxury items decades ago. Household size has fallen (from ~3.3–3.5 in the mid-20th century toward ~2.5–2.6), so living space per person has risen even more. 
Quality-adjusted indexes show real price increases, but raw medians overstate the pure “same house” cost rise because the average house https://t.co/Oy9k9TQDh3
Mortgage rates, land-use rules/zoning that constrain supply, construction costs, and investor activity all matter. The national ratio is elevated, but location choice still makes a large difference.
Broader Costs and the Expanded BundleOther pillars have also gotten more expensive relative to typical incomes:College tuition (especially the expectation that kids will attend) has risen far faster than general inflation or wages.

Healthcare costs and insurance burdens are higher.
New cars cost more in absolute terms (though they deliver far more safety, reliability, and features).

Lifetime-cost estimates of a full modern “American Dream” package (home, retirement nest egg, raising and educating two kids, periodic new cars, healthcare, vacations, etc.) often land in the multi-million-dollar lifetime range—well above what a single median earner typically accumulates. Dual-income households change the arithmetic, but so do higher baseline expectations. Some categories (many consumer goods, electronics, food share of budget in some periods) have become relatively cheaper. The squeeze is concentrated in housing, education, and healthcare—the items hardest to substitute or downsize without changing lifestyle goals.
Expectations Have Moved the Goalposts
The phrase “American Dream,” popularized by James Truslow Adams in 1931, originally emphasized opportunity, a better and fuller life according to ability, and a social order allowing people to reach their potential—not primarily motor cars and high wages. Post-WWII it solidified around homeownership, a stable job, and a modest suburban household. Today’s common version often includes a larger/better-appointed home, reliable cars with modern features, good healthcare, college for the children, retirement security beyond Social Security, and various lifestyle https://t.co/AI2QfN43Ct

#Baltoro_Glacier 63KM 
 
A Masterpiece of the Karakoram
Deep in the heart of the Karakoram lies the magnificent Baltoro Glacier one of Pakistan’s most spectacular natural treasures. It is far more than a vast river of ice it is a living part of the region’s mountain and water system.

Surrounded by some of the world’s highest peaks, including K2 Broad Peak and the Gasherbrum massif Baltoro offers landscapes that are almost beyond imagination. Towering granite walls snow covered summits, brilliant blue ice and streams of glacial meltwater create a scene that feels like nature’s own grand cathedral.

At Concordia where several great mountain valleys and glaciers meet the landscape becomes particularly breathtaking. The silence immense peaks and endless ice make you feel incredibly small in the presence of the Karakoram.

But Baltoro is not only about beauty.

Its meltwater feeds the Shigar River system which ultimately joins the
Indus River. More broadly glaciers and seasonal snowmelt across the Upper Indus Basin are a critical source of water for Pakistan.
Studies indicate that meltwater makes up a very substantial portion of Upper Indus flows. One assessment estimated that around 70% of annual flow upstream of Tarbela comes from meltwater approximately 26% from glacier melt and 44% from snowmelt.
This makes Baltoro more than a destination for trekkers and mountaineers. It is part of Pakistan’s natural water infrastructure a frozen reservoir feeding the river system that sustains millions of people.
Baltoro is not simply a glacier to admire. It is a reminder that the breathtaking beauty of the Karakoram is deeply connected to Pakistan’s water security and its climate future.
