text:
I have been telling people that beyond any reasonable doubt, Babu Owino will eventually return to ODM and take over the party. You can take this to the bank or under your mattress. 

It won't be easy, it will be like a coup. It will not happen today, but in fullness of time it will happen. 

Right now, ODM leadership lacks youthful aura apart from Joho. Kasamuel of these world is a political greenhorn and more of a chatterbox. 

Listen to Babu's speech in Homabay in the burial he attended few days ago.

 Standing before the people of Nyanza, Babu poured scorn on rumours that ODM might hand Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja its ticket for the 2027 gubernatorial race. 

He listed Sakaja’s political sins with the precision of a man who still feels the old party’s pulse. Support for Kibaki in 2007, Uhuru in 2013 and 2017, Ruto in 2022, never for Raila.

If Babu has truly turned his back on ODM, if Linda Mwananchi is now his political home and the Orange tree no longer offers him shade, why does the mere rumour of Sakaja’s embrace by the party stir him so deeply?

 A man who has washed his hands of a house does not keep checking whether strangers have been given the keys. The heart, it seems, still lives where the mouth claims it has left.

This is no ordinary restlessness. 

Babu has already mapped his own path with bold strokes. Nairobi’s governorship in 2027, one term only, then the long climb toward State House in 2032.

 Edwin Sifuna, his comrade in the Linda Mwananchi ranks, is widely expected to seek the presidency in 2027 itself.

 Should Sifuna succeed, 2032 becomes the year of his re-election bid, the very season Babu has marked for his own presidential charge. Even if Sifuna isn't elected, I believe he will still view come 2032.

Two ambitious men, once walking the same road, will find themselves competing for the same crown. Two bulls can't drink from the same hole. 

And that's where Babu Owino will return to ODM and stage a coup. His outburst over Sakaja is the first public sign that he still regards ODM’s tickets, its symbols, and its Nyanza heartland as matters too important to ignore.

Thus the logic of ambition closes in. 

To challenge Sifuna or to succeed him, Babu will need more than personal charisma and the energy of the streets. 

He will need a party with history, with branches, with the capacity to bargain and to command. 

And so, in the fullness of time, the prodigal is likely to return, not as a penitent son seeking forgiveness, but as a claimant determined to seize the house. 

 When the clash with Sifuna hardens and the 2032 presidential road demands a stronger vehicle, the path of least resistance, and greatest power, will lead him back to the Orange Democratic Movement. 

Not to ask politely for a seat at the table, but to take the table itself.

text:
I was in the USAF and assigned to the US Embassy in Bamako in 2016, Mali. A 90% Muslim country. It was a diplomatic assignment and my family was going with me. We were excited to represent the United States and unofficially the Church. The Church was not there and I was told there were no members living there. 

Two weeks before going there was a terror attack and I was notified that my family could not accompany me. They moved to Utah, I went to Mali for 2 years without them. 

It felt like my heart was RIPPED out but I knew I was supposed to go anyway so I did.

My son at BYU met a fellow student from Mali whose brother wanted to talk to me. He visited my house in Mali and he only wanted to talk about the Church. After our conversation he said he wanted to be baptized. I told him, the Church wasn't there - it would be years. He said there were people meeting at a chicken farm an hour south of the capital. I said, "no, the Area President would have told me". He insisted it was true so on that Sunday we went there and sure enough there were 30 people worshipping in a stinky chicken coop. It was led by a Returned missionary who had recently moved there and had misunderstood some guidance from the previous Area President but was acting in faith to do what he thought was right (hold Church meetings). He had a family committed to baptism and had arranged travel to Ghana (paid for by an American from Utah). I called the American and arranged for my friend to join them in Ghana. His impossible desire came true in days not years.

During my two years there I saw tender mercies and miracles that made it clear that the Lord is weaving His work throughout the world. I saw Muslim families who were more righteous than many Latter-day Saint families and I struggled with the "One True Church" concept myself. It was at that point that I read the Bible where Jesus says "I am the way, the truth and the life" and I suddenly realized that TRUTH is so much bigger than I have the capacity to comprehend. That the work is so much bigger  than my American and Utahn (Utah pioneer heritage for several generations) mindset can even pretend to understand. It was like my head exploded. 

I was living in one of the poorest countries on our planet, representing perhaps the most powerful military in the history of the world and suddenly I knew that I was NOTHING. I subsequently met a starving infant but was powerless to save her (I tried). I saw a young father of 7 thrown in jail for trespassing on a wealthy landowner's vacant lot. He was in jail for 7 months, caught some illness and died leaving behind a family who needed him. I was pissed and felt helpless at how big the world's problems really are.

For perhaps the first time in my life I understood why the world needs Zion. A place of peacemaking where there are no poor among us. This idea of Zion goes beyond what our culture and politics can offer and understand but the Lord is going to humble us until we do.

When I retired and returned to Utah, I was dismayed at how many people had intertwined their religion with Trumpian politics and worse, the poor behavior - it sickened me. 

My personal contrast between seeing the problems we need to solve and the pride we are displaying before what will surely be our destruction has taught me that 1) letting God prevail means letting Truth prevail in my personal life (no matter the source) and 2) self-annointed gatekeepers have no vote in my life - there is only one Gatekeeper, Jesus Christ (also named "Truth") who loves ALL and will accept anyone who wants to be a helper in building Zion.

You have previously shared tender mercies that have blessed me when I was struggling and I just wanted to share how I came to find some peace as I also wrestle with "the big questions".

text:
Harry and Meghan Didn’t Come Home. They Came Back for What They Could Still Get While Charles Is Still King.

Harry and Meghan did not return to Britain because the country suddenly became safe, kind, or worth belonging to. They came back because the version of themselves they built in California stopped working as well as they needed it to, and the family they spent six years tearing apart is still the only institution that can make them matter at the level they want.

That’s the part the sentimental coverage won’t say.

The speeches, interviews, book and documentaries were not just a cry for help. They were a strategy. Tear down the royals’ moral standing. Make Britain the villain. Sell leaving as an act of courage. Then make money from the fallout.

And it worked for a while. Deals get signed when the wound is fresh. It gets a lot harder when the story is old and people have already heard it over and over again.

So now they’re back, with the one reason nobody is supposed to question: the children.

School in the Cotswolds. Roots. Family. Grandfather. It’s the perfect shield. Two school-age children living in Britain changes the whole conversation around security, residency and whether they really “left” for good.

You don’t put your children into a country you spent years describing as racist and unsafe unless something has changed.

The calculation changed.

And living in Britain as private, non-working royals isn’t some great act of humility. It looks an awful lot like the arrangement they wanted back in 2020 and couldn’t get on their terms.

Keep the commercial freedom. Keep the titles. Live near the King. Use the charities, the royal connections, the surname and the calendar when it suits you. Stay close enough to the institution to benefit from the legitimacy it gives you, but far enough away that you don’t actually have to serve it.

Exile was the pressure tactic.

Return is the harvest.

And then there’s William.

Charles is the route in. William is the brick wall.

Harry and Meghan know William isn’t going to entertain them, and they know he will eventually be the one calling the shots. So while they can’t get what they want from William, they can still try to get whatever they can from Charles: access, goodwill, family occasions, royal connections, legitimacy, and whatever else comes with being close to the King and his grandchildren.

That’s why the grandchildren matter so much.

Charles can be softened by his grandchildren and a late phone call. William is a completely different problem.

A Sussex household back in Britain, in the same countryside, the same social circles and the same media storm as the future King isn’t exactly family healing. It’s a permanent complication sitting next to the heir.

And it puts William in an awkward position. If he draws a hard line, he looks cold and unforgiving. If he doesn’t, Harry and Meghan get back into the royal orbit without having to accept any of the responsibility that comes with it.

They don’t need William to welcome them back.

They just need Charles to give them enough access to keep the door open.

That isn’t reconciliation.

It’s leverage.

And let’s not pretend the British public are being offered an apology. They’re being offered royal drama again.

Outrage still gets attention. Security rows still get attention. Even speculation about which school gate they’ll be seen at gets attention.

They already proved they can live off the feud.

This isn’t reconciliation.

It’s occupancy.

They spent years setting fire to the house so they could negotiate their way back into a wing of it, with the children as the reason nobody is supposed to say what’s actually happening.

Call it what it is.

They didn’t come home.

They came to collect.

text:
The man who taught America's first paramedics how to work a street corner spent the next thirty years driving a yellow cab. George McCary helped build Freedom House Ambulance Service in Pittsburgh's Hill District, the first paramedic corps in the United States, and when the city replaced it in 1975 with a service staffed entirely by white medics, he did not go with it. So he told the story to strangers in his back seat instead, because nobody else was telling it.

On an afternoon in the fall of 1975, a Pittsburgh police officer stood in a street in Squirrel Hill and screamed into his radio.

A car had struck a pedestrian. The officer told dispatch what was in the road, and then he named the ambulance crew he wanted.

He asked for Freedom House.

Squirrel Hill was one of the wealthiest sections of Pittsburgh, and Freedom House Ambulance Service had never once been allowed to run a call there. The mayor had ruled that the police would cover those streets.

Another crew reached the man first, sent from somewhere else in the city. Seconds later the officer keyed his radio again and said the medics on scene were panicking and he needed somebody who actually knew what to do.

Nancy Caroline was sitting in the front seat of a worn out ambulance at the Freedom House station when it came over the air. She started the engine.

Freedom House had six weeks left.

Before any of this, if something happened to you in Pittsburgh, the police came. Two officers loaded you into the back of a wagon and both of them rode up front.

John Moon called that system "swoop and scoop." A canvas stretcher, a half empty oxygen tank, a pillow that could close off your airway, and nobody in the back with you.

A Pittsburgh filmmaker named Gene Starzenski watched it happen to his own grandfather in the early 1960s. The old man went down with his head bleeding badly, and the men who arrived had no equipment, so they asked the family for a towel, wrapped his head in it and drove off.

The towel was the good version. In the Hill District the wagon often did not come at all.

The Pittsburgh Courier kept printing the cases, the ones where help was late and the ones where help never arrived.

Phil Hallen, who ran the Maurice Falk Medical Fund and had once driven an ambulance himself, put it plainly years later. Nobody would go up to the Hill District, he said, and he named the cab drivers in the same breath as the ambulances.

The wagon was no better for the people it did come for. On the night of November 4, 1966, a man who had been mayor of Pittsburgh and governor of Pennsylvania collapsed on a stage at a campaign rally.

The police loaded David Lawrence into a wagon and drove ten minutes to Presbyterian University Hospital. A nurse who happened to be standing in the crowd climbed in and tried to keep him alive on the way.

The resuscitator in the wagon was broken. The vehicle rocked so hard that she kept losing her balance and had to stop compressions.

Dr. Peter Safar met that wagon at the door. Lawrence had suffered a massive heart attack, his brain had gone too long without oxygen, and he never regained consciousness.

Five months earlier, Safar's eleven year old daughter Elizabeth had an asthma attack and stopped breathing. She got no treatment on the way to the hospital, and by the time her father reached her he could restart her heart but could not bring her back.

Safar had spent his career proving that the minutes before the hospital were the minutes that decided everything. Now he had a governor and a daughter to prove it with, and he had heard there was a man at a local foundation already trying to build something.

Hallen wanted a real emergency service for the city, and he wanted it staffed by young Black men from the Hill District, the men the local press had taken to calling the unemployables.

Freedom House Enterprises did the recruiting. It was a Black run organization out of the Hill that registered voters, ran NAACP meetings and found people work, and it needed a set number of bodies in the room by the first day of class.

Some recruits knew what they had signed up for. Others were pulled off Centre Avenue hours before the course began, and once they understood what was on the table, most of them stayed.

Half of them had not finished high school. Some had felony records, and some had just come home from Vietnam.

Moon was still in high school then, four years away from getting in, and he has spent the rest of his life on the punchline. Society had them down as the least likely men in the city to succeed, and, as he puts it, "No one told us that."

Safar put the class through thirty two weeks. Anatomy, physiology, CPR, advanced first aid, nursing and defensive driving, with rotations through operating rooms, emergency rooms and the city morgue.

The men who had not graduated were walked through their GEDs at the same time. Inside the hospital, nurses kept mistaking them for orderlies and asking them to mop.

One of those rotations had them two hundred and forty miles from home, in Baltimore with Safar, when the news came on April 4, 1968 that Martin Luther King Jr. had been shot in Memphis.

The Hill District went up. Moon, still a senior at Fifth Avenue High School and not yet one of them, walked out of class with the rest of the Black students and ran the half mile to Centre and Crawford, where a bottle sailed past his shoulder and took out a plate glass window.

The Freedom House men in Baltimore came straight back. They had no ambulances of their own yet, so they rode with the police, the same police the Hill would not call, and worked the injured out of their own burning neighborhood.

There was less of the Hill left to burn than there had been. The city had razed thirteen hundred homes and businesses there in 1956 to build a civic arena with a parking lot, displacing eight thousand people.

Moon said the city let the rest of it go as long as the fires stayed penned in.

Three months after the fires, Freedom House took its first call in an ambulance of its own. It was July 15, 1968, and a woman was having a seizure on a city bus.

She lived.

She was the first of 5,868 runs that year, out of which the medics transported 4,627 patients and were credited with two hundred lives.

They reached most patients in under ten minutes, averaged fifteen calls a day and posted a dead on arrival rate of 1.9 percent.

The city's own safety director called the service excellent. The service still had to beg for money.

When a contact at the Ford Foundation admitted on the phone that he did not understand what Freedom House was, Hallen loaded some trainees into an ambulance, drove to Manhattan and parked outside the foundation's door on 43rd Street. People climbed in and looked around all day, the trainees taught CPR on the sidewalk, and the grant came through.

Nobody yet had a short way of saying what these men did. Mitchell Brown, an original medic and a former military corpsman who became operations director, spent the next fifty years reducing it to one sentence.

"Bring the care to the patient, not the patient to the care."

Moon was working as a hospital orderly when he first saw what that looked like. Two Black men in white tunics pushed a stretcher past him, and one of them flagged down a white doctor with a flick of the wrist, and the doctor followed.

Moon had never seen a Black man in that hospital give an instruction and have it obeyed. He went and asked how to join.

The operations manager told him there was no application. He would have to go take the course on his own time and come back.

So he did. When they finally handed him the white tunic, Moon said it felt like putting on a five hundred dollar suit.

Twelve hours later he was in the passenger seat beside George McCary, running on a man who had overdosed and stopped breathing on a sidewalk. McCary knew everyone in the crowd and went straight to work on them, joking, turning heads, clearing space.

Moon dropped to his knees alone beside the patient, tore open a ventilator with shaking hands and pushed in a breath. The chest rose.

By the time they reached the hospital the man was awake and laughing with McCary.

That kind of outcome traveled by word of mouth, and it traveled out of the Hill. A boy was hit by a bus in one of the wealthier parts of town, the police on the scene called Freedom House, and the medics splinted the leg and started an IV in the street.

Word got out that the crew from the Hill had saved him. People in the white neighborhoods started asking for a service like that of their own.

The demand reached a mayor who did not want to pay for any of it. Pete Flaherty took office in 1970 opposed to public private partnerships, cut the city's contribution to Freedom House in half, and in 1973 sent none of the money that was supposed to arrive monthly until November.

A Freedom House ambulance cost seven thousand dollars and a police wagon cost seventeen thousand. A Freedom House medic made one hundred fifty three dollars a week and the officer driving the wagon made two hundred thirty.

Then came the ordinance banning ambulance sirens downtown. The stated reason was that the noise bothered the business community, which meant traffic no longer parted for Freedom House while police cars, still permitted their sirens, got there first.

Freedom House asked to expand into the wealthier neighborhoods, where the bills might actually get paid. The mayor said the police already had those covered.

Some of the refusals came one patient at a time. Moon carried a monitor, oxygen and a jump kit up seven floors to a woman clutching her chest in a conference room, and the relief on her face at the sound of footsteps went out when she saw him.

She told him she did not want him touching her. Moon got down on one knee, kept his voice soft, and told her that she would die without care and that his crew was the only crew there.

She let him work.

Safar was running an entire anesthesiology department while all of this went on, and the medics had gone a long stretch with no close medical supervision. The service got a new medical director in the winter of 1974.

Nancy Caroline was thirty one, white, and handed a predominantly Black service whose medics could not see why she belonged. She rode with them, listened to every radio call, and pulled one case apart in front of everybody every single week until the reports got sharp.

She was in the station one lunchtime when a cardiac call came in, and the crew arrived to find a crowd, police and no patient. A cop pointed at an open manhole and said, smirking, that a job down there sounded about right for Freedom House.

Caroline turned to her medics. Walt Brown spread his arms wide and told her to go first.

They found the man ten yards down the sewer in full cardiac arrest, standing in ankle deep water. Caroline ventilated, Walt Brown ran compressions, and when Brown pressed the button on the defibrillator the man's body arced and settled and the monitor showed a rhythm.

The man would not fit up through the hole on a stretcher. So they carried him through the sewer for several blocks behind a city worker with a lamp, got lost, got soaked, and came up somewhere else in the sunlight with the patient breathing on his own.

McCary asked Caroline if she was hungry. He said he knew a place with the biggest fish sandwiches in Pittsburgh, and after a long silence she said she would eat one.

That spring Caroline pushed the men through more than two hundred additional hours. They practiced intubation on mannequins first, and then Moon was called into an operating room where Safar was waiting beside a sedated patient and a steel tray.

Safar gave him thirty seconds. Moon has said he was terrified, and that Safar's whole theory was that you learn a thing fastest with somebody's life on the clock.

Moon could not find the vocal cords. Sweat came up on his neck, and then he caught them, threaded the tube and stepped back.

It had taken him under twenty seconds. The official record would not catch up with that for another half a century.

On May 9 the whole service went on display. Outside the downtown Hilton, Freedom House staged a mass casualty drill in front of nearly a hundred of the best emergency physicians in the world.

Fourteen critically injured mock patients lay among wrecked cars while a doctor read out each injury over a loudspeaker and asked the crowd whether their own town could handle this. Sirens came around the corner.

In roughly twenty minutes the medics from the Hill triaged, treated and cleared every patient off the street.

Weeks later Freedom House won the federal grant to write the first national standards for paramedics in the United States.

The grant was processed through city hall. That summer Flaherty announced a citywide paramedic service that Freedom House was not part of, and every replacement medic the city hired was white.

Caroline was offered the job of running it. She wrote back that thirty people's livelihoods were on the line in the reshuffle and that those thirty outweighed any title Pittsburgh or the university could hand her.

She took the job on three conditions. Hire the Freedom House medics and dispatchers, keep the crews together, and hold a public ceremony saying out loud what Freedom House had done for the city.

Flaherty agreed to the first two. There would be no ceremony, no announcement and no public word of any kind.

What arrived instead was a private letter from city hall thanking the medics for their cooperation during a difficult period. It closed by declaring that the letter was itself the acknowledgment of everything Freedom House had done.

Everything those men had built, and a sentence in an envelope.

On the night of October 15, the crew room went quiet. The men stood around in their white jackets, Moon at the wall of glass watching their reflections, and manager Bob Zepfel picked up the phone and dialed the police dispatcher.

He gave his name and his title. He said it was 11:59 p.m., that this was the arrangement agreed with the City of Pittsburgh, and that "we are now going off the air."

Over eight years, more than fifty Freedom House paramedics and dispatchers had answered more than forty five thousand emergency calls. They had started on two second hand police wagons the city handed down to them and finished with five mobile intensive care units.

Twenty six Freedom House employees went to work for the city. Twelve months later fewer than half were still there.

Crews that had worked together for years were split up. Men with old records were fired, and new pass or fail examinations covered material Freedom House had never been taught.

Moon was not permitted to treat a patient without approval from the ranking person on scene, who almost always had less experience than he did. By the late 1990s the Pittsburgh EMS bureau was ninety eight percent white.

George McCary did not go to the city at all. The man who taught Moon how to work a crowd on his first night, the one Moon called the mayor of the Hill, spent the next three decades driving a yellow cab.

Hallen had named two vehicles that would not come up to the Hill District in 1966. Thirty years on, McCary was driving one of them.

Caroline was quietly pushed out of the city job in 1976. She wrote the first paramedic textbook in the world, then left Pittsburgh for Israel, where she became the first medical director of Magen David Adom and founded that country's paramedic training program.

She taught Israel's first paramedic class in 1979, later ran flying doctor missions across East Africa, and died at fifty eight in a hospice she had founded herself. Safar, who had designed the whole thing, was nominated for the Nobel Prize three times and died the year after her.

Moon stayed thirty four years. He built Pittsburgh EMS's first diversity recruitment program, tore out the rule requiring candidates to have a sponsor, and got recruits paid while they trained so that broke kids could afford to try.

He said he had to sharpen himself constantly to avoid being cut, and put the reason plainly: "We weren't wanted there."

In 2007 he sued the city, saying he had been passed over for deputy chief and that promotions ran on race. On December 21, 2009, Pittsburgh city council gave preliminary approval to a forty thousand dollar settlement under which he agreed to retire.

The city's equal opportunity office held an event honoring him that same evening. He used it to say that Pittsburgh EMS still "fails to acknowledge its foundation."

It was the same word city hall had put in the envelope in 1975.

Pittsburgh's first public acknowledgment came in 2014, a plaque on the 2000 block of Centre Avenue, on the stone face of a building that now holds the Hill District Federal Credit Union.

A woman named Sue Schilling read about it. In 1969 a car had hit her as she crossed the boulevard that separated her white neighborhood from the Hill, and the crew that came for her was Freedom House.

She sat down and wrote them a letter of thanks. Forty five years after they picked her up, and thirty nine after the city decided a letter would do.

She said the men never got the credit they were owed, because of the times they did it in.

One of the two letters was written to close a file. The other was written by somebody who was still alive to write it.

On February 20, 2026, Congresswoman Summer Lee stood at the Thelma Lovette YMCA, a few streets from that plaque, and introduced a bill to award Freedom House the Congressional Gold Medal.

The findings written into it record Moon as the "first non-physician to perform endotracheal intubation in the field," fifty one years after the twenty seconds in that operating room. The bill honors the members as a group and does not list them, so the names come from elsewhere.

Kevin Hazzard printed the roll in his book. Michael Blackman, Harold Brown, Mitchell Brown, Walter Brown, David Clemens, Arthur Davis, Ray Davis, Clyde Dunson, John Franklin, Harvey Gandy.

Tom Grace, Harold Holland, Addie Johnson, Eugene Key, James Kyte, George McCary, Thomas Mitchell, John Moon, Daniel Nickens, William Porter. Raymond Pridgen, Ron Ragin, David Rayzer, Curtis Scott, Ernest Simpson, Carl Staten, Wallace Sullivan, David Thomas, Thomas Wade, Kenneth Williams.

Congress found in writing that Addie Johnson and Pearl Porter were the first women to finish the training, which is worth knowing every time somebody tells you this was twenty five men and nothing else.

The bill is still in the first stage of the process. Fifty one years have passed, and the ceremony they asked for in 1975 has still not been held.

Those names are the errand. Pick two, keep them, and use them the next time somebody tells you paramedics started in California.

Moon has spent a decade saying it in schools, in union halls, at Stanford and at Brown: "It began right here in the Hill District with a group of Black men."

McCary said his version from behind the wheel, to strangers who got in with no idea who was driving them. He would tell them there is no way for them to meet the first doctor who ever lived, and no way to meet the first police officer.

Then he would look in the mirror. "But you can say you met one of the first American, worldwide, EMT paramedics."

I put a lot of effort into researching and sharing stories that matter. If you'd like to support the work, here's the link:
https://t.co/AeER0VXcAK
Every coffee helps me keep creating.

text:
Australians who have driven in the US—and Americans who drive there regularly—what advice would you give a first-time visitor?

I recently made a post asking about the United States, and I’ve been genuinely amazed by the number of people who have reached out to share their thoughts, experiences and wisdom. Thank you to everyone who took the time to respond. Your answers have made me even more interested in visiting, and I’ll be working extra hard to hopefully make the trip happen within the next year or two.

My biggest concern is driving. I live in Sydney, where public transport is average but manageable, and I’ve only ever driven in Australia. I’ve never driven on the opposite side of the road or in another country.

To Australians who have driven in the US: how difficult was the adjustment? What were the biggest differences or challenges, and how long did it take before you felt comfortable?

To my American friends who drive regularly: what advice would you give an outsider or tourist driving in the United States for the first time? Are there any road rules, highway customs, safety issues or common mistakes that visitors should know about?

I’ll predominantly be visiting Utah and Idaho, with perhaps a brief stay in California because that is most likely where I’ll be landing. From what I understand, having a car will be almost essential once I’m outside the major cities.

Admittedly, much of what I know comes from sensationalised media reports and YouTube crash compilations, which probably don’t provide a fair or balanced picture of everyday driving in America!

Once again, I’m deeply grateful to everyone who has reached out and generously shared their thoughts and wisdom. I would really appreciate any practical advice you can offer a first-time Australian driver in the United States.

text:
Terence Atmane vs Jaume Munar — the left arm against the grinder

Court 13 gets an all-European first round with a genuine surface question attached: Jaume Munar, ranked 55th and one of the more relentless retrievers on tour, against Terence Atmane, the 24-year-old French left-hander ranked 92nd whose best week anywhere came on American hard courts. The two have never played.

The matchup

No head-to-head, no shared history — the ATP record between them is blank at every level. That puts the weight on profiles, and the profiles diverge sharply.

Munar is 29, 6ft 0in, right-handed, and has built a career out of court coverage and depth rather than weapons: 132 tour-level wins, no titles, and prize money of $7,644,662 accumulated largely by making opponents play an extra ball. Atmane is 6ft 4in and left-handed, a combination that produces awkward serve angles on the deuce court and a forehand that comes across the court at a shape most players see rarely.

The relevant precedent is Cincinnati last year, where Atmane reached the semi-finals of a Masters 1000 on this exact surface before losing to Jannik Sinner 7-6(4) 6-2. That was not a fluke run built on retirements; it was a week in which the serve landed and the forehand held up against high-quality opposition. He has not repeated it, but the ceiling is on record.

Form & hard courts

Neither man has had a comfortable season at tour level. Atmane is 16-20, Munar 11-14 — five more tour-level wins for the lower-ranked man, and eleven more matches played. Munar's ranking advantage rests on a body of work that leans heavily on clay, where his defensive game is worth most and where the extra half-second on every ball lets him turn defence into attack.

New York offers him neither the bounce nor the time. Hard courts reward the player who can end points, and Munar's problem in this match-up is that he has to hit a great many balls to win one point while Atmane can win one with a serve.

The deciding factor

Consistency of the French serve, and nothing much else. Atmane's losses tend to come when he sprays and hands back the free points his height should guarantee; his wins come when the first-serve percentage holds and Munar is left returning from well behind the baseline with no way in. Over best-of-five that swing is wide in both directions, which is why this reads as a close match rather than an obvious one.

Munar's route is the familiar one: extend rallies, take pace off, make a streaky opponent play four hours and see whether the level survives. It is a real plan and it has beaten better players than Atmane. On this surface, though, it asks him to do the harder job of the two.

The call

A coin-toss with a lean. Terence Atmane to win, low-medium confidence.

The Cincinnati and Hamilton County Library

Considered "the finest library built in the country", it was built in 1853 according to the plans of architect J.W. MacLaughlin. Its architecture did not fail to impress its contemporaries.  
 
"The first thought that comes to mind as you enter the hall is how many books the five-tiered shelves can hold; your eyes are then drawn to and gratified by the neat architecture," wrote Harpers Weekly.

The first library in the United States to open on Sundays, it offered daily services from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. - and became very well known as a result. According to William F. Poole, director from 1869 to 1873, the Sunday service was so successful that "every seat was occupied from afternoon to evening".

text:
Rocky Mountaineer GoldLeaf Service: Canada’s Premier Luxury Rail Experience
For many travelers, the Rocky Mountaineer GoldLeaf Service is considered one of the world's great rail journeys. Rather than simply transporting passengers between destinations, the train is designed as a luxury sightseeing experience through some of Canada's most spectacular mountain landscapes.
History of Rocky Mountaineer
Rocky Mountaineer began operating in 1990 as a privately owned luxury tourist railway focused on showcasing the Canadian Rockies. Since its inaugural journey, it has become one of Canada's most celebrated travel experiences, carrying visitors through British Columbia and Alberta while emphasizing daylight travel so passengers never miss the scenery.
Unlike traditional overnight trains, Rocky Mountaineer operates exclusively during daylight hours. Guests spend evenings in hotels at destinations along the route, ensuring that every mile of mountain, canyon, glacier, river, and forest can be viewed during the day.
Where the Train Travels
Rocky Mountaineer's Canadian routes pass through two of Canada's most beautiful provinces:
British Columbia
Vancouver
Fraser Valley
Fraser Canyon
Kamloops
Whistler (on selected routes)
Quesnel
Coastal rainforests
Thompson and Cariboo regions
Alberta
Banff
Lake Louise
Jasper
Canadian Rockies National Parks
Major Canadian routes include:
First Passage to the West
Vancouver → Kamloops → Banff/Lake Louise
Highlights:
Fraser Canyon
Spiral Tunnels
Glacier National Park
Castle Mountain
Banff National Park
Journey Through the Clouds
Vancouver → Kamloops → Jasper
Highlights:
Pyramid Falls
Albreda Glacier
Mount Robson (the highest peak in the Canadian Rockies)
Rainforest to Gold Rush
Vancouver → Whistler → Quesnel → Jasper
Highlights:
Pacific coastal rainforest
Gold Rush country
Cariboo Plateau
Northern Rockies
GoldLeaf Service: The Highest Level of Luxury
GoldLeaf is Rocky Mountaineer's premium class and is widely regarded as the finest way to experience the Canadian Rockies by rail.
Glass-Dome Coaches
The signature feature is the bi-level glass-dome railcar.
Upper level:
Oversized reclining seats
Panoramic windows extending into the roof
Unobstructed mountain views
Attentive onboard hosts
Lower level:
Dedicated dining room
Full-service meal experience
Guests also enjoy access to a private outdoor viewing platform for photography and wildlife viewing.
Fine Dining and Cuisine
GoldLeaf dining rivals many luxury hotels.
Meals are freshly prepared onboard by Executive Chefs using regional Canadian ingredients such as:
Alberta beef
Pacific salmon and tuna
Fresh local produce
Okanagan fruits
Canadian maple products
Sample menu selections include:
Eggs Benedict
Smoked Salmon Avocado Toast
AAA Alberta Striploin Steak
Fraser Valley Chicken Paillard
Seared B.C. Albacore Tuna
Handmade Gnocchi
Gourmet desserts and wine pairings
Meals are served on china in a dedicated dining room with full table service. Complimentary alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages are included throughout the journey.
Service and Amenities
GoldLeaf guests receive:
Award-winning hosts
Complimentary beverages
Storytelling and regional interpretation
Wildlife spotting assistance
Spacious seating
Personalized service
The atmosphere is elegant without being formal. Most passengers describe it as comparable to a five-star resort experience on rails.
Accommodations
Because the train does not operate overnight, accommodations are included in most vacation packages.
Common premium hotel partners include:
Fairmont Jasper Park Lodge
Fairmont Chateau Lake Louise
Banff Springs Hotel
Luxury properties in Vancouver and Banff
Guests enjoy the comfort of a hotel each evening before continuing by train the next morning.
The Grandeur of Canada's Landscapes
The true star of the journey is the scenery.
Passengers travel through:
Snow-capped peaks
Glacier-fed rivers
Emerald forests
Deep river canyons
Rugged mountain passes
Waterfalls
Turquoise lakes
Vast wilderness inhabited by bears, elk, bighorn sheep, and eagles
Particularly memorable sights include:
Mount Robson
Stoney Creek Bridge
Spiral Tunnels
Fraser Canyon
Glacier National Park
Banff National Park
Jasper National Park
The changing views outside the dome windows often feel cinematic, with dramatic landscapes unfolding continuously throughout the day.
Approximate Costs for a Couple
Pricing varies by season, route, and package length.
GoldLeaf Rail-Only Journeys (2026 Starting Rates)
Route Per Person CoupleFirst Passage to the West CAD $3,200-$4,200 CAD $6,400-$8,400
Journey Through the Clouds CAD $3,200-$4,100 CAD $6,400-$8,200
Rainforest to Gold Rush (3-day) From about CAD $4,500 About CAD $9,000+
Popular Vacation Packages
Package Approximate Cost Per PersonVancouver & Banff Extended Getaway (6 days) From US$3,490
Jasper & Banff Extended Getaway (8 days) From US$4,340
Circle the Rockies (9 days) From US$6,240
For a couple, these packages generally range from roughly:
US$7,000 to US$13,000+, depending on itinerary and season.
Best Time to Travel
June through September
The most popular period.
Advantages:
Warmest weather
Long daylight hours
Excellent wildlife viewing
Peak mountain scenery
May and Early June
Ideal for:
Fewer crowds
Lower prices
Snow-capped mountain views
September
Often considered the sweet spot.
Advantages:
Fall colors begin appearing
Crisp weather
Excellent photography
Slightly fewer tourists
October
Best for value-conscious travelers.
Advantages:
Lower fares
Autumn colors
Less crowded trains
How Far in Advance to Book
For GoldLeaf Service:
12 to 18 months ahead for peak summer departures (June-September).
6 to 12 months ahead for shoulder season travel (May or October).
Luxury packages and preferred hotel combinations can sell out well before departure.
Because GoldLeaf has fewer seats than SilverLeaf and remains the most sought-after class, early booking is strongly recommended. This is particularly true for couples seeking specific travel dates or premium hotel upgrades.
Bottom Line
The Rocky Mountaineer GoldLeaf Service combines five-star hospitality, gourmet cuisine, luxury hotel accommodations, and some of the most awe-inspiring scenery in North America. For many travelers, the First Passage to the West route between Vancouver and Banff is the signature experience, while Journey Through the Clouds offers unparalleled views of Mount Robson and Jasper. Though costly, it is widely regarded as a once-in-a-lifetime Canadian travel experience.

text:
Why Somaliland is so important?👇

Somaliland has emerged as a beacon of stability and democratic governance in the Horn of Africa. 

Its strategic geographical location along the Gulf of Aden, near the Red Sea, with approximately 850 kilometers of coastline, together with the deep-water Berbera Port, provides a strategically important maritime position suitable for commercial port development and potentially for military and logistical facilities. 

Somaliland’s proximity to the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, extensive marine and coastal resources, potentially significant mineral resources, political stability and democratic governance, and maritime security capabilities are making Somaliland increasingly important to global and middle powers. 

These strategic realities provide a strong foundation for deeper economic, diplomatic, and defense cooperation.
Somaliland’s formal recognition by Israel in late December 2025 marked a significant development on the global stage. 

However, Somaliland continues to seek broader international recognition, particularly from Western powers led by the United States. For the United States, Somaliland could offer a strategically located partner for strengthening maritime security, protecting international shipping, and responding to growing geopolitical competition in the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. 

For Somaliland, closer strategic cooperation with the United States could create opportunities to strengthen its security capabilities, attract investment, expand diplomatic engagement, and advance its long-term objective of broader international recognition. 

The strategic choice for Somaliland is therefore not simply to seek recognition, but to transform its geopolitical advantages into sustainable strategic partnerships

text:
When Stephen Carr's Footballing World Fell Apart

Back in 2001, Stephen Carr was not only one of the best full-backs in the Premier League, but one of the hottest properties in European football.

At 25, the Dubliner was flying high at Tottenham Hotspur. After a bit of a dispute, he signed a lucrative deal at the club where he was voted fans’ player of the season.

Although that didn’t stop Barcelona sniffing around. The club had been on a charm offensive for himself and Spurs captain Sol Campbell, so they flew the pair out at great expense to watch the Catalan giants clinch a Champions League with a dramatic 3-2 win over Valencia,

That was June 2001, the one with Rivaldo’s bicycle kick.

Carr began suffering persistent groin strains and early wear-and-tear in his knee joint while playing for Spurs in January of that year, something that would persist until August.

Things got even worse when severe inflammation in his knee joint forced him to rest completely ahead of the 2001/02 season. He attempted a comeback and a return to training in early 2002 but suffered a serious setback/relapse. He would miss the entire 2001-02 season.

After visiting specialists in Colorado in April of 2002, it was confirmed he needed further recovery time, forcing him to miss the 2002 FIFA World Cup with the Boys in Green, too.

Carr wouldn’t get back to full fitness until October 2002 and would subsequently be sold to Newcastle United for a fee of just £2m in 2004.

After such a long time out of football, he never quite hit the heights of a few years before. He struggled with injury at Newcastle and would eventually retire from football in the Summer of 2008 at the age of just 32.

Incredibly, just a few months later (February 2009) he was training at Birmingham, who were in the Championship and was eventually offered an initial one-month contract. He kept impressing, so he kept receiving multiple short-term deals. He won promotion to the Premier League that season and won the League Cup in 2011, despite being relegated that season.

He would eventually retire in 2013 for good, having missed the prior season due to injury.

Stephen Carr has had a career many would love to have, and his short second half was quite remarkable. But I can’t help but feel a tinge of sadness. He really could have gone all the way; his knee just wouldn’t let him.

David

text:
COMMENTARY

PROP 132 DOESN’T SOLVE COLORADO’S FENTANYL CRISIS. IT JUST PUTS MORE PEOPLE IN PRISON.

Colorado absolutely has a fentanyl problem.

People are dying. Families are losing loved ones. Communities are dealing with addiction, overdoses and an increasingly dangerous illicit drug supply.

But Proposition 132 appears to offer Colorado the oldest political response in the book: increase criminal penalties, send more people to prison and call it a solution.

That is a crock of shit.

According to materials distributed by the Colorado Criminal Justice Reform Coalition, Proposition 132 would make possession of any amount of fentanyl a felony, including first-time cases and cases in which a person allegedly did not know fentanyl was present.

The coalition says the proposal would also impose an eight-to-32-year mandatory prison sentence for selling or sharing any amount of fentanyl, potentially including a single pill.

According to CCJRC, that punishment could apply even on a first offense, even when no money changed hands and even when the person did not know fentanyl was present.

Those are extraordinary penalties.

And here is the part that should concern anyone who actually wants to reduce overdose deaths:

According to CCJRC, Proposition 132 provides no new money for treatment or harm reduction.

None.

You cannot incarcerate your way out of addiction.

Someone struggling with substance use does not suddenly stop having a substance-use disorder because lawmakers changed the classification of an offense. A longer prison sentence does not make the illicit drug supply safer. It does not put naloxone into more hands. It does not create treatment beds. It does not provide long-term recovery services.

And it certainly does not bring anyone who died from an overdose back to life.

CCJRC says a Colorado-specific scientific analysis projected that the measure could increase overdose deaths by 41 percent, amounting to more than 1,700 additional deaths over five years. The coalition argues that fear of prosecution can make people more reluctant to call 911 when someone is overdosing.

Those projections are CCJRC’s and should be examined alongside the underlying research, but the concern itself deserves serious attention.

When fentanyl is involved, minutes matter.

Public policy that makes someone hesitate before calling 911 can have deadly consequences.

Then there is the cost.

CCJRC estimates Proposition 132 would send nearly 900 additional people to prison every year and cost more than $433 million during its first five years.

Again, those are the coalition’s projections.

But even setting those numbers aside, incarcerating substantially more people for substantially longer periods obviously carries a cost.

Imagine what hundreds of millions of dollars could accomplish if Colorado invested it directly in prevention, detoxification, evidence-based treatment, recovery programs, mental-health care, housing assistance and harm reduction.

Those interventions actually address why people use drugs and how people stay alive long enough to recover.

Prison is not drug treatment.

CCJRC says more than 100 organizations and faith communities have joined its “Get the Facts on Prop 132, the Fentanyl Measure” campaign opposing the proposal.

The organization also identifies Advance Colorado as the political organization behind the measure.

Colorado voters should absolutely demand action on fentanyl.

They should demand aggressive action against people knowingly trafficking dangerous drugs for profit. They should demand accountability. They should demand resources for families and communities devastated by addiction.

But “do something” cannot mean “do anything.”

A policy should be judged by whether it actually saves lives and makes communities safer, not by how severe its prison sentences sound in a campaign advertisement.

If Colorado is going to spend hundreds of millions of dollars responding to fentanyl, those dollars should be spent on policies demonstrated to prevent deaths and help people escape addiction.

Locking more people away for longer while failing to expand treatment is not a comprehensive fentanyl strategy.

It is punishment masquerading as one.

And Colorado can do better.

At least four people have climbed up the exterior of the museum’s new $45 million building, according to police reports and other accounts.

The Aspen Police Department this week pressed charges against two people for trespassing after they climbed up the outside of the building.

“Our number one concern is always the health and safety of the folks who live here, work here and choose to recreate here,” Aspen Police spokesperson Blair Weyer says. “Climbing up high on any building poses some serious dangers.”

A museum security guard discovered Lauren Ashley Twohig, 20, and Cooper Donald Means, 22, climbing the four-level museum while a third person attempted to photograph the act on Sunday around 6:30 p.m.

According to the Aspen Daily News:

All three were issued trespassing citations, but the next day, police dropped the charge against the photographer because he never admitted to climbing the outside of the museum. Twohig appeared in Aspen Municipal Court on Wednesday and received a six-month deferred judgment. Means is due in court next week.

Weyer says Aspen Police also received a report on August 2 of someone climbing and possibly falling from the museum's facade, but officers were unable to locate a suspect.

The museum has received mixed reviews. Artist and State Senate candidate Lee Mulcahy is one of the vocal critics. Mulcahy -- who is presently banned from the museum -- offered to pay $100 to the first person to climb the museum, a reward he says he’s already paid to a French citizen.

“I know we have a lot of mountain climbers in our communities,” Mulcahy says. “And if a French girl can get up there, I think Colorado residents owe it to themselves to stand up for liberty.”

Mulcahy says he is now offering a $500 reward to the next full-time area resident who climbs to the top of the museum, photographs the act, and posts it on Twitter.

Weyer says the Aspen Police Department was aware of the possibility of climbers and will continue to respond to calls from the museum and its security staff.

“Officers were ready to be on the lookout,” Weyer says. “We’re not sitting outside the doors waiting for it to happen, but we are responding to any calls from the art museum and its security staff, who are paying pretty close attention to this issue.”

The Aspen Art Museum did not return phone calls requesting comment.

text:
Selections of Pope Innocent III’s writings on the Jews:

Constitution for the Jews (1199 AD)
Although in many ways the disbelief of the Jews must be reproved, since nevertheless through them our own faith is truly proved, they must not be oppressed grievously by the faithful as the prophet says: “Do not slay them, lest these be forgetful of Thy Law,” [Ps. 58 (59):12] as if he were saying more openly: “Do not wipe out the Jews completely, lest perhaps Christians might be able to forget Thy Law, which the former, although not understanding it, present in their books to those who do understand it.”

Just as, therefore there ought not to be license for the Jews to presume to go beyond what is permitted them by law in their Synagogues, so in those which have been conceded to them, they ought to suffer no prejudice. These men, therefore, since they wish rather to go on in their own hardness than to know the revelations of the prophets and the mysteries of the Law, and to come to a knowledge of the Christian faith, still, since they beseech the help of Our defense, We, out of the meekness proper to Christian piety, and keeping in the footprints of Our predecessors of happy memory, the Roman Pontiffs Calixtus, Eugene, Alexander, Clement, and Celestine, admit their petition, and We grant them the buckler of Our protection.

For we make the law that no Christian compel them, unwilling or refusing, by violence to come to baptism. But if any one of them should spontaneously,a nd for the sake of faith, fly to the Christians, once his choice has become evident, let him be made a Christian without any calumny. Indeed, he is not considered to possess the true faith of the Christianity who is recognized to have come to Christian baptism, not spontaneously, but unwillingly.

Too, no Christian ought to presume, apart from the juridicial sentence of the territorial power, wickedly to injure their persons, or with violence to take away their property, or to change the good customs which they have had until now in whatever region they inhabit.

Besides, in the celebration of their own festivals, no one ought to disturb them in any way, with clubs or stones, nor ought any one try to require from them or to extort from them services they do not owe, except for those they have been accustomed from times past to perform.

In addition to these, We decree, blocking the wickedness and avarice of evil men, that no one ought to dare to mutilate or diminish a Jewish cemetery, nor, in order to get money, to exhume bodies once they have been buried.

If anyone, however shall attempt, the tenor of this decree once known, to go against it – may this be far from happening! – let him be punished by the vengeance of excommunication, unless he correct his presumption by making equivalent satisfaction.

We desire, however, that only those be fortified by the guard of this protection who shall have presumed no plotting for the subversion of the Christian faith.

Given at the Lateran, by the hand of Raynaldus, Archbishop of Acerenza, acting for the Chancellor, on the 17th day before the Kalends of October, in the second indiction, and the 1199th year of the Incarnation of the Lord, and in the second year of the pontificate of the Lord Pope, Innocent III.

Source. Internet Medieval Sourcebook – D. Andrew Byler. Innocent III, Constitution for the Jews. Migne, PL 215. 1855.

Etsi Non Displiceat (1205 AD)
Even if it may not displease the Lord, but rather be acceptable to Him that the dispersion of the Jews lives and serves under Catholic kings and Christian princes, whose remnants will finally be saved when in those days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell securely, nevertheless they greatly offend the eyes of divine majesty, who prefer the sons of the crucifiers, against whom the blood still cries in the Father’s ears, to the co-heirs of the crucified Christ, and as if the son of the handmaid could and should be heir with the son of the free woman, they place Jewish servitude before the freedom of those whom the Son has freed.

Indeed, you should know that it has come to our attention that in the Kingdom of France the Jews have become so insolent that, under the appearance of usurious wickedness, through which they extort not only usury but usury upon usury, they usurp the goods of churches and possessions of Christians, and thus what the prophet laments in the person of the Jews seems fulfilled among the Christian people: “Our inheritance,” he says, “has been turned over to strangers, our houses to foreigners” (Lamentations 5).

Moreover, although it was established in the Lateran Council that Jews should not be permitted to have Christian servants in their houses, neither under the pretext of raising children, nor for service, nor for any other cause, and that those who presume to live with them should be excommunicated, they themselves do not hesitate to have Christian servants and nurses, with whom they sometimes commit abominations which it is more appropriate for you to punish than for us to explain.

Furthermore, although the same council has decided that the testimony of Christians against Jews in common causes should be admitted, since they also use Jewish witnesses against Christians, and has decreed that whoever would prefer Jews to Christians in this matter should be anathematized, they are shown such deference in the Kingdom of France that Christian witnesses are not believed against them, but they are admitted to testify against Christians.

But if sometimes those to whom they lend their money under usury produce Christian witnesses regarding a payment made, more credence is given to the document which the debtor had carelessly left with them through negligence or carelessness, than to the witnesses introduced; indeed, witnesses are not even received in this matter against them. They have even become so insolent—which we relate with embarrassment—that in Sens, near a certain old church, they have built a new Synagogue, considerably higher than the church, in which, not as formerly before they had been expelled from the kingdom, with a lowered voice, but with a great clamor, celebrating their services according to the Jewish rite, they do not hesitate to impede the celebration of divine services in that church.

Moreover, blaspheming the name of the Lord, they publicly insult Christians that they believe in a certain rustic hanged by the Jewish people, whom indeed we do not doubt was hanged for us, since he bore our sins in his body upon the tree, but we do not confess him to be rustic in manners or lineage; indeed, even they cannot deny that he descended according to the flesh from a priestly and royal line, and his manners were distinguished and honorable.

Also on the day of preparation (Good Friday), Jews, contrary to the old custom, publicly running through the streets and squares, mocking Christians gathering from all sides according to custom to adore the crucified one on the cross, and by their reproaches they try to recall them from the duty of adoration. The doors of the Jews also remain open to thieves until midnight, and if anything stolen is found among them, no one can obtain justice from them.

Therefore, the Jews abuse the royal patience, and, while remaining among Christians, they take advantage of their hosts and secretly kill Christians when they have the opportunity, as is said to have happened recently, when a certain poor scholar was found dead in their latrine.

Therefore, lest the name of the Lord be blasphemed through them, and lest the liberty of Christians be worse than the servitude of Jews, we admonish your royal serenity and exhort you in the Lord, and enjoin you for the remission of sins, that you should restrain the Jews from such presumptions, and endeavor to abolish such abuses from the Kingdom of France, that you may be seen to have zeal for God according to knowledge, and since even secular laws punish more severely those who blaspheme the name of the Lord, so punish such blasphemers that the punishment of some may be the fear of all, and that the ease of pardon may not provide an incentive for wrongdoing.

Furthermore, rise up powerfully to eliminate heretics from the Kingdom of France, and let not the royal highness permit wolves hiding under sheep’s clothing to destroy the sheep to remain hidden in his land, but demonstrate in their persecution the fervor with which he pursues the Christian faith.

Given at Rome, at Saint Peter’s, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of February, in the seventh year.

Source. Patrologia Latina –  Innocent III, Etsi Non Displiceat. Migne, PL 215. 1855.

Etsi Judaeos (1205 AD)
As for those Jews, whom their own guilt has subjected to perpetual servitude since they crucified the Lord, whom your prophets had predicted would come in the flesh for the redemption of Israel (471), Christian piety accepts and sustains their cohabitation. Meanwhile, because of their perfidy, the Saracens who persecute the Catholic faith and do not believe in the one crucified by them cannot sustain themselves, but rather have been expelled from their territories. Yet they cry out more vehemently against us because we tolerate among us those who truly confess our Redeemer condemned by them to the torture of the cross. Nevertheless, they ought not to be ungrateful to us, repaying Christians with insult for grace and with contempt for familiarity. Having been mercifully admitted into our familiarity, they repay us in the way that, according to the common proverb, the mouse in the pouch, the serpent in the lap, and the fire in the bosom are accustomed to reward their hosts.

We have learned that the Jews, whom the grace of princes has admitted to their lands, have become so insolent that they commit excesses against the Christian faith that are not only unspeakable but even wicked to contemplate. For when Christian women serve as nurses for their children (479), on the day of the Lord’s Resurrection, when they receive the body and blood of Jesus Christ, for three days before they nurse them, the Jews make them pour their milk into a latrine. Furthermore, they commit other detestable and unheard-of acts against the Catholic faith, because of which the faithful should fear incurring divine indignation, since they allow them to perpetrate with impunity things that bring confusion to our faith.

Therefore, we have asked our most beloved son in Christ, Philip, the illustrious King of France (473), and we have also commanded the noble men… the Duke of Burgundy and the Count of Troyes, to repress the excesses of the Jews in such a way that they may not presume to raise the neck submitted to the yoke of perpetual servitude against the reverence of the Christian faith. We strictly forbid (474) that henceforth they have Christian nurses or servants (475), lest the children of the free woman serve the children of the slave, but as servants rejected by the Lord, against whose death they wickedly conspired, let them at least through their actions recognize themselves as servants of those whom Christ’s death made free and them servants. For since they have already begun to gnaw like a mouse and to sting like a serpent, it is to be feared that the fire received in one’s bosom may consume those who harbor it.

Therefore, we command your fraternity by apostolic writings, ordering that you diligently admonish and effectively induce the aforementioned king and others on our behalf, so that the perfidious Jews may in no way become insolent, but under servile fear may always display the shame of their guilt and revere the honor of the Christian faith. If, however, the Jews do not dismiss Christian nurses and servants, you, supported by our authority, under penalty of excommunication, strictly forbid all Christians from daring to engage in any commerce with them.]

Given on the Ides of July.

Source. Patrologia Latina – Innocent III, Etsi Judaeos. Migne, PL 215. 1855.

Letter to Master Peter, Presbyter of Santa Columba (1205 AD)
Latin Text
Non decet eos, quos unda baptismatis regeneravit in Christo et adoptavit in filios veræ lucis, ut cohabitent illis, quos duritia cordis ab aguilione [veri luminis extracavit, ne in eorum obfen ebretur…] pias adimplere morientium voluntates. Nulli ergo, etc. Si quis autem, etc.

Datum Romae, apud Sanctum Petrum, IX Kalendas Februarii, anno septimo.

English Translation
It is not fitting that those whom the waters of baptism have regenerated in Christ and adopted as sons of true light should cohabit with those whom hardness of heart [has removed from the stimulus of true light…] to piously fulfill the wills of the dying. Let no one therefore, etc. But if anyone, etc.

Given at Rome, at St. Peter’s, on the 9th day before the Kalends of February, in the seventh year.

Source. Patrologia Latina – Innocent III, Letter to Master Peter. Migne, PL 215, col. 507. 1855.

Letter to the King of Castile (1205 AD)
Latin Text (excerpts)
Non minus pro illorum peccato qui faciunt, quam pro eorum qui sustinent detrimento, dolemus et graviter conturbamur, quod regia celsitudo illis se gravem exhibet et severam, quibus benigna et propitia deberet adesse, illosque molestat, quos praecipue fovere deberet. Accepimus autem, quod, cum universos clericos regni tui ab omni exactione absolveris et collecta, mutata tandem post tempora voluntate, ipsis, pro velle tuo, collectas et exactiones imponis, cum, servi Judaeorum empti sive vendicti convertuntur ad fidem, licet pretium quod pro talibus dari debet, in canone sit taxatum, per Judaeos ipsos tantum facis de bonis episcopalibus detineri, quantum ipsi eosdem servos valuisse firmaverint juramento.

Unde, nuper a venerabili fratre nostro…. Burgensi episcopo, pro quadam Sarracena, Judaei cujusdam ancilla, quam vix asserit decem solidos valuisse, ducentos aureos recipi mandavisti, et, licet, super eo quod Judaeos et Sarracenos tui regni compelli ad solvendas decimas de possessionibus non permittis, litteras tibi apostolicas duxerimus transmittendas, tu tamen, nequidem eos noluisti ad decimarum solutionem inducere, verum etiam liberiorem eis decimas non solvendi et etiam ampliores possessiones licentiam tribuisti, ut, Synagoga crescente, decrescat ecclesia, et libere praeponatur ancilla…

Ne igitur, charissime in Christo fili, ecclesiasticam libertatem deprimere, et Synagogam, ac Moschiam extollere videaris, neque in Ecclesiam, sponsam Christi, aut ministros ipsius exerceas quae tuae fidei puritatem offuscent, serenitatem regiam monemus in Domino et hortamur, quatenus praedicta omnia et in te corrigas perfecte, et in aliis corrigi concessa tibi facias potestate.

English Translation
We grieve and are gravely disturbed no less for the sin of those who commit these things than for the harm of those who suffer them, that your royal highness shows itself harsh and severe to those to whom it ought to be kind and favorable, and harasses those whom it especially ought to cherish. Moreover, we have learned that, although you absolved all the clergy of your kingdom from every exaction and collection, having changed your will after a time, you impose collections and exactions upon them according to your pleasure; and when servants of Jews, whether bought or sold, are converted to the faith, although the price which ought to be paid for such persons is fixed by canon law, through the Jews themselves you cause to be withheld from episcopal goods as much as these same Jews affirm under oath that those servants were worth.

Wherefore, recently from our venerable brother… the Bishop of Burgos, for a certain Saracen woman, the handmaid of a certain Jew, whom he asserts was scarcely worth ten solidi, you commanded two hundred gold pieces to be received; and, although concerning the fact that you do not permit the Jews and Saracens of your kingdom to be compelled to pay tithes on their possessions, we have deemed it necessary to send you apostolic letters, nevertheless you not only refused to induce them to payment of tithes, but indeed you granted them freer license not to pay tithes and even to acquire larger possessions, so that, with the Synagogue increasing, the Church decreases, and the handmaid is freely preferred…

Therefore, lest you, most beloved son in Christ, should appear to oppress ecclesiastical liberty and to exalt the Synagogue and the Mosque, and lest you practice against the Church, the bride of Christ, or her ministers, things which obscure the purity of your faith, we admonish and exhort your royal serenity in the Lord that you perfectly correct all these things in yourself, and cause them to be corrected in others by the authority granted to you.

Source. Patrologia Latina – Innocent III, Letter to the King of Castile. Migne, PL 215, col. 616. 1855.

Letter to the Clergy of Barcelona (1208 AD)
Latin Text (excerpts)
Orta tempestate in hoc mari magno et spatioso, et in ea genere periclitante humano, verus Jonas, Dei Filius, Jesus Christus, in altitudinem ejus veniens, se permisit ab ipsa tempestate demergi, ut nos Deo reconciliaret in suo sanguine, ac in suam imaginem transformaret, innovaretque per lavacrum regenerationis ejusdem sanguine consecratum, non excludens conditionem vel sexum, sed, sine personarum acceptione, illud commune instituit sacramentum, per quod in adoptione filiorum Dei ex omni genere poterit assumi…

Sane, ad nostram noveritis audientiam pervenisse, quod, cum generale baptismum in ecclesia vestra celebratur, quamplures Saraceni, concurrentes ad ipsum, cum instantia postulant baptizari, quorum domini, tam Judaei quam et Christiani, timentes amittere commodum temporale, eos prohibere praesumunt, ab Ecclesia pretium requirentes pro illis quos regenerat Domino per baptismum, et pignora violenter pro ipsis per violentiam auferentes, inferendo alias gravamina nihilominus et jacturas.

Cum igitur Ecclesia quoslibet venientes ad agnitionem fidei, relictae vetustatis errore, recipere debeat et pulsantibus gremium aperire, et auster prohibere non debeat baptizari filios aquilonis, universitati vestrae per apostolica scripta praecipiendo mandamus, quatenus nemini petenti sacramentum fidei denegetis, sed tam Judaeos quam Saracenos, illud humiliter postulantes, in nomine Patris, et Filii, et Spiritus sancti, ad Redemptoris gloriam baptizetis, Christianos, qui praesumpserint impedire, vel ab Ecclesia exigere praemium pro renatis, ab hujusmodi praesumptione cessare, monitione praemissa, per censuram ecclesiasticam, appellatione postposita, compellentes.

Judaeis autem, nisi per charissimum in Christo filium nostrum… Aragonum regem illustrem, ab hac nequitia fuerint revocati, Christianorum commercia per districtionem ecclesiasticam, appellatione postposita, subtrahatis.

Datum Ferentini, VII Kalendas Septembris, anno nono.

English Translation
When a tempest arose upon this great and spacious sea, and in it the human race was in peril, the true Jonas, the Son of God, Jesus Christ, coming into its depths, permitted himself to be submerged by that very tempest, that he might reconcile us to God in his blood, and might transform us into his own image and renew us through the washing of regeneration consecrated by that same blood, excluding neither condition nor sex, but without respect of persons he instituted that common sacrament by which from every race people might be adopted as sons of God…

Indeed, you should know that it has come to our attention that, when general baptism is celebrated in your church, very many Saracens, flocking to it, urgently seek to be baptized, whose masters, both Jews and Christians, fearing to lose temporal profit, presume to prohibit them, demanding a price from the Church for those whom the Lord regenerates through baptism, and violently seizing pledges for them, besides inflicting other burdens and losses.

Since therefore the Church ought to receive all who come to the knowledge of the faith, abandoning the error of antiquity, and to open her bosom to those who knock, and the south wind ought not to prohibit the baptism of the sons of the north, we command your community by apostolic writings that you deny the sacrament of faith to no one seeking it, but baptize both Jews and Saracens who humbly request it, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit, to the glory of the Redeemer, compelling by ecclesiastical censure, with appeal set aside, those Christians who presume to hinder this or to demand payment from the Church for the reborn, to cease from such presumption, warning having been given beforehand.

But from the Jews, unless through our most beloved son in Christ… the illustrious King of Aragon, they shall have been recalled from this wickedness, you shall withdraw Christian commerce through ecclesiastical stricture, with appeal set aside.

Given at Ferentino, on the 7th day before the Kalends of September, in the ninth year.

Source. Patrologia Latina – Innocent III, Letter to the Clergy of Barcelona. Migne, PL 215, col. 977. 1855.

Letter to King Philip of France (1208 AD)
Latin Text
Ut contra crudelissimos hostes suos Ecclesia sancta Dei, [etc., ut in alia] usque: Quapropter serenitatem regiam rogandam duximus et monendam, in remissionem sibi peccaminum injungentes, quatenus cum a praedictis legatis fueris requisitus, consilium eis ad hoc et auxilium opportunum impendas, populos tibi subditos inducendo ut ad opus tam sanctum tam per se quam per sua obsequium Deo devotum et subsidium Ecclesiae necessarium exhibere procurent, scientes remissionem peccaminum [etc., usque] obtulerint vero Deo.

Quia igitur apud eos districtio forte poterit proficere temporalis a quibus super hoc spiritualis inductio non admittitur, tuam regalem mansuetudinem in Domino deprecamur quatenus Judaeos sub tuo dominio constitutos inducas regiaque potestate compellas ut debitoribus suis in hujusmodi Dei obsequium profecturis omnino relaxent usuras, et terminos ad exsolvendum sortem praefixos, si fieri potest, prorogent competenter; ut praeter subventiones alias quas Ecclesiae in tam sancto negotio ministraveris, ex hoc quoque merces tibi aeterna retributionis accrescat.

Datum Ferentini, VII Idus Octobris, pontificatus nostri anno undecimo.

English Translation
That the holy Church of God may prevail against her most cruel enemies, [etc., as in another letter] up to: Wherefore we have deemed it necessary to ask and admonish your royal serenity, enjoining upon you for the remission of your sins, that when you shall have been requested by the aforesaid legates, you should give them counsel and opportune assistance for this purpose, inducing the peoples subject to you that they may endeavor to render both personally and through their possessions devout service to God and necessary aid to the Church for so holy a work, knowing the remission of sins [etc., up to] they shall have offered to the true God.

Since therefore temporal stricture may perhaps avail with those from whom spiritual inducement on this matter is not admitted, we beseech your royal gentleness in the Lord that you induce the Jews established under your dominion and compel them by royal power that they entirely remit usuries to their debtors who are setting out in this service of God, and, if it can be done, suitably extend the terms fixed for paying back the principal; so that besides the other aids which you shall have ministered to the Church in so holy a business, from this also may eternal reward of recompense increase for you.

Given at Ferentino, on the 7th day before the Ides of October, in the eleventh year of our pontificate.

Source. Patrologia Latina –  Innocent III, Letter to King Philip of France. Migne, PL 215, col. 1340. 1855.

text:
Butter was peasant food in this country for centuries, and the people who sneered at it were eating worse.

A cottager's wife sits with the churn between her knees and works it until the milk turns from slop to grain to gold, with a boy hanging about waiting on the buttermilk. That block is the family's entire ration of fat for the week. It goes on the bread, into the pot, over the greens, onto anything that will hold still.

It is what gets everybody to Friday.

Up at the hall they would not touch it. The gentry ate flesh and had olive oil shipped in, largely to prove that they could. Dairy went into the accounts as white meats, the food of people with mud on them.

The Greeks used butter-eater as an insult. The Romans put it on wounds rather than bread. And the Church banned it through Lent on the grounds that fat was a hot food and hot foods led men toward vice, which is the one claim in this story anybody ever proved.

Northern Europe could not do Lent without butter, so Rome sold dispensations, and enough people bought their way back to it that the cathedral at Rouen put up a tower on the proceeds. It is still there. Locals have called it the butter tower for five hundred years. A sin taxed hard enough to be quarried into stone, and the sin was fat on bread.

Then the sneer collapses, for the oldest reason there is. The food is better, and everyone in the kitchen already knew.

Butter creeps into the cookery books through the 1500s. By 1600 it is standing in the kitchen of every great house in England, having come up from the yard by the servants' entrance.

By the Georgian period the pretending is over. A Swedish botanist touring England in 1748 finds bread and butter in every house he enters, eaten by everyone, at all hours, and writes it down as a national curiosity. In Nottingham a few years later a local man notes that even a washerwoman expects hot buttered bread with her tea, as a right rather than a kindness.

Butter on the table of the labourer and the duke alike. Pound cake, named for the pound of it that went in. The continental joke was that England had sixty religions and one sauce, and the sauce was melted butter.

Centuries of being told it was beneath them, and the cottagers were right the whole way through.

The demolition was quicker. A prize offered in France, a chemist obliging in 1869, a tub with a heart on the lid, and an American committee in 1977 that turned a food into a moral position.

Centuries up. Thirty back down, on a pamphlet.

And they are at it again this month, explaining that butter is basically a flavouring and that better sources exist. Vitamin A was found in butterfat because rats fed olive oil went blind and rats fed butter did not. The thing they keep calling empty is the standard every other fat was tested against.

A Greek insult, a Lenten fine, a French laboratory, a committee. It came back every time.

Cut it thick. The woman with the churn is watching.
