text:
Lisa McVey (born March 1967) is a retired American Hillsborough County School Resource Deputy, published author and motivational speaker from Tampa, Florida. At age seventeen, she was abducted by Bobby Joe Long, a serial killer and rapist who sexually assaulted and murdered at least ten women in the Tampa Bay area in 1984. 

McVey was Long's last victim, and the information she provided to police both led to his capture and inspired her 30 year career in law enforcement.

McVey has candidly recounted her experience as a victim of abuse, even before her abduction. She had been forced by her mother to move in with and take care of her grandmother at age fourteen. Previously, she had been in and out of foster care. "I was being sexually abused at home. 

My grandmother's boyfriend used to put a gun to my head every time he molested me for three years. It was nothing new to me. One bad situation got me to another bad situation is what saved my life. Because the night before the abduction I'm doing my suicide note and the next night I'm fighting for my life.

On November 3, 1984, McVey was snatched from her bicycle on the ride to her grandmother's home after work.She was blindfolded, held at gunpoint, raped, and tortured for 26 hours.She would later learn that the perpetrator was Bobby Joe Long, who was responsible for at least 10 murders and over 50 rapes.

During her captivity, McVey offered to be his secret girlfriend. She then elicited sympathy from Long by claiming to be the only child of an ill father. He was persuaded to release her and did so in a remote location, instructing her to keep her blindfold on for five minutes while he escaped. 

Upon arriving at home, she was beaten by her guardian’s boyfriend and interrogated for five hours about her whereabouts. Her account remained consistent and finally a phone call was made to the police.

McVey had committed to memory several details about her abduction and intentionally left fingerprints on several surfaces in Long's bathroom to help police identify her in the event of her death.Through her description of her captor, his vehicle, the route they took, and other details, police were able to track down Long and connect him to other crimes.

Officers began a surveillance operation and arrested Long on November 16, 1984, for sexual assault and kidnapping of McVey.

On September 23, 1985, Long pled guilty to his crimes against McVey and to an additional eight counts of first-degree murder, eight counts of kidnapping, and seven counts of sexual battery. He received life sentences on every count in Hillsborough County. Additionally, he received two death sentences for the murders of Michelle Denise Simms and Virginia Johnson.

When Long was executed on May 23, 2019, McVey and another survivor, Linda Nuttall, were present.

text:
Best Mysteries With Veterinarian Sleuths
#mystery #dogs #cats #horses

A muddy paw print on a clinic floor can be more than a housekeeping problem. In the best mysteries with veterinarian sleuths, it may be the first quiet clue that something is very wrong. A veterinarian notices details other people miss: an unusual wound, a missing medication, a frightened horse, or a dog reacting to the one person everyone else trusts.

That is the special pleasure of this cozy mystery niche. Veterinary sleuths bring practical skills, compassion, and a ready-made connection to a whole community of pet owners. They can move naturally from a farm call to a charity dog show, from the exam room to a historic downtown shop, all while asking the questions that make a murderer uncomfortable.

## What makes veterinarian mysteries so satisfying?

A veterinarian is an especially believable amateur detective because the work invites confidences. People tell the person caring for their beloved animal things they might not tell a neighbor, deputy, or reporter. They worry aloud. They argue about bills. They mention old grudges without realizing a careful listener is putting the pieces together.

Animals also add stakes without taking over the story. A good veterinary cozy respects the bond between people and pets. The mystery may begin with an animal in danger, but the animal is never merely a prop to make readers sad or to force a plot twist. Instead, the pet often reveals character. A devoted owner may be hiding something. A neglected animal may point toward a larger crime. A sharp-eyed dog may sense a threat long before the humans catch on.

Then there is the medical know-how. A veterinarian can recognize when an injury does not match the explanation, understand the consequences of a toxic substance, or notice that an animal’s symptoms are part of a human scheme. The best authors use that knowledge as seasoning, not a lecture. Readers should feel they have learned something interesting while still racing to discover who had motive, means, and opportunity.

## The best mysteries with veterinarian sleuths balance four things

Not every mystery featuring a clinic, a puppy, or a horse qualifies as a veterinarian-sleuth story. Some animal cozies star groomers, trainers, pet sitters, breeders, or veterinary technicians. Those can be delightful reads, but a veterinarian protagonist brings a different perspective and responsibility.

When choosing your next book, look for a mystery that gives the vet a genuine role in solving the case. The medical background should matter to the plot, whether through careful observation, professional contacts, or ethical questions that complicate an easy answer. A random clinic scene is not enough.

The setting matters just as much. Small towns are especially inviting because a vet knows nearly everyone, or at least knows their animals. That closeness makes suspicion tricky. The friendly shopkeeper may be a client. The mayor’s terrier may have been treated last week. The person asking for help may also be the person with the strongest reason to lie.

Humor is another essential ingredient. Cozy mysteries can handle real danger and tender feelings, but they need room for a wry observation, a stubborn pet, or a well-timed interruption from a curious neighbor. The warmth should come from affection for the characters, not from pretending that a crime has no consequences.

Finally, the solution needs to be fair. A veterinarian’s expertise may identify the clue, but it should not magically produce an answer no reader could have guessed. The most rewarding endings let you look back and think, “Of course. The clues were there all along.”

## A strong place to start: Eileen Brady’s Kate Turner mysteries

Readers who want a true veterinary lead can start with Eileen Brady’s Kate Turner series, beginning with *Muzzled*. Kate is a veterinarian whose professional life and personal instincts pull her into suspicious deaths. The series understands why veterinary work is such fertile mystery ground: animals and their people arrive with complicated histories, strong emotions, and plenty of secrets.

What makes this kind of series appealing is its balance of competence and vulnerability. Kate is not a detective who happens to own a stethoscope. Her veterinary training shapes the way she observes a scene and weighs evidence. At the same time, she is not invincible. Her concern for animals and people can put her in difficult positions, which gives the mysteries heart as well as momentum.

If you enjoy a little more tension alongside your cozy comforts, this is a worthwhile choice. Readers seeking an entirely gentle small-town atmosphere may prefer a lighter series, so it helps to sample the first book and see whether its level of danger suits your taste.

## Why canine narrators make the clue trail fresher

A dog’s viewpoint can add an extra spark to a veterinarian mystery, especially when the narrator has a warm snout, a sharp nose, and opinions about the humans making questionable decisions. A canine narrator can notice a familiar scent, a nervous voice, or a change in routine before the people around them understand its importance.

That perspective works best when it stays playful but clear. Readers want canine wit, not confusion. The dog should help us see the human world from an endearing new angle while the veterinarian remains a capable investigator who can interpret what the animal observes.

The Doc and Daisy Mysteries use that partnership to bring together Florida small-town charm, canine forensics, and the affectionate, occasionally exasperated voice of Daisy the dog. For readers who like their clues served with a wag and their local history tucked into the scenery, it is a particularly cheerful corner of the veterinary-mystery shelf.

https://t.co/m3ho5RGXEX

## How to find your perfect veterinary cozy

Your ideal pick depends on what you want from the animal side of the story. Dog lovers may gravitate toward cases involving canine behavior, agility events, rescues, or neighborhood pets. Cat lovers may prefer books where independent feline characters quietly complicate their humans’ lives. Horse-centered mysteries often offer wider landscapes, rural rivalries, and the practical realities of barns and breeding operations.

Consider how much veterinary detail you enjoy, too. Some readers love clues rooted in toxicology, anatomy, and animal behavior. Others prefer the clinic as a lively backdrop for gossip and community connections. Neither approach is better. The right one is the one that leaves you eager to turn one more page after bedtime.

It is also wise to check the emotional temperature. Many cozy readers want animals kept safe, even when a crime is under investigation. Others are comfortable with more serious veterinary cases if the story treats them thoughtfully. Book descriptions and early chapters usually signal whether a mystery leans light and funny, tender and poignant, or a little darker.

## The clues are often closer than they look

Veterinarian sleuths remind us that attention is a form of care. They listen when an animal cannot speak, notice what a rushed person overlooks, and understand that the smallest detail can carry a whole story. That makes these mysteries comforting companions for readers who love clever puzzles, lively towns, and animals with excellent instincts.

The next time you choose a cozy mystery, follow the paw prints toward a sleuth with a medical bag, a curious mind, and a patient four-legged sidekick. You may find that the most suspicious character in town is not the one growling at the door.

🚨 NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is scheduled to launch today, August 30, 2026, aboard a SpaceX Falcon Heavy from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

What will the Roman Telescope do?

• The mission is estimated to cost around $4.3 billion.
• It will survey huge areas of the sky in infrared light.
• Its camera has around 300 megapixels.
• It will offer Hubble-like sharp imaging with a field of view roughly 100× larger than Hubble’s.
• Scientists will use it to better understand dark matter and dark energy.
• The mission could discover thousands of exoplanets, with some estimates suggesting up to ~100,000.
• After launch, Roman will travel to the Sun-Earth L2 region, roughly 1 million miles from Earth.

The most interesting part?

Roman won’t replace Hubble or James Webb.

It will work alongside them. Webb can study specific targets in incredible detail, while Roman will rapidly survey much larger portions of the universe.

In simple terms: NASA is building a massive cosmic survey camera to map the universe on an unprecedented scale.

text:
Today at Let’s Talk About Verticals, I’m joined by actor Jason Caceres @jasonscaceres — one of the true veterans of the Vertical Space, with more than 100 vertical productions already under his belt! 🤯🎬

Born and raised in Miami as the son of Cuban immigrants, Jason discovered acting at a young age. What initially began as a way for a shy child to come out of his shell eventually developed into a genuine passion. He later earned his Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre Performance from Florida International University before facing an important post-college realization: New York’s temperatures and this sun-loving human were simply not meant for each other. ☀️🥶 So, he traded the East Coast cold for Los Angeles — and has now been successfully working there as an actor for many years.

Alongside his enormous body of work in Verticals, Jason’s career also includes appearances in well-known television productions such as Criminal Minds, Hacks, Pam & Tommy, Insatiable and Kidding. He has also become a recognizable presence in queer storytelling through projects including Boy Culture: Generation X, Open To It and Laid Bare. 

During our conversation, Jason takes us behind the scenes of his remarkable Vertical journey. We talk about the sometimes stupid titles, how the industry has changed over the course of more than 100 productions, what keeps him returning to this fast-moving format and what he has learned from working with so many different teams, platforms and characters.

And while Los Angeles remains his home base, Jason has become more than comfortable packing his suitcase and traveling abroad for Vertical shoots. 🌍✈️ For him, international productions offer not only exciting new projects, but also the opportunity to experience different working environments, creative approaches and cultures.

A warm, entertaining and insightful conversation you shoudn't miss. 🎭🎬✨

Today, we give thanks to Almighty Allah as we celebrate the 75th birthday of Distinguished Senator Muhammad Abba Aji—a distinguished son of Borno, accomplished public servant, politician, scholar, lawyer, mentor, family man and community leader whose life has been defined by service, excellence and an enduring commitment to humanity.
Born into the distinguished family of the late Abba Aji, the Aji Sudani of Dikwa Emirate, Senator Abba Aji comes from a heritage deeply rooted in leadership, service, family values and responsibility to the community.
His life story is a remarkable testimony to determination, continuous learning, discipline and the pursuit of excellence.
He began his professional journey as a Nursing Officer with the Borno State Ministry of Health, after obtaining his Diploma in Nursing from the Borno State School of Nursing. From that professional beginning, he proceeded to the University of Manchester, United Kingdom, where he obtained a First Class degree in Public Health Administration in 1979.

His thirst for knowledge remained insatiable. He subsequently obtained a Master's degree in Public Administration from Florida International University, USA, a PhD in Development from the University of Manchester in 1990, and a Postgraduate Diploma in Public Finance and Accounting from the same university.

He later embarked on another demanding academic journey in Law, commencing his studies in New Zealand, continuing at Baze University, Abuja, and thereafter undergoing rigorous professional training at the Nigerian Law School.

His educational journey, complemented by Islamic learning, represents a remarkable combination of knowledge, versatility and lifelong intellectual development.
From his early days as a Nursing Officer, Senator Abba Aji rose through the ranks of public service and occupied several important positions, including:
Executive Secretary, Borno State Health Management Board; Permanent Secretary, Local Government and Chieftaincy Affairs; Permanent Secretary, Finance; Managing Director, Nigeria Social Insurance Trust Fund (NSITF), 1995–2002; and Executive Secretary, North East Governors' Forum
He also served as Chairman of the Boards of various government institutions, among several other responsibilities. His career reflects an extraordinary breadth of experience spanning public health, administration, finance, development, law, institutional management and national governance.
In 2003, he entered elective politics and was elected Senator representing Borno Central Senatorial District, serving from 2003 to 2007.
He subsequently served as Adviser to the President on National Assembly Matters, under two Presidents of the Federal Republic of Nigeria—the late President Umaru Musa Yar'Adua and President Goodluck Ebele Jonathan.
Yet, beyond the impressive offices, titles and national assignments, perhaps the most enduring testimony to Senator Abba Aji is found in the people he has helped to shape.

He has mentored and supported many people within his nuclear and extended family, the wider community and beyond. He has encouraged education, supported careers, opened doors, offered counsel and provided assistance at critical moments in the lives of many.

We celebrate you for the life Allah has given you, the knowledge He has blessed you with, the opportunities He has granted you, the responsibilities you have carried and the many lives He has allowed you to touch.
For us, your mentees and beneficiaries, today is an opportunity to say, thank you for your guidance.
May Allah forgive your shortcomings, accept your good deeds, increase you in wisdom and grant you Husnul Khatimah and Jannatul Firdaus.
May Allah preserve you, honour you, increase you in good health and grant you many more fruitful years.

Written by Mentees of Senator Abba-Aji

text:
This were games we strongly considered as best on https://t.co/707wwLjlqj

JACKSONVILLE STATE +6.5 over North Dakota State

North Dakota State is receiving 58% of the spread bets, making Jacksonville State the contrarian side. Jacksonville State is also getting more than a field goal, strengthening the value of taking the points.

Jacksonville State has the more established quarterback in Caden Creel, who exceeded 1,000 yards both passing and rushing last season. NDSU's Nathan Hayes makes his first career start in the program's first game as an FBS member.

The problem is price. The official outlaw line was approximately NDSU -10 and the market has crashed to roughly -6.5. That's a massive 3.5-point move, and buying Jacksonville State after that adjustment means taking considerably less value than was originally available.

Lean — JACKSONVILLE STATE +6.5

+7 would be preferable.

MEMPHIS +4.5 over UNLV

The ticket count is essentially divided, with 50% of spread bets on each team, so there is no meaningful contrarian advantage at the current split.

The attraction is instead the matchup and independent sharp support. A respected handicapper released Memphis +5.5 with a projected line of UNLV -1, emphasizing Charles Huff's defensive personnel and its ability to defend the run.

That matters because UNLV's offensive strength is its ground attack, led by Jai'Den Thomas after a 1,000-yard season at approximately seven yards per carry.

Memphis remains a lean because Huff is beginning his first season with substantial roster turnover, while UNLV has greater program continuity. The loss of a full point from the recommended +5.5 to the current +4.5 also reduces the edge.

Lean — MEMPHIS +4.5

Prefer +5 or better.

NC STATE +4.5 over Virginia

The football case for NC State remains attractive, but the overall weighting is not sufficient for premium status.

Virginia has important personnel issues. Starting receiver Rico Flores Jr. is out. Running back/return specialist Solomon Beebe is unavailable, while impact linebacker Kam Robinson's return from a torn ACL remains an important variable.

NC State has the established quarterback in CJ Bailey, who exceeded 3,000 passing yards last season with a 25-to-9 touchdown/interception ratio.

However, 53% of spread bets are already taking NC State, so this is not a contrarian position. Virginia also possesses an extremely experienced offensive line protecting transfer quarterback Beau Pribula.

The personnel argument favors taking the points, but the complete premium-bet framework does not produce enough separation.

Lean — NC STATE +4.5

Take +4 or better.

USC Team Total OVER 48.5

USC's team total offers an alternative to chasing the full-game total after its substantial move.

The full total opened around 55.5 and has climbed to approximately 61.5, a six-point adjustment that far exceeds the four-point threshold for a significant totals move.

San Jose State's defensive turnover creates the fundamental case for USC scoring independently of whether the Spartans contribute enough to send the entire game OVER. There is also independent handicapper support for USC's team total.

Lean — USC Team Total OVER 48.5

Playable to 49.5.

FLORIDA STATE -17.5 1st Half over New Mexico State

Florida State's enormous personnel advantage is better expressed in the first half than by laying more than four touchdowns for the entire game.

The contrarian component is exceptional. 95% of spread bets are taking New Mexico State, making Florida State a very strong worldwide contrarian position.

New Mexico State quarterback Trey Hedden transfers from Furman after throwing 22 interceptions in 20 career starts. Florida State should have opportunities to create negative possessions and short fields against an opponent facing an enormous jump in defensive athleticism.

The matchup is favorable offensively as well. New Mexico State allowed 4.4 yards per rushing attempt last season, giving Florida State an obvious avenue for establishing control without exposing its offense to unnecessary early-game risk.

There is also independent sharp support for Florida State -17.5 in the first half.

The full-game line is considerably less attractive. Florida State opened around -28.5 and has moved beyond -31, crossing the key 31 threshold in the process. Rather than chase that substantial move for four quarters, the first-half position isolates the period in which Florida State's starters and motivation should be at their highest.

3* Major — FLORIDA STATE -17.5 1st Half over New Mexico State

Playable to -18.

NORTH CAROLINA–TCU 1st Half UNDER 24

This is one of Saturday's most pronounced public-total fades.

The full-game market has 82% of all total bets on the OVER. That makes the UNDER side exceptionally contrarian across a sample of more than 33,000 tracked wagers.

The football matchup supports attacking the first half rather than requiring the game to remain low scoring for four quarters.

TCU begins the Jaden Craig era under Gordon Sammis, whose offense at UConn operated at a relatively methodical pace. North Carolina is installing Bobby Petrino's offense around Billy Edwards Jr., with an emphasis on establishing the running game before exploiting deeper opportunities.

Ball security should also be emphasized by UNC after turnovers contributed directly to last season's 48-14 loss to TCU.

The Dublin setting provides additional support. Recent games at Aviva Stadium have generally produced modest scoring environments, and an international opener involving quarterbacks operating new offenses creates additional potential for deliberate early possessions.

There is also independent sharp support for 1st Half UNDER 24.

3* Major — NORTH CAROLINA–TCU 1st Half UNDER 24

24 is playable. Prefer 24.5 whenever available.

text:
Regarding Trulieve's success in Georgia, Bruiser & I called it 5 years ago:
-
Being the only publicly traded MSO to directly win in Georgia has not only strengthened Trulieve’s stranglehold on the southeast, but shows they can prudently expand without sacrificing significant amounts of equity for partnerships or capital to purchase already issued licenses. The likes of Boris Jordan and Curaleaf are probably scratching their heads wondering how did Kim & Trulieve accomplish this?

Trulieve started to lay it’s groundwork in Georgia early and forcefully. They overpowered their opponents in key areas in achieving the highest point score of all those applied. Achieving a 106.25 higher positive point differential than that of Curaleaf. This didn’t happen by chance. Numerous strategic events leading up to the latest announcement insured Trulieve would not just win but dominate.

For instance, Trulieve contracted the highest number of lobbyists in Georgia as a public MSO (11), with Curaleaf coming in second with 5. Trulieve hired the state House Speaker David Ralston son, Matthew Ralston, as one of its lobbyists. While it’s also been said that Trulieve’s main Florida lobbyist group in Ballard Partners. Has built a reputation for having far reaching influence stretching to many parts of the southern US including that of Georgia.

When things didn’t seem like they were going in Trulieve’s favour in Georgia. Just a few days before the application deadline. Not only did they file a protest with the regulators. They sued the state challenging the requirement that applying entities must have operated in GA for a minimum of 5 years. Giving Trulieve the necessary time to submit a robust Request for Proposal and ultimately change their subsidiary in Georgia from one formed in 2019 to one formed in 1993. Only to withdraw the protest and lawsuit almost a month after filing.

While Trulieve has been dismissed by other MSO’s as simply being a Single-State-Operator. Achieving first mover advantage has always been their preferential strategy for entering a limited license state. This is strategy in Florida and this is the strategy they are looking to employ in every emerging market - for instance, they already have entities established in preparation for application rounds in Alabama, Mississippi, Texas, Virginia, and New Jersey.

...

Now that the smoke has cleared surrounding the license applications. There remains to be three elephants in the room: The 5% THC limit on all products, no availability of smokable flower/edibles and the limited number of conditions. However our thought process remains steadfast that Georgia will follow the lead of Florida. If you recall the initial legalization efforts in Florida. The THC limit was originally just 0.8% THC & 10% CBD with the conditions limited to patients with cancer or a “physical medical condition that chronically produces symptoms of seizures or severe and persistent muscle spasms” may qualify for the program if no satisfactory alternative treatment options exist.

As one can imagine, the regulators of respective state medical cannabis programs talk to one another to gain insight and lessons learned. When early movers such as Florida implemented low-THC programs, their program administrators had little to draw upon other than west coast markets that were highly volatile and mostly not politically congruent. Now that Georgia’s Commission has mature highly regulated medical markets such as Florida, Pennsylvania, Ohio, and Connecticut to draw years of wisdom from, there is reason to believe their market’s development will be accelerated compared to the aforementioned.

Additionally, the Georgia Commission’s independent work will only be compounded by the work of licensees. If you want to get additional qualifying conditions such as anxiety added to a program, you need to prove the merits of cannabis treatment to the Commission. This is why partnering with medical institutions is just as important for winning a license as it is for operating. Public-private partnerships such as Trulieve’s partnership with the Morehouse School of Medicine, and Botanical Science’s partnership with Georgia Southern will prove incredibly useful to prove the efficacy of medical cannabis to regulators.

...

Overall, the short-medium term benefits of operating in Georgia are obvious: a highly restricted market with a large population, in the region that’s the final frontier of US cannabis legalization. In the long-term, the state’s microclimate and low environmental risk offer the opportunity to establish production facilities that can supply much of the southeast and greater east coast.

𝗗𝗘𝗡𝗜𝗦𝗘 "𝗡𝗜𝗦𝗬" 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗟𝗜𝗦𝗛

Earlene Denise “Nisy” Green-English was born on February 5, 1959, in Harlem, New York.
She was raised by her mother, who was originally from North Carolina, and her Native American father. 
She began playing basketball from the age of 8 and went on to graduate from Christopher Columbus High School in the Bronx in 1977 with PSAL All-City honors as well as an AAU national standout.
From the playgrounds of Harlem and The Bronx, to the national and international basketball stage, Nisy built a legacy as an outstanding 5'5" shooting guard and an inspirational leader, on and off the basketball court.

After graduation from Christopher Columbus HS and spending time in the US Army, she accepted a scholarship offer from Georgia State University in downtown Atlanta. Family issues prevented her from taking full advantage of her college experience and  returned to New York.
She later played for elite teams including the Afro Sisters, Each-One-Teach-One, and the NY Chuckles. She played in the Women’s Professional Basketball League and was inducted into the Rucker Professionals Basketball Hall of Fame in 2014.

Nisy has found her niche in mentoring young athletes  leading youth training camps in the Bronx, coaching championship teams in Yonkers, and working with girls and boys across North Carolina, including semi-pro Team Elite, in Greensboro and youth programs in Carthage.
In 2025 she was hired as Middle School and Varsity girls basketball coach at The O'Neal School in Southern Pines, North Carolina, back near her mother's original home.
Nisy English is a New York basketball treasure that leaves a legacy of excellence everywhere she goes. Continued blessings!

text:
I WANT TO THANK EVERYONE WHO FOLLOWED OUR EPIC “YOU ARE THERE” PROJECT

I want to offer my sincere thanks to everyone who followed our epic “YOU ARE THERE” project as we traveled day by day through the Mary Phagan case as it was reported in the Atlanta press from April 28, 1913, through August 26, 1913.

Our goal was simple: to give people a chance to experience the case as readers in Atlanta experienced it in 1913, through the newspapers published while the investigation, coroner’s inquest, grand jury proceedings, trial, verdict, and sentencing were actually taking place.

We concentrated on the three major Atlanta newspapers whose coverage forms such a large part of the surviving public record:

The Atlanta Constitution (AC): 413 article entries

The Atlanta Journal (AJ): 295 article entries

The Atlanta Georgian (AG): 455 article entries

Total: 1,163 newspaper article entries covering April 28 through August 26, 1913.

That is 1,163 individual pieces of contemporary newspaper coverage spread across a period of only 121 days. It works out to an average of about 9+ article entries for every calendar day in the period.

And August 26, 1913, is not the end of “YOU ARE THERE.”

It is the beginning of our next chapter.

We are going to extend the project beyond the trial and begin building out the newspaper record from August 26, 1913, through August 17, 1915, when Leo Max Frank was extrajudicially hanged near Marietta, Georgia, followed by the immediate aftermath of the case.

There are nearly two more years of history to cover: the post-trial motions, appeals, extraordinary motion for a new trial, Georgia Supreme Court proceedings, the United States Supreme Court fight, the national campaign surrounding the case, Governor John M. Slaton’s June 21, 1915 commutation of Frank’s death sentence, the July 17, 1915 prison attack on Frank, his removal from the Georgia State Prison Farm on the night of August 16, and his hanging during the early morning hours of August 17, 1915.

And the story did not stop there.

We intend to follow the aftermath as well.

We are truly grateful to everyone who read, watched, shared, commented on, and followed our first “YOU ARE THERE” series. Seeing people engage with original newspaper reports that are now more than 113 years old has encouraged us to expand this work dramatically.

We are proud of the work that has already been accomplished, and none of it would be possible without the time, energy, encouragement, research, transcription work, technical help, and historical interest of the people who have contributed along the way.

A special thank-you goes to Team Phagan.

This has become a much larger preservation project than we first imagined, and Team Phagan has helped us keep it moving forward.

Our long-range goal is to build what we hope will become the largest publicly accessible library of Mary Phagan and Leo Frank case transcripts, audiobooks, primary legal records, newspaper clipping videos, historical photographs, trial testimony, and contemporary newspaper coverage anywhere in the world.

We do not want these records sitting unseen in archives or buried in old microfilm.

We want people to be able to read them.

We want people to be able to hear them.

We want people to be able to watch them.

We want people to be able to search them.

And most of all, we want these records preserved for future generations.

One of our largest goals is the creation of more than 2,000 newspaper clipping videos covering the Mary Phagan Case and Leo Frank trial and appeals. We want people anywhere in the world to be able to see an original article, read its text, hear it read aloud, and understand exactly when and where it appeared. 

The newspaper clipping videos are only one part of what we are building.

We are also working on a podcast devoted to the case, and we have additional podcast appearances and discussions lined up for the days, weeks, and months ahead.

We also hope to undertake one of our most ambitious preservation projects yet: creating historical lip-sync presentations of the closing arguments delivered by the trial counsel in August 1913.

Frank Arthur Hooper, Luther Zeigler Rosser, Reuben Rose Arnold, and Solicitor General Hugh Manson Dorsey spoke for many hours. Reconstructing their arguments from the surviving newspaper accounts and primary records will produce extremely long presentations, in some cases running for hours, but we believe they are worth preserving in a form that people can watch and hear.

Imagine being able to sit down more than a century later and listen to the arguments presented to the jury in the Fulton County courthouse in Atlanta during the final days of one of the most famous murder trials in American history.

That is the kind of historical library we want to build.

We are continuing to transcribe newspaper articles. We are continuing to create audiobooks. We are continuing to digitize legal records. We are continuing to locate forgotten documents, photographs, testimony, affidavits, exhibits, court filings, newspaper reports, and other primary-source materials connected with the case.

So far, our library contains more than 10,000 transcribed pages of primary-source material.

Our next goal is 15,000 pages.

That means adding at least another 5,000 pages to what we have already assembled, an increase of about 50 percent.

And we intend to keep expanding beyond that.

Our aim is not simply to build a website. We are trying to build a permanent historical library containing transcripts, audiobooks, videos, newspaper clippings, legal records, photographs, and other surviving evidence from 1913 through 1915.

These are not simply modern accounts written about events that took place generations ago. Much of this material consists of the words recorded in 1913, 1914, and 1915: testimony, legal records, affidavits, court proceedings, newspaper interviews, investigative reports, arguments, contemporary photographs, and the daily reporting of journalists who were actually there.

We believe the strongest answer to more than a century of selective quotation, mythology, polemics, and secondhand retellings is to put the original record before the public.

Read the newspapers.

Read the Brief of Evidence.

Read the testimony.

Read the affidavits.

Read the appellate records.

Read what the prosecution said.

Read what the defense said.

Read what the witnesses actually said.

Then decide for yourself.

One of the central purposes of the Mary Phagan-Kean Legacy Project has always been to make these records accessible to ordinary people. You should not have to travel to an archive in Atlanta, own a rare century-old newspaper, purchase an expensive historical volume, or depend upon somebody else’s interpretation of a document that you have never been allowed to examine for yourself.

We want the record available anywhere in the world.

We want to build the largest collection we possibly can.

Thousands of pages.

Thousands of newspaper articles.

Thousands of videos.

Hundreds of Hours upon hours of audiobooks.

Trial testimony.

Legal records.

Closing arguments.

Newspaper coverage.

Photographs.

Court documents.

And material that might otherwise disappear from public memory.

We also intend to continue challenging what we believe are serious distortions surrounding the case, including what we have described as the “Leo Frank industrial complex,” a century-long body of advocacy, retelling, and selective presentation that we believe has too often replaced the complete historical record with a predetermined narrative. We reject the use of the case as a weapon for smearing Christians, Southerners, Georgians, or any other broad group of people.

The answer is more evidence, more documents, more context, and greater public access to the original sources.

There is still an enormous amount of work in front of us.

More newspapers.

More legal records.

More transcripts.

More audiobooks.

More clipping videos.

More historical presentations.

More podcasts.

More photographs and documents to preserve.

More than 2,000 clipping videos are our long-range goal. Fifteen thousand transcribed pages are our next major documentary goal. And as new material is located, those goals may grow again.

The first 121 days of “YOU ARE THERE,” from April 28 through August 26, 1913, gave us 1,163 Atlanta newspaper article entries from the Atlanta Constitution, Atlanta Journal, and Atlanta Georgian alone.

Now we continue beyond the courtroom.

From the verdict and sentence into the appeals.

From Atlanta to the Georgia Supreme Court.

From Georgia to the United States Supreme Court.

From the death sentence to Governor Slaton’s commutation.

From the prison attack to the events of August 16 and 17, 1915.

And then into the aftermath.

We have a steep climb in front of us and a long journey ahead.

To everyone who has followed, shared, watched, read, encouraged us, contributed material, helped with research, or simply kept an interest in the project alive, thank you.

And once again, thank you to Team Phagan.

We are proud of what we have built together, and we are even more excited about what we can preserve in the years ahead.

Stay with us.

Share the primary sources. Preserve the historical record. Help other people discover the original documents.

And please follow me on X as we begin the next phase of “YOU ARE THERE.”

The work goes on. The fight continues to prevent the exoneration of Leo Frank. We will never give up.

text:
Crew 👀 sniff test on @TickleTexts. Her words first. Then why each piece matters. Then you tell me block or keep.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1️⃣ THE DEBT AND THE SURGERY 💸🧠
Her words, Aug 12, 2026:
“Wednesday morning I’ll be having another brain cancer related surgery. Yes, I’ve decided that $1.3m of medical debt isn’t enough…”

Aug 7, 2026:
“Smile if you’re not $1.3m in medical debt!”

Why it matters:
$1.3 million is an extreme number even for years of uninsured cancer care. She posts it as fact. No bill, no hospital name on a statement, no court or collections record has been shown. Big number + ask for money with nothing public to check = first flag. 🚩

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2️⃣ THE MEDS ASK 💊
Her words, Aug 27, 2026:
“Thanks @TexasGalReborn for subscribing. Every penny helps me pay for cancer meds”

Also:
“My subs are old friends and they know their $3 goes towards paying for my cancer meds.”

Why it matters:
She is directly tying subscriptions and X Money to cancer treatment. That is fine if the illness is real and documented. It is a problem when the illness, the surgeries, and the $1.3M are all self-reported and have been questioned for years.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3️⃣ HOMELESS / MOTEL / BANKRUPT 🏨
Her words:
“Yeah! To hell with brain cancer & homelessness”
“Yes, I’m medically bankrupt at this point and living in a motel week-to-week”
She also posted that Cash App froze her because she could not prove a motel address with a utility bill or lease.

Why it matters:
Motel + medical bankruptcy + $1.3M debt is a hardship story. Same week she is describing meetings with senators in DC and being “given data to release.” Those two lives do not usually exist at the same time. ⚠️

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4️⃣ HOW MANY SURGERIES / TUMORS 🏥
Her words, June 2026:
“Sorry I’ve quiet for several days. I’m back in hospital. New brain tumor confirmed… Tumor number four after three brain surgeries is not on my to-do list.”

Aug 17, 2026:
“I’m recovering from three brain surgeries, in Houston. Plus an adjacent surgery just last week!”

2024 account post (as a friend “Miz”):
she was at MD Anderson Houston for “Glioma with Proton treatment”

She also said she was “offline 2024-26 battling brain cancer.”

Why it matters:
The count keeps moving: three surgeries, then four tumors, then another procedure last week. MD Anderson and proton therapy for glioma are real things. The issue is there is still no public record, no named doctor, no dated discharge, and one hospital photo she used had a 2025 date overlay on a 2026 procedure story.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5️⃣ TRUTH SOCIAL JOB 📱
Her words, March 2026:
“I worked for Truth Social during its first year. Dilley begged me for early entry. Then also for his newest wife. Then demanded they both have red verification checkmarks… The inside info I have would bring down so many”

Later:
“Thousands here know and remember me working at Truth Social.”

Why it matters:
Truth Social’s first-year team was about 40 people. The executives and early staff names are public. No match has been produced. “Thousands remember me” does not fit a 40-person company. When people checked names from that era, she did not know them. 🚩

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6️⃣ TWITTER / “THE PLATFORM” 🐦
Her words:
“FYI I used to work for the platform.”
“I saw these labels, live, as an employee and the public saw them during the Twitter Files release.”

Why it matters:
Same test. Early Twitter/Periscope people from the period she implied were named. She said she did not know one of them and he “must be new.” That answer did not fit the timeline. No offer letter, no coworker on the record, no Slack/email screenshot with her name.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7️⃣ CENSUS / FED / DHS 🇺🇸
Her words:
“I know because I worked on the web version of the census!”
Bio: “May be a Fed” + https://t.co/l5H1zAHVFQ link

Why it matters:
Working the 2020 Census web form and being a “fed” are checkable in principle. Nothing public confirms either one. “May be a Fed” in the bio while also describing motel living and $1.3M debt is another stack that does not sit clean.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8️⃣ DC, SENATORS, “GIVEN DATA” 🏛️
Her words, July 30, 2026:
“Arrived safely in DC, very tired. Met with Ted Cruz and one other Senator. Todays plans are to meet with a group from Congress… The topic is a personal lawsuit against Fauci not an official class action!”

Later:
“I was recently in DC and given data to release. It’s not uncommon!”
“I was recently in DC, also given a few ‘gifts’ then asked to sit on them until further notice. Prior to brain cancer, I was the one revealing (usually) public ‘secrets’”

Why it matters:
Meeting Cruz and other members of Congress while in the middle of repeated brain surgeries, CSF leaks, a shunt, and motel living is the core contradiction. Federal / high-access environments have medical fitness standards. She has not shown a photo with Cruz, a readout, a staff name, or a filing. “Given data to release” is an insider claim with no document attached. 🚩

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9️⃣ THE OLDER PATTERN (2021 and 2024) ♻️
Not her current posts — the prior public disputes:
People in her Spaces circle said they heard stories about intelligence work, an overseas rescue, a Red Sox-owner husband, a deceased triplet, and earlier medical crises. When pushed, those stories were denied or the pic/name changed and she left for a while. Same outline: big story, money or status attached, then fog when checked.

Why it matters:
One unverified story can be a misunderstanding. The same shape repeating across 2021, 2024, and 2026 is the pattern.

━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
THE STACK 📦
Put it in one line:

Three/four brain surgeries + new tumor + shunt + $1.3M debt + motel
AND
Twitter employee + Truth Social first-year insider + census web + maybe a Fed + just met senators and got data to release

Hospital photos exist. MD Anderson exists. That is not enough to carry the rest. After years of this there is still no named coworker, no payroll, no medical document, no meeting photo.

Sniff test: pass or fail. ✅❌

text:
“Seeking treatment for stress is not evidence that you were dangerous. Properly presented, it may demonstrate that you recognized pressure and sought help responsibly.”

Over the next several weeks, I rented Daniel a modest three-bedroom apartment in Evanston, close enough to the boys’ normal routines that nobody could reasonably argue he was trying to move them away.

A former colleague offered him a job at a technology company after reviewing his work history and dismissing the rumors surrounding the divorce.

We never pretended my help made Daniel instantly independent.

We documented it honestly.

Family support was part of his stability, not something to hide.

Meanwhile, Melissa began tracing the money.

Detective Blake couldn’t simply give us confidential police information or manufacture evidence for a custody dispute.

She could point us toward public records and explain which concerns deserved professional examination.

Charles Whitaker’s name appeared in earlier financial disputes involving unusually structured business transactions.

Nothing publicly available established that he had stolen from Daniel.

But there was enough reason to examine the records carefully.

Melissa retained Ethan Cho, a forensic accountant whose quiet demeanor made him look more like a university librarian than someone capable of dismantling financial stories transaction by transaction.

Three weeks later, Ethan placed a flowchart on the conference table.

“The original $150,000 investment moved into the startup exactly as expected. Later, $150,000 left the operating account and went to an account controlled by Charles Whitaker under a description reading ‘vendor settlement.’”

I leaned forward.

“Where is the vendor agreement?”

“We have not found one. No invoice, no executed loan agreement, and no identifiable service matching the payment.”

He turned the page.

The issue went beyond that single transfer.

Across approximately fourteen months, smaller amounts moved from the company into accounts controlled by Lauren, then onward to entities associated with Charles.

Five hundred dollars.

A thousand.

Several thousand.

Individually, many transactions appeared ordinary.

Together, they formed a pattern.

Shortly before the separation, most remaining operating capital had been depleted.

Ethan’s preliminary reconstruction identified roughly $280,000 in transfers requiring explanation.

Daniel went pale.

“I was working eighteen-hour days trying to keep the company alive while money was leaving behind me.”

Melissa raised one hand.

“We do not call it theft until the evidence supports that conclusion. What we can say is that substantial funds moved through related accounts without the documentation we would expect.”

That discipline became important.

We weren’t going to fight Lauren’s exaggerated story by creating an exaggerated story of our own.

We wanted to reconstruct what actually happened.

The next issue was visitation.

Diane Whitaker’s notes repeatedly described Daniel as aggressive, intrusive, unpredictable, and frightening around the twins.

Daniel described Lego towers, snacks, shoelaces, hugs, and constant criticism from Diane.

Melissa investigated the applicable Illinois recording rules and the circumstances surrounding the visits.

Rather than assuming Daniel could secretly record everything, she obtained proper guidance and requested that future visits be supervised through a neutral professional service whenever possible.

That decision eventually mattered more than we expected.

text:
Top 10 Tech Business News | Aug. 23–29, 2026
My overall take: This was a full-stack AI consolidation week. Capital, compute, models, cloud capacity and enterprise applications are becoming tightly coupled—but custom silicon, financing concerns and government policy are thought of beginning to challenge @Nvidia’s expanding control.

My Activities: It was great being at @Glean’s #GleanGo 2026 in San Francisco, and comparing notes with Amar Maletira, COO, Glean and several other tech leaders! Haseeb Budhani @haseebbudhani, CEO of @RafaySystemsInc visited my office in Santa Clara. Had a great talk over dinner with @gssahni, CMO of @Altimetrik in Palo Alto. I had a great discussion with @efipm this week! Video will be out soon.

Here are top 10 news of the week:

1. Nvidia’s quarterly revenue crosses $96 billion

Nvidia reported record quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106% year over year. Data-center revenue reached $89 billion, up 117%, while the company guided to $108 billion for the next quarter. Nvidia expects supply (not demand) to remain bottleneck at least through the end of 2028 says Nvidia CFO, Colette Kress. 

Nvidia customers reportedly warned about AI-related price hikes. Jensen confirmed this to take effect at a later date, during earnings call. 

My take: Nvidia is no longer simply riding the AI infrastructure buildout—it is defining its pace. However, with data centers generating more than 90% of revenue, Nvidia’s exposure to AI infrastructure spending is also becoming systemic. Nvidia giving 2028 full year growth outlook was their first such move. 

WSJ Scoop: Nvidia paused some deals in a new financing initiative that offered credit support to AI cloud providers in exchange for a share of revenue.

#Earnings #Nvidia #AIInfrastructure #Semiconductors

2. Nvidia reportedly agrees to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9 billion

Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire open-model platform Hugging Face, although neither company has officially confirmed the transaction. 

My take: The strategic logic is stronger than the near-term financial logic. Hugging Face gives Nvidia developer, model and data distribution gravity across the open AI ecosystem—but the deal will likely attract serious antitrust scrutiny. One question coming to my mind is, if Nvidia over-indexing on OpenSource, but then again, this move cannot hurt Nvidia, it can only benefit them..

#OpenModels #Nvidia #DeveloperEcosystem

3. Anthropic reportedly commits $45 billion to Nscale

Anthropic reportedly signed a six-year agreement to rent approximately 460 megawatts of AI computing capacity from @Nscale’s West Virginia data-center campus, using Nvidia Vera Rubin systems. 

My take: Frontier-model companies are increasingly behaving like hyperscalers. Model competition is becoming a contest of balance sheets, power contracts and access to physical infrastructure—not just model quality.

#Anthropic #DataCenters #AIInfrastructure #Investment

4. AWS plans to deploy two million additional Nvidia GPUs

@AWSCloud and Nvidia announced plans to deploy two million additional Blackwell Ultra, Rubin and Rubin Ultra GPUs during 2027–2028. The partnership also includes secure AI factories for the U.S. government and deeper robotics collaboration. Amazon

My take: This is huge, IMO! AWS is simultaneously investing in its own Trainium silicon and dramatically expanding Nvidia capacity. Hyperscalers will promote custom chips for economics while continuing to offer Nvidia for workload portability and customer demand.

#AWS #Cloud #Nvidia #AIInfrastructure

5. OpenAI publishes the first benchmarks for Jalapeño (their accelerator chip)

OpenAI said its Broadcom-developed Jalapeño inference ASIC delivered 1.5–1.9 times more AI work per watt and 1.7–3.6 times lower latency than the comparison systems in its tests. 

My take: Specialized inference is where Nvidia’s general-purpose GPU premium will face the greatest pressure. Benchmark caveats matter, but custom silicon economics are moving from theory to production. Jensen wrote it off in his remarks as it's not a generic solution.

#OpenAI #CustomSilicon #Inference #HotChips

6. Nvidia Groq 3 LPX enters full production

Nvidia announced that Groq 3 LPX is now in full production, extending Vera Rubin systems with faster token generation for agentic and latency-sensitive inference. Nebius will be its first AI-cloud adopter.

My take: Nvidia is evolving from a GPU company into a heterogeneous AI-systems company. By combining GPUs, CPUs, networking and specialized LPUs, it can defend its economics even as inference workloads become more specialized.

#Nvidia #Groq #AgenticAI #Inference

7. Salesforce reports measurable AI revenue momentum, strikes deal with @AnthropicAI announcing #Claudeforce

Salesforce reported $11.35 billion in quarterly revenue. Agentforce and Data 360 ARR approached $3.9 billion, up more than 210%, while Salesforce and Anthropic introduced Claudeforce. Salesforce results, #Claudeforce announcement

My take: Salesforce finally has a measurable AI monetization story. However, bundled AI-and-data ARR should not be confused with standalone agent revenue—the durability of consumption will matter more than bookings. Claudeforce announcement with Anthropic is a bold move. 

#Salesforce #EnterpriseAI #Agentforce #Earnings

8. Nvidia pauses some AI-cloud revenue-sharing deals

Nvidia reportedly paused parts of a financing initiative that provided smaller AI-cloud companies with credit support in exchange for revenue sharing. The arrangements raised concerns about circular demand and potential antitrust exposure. 

My take: This is a healthy correction. When a supplier finances its customers, guarantees capacity and participates in their revenue, it becomes increasingly difficult to distinguish organic demand from financially engineered demand.

#AIEconomics #Neoclouds #TechPolicy

9. SK Hynix breaks ground on its $4 billion Indiana HBM facility

SK Hynix began construction of its first U.S. advanced HBM packaging facility, targeting mass production in late 2029. The company expects memory shortages to persist through 2030. 

My take: Memory is moving from a supporting component to a strategic AI bottleneck. If shortages persist through 2030, more of the AI infrastructure profit pool will migrate from GPUs toward memory and advanced packaging.

#HBM #Memory #CHIPSAct #AISupplyChain

10. Federal judge blocks the Pentagon’s Anthropic blacklist

A federal judge ruled that the Pentagon’s designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk was unlawful, finding violations of the company’s First and Fifth Amendment rights. 

My take: AI safety policies are now colliding with government procurement power and constitutional rights. The ruling limits the government’s ability to use market access as leverage in disputes over acceptable AI use.

#Anthropic #AIPolicy #DefenseTech #Governance

text:
Next up in my Iowa State Fair booth reviews: Midwest Construction from Des Moines.

Midwest Construction specializes in windows, siding, roofing, decking and sunrooms—and they found a pretty effective way to explain that without saying much at all.

They built a house.

With just over a 10x10 footprint, they turned their booth into a miniature home featuring different windows, siding and other products they offer.

You could literally walk around the booth and see their products installed the way you would see them on your own home.

Inside, they used the remaining space for additional product samples and information.

Could someone initially think they’re a home builder? Possibly. But their signage quickly explains exactly what they do: siding, windows, sunrooms and seamless gutters.

That’s what makes the concept work.

Instead of putting those products on a table and asking attendees to imagine what they’ll look like installed, Midwest Construction showed them.

And from across the aisle, the booth immediately makes you curious because there’s a house sitting in the middle of an exhibit hall.

Sometimes the best booth strategy is incredibly literal.

If your products go on a house, make your booth a house.

They maximized a relatively small footprint and turned the booth itself into the product demonstration.

Simple idea. Great execution

REGIONAL SPORTS ROUNDUP
August 25, 2026

HIGH SCHOOL

FALL SPORTS REPORT
In volleyball, Calloway County defeated Fulton County 3-1 last night. The set scores were 25-21, 25-16, 21-25, 25-17. The Lakers are now 4-4 and are off until next Tuesday's match at Graves County. Tonight, 6-3 Murray High visits 0-4 St. Mary. 

LAKERS VS TIGERS
It is Crosstown Classic week and that means Calloway County and Murray High soccer will tangle in doubleheader action tonight at the Mallary France Soccer Complex. The Calloway girls are 7-1 after winning the championship of the Smoky Mountain Cup, while Murray enters the night with a 4-1 record. The Calloway boys enter the night 2-5 while Murray comes into the match with a 6-1 mark. 

LANGHI COMMITS
Marshall County basketball's Matthew Langhi announced on social media on Monday that he has committed to Bellarmine. The 6'6" senior averaged 27 points a game for the Marshals last season, leading his team to the Region 1 championship and the KHSAA State Quarterfinals. Langhi also held offers from Southern Indiana, Indiana State, and Jacksonville State. His father, Dan, played at Vanderbilt and was the Co-SEC Player of the Year in 2000.

TACKETT RETIREMENT
The longtime leader of the Kentucky High School Athletic Association is ready to move on.  KHSAA Commissioner Julian Tackett announced his retirement plans yesterday.  Tackett has been with the association for more than 40 years and has served as commissioner since 2010.  He says he will be stepping down from his position later on this school year. It was also reported yesterday that Senior Associate Commissioner Butch Cope would retire next July. 

COLLEGE

UPGRADES AT THE STEW
Murray State Athletics has completed $4 million in upgrades to Rudolph Family Field at Roy Stewart Stadium, including renovations to the Draffen Family Performance Center, a new FieldTurf playing surface, a navy track and an auxiliary practice field. The upgrades enhance strength and conditioning, sports medicine and student-athlete spaces while improving the game-day environment. A new videoboard and the Draffen Family Founders Club are also planned. The improvements are part of Murray State’s $100 million Leading The Pack fundraising campaign, which has raised $52.75 million.

DAWN WINS SEC HONOR
Kentucky freshman Kyla Dawn was named SEC Freshman of the Week after totaling three goals and two assists in wins over Kent State and Dayton. The Dallas native scored twice in a 12-minute span against Dayton and now leads the Wildcats with 10 points, four goals and two assists.

FRESHMAN WINS VOLS QB JOB
A true freshman will lead the Tennessee Volunteers' offense out onto the field to start the season.  ESPN reports Faizon Brandon won a three-way competition to be the Vols' Week One starter over sophomore George MacIntyre and Colorado transfer Ryan Staub.  Brandon inherits an offense with eight returning starters for next week's season opener at home against Furman.

PROS

CARDINALS REPORT
After a day off the Cardinals are back on the diamond tonight.  The team squares off against Pete Alonso and the Orioles in the first of three games at Busch Stadium.  St. Louis hopes to bounce back after getting swept by Philly and will send Matthew Liberatore (5-11, 5.04 ERA) against Chris Bassitt (4-4, 5.08 ERA). First pitch is scheduled for 6:45 with a 5:50 pregame show airtime on WNBS. 

TITANS REPORT
Titans' starters struggled Sunday despite a preseason victory over the Seattle Seahawks.  Tennessee won 19-to-16 on Sunday, but its starters were outscored 16-3 during the opening three possessions.  Cam Ward completed eight of 12 passes for 69 yards, although the starting offense failed to reach the end zone.  The starting defense allowed touchdowns of 36 and 69 yards against Seattle's reserves and failed to record a sack.  Tennessee committed 11 penalties for 100 yards, including infractions that erased an interception and a touchdown.

AREA NFL REPORT
Longtime Cincinnati Bengals tight end CJ Uzomah is hanging up his helmet after ten years in the NFL.  The 33-year-old returned to Cincinnati today to retire with the team that made him a fifth-round draft pick out of Auburn in 2015.  Uzomah spent seven seasons in the Bengals' stripes before a two-year run with the New York Jets and one with the Philadelphia Eagles.  He caught 192 passes for nearly 19-hundred yards and 16 touchdowns. 

NFL teams are gearing up for the end of the preseason as Week Three kicks off on Thursday with four matchups on the slate.  Meanwhile, the Chiefs host the Seahawks, and the Falcons visit the Dolphins on Friday while the Bears visit the Titans on Saturday to put a bow on exhibition play.

Comical when people lean on this memorandum, which actually concedes that Centene’s $10 million payment to Hope Florida was made “in exchange for the releases.” Florida law treats a contractual undertaking to benefit a designated third party as consideration furnished to the promisee. Consideration. That's the issue. 
The State was the promisee and supplied the release. Hope Florida was merely the State-selected recipient. 
The memorandum offers no authority for the proposition that executive officials may remove settlement consideration from sections 45.062(5) and 216.216 by changing the destination line on the check. If that theory were correct, both statutes would be optional. They are not. There's a few "shalls" in there. 
The memorandum never addresses section 216.216, which separately requires money received through settlement of a State action to be placed in General Revenue or the trust fund associated with the agency’s authority. It also ignores the appropriation and separation-of-powers issue.
Authority for a DSO to accept genuine charitable donations does not establish authority for State officers to divert settlement consideration to it. And the tobacco analogy is not a holding interpreting sections 45.062 or 216.216.
And of course, the discussion of Hope Florida’s admirable mission, SMMC 3.0, Centene’s procurement award, and the tobacco settlement is mostly political insulation, and sounds like @RonDeSantis logical fallacy ridden speech the other day - where interestingly, he quoted our founders. 
Well, the fundamental concern of keeping the individual branches separate is that the fusion of the powers of any two branches into the same department would ultimately result in the destruction of liberty. Ponder v. Graham, 4 Fla. 23, 42-43 (1851); (citing The Federalist No. 47 (James Madison), No. 51 (Alexander Hamilton or James Madison)).
@davidjollyfl is right for going after this. So was @ScottforFlorida and others. Look, I get that we are not in charge anymore, dark money rules the waves, but for God sakes at least honor pathos, ethos and logos.

text:
James Madison explained that splitting the legislative branch into two chambers with different MODES of election was one of the ways to prevent the natural predominance of the legislature in a republic.

In Federalist No. 51, Madison identified a structural problem inherent to republican government: the legislative branch, by its nature, tends to predominate. It commands the purse, enacts the laws, and stands closest to popular sentiment. Because none of the three branches can be given equal power of self-defense, Madison argued that the remedy for this imbalance must be found inside the legislature itself:

“In republican government, the legislative authority necessarily predominates. The remedy for this inconveniency is to divide the legislature into different branches; and to render them, by different modes of election and different principles of action, as little connected with each other as the nature of their common functions and their common dependence on the society will admit.”

The original Constitution implemented this prescription with precision. The House of Representatives was chosen directly by the people; the Senate was chosen by the state legislatures. These distinct modes of election produced distinct constituencies, distinct electoral incentives, and distinct time horizons. One chamber represented the people in their individual capacity; the other represented the states as corporate political communities. The resulting disconnection between the two houses was not an accidental feature of bicameralism. It was the mechanism Madison prescribed to check the very predominance he had diagnosed.

The Seventeenth Amendment (1913) abolished that distinction. By substituting popular election for election by state legislatures, it placed both chambers on the same electoral foundation. Senators and Representatives now answer to overlapping popular majorities, compete in similar media environments, and face similar interest-group and partisan pressures. The “different modes of election” Madison identified as essential to keeping the two houses “as little connected with each other as feasible” were eliminated.

The structural consequence follows directly from Madison’s own logic. Removing the differentiated electoral base reduced one of the principal internal restraints on legislative power. The Senate ceased to function as an institutional representative of the states qua states and became a second popular chamber, distinguished from the House chiefly by longer terms and equal state representation rather than by a fundamentally different source of authority. In Madisonian terms, the amendment therefore weakened the very remedy he offered against legislative predominance.

The amendment deliberately discarded a check that the framers had designed specifically to counteract the natural tendency of the legislative branch to dominate the other departments and to absorb the residual powers of the states.

In short, the Seventeenth Amendment did not merely alter the method of choosing senators. It altered the internal balance Madison regarded as indispensable to keeping a republican legislature from becoming the predominant, and potentially oppressive, branch of government.

He is up against our constitution. Our constitution is like anti-communism pill. And even if Mamdani did take property he is constitutionally obligated to pay the owner just compensation. If this went to the Supreme Court the owner would win. 

 In the United States, protection of private property is deeply embedded in the Constitution, although it is not absolute.

The strongest protection comes from the Fifth Amendment, which states:

“…nor shall private property be taken for public use, without just compensation.”

This is known as the Takings Clause.

It means the government generally cannot simply seize your property and keep it. If it takes property for a public purpose—such as a highway, dam, military base, or utility project—it must provide “just compensation,” usually fair market value.

A few key protections:

Public Use Requirement
The government must have a legitimate public purpose.

The definition of “public use” has been interpreted broadly by courts.
Just Compensation

If the government takes property, it must pay for it.

Owners can challenge the amount offered.

The owner is gets “Due Process”

The Fifth Amendment (federal government) and Fourteenth Amendment (state governments) require due process before deprivation of property.

The government generally must follow legal procedures and provide an opportunity to contest the action.
Regulatory Takings

Sometimes the government doesn’t physically seize land but regulates it so heavily that it loses much of its value. This is happening in New York. They rent control, Landlord can’t afford to renovate,  Mamdani thinks he can just take your home. 

Courts have held that some regulations can become a “taking” requiring compensation. In other words. Rent control, then taking the property means the owner is owed compensation. 

From a philosophical perspective, the Founders generally viewed property rights as one of the fundamental liberties government exists to protect. James Madison wrote extensively that protection of property was a central purpose of government.

So the short answer is: No, the government cannot ordinarily just take your property. The Constitution requires legal authority, a public purpose, due process, and usually compensation. The real legal battles tend to be over what counts as a public purpose, whether a regulation goes too far, and what compensation is actually fair.

text:
Everyone in this industry is trying to lock clients in for longer.

Back in January I spent a month with Brian Dukes training his team to fire me. He'd just done $2M from LinkedIn. I couldn't be happier. Here's exactly how we did it:

Brian runs an M&A consultancy in Michigan called Exitwise, helping founders scale and exit.

When we met he had been through 7 vendors. He was done with it, and I didn't blame him.

He told me: "none of them had an audience themselves. I'm a firm believer you've got to be a practitioner to prove you can do the thing."

He also had under 5,000 followers, which everyone treats as the problem.

It never was.

Two years on, Brian puts the revenue he can attribute to it at $2M to $4M.

1) The offer.

Everyone in M&A looks the same. Bankers with a reputation for selling founder clients down the river, far below what those businesses are worth.

We repositioned him founders-for-founders and moved him to pay on a successful exit. Now he sold the outcome his buyers lie awake about, and only got paid when it happened.

In 3 months that took him from zero inbound off his posts to 4-6 qualified calls a month. Founders in the $2-4 million EBITDA range, looking to sell.

Catching those founders at the exact moment they consider a sale is like finding a needle in a haystack.

2) The positioning.

We wrote down what is broken in his industry and why. That became the lens for every post, every DM, every call.

Bankers became the enemy. Exitwise became the advisor in the founder's corner, there to answer two questions. Are you even ready to sell? And can we get 15% above what a banker-owned shop would?

3) The content system.

Five posts a week on two hours of his time a month.

Reach posts to get in front of founders. Authority posts to prove he could think. In-depth playbooks on the sale process, because his LTV justified it.

Then sales posts to make the ask. Most people run one of the three and wonder why content never turns into money.

4) Warm outbound.

Like most founders, Brian never had time to connect his content to his outbound. Let alone how to move a chat to a call.

We went after the people already engaging with his posts, opened real conversations, and moved the right ones to a call.

That added another 3-4 calls a month, and a $300K deal inside 6 months.

5) The ecosystem.

A newsletter adding roughly 100 subscribers a week, and a valuation calculator so founders got something useful out of him before booking a call.

Then we handed the whole thing over. His team runs it in-house now, without me.

That is the job.

Doing everything for people builds dependency, not capability.

So here is the Monday morning test. If you fired your agency today, could your team run your LinkedIn on Monday?

If not, after two years and whatever you paid, you didn't buy a system. You bought a subscription.

Brian and I recorded a 60 minute breakdown of the build: https://t.co/JOtJ9Bq16k
