text:
The January 2026 market provides an important warning against assuming Venezuelan barrels will always be the cheapest. Merey-16 was offered to Gulf Coast refiners at approximately a $6/bbl discount to Brent, while WCS delivered in Houston traded at approximately a $12.50/bbl discount. WCS was therefore substantially more attractive before accounting for refinery-specific quality and yield. Increased Venezuelan availability is beneficial only if cargoes are priced competitively. A destination guarantee to the U.S. does not itself guarantee a below-market transfer price. 

Direct contracting can change where the economic rent accrues. PDVSA has been moving from trader-dominated sales toward direct contracts with refiners and joint-venture partners, partly to obtain better prices and reduce intermediary margins. This may improve transparency and reliability for PADD 3 refiners but could also transfer trading margin back to PDVSA or the upstream operator. PSX began direct purchases in May, VLO was expected to begin direct buying, and DOE has listed XOM, MPC, PSX and VLO among U.S. importers. The companies are therefore already participating before execution of the new field agreements. 

Additional Venezuelan crude can also displace high-sulfur residual fuel oil that some Gulf Coast refiners have been buying as secondary-unit feedstock during periods of heavy-crude scarcity. Residual fuel can be upgraded in cokers, but it is generally a less complete feedstock than crude because valuable atmospheric products have already been removed. Replacing imported fuel oil with competitively priced Venezuelan crude can improve crude-unit utilization, product integration and overall refinery optimization. 

The strategic benefit is therefore optionality rather than dependence. A Gulf Coast refiner with access to Venezuela, Canada, Mexico, Colombia, the Middle East and domestic grades can continually select the highest netback crude. The largest value may arise not from maximizing Venezuelan throughput but from using Venezuelan offers to improve the purchase price of every competing heavy barrel.

GASOLINE AND PRODUCT-PRICE IMPLICATIONS

A rapid and substantial decline in U.S. gasoline prices is not the base-case near-term outcome. Existing Venezuelan production is already being exported, and a geographic redirection toward the U.S. does not materially alter the global crude balance. PADD 3 also has limited spare crude-unit capacity. The first-order effect of cheaper feedstock is therefore higher refinery capture rather than sharply higher gasoline production.

Retail gasoline reflects crude prices, refinery cracks, blending economics, inventories, distribution costs, seasonal specifications, taxes and local market conditions. Venezuelan extra-heavy crude is not a direct gallon-for-gallon gasoline addition. It produces a large residual fraction that must be converted in cokers and hydroprocessing units, consuming hydrogen and energy. The resulting product yield depends on the specific crude assay and refinery configuration.

The gasoline-price case becomes more credible if Venezuelan output increases by several hundred thousand barrels per day on a sustained basis. Incremental production would add to Atlantic Basin crude supply, pressure global heavy and medium-sour prices and potentially reduce Brent and WTI at the margin. The magnitude would depend on contemporaneous OPEC policy, geopolitical outages, global demand and inventories. A 100kb/d increase is immaterial relative to the global market. An eventual 1mb/d increase is material but remains a multi-year outcome.

There is also a long-term offset for refiners. Rehabilitation of Venezuelan refineries could eventually increase Venezuelan gasoline, diesel and fuel-oil exports into the Atlantic Basin. Higher product supply would compress Gulf Coast cracks, particularly if global refinery capacity is no longer constrained. The sequence is therefore favorable to U.S. refiners initially: crude supply and heavy discounts improve before Venezuelan product exports recover. Over a longer horizon, part of the feedstock benefit could be competed away through lower product margins.

VALERO ENERGY

VLO has the strongest direct physical exposure and the cleanest equity sensitivity among the 4 companies. Its Gulf Coast system processed approximately 1.829mb/d in Q2 2026 and generated approximately $2.893bn of adjusted refining operating income. Across the company, adjusted refining operating income was approximately $4.4bn on 3.0mb/d of throughput. The Gulf Coast accounted for the majority of refining earnings, making changes in Gulf Coast crude differentials highly relevant to consolidated cash flow. 

VLO’s relevant assets include Port Arthur, St. Charles, Corpus Christi, Houston, Texas City, Meraux and other Gulf Coast facilities with varying degrees of sour, residual and heavy-crude capability. The company has specifically described its ability to process high volumes of Venezuelan heavy, high-acid crude as a competitive advantage. Management stated that VLO has historically been the largest U.S. consumer of Venezuelan crude and expects processing in coming months to exceed its previous historical maximum. 

VLO processed approximately 536kb/d of heavy sour crude during 2025. Applied mechanically to that slate, every $1/bbl of sustainable improvement in heavy-sour feedstock economics represents approximately $196m of annual gross margin. A $3/bbl improvement would represent approximately $587m, and a $5/bbl improvement approximately $978m. These calculations are not earnings guidance and assume an unrealistic 100% pass-through across the full heavy-sour slate. Actual capture would be reduced by crude substitution, quality differences, hedging, inventory timing, product yields, higher hydrogen and catalyst costs and competitive pricing. They nevertheless illustrate the materiality of heavy-crude differentials to VLO. 

VLO’s benefit does not require an upstream investment in Venezuela. It can capture additional supply and wider competing-grade discounts while leaving field-development capital, political risk and reserve uncertainty with producers. This asymmetric exposure is attractive. If VLO is granted direct long-term offtake, preferential loading or a field-level marketing role, procurement reliability and intermediary-margin capture could provide additional value. If it receives only market-priced cargoes, the benefit will primarily occur through broader differential pressure.

The principal VLO risks are cargo overpricing, unstable quality, corrosion and maintenance burden, terminal delays, inability to secure loading slots, and eventual compression of product cracks. VLO also has the greatest refining purity, so the same operating leverage that creates upside from wider heavy discounts creates downside if global product margins normalize. The transaction is therefore a strong positive catalyst for relative crude-slate economics, not a guarantee of higher absolute refining margins through the full cycle.

MARATHON PETROLEUM

MPC has enormous physical capacity to benefit but is more agnostic regarding the source of the heavy barrel. Galveston Bay and Garyville have operable capacities of approximately 631kb/d and 617kb/d, respectively, for a combined 1.248mb/d. MPC’s Gulf Coast system ran at 100% utilization in Q2 2026 and generated approximately $27/bbl of adjusted EBITDA, with crude optimization identified as a major contributor. Systemwide R&M adjusted EBITDA was approximately $6.7bn on 2.9mb/d of throughput at 94% utilization. 

MPC processed more than 2x as much Venezuelan crude in Q2 as in Q1 while simultaneously running record volumes of Canadian heavy crude on the Gulf Coast. This demonstrates that the assets can accept Venezuelan barrels without abandoning WCS. It also confirms that the purchasing response had begun before the new announcement. 

Management’s statement that Canadian heavy wins the economic comparison with Venezuelan crude approximately 8 of 10 times is critical. MPC should not be viewed as a simple Venezuelan-volume beneficiary. The core advantage is the ability to arbitrage between WCS and Venezuelan crude at Garyville and Galveston Bay. Additional Venezuelan supply forces both grades to compete, improving MPC’s negotiating position regardless of which barrel is ultimately processed. Management explicitly indicated that greater Venezuelan availability should pressure WCS pricing. 

MPC may therefore receive a larger indirect benefit through Canadian differentials than through direct Venezuelan throughput. A Venezuelan cargo delivered at an insufficient discount can be rejected in favor of WCS. The rejected barrel still contributes to market competition and can push WCS wider. This dynamic is particularly valuable because MPC has one of the largest Canadian crude appetites in the U.S. and substantial logistics connectivity.

Garyville is especially relevant because of its scale, waterborne access and high conversion capability. Galveston Bay provides similar crude-slate flexibility and direct marine access. A mechanical $1/bbl benefit across the full 1.248mb/d combined capacity would equal approximately $456m annually, but this is not an appropriate earnings sensitivity because only a portion of throughput is heavy crude and capture varies materially by grade and unit configuration. The calculation is best viewed as an upper-bound illustration of system scale.

MPC’s equity sensitivity is diluted by its large MPLX ownership and broader value chain, which reduces pure refining beta but supports cash-flow stability. The transaction is clearly positive for MPC’s commercial optimization platform. It is less likely to produce a uniquely differentiated advantage because MPC will continue to select WCS whenever Canadian economics are superior.

PHILLIPS 66

PSX has the clearest disclosed quantitative sensitivity to the secondary market effect. Management stated that structurally increasing heavy supply from Canada and Venezuela should widen WTI-WCS differentials and that every $1/bbl widening in the WTI-WCS spread adds approximately $140m to annual EBITDA. A $3/bbl widening would therefore imply approximately $420m of annual EBITDA under a linear, all-else-equal scenario, while a $5/bbl widening would imply approximately $700m. These are mechanical applications of management’s sensitivity, not forecasts, and actual results would be influenced by throughput, turnarounds, hedging, crude location, freight, product margins and operating performance. 

PSX also has direct Venezuelan processing capability. Management has stated that Lake Charles and Sweeny can process a combined couple hundred thousand barrels per day of Venezuelan crude. The company began buying direct PDVSA cargoes in May and was allocated multiple Merey-16 cargoes for July loading. This creates direct feedstock exposure in addition to the WCS differential benefit. 

PSX is well positioned to capture commercial and logistics margins because it combines refining, crude procurement, marine access, pipelines, storage and trading. A controlled U.S.-Venezuela corridor involving southbound diluent and northbound heavy crude can generate value beyond the refining margin. Direct contracting can also reduce reliance on traders, improve crude-assay visibility and secure loading priority.

The company’s Q2 2026 realized refining margin was approximately $24.08/bbl, crude capacity utilization was 96%, and refining adjusted pre-tax income was approximately $3.086bn. These figures indicate high current operating leverage. The incremental Venezuelan benefit is therefore meaningful but should be evaluated against a strong existing margin environment rather than against trough earnings. 

PSX’s advantages are partly offset by lower equity purity than VLO. Midstream, chemicals, marketing and renewable fuels can dampen the stock’s sensitivity to refining differentials. Net debt was approximately $16.5bn at the end of Q2, making cash allocation and deleveraging relevant to the equity response. Nevertheless, PSX may have the most attractive combination of direct Venezuelan intake, WCS differential exposure and logistics optionality.

EXXON MOBIL

XOM has substantial Gulf Coast refining exposure through Baton Rouge, Baytown and Beaumont, with respective crude capacities of approximately 523kb/d, 565kb/d and 612kb/d. Combined PADD 3 crude capacity is approximately 1.7mb/d. Baytown and Baton Rouge have substantial integration and conversion capability and can benefit from additional sour and heavy feedstocks. DOE has listed XOM as a U.S. importer of Venezuelan oil, confirming that the company is already capable of participating in the trade. 

The full 1.7mb/d should not be treated as Venezuelan-capable incremental demand. Beaumont’s 250kb/d expansion was specifically designed around Permian crude and connected to Exxon’s Permian pipeline system. That new train is principally a light-crude optimization asset, although other parts of Beaumont’s legacy configuration can process broader feedstocks. Baytown and Baton Rouge are more relevant to the Venezuelan thesis than assuming the entire Beaumont system can pivot to extra-heavy crude. 

XOM’s downstream operations benefit from wider heavy discounts in the same manner as VLO, MPC and PSX. The consolidated equity effect is less straightforward because XOM is a major upstream producer. A sustained increase in Venezuelan supply that lowers global oil prices would reduce upstream realizations while increasing downstream feedstock margins. Given the relative scale of XOM’s upstream business, the negative crude-price effect can offset or exceed the refinery benefit.

A field award would change the analysis. Access to large Venezuelan resources on favorable fiscal terms could create substantial long-duration upstream option value. However, no public field allocation to XOM has been disclosed, and XOM is absent from the current General License 50C operator annex. XOM’s historical Venezuelan assets were expropriated, increasing the importance of contractual protections, legacy-claim treatment, international arbitration, payment security and political-risk returns. 

No Venezuelan reserves should be attributed to XOM’s valuation until a field award, economic entitlement, development plan and SEC-compliant reserve basis are disclosed. Even then, a high country-risk discount and substantial capital requirement would be appropriate. Near-term XOM exposure is best characterized as a modest downstream positive, a potential upstream option and a partial upstream commodity-price hedge against the benefits accruing to pure refiners.

RELATIVE COMPANY CONCLUSIONS

VLO is the cleanest direct beneficiary. Its system is physically suited to Venezuelan high-acid heavy crude, it has historically been the largest U.S. processor, management expects volumes above prior maximums, and the company’s earnings are highly concentrated in refining. The primary risk is that the market capitalizes the heavy-differential benefit before sustained discounts are visible or that stronger crude availability is offset by weaker product cracks.

PSX is the strongest quantified differential beneficiary. The disclosed $140m annual EBITDA sensitivity for every $1/bbl widening in WTI-WCS provides a direct framework for estimating indirect Venezuelan impact. Its direct intake capability and logistics platform add further upside. VLO likely has greater pure physical exposure, while PSX may have greater transparent sensitivity to the broader heavy-crude repricing.

MPC is a substantial but more balanced beneficiary. Its 2 major Gulf Coast refineries provide enormous scale and flexibility, but management’s explicit preference for Canadian heavy in most comparisons means the investment thesis is crude optimization rather than Venezuelan dependence. The new supply is favorable because it increases competition and widens the opportunity set.

XOM is the least pure near-term refiner expression. Its large Gulf Coast system benefits, but the effect is diluted by corporate scale and offset by upstream oil-price exposure. A future upstream award could be highly valuable, but current public licensing and contract disclosures do not support assigning that value.

The relative near-term ranking is therefore VLO and PSX as the highest-conviction beneficiaries, MPC as a meaningful but less differentiated beneficiary, and XOM as a mixed integrated exposure. VLO marginally leads on direct refining purity. PSX may outperform if the principal market effect is a material widening of WCS rather than a large direct Venezuelan processing increase.

SCENARIO ANALYSIS

Under an execution-light scenario, the agreement formalizes current flows but fails to resolve port, power and field constraints. U.S. imports remain near 700-900kb/d, Venezuelan national production increases only modestly, and most of the effect is redistribution from non-U.S. buyers. VLO, MPC and PSX receive a modest positive through crude optionality and direct procurement, while the effect on Brent, WTI and gasoline prices is limited. This scenario is plausible because current U.S. imports are already near the pre-2019 level and export terminals are operating near their practical ceiling.

Under an operational-recovery scenario, field workovers, diluent availability, improved payment security and infrastructure repairs add approximately 300-800kb/d over several years. Venezuelan crude competes aggressively with WCS, Maya and Atlantic Basin sour grades. PADD 3 refiners capture wider heavy discounts, with VLO and PSX showing the strongest relative earnings benefit. Canadian heavy producers face lower netbacks, while Mid-Continent and Gulf Coast refiners with WCS exposure benefit. Global crude prices experience some downward pressure, but the effect remains dependent on OPEC, geopolitical outages and demand.

Under a transformational-development scenario, the legal framework survives political transitions, approximately $100bn of capital is deployed, major Orinoco projects are sanctioned and Venezuelan production moves toward 2-3mb/d over 5-10 years. This would become material to the global crude balance. Pure refiners would initially benefit from abundant heavy crude but could later face lower product cracks as global refining and Venezuelan product output adjust. XOM’s integrated upstream offset would become more significant unless it receives attractive Venezuelan field interests.

Under a failure scenario, Venezuelan courts or political actors challenge the contracts, OFAC permissions are reversed, companies dispute fiscal terms, ports remain constrained, payments are delayed or a future government repudiates the framework. Current imports could decline rapidly, heavy crude differentials would tighten and PADD 3 refiners would return to WCS, Maya, Middle Eastern heavy and residual fuel. VLO would have the highest direct negative exposure to a reversal, while XOM would be least affected on a consolidated basis.

KEY ISSUES THAT DETERMINE INVESTMENT VALUE

The next field-level disclosures are more important than the 65bn-barrel headline. The critical variables are the identity and location of the 17 fields; independently audited reserves; current production and decline rates; operator and working-interest allocations; cost-recovery priority; royalty and tax terms; domestic-market obligations; export and pricing rights; capital commitments; control of diluent, terminals and blending; treatment of environmental and abandonment liabilities; dispute venues; sanctions-snapback protection; legacy creditor rights; and the ability to book reserves.

Crude pricing is the most important near-term observable for VLO, MPC and PSX. The relevant indicators are Merey-16 delivered Gulf Coast relative to Brent, WCS Houston and Hardisty differentials, Maya pricing, medium-sour benchmarks, tanker demurrage, diluent cost, crude quality and refinery yield. Rising Venezuelan volume with a narrowing discount may provide less refiner value than flat volume with a sharply wider discount.

Loading reliability is equally important. Export data above 1.25mb/d, shorter tanker waits, improved Jose throughput and lower demurrage would signal that physical bottlenecks are being removed. Production headlines without corresponding export improvement should not be capitalized into refinery earnings.

The identity of field operators will determine whether the announcement creates upstream value for XOM or remains principally a CVX, Shell, BP, Eni, Repsol and oilfield-services event. Addition of XOM to a public OFAC operator license, disclosure of an XOM production-sharing contract or a formal field tender award would materially alter the current assessment.

For VLO, MPC and PSX, disclosure of long-term purchase agreements, preferential offtake rights, direct-loading allocations or equity participation would represent a stronger catalyst than generic statements about U.S. control. A refiner purchasing market-priced crude captures only the differential benefit. A refiner with preferential offtake, blending or marketing rights can capture additional upstream, logistics and trading margin.

BOTTOM LINE

The announcement materially improves the strategic outlook for heavy-crude availability in PADD 3, but it does not create 65bn barrels of immediately available U.S. oil, does not transfer those reserves onto refiner balance sheets and does not guarantee an imminent collapse in gasoline prices. The most probable near-term outcome is an institutionalized Venezuela-U.S. crude corridor that increases competition among heavy grades and shifts economic value toward complex Gulf Coast refiners.

The immediate physical impact is smaller than the headline because Venezuelan flows to the U.S. have already risen to approximately 786kb/d, close to the approximately 800kb/d processed before sanctions. The incremental catalyst is durability, direct contracting, improved payment security, lower intermediary dependence and the prospect of future production growth. The short-term global supply effect is limited unless output rises rather than cargoes merely being redirected.

VLO is the clearest direct beneficiary because of its heavy, high-acid capability, Gulf Coast earnings concentration and stated intention to exceed historical Venezuelan processing levels. PSX is an equally compelling expression where the dominant effect is wider WTI-WCS differentials, supported by its disclosed $140m annual EBITDA sensitivity for every $1/bbl widening. MPC benefits substantially through Garyville, Galveston Bay and its large WCS position, but its procurement strategy remains disciplined and Canadian heavy frequently offers superior economics. XOM benefits downstream but has the least pure equity sensitivity because of integrated upstream exposure, Permian-oriented Beaumont capacity and the absence of a publicly disclosed Venezuelan operating authorization or field award.

The principal investment risk is not whether Venezuela possesses the resource. The resource is established. The decisive risk is whether legally durable contracts, commercially competitive crude pricing, functioning infrastructure and secure capital recovery can convert the resource into reliable production. Until those conditions are demonstrated, the transaction should be capitalized primarily as a positive heavy-crude differential and procurement-optional­ity catalyst for VLO, PSX and MPC, with only limited value assigned to the 65bn-barrel reserve headline itself.

text:
DT: I think it’s pretty clear that they’ll keep five defensive tackles, the only question is who earns that fifth spot.

I know we’ve heard positive things about Jonathan Bullard and Tommy Dunn, but at the end of the day, I think Jay Toia takes it. Bullard will likely begin the season on IR, while Dunn should make his way onto the practice squad.

OLB/EDGE: I don’t see a scenario where they don’t keep six players here, especially with how this defense will be schemed and the uncertainty that still exists within the group.

That doesn’t mean I doubt their talent, but Gary and Miller are the only truly proven players in the room. Gary has experienced some ups and downs throughout his career, while Miller is now 37 years old.
With that being said, I think this group will surprise a lot of people and become an absolute sack-machine unit.

As I’ve preached all year, Liufau is not battling for the sixth spot. He will make this team because of his versatility, special teams value and the draft capital Dallas invested in him.

The final decision comes down to James Houston or Sam Williams. I’m going with Williams because he offers more special-teams value, and I believe Dallas will try to move Houston in a trade.

ILB: I think this group is pretty self explanatory. These are your four best inside linebackers.

Justin Barron made a strong push this offseason, but I think one more year on the practice squad could do wonders for his development. That’s assuming the Rams don’t come in and claim him (which I think is a very realistic possibility.)

CB: I know this prediction will shock a lot of people, but these are currently the only three game ready boundary cornerbacks on the roster.

I don’t trust anyone else enough right now. Carson appears to have lost his confidence, Devin Moore is still extremely raw, and while I like Trikweze Bridges I don’t see him making the team. Ameer Speed has been a pleasant surprise but he’s most likely headed for the practice squad. As for Josh Butler, I haven’t heard anything about him all year.

NB: This helps explain my reasoning at cornerback. Because Dallas is thin on the boundary, I think they’ll keep extra depth at nickel.

Derion Kendrick and Reddy Steward are easily the next best cornerbacks on the roster. Steward also brings tremendous versatility and communication skills and deserves to make this team.

S: Finally, I think we’ve all had the safety room figured out for at least a week especially after Schotty basically stood on the table for Markquese Bell.
I don’t mind that decision. Bell offers outstanding versatility near the line of scrimmage, which I’d like to see utilized more in this new scheme, and he brings legitimate special teams value.

The only player who was truly pushing Bell for that spot was Julius Wood. I’m a BIG fan of Wood and I think he is a better pure safety than Bell. However his concussion could allow Dallas to place him on IR and keep him around without immediately using an active roster spot.

text:
In 2015, Courtney Holmes, a barber at Spark Family Hair Salon in Dubuque, Iowa, came up with a special way to help children enjoy reading.

During the city’s second annual Back to School Bash at Comiskey Park on August 8, Courtney offered free haircuts to children who would read books aloud to him. The event was organized in part by the Dubuque Black Men Coalition.

Courtney wanted the children to see reading as something fun, not something they had to be forced to do. He welcomed them to choose a book they liked and then read it to him while they waited for their haircut.

He explained, “The kids would come in, and I would say, ‘Go to the table and get a book you might like, and if you can't read it, I'll help you understand and we can read it together.’”

Courtney called his idea “Tales 4 Trims.” What started at the Back to School Bash soon became a regular program at his salon.

After a child finished reading, Courtney would ask questions about the book to see what they had learned. He also gave the children books to take home so they could continue reading.

His simple idea soon received attention beyond Dubuque. Similar programs that combined haircuts and reading were later started in places including Ypsilanti, Michigan, Houston, and Columbus, Ohio.

Courtney showed that something as simple as a haircut could become an opportunity to encourage children to read, learn, and take books home with them.

text:
USA. A state fair in Iowa. I watched a man pay four dollars and receive a fried cookie on a stick.

Fried. Cookie. On a stick.

I asked the vendor to confirm what I was seeing.

"Deep-fried Oreo, man. Want six?"

Six. He offered six as the default.

In my country, oil is a discipline. Tempura is restraint made edible. A thin robe, a brief bath, out. The oil serves the food.

Here, the oil has ambitions.

I walked the fairgrounds and recorded what this nation has fried. Cookies. Butter. Butter, fried, as a dish, on purpose. And then a stall that fried Coca-Cola, which is a liquid, which means that somewhere an American looked at a beverage and said: it can be done.

I tried it. I will not be writing home about this one. My ancestors already doubt my letters, and fried Coca-Cola would finish me. Struck from the family scrolls. Over a beverage.

This is a nation so rich in joy that it ran out of solid foods to celebrate, and kept going.

"You want powdered sugar on that?" the woman asked.

There is no version of that question that ends in no.

Before the fried butter, I assumed a stance. A woman beside me said, "Honey, it's just butter."

It was not just butter. Nothing that requires a stance is just anything. She patted my armor twice, the way you calm a horse, and went on with her day.

It tasted like a holiday that should not exist, and does, every August.

By late afternoon I was on a bench, holding a funnel cake I do not remember purchasing. My armor no longer closes at the third clasp. A passing farmer looked at me with the softness of a man who had seen this before.

"First fair, buddy?"

Nothing here is safe from the oil.

In my land we fry to preserve a thing's true shape. Here they fry to set it free.

I know this nation's true border now. It is not land or sea. Everything in this world divides in two: that which has been fried, and that which Iowa has not gotten to yet.

Next year I will eat one vegetable before entering the gates. I checked the menu. It is a fried pickle.

I have already ordered six.

Melting Arctic ice directly affects India’s monsoons and contributes to storms, cyclones and other extreme weather.
India already has a substantial Antarctic presence (around 45 expeditions and the Maitri research station).
Both regions form part of the cryosphere (the frozen part of Earth’s surface holding ~70% of the planet’s water). Climate-driven melting creates climate-related threats for India while also opening new opportunities, such as shorter sea routes. For Example already realised, the Chennai–Vladivostok route has cut transit time from about 40 days to 24 days. Further Arctic route openings could offer similar gains.
India is an observer in the Arctic Council, an original signatory of the 1920 Svalbard Treaty (giving certain rights), and conducted its first Arctic exploration in 2007.

text:
America has been engaged in arguments over what the extent of federal authority should be for a very long time.

The Kentucky and Virginia Resolutions offer a glimpse into what those contentions looked like during the nation's early years, when Americans were still figuring out what the Constitution really meant, and what the balance between the states and the new federal government should really look like. 

Two of the most important figures of the founding generation, Thomas Jefferson and James Madison, were attempting to confront a problem that they knew could have tremendous consequences. 

Their arguments draw attention to the necessity of preventing a government from becoming more powerful than the people it was created to serve.

text:
UCLA’s football history features transformative coaches who elevated the Bruins through sustained excellence,

Henry Russell “Red” Sanders coached UCLA from 1949 to 1957, compiling a 66-19-1 record (.773 winning percentage)—still the highest in school history. He guided the Bruins to three Pacific Coast Conference championships (1953–1955), two Rose Bowl appearances, and a 6-3 mark against rival USC. In 1954, his undefeated 9-0 team claimed the Coaches Poll national championship (sharing recognition in some systems with Ohio State), leading the nation in both scoring offense and defense while outscoring opponents 367-40. Sanders also redesigned the uniforms, introducing the distinctive lighter “powder-keg blue,” shoulder stripes, and number styles that became iconic. His teams finished ranked in the top 10 multiple times, and he was later inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame.

Dick Vermeil served as head coach for just two seasons (1974–1975), posting a 15-5-3 record (.717). In 1975 he directed the Bruins to a shared Pacific-8 Conference title and a 9-2-1 overall mark, culminating in a signature 23-10 Rose Bowl victory over previously undefeated, No. 1-ranked Ohio State. That win denied the Buckeyes a clear national championship path and marked UCLA’s first conference title in a decade. Vermeil’s rapid success propelled him to the NFL, where he later earned Pro Football Hall of Fame induction after Super Bowl and multiple playoff achievements.

Terry Donahue, a former UCLA player, took over in 1976 and coached through 1995, amassing a school-record 151-74-8 mark (.665) and a conference-record 98 Pac-10 victories. His Bruins captured or shared five Pac-10 championships, appeared in 13 bowl games (8-4-1 record), and played in four Rose Bowls, winning three (1983, 1984, and 1986). Donahue became the first coach to win bowl games in seven consecutive seasons and produced multiple Top-10 finishes, 34 first-team All-Americans, and numerous NFL draft selections (including first-rounders). He remains the only person to win a Rose Bowl as a UCLA player, assistant, and head coach. Donahue was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame and other halls of honor; the Rose Bowl press box bears his name. 

These coaches delivered UCLA’s sole national title, multiple conference crowns, and a tradition of Rose Bowl excellence while building lasting program identity.

Bob Chesney, hired in December 2025 as UCLA’s 20th head coach, arrives with a proven record of building winners at every level. His career head-coaching mark exceeds 130 wins against roughly 50 losses, spanning Division III (Salve Regina), Division II (Assumption), FCS (Holy Cross, where he won multiple Patriot League titles and made playoff runs), and FBS (James Madison). In two seasons at JMU he went 21-5 (or 21-6 including postseason), secured an undefeated conference record and the program’s first Sun Belt title in 2025, earned Coach of the Year honors, and guided the Dukes into the College Football Playoff. 

Chesney’s consistent ability to elevate programs—through disciplined culture, situational preparation, player development, and conference dominance—positions him well at UCLA. The Bruins offer elite recruiting access in Southern California, Big Ten resources and visibility, strong academic standing, and a passionate fan base at the Rose Bowl. His track record of rapid turnarounds and championship contention at ascending levels suggests he can restore sustained excellence, compete for Big Ten titles, and position UCLA for College Football Playoff success. With institutional commitment to a championship standard and Chesney’s demonstrated formula for building winners, a national championship represents a realistic long-term outcome for the program under his leadership.

text:
Colorful Songs: Nights in White Satin

This is one of those songs that truly defined the 60s. However, even though it was released in 1967, it didn't become a major hit until 1972 when it was re-released, just as the Moody Blues were breaking up. Also, it didn't feature the band's original members. Yes, just like yesterday's focus on Stevie Nicks and Fleetwood Mac, the Moody Blues were a band that was floundering until the addition of a pair of singer/songwriters revitalized things, making the Moody Blues international stars.

The Moody Blues were formed as a straightforward British beat band in Birmingham in 1964. It all started in 1958 when a rock band called El Riot & the Rebels got together, featuring Ray Thomas as vocals, harmonica, flute, and saxophone, and John Lodge as bass (remember that name). They were joined by keyboardist Mike Pinder in 1963, who'd just completed his army duty (similar to how Bill Wyman joined the Rolling Stones around the same time). Other bands were playing in Birmingham around this time, including Danny King & the Dukes with bassist Clint Warwick, Denny & the Diplomats with Denny Laine and future Move/ELO drummer Bev Bevan, and Gerry Levine & the Avengers with drummer Graeme Edge and future Move/ELO/Wizzard guitarist Roy Wood. In 1963, Lodge left to go to college, so Thomas and Pinder recruited Edge, Warwick and Laine to form a new band called the Krew Kats, then M&B5 in an effort to get sponsored by a local Mitchells & Butlers Brewery. When that fell through, they settled on the Moody Blues taken from Duke Ellington's Mood Indigo. 

Signed to a contract with Decca Records, the band quickly released a cover of Bessie Banks's Go Now that climbed the charts to number one in the UK and 10 in the US, landing them on Ready Steady Go! However, the band couldn't come up with a popular follow up single, and quickly faded from memory. In 1966, Laine and Warwick left the band. So, Thomas recruited his old friend John Lodge to rejoin, and the Moody Blues added singer/songwriter/guitarist Justin Hayward on the recommendation of Eric Burdon of the Animals. Hayward had been playing guitar in Marty Wilde's band. With the new lineup, the Moody Blues chose to start work on a new record. At Decca, they met producer Tony Clarke who began to work with the Moodies, releasing a minor hit Fly Me High written by Hayward, followed up by Love and Beauty written by Pinder, which featured his newly acquired Mellotron. This helped cement the signature psychedelic sound of the Moody Blues.

The Moody Blues' contract with Decca was set to expire in late 1967, and they still owed the label several thousand pounds in advances. Rather than lose money, they took Decca's offer to record a rock version of Antonin Dvorak's New World Symphony to serve as a promotional record to be used by people selling Decca's new Deramic Stereo Sound equipment. Securing artistic control, the Moodies kept the idea of an orchestra supporting them, but then put together a song cycle of original tunes for a concept album centered on the life of a person. Days of Future Past included such songs as Dawn is a Feeling and Tuesday Afternoon. Nights in White Satin would close the album, followed by Graeme Edge's poem Late Lament, recited by Pinder. It would be a major hit, getting the Moody Blues out of their debt to Decca Records, and leading to six more hit albums for the band.

Nights in White Satin was written by Hayward when he was 19. He was on tour in Belgium and a girlfriend sent him a set of white satin bedsheets. When Hayward played it for Pinder, the keyboardist added the Mellotron flourishes, which were joined by Thomas's flute solo. The song also features Lodge on bass and Edge on drums, backed by the London Festival Orchestra. The version on the album ran for 5:38, so a cutdown single version was released in 1967 that ran for 3:05. It met with some success, but nothing could match the re-release in 1972, that ran for 4:26 and met with even bigger success in the US and Canada. The 1967 release got to one in Belgium and the Netherlands, but only hit 19 in the UK and 30 in Canada, while getting stuck at 103 in the US. Five years later, Nights in White Satin would top the charts in Canada, reaching 2 in the US and 9 in the UK.

Days of Future Past set the scene for the Moody Blues. They began making concept albums, such as In Search of the Lost Chord and A Question of Balance. The songs would often be built around a similar theme, with a number of them having later refrains (House of Four Doors and I Never Thought I'd Live to be 100), all bookended by poems written by Edge and recited by Pinder. 

While the band was fairly egalitarian with each member contributing songs, most of the hits were penned by Hayward and Lodge. By 1974, following the Seventh Sojourn, the five Moodies needed a break.  Pinder moved to LA to raise his family, Lodge and Hayward worked together and solo, while Thomas and Edge released solo albums that didn't sell well. In 1977, the Moody Blues got back together, but at Pinder's insistence, chose to record in LA. With their luck, though, the studio they started working in burned down, and when they moved to Pinder's home studio, landslides caused by torrential rains trapped the band for weeks. When Octave was released in 1978, Pinder had decided not to tour, effectively marking his departure from the band he had helped form. He was replaced by Patrick Moraz on keyboards, who would contend that he was a member of the Moody Blues, an issue that would wind up in litigation.

The third version of the Moody Blues would prove almost as successful as the second, releasing hits like Gemini Dream, The Voice and Your Wildest Dreams. The Moodies would continue to tour until 2018, but Ray Thomas left in 2002, passing away in 2018. Edge died in 2021, Pinder in 2024, and Lodge in 2025, leaving Justin Hayward the only remaining member of the Moody Blues, leaving behind a legacy of great music.

text:
For most of the 2010s I was a regular lecturer on economics and econ history at seminars and workshops for college students around the US. Most came from the free-market classical liberal/libertarian and conservative spaces. 

Around 2014 or 15 I started noticing that a small but vocal cohort of the students who showed up at these events were drifting into weird reactionary traditions associated with figures such as Thomas Carlyle. A smaller subset of those were into overtly fascist thinkers such as Carl Schmitt and Julius Evola. They almost always turned to these creeps as a backlash to campus "wokeness," but few if any had more than a superficial understanding of Carlyle, Evola, or Schmitt.

It was concerning enough that I started adding a lecture to my repertoire about Carlyle's dubious place in history, juxtaposing him with his contemporary Karl Marx. It also coincided with the 150th anniversary of the Eyre Controversy, which offered an opportunity to display some of the worst tendencies of Carlyle. A number of the students who entered into the seminars as Carlyle enthusiasts would come up afterward and say "I had no idea about that" and admit that they had only read a bit about him online (almost every time, it involved something mind-numbingly stupid that they read on Curtis Yarvin's blog). 

Unfortunately, not much else was done to dispel Carlyle at the time, who had become a neglected figure outside of academic specialties. And Evola and Schmitt were even more of an eccentric "niche," so there was little interest in even engaging them. 

It turns out that was a mistake. And a decade later, all three figures have very dark internet subcultures around them albeit with the same levels of superficiality. Unfortunately, they've also been boosted by Postliberal academics who moved into that space and proselytized these and similar cranks, crackpots, and bigots from the reactionary past as if they're suitable "conservative intellectual" alternatives to John Locke, James Madison, Adam Smith, and Edmund Burke.

And therein hangs a tale of the groyper-curious intern problem.

A 12th century chronicler criticises the Second Crusade;

"Because of our sins, God permitted the western Church to be afflicted. For there arose certain pseudo-prophets, sons of Belial, witnesses of the anti-Christ, who seduced Christians with foolish words, and with false preaching forced all the human race to march against the Saracens for the liberation of Jerusalem. Their preaching was so effective that almost all the inhabitants of these regions freely offered themselves to the common disaster, and not only ordinary men, but even kings, dukes, margraves and other powerful men of this world, thinking that they were taking up the service of God, with bishops, archbishops, abbots and other servants and prelates of the Church joining them in this error, acting in such a way that they placed both their souls and bodies in mortal danger. Nor is this to be wondered at since (I know not for what secret reason) the Lord Eugenius (Pope Eugene III), pontiff of the Roman See, persuaded into this by Abbot Bernard of Clairvaux, wrote to Conrad, the most pious king of the Romans and of the whole empire, to the kings of France and England, and indeed to all the kings of Christian faith and religion, and also to their great men and subjects, advising them in these letters to prepare for this journey"

text:
Ben Jones, Dukes of Hazzard star and former Congressman, dies at 84

Ben Jones, best known as the lovable mechanic Cooter Davenport on The Dukes of Hazzard, passed away Sunday at the age of 84.

His wife, Alma Viator, shared the news:

“I lost the love of my life today. Ben passed from a massive heart attack… He was home resting in his favorite chair waiting for the Braves to come on and whoop the Yankees. Ben had the most amazing rich full life. He loved and was loved by so many.”

Jones played Cooter across all seven seasons of the classic series (1979–1985) and later served two terms in the U.S. House of Representatives representing Georgia.

Co-star Tom Wopat (Luke Duke) remembered him warmly:

“Ben Jones was a fine friend and a fierce advocate of all the best things we can offer in the entertainment business… I feel like we lost a Duke cousin today.”

I grew up watching The Dukes of Hazzard. Cooter was a lovable character played perfectly by Jones. It was a smaller role, but he made it leave a big impression. Rest in peace, Cooter.

An Amazon drone delivery in Texas took an unexpected dive on Monday, dropping the customer's package into her pool.

Lindsey Austen, who lives in Richmond, Texas, received an alert on her phone that her scheduled package would be delivered via drone for the first time. She heard a whirring noise, then ran outside to record the novel delivery method. The greater Houston area began receiving Amazon Prime Air drone deliveries in May.

“When it went into the pool, I was shocked,” Austen said. “I don’t think I’ll be wanting any more drone deliveries.”

Amazon launched its Prime Air drone delivery service in 2022 and currently offers it in 11 U.S. metro areas, including Baton Rouge, Dallas, Detroit, Houston, Kansas City, Omaha, Phoenix, San Antonio, Tampa, and Waco.

Amazon announced Wednesday that it plans to expand Prime Air to 500 cities by the end of the year, with deliveries in some areas arriving in as little as 30 minutes.

He notes that signs of this development have appeared for some time and that he has previously reported on related developments. The discussion is not limited to Catholics associated with the Society of St. Pius X (SSPX). Official sources now explicitly identify the Priestly Fraternity of St. Peter (FSSP) as presenting a comparable problem. Stine frames the situation as a broader challenge directed at anyone attached to traditional liturgy and the pre-conciliar understanding of the Church.

1:02 MASSIMO FAGGIOLI’S COMMONWEAL ARTICLE ON SSPX AND POPE LEO

Stine turns to an article published in Commonweal magazine by Massimo Faggioli, whose name he pronounces carefully to avoid platform issues and whose surname roughly translates as “Max Beans.” The headline reads “SSPX and the Pope: Leo’s Forceful Response Shouldn’t Come as a Surprise.” Faggioli recapitulates the standard post-conciliar narrative of the SSPX, beginning in 1976, including the number of priests and the claim that the Society broke away from Rome. Stine disputes the accuracy of that breakaway characterization, noting that the original 1988 excommunications were invalid on their face.Faggioli continues through Traditionis Custodes and the 2022 document Desiderio Desideravi. He quotes the formal assertion that the Latin Mass, which developed organically from apostolic times and remained in force until the late 1960s, does not fit the ecclesiology of the post-Vatican II Church. Stine emphasizes that ecclesiology concerns the fundamental theology of the Church—its identity, mission, relationship to God and to man. When authorities declare that the traditional Mass is incompatible with post-conciliar ecclesiology, they are effectively stating that a new Church has emerged. There is, in Stine’s view, no other coherent interpretation.

When authorities declare that the traditional Mass is incompatible with post-conciliar ecclesiology, they are effectively stating that a new Church has emerged. There is, in Stine’s view, no other coherent interpretation.

2:54 LEO XIV TAKES UP THE CHALLENGE AFTER THE JULY 1 ORDINATIONS

Faggioli describes Pope Leo XIV as taking up the challenge posed by the SSPX. The Pope attempted through public appeals to persuade the Society to reverse its decision to ordain four new bishops, an act that risked renewing the 1988 situation and automatic excommunications. On July 1 the SSPX proceeded with the ordinations. Italian journalist Jacopo Scaramuzzi characterized the ceremony as “the traditionalist Woodstock—part Latin Mass, part TripAdvisor.” Faggioli concludes that there was never much room for negotiation because radical opposition to Vatican II and the post-conciliar magisterium constitutes the entire raison d’être of the SSPX. A twenty-eight-page profession of faith published by the Society on June 24, longer and more detailed than Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre’s 1974 declaration, confirms this stance.

Stine praises Faggioli for unusual honesty on this point. Many bishops have suggested that relaxing restrictions on the Latin Mass would draw people away from the SSPX. Stine counters that the deeper issue is not the liturgy alone but the changed ecclesiology, theology, and doctrines of the faith, together with the tolerance and occasional promotion of heresy even from the Holy See. The problem originates in Vatican II yet was fermenting long before the Council. Faggioli correctly states that the SSPX’s difficulty with the Council has never been merely liturgical; those who claim otherwise are willfully ignorant or intentionally dishonest. Stine agrees almost entirely, adding a third possibility: simple ignorance of the full scope of the changes.

5:31 ROME’S RAPID RESPONSE AND ITS IMPACT ON FSSP ARRANGEMENTS

Rome’s response to the July 1 ordinations arrived within twenty-four hours and included excommunication measures. Faggioli notes that this new approach affects the informal motus vivendi that some local bishops had established with the SSPX in their dioceses. The range of interpretive statements issued by bishops, especially in the United States, reflects this shift. Archbishop Paul Coakley of Oklahoma City, president of the USCCB, is cited as one example. The United States is described as one of the countries most affected.

Stine reports that people present at the consecrations who maintain good contacts inside the SSPX observed an effective transfer of focus from France to the United States. Bishop Michael Galarza (sometimes rendered Guldi or Gulady in the transcript) was the first to speak. Although one-third of SSPX members still come from France, the United States now supplies the largest contingent, hosts the Society’s largest seminary, and has the greatest number of seminarians. Galarza himself grew up in St. Mary’s, Kansas—site of the world’s largest SSPX church—was ordained at St. Thomas Aquinas Seminary in Winona, Minnesota, in 2004, and later served as prior in Kansas City.

7:14 THREE ASPECTS OF THE SSPX MATTER RELEVANT TO THE WIDER CHURCH

Faggioli identifies three aspects of particular relevance. The first is the reaction of Catholics in full communion with Rome—bishops, clergy, and theologians—who nonetheless support the SSPX or traditionalist Catholics on the liturgical question. Pressure is mounting on Pope Leo and the Vatican to concede more ground. The normalization of liturgical traditionalism is portrayed as a posthumous victory for Benedict XVI. Traditionalist communities are no longer a marginal group oscillating between crypto-Lefebvrism and orthodoxy. In Faggioli’s framing, traditional Catholicism is presented as something other than orthodox Catholicism.

He observes that for certain groups Catholicism is becoming attractive precisely because it is a minority phenomenon. It appeals to reactionary political-theological ideologues, addresses desires for spiritual intensity and charismatic experience, and offers a return to classic religious observance. At least in Europe the matter remains more ecclesial than political for the present, yet Faggioli warns that long-term denial of Vatican II would prove catastrophic for the political culture of Catholics. Stine highlights this as a striking admission: if the Vatican II project fails, the Church’s political standing in the world will suffer. Secular news outlets that comment knowledgeably on Vatican II should therefore alarm Catholics, because the Church’s contemporary focus is secular and political.

Some traditional groups now look beyond merely rolling back liturgical improvisations; they express a nostalgic desire to use doctrine and theology to undo the “inculturation” that began with Vatican II. Stine interprets this language as a euphemism for the secularization of the Church that followed Pope John XXIII’s call to open the windows to the modern world. Faggioli acknowledges that dealing with non-SSPX liturgical traditionalism will require pastoral and theological discernment, possibly differentiated solutions in different regions. A purely ritualized defense of Vatican II will not suffice. Conversely, any agnosticism toward or reversal of the liturgical reform would leave the rest of the Council untouched. In other words, restoration of the traditional Latin Mass threatens the entire Vatican II project—an assessment Stine considers accurate, because attendance at the traditional Mass regularly prompts questions about other post-conciliar developments.

10:40 THE “SCHISM” WAS NOT THE RESULT OF FAILED NEGOTIATIONS

The second point Faggioli makes is that the so-called schism did not stem from failed negotiations with the Holy See; he places responsibility on Benedict XVI. Joseph Ratzinger was one of the great theologians of Vatican II, yet the present moment, according to Faggioli, puts to rest the delusion that the liturgical question was the sole problem and that the pre-conciliar liturgy was the solution. Stine concurs that Leo’s forceful response should not surprise anyone. Unity is a dominant theme in the new Pope’s teaching, appearing already in the homily of his inaugural Mass: a united Church that becomes leaven for a reconciled world.

Leo XIV explained his choice of name by recalling Leo XIII and the development of social doctrine in response to industrial capitalism. Stine corrects the historical record: Rerum Novarum was not primarily about industrial capitalism; it also contained an unequivocal rejection of socialism as an erroneous response to the excesses of unregulated nineteenth-century capitalism. Faggioli offers another complementary explanation: Leo XIII, elected eight years after the loss of the Papal States, moved beyond Pius IX’s intransigent rejection of the Enlightenment, the French Revolution, liberal states, and rationalism, and beyond the 1864 Syllabus of Errors. In this light Leo XIV’s first encyclical on artificial intelligence can be read as a “counter-syllabus.” Stine notes the error in equating Leo XIII with later progressive currents; Leo XIII was an anti-modernist pope who issued numerous encyclicals on the Rosary and condemnations of modernist errors, even if the precise terminology of modernism was coined by his successor.

13:30 THE FORMAL FORMULA OF ADHERENCE AND THE IMPLIED WARNING

In recent decades the Vatican tolerated traditionalist criticism of Vatican II that extended beyond liturgy. Now, however, SSPX members who wish to return to communion must sign a formal formula of adherence acknowledging obedience to the Pope and the Catholic hierarchy as well as acceptance of all of Vatican II. Faggioli’s closing remark is the giveaway: “It would be interesting to see what would happen if every Catholic from the bishops to the lay faithful were asked to do the same.” Stine and other commentators treat this as a clear warning rather than a throwaway line.

14:00 REACTIONS AND THE APRIL ARTICLE BY MIKE LEWIS

Non Venenum Pacem responds that the time has come for cleaving: “What kind of document are you willing to sign? Are you ready to sign up for the post-conciliar Church?” Stine then revisits an April article by Mike Lewis at Where Peter Is that analyzes a La Croix report on the French bishops’ spring plenary assembly in Lourdes. According to La Croix sources, Pope Leo personally expressed to Cardinal Jean-Marc Aveline during the January consistory his wish that avenues be explored for resolving tensions surrounding the Tridentine liturgy. Leo is concerned about unity and asked the French episcopate to think the matter through. The Pellegrino letter formed part of that ongoing conversation.

Lewis, who supports the post-conciliar settlement, finds the most encouraging element to be the bishops’ agreement on the nature of the problem: it is not simply a matter of liturgical sensibilities. All the French bishops broadly share the same diagnosis—the traditional Mass is not in reality the central issue. Behind the liturgical question lie problems of doctrine and ecclesiology, specifically the question of acceptance of Vatican II. Bishop Olivier Degenne observed that it was the first time he had heard so clearly that the subject must be addressed at a theological level rather than merely in a pastoral or emotional way. This framing differs sharply from English-language outlets that treat the matter as one of access to a rite. The French bishops insist the deeper issue is whether communities attached to the older liturgy—including the FSSP—accept the authority of the Second Vatican Council and participate in the life of the local church.

That diagnosis is consistent with the 2020 survey synthesis that Francis used as justification for Traditionis Custodes, which described “two worlds that do not meet.” Stine notes the survey contained significant data problems; many bishops reported never receiving it. Nevertheless, the returns that arrived highlighted the refusal of full-communion traditional priests to concelebrate the Novus Ordo at diocesan Chrism Masses. Many such priests, when questioned privately about Vatican II and the new Mass, sound remarkably like SSPX clergy. The authorities know this and regard it as the core difficulty.

18:37 FRENCH BISHOPS’ TWO CAMPS AND THE ULTIMATE GOAL OF A SINGLE RITE

According to La Croix the French bishops fell into two camps: those who want Leo to uphold firmly the norms established by Francis, and those open to accommodations but only under strict conditions. Neither group calls for a rollback of Traditionis Custodes. There is general agreement on the ultimate goal of liturgical and ecclesial unity and alignment with Vatican II—meaning the new Mass is the one and the old Mass must ultimately disappear. The proposals of the more accommodating group go beyond Traditionis Custodes. Rather than simply restricting access, they require traditional communities to move closer to the reformed liturgy and make real concessions.

Specific conditions reported by La Croix include adoption of the readings and calendar of the reformed Missal (rendering the 1962 calendar obsolete and necessitating a new Missal), celebration of the other sacraments—baptism, marriage, confirmation—according to the new rite (Latin still permitted), resumption of direct diocesan oversight so that the FSSP loses its relative independence, and an end to the categorical refusal by priests to celebrate the reformed liturgy. The bishops label such refusal “exclusivism” and declare it unacceptable because it contradicts the mutual enrichment envisioned by Benedict XVI in Summorum Pontificum. One bishop lamented that young traditional priests possess great missionary zeal yet could help the dioceses only if they agreed to celebrate in both rites. Stine notes the parallel desire that young traditional laity attend both rites. The letter accompanying Traditionis Custodes itself stated that the goal is to bring traditional Catholics out of traditional Masses and into neighborhood parishes.

None of this constitutes a move toward liberalization or restoration of broad permissions. On the contrary, the proposals demand more of traditionalist communities than the current framework. The language of “generous inclusion” is paired with the expectation that traditionalist communities participate fully in the life of the local church rather than maintain parallel structures—language that effectively accuses them of schism. As Bishop Degenne put it, the ultimate goal is a single rite allowing everyone, whatever their sensibility, to coexist in common prayer. In short, the French bishops intend to “Vatican II up” the traditional Mass and will propose this model to the universal Church. Stine predicts the proposal will be accepted.

23:07 THE STATUS QUO IS UNSUSTAINABLE AND A CLARIFICATION IS EXPECTED

La Croix reports that the bishops recognize the status quo as unsustainable because Francis himself granted exemptions after issuing Traditionis Custodes; the motu proprio has become “difficult to apply.” A papal clarification is regarded as inevitable. Stine warns viewers not to be shocked if Cardinal Fernández or Archbishop Roche issues a clarification signed by Pope Leo that strips away remaining exceptions. By contrast, many United States bishops have denied the existence of theological and ecclesial problems within the traditionalist movement and sought exemptions. By inviting the French bishops to develop concrete proposals, Leo has given them a meaningful voice in shaping what comes next. The direction emerging from Lourdes looks nothing like the narrative constructed by English-language outlets.

24:40 SUPER CHAT AND THE FATE OF EASTERN RITES

A member super chat observes that the wheat is being separated from the chaff and that Rome’s colors are becoming clearer. In response to a question about Byzantine Catholics and other Eastern rites, Stine advises against complacency: signals already exist that authorities wish to “synodalize” the Eastern rites as well. They will eventually reach those communities.

25:19 DIVERGENT FSSP RESPONSES TO THE SSPX CONSECRATIONS

FSSP responses to the SSPX consecrations have not been uniform. Some parishes ignored the events and continued business as usual; others issued statements. One document posted by a traditional commentator is described as an “utterly vomitous” welcome package for SSPX attendees. It distinguishes between lay members of the SSPX Third Order, habitual participants who share doctrinal positions, and those who attend solely for liturgical or spiritual reasons while not rejecting the magisterium or the authority of the Pope. 

A series of self-examination questions is provided: Do I believe the Church has fallen away from being the authentic Church of Christ? Have I held that a pope was not a valid pope? Have I always considered the legitimate line of successors since Pius XII? Have I ever held the Novus Ordo English Mass invalid? Affirmative answers trigger a profession-of-faith process. Stine notes that the questions effectively conflate ordinary SSPX attendees with sedevacantists. Similar bulletins have appeared near the Immaculata in St. Mary’s, Kansas, and other locations. Some high-profile Catholic commentators may have altered public positions because they face uncomfortable questions from their bishops under Roman direction.

29:09 FURTHER RESTRICTIONS ON LAY PARTICIPATION

Another letter addresses both the SSPX and the CMRI (a sedevacantist group). The local archdiocese does not want children enrolled in SSPX schools. SSPX members cannot serve as godparents or confirmation sponsors. Lay people may no longer attend marriages at SSPX chapels—even though attendance at Protestant weddings remains permissible under certain conditions. Confession cannot be received at the Immaculata; funerals may be attended passively for a sufficient reason but without receiving Communion. These measures vary by parish, yet Stine expects them to be generalized once the French bishops’ proposal advances.

30:36 RUMORS OF A NEW CONSISTORY AND THE END OF THE TLM AS KNOWN

A number of cardinals are aging out of electoral status this year; the number of electors is about to fall below the formal cap of 120. A consistory to name new cardinals is therefore expected, possibly in December or January. Once the July consecrations are in the rear-view mirror, the liturgy topic deferred from the earlier consistory can return. 

Reports indicate that the French bishops’ proposal enjoys support among the French episcopate and is popular among other cardinals. Adoption would mean the end of the traditional Latin Mass as currently known. A more reverent version of the Novus Ordo would be promulgated as a temporary liturgy—mirroring in reverse the transitional rites of the mid-1960s. Along with liturgical changes would come the requirement that priests and eventually laity swear an oath of acceptance of Vatican II. Priests already know which parishioners regularly attend SSPX chapels; the diocese keeps tabs. Traditional Catholics of every stripe are being conflated, which is why mutual charity among them is advisable even while principles remain firm.

34:50 THE ONLY LIMITED GOOD NEWS AND A CALL TO PRAYER

he sole positive note Stine can discern, apart from reported SSPX expansion in certain places, is that some bishops are quietly pressing Rome to clean up liturgical abuses in the new Mass—priests inventing their own consecration formulas, liturgical dancing, and similar practices. He is not confident of success. Anyone who has ever used the phrase “ape of the Church” falls under the scrutiny of the FSSP-style questionnaires. 

Stine invites comments and asks viewers to pray for the priests and bishops of the SSPX, the FSSP, the Institute of Christ the King, and every similar group. They need prayerful support regardless of disagreements, because a time of testing has arrived. The Church is in what Lefebvre called “Operation Survival”—the effort to keep the pre-conciliar faith alive in the face of the public building of the ape of the Church. Whether that process is at its beginning or near its end is left for the viewer to decide. 

Stine closes by asking for prayers for everyone mentioned and for the Church itself.

🚨 JUST DECIDED (8/19/26): For decades, selling a house meant paying the buyer's agent too. A jury called that price fixing and set the damage at $1.785 billion. The settlement that ended it just survived.

Here's the story. When you sell a house, your agent lists it on a shared site that every local agent uses to find homes for their buyers. The National Association of Realtors had a rule, going back to 1996, that you could only list there if your agent promised a cut to whoever brought the buyer.

So the seller paid both sides, usually 5 to 6 percent split between the two agents. The buyer's agent was supposed to be fighting for the buyer, but the seller signed her paycheck. That cost got baked into the price of the house.

In 2019, a group of Missouri home sellers sued and said every big brokerage following the same rule is price fixing. A jury agreed in October 2023 and awarded $1.785 billion, an amount a judge can triple under antitrust law.

That threat is why everyone settled instead. The Realtors paid $418 million, HomeServices added $250 million, the fund passed $1 billion, and the rule is gone. Sellers no longer have to offer the buyer's agent anything, and agents have to say out loud that commissions are negotiable.

Seven groups tried to blow up the deal on appeal. They said the class lawyers were taking too much at $333 million, and that the judge set the make-or-break hearing two days before Thanksgiving and made objectors fly to Kansas City or lose their objection.

THE OUTCOME: The appeals court sided with the settlement on every point. If you sold a home listed on one of these sites between roughly 2014 and 2024, you are in the class, you cannot sue over this separately, and more than two million people have already filed claims. The lawyers keep the $333 million.

Notice reached over 99 percent of the class. Thirty-nine people opted out.

🤖 Written by CiteLaw AI
🔗 Rhonda Burnett v. Spring Way Center, LLC (8th Cir. 2026)
