text:
Lina has described the disease with remarkable accuracy. What she stops short of is mentioning the only Physician who can cure it.

She asks, “What happens when a society can no longer define good and bad?” Then she shows us. A thief steals, and we immediately begin manufacturing excuses: he was hungry, he was poor, his circumstances were hard. The act itself is no longer judged; the motive is. That is situation ethics, the very doctrine Joseph Fletcher popularized in the 1960s and which the Left has since baptized as compassion. “The end justifies the means.” Once you accept that principle, there is no act you cannot eventually justify if the story is sad enough.

She’s correct that consensus is always incomplete. She’s right that it fragments. Of course it does. Consensus is produced by fallen men and women who, Scripture says, “suppress the truth in unrighteousness” (Romans 1:18). You cannot get a perfect, unchanging moral law out of ever-changing human hearts. That is like asking a committee of drowning men to invent a lifeboat.

The culture does not annul the law of God. God’s law stands whether the culture stands or not. “Thou shalt not steal.” That commandment did not come from a show of hands. It came from the holy character of the God who said, “Be ye holy, for I am holy.” When we lose the ability to call theft theft, we have not become more nuanced; we have simply decided we no longer wish to be under authority.

Everybody needs what God says. The Ten Commandments are not suggestions offered for our consideration. They are the external standard because they flow from the unchanging nature of the Moral Law-Giver Himself. Without that external source, all you have left is the shifting sand of “our combined effort to improve consensus.” History is littered with the wreckage of those efforts.

Lina has diagnosed the problem. The remedy is not a better social contract. The remedy is the One who wrote the Law on tablets of stone and then came in flesh to keep it perfectly and to die for those of us who never could.

Until a society bows again to that external Authority, it will keep inventing new reasons why the thief was really the victim. And the house built on that sand will fall.

text:
Picture a nineteen-year-old in Paranaguá, a coastal town about fifty-six miles east of Curitiba. Over his first year there he has shed fifteen pounds of muscle, most days eating beans and rice. Ask him whether he could play a football game that afternoon and he says he would get crushed.

​Rewind two years and it will not reconcile. More than thirty programs had offered him a scholarship. Alabama. Texas. Texas A&M. Washington. Stanford. An Elite 11 finalist, rated four stars, the kind of quarterback whose phone rings with head coaches on it. Nick Saban made one of those calls himself.

​The odd part was that everybody recruiting him knew he was leaving. Texas told him he was the first prospect they had knowingly recruited in over a hundred years who had a mission scheduled before a snap.

​He signed with Stanford in 2018. He had been raised rooting for the Cougars and picked the Cardinal regardless, and he said the reason was the education rather than the depth chart.

​Then he got on a plane. At nine he had said out loud that he believed he would end up in Brazil, the sort of thing a family only remembers afterward.

​He returned two full seasons behind every quarterback he had been measured against, and lighter than all of them. David Shaw, his coach at Stanford, had encouraged the detour rather than argued him out of it.

​Philadelphia spent a sixth-round pick on him in 2023. He then sat. Behind Jalen Hurts. Behind Marcus Mariota. Behind Kenny Pickett. In 2024 he got into two games, started one, and threw for 323 yards and four scores. He is believed to be the first returned missionary quarterback ever to reach a Super Bowl.

​His name is Tanner McKee.

​There is a second half.

​On the twenty-second of August this year, in a preseason game, he threw a screen pass to a receiver listed at five foot eight and 170 pounds. Nobody drafted him in 2022. He was waived, signed to a practice squad the next day, and worked his way onto an active roster.

​That receiver had also lost two seasons, 2016 and 2017, and he had lost them the same way. Not to injury. To Chile.

​He took the screen and ran it fourteen yards into the end zone.

His name is Britain Covey.

​Two men, two continents, two years apiece handed over at the age the sport wanted them most. One throws, one catches, and it lands in a box score on an ordinary August night in a game their team lost.

​Now you see the whole picture.
​

Strengthening its global outreach and commitment to emerging technologies, IIT Kharagpur has expanded its international engagement through the Texas AI Learning Center, established in collaboration with the IIT Kharagpur Outreach Course Network (OCN) at the Tagore Center, Houston.

In his special address, Prof. Chakraborty envisioned the Learning Center evolving into a broader Pan-IIT Outreach Center—a collaborative platform for IIT alumni and stakeholders to offer professional development programmes and develop solutions to industry challenges.

The initiative also received encouraging messages and support from Ms. Kathy Giles-Diaz, U.S. Consul General in Kolkata, and Mr. Arjun Malhotra, Co-founder, HCLTech and Life Fellow, IIT Kharagpur. Marking the beginning of its academic activities, the Center is conducting a two-day AI Certificate Boot Camp, coordinated by Dr. Debyajoti Banerjee, Professor, Texas A&M University.

From Kharagpur to Houston, the initiative represents another step towards building global networks for learning, innovation and impact through Artificial Intelligence.

text:
🚨 SOFTBANK’S OHIO GAS MEGAPROJECT DRAWS UNEASY LOCAL CROWD.

PIKETON, UNITED STATES - Residents of a small Ohio community turned out this week to examine plans for what is set to become the largest natural gas power plant in the United States, a sprawling project backed by SoftBank and tied to a massive new data center campus. The meeting offered the first detailed public look at the proposal, which would place a 9.2 gigawatt gas-fired facility on federal land just south of the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant, a Cold War-era uranium enrichment site now undergoing long-term cleanup.

Locals walked through poster displays outlining turbine types, transmission upgrades, and the footprint of the PORTS Technology Campus, a 10 gigawatt data center complex expected to draw thousands of construction workers and eventually employ more than two thousand people. Some residents questioned the need for such a large data center and expressed concern about industrial expansion near a contaminated federal site. Others said they were still gathering information or welcomed the prospect of new jobs in a county that has struggled with high unemployment for years.

The project’s scale has raised questions among energy analysts, who point to the volatility of natural gas prices and the financial risks of building a plant of unprecedented size. The site’s history adds another layer: the former enrichment plant once supplied material for the nation’s nuclear arsenal, and cleanup of radioactive and chemical waste continues across the campus. The new development would occupy hundreds of acres of that land, with power expected to begin flowing in 2029.

Despite the mixed reception, the meeting unfolded without organized opposition, a contrast to other communities where large data centers have faced pushback. The plant’s location near the old enrichment facility remains one of the most striking aspects of the plan, linking the region’s Cold War past to a future built around artificial intelligence infrastructure.

The Pirate 🏴‍☠️ Empire.
Read the sequence, then tell me what to call it. In January the 🇺🇸 seized 🇻🇪's president in a night raid on Caracas and flew him and his wife to a courtroom in Manhattan, where they go on trial next year. His vice-presidenty became interim president. That same month Caracas passed a hydrocarbons law gutting PDVSA and letting private firms work the wells directly. Sanctions came off. And on Fridayy night that same interim president signed, handing Washington 55 per cent of a venture holding hundred-year concessions over 63bn barrels of proven reserves. 8 months from the raid to the signature. The counterparty holds office because Washington removed the last one.
Ricardo Hausmann, once Venezuela’s planning minister, now at Harvard, says the government has no legitimacy to strike an unconstitutional deal. Francisco Rodríguez calls it predatory, says it contravenes the constitution, and adds the four words that settle it, at gunpoint. Both are economists. Neither is a politician. And this is why it will not last. The first constitutional government Venezuela produces will repudiate it, and the brief writes itself. Signed under duress. Signed by an administration the buyer installed. Signed over resources the constitution reserves to the nation.
A hundred-year asset resting on a defective title from the first day. The Anglo-Persian concession was written to run sixty years. It was nationalised at fifty and the coup came two years after that, and everyone in Latin America knows how that story ends.
But notice what separates this from the old imperialism. Trump announced it on Truth Social in capital letters and promised it would lower petrol prices for Americans. Not strategy, not security, not even the pretence of development. A South American country’s oil, sold to voters as relief at the pump ten weeks before an election. And it is a template, by his own admission. Threatening to seize Kharg Island last week, he said the United States would assume total control of Iran’s oil and gas markets, much like we have with Venezuela, which is working out brilliantly. Venezuela was the pilot. This is what a government looks like once the line between the state and the family running it has dissolved. At home, a Justice Department shielding the president’s tax records, a fund of 1.8bn to pay allies with public money, his face pressed onto a proposed banknote, and two sons holding both bitcoin and a dollar stablecoin so that no currency outcome can hurt them.

Abroad, the same operation with a flag over it. The looting simply found a bigger jurisdiction. Moscow does this openly now. Washington has decided to compete. Every government in this hemisphere sitting on lithium, copper or crude watched the whole sequence, from the raid to the signature to the price of gasoline in Ohio, and they will go looking for a counterweight. There is only one on offer. The era of open imperialism was supposed to be over. What ended was the shame.

text:
Ro Khanna’s 2025 financial disclosure just dropped and it should end the act.

He reported 5,402 stock trades across 244 of 251 trading days, a total volume of up to $165 million, as much as $10.8 million in dividends and distributions, and a household net worth as high as $167 million. When he entered Congress he was worth as much as $78 million. His minor children hold ownership stakes in three private Ohio golf courses that generate substantial unearned income. The same filing sits next to a $6 million D.C. house with an elevator, a move toward a $9 million Virginia home, and a $190,000 Range Rover.

This is the congressman who campaigns to ban stock trading by members of Congress. The same man who posts about the cost of living crisis, lectures about “workers over billionaires,” and spent the last year demanding a 5 percent wealth tax on California billionaires while capital fled the state. He tells the public the system is rigged for the rich. His own disclosure reads like a trading desk.

Khanna’s answer is that he has “zero knowledge” and “zero say.” That line does not survive contact with reality. The disclosure is filed under his name. The political brand is his. The lifestyle is his. He files the old analog checkbox format that makes the record harder to search, then claims innocence when the numbers come out. A politician who wants a congressional trading ban cannot hide behind a technicality while his household executes more than twenty trades on a typical market day.

The hypocrisy is not a side issue. It is the whole story. He attacks hedge funds while his household holds them. He attacks concentrated wealth while his children collect income from exclusive golf clubs. He attacks the billionaire class while pushing a tax that other people’s founders cannot practically pay in cash, then lives like the exact class he claims to fight. He talks economic patriotism in Pennsylvania steel towns and files a Silicon Valley multimillionaire’s trading log in Washington.

This is not a reformer exposing the system. This is a man using the language of the system’s victims while enjoying every privilege the system offers. The numbers are public. The contradiction is complete. He does not get to run for higher office on a platform of taxing the rich and restoring trust while this filing exists.

Homes for Texas Heroes: Tailored DPA and low-interest rates for teachers, firefighters, EMS personnel, police officers, correctional officers, and veterans. 

Additional Financial Tools

Mortgage Credit Certificate (MCC): Allows qualifying buyers to claim a federal income tax credit for a portion of the mortgage interest paid each year.

Texas Bootstrap Loan Program: A 0% interest owner-builder program helping low-income families construct or repair their own homes.

In 2024, pediatric nurse Vanessa Sivadge was fired from her position at Texas Children's Hospital (TCH) for anonymously blowing the whistle on what she described as the hospital's alleged illegal use of Medicaid funds to prescribe cross-sex hormones and puberty blockers to minors, in violation of Texas state law.

Fast forward to 2026: As RedState reported at the time, according to an unprecedented settlement secured by Sivadge with the assistance of the Burke Law Group and Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, TCH must pay $10 million in penalties for their alleged misuse of Medicaid funds, the five physicians who were allegedly involved in the practice of transitioning minors have been terminated, and the most groundbreaking part of this win: TCH must establish a detransitioner clinic which offers free services to anyone nationwide who has been victimized by the practices of the gender cult.

This was huge, especially for detransitioners like Chloe Cole and Fox Varian, who had to face the process of reintegrating back into their biological sex with little medical or psychological support. Cole called this win a huge victory, and Paxton called the settlement an historic one.

Vanessa Sivadge, a Christian nurse who was fired from her job at Texas Children's Hospital (TCH) after exposing alleged Medicaid fraud related to the illegal castration of minors, secured a settlement that includes the hospital establishing the first free detransitioner clinic in the United States.

Under the settlement agreement, TCH must open the clinic by the end of October, pay $10 million in penalties to resolve Medicaid fraud claims, and fire five physicians who carried out sex-rejecting procedures in violation of Texas law, according to a Wednesday press release from Burke Law Group, which represented Sivadge.

---

I blew the whistle on two doctors: but the government found THREE more.

I personally witnessed two physicians committing Medicaid fraud through the gender clinic. They allegedly falsified medical records, used vague diagnosis codes to conceal sex-rejecting hormones, and misdiagnosed patients so Medicaid would reimburse treatments it otherwise shouldn't: a flagrant violation of Texas law that went unchecked for far too long.

I knew about those two doctors: but what I didn't know was that as the government dug deeper, they uncovered three more physicians.

That stopped me in my tracks.

It means the corruption ran deeper than I ever imagined. There were more ideologues behind the curtain. More people willing to sacrifice children while taxpayers footed the bill.

They might have fired me, but I took 5 of their most devoted trans doctors with me.

No regrets.

In an update to this story, KHOU-11 reported last week on Paxton's announcement that the "legal settlement requiring Texas Children's Hospital to create what Attorney General Ken Paxton calls the country's first 'detransition clinic' has been finalized."

This settlement and the institution of a detransitioner clinic are creating a model for other states to follow, setting the precedent as other lawsuits are being waged against hospitals that allegedly performed gender transition surgeries on minors.

The clinic is slated to provide free treatment for patients up to age 21 who underwent trans procedures at TCH or elsewhere and need help healing from fertility-related injuries, endocrine system damage, psychiatry and other long-term health damage. The clinic's services must be provided at no charge to patients for a minimum of five years.

TCH must also commit to institutional reforms that include training healthcare professionals on the dangers of sex-rejecting procedures, rewriting its bylaws to require physicians who perform them on minors to lose their clinical privileges, and commit to banning them at their facilities.

The settlement, which was part of a years-long investigation aided by the Office of the Texas Attorney General and the U.S. Department of Justice, resolves alleged violations of the federal False Claims Act, the Texas Medicaid Fraud Prevention Act, the federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, as well as federal fraud and conspiracy laws.

This is also a huge coup for AG and Republican U.S. Senate nominee Paxton, who called the settlement, "a resounding defeat for the radical gender ideology that has preyed on children under the guise of 'care.'"

"The settlement gives Texas Children's Hospitals three months to open that clinic and will provide FREE care to people who want to reverse gender reassignment procedures," Fox News reported.

With Paxton's Democrat Senate opponent James Talarico's stated passion for transgender children, Paxton's role in securing aid and salvation for children who have fallen sway to the gender cult and need help to escape it will play an outsized role in his candidacy.

Sivadge was not only a key whistleblower in exposing TCH's alleged illegal gender-affirming care practices; after she was fired by TCH, the Biden DOJ targeted her, showing up at her front door.

The day before that, on June 18, 2024, a doctor who also blew the whistle on the alleged illegal transitioning going on at TCH was indicted by Biden's DOJ on trumped-up charges, as RedState reported.

Haim, a Dallas surgeon, previously had done some work at Texas Children's Hospital as part of his residency. text:
Three takeaways from @geoffreylitt's excellent talk, or how to take a rabbit hole seriously: Optimize for interesting. Find community. Try different types of organizational structures.

The talk was officially titled "Dynamic Documents as Personal Software," but Geoffrey said its unofficial title was "Taking a rabbit hole seriously," because it also chronicled the curious path his career has taken, which he sees as one long rabbit hole he's been going down since coming to the @RecurseCenter in 2018.

Here are the things Geoffrey shared that had an outsized impact on his career and helped him build a life filled with meaningful work:

1. Optimize for interesting. Don't just take the more lucrative or prestigious path; follow your curiosity, and consider going off the beaten path. Do things that are a bit weird. E.g., Geoffrey chose to submit his side project to a niche academic workshop, and later to leave his tech job to work at an independent research lab.

2. Find community. Seek out people who can give you substantive feedback, expose you to new ideas, and nerd out deeply on the things you're interested in.

3. Try different types of organizational structures. There are more types of organizations than you think there are! Look for interesting ones, think about what each one provides you, and consider inventing a new one if you can't find one that bundles the right set of things. Sampling a variety like Geoffrey has (small startups, RC, Ink & Switch, MIT, Notion) helps you learn the benefits and tradeoffs each offers.

We'll be posting the video from the talk online in a few weeks. Stay tuned!

text:
Casual rant video.

Top mental health tip of the day:

• Turn off ALL social media notifications (likes, follows, DMs ALL alerts). Check social media only on purpose and with intention, not reaction.

Video Content in chronological order:

• Back after a stretch of what he thinks was long COVID

• He has a stack of notes. First instinct is to throw the notes away. People cling to work because of sunk-cost thinking.

• Image he uses: monks making a sand mandala, then destroying it. Practice of making something, then letting it go. Burn away bad ideas. Help the mind process to deeper layers.

• Mentions Darryl Anka / Bashar. His primary teaching: "Follow your highest excitement in every present moment."

• Unsure if the channeling is performance. Some of it was interesting. Watched a lot at 26 while recovering from cancer the first time.

• Separate from whether Anka is genuine: he believes channeling as a phenomenon can be real.

• After years of daily formal sitting (about 30–60 min), he started getting urges to form mudras and hearing more inner voices. He notes the schizophrenia accusation XD.

• Recalled a Vancouver client (“Elyse”) who wanted contact with someone who had died. Not his usual work (meditation coaching for OCD / depression / anxiety).

• He had met her through breathwork. Session was in his home office while running Action Compassion.

• During the session, mudras came; Larry went into trance and began sharing some information. She later said she felt she had made contact. Memorable because the client was very happy and satisfied.

• Position: physical science does not explain everything yet. Maybe it needs better instruments for subtle frequencies / very small particles. Mentions Dr. Tang’s interest in zero-point / dark energy / unified field.

• People judge too fast. Everyone is informed; they just run the same facts through different frames, so they cannot agree on what to do among other factors.

• Not enough resources go to ordinary working people’s wellbeing; a lot of money goes to “foreign adventures.”

• Reason: otherwise a ping hits you at the playground and you stop being a present father. 

• Most of it is noise. His split: 80% noise, 20% signal.

• Video games (EverQuest / RPGs) built a lot of his vocabulary.

• Don’t give a 3-year-old an iPad for 12 hours. That fries dopamine / neurotransmitters and changes the brain in ways we don’t fully understand.

• Also don’t raise Luddites. Kids still have to function in a rapidly advancing tech world.

• The work is balance. Meditation is balance training. Each day’s sit is different because the imbalance that day is different.

• Meditation lets you see patterns: what you are overweighting, what beliefs/feelings keep showing up. 

• “Buddha = anti-teacher”: meditation is the tool that cuts and shapes your own intellect, not a new belief system to swallow.

• Conversation with online friend Remington: low-IQ people can be brainwashed and hypocritical. High-IQ people can too. Smarter people are often better at rationalizing why the hypocrisy is necessary.

• Line he used to say in classes: you can convince yourself of anything. The mind can rationalize anything.

• In meditation you do not believe every thought. You observe every thought.

• Posture image: open palm. Thoughts land on it. You receive without grabbing. When the palm is full, things fall off by themselves.

• If you have OCD / anxiety / ugly thoughts, sitting is the time you meet those thoughts with kindness instead of criticism or annoyance.

• Belief since around age 30 (he just turned 40 in July): souls come from many places.
Cites Dr. Tang: souls can split and recombine; they connect in many ways.

• He holds that Earth has souls from different planets / thought-realms / religious “heavens,” and that those can coexist inside one information field (Hindu Akasha / space element as information). That is his working logic for how meditators access material. Also fine if someone calls it crap.

• Online critic “Batur” challenges him for talking Taiwan/China while living comfortably in a Canadian island city. I have to be a soldier on the frontline to speak about politics?

• Reply: he is not a soldier. He has confronted family abuse and corporate exploitation, but that is not the same as being a fighter by role.

• If Canada ever put Chinese people in camps, he would offer language / analysis work toward peace between China, Canada, and the US.

• Not every soul is a soldier / berserker. Some are mages, wizards, enchanters, druids, shamans. Different functions.

• Dark has a use. If roots do not go into the dark, tree branches do not reach heaven. Yin and yang. Ego has logic; don’t mutilate it with spiritual “shoulds.”

• In meditation, drop the shoulds as much as possible, the mind will keep judging but you keep bringing in love. Be true. Trust an inner evolutionary process. Awareness speeds it up.

• Chinese metaphysics / Feng Shui: we are in the fire trigram period until 2043. The fire has a feminine character; I Ching imagery of rising female power. 离 ☲

• He thinks that rise is visible. Uses Lindsay Clancy as an example, then asks whether feminine power will mature into something that serves women, men, children, and the elderly. He hopes so and thinks a good outcome is possible.

• Meanwhile people die every day and are born every day. He is sometimes melancholic about that. World is brutal and beautiful.

• Too many impressions hitting consciousness / subconscious. Buddhist model: eight (or more) layers of consciousness filtering outer input and inner-generated impressions.

• That is why he meditates: get clear on what you generate that you can steer, and what you generate that you cannot.

• The gains are mostly invisible. Hard to convert into clout or money, which is what the era rewards. But the gifts from meditation are of the highest order.

• Fire period also means appearances start beating substance: image over signal, carbs over protein.

• He reads Peter Thiel–funded Clavicular transhuman / post-human projects as part of that, and tends to think it is bad, or at least a painful birth stage of a fast-changing world.

• Joke history: “Al Gore invented the internet,” then we arrived here. Past the ICQ / eccentric-personal-website golden age.

• Logic is global, but different AIs (Kimmi, Grok, GPT, Gemini) apply it differently.

• The world often runs on appeal-to-majority. That is a fallacy, and also you cannot just ignore the masses. Tension: what people want vs what we think they want vs what elites think they want.

• In a Spaces with Remington @westasiapost  they listened to music across languages. He rejects the white-supremacist line that non-white people cannot feel beautiful music.

• Beauty, empathy, and the capacity to feel it are human, not racial property.

• Closes: souls from everywhere wearing human bodies. Let’s see how it goes.

🚨How Data Centers can be a Win - Win

The key is in LOCAL NEGOTIATIONS.......

KNOW WHO IS NEGOTATING & WHAT IS BEING NEGOTIATED:
In local communities, negotiations are led by county managers and zoning boards who hammer out tax deals, noise limits, and green buffers. Alongside them, municipal utility directors protect local water and power grids, while neighborhood coalitions and school boards fight for binding community benefit agreements to ensure the tech investment directly funds local infrastructure and classrooms.

FOREIGN INFLUENCE:
OpenAI Findings: In mid-2026, OpenAI reported that it banned covert accounts originating in China. These accounts used AI to create social media posts and images that complained about data centers raising electricity prices.

Data centers provide the fundamental physical infrastructure required for the modern digital economy, driving technological innovation, regional economic development, and critical public services.

PROS:
*Massive Capital Investment - Tech companies inject hundreds of millions of dollars into local economies to acquire land, clear sites, and construct facilities.
*Construction Job surges & maitenance Jobs -  Projects generate thousands of high-paying, multi-year jobs for local electricians, engineers, heavy equipment operators, and laborers.
*Substantial Tax Revenue - Facilities pay millions annually in property and equipment taxes, directly funding local public schools, parks, roads, and emergency services.
*Enabling Digital Services: They provide the backbone for essential daily tools, including cloud storage, online banking, telemedicine, and remote work infrastructure.
*Accelerating AI Advancement: Specialized hardware inside data centers powers complex artificial intelligence models, driving breakthroughs in medical research, climate modeling, and logistics.
*Enhanced Data Security: Centralized facilities offer superior cybersecurity defenses, physical surveillance, and redundant power systems to protect sensitive user and corporate data from loss.
*Renewable Energy Finance: Tech corporate buyers fund a massive share of new wind and solar projects, accelerating the transition of the entire public energy grid.
*Grid Efficiency Innovations: High demand forces utilities to modernize transmission lines and adopt smart-grid software, improving overall energy reliability for nearby residents.

CONS & HOW TO ADDRESS THEM:
Data center operators, utilities, and governments are adopting advanced technologies, stricter regulations, and new energy frameworks to eliminate community and environmental concerns.

Solving Environmental and Resource Impacts -
*Next-Generation Cooling: Shifting to closed-loop liquid cooling eliminates water evaporation and slashes facility water consumption to near zero.
*Geothermal and Nuclear Power: Tech companies are signing deals for advanced nuclear (SMRs) and deep geothermal energy to power facilities without straining the public grid.
*Grid-Interactive Batteries: Replacing diesel backup generators with massive utility-scale battery systems eliminates local air pollution and helps stabilize the local grid.

Solving Economic and Infrastructure Concerns -
*Tiered Utility Rates: Utilities are introducing "large power user" rate structures, ensuring data center operators pay for their own grid upgrades so residential bills do not rise.
*Waste Heat Re-use: New facilities redirect their excess heat into local municipal district heating systems, warming nearby homes, greenhouses, or public pools for free.
*Aggressive Tax Recapture: Local governments are restructuring tax incentives, tying exemptions directly to mandatory community infrastructure investments and long-term local job metrics.

Solving Quality of Life Disruptions -
*Acoustic Engineering: Enclosing cooling towers in sound-dampening walls and using ultra-quiet, low-frequency fans reduces boundary noise to match normal neighborhood background levels.
*Subterranean and Multi-Story Builds: Building vertically or partially underground shrinks the physical footprint, preserving local landscapes and keeping facilities out of sight.
*Industrial Zoning Buffers: Stricter local zoning laws enforce mandatory mile-wide green buffers, dense tree lines, and setback distances between data center walls and residential zones.

Advanced Site Selection to Avoid Agricultural Land -
*Brownfield and Industrial Redevelopment: Building exclusively on abandoned factories, retired coal plants, old malls, or closed airports completely bypasses agricultural areas.
*Co-location with Energy Infrastructure: Positioning facilities directly next to nuclear plants or oil refineries keeps them confined to heavy industrial zones.
*Stricter Urban Enterprise Zones: Directing development toward existing municipal boundaries using designated technology zones shields outer rural sectors from expansion.

Protective Local Policy and Restoration -
*Agricultural Zoning Firewalls: Enacting strict local zoning laws that completely ban data centers from Prime Farmland or Soils of Statewide Importance.
*Farmland Preservation Offsets: Requiring developers to buy and permanently conserve two acres of vulnerable local farmland for every one acre they build on.
*Agrivoltaics integration: Forcing adjacent solar panels that power the facility to be elevated, allowing livestock grazing or shade-tolerant crops to grow underneath.

text:
Elon Musk put his entire $180 million fortune into three companies nobody believed in.
  
Here's the talk where he explains why, point by point: 

1. He walked away from PayPal with $180 million and then ran out of money. He put all of it into spacex, tesla and solar city. The entire fortune, into three of the most capital-hungry industries that exist. It got to the point where he had to borrow money from friends to pay his bills. He called that a bit awkward.  

2. He picked his three problems before he had money for any of them. In college he asked what would most affect the future of humanity and came up with three answers: the internet, the transition to sustainable energy, and space exploration. He never expected to work in space. It was an abstract list. The internet money is what eventually bought him the ticket into the other two.  

3. He went to Stanford for the labs, not the degree. The plan was a phd in applied physics with a pragmatic goal underneath it: solve energy storage for electric cars. He wanted free lab access, so he enrolled. He still thinks the idea is worth trying, and he gave it away on stage: use advanced chip-making equipment to build a solid state ultra high energy density capacitor. If it worked, it would supersede all batteries. He is not sure success is one of the possible outcomes.  

4. He deferred instead of quitting, and the chairman knew better. By summer 1995 he saw the choice clearly: spend years as a grad student watching the internet happen, or take part in it. He called the chair of his department and said he would be back in about three months. The chair told him this was probably the last conversation they would have. he was correct.  

5. He never wanted to start a car company. Gm and toyota already had electric cars on the road. He assumed the momentum was there and no new entrant was needed. Then both companies recalled the vehicles and gm crushed theirs in a lot. Owners tracked down the wrecking yard and held a candlelit vigil for the cars. His takeaway is a warning to every company: when your customers hold vigils for a product you killed, that is unusual, and you should notice.  

6. The goal was never a good electric car. It was a car people would buy even if the electric part did not exist. Best in safety, ride, handling, performance, looks. He is blunt about why. You do not want people to have to accept a list of negatives in order to be environmental. If only the environmentalists buy it, you have not changed anything.  

7. He sold his technology to his competitors on purpose. Daimler, the company that invented the combustion engine car, was buying battery packs and powertrains from tesla. So was toyota, the largest carmaker in the world. He was not holding anything close to his vest. The stated goal of tesla was to be a catalyst that speeds up the whole transition, and that only works if other people copy you.  

8. He put a date on the end of the gas car and offered to take bets. By 2030, he said, the majority of all new cars manufactured in the united states will be pure electric. By mid-century, the majority of cars on the road. He said he was comfortable making the prediction because he thought it would happen sooner, and if anyone wanted to bet him, he was happy to bet them. Everything goes electric except rockets, and only because you cannot get around newton's third law.  

9. The most common flaw he sees in people is wishful thinking. He says it is innate. You want things to be a certain way, so you filter out the information that says otherwise. The second failure is doing something because everyone else is doing it, which works right up until the crowd walks off a cliff. His alternative is the physics habit: find the fundamental truths in a field, and make sure every conclusion is derived from those.  

10. He does not trust ideas until they exist in physical form. His advice to founders is to get to a useful prototype as fast as possible, on as little money as possible. The reason is that a deck proves nothing. Everything works on powerpoint. People discount a presentation and believe working hardware. Tesla's first roadster prototype was, in his words, somewhat of a hack, and it still gave people the feeling of what the thing could be. It also tells you fast if what you are attempting is impossible.  

11. Big companies kill innovation with math, not malice. As they grow, failure gets punished severely and success gets rewarded moderately. Once that asymmetry exists, nobody takes risks, and innovation by definition produces a lot of attempts that do not work. His answer is to tolerate a certain amount of chaos, let people work on odd projects without routing them through a manager, and stay a little irreverent so nobody thinks there is a conformist police coming for them.  

12. He admits the criticism actually got to him. The host praised his fortitude through the years when tesla nearly died and general motors went bankrupt. Musk's response was that the naysayers did get him down. He still says never give up unless you are forced to, then immediately warns the rule can be misapplied if what you are doing is trying to get through a brick wall with your head. And then the line: starting companies is like eating glass and staring into the abyss of death. If that sounds appealing, be an entrepreneur.  

13. He refuses to argue about climate and argues about odds instead. Whatever you think of the debate, he says, it is probably not a good idea to run the experiment of finding out how much co2 the atmosphere can hold. Even if it is 99% likely to be fine, that is still not good enough. It is a risk argument, not a political one, and it is harder to dodge.  

14. What he actually enjoys is none of this. Asked what gets him up in the morning, he did not say building companies or winning. He said he is primarily an engineer, and engineering is where the satisfaction comes from. He had been awake until 5am that morning working on an improvement to a rocket, and hoped it worked out, because otherwise it was a lot of wasted sleep.

Plenary Meeting of the General Assembly of the United Nations on
Monday, September 26, 1960.

Part 3/6       III  of VI

There have been dozens of victims in the war; eighty families were shattered by an explosion;
there were forty victims caused by an airplane that was "peacefully" flying over our territory. The
authorities of the United States Government denied the fact that these planes came from United
States territory. What is more, they said that the plane was safely in its hangar. But when one of
our magazines published the photograph of this plane in its hangar, then the United States authori-
ties took possession of the plane. And, as expected, a version of the affair was issued to the effect
that this was not very important and that these victims had not died because of the bombs but be-
cause of the anti-aircraft fire and those who were to blame for this crime, and those who had caused
these deaths were wandering about peacefully in the United States, where they were not even pre-
vented from continuing these acts of aggression. '
To his Excellency the representative of the United States, I may perhaps take the opportunity
of telling him that there are many mothers in Cuba who are still hoping to receive a telegram of
condolence from the United States Government for the children who were murdered by bombs from
the United States.
The planes went and came back. There was no evidence; there was no proof unless you define
what you mean by proof. That plane was there, photographed and captured. Yet we were told that
this plane did not drop any bombs. It is not known how the United States authorities were so well
informed. These pirate planes continued to fly over our territory dropping incendiary bombs. Mil-
lions upon millions of pesos were lost in the burning fields of sugar cane. Many people of the towns,
humble people of Cuba, who saw this wealth burning, a wealth which was now theirs, were them-
selves burned in the struggle against these fires, against these persistent and tenacious bombings
by these pirate airplanes.
Until one day, while flying over one of the sugar refineries, a bomb explodes, the plane ex-
plodes and the Revolutionary Government has the opportunity of gathering the pieces of the pilot,
who in fact was an American pilot, whose papers were found, and a North American plane and all
the proofs of the field from which he had taken off. That plane had passed between two bases in the
United States.
Then, in view of this irrefutable proof, the United States Government gave an explanation to
the Cuban Government. Its conduct in this case was not the same as it was in connection with, the
U-2. When it was proved that the planes were leaving the United States, the Government of the
United States did not proclaim its right to burn our cane fields. The United States Government
apologized, and said it was sorry. Well, we were lucky, after all, because after the incident of the
U-2 the United States Government did not even apologize; it proclaimed its right to carry out over-
flights over Soviet territory. That is bad luck for the Soviets.
But we do not have too many anti-aircraft batteries and further planes were able to continue
until the sugar was harvested. When there was no more cane in the fields, the bombs stopped. We
believed we were the only country in the world in which this happened, although I do recall that at
the time of his visit President Sukarno told us that this was not the case, that we were not the only
people in the world, that they, too, had suffered certain problems with certain American planes
which flew over their territory. I do not know whether I have committed an indiscretion in men-
tioning this; I hope not. \\'-t

The fact of the matter is that, at least in this peaceful hemisphere, we were the country that,
without being at war with anyone, had to stand the constant attack of pirate planes. And could those
planes leave and enter North American territory with impunity? Well, gentlemen, we invite you to
think about this for a little while and we also invite the people of the United States, if by chance the
United States people have the opportunity of knowing the matters which are discussed here — to
12
meditate upon this matter for, according to the statements of the United States Government itself,
the territory of the United States is completely protected against any air incursion and that the de-
fense measures in United States territory are infallible. It is stated that the defense of the world
that they call "free" — because, so far as we are concerned, it has not been free, at least not until
January 1, 1959 — is complete and impregnable. If this be the case, and I am not talking about
stratosphere planes, I am merely speaking of little aeroplanes that can barely fly 150 miles an hour,
how is it that these planes are able to come in and out of American national territory undetected
and that they can go through two bases and go back over these two same bases without the United
States Government even being aware of the fact that these planes are coming in and out?
This means one of two things. Either the United States Government is lying to the people of
the United States and the United States is not impregnable against aerial incursions or the American
Government was an accomplice in these aerial incursions.
The aerial incursions finally ended, and then came economic aggression. What was one of
the arguments adduced by the enemies of the agrarian reform? They said that the agrarian reform
would cause chaos in agricultural production; that production would diminish considerably and that
the United States Government was concerned because Cuba might not be able to fulfil its commit-
ments regarding supplies to the American market.
That was the first argument, and I think it appropriate that at least the new delegations in the
General Assembly should become somewhat familiar with some of the arguments that are adduced,
because sometimes they may have to answer similar arguments that agrarian reform would bring
about the ruin of the country.
That was not the case. Had the agrarian reform brought about the ruin of the country, had the
agricultural production been reduced so drastically, then the United States Government would not
have had to carry on its economic aggression. They truly believed in what they said. Did they sin-
cerely believe in what they said when they asserted that the agrarian reform was going to bring
about a decrease in production? Perhaps they believed it. It Is logical that everyone believes In
the manner in which he has prepared his mind to believe. It is possible they imagined that if the
all-powerful monopolies did not produce the sugar, we Cubans were incapable of doing so. It is
possible and perhaps they even trusted in our ruining the country. And it is plain that if the revo-
lution had ruined the country, the United States would not have had to attack us. They would have
left us to sink or swim and the United States would have appeared as a good and honorable govern-
ment while we revolutionaries came in and ruined our country, and it would have been proof that
you cannot carry out a revolution because revolutions ruin countries.
Fortunately, that is not the case. There is living proof that revolutions do not ruin countries
and the proof has just been given by the Government of the United States of America. It has proved
many things, but, among others, it has proved that revolutions do not ruin countries and that the
imperialist governments do try to ruin countries. Cuba was far from being ruined and, therefore,
it had to be ruined. Cuba needed new markets for its products, and we would honestly and frankly
ask any delegate present which country does not want to sell what it produces. Which country does
not want its exports to increase? We wanted our exports to increase, and this is what all countries
want. This obviously must be a universal law, because only egotistical interests can oppose the
universal interests for trade and commercial exchange, which surely is one of the most ancient
aspirations and needs of mankind.
We wanted to sell our products and we went to seek new markets. We signed a trade treaty
with the Soviet Union, according to which we would sell one million tons and we would purchase a
certain amount of Soviet products or articles. Surely no one can say that this is incorrect. There
may be some who do not do so because it is not in keeping with certain Interests. We did not have
to ask permission of the State Department in order to sign a trade treaty with the Soviet Union be-
cause we considered ourselves and we continue to consider ourselves and we will always consider
ourselves a truly Independent and free country.
When the supplies of sugar began to diminish in our favor, then we received the hard blow.

But what happened in Costa Rica? Lo and behold, by an ingenious production a miracle hap-
pened in Costa Rica, What resulted from Costa Rica was not a condemnation of the United States
or the Government of the United States. I do wish to avoid any misunderstanding about our feelings:
we regard the Government of the United States and the people of the United States as two completely
different entities. The Government of the United States was not condemned in Costa Rica for the
sixty overflights by pirate aircraft. The Government of the United States was not condemned for the
economic and other aggression of which we had been the victim. No, the Soviet Union was condemned.
That was really bizarre. We had not been attacked by the Soviet Union. We had not been the victims
of aggression by the Soviet Union. No Soviet aircraft had flown over our territory. Yet in Costa
Rica there was a finding against the Soviet Union for interference.
The Soviet Union only said that, figuratively speaking, if there was military aggression against
our country the Soviet Union could support the victim with rockets. Since when is support for a
weak country, support conditioned on an attack by a powerful country, regarded as interference? In
law there is something called an impossible condition. If a country considers that it is incapable of
committing a certain crime, well then, it is enough for it to say that there is no possibility that the
Soviet Union will support Cuba, because there is no possibility that they will attack the little country.
The principle was established that the intervention of the Soviet Union had to be condemned. About
the bombing of Cuba nothing was said. Of the aggression against Cuba, nothing.
After all, there is something which we should remember and that in some way should worry
all of us. We are all, without any of those present being excluded, actors and participants in a cru-
cial moment in the history of humanity. At times, apparently, we are not made aware of censure,
that is, apparently we are not aware of criticism and that is so especially, when we forget that, as
we have had the privilege of playing a part in this all-important moment of history, some day his-
tory too will judge us for our acts.
And in the face of the refusal to defend our country in Costa Rica, we smile, because history
will judge that episode. And I say it without bitterness. It is difficult to condemn men. Many times
men are the playthings of circumstances and we, who know what the history of our country was and
who, in addition, are unusual witnesses of what our country is going through today, understand how
terrible it is for the economy and the whole life of the nations to be subjected to the power of an
alien economy.
I need only note that my country was left defenseless in Costa Rica. Furthermore, there was
an interest in not bringing this matter back to the United Nations — perhaps because it was felt that
it is easier to obtain a mechanical majority in the OAS and after all, that fear is not easy to explain
when we have observed that in the United Nations mechanical majorities very often operate. With
all due respect to this Organization, we must say here that is the reason why the people, our people,
yes, our people, that people who are over there in our homeland, who are a people who have learned
much and who are a people — we say it with pride — who are equal to the role they are playing in this
moment and of the heroic struggle which they are carrying on, that is why our people, who have
learned much in the school of these recent international events, know that in the end, when its rights
have been denied, when the aggressive forces fall upon it, it has the supreme recourse and the
heroic recourse of resisting when its rights are not safeguarded either in the Organization of Amer-
ican States or in the United Nations.
That is why we, the small countries, still do not feel so sure that our rights will be preserved.
That is why when we small countries want to be free we know that we are doing so at our risk, and
because in truth the peoples, when they are united, when they defend a just cause, can depend on
their own energies, because it is not a matter of a few men, as they have tried to make it appear,
ruling a country. It is a matter of a whole people ruling a country, firmly united and with a great
revolutionary conscience defending its rights. And the enemies of the Cuban revolution should know
that, because if they do not know that they are committing a terrible error.
Those are the circumstances in which the revolutionary process in Cuba has taken place. How
did we find the country? Why have the difficulties arisen? And yet the Cuban revolution is chang-
ing things. What was yesterday a hopeless land, a land of misery, a land of illiterates, is gradually
becoming one of the most enlightened, advanced and developed lands of this Continent.
I
I
The Revolutionary Government, in but twenty months, has created 10,000 new schools. In this
brief space of time, we have doubled the number of rural schools that had been set up in fifty years
and Cuba today is the first country of America that has fulfilled all its scholastic needs, that has a
teacher in the farthest corner of the mountains. In this brief period of time, the Revolutionary Gov-
ernment has built 25,000 houses in the rural zones and also in the urban areas. Fifty new townships
are this moment being built in our country. The most important military fortresses today house
tens of thousands of students. In the coming year, our country intends to start its great battle against
illiteracy, with the ambitious goal of teaching every single inhabitant of the country to read and write.
And with that end in view, organizations of teachers, of students, of workers, are going out, that is
— the entire people, is preparing itself for an intensive campaign to wipe out illiteracy. Cuba will be
the first country of America which, after a few months, will be able to say it does not have one single
solitary illiterate in the country.
Today our people are receiving the assistance of hundreds of doctors who have been sent out
into the rural areas to fight against the endemic sicknesses, the parasitism, and to improve the san-
itary conditions of the nation.
In another aspect, in the preservation of the natural resources, we can also point with pride
to the fact that in one year, in the most ambitious plan for the conservation of natural resources
being carried out in this continent, including the United States of America and Canada, we have
planted close to fifty million timber-yielding trees.
Youths who were unemployed, who had no schools, have been organized by the Revolutionary
Government and today are being gainfully and usefully employed by the country, and at the same
time they are being prepared for productive work. Agricultural production in our country has noted
an almost unique event, the increase of production since the first moment. Since the first moment,
we have increased our agricultural production. Why? Because, first of all, the Revolutionary Gov-
ernment turned more than 100,000 agricultural workers into landowners, and at the same time they
preserved the large-scale production by means of agricultural co-operatives — that is to say, the
large-scale production was maintained, and it was maintained through co-operatives — thanks to
which we have been able to apply the most modern technical procedures and processes to our agri-
cultural production, and since the very beginning we have noted an increase in production.
All these enterprises of social benefit — of teachers, of houses, of hospitals — have been car-
ried out without sacrificing the resources that we had earmarked for development. At this moment,
the Revolutionary Government is carrying out a program of industrialization of the country, and the
first plants are already being built in Cuba.
We have reasonably and sensibly utilized the resources of our country. Previously, for ex-
ample, $35,000,000 worth of cars were imported into Cuba, and $5,000,000 worth of tractors. A
principally agricultural country imported seven times more automobiles than tractors. We have
turned this fraction upside down, and now we are importing seven times more tractors than auto-
mobiles.
Close to $500,000,000 was recovered from the politicians who had enriched themselves during
the tyranny; close to $500,000,000 in cash and in assets is the total value of what we were able to
get back from the corrupt politicians who had been sucking the blood of our country.
The correct investment of this wealth and of these resources is allowing the Revolutionary
Government at the same time to carry out a plan of industrialization and of increase in agriculture,
to build houses, build schools, send teachers to the farthest comers of the country, and give medi-
cal assistance to everybody, in other words, carry out a true program of social development.
And precisely now, at the Bogota meeting, as you know, the Government of the United States
proposed a plan. But, was it a plan for economic development? No, it proposed a plan for social
development. Now, what does this mean? What is understood by this? Well, it was a plan for
building houses, building schools and building roads. But does this settle the problem? Does this
solve it all? How can there be a solution to the social problems without a plan for economic de-
velopment? Is it that they want to hoodwink the other people of Latin America? What are the
16 -
families going to live on when they inhabit those houses, if those houses are actually built? What
shoes, what clothes, are they going to wear, and what food are they going to eat, when they go to
those schools, if those schools are actually built? Or perhaps is it not known that, when a family
does not have clothes or shoes for the children, the children are not sent to school? With what re-
sources are they going to pay the teachers? With what resources are they going to pay the doctors?
With what resources are they going to pay for the medicines? Do you want a good way of saving on
medicines? Increase the nutrition of the people for what is spent in feeding the people will not have
to be spent on hospitals.
In view of the tremendous reality of underdevelopment, the Government of the United States
now comes out with a plan for social development. Naturally it is something that it is concerning
itself with some of the problems of Latin America. Thus far it has not cared very much. Is it not
a coincidence that now, at this juncture, it is worried about these problems? And any similarity
with the fact that that concern has arisen after the Cuban revolution, well, possibly they'll say that
it's purely coincidental.
Thus far the monopolies have certainly not cared very much except for exploiting the under-
developed countries, but suddenly the Cuban revolution rears its head and the monopolies start
worrying. While our economy is attacked and they try to squash us, with the other hand the United
States Government offers charity to the peoples of Latin America, not the resources for develop- _
ment which is what Latin America wants but resources for social development, for houses for
people to live in who have no work, for schools to which children cannot go, and for hospitals that
would not be necessary if there were enough food to eat in Latin America.
After all, although some of my Latin American colleagues may feel it is their duty to be
discreet here, I would welcome a revolution such as the Cuban revolution which at any rate has
forced the monopolists t6 return at least a small part of what they have been taking in natural re-
sources and of the sweat of the peoples of Latin America.

text:
This photo was taken in 1970s Afghanistan.
The statue behind those people is 1,500 years old. Carved directly into a sandstone cliff in the Bamiyan Valley. Standing 55 meters tall. One of the greatest artistic achievements in human history.
Afghanistan in the 1970s had universities, cinemas, women in miniskirts, and tourists from around the world coming to see wonders like this.
Then came the wars.
On March 11, 2001, the Taliban spent 25 days dynamiting both Bamiyan Buddhas into rubble. They used anti-aircraft guns, rockets, and tanks. The world watched in horror.
1,500 years of history.
Gone in 25 days.
The empty niches still stand in the cliff today. Hollow. Silent. A wound that never healed.
UNESCO declared it a World Heritage Site in 2003. Two years too late.
Japan offered to fund reconstruction. The Taliban said no.
Some things can be destroyed in a moment that took centuries to build.
Afghanistan did not lose the Buddhas in 2001.
The world did. 🕊️

While India sleeps, at 3 AM, EtherealX strikes 🔥

EtherealX is developing a new rocket engine cycle (Full Flow Segregated Cooling Cycle - FFCC) specifically designed around the requirements of full rocket reusability, something the company says is a first-of-its-kind approach in rocketry.

A few CRAZY things they announced:
> 80 launches/year with just 4 rockets: targeting ~20 launches per rocket annually.
> Designing the engine around full reusability, not bolting reusability onto an existing architecture.
> Claiming >99% efficiency 🤯 while aiming for mass-producible, lower-complexity engines.
> They claim RP-1 offers 3–4× higher heat-sink capability than cryogenic fuels, helping with thermal management.
> Targeting 100 bar chamber pressure with a simpler engine architecture instead of ultra-complex staged-combustion designs.
> Instead of betting everything on one untested cycle, they're developing an entire family of engine cycles and letting testing determine the winner.

text:
$RKLB | THE DANGER OF THE ROCKET LAB MINDSET

Rocket Lab attracts a particular kind of low-intelligence investor because it offers instant comprehension. Rocket. Flame. Launch. Space. Exciting. The entire thesis can be absorbed through a ten-second video without understanding markets, economics, competitive structure or where the greatest future value may actually accumulate.

That simplicity produces misplaced intellectual confidence. People who understand very little become certain they understand everything. They latch onto the most visually obvious company, form a tribe around it, then ridicule anything requiring greater imagination, patience or mental range. They cannot see beyond themselves, so whatever exceeds their comprehension must be fraudulent, inferior or impossible.

That is what makes them dangerous. Low intelligence by itself is merely limiting. Low intelligence combined with tribal certainty becomes corrosive. It attacks complexity, punishes independent thought and tries to bury superior opportunities beneath repetition, mockery and noise.

Rocket Lab may be a perfectly respectable company. The embarrassing part is the investor culture that treats recognizing a rocket as evidence of exceptional insight. Rockets have fascinated children for generations. Pointing at one and shouting “future” is not discernment.

There are greater companies, greater ideas and greater asymmetric opportunities throughout the market. Finding them requires looking past spectacle and understanding what others cannot yet see.

The Rocket Lab cult does the opposite. It mistakes visibility for value, familiarity for intelligence and group enthusiasm for independent thought.

The rocket is not proof that they can see farther.

It is proof that they stopped looking at the first shiny object they understood.

🚨US IN SHOCK: Global Defence Buyers Choosing Affordable Indian Missiles and Akash Defence System Over Patriot Air Defence System, BrahMos Order Book Surges Toward $6 Billion

The global defence market is witnessing a significant shift as India's indigenous Akash surface-to-air missile system emerges as an increasingly attractive alternative to expensive Western air-defence platforms.

The wars in Ukraine and West Asia have demonstrated the importance of affordable, replenishable air defence. When low-cost drones and rockets are launched in large numbers, relying exclusively on extremely expensive interceptors becomes difficult to sustain. Akash offers a different proposition: effective capability, lower cost and scalable Indian production.

Developed by DRDO and manufactured through India's domestic defence ecosystem, Akash reduces dependence on foreign supply chains. Its upgraded variants, including Akash Prime and Akash-NG, are further expanding India's air-defence capabilities.

Its export success, particularly the deal with Armenia, has strengthened India's credibility as a defence supplier, with interest from other countries also growing.

Then comes BrahMos, India's other major missile success story. Following the Philippines deal, international interest in the supersonic cruise missile has expanded significantly, with the BrahMos order pipeline now widely reported at around $6 billion.

The significance goes beyond individual weapons. India is increasingly offering countries what many defence buyers need most: capable systems that are affordable, scalable and backed by a domestic production ecosystem.

India has not replaced America's Patriot—and the comparison should not be reduced to a simple winner-versus-loser contest. But the emergence of Akash as a credible alternative, alongside BrahMos' expanding global demand, marks a powerful change in the defence market.

India is no longer merely buying weapons from the world. It is increasingly building them, and selling them to the world.

text:
$ASTS | WHERE DOES THE VALUE ACTUALLY RESIDE IN SPACE?

Ricky’s post offers a useful example of how easily the space industry can be viewed through the wrong end of the telescope. He treats ownership of launch capability as the decisive competitive advantage and concludes that a company purchasing rides to orbit must therefore be structurally weaker than companies owning rockets.

Read his argument and then my response as a short primer on the space value chain. Launch is essential infrastructure, but infrastructure is not necessarily where the scarce intellectual property, customer access, regulatory position, or economic moat resides. As launch capacity expands across competing providers, the greater value increasingly belongs to companies building capabilities that cannot simply be purchased from a manifest.

In AST SpaceMobile’s case, the difficult achievement is not carrying a satellite into orbit. It is building a satellite, spectrum, semiconductor, network, regulatory, and carrier-distribution architecture capable of delivering broadband directly to ordinary phones from orbit. Rockets can be hired. That collection of capabilities cannot.
